Also, people with color-music synesthesia more often than not have had early musical training.
Once thought to be extremely rare, synesthesia is now found to affect about one to four percent of the population. [4] As is often observed, most of us tend to associate lower notes with darker colors and higher notes with brighter colors. Researchers further point out that in most people synesthesia is active only during the first months of their infancy, while this ability remains forever in certain individuals.
options: This consistency serves as a proof that synesthesia is real.
Meanwhile, environmental influences seem to shape a person’s synesthesia.
People with synesthesia used to be accused of making their experiences up.
Some studies even show that people may all be synesthetic to some degree.

optionsZh.C: 有聯覺的人過去常被指責是自己編造這些經驗。
optionsZh.A: 這種一致性可作為聯覺確實存在的證據。
optionsZh.B: 同時，環境的影響似乎也會形塑一個人的聯覺。
optionsZh.D: 有些研究甚至顯示，所有人可能都或多或少有聯覺。

篇章結構.passageZh:
你有沒有想過要幫星期一到星期日「上色」？聽別人說話的時候，你會看見一片彩虹般的顏色嗎？或者，莫札特的音樂嘗起來像蘋果派？如果是這樣，你很可能有聯覺。
聯覺是一種感官彼此交混的狀況。有些人有聯覺，在聽到、讀到、甚至只是想到字母和數字的時候，會經驗到顏色。另一些人則是文字會在舌頭上引發真實的味覺。
[1] 不過在一九九○年代初期，科學家注意到聯覺產生的顏色不會隨時間改變。問他們某個字母或數字會引發什麼顏色，即使兩次測驗相隔數月甚至數年，有聯覺的人始終給出同樣的答案。[2] 不過最有力的支持來自腦部掃描：這些人聽到某些字詞時，腦中負責處理顏色的區域會亮起來。
聯覺是遺傳來的，還是出生之後才有的？科學家同意聯覺有遺傳基礎，因為它常常在同一個家族裡出現。但真正的聯覺基因（或多個基因）目前還沒有找到。[3] 舉例來說，有「味覺—文字」聯覺的人嘗到的味道，通常是童年的味道，像巧克力或草莓。另外，有「顏色—音樂」聯覺的人，多半很小的時候就受過音樂訓練。
聯覺一度被認為極為罕見，現在則發現大約百分之一到百分之四的人口有這種現象。[4] 常見的觀察是，我們多數人都傾向把較低的音和較暗的顏色連在一起，把較高的音和較亮的顏色連在一起。研究者進一步指出，多數人的聯覺只在嬰兒期的頭幾個月活躍，某些人身上這個能力則會一直保留下來。

explanations.1:
先看空格的位置。它在第三段的第一句。前面兩段一段用問句破題、一段給定義，從頭到尾沒有人對聯覺表示過懷疑。
再看空格後面第一句。後面是 `In the early 1990s, however, scientists noticed that synesthetic colors do not change over time.`（然而到了一九九〇年代初，科學家注意到聯覺產生的顏色不會隨時間改變。）`however` 表示語意轉折——**要轉，前面得先有一個相反的立場。**
往下讀完整段：顏色不變、隔數月數年再問答案仍相同、最後腦部掃描提供最有力的支持。整段在數證據。既然結局是證明，開頭被轉掉的那個立場就是「不被相信」。

C 講的正是這件事，`used to`（過去曾經）與後面的 `In the early 1990s` 前後成對。

**這題只有四成一的人答對**：空格在段落第一句，前面隔著段落分界，往前找找不到；線索全在**後面**那個 `however`。四個選項又都在同一個話題上，光比對「有沒有關係」分不出來。
空格在段首、後面第一句就有 `however`，先問「它要轉掉的是哪一種說法」。那種說法就在空格裡。
explanations.2:
先看空格前面。前一句說：問聯覺者某個字母或數字讓他們看到什麼顏色，就算相隔數月或數年再測，他們始終給同樣的答案。這只是一個**現象**，還沒有人說它代表什麼。
再看空格後面。後面是 `The most compelling support, however, comes from brain scans`（然而最有力的支持來自腦部掃描）。「最有力的」是比較過的說法——**要說最有力，前面得先有一項沒那麼有力的支持。**
前面只有現象、後面要比支持，中間缺的就是把現象認定為證據的那一句。A 的 `This consistency` 指的正是前一句「始終同樣的答案」，`a proof that synesthesia is real` 就是那項比較弱的支持。
後面出現「最有力的證據／支持」這種比較過的說法，先回頭找那項比較弱的。前面找不到，它就在空格裡。
explanations.3:
先看這一段開頭的問句。第四段第一句是 `Is synesthesia genetically inherited or acquired after birth?`（聯覺是遺傳來的，還是出生以後才形成的？）問句擺明這一段要講**兩邊**：先天與後天。
再看空格前面。前面兩句都在講先天：聯覺有基因基礎，因為常有家族性；但真正的基因還沒找到。先天這一邊已經講完。
再看空格後面。後面是 `For example`，舉的是童年的巧克力、草莓味道，以及從小學過音樂——都是**後天環境**裡的事。既然是舉例，前面一定要有一句被它證明的話。
B 就是換邊的那一句。
段落開頭是「是 X 還是 Y」的問句，往下就邊讀邊分哪幾句屬 X、哪幾句屬 Y。空格常常是換邊的那一句。
explanations.4:
先數空格前後的人數。前一句說聯覺過去被認為極為罕見，現在發現約有 `one to four percent of the population`（百分之一到四的人）有。後一句卻說 `most of us tend to associate lower notes with darker colors`（我們大多數人會把低音和深色連在一起）。**從百分之一到四，一下子變成「我們大多數人」**，中間必須有一句把範圍推開。
D 正是那一句。`even`（甚至）承接前一句的百分比往上加，`all`（所有人）與 `to some degree`（或多或少）也正好帶出後面的 `most of us`。
前一句說「只有少數人」、後一句說「我們大多數人」，空格就是把範圍推開的那一句。前後兩句涵蓋的人數對不起來，中間一定缺一句。

篇章結構.title: 受傷之後還能不能運動（Exercising with Sports Injuries）
篇章結構.passage:
While Dr. Weinstein, a surgeon at Dartmouth College, was trying to lift a heavy box, he twisted his back. The pain was agonizing. The surgeon could not sit, and when he lay down he could barely get up. So he decided to go out for a run. He took an aspirin, iced the injured area, and off he went. When he returned, he felt “pretty good.”
[1] When people have sprained a muscle or tendon, they are usually advised not to go right back to exercising until the pain goes away. But Dr. Weinstein says that approach is outdated and counterproductive. In fact, when active people consult him, he usually tells them to just keep exercising.
Dr. Weinstein is not alone in his treatment of sports injury, but the specific advice can differ from specialist to specialist. [2] They nevertheless caution that a cutback may be necessary, such as running shorter distances or going more slowly. Others say the patients may need to engage in sports outside of their usual, main sport (that is, to cross-train), at least some of the time. Still others say the safest thing to do is cross-train all the time until the pain is gone. [3] Their consensus, however, is that unless the injury involves something as serious as a broken bone or a ripped muscle, moderate exercise can actually speed healing.
[4] Thus, more and more patients are now advised to keep moving despite the pain. The rule of thumb, however, is to see a doctor first and get an accurate diagnosis. If a serious injury is ruled out and the pain is not getting worse after exercising, then the exercise “makes a lot of sense.”
options: For example, an injured runner might end up cycling and swimming instead of running.
Over time, researchers have come to realize the importance of exercising when injured.
Many suggest that most patients can continue with the sport they love.
This seems to run counter to the common practice.

optionsZh.D: 這似乎和一般的做法相反。
optionsZh.C: 許多醫師認為，大多數病人可以繼續從事自己喜愛的運動。
optionsZh.A: 例如，受傷的跑者可能改成騎車和游泳，不再跑步。
optionsZh.B: 久而久之，研究者逐漸體認到受傷時運動的重要性。

篇章結構.passageZh:
達特茅斯學院的外科醫師溫斯坦，在搬一個重箱子的時候扭傷了背。那個痛非常難受。他坐不下來，躺下去之後又幾乎爬不起來。於是他決定出門去跑步。他吃了一顆阿斯匹靈，在受傷的地方冰敷，然後就出發了。回來之後，他覺得「還滿不錯的」。
[1] 一般人拉傷肌肉或肌腱之後，通常會被勸告先別馬上恢復運動，要等到不痛了再說。但溫斯坦醫師表示，那套做法已經過時，而且效果適得其反。事實上，有運動習慣的人來找他，他通常會叫他們繼續運動就好。
在運動傷害的處理上，抱持這種看法的不只溫斯坦醫師一人，不過各個專科醫師給的建議並不完全一樣。[2] 但他們仍提醒，減量可能是必要的，例如把距離縮短、或是跑慢一點。另一些醫師則說，病人至少有一部分時間需要從事自己主要運動以外的項目，也就是交叉訓練。還有一些醫師認為，最安全的做法是全程改做交叉訓練，直到不痛為止。[3] 不過他們的共識是：只要傷勢沒有嚴重到骨折或肌肉撕裂的程度，適度運動其實能加快復原。
[4] 因此，現在越來越多病人被建議即使會痛也要繼續活動。不過大原則是：先看醫師，取得正確的診斷。如果排除了嚴重傷害，而且運動之後疼痛沒有加劇，那麼運動就「很有道理」。

explanations.1:
先看空格的位置。它在第二段的第一句，而第一段整段在講一個故事：Weinstein 醫師搬重物扭到背，痛到坐不住，結果他決定出去跑步，回來反而覺得還不錯。
再看空格後面。後面說「人們拉傷肌肉或肌腱時，**通常會被建議**等不痛了再運動」。這句話講的正是「一般的做法」。
第一段是一個反常的故事，第二段要把它接到一般做法上，中間需要一句話點破兩者相反。D 的 `This` 指的就是第一段那整件事，`the common practice` 也讓後一句有了名目。
第一段講一個故事、第二段開頭是空格，先問「這個故事跟接下來要講的道理是什麼關係」——多半是相反。
explanations.2:
先看空格後面。後面是 `They nevertheless caution that a cutback may be necessary...`（他們仍然提醒，可能得減量，例如跑短一點或慢一點。）出現兩個問題：**`They` 是誰？** 前一句的主詞是「具體建議因專家而異」，沒有一群人可以指。**`nevertheless` 要轉什麼？** 前面得先有一個比較寬鬆的說法。
C 一次補上兩個：`Many` 給 `They` 當對象，「可以繼續原來的運動」正是那個寬鬆說法，後面才轉成「不過要減量」。

**再看這一整段的排法。** 往下讀會看到 `Others say...`、`Still others say...`。既然有「其他人」，前面一定要先有**第一群人**。C 的 `Many` 就是那第一群。
看到 `Others`、`Still others`，先確認前面有沒有「第一群人」。沒有，第一群就在空格裡。
explanations.3:
先看空格前面。前一句說：還有些醫師認為最安全的做法是一直做交叉訓練（cross-train），直到不痛為止。`cross-train` 是一個專門的詞，括號裡只解釋成「從事平常主項以外的運動」，**還沒有具體例子**。
再看空格後面。後面是 `Their consensus, however, is that...`，這是收尾，要把整段幾派說法收攏。收尾之前，那幾派說法必須已經講完。
A 正好補上具體例子：跑者改騎車和游泳，就是 cross-train 的樣子。
前面出現一個專門的詞卻沒舉例，空格常常就是那個例子。看到 `For example` 開頭的選項，先找它要說明哪一句。
explanations.4:
先看空格後面。後面是 `Thus, more and more patients are now advised to keep moving despite the pain.` `Thus`（因此）表示因果關係——**因此之前必須有原因**。
再看空格的位置。它在最後一段的第一句。前面三段講的是一位醫師的故事和幾位專家的說法，最後一段要把個案拉高到整體趨勢。
B 正好是那個原因，也正好是那個拉高。
空格後面第一個字是 `Thus`、`Therefore`、「因此」，空格裡放的一定是原因。

篇章結構.title: 膠囊旅館（Capsule Hotels）
篇章結構.passage:
A capsule hotel, also known as a pod hotel, is a unique type of basic, affordable accommodation. Originated in Japan, these hotels were initially meant for business professionals to stay close to populated business districts without spending a lot. [1]
A typical room of a capsule hotel is roughly the length and width of a single bed, with sufficient height for a guest to crawl in and sit up on the bed. The walls of each capsule may be made of wood, metal or any rigid material, but are often fiberglass or plastic. [2] Each capsule is equipped with a comfortable mattress, a small light, and sometimes a television or other entertainment options. Such minimalist design is what makes these hotels both inexpensive and efficient, providing only the essential elements for a good night sleep.
The first capsule hotel, the Capsule Inn Osaka, opened in 1979. Since then, capsule hotels have quickly spread to other cities and countries. Chains have emerged in Taiwan, Singapore, and even on resort islands like Bali. Pod hotels are also seen in Europe and North America, especially in big cities like New York, London, and Paris. [3] Instead of the traditional bare pod-sized style, new chains now feature interior design that appeals to digitally connected travelers from around the world. Guests may enjoy facilities such as free Wi-Fi, mobile charging, and even a soundless alarm system that raises the sleeping guests into a seated position while gradually brightening the lights.
While offering budget-conscious travelers a unique option, capsule hotels may not be suitable for everyone. Some hotels may not provide air conditioning in the capsules, leading to poor air flow. [4] Also, you may have to share common facilities (such as bathrooms) with other guests. And, if you’re worried about feeling claustrophobic in small spaces, you’d better think twice before making a reservation.
options: In response to rising demands, these hotels are embracing a wave of innovation.
The room’s thin plastic walls easily transmit the sound of snoring made by neighboring guests.
The chambers are stacked side-by-side, two units high, with the upper rooms reached by a ladder.
Today, they provide low-budget, overnight lodging in commerce centers in large cities worldwide.

optionsZh.D: 如今這類旅館在全球大城市的商業中心提供平價的過夜住宿。
optionsZh.C: 這些艙間並排堆疊，上下兩層，上層要爬梯子上去。
optionsZh.A: 為因應日益增加的需求，這類旅館正迎向一波創新。
optionsZh.B: 房間的塑膠薄牆很容易傳來隔壁客人的打呼聲。

篇章結構.passageZh:
膠囊旅館又稱為艙式旅館，是一種很特別的簡便平價住宿。這類旅館源自日本，最初是為了讓商務人士能住在人潮密集的商業區附近，又不必花太多錢。[1]
膠囊旅館典型的房間，長寬大約就是一張單人床的尺寸，高度則剛好夠客人爬進去、在床上坐直。每個艙間的牆面可以是木頭、金屬或任何堅硬的材質，但常見的是玻璃纖維或塑膠。[2] 每個艙間都配有舒適的床墊、一盞小燈，有時還有電視或其他娛樂設備。正是這種極簡的設計，讓這類旅館既便宜又有效率，只提供一夜好眠所需的基本要素。
第一家膠囊旅館「大阪膠囊旅館」於一九七九年開幕。從那時起，膠囊旅館很快擴散到其他城市與國家。台灣、新加坡都出現了連鎖品牌，連峇里島這樣的度假島嶼也有。艙式旅館在歐洲和北美也看得到，尤其是紐約、倫敦、巴黎這些大城市。[3] 新的連鎖品牌不再走傳統那種空蕩蕩、只有一個艙位大小的路線，而是主打室內設計，要吸引世界各地隨時連著網路的旅客。房客可以享有免費無線網路、手機充電，甚至還有無聲的鬧鐘系統——它會把還在睡的客人緩緩升成坐姿，同時把燈光逐漸調亮。
膠囊旅館雖然為精打細算的旅客提供了一個特別的選擇，卻不見得適合每個人。有些旅館的艙間裡沒有空調，空氣流通不佳。[4] 另外，你可能得和其他房客共用公共設施（例如浴室）。還有，如果你擔心自己在狹小空間裡會有幽閉恐懼的感覺，訂房之前最好再想一想。

explanations.1:
先看空格前面。前一句說膠囊旅館源於日本，`initially`（最初）是給商務人士用的，讓他們住得離商業區近又不必花大錢。看到「最初」，就要想到**還有「後來」**。
再看空格的位置。它是第一段的最後一句，第二段開始講房間長什麼樣。所以這一格要把「起源」這一段收掉。
D 的 `Today`（如今）正好與 `initially` 成對，`they` 指前面那些旅館，`worldwide`（全球）也把「日本起家」推到「哪裡都有」。
看到 `initially`、`at first`、「最初」，先找「後來怎麼了」。段落最後一格常常就是那句「後來」。
explanations.2:
先看這一段在講什麼。第二段從頭到尾是**規格說明**：房間多大、牆用什麼材料做、裡面有什麼設備。空格夾在「牆的材質」和「每個艙間配有床墊、小燈」之間。
再看空格後面。後面是 `Each capsule is equipped with...`（每個艙間配有……），已經講到艙間**內部**了。空格要放的，是還沒交代的**整體排列**。
C 講的正是排列方式，`The chambers`（這些艙間）用定冠詞，指的就是前面說的 capsule。
選項和上一句有同一個字，先別急著填。再問一次：這一句的**語氣**跟這一段合不合？
explanations.3:
先看空格後面。後面說 `Instead of the traditional bare pod-sized style, new chains now feature interior design that...`（新的連鎖店不再走傳統那種光禿禿的小艙風格，改以室內設計吸引……）。`Instead of the traditional`（不再走傳統的）表示**要講新東西了**，可是「新東西」這件事還沒有人宣布過。
再看空格前面。前面一直在數地點：台灣、新加坡、峇里島、紐約、倫敦、巴黎。都是「開到哪裡」，不是「變成什麼樣」。
A 就是那個宣布：這類旅館正迎向一波創新。有了它，後面的新設計、免費 Wi-Fi、無聲鬧鐘才有名目。
後面出現 `Instead of the traditional...`、`no longer...`，先確認前面有沒有人宣布過「要改了」。沒有，那句宣布就在空格裡。
explanations.4:
先看空格後面。後面是 `Also, you may have to share common facilities...`（此外，你可能得和其他客人共用浴室等公共設施）。`Also`（此外）表示這是**清單上的又一項**，前面至少已經列過兩項。
再看空格前面。前面只列了一項：有些旅館艙內沒空調，空氣不流通。
一項不夠撐起 `Also`，空格要補的就是第二項缺點。B 講打呼聲穿牆，正好是同一類的抱怨。

**回頭看一件事**：第二段說牆常用玻璃纖維或塑膠做，那時只是中性的規格；到了第四段，同一件事變成缺點。**同一個事實放在不同段落，任務不一樣**——這也是第 32 題不能選 B 的原因。
看到 `Also`、`Besides`、「此外」，先數前面已經列了幾項。只有一項，空格就是還缺的那一項。

篇章結構.title: 雲霄飛車是怎麼設計的（Designing a Roller Coaster）
篇章結構.passage:
Roller coasters have been known for their agonizingly slow starts, near heart-stopping drops and scream-inducing turns and loops. [1]
The designers must first consider what kind of riders will use the coaster. If the coaster is designed for small children, the hills and curves will be gentle, and the car speed will be relatively slow. Families usually want a somewhat faster ride with plenty of turns and moderate force. Ultimate thrill seekers want extreme heights and speed.
[2] Roller coasters usually take up a lot of room not only on the ground but also in the air. Designers must take into consideration surrounding rides, power lines, and other obstacles. Some amusement parks have added so many rides that a new roller coaster has to be designed to make its way through existing rides and walkways.
The next objective for the designers is to achieve a unique “feel” for the coaster. [3] Once up the incline, the first drop is usually designed to be the steepest, and therefore the fastest and scariest. Other drops can be designed with a brief flattened section in the middle, and are called double dips. Drops with very abrupt transitions to a flat or upturned section are called slammers because they slam the passengers down into their seats. Letting the cars run close to the ground, in what is called a gully coaster, gives the illusion of increased speed.
[4] Only after its safety is assured can the design be used to build a new roller coaster.
options: Designers must then consider the space available for the coaster.
Building an exciting roller coaster starts with a brilliant design.
Theme and type are also important aspects to consider in coaster design.
Designers can draw on a number of techniques to provide a memorable ride.
When the design is complete, detailed calculation and careful testing procedures will follow.

optionsZh.B: 要造出一台刺激的雲霄飛車，得從一份出色的設計開始。
optionsZh.A: 設計者接著必須考慮這台車可用的空間。
optionsZh.D: 設計者可以運用多種技法，做出令人難忘的乘坐體驗。
optionsZh.E: 設計完成之後，接著是詳細的計算與仔細的測試程序。
optionsZh.C: 主題與類型也是雲霄飛車設計時要考慮的重要面向。

篇章結構.passageZh:
雲霄飛車向來以幾件事出名：起步慢得讓人難熬、俯衝幾乎讓人心跳停止、轉彎和翻圈讓人忍不住尖叫。[1]
設計者必須先考慮這台車會有哪一種乘客。如果是為小朋友設計的，坡度和彎道都會比較平緩，車速也相對慢。全家一起搭的，通常會想要快一點、彎道多一點、力道適中的體驗。至於一心追求刺激的人，要的是極端的高度與速度。
[2] 雲霄飛車占掉的空間通常很大，不只是地面，連上方的空間也是。設計者必須把周邊的遊樂設施、電線和其他障礙物都算進去。有些遊樂園加蓋的設施太多，新的雲霄飛車只好設計成從既有的設施和步道之間穿過去。
設計者的下一個目標，是讓這台車有獨特的「感覺」。[3] 車子爬上斜坡之後，第一段俯衝通常會設計成最陡的一段，也因此最快、最嚇人。其他的俯衝可以在中間設計一小段平緩處，這種叫做 double dips（dip 是「往下沉一下」，double dip 就是一連沉兩次）。俯衝之後突然轉成平段或上揚段的叫做 slammers（slam 就是「用力摔、用力壓」），因為它們會把乘客狠狠壓進座位裡。讓車子貼近地面跑，也就是所謂的 gully coaster（gully 是地面的凹溝，等於讓車子在溝裡跑），會製造出速度變快的錯覺。
[4] 要等到安全性獲得確認之後，這份設計才能用來造出一台新的雲霄飛車。

explanations.1:
先看空格前面。第一段只有一句話：雲霄飛車以慢得磨人的起步、幾乎讓人心跳停止的落差，以及令人尖叫的轉彎和翻轉聞名。這一句從頭到尾在講**坐起來的感覺**，沒提過任何人。
再看空格後面。第二段第一句是 `The designers must first consider what kind of riders will use the coaster.`（設計者必須**先**考慮會是什麼樣的人來坐。）這裡有兩個字要抓：
- `The designers`：用了定冠詞，表示「設計者」前面已經提過。可是第一段一個人都沒有。
- `first`（首先）：表示接下來要一步一步數下去。既然有第一步，前面一定先宣布過「這件事要開始了」。

B 一次補上兩件事：`design`（設計）帶出後面的設計者，`starts with`（從……開始）宣布整篇要開始講設計流程。這一句也是全篇的主旨句。
空格後面出現 `first`、`then`、「首先」，先確認前面有沒有人宣布過「要開始一連串步驟了」。沒有，那句宣布就在空格裡。
explanations.2:
先看空格的位置。它在第三段的第一句，而上一段的第一句是 `The designers must first consider...`（必須**先**考慮……）。**上一段用 `first`，這一段的段首就該接 `then`。**
再看空格後面。後面說雲霄飛車很占地方，不只地面，連空中也是；設計者得把周邊設施、電線和其他障礙物都算進去。整段講的是**空間**。
A 的 `then` 接上了上一段的 `first`，`the space available`（可用的空間）也正是後面那一整段的內容。段首這一句要罩得住整段，A 剛好。
段首的空格，先把整段讀完再回頭挑。選項只要有一個關鍵詞在這一段裡找不到對應的內容，就不是它。
explanations.3:
先看空格前面。前一句說：設計者接下來的目標，是做出獨一無二的乘坐感（`a unique “feel”`）。這只說了**目標**，還沒說**怎麼做到**。
再看空格後面。後面是一長串具體做法：第一個落差通常設計得最陡、最快、最嚇人；中段做一小截平路的叫 double dips；落差末端突然轉平或上翹、把乘客壓進椅背的叫 slammers；讓車廂貼著地面跑的叫 gully coaster。**數一數，四種。**
一個目標後面接四種做法，中間需要一句話先說「有好幾種手法」。D 的 `a number of techniques`（多種技法）正是那一句，後面四種就是它的清單。
前面給目標、後面接一串具體做法，空格通常是「有好幾種辦法」這種概括句。先數後面列了幾項，再找哪個選項罩得住。
explanations.4:
先看空格後面。最後一段只有兩句，後面那句是 `Only after its safety is assured can the design be used to build a new roller coaster.`（唯有在安全獲得確認之後，這份設計才能拿去造出一台新的雲霄飛車。）
**「安全獲得確認」是誰確認的？** 要確認安全，前面必須先有檢驗這件事。可是前面三段從頭到尾在講怎麼設計，沒有任何一句提到檢驗或測試。

E 補上的正是這一步。`testing procedures`（測試程序）讓後一句的「安全獲得確認」有了來歷，`When the design is complete`（設計完成之後）也把前面三段的設計流程一次收掉。
後面那一句把某件事當作已經做過（「確認之後」「檢查完畢」），先回頭找那件事在哪裡做的。找不到，它就在空格裡。

篇章結構.title: 微笑背後的因素（What Shapes a Smile）
篇章結構.passage:
Smiling is a gesture that many people engage in dozens of times a day without thought. Most people believe that smiling is an expression of good feelings, a simple way to show happiness and friendliness. But does this hold true across time and cultures?
[1] In the West, for example, portraits of men and women before the 1700s typically depicted them with a serious, unsmiling expression. The absence of smiles stemmed partly from the attempt to hide their decayed teeth caused by poor dental hygiene. More importantly, smiling and laughter had long been perceived in the society as manifestations of a lack of self-control and good manners. Paintings with white-toothed smiles emerged after the 1700s, with the gradual rise of a culture that valued perception and responsiveness.
Recent studies also show that interpretations of smiling may vary from culture to culture. While in most cultures smiling is associated with positive emotions, in certain cultures the same person can be judged as less intelligent when smiling. [2]
The amount people smile is culturally influenced as well. People smile more when they are from countries that are high in individualism and low in population. These are often places where the needs and rights of the individual take precedence over those of the group. [3] Newcomers from different parts of the world are found to smile more. Without a shared language, they often resort to smiling to get along with others. For them, smiling is a straightforward way to indicate that one is reliable and trustworthy.
[4] As many psychologists now point out, this simple gesture is in fact far more complicated than it may appear.
options: Another crucial factor is a society's immigration diversity.
Various factors have thus contributed to the phenomenon of smiling.
For most of recorded human history, the open smile has been deeply unfashionable.
A genuine smile indicates contentment, while a forced smile suggests underlying distress.
In fact, there is a well-known Russian proverb that goes, "Smiling with no reason is a sign of stupidity."

optionsZh.C: 在有文字記載的歷史裡，絕大多數時間，露齒而笑都很不受青睞。
optionsZh.E: 事實上，俄羅斯有一句廣為人知的諺語：「無緣無故地笑是愚蠢的表現。」
optionsZh.A: 另一個關鍵因素是一個社會的移民多樣性。
optionsZh.B: 因此，種種因素共同造就了微笑這個現象。
optionsZh.D: 真心的笑代表滿足，強擠出來的笑則透露內心的不安。

篇章結構.passageZh:
微笑是許多人一天做上幾十次、卻從來不會多想的一個動作。多數人相信微笑是好心情的表現，是表達快樂與友善最簡單的方式。但這件事在不同的時代、不同的文化裡都成立嗎？
[1] 以西方為例，一七○○年代以前的男女肖像畫，畫中人物通常表情嚴肅、不帶笑容。畫裡沒有笑容，一部分是為了遮掩因口腔衛生不良而蛀壞的牙齒。更重要的是，在當時的社會裡，微笑與大笑長久以來都被看成缺乏自制與教養的表現。露出白牙微笑的畫作要到一七○○年代之後才出現，當時社會逐漸興起一種文化，看重一個人能不能察覺別人的心思、並且做出回應。
近期的研究也顯示，各文化對微笑的解讀可能不同。在多數文化裡，微笑和正面情緒連在一起；但在某些文化裡，同一個人只要笑了，就可能被認為比較不聰明。[2]
人們笑的次數多寡同樣受文化影響。一個國家如果個人主義色彩濃、人口又少，那裡的人就笑得比較多。在這些地方，個人的需求與權利往往優先於群體。[3] 研究發現，來自世界各地的新移民笑得比較多。在沒有共同語言的情況下，他們常常靠微笑來和別人相處。對他們來說，微笑是最直接的方式，用來表示自己可靠、值得信任。
[4] 正如許多心理學家現在所指出的，這個看似簡單的動作，其實遠比表面上複雜得多。

explanations.1:
先看空格前面。第一段最後一句是問句：`But does this hold true across time and cultures?`（但這在不同的時代和文化裡都成立嗎？）問句丟出兩個面向：**時代**和**文化**。
再看空格後面。後面是 `In the West, for example, portraits of men and women before the 1700s typically depicted them with a serious, unsmiling expression.`（例如在西方，一七〇〇年代以前的人像畫，畫中人多半表情嚴肅、不帶笑容。）既然是舉例，前面一定有一句被它證明的話。
這個例子有兩個特徵：講的是**過去**、講的是**不笑**。空格裡那一句必須同時對上這兩點。C 的 `For most of recorded human history`（歷史上大多數時間）是時代，`deeply unfashionable`（很不受青睞）是不笑，而且正好接上問句的第一個面向。
空格後面第一句就有 `for example`，先把那個例子的特徵一項一項列出來（講的是什麼時候？講的是什麼現象？），空格裡那一句必須每一項都對上。
explanations.2:
先看空格的位置。它在第三段的**最後一句**，段末的空格通常是補一個例子或收個尾。
再看空格前面。前一句說：在多數文化裡微笑代表正面情緒，但在某些文化裡，同一個人笑的時候反而會被認為 `less intelligent`（比較不聰明）。這是一個聽起來很反常的說法，說完就沒有下文了。
E 補的正是佐證。注意兩個字的對應：諺語裡的 `stupidity`（愚蠢）對上前一句的 `less intelligent`，`Russian`（俄羅斯）也讓「某些文化」有了具體對象。**兩處都不是同一個字，但意思一個接一個。**
前一句拋出一個聽起來很反常的說法，後面卻沒有下文，空格多半是那個佐證。看到 `In fact` 開頭的選項，先確認前面有沒有一句話等著被補強。
explanations.3:
先看空格前面。前面兩句在講第一個因素：個人主義高、人口少的國家，人們笑得比較多；那些地方個人的需求和權利先於團體。
再看空格後面。後面說 `Newcomers from different parts of the world are found to smile more.`（來自世界各地的新住民笑得更多。）**「新住民」是突然冒出來的**——前面講的是個人主義，一個字都沒提到移民。
空格要做的就是把話題轉到第二個因素。A 的 `Another crucial factor`（另一個關鍵因素）表示前面已經數過第一個，`immigration diversity`（移民多樣性）也正好帶出後面的新住民。
後面突然冒出一群前面沒提過的人，空格裡一定先把那群人帶出來。看到 `Another`，先回頭數「第一個是什麼」。
explanations.4:
先看空格的位置。它在最後一段的第一句，而最後一段只有兩句話。前面三段各講一個面向：時代、文化解讀、社會組成。到這裡，該講的都講完了。
再看空格後面。後面是 `As many psychologists now point out, this simple gesture is in fact far more complicated than it may appear.`（許多心理學家指出，這個簡單的動作其實遠比看起來複雜。）**要說「比看起來複雜」，前面得先有一句話說明複雜在哪裡。**
B 就是那一句：`Various factors`（種種因素）把前面三段一次收攏，`thus`（因此）表示因果，是從前面推出來的結論。
空格在最後一段的第一句，先回頭數這篇一共講了幾件事。最後一段要的通常是「把前面全部收起來」的那一句，不是再加一項。

閱讀測驗.title: 卡內基獎章：表彰英雄事蹟（Carnegie Medal: Honoring Heroic Deeds）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Most heroes are people like you. But what makes them heroes? They find special courage when they need it. They are brave enough to help in an emergency while others may stand by. A hero sees what needs to be done and does it.

Sometimes heroes are rewarded for their brave acts. One such reward is the Carnegie Medal. It is given to people who act bravely and face danger to save the lives of others.

The medal was named after Andrew Carnegie. In 1886, Carnegie heard about a young man by the name of William Hunter who lost his life trying to save two other boys from drowning. Carnegie became a very rich businessman and set aside money to honor heroes like William. Sometimes these heroes are in need or are hurt. If so, they receive money as well as the Carnegie Medal.

Over 6,000 people have received the Carnegie Medal. Some have saved people from drowning or from burning buildings. Others have pulled people in front of moving trains or saved them from attacks by wild animals. All these heroes have one thing in common, however. They put someone else's safety ahead of their own.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
大部分英雄都是像你一樣的平凡人。那麼，是什麼讓他們成為英雄呢？他們在需要的時候，能找到特別的勇氣。遇到緊急狀況，其他人可能只是站在一旁，他們卻勇敢地出手幫忙。英雄看到需要做的事，就去做。

有時候，英雄的勇敢行為會得到獎勵。卡內基獎章就是其中一種。這個獎章頒給勇敢行動、冒著危險去救別人性命的人。

這個獎章是以 Andrew Carnegie 的名字命名的。1886 年，Carnegie 聽說一位名叫 William Hunter 的年輕人，為了救兩個溺水的男孩而失去了性命。Carnegie 後來成了非常富有的商人，撥出一筆錢表揚像 William 這樣的英雄。有時候這些英雄生活困難或受了傷，這樣的話，他們除了卡內基獎章，還會得到一筆錢。

已經有 6,000 多人獲得卡內基獎章。有些人從水裡或失火的建築物裡救出別人；也有人把人從疾駛而來的火車前拉開，或從野生動物的攻擊中救人。不過，這些英雄都有一個共同點：他們把別人的安全放在自己的安全之前。

items.stem: The Carnegie Medal is given to those who are
items.explanation:
It is given to people who act bravely and face danger to save the lives of others.
They put someone else's safety ahead of their own.
第 2 段說卡內基獎章頒給勇敢行動（act bravely）、冒著危險救人性命的人；第 4 段說這些英雄都把別人的安全放在自己的安全之前。勇敢又無私，選項換成 unselfish and courageous，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 3 段的 young，William Hunter 是年輕人，但獎章並不限年輕人；(B) 照抄 rich，有錢的是設立獎章的 Carnegie；(A) 第 3 段說英雄如果生活困難或受了傷，還會另外得到錢，生病、貧窮不是頒獎的條件。

items.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: William Hunter was a very brave boy.
Some heroes have been rewarded for their bravery.
Carnegie was a rich businessman and liked to help people.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說英雄是在緊急時刻勇敢出手的人，第 2 段說英雄有時候會因為勇敢的行為得到獎勵，接著第 3、4 段介紹卡內基獎章的由來和得獎的人。全文的主旨是有些英雄因為勇敢得到表揚，所以是 (C)。(A) William Hunter 的故事只在第 3 段，是獎章的由來，過於狹隘；(D) Carnegie 是富有的商人，也只在第 3 段，過於狹隘；(B) 原文說 Hunter 是為了救兩個男孩而死，不是救了 Carnegie，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
options: Brave deeds can take many different forms.
Over 6,000 people are Carnegie Medal recipients.
Some heroes have received money as well as the Medal.
items.explanation:
Carnegie heard about a young man by the name of William Hunter
第 3 段說 Carnegie 是「聽說」（heard about）William Hunter 的事，看不出他認識 Hunter 本人，所以和原文不符的是 (A)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：第 4 段說有人從水裡、火場救人，有人把人從火車前拉開，英勇的行為有很多種形式，是 (B)；已經有 6,000 多人獲得獎章，是 (C)；第 3 段說生活困難或受傷的英雄，除了獎章還會得到一筆錢，是 (D)。

閱讀測驗.title: 徒手攀爬世貿中心的George Willig（George Willig's World Trade Center Climb）
閱讀測驗.passage:
On May 26, 1977, George Willig traveled to the top of the 1,350-foot-tall World Trade Center in New York City. He did not take the elevator, however. Instead, like a human fly, George Willig climbed the outside of the immense 110-story building. His climb, which began at 6:30 a.m., took three and a half hours to finish.

At the top, Willig was greeted by both police and reporters. Some of the police officers asked him for his autograph. Then they wanted to put him in jail and charged him with violation of law for climbing the building without a permit. Furthermore, the city also planned to sue him for a quarter of a million dollars. The amount, the police department reported, would pay the costs of rushing special equipment and eighty police officers in order to save him.

By the next day, city officials had reevaluated the situation. At City Hall, Mayor Abraham Beame hosted a news conference that turned into a ceremony in George Willig's honor. Beame announced that the city would not punish "The Human Fly." Instead, he would be fined a penny for each of the 110 floors he had climbed. Instead of punishing Willig, the city treated him as a hero who attempted the impossible and met the challenge.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
1977 年 5 月 26 日，George Willig 登上了紐約市 1,350 英尺高的世界貿易中心頂端。不過，他不是搭電梯上去的，而是像蒼蠅一樣，貼著這棟 110 層樓的巨大建築外牆往上爬。他從早上 6 點 30 分開始爬，花了三個半小時才爬完。

到了頂樓，迎接 Willig 的有警察，也有記者。有些警察還向他要簽名。接著警方想把他關進監獄，控告他未經許可攀爬大樓，觸犯法律。不只這樣，市政府還打算向他求償 25 萬美元。警察局說，這筆錢是用來支付緊急調派特殊裝備和 80 名警察去救他的費用。

到了第二天，市府官員重新評估了整件事。市長 Abraham Beame 在市政廳舉行記者會，結果記者會變成了表揚 George Willig 的典禮。Beame 宣布市政府不會處罰這位「人蒼蠅」（The Human Fly），只會照他爬的 110 層樓，每一層罰他一美分。市政府沒有處罰 Willig，反而把他當成敢於挑戰不可能、而且成功完成挑戰的英雄。

items.stem: George Willig reached the top of the World Trade Center in New York at
options: six thirty in the morning of May 26, 1977.
six thirty in the evening of May 26, 1977.
ten o'clock in the morning of May 26, 1977.
ten o'clock in the evening of May 26, 1977.
items.explanation:
His climb, which began at 6:30 a.m., took three and a half hours to finish.
第 1 段說 Willig 早上 6 點 30 分（6:30 a.m.）開始爬，花了三個半小時才爬完。6 點 30 分加上三個半小時是 10 點，所以他在早上 10 點到達頂端，是 (C)。(A) 6 點 30 分是他開始爬的時間；(B)、(D) 是晚上，原文寫的是 a.m.，指的是上午。

items.stem: This passage is a story about
options: a man who enjoys dangers and risks.
a human being who can fly like a fly.
a man who has escaped from the jail.
a fly which climbs like a human being.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說 Willig 不搭電梯，貼著 110 層樓的外牆爬上世界貿易中心，第 3 段說市政府把他當成敢於挑戰不可能的英雄。這是一個喜歡冒險、不怕危險的人的故事，所以是 (A)。三個錯誤選項都偏離主題：(B) 照抄 fly，human fly 是形容他像蒼蠅一樣爬牆，他並不會飛；(D) 也照抄 fly，故事的主角是人，不是蒼蠅；(C) 照抄 jail，第 2 段說警方想把他關進監獄，但他沒有坐牢，更沒有越獄。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
options: Willig was sent to prison for a year.
Willig was honored in a party and fined only $1.10.
Willig climbed the World Trade Center with permission.
items.explanation:
a ceremony in George Willig's honor
Instead, he would be fined a penny for each of the 110 floors he had climbed.
第 3 段說市長舉行的記者會變成了表揚 Willig 的典禮（a ceremony in George Willig's honor），而且只照他爬的 110 層樓，每層罰一美分。110 美分就是 1.10 美元，所以是 (C)。(A) 25 萬美元是市政府原本打算向他求償的金額，第二天就改了；(B) 警方原本想把他關進監獄，但原文沒有說他坐了一年牢；(D) 第 2 段說他是未經許可（without a permit）攀爬大樓。

閱讀測驗.title: 印刷術的發展歷程（The Development of Printing）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Printing is one of the most important means of communication. Without it you would not now be reading this passage. Even the development of radio and television has not diminished the importance of printing.

The first printing was done from wood blocks one letter at a time by hand. This was a slow process, requiring much skill and patience, and every page of every book had to be cut separately.

A great step forward was the use of movable type. The Chinese discovered this in the 11th century, but it was not known in Europe until about 1440. In this method of printing, individual letters were made from separate pieces of metal. If these letters were inked over and pressed on to paper, they would print the words. When the printing was finished, the letters could be taken apart and rearranged to print something else.

One of the first European books to be printed in movable type was Johannes Gutenberg's 42-line Bible. The first book to be printed likewise in English was about the history of Troy. It was printed in Flanders in 1474 by an Englishman, William Caxton. In 1476 he returned to England and established a printing press at Westminster. Altogether he printed nearly 80 books, many being his own translations from the French.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
印刷是最重要的溝通方式之一。要是沒有印刷，你現在就不會在讀這篇文章。即使有了廣播和電視，印刷的重要性也沒有減少。

最早的印刷是用木板，一次一個字母，全靠手工雕刻。這個過程很慢，需要很多技巧和耐心，而且每一本書的每一頁都得分開來刻。

一大進步是活字的使用。中國人在 11 世紀就發明了活字，但歐洲一直到 1440 年左右才知道。用這種方法印刷，每個字母都是用一塊塊分開的金屬做成的。字母塗上墨水、壓到紙上，就能印出字來。印完以後，這些字母可以拆開來重新排列，印別的東西。

歐洲最早用活字印刷的書籍之一，是古騰堡的《四十二行聖經》。第一本同樣用活字印刷的英文書，內容是特洛伊的歷史，1474 年由一位英國人 William Caxton 在法蘭德斯印製。1476 年他回到英國，在西敏設立了一家印刷廠。他總共印了將近 80 本書，其中很多是他自己從法文翻譯過來的。

items.stem: Printing is important because
options: it has made reading books possible.
it has helped to develop radio and television.
William Caxton printed 80 books in English.
items.explanation:
Without it you would not now be reading this passage.
第 1 段說要是沒有印刷，你現在就不會在讀這篇文章（would not now be reading this passage），也就是印刷讓閱讀成為可能，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 radio and television，原文說即使有了廣播和電視，印刷的重要性也沒有減少，沒有說印刷幫助了廣播、電視的發展；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 William Caxton，他印書是印刷發展的一段歷史，不是印刷重要的原因；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 Chinese，中國人發明的是活字，這也不是印刷重要的原因。

items.stem: The use of movable type was first introduced by
items.explanation:
The Chinese discovered this in the 11th century, but it was not known in Europe until about 1440.
第 3 段說中國人在 11 世紀就發明了活字（The Chinese discovered this），歐洲一直到 1440 年左右才知道，所以最早使用活字的是中國人，是 (D)。(B) 照抄 Europe，歐洲知道活字比中國晚了大約四百年；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 Gutenberg，古騰堡的聖經是歐洲最早用活字印刷的書之一；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 Caxton，他印的是第一本用活字印刷的英文書，時間更晚。

items.stem: According to the passage, the use of movable type was considered as a "great step forward" because
options: it did not need a lot of wood.
it required less skill and patience.
the printing letters could be reused.
every page of every book required individual carving.
items.explanation:
the letters could be taken apart and rearranged to print something else.
第 3 段說用活字印完以後，字母可以拆開來重新排列，印別的東西（rearranged to print something else），選項換成 could be reused，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 every page of every book，每一頁都得分開來刻，是木板印刷的缺點；(B) 照抄 skill and patience，需要很多技巧和耐心的也是木板印刷，原文沒有比較活字需要的技巧；(A) 照抄 wood，木板是舊的印刷方法，原文沒有說活字的好處是省木材。

items.stem: The first English book printed in movable type was
options: done from wood blocks one letter at a time.
done in a printing press at Westminster.
items.explanation:
The first book to be printed likewise in English was about the history of Troy.
第 4 段說第一本同樣用活字印刷的英文書，內容是特洛伊的歷史（about the history of Troy），所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 Gutenberg，古騰堡的聖經是歐洲最早的活字印刷書之一，不是英文書；(B) 照抄 Westminster，那本書 1474 年在法蘭德斯印製，Caxton 1476 年回英國以後，才在西敏設立印刷廠；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 wood blocks，用木板一個字母一個字母刻，是活字出現以前的方法。

閱讀測驗.title: 電腦駭客與網路犯罪（Computer Hacking and Cybercrime）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Breaking into the computer codes (known as 'hacking') of banks, large companies or even government departments is the latest game for super-intelligent teenagers. One young hacker said, "Hacking is just intellectual. It's your brain against the computer. It's like climbing Mount Everest—it's something you have to do. You don't even need a very expensive computer—but you must understand everything about all kinds of computers."

At the moment most of these games are just fun for young people. But how long will it be before criminal gangs, like the Mafia, start to use computer experts to help them in their crimes? Future bank robbers will not need explosives to blow open bank safes—all they will need is someone who can break computer codes. Already in Britain people say that computer crimes are costing companies between 500 million pounds and 2.5 billion pounds a year.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
破解銀行、大企業，甚至政府部門的電腦密碼（也就是所謂的「駭客入侵」），是超級聰明的青少年最新的遊戲。一位年輕的駭客說：「當駭客純粹是動腦的事，是你的頭腦和電腦對決。就像爬聖母峰一樣，是你非做不可的事。你甚至不需要很貴的電腦，但你一定要了解各種電腦的一切。」

目前，這些遊戲大多只是年輕人的消遣。可是，再過多久，像黑手黨這樣的犯罪集團就會開始找電腦專家幫他們犯罪呢？未來的銀行搶匪不需要用炸藥炸開銀行金庫，他們只需要一個能破解電腦密碼的人。在英國，已經有人說電腦犯罪每年讓企業損失 5 億到 25 億英鎊。

items.stem: The preceding passage refers to the word 'hacking' in the context of
items.explanation:
Breaking into the computer codes (known as 'hacking')
第 1 段開頭就用括號說明，破解電腦密碼就是所謂的 hacking（Breaking into the computer codes (known as 'hacking')），所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 climbing Mount Everest，爬聖母峰是年輕駭客拿來比喻非做不可的事；(B) 照抄 game，原文說駭客入侵是青少年的遊戲，這是在說它的性質，不是 hacking 這個字的意思；(D) 把實體物品拆開，原文沒有提到。

items.stem: According to the passage, breaking into computer codes of banks, large companies, and government departments is
options: a game for computer literate individuals.
being studied by the Mafia for fun.
soon to replace coding bank safes.
items.explanation:
is the latest game for super-intelligent teenagers
but you must understand everything about all kinds of computers
第 1 段說破解電腦密碼是超級聰明的青少年（super-intelligent teenagers）最新的遊戲，而且要了解各種電腦，選項換成 a game for computer literate individuals，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 Mafia，原文是在問黑手黨這類犯罪集團多久以後會找電腦專家幫忙，不是說他們在研究好玩；(D) 照抄 bank safes，原文說未來的搶匪不需要炸開銀行金庫，和破解電腦密碼取代金庫無關；(A) 第 2 段說目前大多只是年輕人的消遣，還不是普遍的犯罪手法。

items.stem: Based on the passage, in order to break into computer codes, one needs
options: an elaborate and expensive multi-media computer.
a group of computer science students.
the help and financial support from the Mafia.
a thorough understanding of a variety of computers.
items.explanation:
but you must understand everything about all kinds of computers
第 1 段的年輕駭客說，一定要了解各種電腦的一切（understand everything about all kinds of computers），選項換成 a thorough understanding of a variety of computers，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 expensive，原文說的正好相反，不需要很貴的電腦；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 Mafia，黑手黨是可能找電腦專家幫忙的犯罪集團，不是駭客需要的支援；(B) 原文沒有提到一群念電腦科學的學生。

閱讀測驗.title: 大型車輛導致交通事故與資源消耗（Large Cars Causing Accidents and Resource Depletion）
閱讀測驗.passage: There is increasing scientific evidence that large cars cause more highway accidents than small cars. In the news recently was the story of a woman who died of a heart attack while driving her station wagon. The car was moving so fast that it went through the highway-dividing fence, resulting in a collision in which five people died. Those unnecessary deaths are attributable in part to the woman's choice of a large automobile. A lighter and smaller car probably wouldn't have gone through the fence, its remaining energy would have been much less, and this would have reduced the chances of serious injury or death. Because of its small size, it might have missed the other car completely. The present design of the oversized automobile is largely responsible not only for increasing death toll on the highways but also for the rapid depletion of our resources of petroleum, for the pollution of our environment, and for the congestion and inconvenience of our cities.
閱讀測驗.passageZh: 愈來愈多科學證據顯示，大型車在公路上造成的事故比小型車多。最近新聞報導，一位女士開著她的旅行車，在途中心臟病發死亡。車子開得太快，衝破了公路的分隔護欄，造成一場五個人死亡的車禍。這些原本可以避免的死亡，部分要歸咎於這位女士選擇了大型車。換成輕一點、小一點的車，大概就不會衝破護欄，剩下的能量也會小得多，嚴重受傷或死亡的機會就會降低。而且小車體積小，說不定能完全避開另一輛車。目前這種超大型汽車的設計，不但是公路死亡人數增加的主要原因，石油資源迅速枯竭、環境汙染，以及城市的交通擁擠和不便，也大多是它造成的。

items.stem: For the five highway deaths, the author blames
options: the lack of more smaller vehicles.
items.explanation:
Those unnecessary deaths are attributable in part to the woman's choice of a large automobile.
原文說這些原本可以避免的死亡，部分要歸咎於這位女士選擇了大型車（a large automobile），也就是她開的那輛旅行車，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 heart attack，心臟病發是車禍的起因，但作者怪的是車子太大；(D) 照抄 highway-dividing fence，作者說換成小車大概就不會衝破護欄，問題在車子，不在護欄；(B) 作者主張的是這位女士該選小車，不是路上小車太少。

items.stem: What is the author's main point in the passage above?
options: Large cars should be banned by the government.
Large cars are less safe and less economical than small cars.
Small cars are safer for the occupants than large cars.
A woman's heart attack caused the death of five people.
items.explanation: 文章開頭說大型車造成的事故比小型車多，接著用一場車禍說明大型車比較危險，最後說大型車還造成石油枯竭、環境汙染和交通擁擠。作者的主要論點是大型車比小型車不安全、也不經濟，所以是 (B)。大考中心公布的答案是 (B) 或 (C)，選 (C) 小型車對乘客比大型車安全，也算答對。(D) 這位女士心臟病發只是作者舉的例子，作者要怪的是她開的大型車，過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有說政府應該禁止大型車，偏離主題。

items.stem: The author's statement about the highway fence's ability to retain a smaller and lighter car
items.explanation:
A lighter and smaller car probably wouldn't have gone through the fence
it might have missed the other car completely
作者說換成輕一點、小一點的車，「大概」（probably）就不會衝破護欄，下一句又用 might have missed，這些都是作者自己的推測，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 scientific evidence，開頭的科學證據說的是大型車造成的事故比較多，不是小車能不能擋在護欄內；(C) 小車會不會衝破護欄並沒有真的發生，不是事實；(D) 原文沒有說這種說法永遠無法證實。

閱讀測驗.title: 受困鯨魚的救援與野放（Rescue and Release of Stranded Whales）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Three pilot whales are believed to be swimming freely off the Atlantic Coast today. Their names are Tag, Notch, and Baby. These seagoing mammals are among the lucky survivors of a whale-stranding last December at Cape Cod.

As many as 60 pilot whales swam ashore. Scientists are still trying to find out why whales have this self-destructive behavior. Many of the whales died on the beach—crushed by their own weight. Whale experts found Tag, Notch, Baby alive. The three were believed to be too young to survive on their own or returned to sea.

The three whales were taken in a van to the New England Aquarium in Boston, Mass. They were kept in a 60,000-gallon tank for seven months. Only a few people worked with the whales so that they would not become too accustomed to human beings.

Early this past summer the three whales were pronounced fit enough to be returned to the Atlantic Ocean. A month after their release, the whales were spotted. They were found in a group of 50 whales about 60 miles from where they had been set free.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
一般相信，今天有三隻領航鯨正在大西洋沿岸外海自由自在地游著。牠們的名字是 Tag、Notch 和 Baby。去年 12 月鱈魚角發生鯨魚擱淺，這三隻海洋哺乳動物是少數幸運的倖存者。

多達 60 隻領航鯨游上了岸。科學家還在設法找出鯨魚為什麼會有這種自我毀滅的行為。很多鯨魚死在海灘上，是自己的體重把自己壓死的。鯨魚專家發現 Tag、Notch 和 Baby 還活著。一般認為這三隻年紀太小，沒辦法自己活下去，也沒辦法直接送回海裡。

這三隻鯨魚用廂型車載到麻州波士頓的新英格蘭水族館，在一個 60,000 加侖的水槽裡養了七個月。只有少數幾個人照顧牠們，以免牠們太習慣人類。

今年夏初，這三隻鯨魚確定夠健康，可以回到大西洋了。野放一個月後，有人看到了牠們。牠們和一群 50 隻鯨魚在一起，距離野放的地點大約 60 英里。

items.stem: The 60 pilot whales swam ashore as a result of
options: a large winter storm off the coast of Cape Cod.
a behavior currently unknown to scientists.
a genetic phenomenon currently being studied by whale experts.
the return to their annual spawning ground near Cape Cod.
items.explanation:
Scientists are still trying to find out why whales have this self-destructive behavior.
第 2 段說多達 60 隻領航鯨游上岸，科學家還在設法找出鯨魚為什麼會有這種自我毀滅的行為（still trying to find out why），也就是原因目前還不清楚，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 whale experts，鯨魚專家是發現三隻小鯨魚還活著的人，原文沒有說他們在研究遺傳現象；(A) 擱淺發生在 12 月，但原文沒有提到暴風雨；(D) 原文沒有說鱈魚角是鯨魚每年產卵的地方。

items.stem: The pilot whales died on the beaches of Cape Cod due to
options: the lack of salt water to facilitate their respiration.
the lack of nutrition to maintain their enormous body weight.
their body structure unable to support their body weight out of water.
a phenomenon yet to be figured out by scientists.
items.explanation:
Many of the whales died on the beach—crushed by their own weight.
第 2 段說很多鯨魚死在海灘上，是自己的體重把自己壓死的（crushed by their own weight）。鯨魚離開了水，身體承受不了自己的重量，選項換成 unable to support their body weight out of water，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 weight，原文說的是體重壓死了自己，不是缺乏營養；(D) 科學家還不清楚的，是鯨魚為什麼游上岸，不是牠們為什麼死；(A) 原文沒有提到海水和呼吸。

items.stem: The three whales Tag, Notch, and Baby were rescued because
options: younger whales have a greater chance of survival than the others.
amongst the many whales found beached, these three were deemed the healthiest.
they were alive when the rescue team found them.
the rescue crew liked them very much.
items.explanation:
Whale experts found Tag, Notch, Baby alive.
第 2 段說鯨魚專家發現 Tag、Notch 和 Baby 還活著（alive），這三隻才送到水族館照顧，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 young，原文說這三隻年紀太小，沒辦法自己活下去，正好和選項說年紀小比較容易活下去相反；(B) 原文沒有說牠們是最健康的三隻；(D) 原文沒有說救援人員特別喜歡牠們。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT true?
options: Scientists are studying the suicidal behavior of pilot whales.
Tag, Notch, and Baby were too young to survive by themselves in the sea.
Pilot Whales are mammals that can become used to human beings.
After their release, Tag, Notch, and Baby were never seen again.
items.explanation:
A month after their release, the whales were spotted.
第 4 段說野放一個月後，有人看到了牠們（the whales were spotted），牠們和一群 50 隻鯨魚在一起，所以和原文不符的是 (D)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：第 2 段說科學家還在研究鯨魚自我毀滅的行為，是 (A)；三隻鯨魚年紀太小，沒辦法自己活下去，是 (B)；第 3 段說只讓少數人照顧，以免牠們太習慣人類，可見鯨魚是會習慣人類的，是 (C)。

閱讀測驗.title: 家書：恭賀Tom大學入學（Family Letter: Congratulating Tom on College Acceptance）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Oct. 6, 1996

Dear Tom,

It seems only yesterday that Jack and I were helping you learn your ABC's—and now you have finished high school and been accepted at Taipei University.

We are both very proud of you, Tom. We have followed your high-school career with joy and pleasure and know that your four years at college will be even more rewarding. A word of congratulation just doesn't seem enough, so I am sending you a gift that I'm sure you will find useful—an unabridged dictionary. Jack says you'll not only find it handy in your studies, but a great argument-saver when playing Scrabble with your friends.

Mom and Dad are coming here for a weekend next month. Please try to take a few days off and come to join us. We are looking forward to seeing you.

Love,
Sally
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
1996 年 10 月 6 日

親愛的 Tom：

好像昨天 Jack 和我才在教你學 ABC，現在你已經高中畢業，還考上了台北大學。

Tom，我們兩個都非常以你為榮。我們一路看著你念高中，又開心又欣慰，也知道你大學四年會過得更充實。只說一聲恭喜好像不夠，所以我要送你一份禮物，相信你一定用得上：一本未刪節的大辭典。Jack 說，這本辭典不但讀書時很好用，和朋友玩 Scrabble 拼字遊戲的時候，也是避免爭吵的好幫手。

爸爸媽媽下個月要來我們這裡過週末。請盡量空出幾天來和我們聚一聚。我們很期待見到你。

愛你的 Sally

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a reason for writing the letter?
options: To congratulate Tom on his wonderful achievement.
To tell Tom of his parents' planned visit.
To invite Tom to join a weekend family get-together.
To ask Tom to go home for the weekend.
items.explanation:
A word of congratulation just doesn't seem enough
Mom and Dad are coming here for a weekend next month.
Please try to take a few days off and come to join us.
Sally 寫信的理由有三個：第 4 段恭喜 Tom 考上大學，是 (A)；第 5 段告訴他爸媽下個月要來過週末，是 (B)；請他空出幾天來和大家聚一聚，是 (C)。Sally 說爸媽要來的是「這裡」（coming here），請 Tom 過來一起聚，不是叫他回家，所以選 (D)。

items.stem: "Scrabble" is
items.explanation:
a great argument-saver when playing Scrabble with your friends
第 4 段說辭典是 a great argument-saver when playing Scrabble with your friends。Scrabble 是要「玩」（playing）的，還要和朋友一起玩，玩的時候查辭典可以避免爭吵，可見 Scrabble 是一種拼字遊戲，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 argument-saver，(B) 照抄 dictionary，(D) 照抄 gift，這三個選項說的都是那本大辭典。

items.stem: On the basis of the letter, what is the most likely relationship between Sally and Tom?
items.explanation:
Jack and I were helping you learn your ABC
Mom and Dad are coming here for a weekend next month.
第 5 段 Sally 寫信給 Tom，說 Mom and Dad 下個月要來，要 Tom 一起來聚；她對 Tom 直接稱 Mom and Dad，說的就是兩人共同的爸媽。第 3 段又說 Sally 和 Jack 在 Tom 小時候教他學 ABC，可見 Sally 是 Tom 的姊姊，所以是 (B)。如果是 (A) 母子，Mom and Dad 就成了 Tom 的祖父母，Sally 寫給兒子時不會這樣稱呼；(C) 祖孫也一樣說不通；(D) niece 和 nephew 是同一位長輩的姪女和姪子，兩人不會有同一對爸媽。

閱讀測驗.title: 外國人入境台灣的簽證規定（Visa Regulations for Foreigners Entering Taiwan）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Generally speaking, all foreigners coming to Taiwan should apply for entry visas through the embassies or consulates of the Republic of China, or agencies authorized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

As of May 1, 1995, all nationals of the following 15 countries are exempted from securing visas for entry into the Republic of China: U.S.A., Japan, Canada, Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Holland, New Zealand, Australia, Austria, Germany, Britain, France, Spain, and Portugal. The maximum duration of stay is 14 days. Requirements for a 14-day non-visa entry are: passport good for at least six months, confirmed onward ticket within 14 days, no violation of law recorded.

If it is necessary to stay more than 14 days and less than 30 days, nationals of the specific countries holding a 14-day non-visa entry should in the meantime apply for a landing-visa with the authorized office in the CKS airport from the Bureau of Consular Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The landing-visa fee is NT$1,500.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
一般來說，所有要來台灣的外國人，都應該透過中華民國的大使館、領事館，或外交部授權的機構申請入境簽證。

自 1995 年 5 月 1 日起，下列 15 國的國民入境中華民國免辦簽證：美國、日本、加拿大、比利時、盧森堡、瑞典、荷蘭、紐西蘭、澳洲、奧地利、德國、英國、法國、西班牙和葡萄牙。停留期限最長 14 天。14 天免簽證入境的條件是：護照效期至少六個月、持有 14 天內離境的確認機票，而且沒有違法紀錄。

如果需要停留超過 14 天、不到 30 天，持 14 天免簽證入境的這些國家國民，應該在停留期間向外交部領事事務局設在中正機場的授權辦事處申請落地簽證。落地簽證的費用是新台幣 1,500 元。

items.stem: When an American lady wants to enter Taiwan for a one-week sight-seeing trip, one of the requirements is
options: to obtain a landing-visa at the CKS airport.
to apply for a visa before leaving the U.S.A.
to make sure her passport was issued before May 1, 1995.
to make sure her passport is valid for more than six months on the date of arrival.
items.explanation:
passport good for at least six months
美國在第 2 段的 15 國名單裡，停留一星期不到 14 天，可以免簽證入境，條件之一是護照效期至少六個月（good for at least six months），所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 landing-visa，停留超過 14 天才要申請落地簽證；(C) 照抄 May 1, 1995，那是免簽證開始實施的日期，和護照什麼時候核發無關；(B) 美國國民免簽證，不必出發前先辦簽證。

items.stem: If a British businessman wants to visit some trade partners in Taiwan for about three weeks, what should he do?
options: He should obtain a visa for entry into the Republic of China before getting on board the flight to Taiwan
He should travel with a friend who is from any of the other 14 countries mentioned.
He must obtain a landing-visa at the CKS airport.
He just needs to apply for a non-visa entry when he arrives at the CKS airport.
items.explanation:
If it is necessary to stay more than 14 days and less than 30 days
should in the meantime apply for a landing-visa with the authorized office in the CKS airport
英國在第 2 段的免簽證名單裡，但是三週大約 21 天，超過 14 天、不到 30 天。第 3 段說這種情況要向設在中正機場的辦事處申請落地簽證，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 non-visa entry，免簽證入境最多只能停留 14 天；(A) 照抄 entry into the Republic of China，第 2 段說的是英國國民入境中華民國免辦簽證，不必出發前先辦；(B) 和其他國家的朋友同行，原文沒有提到。

items.stem: Which of the following is needed for a landing-visa?
options: A passport that is valid for more than six months.
items.explanation:
passport good for at least six months
nationals of the specific countries holding a 14-day non-visa entry
The landing-visa fee is NT$1,500.
第 3 段說申請落地簽證的，是持 14 天免簽證入境的國民，所以要有 (B)；免簽證入境本來就要護照效期至少六個月，所以 (A) 也是條件；落地簽證的費用是新台幣 1,500 元，所以還要繳 (C)。三項都需要，所以是 (D)。

閱讀測驗.title: 大腦兩半球與語言學習（Brain Hemispheres and Language Learning）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The brain, which weighs less than 2.2 pounds, is perhaps the most complicated organ in our bodies. Although scientists have not been able to solve all the mysteries of this amazing organ, they have made some progress. They have found that certain parts of the brain are responsible for learning, memory, and language.

Recent studies indicate that the two halves of the brain—the right hemisphere and the left hemisphere — play extremely important roles in learning and communicating. The left hemisphere deals with rules, lists of information, and short-term memory. In contrast, the right hemisphere deals with feelings, colors, and long-term memory. Scientists recognize the importance of both hemispheres in the learning of all sorts, including language learning.

Scientists now relate left and right hemispheres to the way different individuals learn languages. They believe that some learners use one half of their brains more than the other half. Left-brained learners usually concentrate on memorizing rules and lists. They use logic, definition, and repetition to learn. Right-brained learners look for a general picture and concentrate on relating new information to what they already know. They use associations and intuition to learn. Most people fall into one of these types. If teachers know whether their students are left-brained or right-brained, they can help them learn better.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
大腦重不到 2.2 磅，也許是我們身體裡最複雜的器官。科學家雖然還沒能解開這個神奇器官的所有謎團，但已經有一些進展。他們發現，大腦的某些部位負責學習、記憶和語言。

最近的研究指出，大腦的兩半，也就是右半球和左半球，在學習和溝通上扮演極為重要的角色。左半球處理規則、一連串的資訊和短期記憶。相反地，右半球處理感受、色彩和長期記憶。科學家認為兩個半球對各種學習都很重要，語言學習也包括在內。

科學家現在把左右半球和每個人學語言的方式連在一起。他們認為，有些學習者用其中一半大腦用得比另一半多。左腦型的學習者通常專注於背規則和清單，用邏輯、定義和反覆練習來學習。右腦型的學習者會先看整體的樣貌，專注於把新資訊和已經知道的東西連結起來，靠聯想和直覺來學習。大多數人都屬於這兩型的其中一種。如果老師知道學生是左腦型還是右腦型，就能幫助他們學得更好。

items.stem: Mary is a typical left-brained learner. Which of the following descriptions does NOT fit her?
options: She thinks in a very logical way.
She is very artistic and romantic.
She often scores A in sentence-combining tests.
She is very good at math.
items.explanation:
In contrast, the right hemisphere deals with feelings, colors, and long-term memory.
They use logic, definition, and repetition to learn.
第 3 段說左腦型學習者專注於背規則和清單，用邏輯、定義和反覆練習來學習；第 2 段說處理感受、色彩的是右半球。富有藝術氣息又浪漫，靠的是感受和色彩，比較像右腦型，所以不符合 Mary 的是 (B)。其他三個選項都符合左腦型：思考很有邏輯，是 (A)；句子合併測驗要照規則組合句子，常拿 A，是 (C)；擅長數學要靠邏輯，是 (D)。

items.stem: What is the most significant implication that teachers can draw from the above information? They should
options: show students how to use logic to solve problems
urge students to relate new information to what they already know.
try to find out the best learning styles for individual students.
items.explanation:
If teachers know whether their students are left-brained or right-brained, they can help them learn better.
第 3 段最後說，如果老師知道學生是左腦型還是右腦型，就能幫助他們學得更好。老師要先找出每個學生適合的學習方式，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 rules，背規則是左腦型學習者的方法；(B) 照抄 logic，用邏輯也是左腦型的方法；(C) 照抄 new information to what they already know，連結新舊資訊是右腦型的方法。這三個選項都只適合其中一型的學生。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Damage of one hemisphere does not always cause complete loss of speech.
Remembering one's way home involves short-term memory.
Language learning takes place only in one hemisphere.
Scientists have solved all the mysteries of the brain.
items.explanation:
Scientists recognize the importance of both hemispheres in the learning of all sorts, including language learning.
第 2 段說兩個半球對各種學習都很重要，語言學習也包括在內。語言既然不只靠一個半球，一邊受損時，另一邊還能發揮作用，不一定會完全失去說話能力，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 language learning，原文說的正好相反，語言學習要靠兩個半球；(B) 照抄 short-term memory，回家的路要長久記住，屬於長期記憶；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 mysteries，原文說科學家還沒解開所有謎團。

items.stem: What is the best title of this passage?
options: Discoveries in the Field of Hemispheres
items.explanation: 第 1 段說大腦也許是身體裡最複雜的器官，稱它為 amazing organ，接著第 2、3 段介紹左右半球的分工，以及左右腦和學語言方式的關係，全文談的都是人類的大腦，所以是 (D)。(A) 短期和長期記憶只在第 2 段提到一句，過於狹隘；(B) 左右半球的研究發現是第 2、3 段的內容，沒有涵蓋第 1 段，過於狹隘；(C) 只說是一項最新的科學發現，沒有點出大腦，太過廣泛。

閱讀測驗.title: 木匠店的回收再分配計畫（The Carpenters' Shop: Recycle and Redistribution Project）
閱讀測驗.passage:
I wonder how often your family has bought new furniture, curtains or kitchen equipment and then wondered how to dispose of the old items that still have quite a lot of life left in them.

It was in response to this situation that The Carpenters’ Shop was opened in the town of Walsall, Staffordshire. Run by a team of church volunteers, the shop will collect any surplus, good-quality items and store them until they can be redistributed to the people who are needing those particular things.

Many have been helped through the scheme, including single parents, disabled people and the elderly, and those who have lost all their household possessions through a disaster such as a house fire.

It’s an admirable project, and it is worth finding out if a similar one operates in your hometown. Participation costs the donor nothing and can make such a difference to others.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
我很好奇，你家有多少次買了新家具、新窗簾或新的廚房用具，接著就煩惱舊東西要怎麼處理？那些舊東西其實還能用很久。

正是為了解決這種情況，斯塔福德郡的沃爾索爾鎮開了一家 The Carpenters’ Shop。這家店由一群教會志工經營，會收集任何多餘、品質良好的物品，存放起來，直到可以重新分送給正好需要這些東西的人。

許多人透過這項計畫得到幫助，包括單親家長、身心障礙者和老人，以及在房屋失火這類災難中失去所有家當的人。

這是一項值得讚賞的計畫，也值得查一查你的家鄉有沒有類似的計畫。捐贈者參與這項計畫不必花一毛錢，卻能讓別人的生活大不相同。

items.stem: The phrase dispose of in the first paragraph can best be replaced by ______.
items.explanation:
wondered how to dispose of the old items
第 1 段說家裡買了新家具、新窗簾，就煩惱舊東西要怎麼 dispose of；第 2 段接著說這家店收集多餘的物品，再重新分送出去。可見 dispose of 是把不要的東西處理掉，和 get rid of 意思相同，所以是 (B)。(A) put up with 是忍受，(C) look down upon 是看不起，(D) take notice of 是注意，放進句子都說不通。

items.stem: The purpose of setting up The Carpenters’ Shop was ______.
options: to help those who could not afford certain household items
to open a furniture store run by church volunteers
to teach people how to destroy disposable furniture
to sell good-quality furniture to disabled people
items.explanation:
until they can be redistributed to the people who are needing those particular things
Many have been helped through the scheme
第 2 段說這家店收集多餘、品質良好的物品，再分送給需要的人；第 3 段說受到幫助的有單親家長、身心障礙者、老人和遭遇火災的人。開這家店，是要幫助缺少家用物品、自己又買不起的人，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 church volunteers，教會志工是經營這家店的人，這家店也不是家具行；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 disabled people，身心障礙者是受到幫助的人之一，而且物品是分送，不是賣；(C) 原文沒有說要教人銷毀家具。

items.stem: What is the author’s opinion of an item that someone doesn’t need any longer?
options: It should be donated to charity.
There may be something wrong with it.
items.explanation:
Participation costs the donor nothing and can make such a difference to others.
第 4 段作者稱讚這項計畫，要讀者查查家鄉有沒有類似的計畫，還說捐贈者（the donor）不必花錢，卻能讓別人的生活大不相同。作者認為用不到的東西應該捐出去，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 admirable project，作者稱讚的是這項計畫，不是那件物品；(A) 第 1 段說舊東西還能用很久，作者沒有說它們過時；(D) 第 2 段說收集的是品質良好的物品，不是有問題的東西。

閱讀測驗.title: Jack的磁碟醫生服務（Jack's Disk Doctor Service）
閱讀測驗.passage:
What can you do if you ‘lose’ the data from your disks? To find an expert, who would recover the lost information for you, is probably the easiest solution. Jack Olson is one of these experts. Jack and a few of his friends set up a company called “Jack’s Disk Doctor Service” in 1984. They work from home and give all the money they earn to charity. The fees are always the same, no matter how precious the data on the disk is. Some people, however, are so grateful that they send extra money to Jack or to the charities his company supports. One oil company offered him $2000 for his help and an architect even sent him a blank check.

It would be difficult to put a value on the things rescued by the Disk Doctor. There have been disks containing medical research, television scripts, manuscripts of whole books, a lawyer’s papers for a court case, and even Margaret Thatcher’s travel plan for a visit to eastern Europe. For this last case, Jack had to go in person to Thatcher's office ‘for security reasons’!

Disks are usually sent to the Disk Doctor by post, but sometimes people are in such a hurry that they cannot wait for the mail to come. For example, some radio scripts had to be rushed by taxi to Jack’s house because they were needed for broadcasting the next day. When the material has been recovered, the disk is returned to the sender with a diagnosis and a prescription for avoiding the problem in the future. One grateful client, an author, put a “thank you” to Jack in the front of his book. “Jack saved me from a heart attack,” he wrote. “But,” says Jack, “most people don’t take any notice of the doctor’s advice!”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
如果磁碟裡的資料「不見了」，你該怎麼辦？找專家幫你救回遺失的資料，大概是最簡單的辦法。Jack Olson 就是這樣的專家。1984 年，Jack 和幾個朋友成立了一家公司，名叫「Jack’s Disk Doctor Service」。他們在家工作，把賺來的錢全部捐給慈善團體。不管磁碟裡的資料多珍貴，收費都一樣。不過，有些人感激到另外寄錢給 Jack，或寄給他的公司支持的慈善團體。有一家石油公司給了他 2,000 美元當謝禮，還有一位建築師甚至寄給他一張空白支票。

Disk Doctor 救回來的東西，價值很難估算。這些磁碟裡有醫學研究、電視劇本、整本書的手稿、律師打官司用的文件，甚至還有柴契爾夫人訪問東歐的行程。最後這一件，Jack 還得「基於安全理由」親自到柴契爾夫人的辦公室處理！

磁碟通常是用郵寄的方式送到 Disk Doctor 那裡，不過有時候客戶急得等不及郵件送到。例如，有些廣播稿第二天就要播出，只好用計程車火速送到 Jack 家。資料救回來以後，磁碟會寄還給寄件人，附上一份診斷和一張處方，告訴他們以後怎麼避免同樣的問題。有一位很感激的客戶是作家，他在自己的書前面寫了一段話感謝 Jack：「Jack 讓我免於心臟病發作。」但是 Jack 說：「大部分的人根本不理會醫生的建議！」

items.stem: What does the word rescued in the second paragraph mean?
items.explanation:
who would recover the lost information for you
It would be difficult to put a value on the things rescued by the Disk Doctor.
第 1 段說找專家把遺失的資料救回來（recover the lost information），第 2 段的 the things rescued by the Disk Doctor 指的就是 Disk Doctor 救回來的資料，所以 rescued 和 recovered 意思相同，是 (A)。(B) prescribed 是開處方，第 3 段的處方是資料救回來以後附上的建議；(C) examined 是檢查，(D) discovered 是發現，都不是把遺失的資料救回來。

items.stem: Why did the architect send Jack a blank check?
options: The architect did not have any money
The architect did it for security reasons
The architect always followed the doctor's advice
The architect thought Jack's service was priceless
items.explanation:
Some people, however, are so grateful that they send extra money to Jack or to the charities his company supports.
It would be difficult to put a value on the things rescued by the Disk Doctor.
空白支票讓收款人自己填金額。第 1 段說有些客戶感激到額外寄錢，第 2 段又說 Disk Doctor 救回來的東西價值很難估算（difficult to put a value on），建築師寄空白支票，是覺得 Jack 的服務無價，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 security reasons，基於安全理由親自跑一趟的，是處理柴契爾夫人行程那一次；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 doctor's advice，Jack 說大部分的人都不理會建議，原文也沒有說建築師照著做；(A) 建築師願意讓 Jack 自己填金額，不是沒有錢。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
options: Jack’s Disk Doctor Service has only one standard fee.
Jack and his company have made a fortune from their service.
Margaret Thatcher is a very important person.
Jack’s clients are from all walks of life.
items.explanation:
They work from home and give all the money they earn to charity.
第 1 段說 Jack 和朋友把賺來的錢全部捐給慈善團體（give all the money they earn to charity），他們沒有靠這項服務發財，所以和原文不符的是 (B)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：第 1 段說收費都一樣，是 (A)；處理柴契爾夫人的行程要基於安全理由親自到她的辦公室，可見她是重要人物，是 (C)；客戶有石油公司、建築師、律師、作家，還有電視、廣播節目，各行各業都有，是 (D)。

items.stem: From the statement “But … most people don’t take any notice of the doctor's advice!” we can infer that ______.
options: most people don’t take medicine regularly
many of Jack’s patients would probably get sick again
many of Jack’s clients have sought for his help more than once
most people don’t read the instruction when using a computer
items.explanation:
the disk is returned to the sender with a diagnosis and a prescription for avoiding the problem in the future
most people don’t take any notice of the doctor’s advice
第 3 段說磁碟寄還時，附上診斷和避免同樣問題的處方（a prescription for avoiding the problem in the future），Jack 卻說大部分的人都不理會這些建議。不照建議做，資料就可能再出問題，所以很多客戶不只一次找他幫忙，是 (C)。這裡的 doctor 是 Jack 的 Disk Doctor，處方是保護資料的建議，(A) 吃藥、(B) 病人再生病，都把比喻當成真的醫生；(D) 原文說的是不理會 Jack 的建議，不是不看電腦的使用說明。

閱讀測驗.title: 人際關係的建立與維繫（Building and Maintaining Relationships）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Do you know the meaning of the word “relationship”? Here is an easy way of understanding it. Whenever two people come together, even for a brief moment, they exchange looks, feelings, thoughts, ideas, and energy. Their relationship is how they interact with each other. Everything that happens in the world happens through relationships. We human beings need to love and be loved, and this will come from our relationship with others. Accordingly, anyone who wishes to love and be loved will want to establish lasting relationships.

Here are a few tips to help us create enduring relationships. First, know our steps. The relationship between two people is like the art of dancing. Before we can dance with a partner, we need to be able to dance by ourselves. We need to feel the rhythm of the music, hear how it inspires us to move and learn our unique style of movement and expression. Second, trust. As the key building block for enduring relationships, trust is a bond that evolves as two persons get to know each other and experience safety in opening their hearts. Trust develops when we respect each other’s needs and develop a history of common experience and caring. Third, be intimate. While intimacy is often limited to the sexual bond, we can be intimate with many people without sexuality. That is, by relating heart to heart. We need to be seen and known by another person. In this way, intimacy enables us to thrive and grow. Lastly, treat relationship as an organism. A new relationship is like an embryo that requires time, care and attention to grow into whatever may evolve. In our proper relationship with others, we will be known and seen for who we are, and love will come out of the seeing and the knowing.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
你知道「關係」這個詞的意思嗎？這裡有個簡單的理解方法。每當兩個人碰在一起，即使只有短短一下子，他們也會交換眼神、感受、思緒、想法和能量。他們的關係，就是他們彼此互動的方式。世界上發生的每一件事，都是透過關係發生的。我們人類需要愛人，也需要別人愛，而這份愛來自我們和他人的關係。因此，想要愛人、也想要別人愛的人，都會想建立長久的關係。

下面有幾個建議，幫助我們建立持久的關係。第一，熟悉自己的舞步。兩個人之間的關係就像跳舞的藝術。在能和舞伴一起跳舞以前，我們得先能自己跳。我們要感受音樂的節奏，聽聽音樂怎麼激勵我們舞動，學會屬於自己的獨特動作和表達方式。第二，信任。信任是建立持久關係最關鍵的基石；兩個人逐漸了解彼此，敞開心胸時覺得安心，這份連結就會隨之發展。我們尊重彼此的需要，累積共同的經驗和關懷，信任就會慢慢建立起來。第三，親密。一般人常把親密只當成性方面的連結，但是不涉及性，我們也可以和許多人很親密，也就是心與心的交流。我們需要另一個人看見我們、了解我們。這樣一來，親密讓我們茁壯成長。最後，把關係看成一個有機體。新的關係就像胚胎，需要時間、照顧和關注，才能長成它可能長成的樣子。在和他人適當的關係裡，別人會看見、了解我們真正的樣子，而愛就從這份看見和了解中產生。

items.stem: The author writes the above passage chiefly to ______.
options: encourage readers to build blocks for intimacy
tell readers that things happen through feelings
urge readers to become expert dancers
items.explanation: 第 1 段解釋什麼是關係，說想要愛人、也想要別人愛的人，都會想建立長久的關係；第 2 段接著提出四個建議，幫助讀者建立持久的關係。作者寫這篇文章，是要幫助讀者建立良好的關係，所以是 (C)。(B) 第 1 段說世界上的事都是透過關係發生的，選項換成透過感受（feelings），既改錯了字，也只講第 1 段，過於狹隘；(A) 第 2 段說信任是建立持久關係的基石（building block），選項卻拿來和親密連在一起，偏離主題；(D) 跳舞只是比喻，作者沒有要讀者成為舞蹈高手，偏離主題。

items.stem: The word tips in the second paragraph refers to ______.
items.explanation:
Here are a few tips to help us create enduring relationships.
第 2 段說 Here are a few tips to help us create enduring relationships，接著用 First、Second、Third、Lastly 列出四點做法，可見 tips 指的是幫助我們建立持久關係的建議，所以是 (D)。tip 也有「小費」的意思，(A) 費用就是從這個意思來的，放在這裡說不通；(B) 服務、(C) 限制，都不是接下來列出的四點。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true?
options: Intimacy is limited to the sexual bond.
“Trust” blocks the way to durable relationships.
If you do not dance, you cannot establish relationships.
Exposure of one’s inner thoughts is essential for enduring relationships.
items.explanation:
trust is a bond that evolves as two persons get to know each other and experience safety in opening their hearts
We need to be seen and known by another person.
第 2 段說兩個人逐漸了解彼此、敞開心胸（opening their hearts）時覺得安心，信任就會發展；談親密時又說我們需要另一個人看見、了解我們。敞開心胸，讓別人了解自己的內心，是持久關係不可少的，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 limited to the sexual bond，原文說一般人常把親密只當成性方面的連結，接著用 While 轉折，說不涉及性也可以很親密；(B) 照抄 block，原文說信任是建立持久關係的基石（building block），不是阻礙；(C) 照抄 dance，跳舞是比喻，意思是要先了解自己，不是說不會跳舞就建立不了關係。

items.stem: The love we desire will come from all of the following EXCEPT ______.
items.explanation:
We human beings need to love and be loved, and this will come from our relationship with others.
A new relationship is like an embryo that requires time, care and attention to grow into whatever may evolve.
第 2 段說新的關係就像胚胎（like an embryo），需要時間、照顧和關注才能成長；胚胎是用來比喻新的關係，作者沒有說喜歡胚胎能帶來愛，所以選 (A)。其他三個選項都是原文說的愛的來源：第 1 段說愛來自我們和他人的關係，也就是人與人的互動，是 (B)；第 2 段的信任，是 (C)；心與心交流的親密，是 (D)。

閱讀測驗.title: 俄羅斯父子澎湖獲救記（Russian Father and Son Rescued in Penghu）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Penghu, Nov.24—Two Russians, a father and a son, were rescued Saturday near the Penghu Islands off southwestern Taiwan after their sailboat broke down and began drifting.

Medvedev Vladimir, 43, and his son, Maxsine, 14, sailed from an unnamed eastern Russian seaport on August 18, to begin an ambitious around-the-world cruise.

Their voyage, down the coastline of northeastern mainland China, through the East China Sea, then down the Taiwan Strait and into the South China Sea, had been smooth until four days ago when the mainsail of their twin-mast sailboat “Kawasaki” was smashed by strong winds on the high seas.

The father-and-son team started the inboard engine. However, after less than two days, the engine broke down.

Near the “black ditch” of Penghu, battered by winds of up to 70 knots, the rear sail was torn into shreds. The rudder also stopped responding.

Surprised by the father and son’s “pale faces” and their battered vessel, the Penghu police and fishers in Paisha rescued them. Speaking only limited English, the Vladimirs spent five hours trying to explain their presence.

It is not immediately known whether the “Kawasaki” can be repaired on the fishing island of Penghu, or when the Vladimirs will be able to set off again and continue their around-the-world voyage.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
澎湖 11 月 24 日電：兩名俄羅斯人，一對父子，帆船故障、開始漂流以後，週六在台灣西南外海的澎湖群島附近獲救。

43 歲的 Medvedev Vladimir 和 14 歲的兒子 Maxsine，8 月 18 日從俄羅斯東部一個未透露名稱的港口出航，展開一趟雄心勃勃的環球航行。

他們的航程先沿著中國大陸東北部的海岸線南下，穿過東海，再南下台灣海峽，進入南海。一路都很順利，直到四天前，強風在公海上打碎了他們那艘雙桅帆船「Kawasaki」的主帆。

這對父子發動了船上的引擎。可是不到兩天，引擎就故障了。

在澎湖的「黑水溝」附近，風速高達 70 節的強風猛烈吹打著帆船，後帆撕成了碎片，舵也失靈了。

澎湖的警察和白沙的漁民看到這對父子「臉色蒼白」、船隻破損不堪，都嚇了一跳，於是救起了他們。Vladimir 父子只會說一點英文，花了五個小時，才解釋清楚他們為什麼會出現在這裡。

「Kawasaki」能不能在澎湖這個漁業島嶼上修好，Vladimir 父子什麼時候能再出發、繼續環球航行，目前都還不知道。

items.stem: What was the purpose of the voyage of the Vladimirs?
options: To look for their lost family members.
To start the inboard engine of their vessel.
items.explanation:
to begin an ambitious around-the-world cruise
第 2 段說父子倆從俄羅斯出航，是要展開一趟環球航行（an around-the-world cruise），所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 Penghu，他們是帆船故障、漂流到澎湖附近才獲救，澎湖不是目的地；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 inboard engine，發動引擎是主帆打碎以後的應變；(C) 原文沒有提到尋找失散的家人。

items.stem: Which course (direction) did the Vladimirs take to get to Penghu?
items.explanation:
down the coastline of northeastern mainland China
then down the Taiwan Strait and into the South China Sea
第 3 段說他們沿著中國大陸東北部的海岸線南下（down），穿過東海，再南下台灣海峽，一路往南走，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 East，East China Sea 是東海的名稱，不是航行的方向；(D) 照抄 north，northeastern 說的是中國大陸東北部的海岸，他們是從那裡往南走；(B) 往西航行，原文沒有提到。

items.stem: When did the “Kawasaki” first get into trouble during the voyage?
options: Less than two days after departure from Russia.
About four days before the inboard engine was started.
After it had sailed from Russia for more than three months.
Only after it drifted to Paisha County of the Penghu Islands.
items.explanation:
Nov.24
sailed from an unnamed eastern Russian seaport on August 18
had been smooth until four days ago
第 2 段說他們 8 月 18 日出航，第 1 段的電訊日期是 11 月 24 日，第 3 段說航程一直很順利，直到四天前主帆打碎，也就是 11 月 20 日前後才第一次出問題，這時已經出航三個多月，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 less than two days，那是發動引擎以後不到兩天引擎就故障，不是出航以後兩天；(B) 照抄 four days，四天前是主帆打碎的時間，主帆打碎以後才發動引擎，選項把先後弄反了；(D) 照抄第 6 段的 Paisha，漂到澎湖以前，帆和舵早就壞了。

items.stem: What did the Vladimirs decide to do after they were rescued?
options: To stay in Penghu and do some fishing.
To sell the boat and return to Russia.
To repair the boat and sail back to Russia.
They had not made any decision yet.
items.explanation:
It is not immediately known whether the “Kawasaki” can be repaired
第 7 段說「Kawasaki」能不能在澎湖修好、父子倆什麼時候能再出發繼續環球航行，目前都還不知道（It is not immediately known），也就是還沒有任何決定，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 repair，原文說的是能不能修好還不知道，而且他們要繼續的是環球航行，不是開回俄羅斯；(A) 照抄 fishing，fishing island 是說澎湖是漁業島嶼，不是他們要留下來捕魚；(B) 原文沒有提到賣船。

閱讀測驗.title: 機器人擔任畢業典禮演講者（Robot as a Commencement Speaker）
閱讀測驗.passage:
One of the most unusual graduation speakers of the 1983 commencement season was not a person at all. The speaker was Robot Redford, a robot who delivered the commencement address at a community college in suburban Maryland.

The speaker, carefully programmed, arrived on the stage under its own power and proceeded to tell the audience of 658 graduates, their families, and friends that they would have to learn to work with robots and technology to solve society’s problems. The robot described itself as an extension of a person to help humans increase the workload. Although this particular robot can be programmed to speak, the voice heard wasn’t that of the robot, because it was feared that the robot’s voice was not loud enough to carry throughout the hall. An amplified voice of a human was used instead, while the listeners watched the robot.

Robot Redford was followed by a person, William Bakaleinikoff, who spoke about the need for cooperation between people and technology. Mr. Bakaleinikoff’s experience with his topic included the fact that he had created Robot Redford and had provided the voice for the robot’s words to the graduates.

There was quite a bit of controversy over the choice of a robot as a commencement speaker. Some students thought it was insensitive and degrading to use a robot. Others thought the idea was clever and innovative.

“I’ll never forget this speech,” said one graduate. “You forget a political leader, but you won’t forget a robot.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
1983 年畢業典禮季最特別的畢業演講者之一，根本不是人。這位演講者是 Robot Redford，一個機器人，它在馬里蘭州郊區一所社區大學的畢業典禮上致詞。

這位演講者經過精心設定程式，靠自己的動力走上講台，接著告訴在場的 658 位畢業生和他們的家人、朋友，他們必須學會和機器人、科技合作，來解決社會的問題。機器人把自己形容成人的延伸，能幫助人類完成更多工作。雖然這個機器人可以設定程式說話，但大家聽到的並不是機器人的聲音，因為有人擔心機器人的聲音不夠大，沒辦法傳遍整個禮堂。所以改用擴音的人聲，觀眾則看著機器人。

接在 Robot Redford 後面演講的是一個人：William Bakaleinikoff，他談到人和科技需要合作。Bakaleinikoff 先生對這個題目的經驗包括：Robot Redford 就是他製造的，機器人對畢業生說的話，也是他配的音。

選機器人當畢業典禮的演講者，引起不少爭議。有些學生認為用機器人既不體貼，又有貶低人的意味。也有人認為這個主意很聰明、很有創意。

「我永遠不會忘記這場演講。」一位畢業生說：「政治領袖你會忘記，但機器人你不會忘記。」

items.stem: Robot Redford’s speech was discussed in this article mainly because ______.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說機器人當畢業演講者非常不尋常，第 4 段說選機器人當演講者引起不少爭議（controversy），有人覺得不妥，有人覺得有創意，第 5 段再用畢業生的話收尾。這場演講會寫成報導，主要是因為它引起爭議，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 insensitive，那只是第 4 段部分學生的看法，過於狹隘；(A) 照抄 political，第 5 段的畢業生只是拿政治領袖和機器人比較，演講內容和政治無關，偏離主題；(B) 文章沒有談到心理學，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
options: Robot Redford was a talking machine.
Robot Redford walked to the stage by itself.
Robot Redford made a graduation speech in 1983.
Robot Redford graduated from a college in Maryland.
items.explanation:
a robot who delivered the commencement address at a community college in suburban Maryland.
第 1 段說 Robot Redford 是在馬里蘭州一所社區大學的畢業典禮上致詞（delivered the commencement address），它是演講者，不是畢業生，所以和原文不符的是 (D)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：第 2 段說這個機器人可以設定程式說話，是 (A)；它靠自己的動力走上講台（under its own power），是 (B)；第 1 段說這是 1983 年的畢業典禮季，是 (C)。

items.stem: Which of the following statements can be supported by the passage?
options: A robot was designed to let humans decrease their productivity.
Robot Redford was the brainchild of William Bakaleinikoff.
Everybody in the commencement was pleased with the arrangement.
Robot Redford’s speech was too difficult to understand.
items.explanation:
he had created Robot Redford
第 3 段說 Bakaleinikoff 製造了 Robot Redford（he had created Robot Redford），選項的 brainchild 指的是某人構想出來的心血結晶，所以是 (B)。(A) 第 2 段說機器人能幫助人類完成更多工作，不是降低生產力；(C) 第 4 段說這個安排引起爭議，有學生覺得不妥，不是每個人都滿意；(D) 原文沒有說演講太難懂。

閱讀測驗.title: 父親的夏季家庭學校（Father's Summer Home School）
閱讀測驗.passage: Summers with father were always enjoyable. Swimming, hiking, boating, fishing--the days were not long enough to contain all of our activities. There never seemed to be enough time to go to church, which disturbed some friends and relatives. Accused of neglecting this part of our education, my father still instituted a summer school for my brother and me. His summer course included ancient history, which Papa felt our schools neglected, and navigation, in which we first had a formal examination in the dining room, part of which consisted of tying several knots in a given time limit. Then we were each separately sent on what was grandly referred to as a cruise in my father’s 18-foot boat, spending the night on board, and loaded down, according to my mother, with enough food for a week. I remember that on my cruise I was required to formally plot our course, using the tide table, even though our goal was an island I could see quite clearly across the water in the distance.
閱讀測驗.passageZh: 和父親一起過的夏天總是很愉快。游泳、健行、划船、釣魚，白天再長也裝不下我們所有的活動。我們好像從來沒有時間上教堂，這讓一些朋友和親戚很不以為然。有人指責父親忽略了我們這方面的教育，但他還是替我和我的兄弟辦了一所夏季學校。他的暑期課程包括古代史，因為爸爸覺得我們的學校忽略了這門課；還有航海，航海課我們先在飯廳參加一場正式的考試，考試的一部分是要在規定的時間內打好幾種繩結。接著，我們兩個分別出發，參加一趟他很隆重地稱為「航行」的行程，搭的是父親那艘 18 英尺長的船，晚上就睡在船上；照媽媽的說法，船上裝的食物夠吃一個星期。我記得在我那趟航行中，我得用潮汐表正式規劃我們的航線，儘管我們的目的地是一座小島，我隔著海面遠遠望去就看得清清楚楚。

items.stem: As used in the passage, “navigation” clearly means ______.
options: the practice of sailing a boat
the act of piloting an airplane
a formal examination in a dining room
items.explanation:
part of which consisted of tying several knots in a given time limit
I was required to formally plot our course, using the tide table
原文說航海課要在規定時間內打好幾種繩結，接著搭父親的船出海過夜，還要用潮汐表規劃航線。這些都是駕船出海的本事，所以 navigation 指的是駕駛船隻，是 (B)。(D) 照抄 formal examination，飯廳裡的正式考試只是航海課的一部分；(A) 照抄 summer school，夏季學校是父親辦的整套課程，航海只是其中一門；(C) 文中出海用的是船，和開飛機無關。

items.stem: Which of the following activities was NOT planned by the father for his children’s summer education?
items.explanation:
There never seemed to be enough time to go to church
原文說夏天的活動太多，好像從來沒有時間上教堂（never…enough time to go to church），親友還因此指責父親，所以不在父親安排的活動裡的是 (A)。其他三個選項都在父親的安排裡：開頭列出的夏天活動有健行、游泳，是 (B)、(C)；暑期課程包括古代史，是 (D)。

items.stem: The main reason for holding the summer school was ______.
options: to show the children the importance of religion
to teach the children how to spend a night on board
to reward the children for completing summer school
to make up for things missing in a regular classroom
items.explanation:
His summer course included ancient history, which Papa felt our schools neglected
原文說父親的暑期課程包括古代史，因為他覺得學校忽略了這門課（our schools neglected），選項換成補足一般課堂上缺少的東西（things missing in a regular classroom），所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 night on board，在船上過夜只是航海課的一部分，不是辦夏季學校的主要原因；(C) 照抄 summer school，原文沒有說要獎勵孩子；(A) 有人指責父親忽略了宗教教育，但他辦的課程裡沒有宗教。

閱讀測驗.title: 巴黎千禧年木製艾菲爾鐵塔計畫（Paris Millennium Wooden Eiffel Tower Project）
閱讀測驗.passage:
PARIS, Dec. 9 -- Paris will be given a new Eiffel Tower--but made of wood--for the millennium, city mayor Jean Tiberi said Tuesday, presenting a program of celebration for the year 2,000 which would transform the “city of light” into the “capital of light.”

The new structure will be 200 meters high, 100 meters shorter than the cast-iron Eiffel Tower built 100 years ago.

It will be made of timber as an ecological symbol of “the right to a dignified life on a protected Earth,” said architects Normier, Henni and Lelievre, who were also responsible for the Europe section at the Seville exhibition.

The tower, of pinewood, will be built on eight pillars and will be topped with a flower of five metal petals of 700 square meters each.

The structure, to be erected in the redeveloped areas of the capital’s 13th district, will cost 250 million francs (US$42 million).

Tiberi also said that Paris would be placed under the sign of the lights of “culture and life” and “intelligence.”

“If, in 1900, Paris was consecrated the ‘city of light’, it will become the ‘capital of light’ for the millennium,” Tiberi said.

The mayor said new buildings would be illuminated, notably along the banks of the Seine, which would become a luminous strip, while Notre Dame Cathedral would be lit from the inside to show off its stained glass windows.

A laser clock would be installed on top of the Arc de Triomphe at the top of the Champs Elysees and three laser beams would pick out the hands showing the hours, minutes and seconds in the millennium countdown, Tiberi said.

A giant egg-timer will be set up in the Place de la Concorde and its sand will begin running after a solar eclipse scheduled on April 11, 1999.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
巴黎 12 月 9 日電：巴黎市長 Jean Tiberi 週二表示，巴黎將有一座新的艾菲爾鐵塔，不過是木造的，用來迎接千禧年。他同時提出 2000 年的慶祝計畫，要把這座「光之城」變成「光之首都」。

新的建築高 200 公尺，比 100 年前建造的鑄鐵艾菲爾鐵塔矮 100 公尺。

建築師 Normier、Henni 和 Lelievre 說，這座塔用木材建造，是要作為生態的象徵，代表「在受到保護的地球上，享有尊嚴生活的權利」。這三位建築師也負責過塞維亞博覽會的歐洲區。

這座松木塔將建在八根柱子上，塔頂是一朵有五片金屬花瓣的花，每片花瓣 700 平方公尺。

這座建築將豎立在巴黎第 13 區重新開發的地區，造價 2.5 億法郎（4,200 萬美元）。

Tiberi 也說，巴黎將以「文化與生活」和「智慧」之光為主題。

「如果說 1900 年巴黎獲尊為『光之城』，那麼到了千禧年，巴黎將成為『光之首都』。」Tiberi 說。

市長說，新建築會打上燈光，特別是塞納河兩岸，塞納河將成為一條發光的帶子；聖母院則會從內部點燈，展示它的彩繪玻璃窗。

Tiberi 說，香榭麗舍大道頂端的凱旋門上方會裝設一座雷射時鐘，三道雷射光分別標出時針、分針和秒針，為千禧年倒數計時。

協和廣場將設置一座巨型沙漏，沙子會在預定 1999 年 4 月 11 日發生的日蝕之後開始流動。

items.stem: Why is Paris building a new Eiffel Tower?
options: The old Eiffel Tower must be torn down.
The old iron Eiffel Tower needs to be re-built with wood.
The tower is built to celebrate the Seville exhibition.
The tower is built to celebrate the coming of the year 2,000.
items.explanation:
presenting a program of celebration for the year 2,000
第 1 段說巴黎要蓋一座木造的新艾菲爾鐵塔來迎接千禧年，市長同時提出 2000 年的慶祝計畫（a program of celebration for the year 2,000），所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 Seville exhibition，第 3 段說建築師負責過塞維亞博覽會的歐洲區，蓋塔不是為了慶祝那次博覽會；(B) 照抄 wood，新塔用木頭蓋，但舊的鑄鐵鐵塔並沒有要改建；(A) 原文沒有說舊鐵塔要拆掉。

items.stem: According to Mayor Tiberi, Paris will be decorated mostly by ______.
items.explanation:
which would transform the “city of light” into the “capital of light.”
The mayor said new buildings would be illuminated
市長要把巴黎從「光之城」變成「光之首都」（capital of light），第 8 段說新建築和塞納河兩岸要打燈、聖母院從內部點燈，第 9 段還要在凱旋門上裝雷射時鐘，裝飾巴黎的主要是燈光，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 flower，花是新塔塔頂的造型；(C) 照抄第 8 段的 new buildings，新建築是打燈的對象，裝飾靠的是燈光；(D) 照抄 tower，新塔只有一座。

items.stem: What is “the Seine” mentioned in the passage?
options: The name of the new tower.
items.explanation:
notably along the banks of the Seine, which would become a luminous strip
第 8 段說 the banks of the Seine，bank 是河岸，塞納河兩岸要打上燈光，整條變成一條發光的帶子，所以塞納河是一條河，是 (C)。(B) 新塔的名稱，原文沒有提到；(A) 高聳的紀念碑、(D) 擁擠的街道，都不會有兩岸（banks）。

items.stem: Why is the new tower made of wood?
options: To serve as a symbol of environmental concerns.
To reduce the weight and ensure the safety.
Out of the consideration of the limited budget.
To form a contrast with the iron structure of the old tower.
items.explanation:
It will be made of timber as an ecological symbol of
第 3 段說用木材蓋塔，是作為生態的象徵（an ecological symbol），選項換成 symbol of environmental concerns，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 iron，第 2 段拿舊鐵塔比的是高度，原文沒有說要和鑄鐵形成對比；(B) 減輕重量、(C) 預算有限，原文都沒有提到。

閱讀測驗.title: 寫作目的與文章類型（Purposes of Writing and Text Types）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Authors write for many reasons. Often they write about real or make-believe people, places, or events that may be funny, sad, or scary. Sometimes authors write about these things to entertain readers. Authors also write about these things to inform by giving facts or ideas.

The following two paragraphs are examples of these two kinds.

(1) When he finished with unpacking, Nelson carried all the empty boxes down the hallway. On his way to the dump, the bell rang. He needed to hurry. He had no time to go to the dump. Then, he stopped at Adam Joshua’s office, which happened to be unlocked, and walked away joyfully. Later in the afternoon, Nelson came to Adam’s office with Peter for their biology project. The empty boxes and many other things fell all over them the minute he opened the door. “Adam Joshua!” yelled Nelson, pushing away a basketball and shaking a toy frog off his foot. “This is no way to treat a friend!”

(2) Where the land meets the sea we find seashells. There are many different kinds of shells. They can be round like the moon, long like a jackknife, or shaped like boxes, fans, or tops. The shells we find are usually empty, but once there were soft bodies inside. Animals with hard shells outside and soft bodies inside are called mollusks.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
作者寫作的理由很多。他們常寫真實或虛構的人物、地方或事件，內容可能有趣、悲傷或可怕。有時候，作者寫這些東西是為了娛樂讀者；作者寫這些東西，也可能是為了提供事實或想法，讓讀者獲得資訊。

下面兩段分別是這兩類文章的例子。

(1) Nelson 拆完行李以後，把所有空箱子搬到走廊上。在他要把箱子拿去垃圾場的路上，鈴聲響了，他得趕快。他沒時間去垃圾場了，就在 Adam Joshua 的辦公室停了下來（那間辦公室剛好沒鎖），然後開開心心地走了。那天下午稍晚，Nelson 和 Peter 一起到 Adam 的辦公室做生物科的專題。Nelson 一打開門，空箱子和許多其他東西就掉下來，砸在他們身上。「Adam Joshua！」Nelson 一邊推開一顆籃球、把一隻玩具青蛙從腳上甩掉，一邊大叫：「怎麼可以這樣對待朋友！」

(2) 在陸地和海洋交界的地方，我們可以找到貝殼。貝殼有很多不同的種類：有的圓得像月亮，有的長得像摺疊刀，有的形狀像盒子、扇子或陀螺。我們找到的貝殼通常是空的，不過裡面曾經有柔軟的身體。外面有硬殼、裡面是柔軟身體的動物，稱為軟體動物。

items.stem: What is the best title for this article?
items.explanation: 第 1 段說作者寫作的理由不只一種，可以是娛樂讀者，也可以是提供資訊；第 2 段說下面兩段是這兩類的例子。全文談的是寫作的不同目的，所以最好的標題是 (D)。(A) 只講第 3 段 Nelson 和 Adam 的故事，過於狹隘；(B) 只講第 4 段的貝殼，過於狹隘；(C) 文章談的是寫作的目的，不是哪些題材適合寫，偏離主題。

items.stem: Regarding the first example, which of the following is FALSE?
options: Nelson was not a responsible person.
Adam and Nelson are military officers.
Nelson left his empty boxes in Adam’s office.
Adam played a practical joke on Nelson.
items.explanation:
Later in the afternoon, Nelson came to Adam’s office with Peter for their biology project.
第 3 段說 Nelson 和 Peter 下午到 Adam 的辦公室做生物科的專題，看得出他們是一起做作業的學生；原文的 office 只是辦公室，沒有說他們是軍官，所以和原文不符的是 (B)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：Nelson 沒時間把空箱子拿去垃圾場，就丟在 Adam 的辦公室，是 (C)，這樣做也很不負責任，是 (A)；掉下來的除了空箱子，還有籃球和玩具青蛙，可見 Adam 故意把東西堆在門後捉弄 Nelson，是 (D)。

items.stem: Which of the following is TRUE according to the first example?
options: Nelson and Adam never liked each other.
Adam didn’t know what Nelson put into his office.
Peter complained to Nelson about the empty boxes.
Nelson was taught a lesson by Adam.
items.explanation:
The empty boxes and many other things fell all over them the minute he opened the door.
This is no way to treat a friend!
Nelson 把空箱子丟在 Adam 的辦公室，下午他一打開門，空箱子和許多其他東西就砸在他身上，他大叫「怎麼可以這樣對待朋友」。Adam 用同樣的方法回敬 Nelson，給了他一個教訓，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 Peter，Peter 只是和 Nelson 一起去做專題，大叫抱怨的是 Nelson；(A) Nelson 說 Adam 是朋友，看不出兩人一直合不來；(B) 東西又堆回門後砸下來，可見 Adam 知道 Nelson 放了什麼。

items.stem: According to the author, the second example is intended to
options: show us the beauty of seashells.
items.explanation:
Authors also write about these things to inform by giving facts or ideas.
The following two paragraphs are examples of these two kinds.
第 1 段說作者寫作，有時是為了娛樂讀者，有時是為了提供事實或想法（giving facts or ideas）；第 4 段的第二個例子介紹貝殼的種類、形狀和軟體動物，屬於提供資訊的一類，選項換成 present facts，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 shape，貝殼的形狀只是第 4 段提供的事實之一，不是整段的目的；(A) 這一段沒有發表對貝殼的看法；(C) 這一段也沒有讚美貝殼有多美。

閱讀測驗.title: 考艾島的自然風光與旅遊特色（Kauai Island's Natural Scenery and Tourism）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Kauai, the oldest of the main Hawaiian Islands, has some of the state’s most stunning scenery. Rivers and streams flow slowly through jungles of shaded greens.
