Amy and her mother carried only a few suitcases with them.
items.explanation:
They could take only what they could carry, and her two suitcases were already full.
題幹問的是原文明白寫出來的（explicitly mentioned）。第 2 段說她們只能帶自己拿得動的東西，Amy 的兩個行李箱已經裝滿了，選項換成只帶了幾個行李箱，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 carnations，原文只說要是爸爸在，會摘康乃馨送媽媽，沒有說花是爸爸種的；(C) 照抄 furniture，原文說 Amy 回想房間擺滿家具時的樣子，沒有說家具都賣掉了；(B) 原文只寫到 Laura 來道別，沒有說所有朋友都知道。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT true according to the passage?
options: Amy treasured the gold bracelet Laura gave her.
Amy turned and walked backwards as she left.
Amy’s father was not around when they were leaving.
Amy did not know if she could keep her promise to Laura.
items.explanation:
She watched as Laura walked down the block, turning and waving and walking backwards until she got to the corner.
第 1 段說 Amy 看著 Laura 沿著街道走去，一邊轉身揮手，一邊倒退著走。倒退著走的是 Laura，不是 Amy，所以和原文不符的是 (B)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：Amy 一看就愛上手鍊，出門前還確定手鍊牢牢戴好，是 (A)；第 3 段說要是爸爸在這裡，可見爸爸不在，是 (C)；第 1 段 Amy 答應會回來看 Laura，卻不知道還會不會回來，是 (D)。

閱讀測驗.title: 黃豆的價值與用途（The Value and Uses of Soybeans）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In the last several decades, the western world has been rediscovering the soybean, a plant whose use dates before recorded history in Asia. For thousands of years, the Chinese have valued highly the soybean, considering it one of the five important grains (along with rice, millet, barley, and wheat). Since it is cheap to produce and rich in protein, and has many uses, the soybean could provide food to the world’s growing population. Besides, soybeans can be fed to a variety of other animals ranging from livestock to silk worms.

The soybean is an almost perfect source of protein. If you are a vegetarian, or if your diet includes little meat, soy protein is a good alternative, and may even be essential to maintaining your health. The soybean’s high fiber content is beneficial in preventing digestive disorders. The soybean is free of cholesterol, and more importantly, the soy oil contains some special substances, called Omega 3 fatty acids, which reduce cholesterol and prevent blood from clotting in human body. Research shows that consuming a minimum of 25 grams of soy protein a day can lower blood cholesterol levels in people with high cholesterol problems.

In view of all these strengths, in the 1930s the United States and Canada undertook a research project in which they managed to breed an especially nutritious soybean with a high oil content. Since then, the United States has become the world’s largest producer of soybeans and has exported much of its soybean produce. In recent years, the soybean has been used in making many different foods and has become the atom of health food. Health-conscious Americans are adding tofu, the most popular soybean product, to salads and using it as a meat substitute. In the health food stores of major cities, it is now possible to buy tofu burgers and even tofu hot dogs.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
過去幾十年來，西方世界重新發現了黃豆。在亞洲，人們使用黃豆的歷史，比有文字記載的歷史還早。幾千年來，中國人一直很重視黃豆，把它列為五穀之一（另外四種是稻米、小米、大麥和小麥）。黃豆生產成本低、富含蛋白質，用途又多，可以為不斷增加的世界人口提供糧食。此外，從家畜到蠶，各種動物都可以拿黃豆當飼料。

黃豆幾乎是完美的蛋白質來源。如果你吃素，或是飲食裡很少有肉，黃豆蛋白是很好的替代品，甚至可能是維持健康不可缺少的。黃豆的纖維含量高，有助於預防消化方面的疾病。黃豆不含膽固醇；更重要的是，黃豆油含有一些特殊的物質，叫做 Omega 3 脂肪酸，可以降低膽固醇，防止血液在人體內凝結。研究顯示，膽固醇過高的人每天至少吃 25 公克黃豆蛋白，就能降低血液中的膽固醇。

有鑑於黃豆的這些優點，美國和加拿大在 1930 年代進行了一項研究計畫，成功培育出營養特別豐富、含油量高的黃豆品種。從那時起，美國成為世界上最大的黃豆生產國，並把大量黃豆產品出口。近年來，黃豆用來製作許多不同的食品，成了健康食品的代表。注重健康的美國人把黃豆最受歡迎的製品豆腐加進沙拉，也拿豆腐來代替肉。在各大城市的健康食品店裡，現在甚至買得到豆腐漢堡和豆腐熱狗。

items.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Asians have used soybean produce for thousands of years.
Health-conscious Americans are using more tofu in their diet.
The soybean provides food for the world’s growing population.
The soybean is healthful and has become popular in the western world.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說西方世界重新發現了黃豆；第 2 段說黃豆幾乎是完美的蛋白質來源，對健康有種種好處；第 3 段說美國培育出好品種，黃豆成了健康食品的代表。全文的重點是黃豆有益健康，在西方世界流行起來，所以是 (D)。(A) 亞洲人用了黃豆幾千年、(C) 黃豆能為世界人口提供糧食，都只是第 1 段的細節，過於狹隘；(B) 美國人吃更多豆腐，只是第 3 段的例子，也過於狹隘。

items.stem: One major advantage of the soybean as a food source is that ______.
items.explanation:
Since it is cheap to produce and rich in protein, and has many uses,
第 1 段說黃豆生產成本低（cheap to produce）、富含蛋白質、用途又多，所以是 (B)。另外三個選項都是對的東西放錯地方：(A) 照抄第 2 段的 free of，不含的是膽固醇，第 3 段還說美國培育出含油量高的品種；(C) 照抄 protein，原文說富含（rich in）蛋白質，選項卻說含量低；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 cholesterol，原文說黃豆不含膽固醇，還能降低膽固醇。

items.stem: The soybean helps to keep cholesterol down mainly because it contains ______.
items.explanation:
the soy oil contains some special substances, called Omega 3 fatty acids, which reduce cholesterol
第 2 段說黃豆油含有 Omega 3 脂肪酸（fatty acids），可以降低膽固醇（reduce cholesterol），所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 high fiber content，高纖維說的是預防消化方面的疾病，和膽固醇無關；(A) 照抄 protein，第 2 段最後一句雖然說每天吃 25 公克黃豆蛋白能降低膽固醇，但題幹問的是主要原因（mainly because），原文直接說明能降低膽固醇的成分是脂肪酸；(B) 維生素，原文沒有提到。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
options: Tofu is a rich protein source.
The United States exports most of its soybean produce to Canada.
Vegetarians should eat less than 25 grams of soy protein every day.
items.explanation:
The soybean is an almost perfect source of protein.
tofu, the most popular soybean product,
第 2 段說黃豆幾乎是完美的蛋白質來源；第 3 段說豆腐是最受歡迎的黃豆製品。把兩句合起來，豆腐是豐富的蛋白質來源，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 digestive，能預防消化疾病的是黃豆的纖維，不是蛋白質；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 Canada，加拿大是和美國一起做研究的國家，原文沒有說美國把黃豆出口到加拿大；(D) 照抄 25 grams，原文說的是膽固醇過高的人每天至少（a minimum of）吃 25 公克，不是吃素的人要少於 25 公克。

閱讀測驗.title: 出生順序與人格特質（Birth Order and Personality Traits）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Big brothers and sisters usually develop leadership tendencies early in life, mainly because of the responsibilities for younger children given to them by their parents. Firstborns, under normal circumstances, are usually the most strongly motivated toward achievement. This is mainly a result of parental expectations. Research also suggests that firstborn children generally become more conservative than other children because they receive most of the parental discipline. Used to caring for others, they are more likely to move toward such leadership professions as teaching and politics. Less social and flexible because they become accustomed in the very early years to acting alone, they may have difficulty making close friends.

By contrast, later children are more likely to be more relaxed and sociable because their parents are more relaxed. However, later children are often less ambitious and may be uncomfortable making decisions for others. This may help explain why younger children tend to favor the creative fields such as music, art, and writing. Later children may make good salespersons because persuasion may have been the only tool they had to deal with older siblings. Younger children tend to remain forever “the baby,” enjoyable to be around, but at times overdependent on others.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
哥哥姊姊通常很早就培養出領導的傾向，主要是因為父母把照顧弟妹的責任交給他們。在一般情況下，老大通常最有追求成就的動力，這主要是父母期望的結果。研究也指出，老大一般比其他孩子保守，因為父母的管教大多落在他們身上。老大習慣照顧別人，比較可能走向教書、從政這類需要領導能力的職業。他們從很小就習慣自己一個人做事，所以比較不善交際、也比較不知變通，可能不容易交到知心的朋友。

相對地，後來出生的孩子比較可能輕鬆隨和、善於交際，因為父母已經比較放鬆了。不過，後來出生的孩子往往企圖心比較小，替別人做決定的時候可能會不自在。這也許可以說明，為什麼年紀小的孩子傾向選擇音樂、藝術、寫作這類創作領域。後來出生的孩子可能是好的推銷員，因為面對哥哥姊姊時，說服也許是他們唯一的工具。年紀小的孩子往往永遠是家裡的「寶寶」，大家喜歡和他們相處，但他們有時太依賴別人。

items.stem: The passage is mainly about ______.
options: the personality tendencies of older children
the personality tendencies of younger children
the relation between birth rank and job success
the relation between birth rank and personality
items.explanation: 第 1 段寫哥哥姊姊的個性傾向，第 2 段用 By contrast 轉到後來出生的孩子，兩段對照出生順序和個性的關係，所以是 (D)。(A) 只講年紀大的孩子，是第 1 段的內容，過於狹隘；(B) 只講年紀小的孩子，是第 2 段的內容，也過於狹隘；(C) 文章雖然提到老大傾向教書、從政，後來出生的孩子可能是好的推銷員，但說的是個性適合哪些工作，沒有談工作成不成功，偏離主題。

items.stem: According to the passage, the first child tends to be ______.
items.explanation:
Research also suggests that firstborn children generally become more conservative than other children
第 1 段說研究指出老大一般比其他孩子保守（more conservative），所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 creative、(B) 照抄 sociable，第 2 段說傾向創作領域、善於交際的是後來出生的孩子，第 1 段反而說老大比較不善交際；(C) 第 2 段說說服是後來出生的孩子面對哥哥姊姊的工具，也不是老大的特質。

items.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that a younger child is more likely to be a good ______.
items.explanation:
This may help explain why younger children tend to favor the creative fields such as music, art, and writing.
第 2 段說年紀小的孩子傾向選擇音樂、藝術、寫作（writing）這類創作領域，從事寫作就是作家（writer），所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 teaching，傾向教書、從政的是習慣照顧別人的老大；(A) 圖書館員、(B) 醫生，原文都沒有提到。

items.stem: From the passage, we learn that ______.
options: children’s personalities depend entirely on parental attitudes
artists do not usually like to make decisions for other people
older children are used to taking care of people and are fun to be with
younger children are particularly weak in delivering a speech in public
items.explanation:
may be uncomfortable making decisions for others.
This may help explain why younger children tend to favor the creative fields such as music, art, and writing.
第 2 段說後來出生的孩子替別人做決定（making decisions for others）時可能會不自在，接著用 This may help explain why 說明，這也許就是他們傾向音樂、藝術、寫作這類創作領域的原因。也就是說，從事藝術的人通常不喜歡替別人做決定，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 parental，原文說父母的期望和管教有影響，選項卻說個性完全（entirely）取決於父母的態度，說得太過頭；(C) 習慣照顧別人的是老大，大家喜歡相處（enjoyable to be around）的卻是第 2 段年紀小的孩子，選項把兩者接在一起；(D) 當眾演講，原文沒有提到。

閱讀測驗.title: 醫療廢棄物與戴奧辛污染（Medical Waste and Dioxin Pollution）
閱讀測驗.passage:
According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), medical waste is a major source of dioxin pollution in the country. Linked to the dioxin issue is the use of PVC plastic, which is widely used in the production of blood bags, plastic tubing, and other products in hospitals and health clinics. Dioxin is an unwanted byproduct that is created when PVC is burned. Dioxin travels by air currents and settles onto grass, which is then eaten by cows and chickens in their feed. We eat polluted dairy products and meat and take the dioxin into our bodies, where it is stored in our fat for years and builds up over time. In this way, dioxin is globally distributed, and as a consequence, every member of the human population is constantly exposed to this poisonous substance. This poses special problems for childbearing women, who pass dioxin to an unborn baby or to a breastfeeding baby. In fact, the infant is the most vulnerable member of society to this chemical.

Plastics used to account for as little as 10% of medical waste in the late 1970s, before disposables began rapidly replacing reusables. They now make up as much as 30%. The EPA estimates that the average levels of dioxin in all Americans are so high that we can expect to see a variety of health effects, including cancer. Given the harm caused by the burning of medical waste, physicians and nurses have the responsibility to take a lead in reducing the use of plastics in the hospitals. After all, they can’t be treating cancer on the inside of hospitals and contributing to it on the outside.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
根據美國環境保護署（EPA），醫療廢棄物是美國戴奧辛汙染的主要來源。和戴奧辛問題有關的是 PVC 塑膠的使用；醫院和診所的血袋、塑膠管和其他產品，都大量使用 PVC 製造。戴奧辛是燃燒 PVC 時產生的有害副產品。戴奧辛隨著氣流移動，落在草地上，牛和雞再從飼料裡吃下這些草。我們吃下受汙染的乳製品和肉類，就把戴奧辛吃進體內，戴奧辛會儲存在我們的脂肪裡好幾年，隨著時間累積。就這樣，戴奧辛散布到全世界，結果每一個人都不斷接觸到這種有毒物質。這對懷孕生子的婦女尤其是個問題，因為她們會把戴奧辛傳給腹中的胎兒，或是吃母奶的嬰兒。事實上，在社會上所有人當中，嬰兒最容易受到這種化學物質傷害。

在 1970 年代末期，拋棄式用品開始迅速取代可重複使用的用品之前，塑膠只占醫療廢棄物的 10% 左右；現在則多達 30%。EPA 估計，所有美國人體內的戴奧辛平均含量都已經高到可以預期會出現各種健康問題，包括癌症。燃燒醫療廢棄物造成這麼大的傷害，醫師和護理師有責任帶頭減少醫院裡的塑膠用量。畢竟，他們不能一方面在醫院裡治療癌症，一方面又在醫院外助長癌症。

items.stem: What is the major message the author is trying to convey to readers?
options: All people, especially those working in the hospitals, should reduce the use of plastics.
Americans should lead the world to fight dioxin pollution, or mankind will die out soon.
We had better eat more vegetables than meat in order to reduce the risk of dioxin pollution.
We had better not breastfeed our babies, since babies are most likely to be poisoned by dioxin.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說醫院大量使用的 PVC 塑膠燃燒後產生戴奧辛，散布到全世界，每個人都不斷接觸到；第 2 段說醫療廢棄物裡的塑膠愈來愈多，最後呼籲醫師和護理師帶頭減少醫院裡的塑膠用量。作者要傳達的是大家，尤其是醫院裡的人，應該少用塑膠，所以是 (A)。三個錯誤選項都偏離主題：(B) 原文沒有要美國領導全世界，也沒有說人類快要滅亡；(C) 原文說的是戴奧辛透過飼料進入肉類和乳製品，沒有建議多吃蔬菜；(D) 第 1 段雖然說嬰兒最容易受害，卻沒有叫大家不要餵母奶。

items.stem: Dioxin is produced ______.
options: in the making of hospital blood bags
in the handling of all kinds of medical waste
items.explanation:
Dioxin is an unwanted byproduct that is created when PVC is burned.
第 1 段說戴奧辛是燃燒 PVC 時（when PVC is burned）產生的副產品，PVC 就是一種塑膠，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 blood bags，血袋是用 PVC 做的，製造血袋時不會產生戴奧辛，燒掉時才會；(D) 照抄 medical waste，醫療廢棄物是戴奧辛的主要來源，原因是裡面的塑膠拿去燒，不是處理任何醫療廢棄物都會產生；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 reusables，可重複使用的用品是作者希望恢復使用的，方向正好相反。

items.stem: What does it in the last line refer to?
items.explanation:
After all, they can’t be treating cancer on the inside of hospitals and contributing to it on the outside.
最後一句把醫院裡和醫院外對照：在醫院裡治療癌症（treating cancer on the inside），在醫院外又助長它（contributing to it on the outside）。治療和助長的是同一樣東西，it 指的就是前面的 cancer，所以是 (B)。另外三個選項都在第 2 段出現過，但醫院裡治療的是病，不是戴奧辛、醫療廢棄物或塑膠的使用；它們是在醫院外助長癌症的原因，填進 it 的位置，前後的對照就接不上。

items.stem: Which of the following statements can be inferred from the article?
options: Living in the countryside will keep one safe from dioxin poisoning.
Dioxin can be released from our bodies, if we drink a lot of clean, pure water.
Using reusables as people did in the old days will help lessen dioxin pollution.
You have to lose weight, or the amount of dioxin in your body fat will kill you.
items.explanation:
Plastics used to account for as little as 10% of medical waste in the late 1970s, before disposables began rapidly replacing reusables.
Dioxin is an unwanted byproduct that is created when PVC is burned.
第 2 段說 1970 年代末期拋棄式用品開始取代可重複使用的用品（reusables）之前，塑膠只占醫療廢棄物的 10% 左右，現在多達 30%；第 1 段說戴奧辛是燃燒 PVC 塑膠產生的。塑膠廢棄物變多，是因為改用拋棄式用品，像以前一樣用可重複使用的東西，就能減少戴奧辛汙染，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 fat，原文說戴奧辛儲存在脂肪裡，沒有說減重能解決問題；(A) 第 1 段說戴奧辛散布到全世界，每個人都不斷接觸到，住在鄉下也一樣；(B) 喝水能排出戴奧辛，原文沒有提到。

閱讀測驗.title: 電梯操作員的日常（A Day in the Life of an Elevator Operator）
閱讀測驗.passage:
I usually go to work by subway, and I get to work by 8:00 A.M. Before I start my job, I put on my uniform and look at myself in the mirror to make sure that I look neat. At 8:30 in the morning, I go on duty. I usually eat lunch from twelve to one and generally take a fifteen-minute break in the morning and in the afternoon. At 4:30 in the afternoon, I go off duty.

I enjoy my job very much. I meet all kinds of people and talk to everyone. Many people ask me questions, and I give them the necessary information. I try to be very helpful. I always call out floors very clearly, and I am constantly on the move. Most men take off their hats in my car, and sometimes I have to tell passengers to put out their cigarettes. Some people smile at me, but others just ignore me. In fact, my life can be described as consisting of a series of “ups” and “downs.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
我通常搭地鐵上班，早上 8 點以前到公司。開始工作以前，我會換上制服，照照鏡子，確定自己看起來整整齊齊。早上 8 點半，我開始值班。我通常 12 點到 1 點吃午餐，上午和下午一般各休息 15 分鐘。下午 4 點半，我下班。

我非常喜歡我的工作。我會遇到各式各樣的人，和每個人說話。很多人問我問題，我就提供他們需要的資訊。我盡量幫上忙。我總是把樓層報得很清楚，而且一直在移動。大部分男士進了我的車廂會脫帽，有時候我得請乘客把菸熄掉。有些人對我微笑，有些人卻理都不理我。事實上，我的生活可以說是由一連串的「上上下下」組成的（ups and downs 也指人生的起起落落）。

items.stem: The passage is written mainly to describe ______.
options: what a typical day is like for the author
what kinds of people the author works with
items.explanation: 第 1 段依時間順序寫作者一天的作息：幾點到公司、換制服、值班、吃午餐、休息、下班；第 2 段寫上班時做些什麼、遇到哪些人。全文描述的是作者典型的一天，所以是 (C)。(A) 照鏡子確定自己看起來整齊，只是第 1 段的細節，過於狹隘；(B)「上上下下」的生活只在第 2 段最後一句出現，也過於狹隘；(D) 各式各樣的乘客只是第 2 段的內容，也過於狹隘。

items.stem: We may infer from the passage that the author is a(n) ______.
items.explanation:
I always call out floors very clearly
Most men take off their hats in my car,
my life can be described as consisting of a series of “ups” and “downs.”
第 2 段有三個線索：作者總是把樓層報得很清楚（call out floors）、男士進了他的車廂（car）會脫帽、他的生活是一連串的「上上下下」。報樓層、有車廂、整天上上下下，作者是電梯操作員，所以是 (D)。這裡的 car 指電梯車廂，不是汽車，所以不是 (B) 司機。(C) 照抄 floor，floor cleaner 是清潔地板的人，原文的 floors 是樓層；(A) 警察，原文沒有線索。

items.stem: The expression “constantly on the move” in the passage refers to the fact that ______.
options: the author always calls out floors very clearly
the author seldom stays in one place for a long while
the author meets all kinds of people and talks to everyone
the author frequently helps passengers move their baggage
items.explanation:
I always call out floors very clearly, and I am constantly on the move.
on the move 是一直在移動。電梯操作員整天跟著電梯上上下下，很少在一個地方停留很久，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄同一句前半的 floors very clearly，那是 and 前面的另一件事；(C) 照抄 all kinds of people，那是他喜歡這份工作的原因；(D) 照抄 move，move their baggage 是搬行李，原文沒有說作者幫乘客搬東西。

閱讀測驗.title: 魔術的歷史演變（The History of Magic）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Magic is believed to have begun with the Egyptians, in 1700 BC. A magician named Dedi of Dedsnefu was reported to have performed for the pharaoh, or the king. He was also known to have entertained the slaves who built the pyramids. The “Cups and Balls” trick which he was particularly good at is still performed by magicians all over the world today.

The ancient Greeks and Romans were also fascinated by the idea of magic. Actually, one of their main interests was the art of deception. This explains why at that time the priests even built magic devices into their temples. These devices made it possible for doors to open by themselves and wine to flow magically out of statues’ mouths. This was done mainly to convince people that the priests were powerful.

Magic, however, was not well accepted before the 1800s. Magicians were thought of as freaks and were only allowed to perform in a circus. It was in the 19th century that the magician Robert Houdin came along and changed people’s views and attitudes about magic. It was also because of Robert Houdin that many magicians were able to add Dr. or MD to their names. Today magicians try hard to find new ways to show their practiced skills. Magic is now entertainment for families all over the world.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
一般認為，魔術起源於西元前 1700 年的埃及人。據說有一位叫做 Dedi of Dedsnefu 的魔術師，曾經為法老，也就是國王表演。大家也知道他曾經表演給建造金字塔的奴隸看。他特別擅長的「杯與球」戲法，今天世界各地的魔術師都還在表演。

古希臘人和羅馬人也對魔術很著迷。事實上，他們主要的興趣之一，就是障眼法的技巧。這說明了為什麼當時的祭司甚至在神殿裡裝了魔法機關。這些機關能讓門自己打開，讓酒神奇地從雕像的嘴裡流出來。這麼做主要是要讓人們相信祭司的法力強大。

然而，在 1800 年代以前，魔術並不受到大家接受。魔術師給人看成怪胎，只准在馬戲團表演。直到 19 世紀，魔術師 Robert Houdin 出現，才改變了大家對魔術的看法和態度。也因為 Robert Houdin，許多魔術師才能在名字加上 Dr. 或 MD 的頭銜。今天的魔術師努力尋找新的方式，展現苦練出來的技巧。魔術現在是全世界家庭的娛樂。

items.stem: What is the best title for the passage?
items.explanation: 第 1 段從西元前 1700 年的埃及說起，第 2 段寫古希臘和羅馬，第 3 段寫 1800 年代以前、19 世紀到今天。全文依時間順序介紹魔術的發展，所以是 (D)。(A) 戲法只是第 1、2 段舉的例子，過於狹隘；(B) 偉大的魔術師只講到第 3 段的 Robert Houdin，也過於狹隘；(C) 魔術成為娛樂只是第 3 段最後一句，也過於狹隘。

items.stem: In ancient Greece, what did the priests do to show people they had unusual power?
options: They performed magical tricks to entertain people.
They made the statues in the temples drink wine as they wished.
They treated the people with wine flowing down from statues’ mouths.
They built magic devices in the temples to make doors open by themselves.
items.explanation:
This explains why at that time the priests even built magic devices into their temples.
These devices made it possible for doors to open by themselves
This was done mainly to convince people that the priests were powerful.
第 2 段說祭司在神殿裡裝了魔法機關，能讓門自己打開（open by themselves），這麼做主要是要讓人們相信祭司的法力強大，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 entertain，表演給人看的是埃及的魔術師 Dedi，不是希臘的祭司；(C) 照抄 statues’ mouths，原文說酒從雕像嘴裡流出來，是用來顯示法力，不是請人喝酒；(B) 照抄 statues，原文是酒從雕像裡流出來，不是讓雕像喝酒，方向弄反了。

items.stem: What did people think of magic before 1800?
options: Magic should be used only in temples.
Magic could only be performed in a circus.
Magic was performed by freaks and doctors.
Magic was the major daily activity for the pharaohs.
items.explanation:
Magicians were thought of as freaks and were only allowed to perform in a circus.
第 3 段說 1800 年代以前，魔術師只准在馬戲團表演（only allowed to perform in a circus），所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 freaks，同一句說魔術師給人看成怪胎，但魔術師能加上 Dr. 或 MD 的頭銜，是 19 世紀 Robert Houdin 出現以後的事；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 temples，在神殿裡裝機關是古希臘、羅馬祭司的做法，不是只能在神殿用；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 pharaoh，原文只說 Dedi 曾為法老表演。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true?
options: Dedi of Dedsnefu performed magic for kings only.
Robert Houdin was the first magician to perform magic.
The “Cups and Balls” trick has been performed for about 1,700 years.
items.explanation:
Magic is believed to have begun with the Egyptians, in 1700 BC.
第 1 段說魔術起源於西元前 1700 年。從西元前 1700 年到這份考卷的年代，大約是 1700＋2000＝3,700 年，所以是 (A)。(D) 把西元前 1700 年當成 1,700 年前，「杯與球」是 Dedi 擅長的戲法，也有大約 3,700 年了；(B) 照抄 king，原文說 Dedi 也表演給建造金字塔的奴隸看，不是只為國王表演；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 Robert Houdin，他是改變大家看法的魔術師，最早的魔術師是第 1 段的 Dedi。

閱讀測驗.title: 醫學的三個分支（Three Branches of Medicine）
閱讀測驗.passage:
There are three branches of medicine. One is called “doctor medicine,” or “scientific medicine.” Scientific doctors try to observe sicknesses, look for logical patterns, and then find out how the human body works. From there they figure out what treatments may work. This kind of medicine is believed to date from the 4th century BC. Although nowadays it is successful, in the ancient world this approach probably did not cure many patients.

A second kind of medicine is called “natural cures,” or “folk medicine,” in which less educated people try to cure sicknesses with various herbs. These folk healers also use observation and logic, but they are not so aware of it. They try things until they find something that seems to work, and then they keep doing that. Folk medicine flourished long before the development of scientific medicine and was more successful in ancient times than doctor medicine.

The third kind is called “health spas,” or “faith healing.” Sometimes this may be as simple as touching the holy man and being immediately healed. Other times, a magician may make you a magic charm, or say a spell, to cure you. Some religious groups organize special healing shrines for the sick. In these places people rest, get plenty of sleep, eat healthy food, drink water instead of wine, and exercise in various ways. They also talk to the priests and pray to the gods. If you are feeling depressed or you have been working too hard, going to these places may be just the right thing to make you feel better.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
醫學有三個分支。第一種叫做「醫生醫學」，也就是「科學醫學」。科學派的醫生觀察疾病，尋找合乎邏輯的規律，然後找出人體怎麼運作，再從這些推敲出哪些療法可能有效。一般認為，這種醫學始於西元前 4 世紀。這種醫學雖然今天很成功，在古代這種方法可能治好的病人並不多。

第二種醫學叫做「自然療法」，或是「民俗醫學」，由教育程度比較低的人用各種草藥治病。這些民俗療者也運用觀察和邏輯，只是自己沒有那麼清楚意識到。他們不斷嘗試，直到找到似乎有效的東西，然後就一直這麼做。民俗醫學在科學醫學發展之前很久就已經很興盛，在古代也比醫生醫學更成功。

第三種叫做「健康療養所」，或是「信仰治療」。有時候，這可能簡單到摸一下聖人就立刻痊癒。有時候則是由魔法師替你做一個護身符，或是唸一段咒語來治好你。有些宗教團體為病人設立特別的療養聖所。人們在這些地方休息、睡飽、吃健康的食物、喝水不喝酒，還做各種運動。他們也和祭司談話，向神明祈禱。如果你心情低落，或是工作過度，去這種地方也許正是讓你好起來的方法。

items.stem: Doctor medicine ______.
options: has a longer history than folk medicine
has been practiced for around 1,600 years
bases its treatments on observation and logic
was very successful in curing sicknesses in ancient times
items.explanation:
Scientific doctors try to observe sicknesses, look for logical patterns, and then find out how the human body works.
第 1 段說科學派的醫生觀察（observe）疾病、尋找合乎邏輯（logical）的規律，再推敲出哪些療法可能有效，選項換成名詞 observation and logic，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 successful，原文說這種醫學今天很成功，在古代治好的病人卻不多；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 folk medicine，原文說民俗醫學在科學醫學之前很久就很興盛，歷史比較長的是民俗醫學；(B) 原文說始於西元前 4 世紀，到今天大約 2,300 多年，不是 1,600 年。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT used in health spas?
items.explanation:
Other times, a magician may make you a magic charm, or say a spell, to cure you.
Some religious groups organize special healing shrines for the sick.
In these places people rest, get plenty of sleep, eat healthy food, drink water instead of wine, and exercise in various ways.
第 3 段介紹健康療養所：魔法師做護身符、唸咒語，是 (A) 魔法；宗教團體設立療養聖所、向神明祈禱，是 (C) 宗教信仰；在那裡休息、睡飽、吃健康的食物、運動，是 (D) 健康的生活方式。各種草藥是第 2 段民俗醫學用的方法，不屬於健康療養所，所以選 (B)。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
options: Folk healers choose different herbs to cure diseases without any sound basis.
People who practice folk medicine need lots of formal education on herbs.
The success of folk medicine led to the development of doctor medicine.
Natural cures worked better than scientific medicine in ancient times.
items.explanation:
was more successful in ancient times than doctor medicine.
第 2 段說民俗醫學在古代比醫生醫學更成功（more successful），自然療法就是民俗醫學，醫生醫學就是科學醫學，選項換成 worked better，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 herbs，原文說民俗療者也運用觀察和邏輯，試到有效才一直用，不是毫無根據；(C) 照抄 development，原文只說民俗醫學在科學醫學發展之前就很興盛，沒有說前者促成了後者；(B) 原文說用草藥治病的是教育程度比較低的人，正好相反。

items.stem: The author’s primary purpose in this passage is to ______.
options: argue for the importance of medicine in health care
show the crucial role religion plays in medical treatments
compare the educational background of three different types of patients
items.explanation: 第 1 段開頭說醫學有三個分支，接著第 1、2、3 段依序介紹醫生醫學、民俗醫學和信仰治療。作者寫這篇文章是要說明不同種類的醫學，所以是 (A)。(C) 宗教只出現在第 3 段的信仰治療，過於狹隘；(B) 文章只是說明，沒有主張醫學在保健上有多重要，偏離主題；(D) 文章比較的是三種醫學，提到教育程度的是第 2 段的民俗療者，不是病人，也偏離主題。

閱讀測驗.title: 青少年消費市場與時尚影響力（Teen Consumer Market and Fashion Influence）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Today's teen consumer market is the most profitable it has ever been. Even though 65% of teens claim that they rely on themselves for their fashion ideas, it is estimated that less than 20% of the teen population is innovative enough to drive fashion trends, according to a recent study by a marketing firm. Marketers recognize this fact and often use elements of youth culture to promote their products. Perhaps one of the best examples is their use of hip-hop culture. It is reported that hip-hop fashion alone generates $750 million to $1 billion annually. Sales of rap music and videos each exceed that amount.

Rap's rise and sustained global popularity is a good illustration of how influential youth culture is on youth attitudes and behavior. Remember when Madonna hit the charts with her bra in full view while singing about "virginity"? Soon after that, adolescent girls around the world began wearing their underwear outside their clothes.

Fashion designer Tommy Hilfiger was fully aware of the power of youth culture. He marketed his brand by giving clothes to famous MTV stars and featuring teen stars in his print ads. Picking up on teens' interest in computer games, Hilfiger sponsored a Nintendo competition and installed Nintendo terminals in his stores. The payoff? Teens rated Hilfiger jeans as their number one brand in a survey in 2000.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
今天的青少年消費市場是有史以來獲利最高的。根據一家行銷公司最近的研究，雖然 65% 的青少年聲稱自己的時尚點子是靠自己想的，但據估計，青少年當中只有不到 20% 有足夠的創意，能夠帶動時尚潮流。行銷人員知道這一點，常常利用青少年文化的元素來推銷產品。最好的例子之一，也許就是他們運用嘻哈文化。據報導，光是嘻哈服飾每年就創造 7.5 億到 10 億美元的營收。饒舌音樂和音樂錄影帶的銷售額，各自都超過這個數字。

饒舌音樂興起，並在全球持續流行，正好說明了青少年文化對青少年的態度和行為影響有多大。還記得瑪丹娜一邊唱著和「處女」有關的歌，一邊大方露出胸罩登上排行榜的時候嗎？不久之後，世界各地的少女開始把內衣穿在衣服外面。

時裝設計師 Tommy Hilfiger 非常清楚青少年文化的力量。他送衣服給有名的 MTV 明星，在平面廣告裡請青少年明星入鏡，用這些方式推銷他的品牌。Hilfiger 看準青少年喜歡電玩，贊助了一場任天堂比賽，還在店裡裝了任天堂的遊戲機。成果呢？在 2000 年的一項調查中，青少年把 Hilfiger 牛仔褲評為第一名的品牌。

items.stem: What is the best title for this passage?
items.explanation: 第 1 段說行銷人員利用青少年文化推銷產品，第 2 段說饒舌音樂和瑪丹娜的例子，正好說明青少年文化影響力多大，第 3 段說 Tommy Hilfiger 非常清楚青少年文化的力量。三段都在講青少年文化的影響力，所以是 (B)。(C) 嘻哈服飾只是第 1 段的例子，過於狹隘；(D) Tommy Hilfiger 的成功只是第 3 段的例子，也過於狹隘；(A) 行銷的重要性，範圍比文章大得多，太過廣泛。

items.stem: How much money do sales of rap music and videos together make each year?
items.explanation:
It is reported that hip-hop fashion alone generates $750 million to $1 billion annually.
Sales of rap music and videos each exceed that amount.
這一題要分清楚兩句話各在說什麼。第 1 段說光是嘻哈服飾（hip-hop fashion alone）每年就有 7.5 億到 10 億美元；下一句說饒舌音樂和音樂錄影帶的銷售額各自（each）都超過這個數字（that amount）。題目問的是饒舌音樂和音樂錄影帶加起來（together）的金額：兩樣各自超過 7.5 億，加起來至少超過 15 億，一定超過 10 億美元，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 $750 million to $1 billion，那是嘻哈服飾的營收，不是音樂和錄影帶的。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
options: The purchasing power of teenagers has been decreasing over the years.
Many teenagers make a lot of profits in the fashion market today.
Madonna led the fashion of wearing underwear outside clothes.
Marketers recognize youth culture as a part of hip-hop culture.
items.explanation:
Soon after that, adolescent girls around the world began wearing their underwear outside their clothes.
第 2 段說瑪丹娜露出胸罩登上排行榜，不久之後（Soon after that）世界各地的少女開始把內衣穿在衣服外面，可見這股風潮是瑪丹娜帶起來的，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 hip-hop culture，原文說嘻哈文化是青少年文化的一個例子，選項卻反過來說青少年文化是嘻哈文化的一部分；(B) 照抄 profit，原文說獲利最高的是青少年消費市場，賺錢的是做生意的人，不是青少年；(A) 原文說青少年市場是有史以來獲利最高的，購買力並沒有下降。

items.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that Hilfiger ______.
options: believed that MTV stars could drive fashion trends among teens
sold Nintendo terminals together with teens’ clothes in his stores
sponsored a Nintendo competition out of his own interest in computer games
was rated by teens and adults as the best designer of jeans around the world in 2000
items.explanation:
Fashion designer Tommy Hilfiger was fully aware of the power of youth culture.
He marketed his brand by giving clothes to famous MTV stars and featuring teen stars in his print ads.
第 3 段說 Hilfiger 非常清楚青少年文化的力量，所以送衣服給有名的 MTV 明星，請青少年明星拍廣告。他這樣做，可見他相信 MTV 明星能帶動青少年的時尚潮流，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 computer games，喜歡電玩的是青少年，不是 Hilfiger 自己；(B) 照抄 Nintendo terminals，遊戲機是裝在店裡吸引青少年的，原文沒有說拿來賣；(D) 照抄 2000，2000 年的調查是青少年把 Hilfiger 牛仔褲評為第一名的品牌，評分的只有青少年，也不是全世界最好的設計師。

閱讀測驗.title: 曼谷：一個充滿活力的城市（Bangkok: A Vibrant City）
閱讀測驗.passage: There is a lot to see and do in Bangkok if you can tolerate the traffic, noise, heat (in the hot season), floods (in the rainy season), and somewhat polluted air. The city is incredibly urbanized, but beneath its modern appearance lies an unmistakable Thai-ness. To say that Bangkok is not Thailand, as has been claimed by some, is like saying that New York is not America, Paris is not France, or London is not England. Bangkok caters to diverse interests: there are temples, museums and other historic sites for those interested in traditional Thai culture; an endless variety of good restaurants, clubs, international cultural and social events, as well as movies in several different languages and a modern art institute for those seeking contemporary Krung Thep, the Thai name for Bangkok. As William Warren, an American author now living in Thailand, has said, “The gift Bangkok offers me is the assurance I will never be bored.”

items.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: The city of Bangkok is urbanized but it is also rich in traditional Thai culture.
Visitors to Bangkok might find the weather, the heat, and floods unbearable.
Bangkok is an international city, just like Paris, London, and New York.
There are a variety of restaurants and social events in Bangkok.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as one of the problems that visitors might find in Bangkok?
What can we infer from William Warren’s comment on Bangkok at the end of the passage?
options: Bangkok is a place where visitors can buy many souvenirs.
Bangkok offers attractive travel insurance to visitors.
Bangkok is an exciting place to visit.

閱讀測驗.title: 麥可·傑克森的育兒爭議（Michael Jackson's Parenting Controversy）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Michael Jackson provoked new concerns for his children’s welfare after he took them to the zoo covered in strange, bright-colored veils “to protect them from kidnappers.”

The pop star was pictured walking through Berlin Zoo with his two elder children, Prince Michael, five, and Paris, four.

Both youngsters had their faces completely covered in outlandish see-through burgundy-colored veils—a choice of dress which Jackson’s aides said was designed to disguise the youngsters to protect them from being kidnapped. But as they wandered through the zoo with their famous father, it seemed an unlikely explanation.

The rare appearance came just 24 hours after the singer provoked outrage by dangling his youngest child, baby Prince Michael II, from the fourth-floor balcony of a hotel window.

The nine-month-old boy’s face was covered with a white cloth, which was again said to be a precautionary measure taken by the star to protect his children from becoming kidnappers’ targets.

As people across the world criticized Jackson as an unfit father, child protection groups called on German police to take action against the pop legend. However, Berlin prosecutors said they were not investigating the incident, and an inquiry could only be opened if a complaint was filed against Jackson.

items.stem: This passage is most likely taken from a ______.
What did Michael Jackson do at Berlin Zoo that caught people’s attention?
options: He was involved in the kidnapping of two children named Prince and Paris.
He covered his children in veils to prevent them from being kidnapped.
He tried to protect his children from kidnappers by hiding them in the zoo.
He wandered through the zoo with his face covered in a strange cloth.

items.stem: What does “precautionary measure” mean in the passage?
options: A calculation done with great precision.
A plan carefully designed to achieve a goal.
A step taken to avoid some bad consequences.
A mathematical problem prepared with extreme care.

items.stem: According to the passage, German police could take action against Michael Jackson only when ______.
options: more veils were used to cover the youngsters
an official complaint was made against him
child protection groups called the police again

閱讀測驗.title: 航空安全措施：行李比對爭議（Airline Security Measures: Bag-Matching Controversy）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Since the terrorist attack on America on September 11, hundreds of new security measures have been put in place to make Americans safer, or at least feel safer. Hotels and corporate offices now require guests to present a photo ID at check-ins and entrances. Airlines refuse to let passengers carry razor blades, scissors, or screwdrivers on flights.

At least one surefire way exists to improve security and protect personal privacy: positive passenger bag-matching. It would require that no checked bag be transported on a plane if its owner doesn't board the flight. Bag-matching became standard practice in Europe and Asia in the 1980s after suitcase bombs brought down Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Air India Flight 182 en route to London, and UTA Flight 772 to Paris. In all three cases, the terrorists weren't on board.

Yet, in the U.S., where security is now top priority, authorities have chosen to ignore bag-matching. Instead, the Transportation Safety Administration (TSA) has embraced largely untested electronic-detection systems that screen bags for bombs and other explosives. Critics charge that the TSA has overlooked such an obvious, sensible security measure because U.S. airlines have opposed bag-matching for years. They fear it might delay flights and persuade short-haul travelers to take a train or drive instead.

After September 11, bag-matching was back on the agenda. Yet, struggling airlines complained that implementing it on all domestic flights would drive them into bankruptcy. Such claims have zero merit, says Arnold Barnett, a former chair of the Federal Aviation Administration's technical team. In 1996, the team was asked to investigate the feasibility of bag-matching. In a 1997 experiment, which tested 11 airlines, 50 pairs of cities, 8,000 flights, and 750,000 passengers, Barnett showed that domestic bag-matching would cause delays averaging seven minutes on only one in seven flights and would require no reduction in flight schedules.

Barnett argues that bag-matching would deter bombers far more than electronic-detection systems. It ensures that the terrorist will proceed to the gate to board his plane. If, while he's waiting, detection devices reveal a bomb, he could be quickly located and arrested. “The combination of bag-matching and explosives detection could be far more potent than either measure on its own,” Barnett wrote in a Dec. 17 letter to TSA chief. He received a thank-you note that contained no indication that the TSA is contemplating action.

items.stem: According to the passage, Pan Am Flight 103, Air India Flight 182, and UTA Flight 772 were similar in that ______.
options: they were brought down by terrorist attacks
they crashed because some terrorists were on board
they were the only international flights that crashed in 1980
they crashed because they didn’t follow airline security measures

items.stem: In which paragraph can the definition of bag-matching be found?
Which of the following is one of the reasons that airlines were unwilling to implement bag-matching on their flights?
options: Electronic-detection systems cost less than bag-matching.
Electronic-detection systems worked better in preventing hijacking.
Bag-matching would delay flights and discourage people from taking airplanes.
Bag-matching would invade passengers’ privacy rather than ensure their security.

items.stem: What is one important finding of Barnett’s experiment on bag-matching and flight schedules?
options: Bag-matching on domestic flights resulted in seven-minute delays in only one-seventh of the flights.
Bag-matching forced airlines to reduce their schedules and to sacrifice the quality of their service.
Bag-matching, when tested on 11 airlines, proved to be ineffective and inconvenient for passengers.
Bag-matching caused domestic flights to change their schedules and to reduce their frequency of service.

items.stem: The pronoun he (he could be…) in the last paragraph most likely refers to ______.
options: a security guard at the gate
an ordinary passenger boarding the plane

items.stem: What can we infer from the last sentence in the passage (He received a thank-you note that contained no indication that the TSA is contemplating action.)?
options: The TSA appreciated Barnett’s help and welcomed his suggestions.
The TSA took Barnett’s advice seriously and put it into practice.
The TSA invited Barnett to come to work with them.
The TSA did not plan to implement Barnett’s ideas.

items.stem: The passage was written mainly to ______.
options: point out the necessary trade-offs between privacy and security
highlight the TSA’s mission to improve airline security
argue for bag-matching as an effective security measure
advocate the use of electronic-detection systems

閱讀測驗.title: 雙胞胎心臟移植兄弟的故事（The Story of Twin Heart Transplant Brothers）
閱讀測驗.passage:
A sense of humor is just one of the many things shared by Alfred and Anthony Melillo, 64-year-old twin brothers from East Haven who made history in February 2002. On Christmas Eve, 1992, Anthony had a heart transplant from a 21-year-old donor. Two days before Valentine’s Day in 2002, Alfred received a 19-year-old heart, marking the first time on record that twin adults each received heart transplants.

“I’m 15 minutes older than him, but now I’m younger because of my heart and I’m not going to respect him,” Alfred said with a grin, pointing to his brother while talking to a roomful of reporters, who laughed frequently at their jokes.

While the twins knew that genetics might have played a role in their condition, they recognized that their eating habits might have also contributed to their heart problems. “We’d put half a pound of butter on a steak. I overdid it on all the food that tasted good, so I guess I deserved what I got for not dieting properly.”

The discussion moved to Anthony’s recovery. In the five years since his heart transplant, he had been on an exercise program where he regularly rode a bicycle for five miles, swam each day, and walked a couple of miles. He was still on medication, but not nearly as much as Alfred, who was just in the early stage of his recovery.

“Right now I feel pretty young and I’m doing very well,” Anthony said. “I feel like a new person.” Alfred said his goal, of course, was to feel even better than his brother. But, he added, “I love my brother very much. We’re very close and I’m sure we’ll do just fine.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
幽默感只是 Alfred 和 Anthony Melillo 這對兄弟許多共同點當中的一個。他們是來自 East Haven 的 64 歲雙胞胎，在 2002 年 2 月創造了歷史。1992 年的聖誕夜，Anthony 接受了心臟移植，心臟來自一位 21 歲的捐贈者。2002 年情人節的前兩天，Alfred 也移植了一顆 19 歲的心臟，這是有紀錄以來第一次成年的雙胞胎都接受心臟移植。

「我比他早出生 15 分鐘，可是現在因為我的心臟，我反而比較年輕了，所以我不打算再尊敬他了。」Alfred 對著擠滿一屋子的記者這麼說，一邊咧嘴笑，一邊指著他的兄弟。記者們聽了兩兄弟的玩笑，頻頻大笑。

兩兄弟知道遺傳可能是他們心臟出問題的原因之一，但也承認飲食習慣可能也有關係。「我們會在一塊牛排上抹半磅奶油。只要是好吃的東西，我都吃過了頭，所以我想，飲食沒有節制，落得這樣也是應該的。」

話題轉到 Anthony 的復原情形。心臟移植後的五年間，他一直照著運動計畫，固定騎腳踏車五英里、每天游泳，還走一、兩英里的路。他仍然在吃藥，不過藥量遠比 Alfred 少；Alfred 才剛進入復原的初期。

「現在我覺得自己相當年輕，狀況非常好，」Anthony 說，「我覺得自己像是換了一個人。」Alfred 說，他的目標當然是要覺得比他的兄弟更好。不過他也補充：「我非常愛我的兄弟。我們感情很好，我相信我們都會好好的。」

items.stem: This article is mainly about ______.
options: the danger of heart transplant surgery
becoming young by getting a new heart
the effect of genetics on the heart
the twin brothers who received heart transplants
items.explanation: 第 1 段介紹這對雙胞胎兄弟先後接受心臟移植，創下紀錄；第 2 段是 Alfred 拿新心臟開的玩笑；第 3 段說兩人心臟出問題的原因；第 4、5 段說兩人復原的情形和兄弟感情。全文寫的是這對接受心臟移植的雙胞胎兄弟，所以是 (D)。(B) 換了心臟變年輕，只是第 2 段 Alfred 開的玩笑，過於狹隘；(C) 遺傳對心臟的影響，只在第 3 段提到一句，也過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有談心臟移植手術的危險，偏離主題。

items.stem: What did Alfred and Anthony have in common?
items.explanation:
A sense of humor is just one of the many things shared by Alfred and Anthony Melillo
第 1 段第一句就說幽默感（sense of humor）是兩兄弟許多共同點（shared by）當中的一個，所以是 (C)；第 2 段 Alfred 對記者開玩笑、記者頻頻大笑，也是例證。(B) 照抄第 5 段的 goal，那是 Alfred 希望自己覺得比兄弟更好，不是職業目標；(D) 第 4 段說騎腳踏車的是 Anthony 的運動計畫，不是兩人的共同點；(A) 壽命，文章沒有提到。

items.stem: What did Alfred and Anthony think caused their heart problems?
items.explanation:
they recognized that their eating habits might have also contributed to their heart problems.
第 3 段說兩兄弟承認飲食習慣（eating habits）可能也是心臟出問題的原因，還說在牛排上抹半磅奶油、好吃的東西都吃過了頭，選項換成 Diet，所以是 (B)。同一句前面提到的遺傳（genetics）不在選項裡。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 exercise，運動是 Anthony 移植後復原的方法，不是心臟出問題的原因；(C) 手術、(D) 藥物，都是心臟出問題以後的事。

items.stem: Why did Alfred say, “I’m 15 minutes older than him, but now I’m younger because of my heart” ?
options: His heart transplant surgery was more successful than Anthony’s.
His recovery from the heart surgery was faster than Anthony’s.
His exercise program was better than Anthony’s.
His new heart was younger than Anthony’s.
items.explanation:
Anthony had a heart transplant from a 21-year-old donor.
Alfred received a 19-year-old heart
第 1 段說 Anthony 移植的心臟來自 21 歲的捐贈者，Alfred 移植的是 19 歲的心臟。Alfred 雖然早出生 15 分鐘，換上的心臟卻比 Anthony 的年輕兩歲，所以開玩笑說自己現在比較年輕，答案是 (D)。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 recovery，原文說 Alfred 才剛進入復原初期、吃的藥比 Anthony 多，正好相反；(C) 照抄 exercise program，那是 Anthony 的運動計畫；(A) 哪一次手術比較成功，文章沒有比較。

閱讀測驗.title: 博物館古物歸還爭議（Debate over Returning Ancient Artifacts to Museums）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In 1993, the Metropolitan Museum of Art reluctantly handed over 363 pieces of gold, silver, precious stones, paintings, and sculptures back to Turkey after a court case. Following increasing calls for the return of artistic objects that were removed decades or centuries ago, some of the world’s leading museums have signed a declaration that they will not hand back the ancient artifacts to their countries of origin. They say people all over the world have only been able to fully appreciate ancient civilizations because these museums have provided access to these artistic objects. The ancient civilizations would not be so deeply admired today if these ancient artifacts were not so widely available to an international public in major museums throughout Europe and America. For example, Egyptian culture would not have become so well-known if the museums had not put Egyptian mummies on show.

The British Museum has not signed the declaration, but says it fully supports it. Over the recent years, it has faced growing pressure to hand back the Elgin Marbles, sculptures taken from the Parthenon in Athens, Greece, in the 19th century. But the British Museum has said that the Museum is the best possible place for them. “They must remain here if the museum is to continue to achieve its aim, which is to show the world to the world,” said the director of the museum.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
1993 年，大都會藝術博物館在一場官司之後，不情願地把 363 件金器、銀器、寶石、畫作和雕塑歸還給土耳其。數十年或幾百年前從原地帶走的藝術品，要求歸還的呼聲愈來愈高；面對這樣的情勢，世界上一些頂尖的博物館簽署了一份聲明，表示不會把古代文物歸還給文物的原屬國。這些博物館說，全世界的人之所以能夠充分欣賞古代文明，只因為博物館讓大家看得到這些藝術品。要不是歐洲和美洲各大博物館把這些古代文物廣泛地展示給世界各地的大眾，這些古代文明今天不會這麼受人推崇。例如，要不是博物館展出埃及的木乃伊，埃及文化不會變得這麼有名。

大英博物館沒有簽署這份聲明，但表示完全支持。近年來，大英博物館面臨愈來愈大的壓力，要求歸還埃爾金石雕；這批雕塑是 19 世紀從希臘雅典的帕德嫩神殿拿走的。但是大英博物館表示，館方就是這批雕塑最好的歸宿。館長說：「博物館要繼續達成它的宗旨，也就是把世界展示給世界看，這批雕塑就必須留在這裡。」

items.stem: What reason do the major museums provide for not handing back the ancient objects?
options: Only in the leading museums can the objects be fully appreciated by the world.
It is better for those objects to remain at a certain place than to be moved around.
They need those well-known ancient objects to attract people from all over the world.
Ancient civilizations can only be admired if they are removed from their home countries.
items.explanation:
They say people all over the world have only been able to fully appreciate ancient civilizations because these museums have provided access to these artistic objects.
第 1 段說這些博物館的理由是：全世界的人能充分欣賞（fully appreciate）古代文明，只因為（only…because）博物館讓大家看得到這些藝術品。選項把 only 移到句首、改成倒裝句 Only in the leading museums can…，主詞也從人換成文物，句型變了，意思相同，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 admired，原文說的是文物在各大博物館展出，古代文明才這麼受推崇，沒有說非得離開原屬國才能受推崇；(C) 照抄 well-known，well-known 在原文是說埃及文化因此出名，不是博物館需要有名的文物來吸引人；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 remain，那是大英博物館館長說雕塑要留在館裡才能達成宗旨，不是說文物留在一處比搬來搬去好。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as one of the “countries of origin” in the article?
items.explanation:
handed over 363 pieces of gold, silver, precious stones, paintings, and sculptures back to Turkey
Egyptian culture would not have become so well-known if the museums had not put Egyptian mummies on show.
sculptures taken from the Parthenon in Athens, Greece, in the 19th century.
countries of origin 是文物原本所屬的國家。第 1 段大都會藝術博物館把文物歸還給 (A) 土耳其；埃及木乃伊來自 (C) 埃及；第 2 段埃爾金石雕是從 (D) 希臘雅典的帕德嫩神殿拿走的。英國只以大英博物館的身分出現，是收藏文物的一方，不是文物的原屬國，所以選 (B)。

items.stem: What does “the world” mean in “show the world to the world”?
items.explanation:
which is to show the world to the world,
They say people all over the world have only been able to fully appreciate ancient civilizations because these museums have provided access to these artistic objects.
show A to B 是把 A 展示給 B 看。第 1 段說博物館讓全世界的人（people all over the world）看得到這些藝術品，因而能欣賞古代文明。展示出來的第一個 the world，是各地的古代文明，所以是 (C)；展示的對象，也就是第二個 the world，才是全世界的人。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 international public，那是第二個 the world 的意思，把兩個 the world 弄反了；(B) 照抄 leading museums，博物館是做展示的一方；(A) 地球村，原文沒有提到。

閱讀測驗.title: 生物發光及其溝通應用（Bioluminescence and Its Communication Uses）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Some animals have organs in their bodies that produce light. When it is dark, they flash their lights on and off to signal to others of their species, to lure prey toward them, or to escape from predators.

Some fish are found to produce light in the blackness of the sea. When night falls over the Red Sea, tiny flashlight fish rise to the surface for food, each with a pair of “headlamps,” one beneath each eye. With the light produced by bacteria living there, they communicate with other flashlight fish to avoid getting too close to each other, so that the fish may spread out evenly to get enough food. And if a flashlight fish is threatened by a predator, it swims away in a zigzag path, flashing its light on and off very quickly to confuse the animal pursuing it.

Certain land animals can also produce light. Fireflies, small beetles that live in many warmer parts of the world, use light to attract a mate. After darkness falls in some parts of North America, female fireflies gather on the ground. The males fly overhead, flashing light from the undersides of their bodies. As there are a number of species of firefly, the males of each kind flash their own particular signal. Recognizing the flashing code of her own species, a female signals back to the male, and he lands beside her.

On land as in the sea, living lights can be deceiving. When they are hungry, some female fireflies lure the males of other species to them. They flash a false response when these males signal overhead, but eat them when they land.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
有些動物體內有會發光的器官。天黑的時候，牠們讓光一閃一閃，用來向同種的同伴傳遞訊號、引誘獵物靠近，或是逃離捕食者。

有些魚在漆黑的海裡會發光。夜幕籠罩紅海時，小小的燈眼魚游到海面上覓食，每一條都有一對「頭燈」，兩隻眼睛下方各一個。燈眼魚靠著住在那裡的細菌發出的光，和其他燈眼魚溝通，避免彼此靠得太近，這樣魚群才能平均散開，每一條都找得到足夠的食物。如果燈眼魚受到捕食者威脅，就會游出鋸齒狀的路線逃走，同時讓光快速地一明一滅，讓追趕牠的動物摸不著方向。

有些陸地上的動物也會發光。螢火蟲是一種小甲蟲，住在世界上許多比較溫暖的地方，牠們用光來吸引配偶。在北美洲的一些地方，天黑以後，雌螢火蟲聚集在地面上，雄螢火蟲在上空飛，從身體下方發出閃光。因為螢火蟲有好幾種，每一種的雄蟲都發出自己特有的訊號。雌蟲認出自己這一種的閃光密碼，就發出訊號回應雄蟲，雄蟲就降落在牠身旁。

在陸地上和在海裡一樣，生物發出的光也可能是騙局。有些雌螢火蟲餓了，會把其他種類的雄螢火蟲引誘過來。這些雄蟲在上空發出訊號時，牠們假裝回應，等雄蟲降落，就把牠們吃掉。

items.stem: Which of the following is the best title for the article?
options: Mating of Flashlight Fish and Fireflies.
Life on Land and in the Sea.
items.explanation: 第 1 段總說有些動物會發光，用光傳遞訊號、引誘獵物或逃離捕食者；第 2 段舉海裡的燈眼魚，第 3、4 段舉陸地上的螢火蟲，說明牠們怎麼用光和同伴、獵物、敵人溝通。全文講的是生物發光和動物之間的溝通，所以是 (C)。(A) 交配只出現在第 3 段螢火蟲的部分，燈眼魚發光不是為了交配，過於狹隘；(B) 黑暗與光、(D) 陸地和海裡的生物，範圍都比文章大得多，太過廣泛。

items.stem: Flashlight fish in the Red Sea give out light at night ______.
options: when they come out for food
as they try to look for their companions
because they want to get rid of the bacteria
so that they can get close to other flashlight fish
items.explanation:
tiny flashlight fish rise to the surface for food,
第 2 段說夜幕籠罩紅海時，燈眼魚游到海面上覓食（rise to the surface for food），選項換成 come out for food，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 close to，原文說燈眼魚用光溝通，是為了避免彼此靠得太近（too close to each other），方向正好相反；(C) 照抄 bacteria，光就是住在眼睛下方的細菌發出的，不是要擺脫細菌；(B) 原文說的是和同伴保持距離，不是尋找同伴。

items.stem: According to the passage, NEITHER flashlight fish NOR fireflies send out light to ______.
items.explanation:
use light to attract a mate.
some female fireflies lure the males of other species to them.
flashing its light on and off very quickly to confuse the animal pursuing it.
題目問燈眼魚和螢火蟲都不會為了什麼發光。第 3 段螢火蟲用光吸引配偶，是 (A)；第 4 段雌螢火蟲用假訊號引誘其他種類的雄蟲來吃，是 (B) 引誘獵物；第 2 段燈眼魚受到威脅時快速閃光，讓追趕的動物摸不著方向，是 (C) 逃離敵人。文章沒有提到用光找路回家，所以選 (D)。

a female signals back to the male,

閱讀測驗.title: 四本兒童/青少年讀物評論（Reviews of Four Children/YA Books）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Brooks, Bruce. Everywhere. HarperCollins, 1990. ISBN0060207299. 70 pages.

Peanuts’ beloved grandfather has suffered a heart attack. Peanuts is sad over the possibility of losing his grandfather. Dooley keeps Peanuts company while the adults in the family attend to Grandfather. Dooley attempts to save the old man by a ritual learned from comic books: killing a turtle and trading his soul for Grandfather’s. With the imaginative assistance of Dooley, Peanuts discovers the healing power of hope and love.

Babbitt, Natalie. Tuck Everlasting. Farrar, 1975. ISBN0374378487. 180 pages.

The Tuck family has discovered a spring whose water brings eternal life. A man learns their secret and threatens to sell the water to the highest bidder. Mrs. Tuck kills the man and is jailed and sentenced to be executed. Though the family knows she cannot be killed, they worry that their secret will be revealed when they try to kill her.

Baylor, Byrd. The Table Where Rich People Sit. Simon & Schuster, 1994. ISBN0684196530. 52 pages.

Around an old kitchen table, a young girl calls a family meeting to show her parents that they should earn more money so they can have nicer things. As she points out they are not sitting at a table where rich people would sit, her parents calculate the value of the desert hills, the blooming cactus, the calls of eagles, and one another’s company. Soon, she realizes that her poor family is rich in things that matter in life. She concludes that this is indeed a table where rich people sit.

Goble, Paul. Beyond the Ridge. Bradbury, 1989. ISBN0027365816. 32 pages.

There is no death; only a change of worlds—the author delivers these reassurances to readers in this book, based on the customs of the Plains Indians in America. The book reads like a prayer, expressing specific beliefs about dying. It describes a woman who is called by her long-dead mother to go “beyond the ridge.” After a steep climb, she discovers a world that is abundantly beautiful, and there she finds the familiar faces of people who have passed that way before her.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
Bruce Brooks 著，《Everywhere》，HarperCollins，1990 年出版，ISBN 0060207299，70 頁。

Peanuts 敬愛的祖父心臟病發作。Peanuts 想到可能會失去祖父，非常難過。家裡的大人忙著照顧祖父的時候，Dooley 陪著 Peanuts。Dooley 想用從漫畫書學來的儀式救老人家：殺一隻烏龜，用烏龜的靈魂換祖父的靈魂。在 Dooley 充滿想像力的幫忙下，Peanuts 發現了希望和愛的療癒力量。

Natalie Babbitt 著，《Tuck Everlasting》，Farrar，1975 年出版，ISBN 0374378487，180 頁。

Tuck 一家人發現了一處泉水，喝了這裡的水就能長生不死。有個男人知道了他們的祕密，揚言要把泉水賣給出價最高的人。Tuck 太太殺了那個男人，結果入獄，判了死刑。雖然一家人知道她死不了，卻擔心行刑的時候，他們的祕密會曝光。

Byrd Baylor 著，《The Table Where Rich People Sit》，Simon & Schuster，1994 年出版，ISBN 0684196530，52 頁。

一個小女孩圍著廚房裡的一張舊桌子召開家庭會議，要讓爸媽知道他們應該多賺點錢，才能擁有好一點的東西。她指出他們坐的不是有錢人會坐的桌子，爸媽就算給她聽：沙漠裡的山丘、盛開的仙人掌、老鷹的鳴叫，還有一家人彼此相伴，各值多少。不久，她明白了自己貧窮的家，其實在人生真正重要的東西上很富有。她最後的結論是：這張桌子的確是有錢人坐的桌子。

Paul Goble 著，《Beyond the Ridge》，Bradbury，1989 年出版，ISBN 0027365816，32 頁。

沒有死亡，只是換到另一個世界——作者在這本書裡，根據美洲平原印第安人的習俗，給讀者這樣的安慰。這本書讀起來像一篇禱詞，表達了對死亡的特定信念。書中描寫一個女人，她早已過世的母親呼喚她到「山脊的另一邊」。爬過一段陡坡之後，她發現了一個美麗非凡的世界，還在那裡見到比她早走這條路的人，一張張都是熟悉的面孔。

閱讀測驗.title: 電影對閱讀的影響：哈利波特現象（Film's Impact on Reading: The Harry Potter Phenomenon）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Six out of ten British children are likely to have seen a Harry Potter film and then read the first two books about the young wizard.

The finding comes from a survey by bookseller Waterstone’s into the impact on children’s reading of the Potter phenomenon, created by Edinburgh-based author J.K. Rowling.

Martin Higgs, Waterstone’s literary editor, said: “Thanks to the PG certification of the Harry Potter films, each release in the cinema is opening up a new generation of young children to the books.”

The two most successful books of the past 12 months for Waterstone’s have both had major film releases—Harry Potter and Lord of the Rings.

Waterstone’s experienced a 300 percent rise in sales of the Harry Potter series after the launch of the first film, Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone, and is expecting another surge of interest after the release this month of Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets.

An even greater rise in book sales was experienced as a result of the first film in the Lord of the Rings series and a repeat of interest in the Tolkien novels is expected next month when the next film in the series is released at cinemas.

Mr. Higgs added: “Parents are recognizing that films are a chance to persuade a reluctant reader to pick up a book and give it a try.”

items.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: Films based on popular books like Harry Potter and Lord of the Rings can sell very well.
Free Harry Potter books were given to British children who went to see the Harry Potter films.
Many British children became interested in reading the Harry Potter and Lord of the Rings books after seeing the films.
Six out of ten British children had already read the Harry Potter books before they saw the Harry Potter films.

a person who prepares books for printing
a writer of a children’s book about a young wizard
a teacher who encourages his students to read books

options: Books made into films are worth reading.

閱讀測驗.title: 台灣地震建築安全問題（Building Safety Issues in Taiwan Earthquakes）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Many buildings in Taiwan have survived earthquakes, but some appear to have fallen over like toys. This, say experts, is a sign that engineers did not pay enough attention to the foundations, or that the quake virtually turned the soft sediment below into a “liquid”—meaning the apartments should not have been constructed in these locations in the first place. According to Dr. David Petley, of the UK’s Portsmouth University, there are widespread occurrences in Taiwan where building codes are ignored and where development has occurred in locations where it should not have been allowed. Having worked on government-backed risk reduction projects in Taiwan since 1991, Dr. Petley further pointed out that there’s quite a lot of illegal construction work going on in Taiwan as a result of the very rapid development.

However, seismologists and engineers say that the government’s use of three building codes formulated to counter the threat of earthquakes may have spared the island from a death toll far higher than that now being revealed. For instance, Walter Mooney, of the US Geological Survey, conducted a research comparing Taiwan’s preparedness for earthquakes with that of Turkey, and found that Taiwan has been doing a good job: Whereas an estimated 65% of buildings in Turkey were illegally constructed, failing many safety tests, Taiwan has been largely successful in enforcing its own laws.

items.stem: This passage was written mainly to ______.
options: warn Taiwan residents about the danger of rapid urban development
propose solutions to the problems caused by earthquakes in Taiwan
discuss the safety problems of buildings in Taiwan during earthquakes
compare the death tolls in Turkey and Taiwan during recent earthquakes

items.stem: Which of the following is mentioned by Dr. Petley as one factor leading to the collapse of buildings when earthquakes strike Taiwan?
options: There is too much water underground.
There is a lack of qualified engineers.

Buildings have been constructed where they shouldn’t have been.

items.stem: The word seismologists in the second paragraph most likely means “experts on ______”.

閱讀測驗.title: 語言實驗室的發展與應用（Development and Application of Language Laboratories）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The best-known technological aid in language teaching is undoubtedly the language laboratory—a room, usually divided into booths, where students can listen individually to tape recordings of foreign language material, and where they may record and play back their own responses, while being monitored by a teacher.

When these laboratories were first introduced, they were heralded as a technique that would improve the rate and quality of language learning. They would take the burden of repetitive drills away from the teacher, provide more opportunities for learners to practice listening and speaking, and enable them to develop at their own rates and monitor their own progress. Many schools were quick to install expensive laboratory equipment. However, within a few years, it became apparent that there would be no breakthrough. The expected improvements did not materialize, and the popularity of the “language lab” showed a marked decline.

There were several reasons for the language lab’s failure to live up to expectations. The taped materials were often poorly designed, leading to student frustration and boredom. The published programs failed to reflect the kind of work the student was doing in class. Few modern languages staff had received training in materials design or laboratory use. And it proved difficult to maintain the equipment once it had been installed.

Today, the strengths and limitations of the laboratory are better realized, and the vastly increased potential of modern electronic hardware has led to a certain revival. There is now considerable interest in language learning laboratories, which contain much more than the traditional systems—in particular, the introduction of interactive computational aids and video materials has proved to be extremely popular.

It is now clear that, when used properly, laboratories can provide a valuable extra dimension to language teaching. For example, the taped material can provide a variety of authentic and well-recorded models for the training of listening comprehension. And laboratories can be used as resource centers, or libraries, giving learners extra opportunities to practice at their chosen level.

items.stem: The passage is mainly about ______.
options: the use of taped materials in a language laboratory
the development of language learning laboratories
the disadvantages of traditional language laboratories
the importance of well-trained staff in a language laboratory

items.stem: Which of the following can be regarded as one of the expected improvements in the second paragraph?

options: Materials used in the language laboratory bored students.
Well-trained staff for the language laboratory was hard to find.

The lessons in language laboratories and those in regular classrooms did not match.

閱讀測驗.title: 新型戶外活動：地理藏寶（New Outdoor Activity: Geocaching）
閱讀測驗.passage: These days, even a walk in the woods can be transformed into an “extreme” sport. Take “geocaching,” for example. Hikers looking for something a little different on their treks created a global hunting game, hiding “caches”—packs filled with goodies like CDs, photographs, and journals—in obscure places throughout the world. They then post the coordinates at www.geocaching.com, where other hikers can use them, along with a global positioning system (GPS), to join the worldwide goose chase. Geocaching works on an honor system: When a geocacher takes something, he leaves a cache of his own behind. Vacationers can get in on this trend at resorts like Utah’s Red Mountain Spa, where they can learn to use GPS and coordinates to find caches filled with spa products.

options: a new form of outdoor activity

one can learn to be a geocacher exclusively in Utah State

閱讀測驗.title: 智慧娃娃：辛蒂（Smart Doll: Cindy Smart）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Even though she’s just 5 years old, Cindy Smart speaks five languages. She’s a good reader. She can tell time and do simple math, including multiplication and division. She’s not a prodigy. She’s just good programming. Cindy looks like an average doll, with long, blond hair, baby-blue eyes, and a button nose. But loaded with some devices, Cindy is the first doll that can see, think, and do as she’s told.

The eagle-eyed Cindy follows in the path of other breakthrough toys like Sony’s barking Robot Aibo, which was the first to popularize voice command in the late 1990s. Cindy takes Aibo’s innovations one step beyond: she not only follows instructions but also recognizes shapes, colors, and words—and remembers. The effect is a doll that appears to be learning.

The toy company which produced Cindy Smart spent a decade trying to see how much human nature it could breathe into an inanimate object. Its engineers began researching basic and affordable artificial intelligence, creating minibots that sense light, sounds, and pressure. However, without the sense of sight, their toys seemed to be lacking one of the keenest abilities that life forms use to react to their environment.

So how do the engineers make a doll actually see? In Cindy’s case, it’s a multistep process. When presented a text like “I love you” and asked “Can you read this?” Cindy identifies it as one of 70 preprogrammed commands. Then the inbuilt digital camera scans a 15-degree radius in search of number- or letter-shaped objects. Buried in her belly, Cindy’s 16-bit microprocessor compares the text with her database of 700 words. If it’s a match, “I love you,” she utters.

閱讀測驗.title: 法蘭克·勞埃德·賴特與古根漢博物館（Frank Lloyd Wright and the Guggenheim Museum）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In June 1943, Frank Lloyd Wright received a letter from Hilla Rebay, the art adviser to Solomon R. Guggenheim, asking the architect to design a new building to house Guggenheim’s four-year-old museum of Non-Objective Painting. The project evolved into a complex struggle pitting the architect against his clients, city officials, the art world, and public opinions. Both Guggenheim and Wright would die before the building’s 1995 completion. The resultant achievement, the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, testifies not only to Wright’s architectural genius, but also to the adventurous spirit that characterized its founders.

Wright made no secret of his disenchantment with Guggenheim’s choice of New York for his museum: “I can think of several more desirable places in the world to build this great museum,” Wright wrote in 1949 to his partner, “but we will have to try New York.” To Wright, the city was overbuilt, overpopulated, and lacked architectural merit. Still, he proceeded with his client’s wishes, considering locations on 36th Street, 54th Street, and Park Avenue (all in Manhattan), as well as in the Riverdale section of the Bronx, before settling on the present site on Fifth Avenue between 88th and 89th Streets. Its nearness to Central Park was key. As close to nature as one gets in New York, the park offered relief from the noise and congestion of the city.

Wright’s design put his unique stamp on Modernist Architecture’s rigid geometry. The building is a symphony of triangles, ovals, arcs, circles, and squares. The delicate vision took decades to be fulfilled. Some people, especially artists, criticized Wright for creating a museum environment that might overpower the art inside. “On the contrary,” he wrote, “it was to make the building and the painting an uninterrupted, beautiful symphony such as never existed in the world of art before.”

In conquering the regularity of geometric design and combining it with the plasticity of nature, Wright produced a vibrant building whose architecture is as refreshing now as it was 40 years ago. The Guggenheim is arguably Wright’s most eloquent presentation and certainly the most important building of his late career.

options: There were already too many people and buildings in New York City.

There was strong objection from Solomon R. Guggenheim.

options: on the outskirts of New York City
in the Riverdale section of Bronx

options: The design of the museum is more powerful than the art works housed in it.
