閱讀測驗.title: 萬聖節糖果與牙齒健康（Halloween Candies and Dental Health）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Most American kids love Halloween treats, but a bucket of Halloween candy can be a dentist’s nightmare. Some parents try to get rid of half of the candy after their children go to bed, but dentists say parents also need to separate the good kinds of treats from the bad.

It is not exactly what a child eats that truly matters, but how much time it stays in his mouth. According to pediatric dentist Dr. Kaneta Lott, the most damaging stuff is something that is sticky or very hard and thus stays in the mouth for a long time. This is because we all have bacteria in our mouths. When we eat, the bacteria take our food as their food and produce an acid that destroys the surface of the teeth, causing cavities to form. The longer the food stays in the mouth, the more likely cavities will develop. Therefore, potato chips are worse than candy because they get stuck between teeth. For the same reason, raisins and crackers are not the best choice. Hard candies take a long time to consume and are also a bad choice for Halloween treats.

If children really love candy, dentists recommend that they eat chocolate instead. Unlike hard candies, chocolate dissolves quickly in the mouth. Besides, chocolate contains tannins, which help to kill some of the bacteria in the mouth. But no matter what a child eats, brushing after each meal is still the best way to fight cavities.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
大多數美國孩子都喜歡萬聖節的糖果，但是一整桶萬聖節糖果，可能是牙醫的惡夢。有些父母會在孩子上床以後，把一半的糖果處理掉；不過牙醫說，父母還要把好的零食和不好的零食分開。

真正要緊的不完全是孩子吃了什麼，而是食物在嘴裡停留多久。兒童牙醫 Kaneta Lott 醫師說，傷害最大的是黏黏的或很硬的東西，因為這些東西會在嘴裡停留很久。原因是每個人的嘴裡都有細菌。我們吃東西的時候，細菌也把我們的食物當成牠們的食物，並產生一種會破壞牙齒表面的酸，造成蛀牙。食物在嘴裡停留越久，就越可能蛀牙。所以洋芋片比糖果更糟，因為洋芋片會卡在牙縫裡。同樣的道理，葡萄乾和餅乾也不是最好的選擇。硬糖要吃很久，也不適合當萬聖節的零食。

如果孩子真的很愛吃糖，牙醫建議改吃巧克力。巧克力和硬糖不一樣，在嘴裡很快就會溶化。而且巧克力含有單寧酸，能幫忙殺死嘴裡的一些細菌。不過，不管孩子吃什麼，每餐飯後刷牙仍然是對抗蛀牙最好的方法。

items.stem: What is the main purpose of this passage?
options: To discuss how cavities can be treated.
To point out the problems with Halloween celebrations.
To tell parents what sweets are less damaging to their children’s teeth.
To teach parents the meaning of Halloween candies for their children.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說牙醫建議父母把好的零食和不好的零食分開；第 2 段說明會在嘴裡停留很久的東西傷牙，洋芋片、葡萄乾、餅乾和硬糖都不是好選擇；第 3 段建議改吃巧克力。全文在告訴父母哪些零食比較不傷孩子的牙齒，所以是 (C)。三個錯誤選項都偏離主題：(A) 文章說的是怎麼預防蛀牙，沒有談蛀牙怎麼治療；(B) 文章沒有批評萬聖節的慶祝活動；(D) 文章沒有談萬聖節糖果對孩子有什麼意義。

items.stem: Why are hard candies especially bad for teeth?
options: They may break the child’s teeth.
They help bacteria to produce tannins.
They stay in the mouth for a long time.
items.explanation:
The longer the food stays in the mouth, the more likely cavities will develop.
Hard candies take a long time to consume and are also a bad choice for Halloween treats.
第 2 段說食物在嘴裡停留越久（stays in the mouth），越可能蛀牙；硬糖要吃很久，所以也是不好的選擇。選項換成 They stay in the mouth for a long time，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 3 段的 tannins，單寧酸是巧克力裡的成分，能殺死細菌，不是細菌產生的；(A) 原文說硬的東西傷牙是因為停留在嘴裡很久，沒說會咬斷牙齒；(B) 原文說的重點正好是吃什麼不完全要緊，要看停留多久，沒有提到含糖量。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is a better choice for Halloween treats?
items.explanation:
If children really love candy, dentists recommend that they eat chocolate instead.
第 3 段說孩子如果真的很愛吃糖，牙醫建議改吃巧克力（chocolate），因為巧克力很快就會溶化，所以是 (A)。三個錯誤選項都照抄第 2 段：(D) 洋芋片會卡在牙縫裡，比糖果更糟；(C) 葡萄乾、(B) 餅乾，原文說同樣的道理也不是最好的選擇。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true of tannins?
options: They are produced when the bacteria digest the food.
They help to get rid of some bacteria in the mouth.
They help chocolate to dissolve more quickly.
They destroy the surface of the teeth.
items.explanation:
Besides, chocolate contains tannins, which help to kill some of the bacteria in the mouth.
第 3 段說巧克力含有單寧酸，能幫忙殺死（kill）嘴裡的一些細菌，選項換成 help to get rid of some bacteria，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 produce、(D) 照抄第 2 段的 the surface of the teeth，細菌產生、會破壞牙齒表面的是酸，不是單寧酸；(C) 照抄 dissolve，巧克力本身很快就會溶化，原文沒說是單寧酸讓它溶化得快。

閱讀測驗.title: 美國公共廣播電視台PBS（Public Broadcasting System）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The largest television network in America is not ABC, CBS, or Fox. Nor is it one of the cable networks such as CNN, which carries only news and news stories. It is not ESPN, the all-sports cable network, or even MTV, which is famous for its music videos. Rather it is PBS, Public Broadcasting System, a non-profit public broadcasting TV service. PBS has 349 member television stations in the U.S. and some member stations by cable in Canada.

PBS only attracts a minority of all TV viewers, about 2 percent. The industry leader, NBC, however, attracts 11 percent of viewers. But the growth of public television in the past two decades has been dramatic. This is especially noteworthy when one considers that public television stations must often survive on very limited budgets, on viewers’ donations, and on private foundations and some governmental funding.

The level of quality of PBS programs, whether in national and international news, entertainment, or education, is excellent. Almost a whole generation of children throughout the world is familiar with Sesame Street and the characters of The Muppet Show. PBS is especially well known for the quality of its many educational TV programs. Over 95 percent of all public television stations have tele-courses. These courses are accepted and supported by more than 1,800 colleges and universities throughout the US. Each year, over a quarter of a million students take courses this way.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
美國最大的電視網不是 ABC、CBS 或 Fox，也不是 CNN 這類只播新聞和新聞報導的有線電視網；不是專播體育節目的有線電視網 ESPN，甚至也不是以音樂錄影帶出名的 MTV。美國最大的電視網是 PBS（公共廣播電視公司），一個非營利的公共電視服務。PBS 在美國有 349 家會員電視台，在加拿大也有一些透過有線電視播出的會員台。

PBS 只吸引了所有電視觀眾中的少數，大約 2%。業界龍頭 NBC 則吸引了 11% 的觀眾。不過過去二十年來，公共電視的成長相當驚人。公共電視台常常得靠非常有限的預算、觀眾的捐款、私人基金會和一些政府補助來維持，想到這一點，這樣的成長就更值得注意。

PBS 節目的品質，不論是國內外新聞、娛樂還是教育節目，都非常出色。全世界幾乎整整一代的孩子，都熟悉《芝麻街》和《大青蛙劇場》裡的角色。PBS 尤其以許多優質的教育節目聞名。超過 95% 的公共電視台都有電視課程，全美有 1,800 多所大專院校承認並支持這些課程。每年有超過二十五萬名學生透過這種方式修課。

items.stem: According to this article, PBS received part of its funding from ______.
items.explanation:
This is especially noteworthy when one considers that public television stations must often survive on very limited budgets, on viewers’ donations, and on private foundations and some governmental funding.
第 2 段說公共電視台常常得靠有限的預算、觀眾的捐款、私人基金會（private foundations）和一些政府補助來維持。基金會是一種機構，選項換成 private organizations，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 public，public 是說 PBS 是公共電視，原文沒說錢來自公立學校；第 3 段的大專院校是承認電視課程，不是出錢；(D) 照抄 television stations，原文說的是公共電視台自己要靠這些來源維持，不是錢來自別的電視台；(C) 廣告公司，原文沒有提到，PBS 是非營利的。

items.stem: What is PBS most famous for?
items.explanation:
PBS is especially well known for the quality of its many educational TV programs.
第 3 段說 PBS 尤其以（especially well known for）許多優質的教育節目（educational TV programs）聞名，題目換成 most famous for，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 news，新聞是 PBS 品質出色的節目之一，但原文用 especially 強調的是教育節目；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 cable，只播新聞的 CNN 才是有線電視網，PBS 只有在加拿大的部分會員台透過有線電視播出；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 donations，觀眾的捐款是 PBS 經費的來源，不是 PBS 出名的地方。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about public television stations?
options: The majority of their viewers are minority people.
Ninety-five percent of their programs are tele-courses.
They are shrinking in number because they make no profits.
Their courses are accepted by many universities in America.
items.explanation:
These courses are accepted and supported by more than 1,800 colleges and universities throughout the US.
第 3 段說全美有 1,800 多所大專院校承認（accepted）並支持公共電視台的課程，選項把 1,800 多所換成 many universities，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 tele-courses，原文說超過 95% 的公共電視台有電視課程，不是 95% 的節目都是電視課程；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 minority，原文說 PBS 只吸引了少數的觀眾，約 2%，不是說觀眾大多是少數族群；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 profit，PBS 是非營利的，但第 2 段說過去二十年來公共電視的成長相當驚人，正好相反。

items.stem: Which of the following has the highest percentage of viewers?
items.explanation:
PBS only attracts a minority of all TV viewers, about 2 percent.
The industry leader, NBC, however, attracts 11 percent of viewers.
第 2 段說 PBS 只吸引約 2% 的觀眾，業界龍頭 NBC 則吸引 11% 的觀眾，所以收視比例最高的是 (C)。(B) PBS 是會員電視台最多的電視網，但觀眾只占 2%，「最大」和「收視最高」是兩回事；(A) ABC、(D) Fox 只出現在第 1 段，原文說它們不是最大的電視網，沒有提到收視比例。

閱讀測驗.title: 時尚界的「無皮草」運動（The "Fur-Free" Movement in Fashion）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Last week Jay McCarroll and The HSUS (The Humane Society of the United States) made a bold fur-free statement on the runway, marking a new chapter for the fashion industry and animal protection. The encouraging response to McCarroll’s show confirmed that change is happening in fashion.

McCarroll has good reasons for rejecting fur. Each year, tens of millions of animals, including dogs and cats, needlessly suffer and die to fuel the fur industry. But what did Jay McCarroll use in place of fur? “I have patchwork pieces that contain all sorts of combinations of fabrics. The rest is cotton, nylon, polyester...you name it. I even have some stuff made out of bamboo/cotton blend. Anything but fur and leather,” he told Fashion Wire Daily.

“So many people want to protect animals and live their lives without causing unnecessary cruelty. More than two thirds of Americans have pets, and we share a bond with animals every day. Saying no to fur can help millions of animals, and we want to show our respect to leading designers like Jay who embrace compassion as the fashion,” said Michael Markarian, executive vice president of The HSUS. “It is great to see leaders in the fashion industry recognizing that the animals need their fur more than we do.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
上週，Jay McCarroll 和美國人道協會（HSUS）在伸展台上發表了大膽的「不用皮草」聲明，為時尚產業和動物保護揭開新的一頁。McCarroll 的服裝秀得到令人鼓舞的回應，證實時尚界正在改變。

McCarroll 拒絕使用皮草有充分的理由。每年有幾千萬隻動物，包括狗和貓，為了供應皮草業而白白受苦、死去。那麼 Jay McCarroll 用什麼取代皮草呢？他告訴《Fashion Wire Daily》：「我有用各種布料組合拼接起來的拼布。其他的有棉、尼龍、聚酯纖維……什麼都有。我甚至有一些用竹纖維加棉織成的布料。除了皮草和皮革，什麼都可以。」

美國人道協會執行副會長 Michael Markarian 說：「很多人都想保護動物，過生活時不造成不必要的殘忍。超過三分之二的美國人養寵物，我們每天都和動物有一份情感上的連結。對皮草說不，可以幫助數百萬隻動物；像 Jay 這樣把慈悲心當成時尚的頂尖設計師，我們要向他們致敬。」他也說：「看到時尚界的領導者認清動物比我們更需要牠們的皮毛，真是太好了。」

items.stem: Which of the following is true about Jay McCarroll?
options: He is a famous fashion designer.
He is the executive vice president of the HSUS.
He is an editor of Fashion Wire Daily.
He is the head of an animal protection organization.
items.explanation:
Last week Jay McCarroll and The HSUS (The Humane Society of the United States) made a bold fur-free statement on the runway
we want to show our respect to leading designers like Jay who embrace compassion as the fashion
第 1 段說 McCarroll 在伸展台上發表不用皮草的聲明，他的服裝秀得到很好的回應；第 3 段美國人道協會的副會長稱他是頂尖設計師（leading designers like Jay），所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 executive vice president，執行副會長是 Michael Markarian；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 Fashion Wire Daily，McCarroll 是接受這家媒體的訪問，不是它的編輯；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 animal protection，動物保護團體是和他合作的美國人道協會，他不是協會的負責人。

items.stem: What does “a new chapter” in line 2, paragraph 1 mean?
options: A new unit of a book.
The beginning of a new trend.
The latest issue of a magazine.
items.explanation:
marking a new chapter for the fashion industry and animal protection.
The encouraging response to McCarroll’s show confirmed that change is happening in fashion.
chapter 本義是書的一章。第 1 段說這場不用皮草的服裝秀為時尚產業和動物保護標示了 a new chapter，下一句又說熱烈的回應證實時尚界正在改變（change is happening）。可見這裡的意思是新的階段、新潮流的開始，所以是 (B)。(A) 書的新單元是字面意思，放在時尚產業接不上；(C) 雜誌的最新一期、(D) 新成立的組織，原文都沒有提到。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT recommended for clothing by Jay McCarroll?
items.explanation:
“I have patchwork pieces that contain all sorts of combinations of fabrics.
The rest is cotton, nylon, polyester...you name it.
I even have some stuff made out of bamboo/cotton blend.
Anything but fur and leather,”
第 2 段 McCarroll 列出他用來取代皮草的材料：patchwork pieces 是 (D) 拼布，polyester 是 (A) 聚酯纖維，bamboo/cotton blend 是用 (B) 竹纖維加棉做的布料。他最後說 Anything but fur and leather，除了皮草和皮革什麼都可以，所以他不建議用的是 (C) 皮革。

items.stem: What do we learn from this passage?
options: Human beings depend emotionally on animals.
Fashion can go hand in hand with compassion for life.
Fur is more effective than bamboo/cotton blend for clothing.
Fur is more expensive than other materials for fashion designers.
items.explanation:
we want to show our respect to leading designers like Jay who embrace compassion as the fashion
第 3 段 Markarian 說要向像 Jay 這樣把慈悲心當成時尚（embrace compassion as the fashion）的設計師致敬；第 1 段也說這場不用皮草的服裝秀得到很好的回應。可見時尚和對生命的慈悲心可以並行，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 bamboo/cotton blend，竹纖維加棉的布料是用來取代皮草的，原文沒有比較哪一種效果比較好；(A) 第 3 段說我們每天和動物有情感上的連結，不是說人在情感上依賴動物；(D) 皮草比較貴，原文沒有提到。

閱讀測驗.title: 男孩與女孩的生物性差異（Biological Differences Between Boys and Girls）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Twenty years ago, most experts believed that differences in how boys and girls behaved were mainly due to differences in how they were treated by their parents, teachers, and friends. It’s hard to cling to that belief today. Recent research has shown that there are biological differences between boys and girls. Understanding these differences is important in raising and educating children.

For example, girls are born with more sensitive hearing than boys, and the difference increases as kids grow up. So when a grown man speaks to a girl in what he thinks is a normal voice, she may hear it as yelling. Conversely, boys who appear to be inattentive in class may just be sitting too far away to hear the teacher.

Likewise, girls are better in their expression of feelings. Studies reveal that negative emotions are seated in an area of the brain called the amygdala. Girls develop an early connection between this area and the cerebral cortex, enabling them to talk about their feelings. In boys these links develop later. So if you ask a troubled adolescent boy to tell you what his feelings are, he often cannot say much.

Dr. Sax, a proponent of single-sex education, points out that keeping boys and girls separate in the classroom has yielded striking educational, social, and interpersonal benefits. Therefore, parents and teachers should try to recognize, understand, and make use of the biological differences that make a girl a girl, and a boy a boy.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
二十年前，大多數專家認為男孩和女孩的行為差異，主要是因為父母、老師和朋友對待他們的方式不同。今天很難再堅持這種看法了。最近的研究顯示，男孩和女孩之間有生理上的差異。了解這些差異，對養育和教育孩子很重要。

例如，女孩一出生聽覺就比男孩敏銳，而且這個差距隨著孩子長大越來越大。所以成年男子用他自認為正常的音量對女孩說話，女孩聽起來可能像在吼叫。反過來說，上課時看起來不專心的男孩，可能只是坐得太遠，聽不到老師說話。

同樣地，女孩比較會表達自己的感受。研究顯示，負面情緒位於大腦一個叫做杏仁核的區域。女孩很早就在這個區域和大腦皮質之間建立連結，所以她們說得出自己的感受。男孩的這些連結比較晚才發展出來。所以如果你要一個心裡有困擾的青春期男孩說出他的感受，他往往說不出什麼。

Sax 博士提倡單一性別教育，他指出，在教室裡把男孩和女孩分開，在教育、社會和人際關係上都帶來顯著的好處。所以，父母和老師應該努力認識、了解並善用這些生理差異，正是這些差異讓女孩成為女孩、男孩成為男孩。

items.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Boys tend to pay less attention in class than girls.
Girls are better than boys in their ability to detect sounds.
Boys and girls behave differently because of biological differences.
Single-sex schools are not good because they keep boys and girls separate.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說最近的研究顯示男孩和女孩有生理上的差異；第 2 段舉聽覺為例，第 3 段舉表達感受為例；第 4 段說父母和老師應該善用這些生理差異。全文在說男孩和女孩的行為不同，是因為生理差異，所以是 (C)。(A) 男孩上課看起來不專心、(B) 女孩聽覺比較敏銳，都只是第 2 段的例子，過於狹隘；(D) 第 4 段說把男孩和女孩分開有顯著的好處，選項說的正好相反，偏離主題。

items.stem: Why do girls express negative feelings better than boys?
options: Girls are more emotional than boys.
Girls have more brain cells than boys.
The amygdala is located in different areas of the brain for boys and girls.
The links between certain parts of the brain develop earlier in girls than in boys.
items.explanation:
Girls develop an early connection between this area and the cerebral cortex, enabling them to talk about their feelings.
In boys these links develop later.
第 3 段說女孩很早（early）就在杏仁核和大腦皮質之間建立連結，所以說得出自己的感受；男孩的這些連結比較晚才發展。選項把兩句合起來，說這些連結女孩發展得比男孩早（earlier），所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 amygdala，原文說負面情緒位於杏仁核，沒說男孩和女孩的杏仁核位置不同，差別在連結發展的早晚；(A) 原文沒說女孩比較情緒化；(B) 腦細胞的多少，原文沒有提到。

items.stem: Which of the following does the author believe?
options: Girls need more training in communication.
Boys and girls should be educated in different ways.
Parents should pay more attention to boys.
Sex differences should be ignored in education.
items.explanation:
Understanding these differences is important in raising and educating children.
Therefore, parents and teachers should try to recognize, understand, and make use of the biological differences that make a girl a girl, and a boy a boy.
第 1 段說了解男女的生理差異對教育孩子很重要；第 4 段引用 Sax 博士說男女分班有顯著的好處，接著說父母和老師應該善用這些差異。可見作者認為男孩和女孩應該用不同的方式教育，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 differences，作者要父母和老師善用性別差異，不是忽略；(A) 原文說女孩比較會表達感受，需要幫忙的反而是男孩；(C) 原文沒說父母要多注意男孩，說的是父母和老師都要了解男孩和女孩的差異。

items.stem: What does the phrase “cling to” in the first paragraph mean?
items.explanation:
Twenty years ago, most experts believed that differences in how boys and girls behaved were mainly due to differences in how they were treated by their parents, teachers, and friends.
It’s hard to cling to that belief today.
Recent research has shown that there are biological differences between boys and girls.
第 1 段說二十年前的專家認為男女的差異來自後天的對待，接著說今天很難 cling to 這種看法，因為最近的研究顯示有生理上的差異。新的研究推翻了舊的看法，所以很難再「維持、堅持」這種看法，cling to 是 (A) maintain。(B) abandon（放棄）正好相反：新研究已經推翻舊看法，放棄它並不難；(C) evaluate（評估）、(D) challenge（質疑），放進句子裡意思接不上。

閱讀測驗.title: 安德魯·卡內基的生平與慈善（Andrew Carnegie's Life and Philanthropy）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Andrew Carnegie, once the world’s richest person, was born in 1835 to a weaver’s family in Scotland. As a child, he was expected to follow his father’s profession. But the industrial revolution destroyed the weavers’ craft, and the family had to leave for new possibilities in America.

In 1848 the Carnegies arrived in Pittsburgh, then the iron-manufacturing center of the country. Young Carnegie took odd jobs at a cotton factory and later worked as a messenger boy in the telegraph office. He was often asked to deliver messages to the city theater, where he would stay to watch plays by great playwrights. He also spent most of his leisure hours in a small library that a local benefactor made available to working boys.

After the Civil War, Carnegie saw great potential in the iron industry. He devoted himself to the replacement of wooden bridges with stronger iron ones and earned a fortune. He further introduced a new steel refining process to convert iron into steel. By 1900, Carnegie Steel produced more of the metal than all of Great Britain.

However, Carnegie often expressed his uneasiness with the businessman’s life. Wishing to spend more time receiving instruction and reading systematically, he once wrote, “To continue much longer overwhelmed by business cares and with most of my thoughts wholly upon the way to make more money in the shortest time, must degrade me beyond hope of permanent recovery.” The strong desire for intellectual pursuit led him to sell his company and retire at 64.

Fond of saying that “the man who dies rich dies disgraced,” Carnegie then turned his attention to giving away his fortune. He abhorred charity; instead, he used his money to help others help themselves. He established over 2,500 public libraries, and sponsored numerous cultural, educational and scientific institutions. By the time he died in 1919, he had given away 350 million dollars.

items.stem: Why did Andrew Carnegie move to the United States?
options: Because his father was offered a good job in Pittsburgh.
Because he did not want to follow his father’s profession.
Because there were serious political problems in Scotland.
Because his family could not make a good living in their hometown.

items.stem: When did Carnegie begin to show his interest in artistic and intellectual pursuit?
options: After he retired from his business.
When he was a young boy back in Scotland.
After he earned his fortune from his iron business.
When he worked as a messenger boy in Pittsburgh.

items.stem: Which of the following best characterizes how Carnegie managed his business?
options: He was willing to make new changes.
He set out to beat all the other competitors.
He was happy to make more money in the shortest time.
He did not hesitate in making investments in his hometown.

items.stem: How did Carnegie handle his fortune after his retirement?
options: He left it to his family and friends after he died.
He gave it to poor people and charity organizations.
He used it to support organizations of higher learning.
He invested it in developing new technology in steel refinement.

閱讀測驗.title: 注意力不足/過動症（AD/HD) (Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Most parents dread a note or call from school saying that their child’s behavior is “not normal.” If your child’s academic performance and social life is suffering because they don’t pay attention, can’t sit still and act without thinking, it is most likely that they have AD/HD (Attention Deficit/ Hyperactivity Disorder).

AD/HD is a neurological disorder which stems not from the home environment, but from biological and genetic causes. Its symptoms typically show up in early childhood. The main characteristics are inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity. Inattentive children have difficulty focusing on completing a task or learning something new. Hyperactive children always seem to be restless. Often they report that they need to stay busy and may try to do several tasks at once. Impulsive children often do not think before they act. They often blurt out inappropriate comments or have difficulty taking turns in conversation.

Most children can be inattentive, hyperactive, or impulsive at times. It is when these behaviors are inappropriate for their age and affect different areas in their lives that the disorder is diagnosed. Depression, anxiety, and learning disabilities may co-exist with AD/HD. Therefore, if a child is suspected of AD/HD, it is very important that he or she be evaluated by a professional.

Once your child is diagnosed with AD/HD, it is important to let the school know so that they can provide appropriate academic and social support. Your child’s school should keep this information confidential and it can usually make accommodations in the classroom to fit your child’s learning needs.

items.stem: What is the cause of AD/HD?
Which of the following are most likely AD/HD patients?
What is the first thing to do if your child is suspected of AD/HD?
options: Wait until the child grows up.
Send the child to a special school.

閱讀測驗.title: 衝突鑽石及其解決方案（Conflict Diamonds and Solutions）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Conflict diamonds, sometimes called blood diamonds, are diamonds that are sold to fund the unlawful and illegal operations of rebel, military and terrorist groups. Countries that have been most affected by conflict diamonds are Sierra Leone, Angola, Liberia and the Democratic Republic of Congo. They are places where citizens have been terrorized or even killed by groups in control of the local diamond trade.

Wars in most of those areas have ended or at least decreased in intensity, but the problem of conflict diamonds hasn’t gone away. Diamonds mined in some rebel-held areas, such as Liberia, are being smuggled into neighboring countries and exported as conflict-free diamonds.

In order to stop blood diamond sales, South African countries with a legitimate diamond trade began a campaign in 2000 to track the origins of all rough diamonds. Their efforts resulted in the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme (KPCS), an international organization to make the world free of conflict diamonds. The goals of the KPCS are to document and track all rough diamonds when they enter a participating country. Shippers are required to place those diamonds in sealed boxes and provide enough detailed information about their origins to prove they did not originate in a conflict zone.

It’s difficult for most of us to imagine what life is like in countries where diamonds are the source of so much chaos and suffering. Furthermore, the connection between terror and diamonds is not something that’s reported heavily in the press. The 2006 movie Blood Diamond, starring Leonardo DiCaprio, should help make the issue more mainstream, if only temporarily. So, take some time to learn more about the problems that conflict diamonds create, and then follow your heart the next time you shop for a diamond.

items.stem: Why are diamonds from some areas called “blood diamonds”?
options: They cause loss of human lives.
They are of exceptionally high quality.

items.stem: What can be inferred from the second paragraph of this passage?
options: Diamonds from Liberia are mostly conflict-free.
Most diamonds from Liberia are labeled correctly.
Diamonds in Liberia are still traded to support wars.
Diamonds from Liberia have been carefully investigated by the KPCS.

items.stem: What is the major task of the KPCS?
options: To promote the sales of rough diamonds.
To produce movies like Blood Diamond.
To penalize those who sell blood diamonds.
To document where the diamonds were mined.

items.stem: What is the author’s attitude towards blood diamonds?

閱讀測驗.title: 吼猴的行為與地域性（Howler Monkeys' Behavior and Territoriality）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Howler monkeys are named for the long loud cries, or howls, that they make every day. They are the loudest land animal and their howls can be heard three miles away through dense forests. Male howler monkeys use their loud voices to fight for food, mates, or territory. Everyone starts and ends the day by howling to check out where their nearest competitors are.

Interestingly, when there are few howler monkeys in an area, the howling routine takes on a different pattern. In Belize, where howler monkeys were newly reintroduced into a wildlife sanctuary, the howler monkeys were heard only a few times a week rather than every day. Apparently, with plenty of space and no other howler monkeys around, there was no need to check on the whereabouts of their competitors. At the sanctuary, keepers now use recorded howler sounds from a distance so that the monkeys feel the need to make the territorial calls as they would do in the wild. In the future when the population grows, there will be no need for the recording because the howler monkeys will have more reason to check in with the neighbors to define their own territories.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
吼猴得名於牠們每天發出的長而響亮的叫聲，也就是吼聲。吼猴是陸地上叫聲最大的動物，吼聲穿過茂密的森林，三英里外都聽得到。公吼猴用宏亮的聲音爭奪食物、配偶或地盤。每一隻吼猴都用吼叫開始和結束一天，藉此查看離自己最近的競爭者在哪裡。

有趣的是，一個地區的吼猴很少的時候，每天吼叫的習慣會變成另一種模式。貝里斯有一處野生動物保護區最近重新引進吼猴，那裡的吼猴一週只吼叫幾次，而不是每天都叫。看來空間充足、附近又沒有其他吼猴，牠們就沒有必要查看競爭者在哪裡。現在保護區的管理員會從遠處播放吼猴叫聲的錄音，讓猴子覺得需要像在野外一樣，發出宣示地盤的叫聲。將來吼猴數量增加，就不需要錄音了，因為吼猴會有更多理由和鄰居互相確認，劃定自己的地盤。

items.stem: Why do howler monkeys howl?
options: To check how popular they are.
To tell others they are going to leave.
To show friendliness to their neighbors.
items.explanation:
Male howler monkeys use their loud voices to fight for food, mates, or territory.
Everyone starts and ends the day by howling to check out where their nearest competitors are.
第 1 段說公吼猴用宏亮的聲音爭奪（fight for）食物、配偶或地盤，每天也用吼叫查看競爭者在哪裡；第 2 段說保護區的錄音是要讓猴子發出宣示地盤的叫聲（territorial calls）。選項換成 claim their territory，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 check，吼猴查看的是競爭者在哪裡，不是自己受不受歡迎；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 neighbors，吼猴和鄰居互相確認是為了劃定地盤，不是表示友善；(C) 原文沒說吼叫是告訴別人自己要離開。

items.stem: Why did the howler monkeys in Belize howl less often?
options: They lived too close to each other.
There was enough food for all of them.
There were no other competitors around.
They were not used to the weather there.
items.explanation:
Apparently, with plenty of space and no other howler monkeys around, there was no need to check on the whereabouts of their competitors.
第 2 段說貝里斯保護區的吼猴空間充足，附近也沒有其他吼猴（no other howler monkeys around），沒有必要查看競爭者在哪裡，所以叫得比較少。選項換成 There were no other competitors around，所以是 (C)。(A) 正好相反，原文說的是空間很充足；(B) 原文說的是空間充足，沒說食物夠吃；(D) 天氣，原文沒有提到。

items.stem: Why do the keepers at the sanctuary use recorded howls?
options: To prevent the howler monkeys from getting homesick.
To help howler monkeys maintain their howling ability.
To trick the monkeys into the belief that there is plenty of space around.
To teach the monkeys how to make the loudest cries to scare people away.
items.explanation:
At the sanctuary, keepers now use recorded howler sounds from a distance so that the monkeys feel the need to make the territorial calls as they would do in the wild.
第 2 段說管理員從遠處播放吼猴的錄音，讓猴子覺得需要像在野外一樣發出宣示地盤的叫聲。保護區的吼猴原本很少叫，錄音讓牠們保持在野外吼叫的習慣，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 plenty of space，錄音的作用正好相反，是讓猴子以為附近有競爭者；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 loudest，吼猴本來就是叫聲最大的陸地動物，吼叫是給其他吼猴聽的，不是嚇走人；(A) 原文沒有提到想家。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about howler monkeys?
options: They howl most often at noon.
People can hear their howls three miles away.
Female monkeys howl to protect their babies.
items.explanation:
They are the loudest land animal and their howls can be heard three miles away through dense forests.
第 1 段說吼猴的叫聲三英里外都聽得到（can be heard three miles away），選項換成主動語態 People can hear their howls three miles away，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 Belize，貝里斯是重新引進吼猴的地方，不是吼猴的原產地；(A) 原文說吼猴在一天開始和結束時吼叫，沒說中午叫得最多；(D) 原文說用叫聲爭奪地盤的是公猴，沒說母猴吼叫是為了保護小猴。

閱讀測驗.title: 冰河國家公園道路的建設與公園合作（Glacier National Park Road Construction and Park Collaboration）
閱讀測驗.passage:
After the creation of the Glacier National Park in Montana, the growing number of park visitors increased the need for roads. Eventually, the demand for a road across the mountains led to the building of the Going-to-the-Sun Road.

The construction of the Going-to-the-Sun Road was a huge task. After 11 years of work, the final section of the road was completed in 1932. The road is considered an engineering feat. Even today, visitors to the park marvel at how such a road could have been built. It is one of the most scenic roads in North America. The construction of the road has changed the way visitors experience the Glacier National Park. Visitors now can drive over sections of the park that previously took days of horseback riding to see.

Just across the border, in Canada, is the Waterton Lakes National Park. In 1931, members of the Rotary Clubs of Alberta and Montana suggested joining the two parks as a symbol of peace and friendship between the two countries. In 1932, the United States and Canadian governments renamed the parks the Waterton-Glacier International Peace Park, the world’s first. More recently, the parks have received several international honors. They were named as a World Heritage Site in 1995. This international recognition highlights the importance of this area, not just to the United States and Canada, but to the entire world.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
蒙大拿州的冰河國家公園成立以後，遊客越來越多，對道路的需求也增加了。後來大家需要一條翻越山脈的道路，促成了「奔向太陽之路」的興建。

興建奔向太陽之路是一項浩大的工程。經過 11 年的施工，最後一段路在 1932 年完工。這條路公認是一項工程壯舉。直到今天，來公園的遊客仍然驚嘆這樣一條路是怎麼蓋起來的。這是北美洲風景最優美的道路之一。這條路改變了遊客體驗冰河國家公園的方式：公園裡有些地方，以前要騎好幾天的馬才看得到，現在遊客開車就能經過。

越過邊界，加拿大那一邊是華特頓湖國家公園。1931 年，亞伯達省和蒙大拿州的扶輪社成員提議把兩座公園結合起來，象徵兩國之間的和平與友誼。1932 年，美國和加拿大政府把這兩座公園重新命名為華特頓冰河國際和平公園，這是世界上第一座國際和平公園。近年來，這兩座公園獲得了幾項國際榮譽，1995 年列為世界遺產。這項國際肯定凸顯出這個地區不只對美國和加拿大重要，對全世界都很重要。

items.stem: What made it necessary to build a road through the Glacier National Park?
options: There were too many parks in Montana.
The park was not sunny enough for visitors.
The existing mountain roads were destroyed.
More visitors were interested in going to the park.
items.explanation:
After the creation of the Glacier National Park in Montana, the growing number of park visitors increased the need for roads.
第 1 段說冰河國家公園成立以後，遊客越來越多（the growing number of park visitors），對道路的需求跟著增加，選項換成 More visitors were interested in going to the park，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 Montana，蒙大拿州是公園所在的州，原文沒說那裡的公園太多；(B) 照抄 Sun，奔向太陽之路是道路的名字，和公園陽光夠不夠無關；(C) 照抄 mountain，原文說需要一條翻越山脈的路，沒說原有的山路毀了。

items.stem: How has the Going-to-the-Sun Road influenced the way people experience the Glacier National Park?
options: The scenery along the road is too beautiful for visitors to drive carefully.
It has become a marvelous experience for people to ride horses on this road.
The road has allowed people to see more of the park in a shorter period of time.
The transportation on the road was so difficult that few people could really enjoy the trip.
items.explanation:
The construction of the road has changed the way visitors experience the Glacier National Park.
Visitors now can drive over sections of the park that previously took days of horseback riding to see.
第 2 段說這條路改變了遊客體驗公園的方式：以前要騎好幾天馬才看得到的地方，現在開車就能經過。從好幾天縮短到開車就到，遊客能在比較短的時間裡看到公園更多地方，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 horse，騎馬是以前的方式，有了這條路以後改成開車；(A) 照抄 drive，原文說這是北美洲風景最美的道路之一，沒說風景美到讓人沒辦法小心開車；(D) 正好相反，原文說遊客開車就能經過那些地方。

items.stem: What does “an engineering feat” mean?
options: A great disaster for the travelers.
items.explanation:
The construction of the Going-to-the-Sun Road was a huge task.
Even today, visitors to the park marvel at how such a road could have been built.
第 2 段前面說興建這條路是一項浩大的工程，花了 11 年才完工；後面說直到今天，遊客仍然驚嘆這樣一條路是怎麼蓋起來的。前後都在說這條路蓋得了不起，所以 an engineering feat 是 (A) 工程上的一大成就。(B) 神奇的建築機器、(C) 遊客的大災難，和遊客驚嘆的語氣接不上；(D) 原文沒有提到工程師覺得施工過程很愉快。

items.stem: What is special about the Waterton-Glacier International Peace Park?
options: It is where the glacier runs to the lake.
It is the first park funded by the whole world.
It is a special park built to protect wild animals.
It is composed of two parks located in two countries.
items.explanation:
In 1931, members of the Rotary Clubs of Alberta and Montana suggested joining the two parks as a symbol of peace and friendship between the two countries.
第 3 段說加拿大那一邊有華特頓湖國家公園，扶輪社成員提議把兩座公園（two parks）結合起來，象徵兩國（two countries）的和平與友誼；1932 年兩國政府把它們命名為國際和平公園。選項換成 composed of two parks located in two countries，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 first，原文說它是世界第一座國際和平公園，後來列為世界遺產，沒說由全世界出資；(A) 照抄 lake，華特頓湖是加拿大那座公園的名字，原文沒說冰河流進湖裡；(C) 原文沒說這座公園是為了保護野生動物而建的。

閱讀測驗.title: 冰雕藝術的挑戰與應用（Challenges and Applications of Ice Sculpting）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Ice sculpting is a difficult process. First, ice must be carefully selected so that it is suitable for sculpting. Its ideal material is pure, clean water with high clarity. It should also have the minimum amount of air bubbles. Perfectly clear ice blocks weighing 140 kg and measuring 100 cm × 50 cm × 25 cm are available from the Clinebell Company in Colorado. Much larger clear blocks are produced in Europe and Canada or harvested from a frozen river in Sweden. These large ice blocks are used for large ice sculpting events and for building ice hotels.

Another difficulty in the process of ice sculpting is time control. The temperature of the environment affects how quickly the piece must be completed to avoid the effects of melting. If the sculpting does not take place in a cold environment, then the sculptor must work quickly to finish his piece. The tools used for sculpting also affect when the task can be accomplished. Some sculptures can be completed in as little as ten minutes if power tools are used. Ice sculptors also use razor-sharp chisels that are specifically designed for cutting ice. The best ice chisels are made in Japan, a country that, along with China, has a long tradition of magnificent ice sculptures.

Ice sculptures are used as decorations in some cuisines, especially in Asia. When holding a dinner party, some large restaurants or hotels will use an ice sculpture to decorate the table. For example, in a wedding banquet it is common to see a pair of ice-sculpted swans that represent the union of the new couple.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
冰雕是一個困難的過程。首先，冰塊必須仔細挑選，才適合雕刻。理想的材料是純淨、乾淨、透明度高的水，氣泡也要越少越好。科羅拉多州的 Clinebell 公司供應完全透明的冰塊，每塊重 140 公斤，尺寸是 100 公分 × 50 公分 × 25 公分。更大的透明冰塊則在歐洲和加拿大生產，或是從瑞典一條結冰的河上採集。這些大冰塊用在大型冰雕活動，也用來蓋冰旅館。

冰雕過程中的另一個困難是控制時間。環境的溫度會影響作品必須多快完成，才不會融化。如果不是在寒冷的環境裡雕刻，雕刻師就必須加快動作，才能完成作品。雕刻用的工具也會影響多久能完成。如果使用電動工具，有些作品只要十分鐘就能完成。冰雕師也會使用專門用來切冰、像剃刀一樣鋒利的鑿子。最好的冰鑿是日本製的；日本和中國一樣，都有製作壯觀冰雕的悠久傳統。

在某些料理中，冰雕用來當作裝飾，在亞洲尤其如此。舉辦晚宴時，有些大型餐廳或飯店會用冰雕裝飾餐桌。例如在婚宴上，常常可以看到一對冰雕的天鵝，代表新人的結合。

items.stem: What kind of ice is ideal for sculpting?
options: Ice with lots of bubbles in it.
items.explanation:
Its ideal material is pure, clean water with high clarity.

閱讀測驗.title: 疼痛的心理與生理元素（Physical and Psychological Elements of Pain）
閱讀測驗.passage:
If you touch your finger to a hot stove, you know it’s going to hurt. However, if you convince yourself beforehand that the pain won’t be so bad, you might not suffer as much. According to a recent study, the part of your brain that reacts to severe pain is largely the same part that reacts to expectation of pain.

Researchers in this study worked with 10 volunteers, ages 24 to 46. Each volunteer wore a device that gave out 20-second-long pulses of heat to the right leg. There were three levels of heat, producing mild, moderate, or strong pain. During training, the volunteers would first hear a tone, followed by a period of silence, and then feel a heat pulse. They then learned to associate the length of the silent pause with the intensity of the upcoming heat pulse. The longer the pause, the stronger the heat pulse would be, causing more severe pain.

A day or two later, the real experiment began. The researchers found that the parts of the brain involved in learning, memory, emotion, and touch became more active as the volunteers expected higher levels of pain. These were mainly the same areas that became active when participants actually felt pain. Interestingly, when the volunteers expected only mild or moderate pain but experienced severe pain, they reported feeling 28 percent less pain than when they expected severe pain and actually got it.

The new study emphasizes that pain has both physical and psychological elements. Understanding how pain works in the mind and brain could eventually give doctors tools for helping people cope with painful medical treatments.

如果你用手指碰到熱爐子，你知道會痛。然而，如果你事先說服自己不會那麼痛，你可能就不會那麼難受。根據最近的一項研究，大腦裡對劇痛起反應的部位，和對預期疼痛起反應的部位，大致是同一個。

這項研究的研究人員找了 10 位志願者，年齡從 24 到 46 歲。每位志願者都戴著一個裝置，裝置會對右腿發出每次 20 秒的熱脈衝。熱度分三個等級，分別造成輕微、中度或強烈的疼痛。訓練期間，志願者會先聽到一個聲音，接著是一段靜默，然後感覺到熱脈衝。他們因此學會把靜默停頓的長短，和接下來熱脈衝的強度聯想在一起：停頓越長，熱脈衝就越強，造成的疼痛也越劇烈。

一兩天後，正式的實驗開始了。研究人員發現，志願者預期的疼痛越強，大腦裡和學習、記憶、情緒、觸覺有關的部位就越活躍。這些部位和參與者真的感覺到疼痛時活躍的部位，大致相同。有意思的是，志願者如果預期的只是輕微或中度的疼痛，實際上卻感受到劇痛，他們說感覺到的疼痛，比預期劇痛而真的遇到劇痛時少了 28%。

這項新研究強調，疼痛同時有生理和心理的成分。了解疼痛在心智和大腦中怎麼運作，最後可能讓醫生有工具，幫助病人面對會痛的醫療處置。

閱讀測驗.title: 樂高積木的歷史與演變（The History and Evolution of Lego Bricks）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The Lego Group had a very humble beginning in the workshop of Ole Kirk Christiansen, a carpenter from Denmark. Christiansen began creating wooden toys in 1932. Two years later, he stumbled on the Lego name by putting together the first two letters of the Danish words Leg and Godt, which mean “play well.” The name could be interpreted as “I put together” in Latin; it also corresponds to the Greek verb meaning “gather” or “pick up.”

In 1947, the company expanded to making plastic toys. At first, the use of plastic for toy manufacture was not highly regarded by retailers and consumers of the time. Many of the Lego Group’s shipments were returned, following poor sales. However, Christiansen’s son, Godtfred Kirk Christiansen, saw the immense potential in Lego bricks to become a system for creative play. As the junior managing director of the Lego Group, he spent years trying to improve the “locking” ability of the bricks and made the bricks more versatile. In 1958, the modern interlocking brick design was finally developed and patented.

Today Lego is sold in more than 130 countries. Every minute 33,824 Lego bricks are made, and kids around the world spend 5 billion hours a year playing with Lego. There will be more than 400 million people playing with Lego bricks this year. On average, every person in the world owns 62 Lego bricks, and about seven Lego sets are sold every second.

This year Lego fans all over the world are celebrating the 50th anniversary of the tiny building blocks. Though already 50 years old, Lego is still the same product it was in the 1950s. Bricks bought then are still compatible with current bricks and that is probably the reason the toy has never fallen out of favor.

It was created by Ole Kirk Christiansen’s son.

閱讀測驗.title: 厭食症的掙扎與自我接納（Anorexia Struggle and Self-Acceptance）
閱讀測驗.passage:
During my ninth-grade year, I suffered from anorexia nervosa. It was not enough to be thin. I had to be the thinnest. Now, however, fully recovered, I can reflect back and realize that my wishes were more complex than fitting into size five pants. Many of my subconscious emotions were related to my relationship with my father. As I was growing up, his work always came first. Sometimes I would not see him for up to two weeks. Not only did he devote his whole self to his work, but he expected me to do the same (“You cannot get anywhere unless you go to the best universities!”). Though, consciously, I never felt pressure to please him, I began dieting after the first time he told me I looked fat.

At the time, all I knew was that I had to be skinny—skinnier than anyone else. Every month my father went to Europe for a week or so and on the days he left, sorrow and emptiness consumed me: Daddy was leaving. Then, I turned to focus on a mysterious weakness—a helpless childlike emotion that came from starving. I liked to know that I needed to be taken care of; maybe Daddy would take care of me.

Now, two years later and thirty-eight pounds heavier, I have come to realize that I cannot alter my father’s inability to express his feelings. Instead, I must accept myself. I know that I am a valuable person who strives to achieve and accomplish. But I cannot strive solely for others. By starving, I attempted to gain pride in myself by obtaining my father’s approval or acknowledgment of my value as a person. But the primary approval must come from me, and I feel secure now that I can live with that knowledge safely locked in my mind.

閱讀測驗.title: 非洲族群分裂與衝突（African Ethnic Divisions and Conflicts）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Africa is a land of many ethnic groups, but when Europeans carved Africa into colonies, they gave no consideration to the territories of African ethnic groups. Some borderlines were drawn that split same groups into different colonies. Other borders threw different groups together. Sometimes the groups thrown together were enemies.

When the colonies became independent nations, these same borderlines were often maintained. Today, the Somali people remain split among Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Djibouti. On the other hand, almost every African nation is home to more than one ethnic group. In Nigeria, for example, live the Hausa, the Fulani, the Yoruba, the Ibo, and many smaller groups.

Conflicts have arisen over the way in which ethnic groups were split apart and thrown together. For example, a war between Somalia and Ethiopia was fought because Somalis wanted all their people to be a part of one nation. A civil war in Nigeria, on the other hand, was triggered partly by conflicts between ethnic groups within that nation. Similar conflicts between ethnic groups arose in Chad, Zaire, and Burundi as well. One principal goal among African nations today, therefore, is to help make it possible for their many ethnic groups to live together in peace.

items.stem: What happened to the territorial lines drawn in Africa by the Europeans?
options: They disappeared as the Europeans no longer ruled the colonies.
They were respected by different ethnic groups.

items.stem: What does the author think to be a reason for conflicts among the Africans?
options: Most ethnic groups have established their own countries.

閱讀測驗.title: 保險公司寫給「無所事事協會」的信（An Insurance Company’s Letter to the Institute of Not Doing Much）
閱讀測驗.passage:
To Whom It May Concern:

Your address was forwarded to us by Why Bother Magazine. All of us here think The International Institute of Not Doing Much is the best organization in the world. You know how to avoid unnecessary activities!

We closely followed the advice in your article. First, we replaced all our telephones with carrier pigeons. Simply removing the jingle of telephones and replacing them with the pleasant sounds of birds has had a remarkable effect on everyone. Besides, birds are cheaper than telephone service. After all, we are a business. We have to think of the bottom line. As a side benefit, the birds also fertilize the lawn outside the new employee sauna.

Next, we sold the computers off to Stab, Grab, Grit, and Nasty, a firm of lawyers nearby. Our electricity bill went way down. Big savings! The boss is impressed. We have completely embraced paper technology. Now that we all use pencils, doodling is on the increase, and the quality of pencilwomanship is impressive, as you can tell from my handwriting in this letter. By the way, if you can, please send this letter back to us. We can erase and reuse it. Just tie it to Maggie’s leg and she’ll know where to take it.

Now it’s very calm and quiet here. You can notice the difference. No more loud chatter on the telephones! All we hear is the scratching of pencil on paper, the sound of pigeons, and the delivery of inter-office correspondence by paper airplane.

Wonderful! I’ve always wanted to work for an insurance company ever since I was a little girl. Now it’s perfect.

Sincerely yours,
Eleanor Lightly
Spokeswoman and Company Hair Stylist
ABC Activity Insurance: Insure against overdoing it
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
敬啟者：

《Why Bother》雜誌把你們的地址轉給了我們。我們這裡的每個人都認為，國際無所事事協會是全世界最好的組織。你們真懂得怎麼避開不必要的活動！

我們完全照著你們文章裡的建議做。首先，我們把所有的電話都換成了信鴿。光是去掉電話鈴聲、換成悅耳的鳥叫聲，對每個人就有了驚人的效果。而且，養鳥比電話費便宜。畢竟我們是做生意的，得考慮最後的盈虧。還有一個額外的好處：這些鳥也替員工新三溫暖外面的草坪施了肥。

接著，我們把電腦賣給附近一家律師事務所 Stab, Grab, Grit, and Nasty。我們的電費大幅下降，省了一大筆錢！老闆很滿意。我們已經全面擁抱紙張技術。現在大家都用鉛筆，隨手塗鴉的情形越來越多，鉛筆字的水準也令人刮目相看，從我這封信的字跡就看得出來。對了，如果可以的話，請把這封信寄回來給我們，我們可以擦掉再用。只要把信綁在 Maggie 的腳上，她就知道要送到哪裡。

現在這裡非常平靜、安靜，你可以感覺到不同。電話裡再也沒有大聲的閒聊了！我們只聽得到鉛筆在紙上沙沙的聲音、鴿子的聲音，還有用紙飛機遞送公司內部信件的聲音。

太美好了！我從小就一直想在保險公司上班，現在一切都完美了。

敬上

Eleanor Lightly

發言人兼公司髮型師

第 4 段說把信綁在 Maggie 的腳上，她就知道要送到哪裡，可見 Maggie 是一隻送信的鴿子；第 3 段說這些鳥也替員工三溫暖外面的草坪施肥（fertilize the lawn），所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄第 5 段的 inter-office correspondence，公司內部的信件是用紙飛機傳的，而且公司已經賣掉電腦，不會用電子郵件；(D) 照抄 handwriting，字跡讓人刮目相看的是寫信的 Eleanor；(A) Maggie 是鴿子，不是經理。

閱讀測驗.title: 加拉巴哥群島的綠色機場（The Green Airport of the Galápagos Islands）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The Galápagos Islands are the Pacific island paradise where Darwin’s theory of evolution was born. They are places filled with giant tree lizards, sandy beaches, and tropical plants. Now they will be famous for one more thing: the world’s first green airport.

This group of islands off the coast of Ecuador has recently contracted Argentine Corporación America to manage the redevelopment of the airport on the island of Baltra. It is estimated that US$20 million is needed to complete the project by 2009. The new development has several important features: use of wind and solar energy, passive heating and cooling systems, as well as concrete runways in place of asphalt, which has a greater carbon footprint during its production cycle. This new development couldn’t be coming at a better time for the Galápagos, which were added to an environmental “danger list” in 2007.

Pacific islands like the Galápagos, Easter Island, and Tahiti, have economies that are driven almost completely by tourism. However, some people think these are “unsustainable models of development.” The number of visitors to the Galápagos rose more than 250% from 1990 to 2006, while the number of commercial flights to the area rose 193% from 2001 to 2006. These increases put great stress on the islands’ resources and environment. Air travel is especially criticized for exhausting natural resources and causing environmental damage. Thus, efforts are being made to reduce the environmental impact of the tourism industry. The greening of airports is just one of these attempts.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
加拉巴哥群島是太平洋上的島嶼天堂，達爾文的演化論就在這裡誕生。這裡有巨大的樹蜥、沙灘和熱帶植物。現在，這些島嶼又要以另一件事聞名：世界上第一座綠色機場。

這個位於厄瓜多外海的群島，最近和阿根廷的 Corporación America 公司簽約，委託這家公司負責巴爾特拉島上機場的重建。估計需要 2,000 萬美元，才能在 2009 年以前完成這項工程。新的建設有幾個重要的特點：使用風能和太陽能、不靠機械設備、利用自然通風和日照的冷暖系統，還有用混凝土跑道取代柏油跑道，因為柏油在生產過程中的碳足跡比較大。加拉巴哥群島在 2007 年列入環境「危險名單」，這項新建設來得正是時候。

像加拉巴哥群島、復活節島和大溪地這些太平洋島嶼，經濟幾乎完全靠觀光帶動。然而，有些人認為這是「無法永續的發展模式」。從 1990 年到 2006 年，到加拉巴哥群島的遊客人數增加了 250% 以上，而從 2001 年到 2006 年，飛往當地的商業航班也增加了 193%。這些增加讓島上的資源和環境承受很大的壓力。航空旅行尤其受到批評，因為它耗盡自然資源，又造成環境破壞。因此，大家正努力減少觀光業對環境的衝擊，機場綠化只是其中一項嘗試。

items.stem: What is this article mainly about?
options: The background of building a green airport.
The history of the Galápagos Islands.
The ease of transportation to the Pacific islands.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說加拉巴哥群島將以世界第一座綠色機場聞名；第 2 段介紹機場重建的工程和特點，並說群島在 2007 年列入環境危險名單；第 3 段說遊客和航班大增，讓島上的環境承受壓力，機場綠化是減少衝擊的一項努力。全文在說蓋綠色機場的來龍去脈，所以是 (B)。(C) 群島的歷史太過廣泛，文章只談機場和觀光帶來的環境問題；(A) 第 1 段提到達爾文的演化論在這裡誕生，只是介紹群島，文章沒有談演化論的問題，偏離主題；(D) 文章談的是航空旅行對環境的傷害，不是去太平洋島嶼的交通有多方便，也偏離主題。

items.stem: Where will the world’s first green airport be built?
items.explanation:
has recently contracted Argentine Corporación America to manage the redevelopment of the airport on the island of Baltra.
第 1 段說加拉巴哥群島會有世界第一座綠色機場，第 2 段接著說要重建的是巴爾特拉島（Baltra）上的機場，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 Argentine，阿根廷是承包工程的公司所在的國家，不是機場的地點；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 Tahiti，大溪地是和加拉巴哥群島並列、靠觀光維生的太平洋島嶼；(D) 原文的 US$ 是說經費用美元計算，不是蓋在美國。

items.stem: What is true about the Galápagos Islands?
options: They are located near Ecuador in the Pacific Ocean.
They have had a great increase in population since 2001.
They will invest US$20 million to promote their tourism.
They have become one of the most dangerous places in the world.
items.explanation:
This group of islands off the coast of Ecuador
第 1 段說加拉巴哥群島在太平洋上，第 2 段說群島位於厄瓜多外海（off the coast of Ecuador），選項換成 located near Ecuador in the Pacific Ocean，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 3 段的 2001，2001 到 2006 年增加的是飛往當地的商業航班，原文沒有提到人口；(C) 照抄 US$20 million，那是重建機場的經費，不是推廣觀光；(D) 照抄 danger，群島列入的是環境「危險名單」，意思是環境岌岌可危，不是說那裡是全世界最危險的地方。

items.stem: What does the project in the second paragraph refer to?
options: The plan to build a green airport.
The research on the production of solar energy.
The task of calculating a carbon footprint.
The study on the exhaustion of natural resources.
items.explanation:
has recently contracted Argentine Corporación America to manage the redevelopment of the airport on the island of Baltra.
It is estimated that US$20 million is needed to complete the project by 2009.
第 2 段前一句說群島委託公司重建巴爾特拉島上的機場，接著說要 2,000 萬美元才能在 2009 年前完成 the project，所以 the project 指的就是重建機場，也就是第 1 段說的世界第一座綠色機場，答案是 (A)。(B) 照抄 solar energy，使用太陽能只是新機場的特點之一，不是研究太陽能的生產；(C) 照抄 carbon footprint，碳足跡是說明為什麼不用柏油，不是要計算碳足跡；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 natural resources，耗盡自然資源是航空旅行受到的批評。

閱讀測驗.title: 牛隻對地磁場的感知能力研究（Study on Cattle's Perception of Earth's Magnetic Fields）
閱讀測驗.passage:
According to popular folklore, many animals are smarter than they appear. Dogs bark before earthquakes; cattle predict rainfall by sitting on the ground. But cattle may have another hidden talent in telling which way is north.

Small animals such as mole rats living underground are known for the use of magnetism to navigate. Dr. Begall and her colleagues wanted to know whether larger mammals also have the ability to perceive magnetic fields. They investigated this possibility by studying images of thousands of cattle captured on Google Earth, a website that stitches together satellite photographs to produce an image of the Earth’s surface.

Grazing animals are known to orient themselves in a way that minimizes wind chill from the north and maximizes the warmth of the sun when they are cold. The researchers therefore had to study a lot of cows grazing in lots of different places at different times of day, in order to average out these factors and see whether cattle could act like compass needles.

The researchers concluded that cattle do generally orient themselves in a north-south direction. This north-south preference has also been noted in flies, termites and honeybees. But unfortunately, even the high resolution of Google Earth is not powerful enough to tell which end of the cow is its head, and which its tail. The researchers were therefore unable to answer their research questions of whether cattle prefer to look north or south, and whether that differs in the northern and southern hemispheres.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
根據民間流傳的說法，很多動物比牠們看起來還要聰明。狗會在地震前吠叫；牛坐在地上，就是預告要下雨了。不過，牛可能還有另一項隱藏的本領：分辨哪個方向是北方。

大家都知道，像鼴鼠這類住在地底下的小動物，會利用磁性來辨認方向。Begall 博士和她的同事想知道，比較大的哺乳動物是不是也能感知磁場。他們研究了 Google Earth 上拍到的幾千頭牛的影像，來探究這個可能性。Google Earth 是一個把衛星照片拼接起來、呈現地球表面影像的網站。

大家知道，吃草的動物覺得冷的時候，站的方向會盡量減少北邊吹來的冷風，並盡量多曬一點太陽。因此研究人員必須研究在許多不同地方、一天裡不同時間吃草的大量牛隻，把這些因素平均掉，才能看出牛是不是能像指南針的指針一樣。

研究人員的結論是，牛確實大致朝南北方向站。蒼蠅、白蟻和蜜蜂身上也觀察到這種偏好南北方向的現象。可惜的是，即使 Google Earth 的解析度很高，還是不足以分辨牛的哪一端是頭、哪一端是尾巴。所以研究人員沒辦法回答他們的研究問題：牛比較喜歡面向北方還是南方？在北半球和南半球是不是不一樣？

items.stem: What is the article mainly about?
options: Whether cattle are superior to other animals.
Whether cattle behave like compass needles.
items.explanation: 第 1 段提出牛可能有分辨北方的本領；第 2 段說 Begall 博士想知道大型哺乳動物能不能感知磁場；第 3 段說研究人員要排除風和陽光的影響，看牛能不能像指南針的指針；第 4 段說結論是牛大致朝南北方向站。全文在探討牛是不是像指南針，所以是 (D)。(C) 狗在地震前吠叫只是第 1 段開頭的民間說法，過於狹隘；(A) Google Earth 只是研究的工具，第 4 段還說它的解析度不夠，偏離主題；(B) 文章沒有比較牛和其他動物誰比較聰明，也偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following factors might affect Dr. Begall’s research result?
items.explanation:
Grazing animals are known to orient themselves in a way that minimizes wind chill from the north and maximizes the warmth of the sun when they are cold.
The researchers therefore had to study a lot of cows grazing in lots of different places at different times of day, in order to average out these factors and see whether cattle could act like compass needles.
第 3 段說吃草的動物冷的時候會調整站的方向，避開北風、多曬太陽，所以研究人員必須研究許多不同地方（different places）、不同時間的牛，把這些因素平均掉。可見牛所在的地點會影響研究結果，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 rainfall、(B) 照抄第 1 段的 earthquakes，那是民間說法裡動物能預知的事，和這項研究無關；(D) 研究經費，原文沒有提到。

items.stem: What is the major finding of Dr. Begall’s study?
options: Google Earth is a reliable research tool.
items.explanation:
The researchers concluded that cattle do generally orient themselves in a north-south direction.
第 4 段說研究人員的結論是牛大致朝南北方向站（orient themselves in a north-south direction），選項換成 Cattle point north-south，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 prefer to look，牛比較喜歡面向北方還是南方，正是研究人員沒辦法回答的問題；(D) 照抄 Google Earth，第 4 段說它的解析度不夠，分不出牛頭牛尾；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 magnetism，研究正是用科學方法探討動物能不能感知磁場。

items.stem: Why couldn’t the researchers get the answer to their research questions?
options: Many cattle in their study were sitting on the ground.
The cattle constantly change directions to avoid wind chill.
There is magnetic difference between the two hemispheres.
They couldn’t tell a cow’s head from its tail in the satellite pictures.
items.explanation:
But unfortunately, even the high resolution of Google Earth is not powerful enough to tell which end of the cow is its head, and which its tail.
第 4 段說 Google Earth 的解析度不夠，分不出牛的哪一端是頭、哪一端是尾巴（not powerful enough to tell which end of the cow is its head），選項換成 couldn’t tell a cow’s head from its tail，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 hemispheres，南北半球有沒有差別是研究人員想回答的問題，不是回答不了的原因；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 wind chill，牛會避開冷風，研究人員已經用大量樣本把這個因素平均掉；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 sitting on the ground，牛坐在地上預告下雨是民間說法。

閱讀測驗.title: 父母如何幫助孩子養成健康飲食習慣（How Parents Can Help Children Develop Healthy Eating Habits）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Children normally have a distrust of new foods. But it’s the parents’ job to serve a variety of foods and expose their children to healthy dieting habits.

Some simple strategies can help even the pickiest eater learn to like a more varied diet. First of all, you don’t have to send children out of the kitchen. With hot stoves, boiling water and sharp knives at hand, it is understandable that parents don’t want children in the kitchen when they’re making dinner. But studies suggest that involving children in meal preparation is an important first step in getting them to try new foods. In one study, nearly 600 children from kindergarten to sixth grade took part in a nutrition curriculum intended to get them to eat more vegetables and whole grains. The researchers found that children who had cooked their own foods were more likely to eat those foods in the cafeteria than children who had not. Kids don’t usually like radishes, but if kids cut them up and put them in the salad, they will love the dish.

Another strategy is not to diet in front of your children. Kids are tuned into their parents’ eating preferences and are far more likely to try foods if they see their mother or father eating them. Given this powerful effect, parents who are trying to lose weight should be careful of how their dieting habits can influence a child’s perceptions about food and healthful eating. In one study of 5-year-old girls about dieting, one child noted that dieting involved drinking chocolate milkshakes, because her mother was using Slim-Fast drinks. Another child said dieting meant “you fix food but you don’t eat it.” By exposing young children to erratic dieting habits, parents may be putting them at risk for eating disorders.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
孩子對新的食物通常抱著不信任的態度。但是準備各種食物、讓孩子接觸健康的飲食習慣，是父母的責任。

有一些簡單的策略，連最挑食的孩子都能慢慢喜歡更多樣的飲食。首先，你不必把孩子趕出廚房。廚房裡有熱騰騰的爐子、滾燙的開水和鋒利的刀子，父母做晚餐時不想讓孩子待在廚房，是可以理解的。不過研究顯示，讓孩子參與準備餐點，是讓他們嘗試新食物重要的第一步。在一項研究中，將近 600 名從幼稚園到六年級的孩子參加了一套營養課程，目的是讓他們多吃蔬菜和全穀類。研究人員發現，自己做過菜的孩子，在學校餐廳吃這些食物的可能性，比沒做過的孩子高。孩子通常不喜歡蘿蔔，但是如果讓他們自己把蘿蔔切好放進沙拉裡，他們就會愛上這道菜。

另一個策略是不要在孩子面前節食。孩子很注意父母喜歡吃什麼，如果看到爸爸或媽媽吃某種食物，他們願意嘗試的可能性就高得多。既然影響這麼大，正在減肥的父母就應該留意，自己的節食習慣會怎麼影響孩子對食物和健康飲食的看法。在一項以 5 歲女孩為對象、關於節食的研究中，有個孩子說節食就是喝巧克力奶昔，因為她媽媽在喝 Slim-Fast 飲品。另一個孩子說，節食的意思是「你做了飯，可是不吃」。父母讓年幼的孩子接觸這些反覆無常的節食習慣，可能會讓孩子面臨飲食失調的風險。

items.stem: What is the main purpose of this article?
options: To explain what causes children’s eating disorder.
To teach children about the meal preparation process.
To advocate the importance of vegetables and whole grains.
To inform parents how they can help their children like varied foods.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說讓孩子接觸各種食物是父母的責任；第 2 段提出第一個策略：讓孩子參與準備餐點；第 3 段提出另一個策略：不要在孩子面前節食。全文在告訴父母怎麼幫孩子喜歡多樣的食物，所以是 (D)。三個錯誤選項都過於狹隘：(A) 飲食失調只在第 3 段最後一句提到；(B) 準備餐點是第 2 段的策略，而且文章是寫給父母看的，不是教孩子；(C) 蔬菜和全穀類是第 2 段那項研究的營養課程內容。

items.stem: Which of the following groups will eat more balanced meals?
options: The children who help cook food.
The children whose parents are on a diet.
The children who do not love radishes.
The children whose parents work in a cafeteria.
items.explanation:
The researchers found that children who had cooked their own foods were more likely to eat those foods in the cafeteria than children who had not.
第 2 段說自己做過菜（cooked their own foods）的孩子，在學校餐廳吃這些食物的可能性比較高，選項換成 The children who help cook food，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 cafeteria，原文的 cafeteria 是孩子吃飯的學校餐廳，不是父母工作的地方；(C) 照抄 radishes，原文說孩子不喜歡蘿蔔，但自己切了就會愛吃，重點在自己動手；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 diet，父母在孩子面前節食，反而可能讓孩子有飲食失調的風險。

items.stem: What does erratic in the last sentence imply?
items.explanation:
Another child said dieting meant “you fix food but you don’t eat it.”
By exposing young children to erratic dieting habits, parents may be putting them at risk for eating disorders.
erratic 本身是「反覆無常、沒有規律」的意思。第 3 段舉的例子：孩子以為節食就是喝巧克力奶昔，或是做了飯卻不吃，可見父母的節食方式讓孩子對飲食有錯誤的認識；最後一句又說這會讓孩子有飲食失調的風險。這裡的 erratic 是負面的意思，四個選項中最接近的是 (D) 不恰當的。(B) 照抄 healthful，前面說父母要留意節食習慣會影響孩子對健康飲食的看法，erratic 的意思正好相反；(A) 明顯的、(C) 不誠實的，和上下文接不上。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about Slim-Fast?
options: It looks like a chocolate milkshake.
It contains a variety of vegetables.
It is intended for slim, fast people.
items.explanation:
In one study of 5-year-old girls about dieting, one child noted that dieting involved drinking chocolate milkshakes, because her mother was using Slim-Fast drinks.
第 3 段說有個 5 歲女孩以為節食就是喝巧克力奶昔（chocolate milkshakes），因為她媽媽在喝 Slim-Fast 飲品。可見 Slim-Fast 是減肥時喝的飲品，看起來像巧克力奶昔，孩子才會弄錯，所以是 (B)。(D) 從產品名字的字面去猜，Slim-Fast 是給想減肥的人喝的，不是給又瘦又快的人；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 a variety of，那是說父母要準備各種食物；(A) 原文沒說孩子喜歡喝。

閱讀測驗.title: 女兒帶去上班日：賦權女性與性別平等（Take Our Daughters to Work Day: Empowering Women and Gender Equality）
閱讀測驗.passage:
April 22, 2010 will be the 18th celebration of the annual Take Our Daughters to Work Day (TOD), a project the National Ms. Foundation for Women of America (NFW) developed to expose girls to expanding opportunities for women in the workplace.

The program offers millions of girls a first-hand view of the many career opportunities available in their futures. Now that women make up 46 percent of the U.S. workforce, girls can find role models in every occupational field—from politics to molecular biology to professional athletics, to name just a few. TOD encourages girls to focus on their abilities and opportunities, not just their appearance.

The NFW developed the project more than a decade ago to address the self-esteem problems that many girls experience when they enter adolescence. At school, boys often receive more encouragement in the classroom, especially in math, science and computer science, the academic fields that tend to lead to the highest salaries. Women receive on average only 73 cents for every dollar that men are paid, and remain vastly underrepresented in top executive positions and technology fields. TOD aims to give girls the confidence and inspiration they need to develop successful careers, particularly in non-traditional fields.

Perhaps because the program had become so widespread and successful, TOD had been criticized for excluding boys, and it was expanded in 2003 to include boys. The program’s official website states that the program was changed in order to provide both boys and girls with opportunities to explore careers at an age when they are more flexible in terms of gender stereotyped roles. “We should also show boys that becoming a child care provider is as acceptable a choice as becoming a police officer or CEO,” added Sara K. Gould, executive director of the NFW.

閱讀測驗.title: 頭髮的歷史與象徵意義（Historical and Symbolic Meanings of Hair）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In all cultures and throughout history hair has had a special significance. In ancient Egypt, as long ago as 1500 BC, the outward appearance expressed the person’s status, role in society and political position. Wigs played an important role in this: they were crafted with great artistry and often sprinkled with powdered gold.

In the 8th century BC, the pre-Roman Celts in Northern Europe wore their hair long. In a man it was the expression of his strength, in a woman of her fertility. The idea of long hair as a symbol of male strength is even mentioned in the Bible, in the story of Samson and Delilah. Samson was a leader of the Israelites. His long hair, which he never cut, gave him superhuman powers. The only person who knew his secret was Delilah. However, she spied for the enemy and betrayed him. One night she cut off his hair and thus robbed him of his strength.

In the classical Greek period, curly hair was not only the fashion, but it also represented an attitude towards life. Curls or locks were the metaphor for change, freedom and the joy of living. The ancient Greek word for curls and locks is related to intriguing and tempting someone.

Hair is also used as a symbol of opposition. The punk protest movement today uses hair as a symbol of disapproval of the “middle-class, conventional lifestyle” by wearing provocative haircuts and shockingly colored hair. A different form of objection could be seen in the women’s hairstyles in the 1960s. Women’s liberation was expressed in a short-cut, straight and simple hairstyle which underlined equality with men without neglecting female attributes. To this day hair has kept its importance as a symbol of power, youth, vitality and health.

閱讀測驗.title: 兒童志願服務的意義與影響（The Significance and Impact of Child Volunteering）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Camille Mahlknecht, 9, has some big fun planned for this weekend. She and other residents of Agoura Hills, California, plan to pick up trash during their city’s annual cleanup. At the same time, Wissam Raed, 12, will be busy volunteering too. Thousands of miles away in Lebanon, Wissam plans to put on a play at an orphanage and bring potted plants to elderly people at a senior citizen center.

Some other children like Nathan White, 10, have personal reasons for volunteering. Nathan’s grandmother died of a heart attack. To help raise money for medical research, Nathan participated in Jump Rope for Heart. He and five other boys took turns jumping rope for two and half hours and collected more than US$1,200 in donations for the American Heart Association.

Millions of children around the globe lend a hand to their communities every year. Schools and parents also contribute to the rise in youth service. For example, many schools offer community service activities for students to join. Teachers either combine volunteer work with classroom lessons or make service work a requirement. Parents, on the other hand, encourage their kids to volunteer and do it with them.

Community service is particularly important in this recession time. As the need for monetary support and other aid has increased, many charitable organizations have experienced a significant drop in donations. Camille and other children who volunteer thousands of hours annually can fill in some of the gaps.

According to research, kids who start volunteering are twice as likely to continue doing good deeds when they are adults. So, grab a paintbrush, a trash bag, or whatever you need to help your community. You’ll love how you feel after helping others. Even dirty work can be lots of fun, if it’s for a good cause.

閱讀測驗.title: 網路非法音樂下載的問題與後果（The Problem and Consequences of Illegal Online Music Downloading）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Downloading music over the Internet is pretty common among high school and college students. However, when students download and share copyrighted music without permission, they are violating the law.

A survey of young people’s music ownership has found that teenagers and college students have an average of more than 800 illegally copied songs each on their digital music players. Half of those surveyed share all the music on their hard drive, enabling others to copy hundreds of songs at any one time. Some students were found to have randomly linked their personal blogs to music sites, so as to allow free trial listening of copyrighted songs for blog visitors, or adopted some of the songs as the background music for their blogs. Such practices may be easy and free, but there are consequences.

Sandra Dowd, a student of Central Michigan University, was fined US$7,500 for downloading 501 files from LimeWire, a peer-to-peer file sharing program. Sandra claimed that she was unaware that her downloads were illegal until she was contacted by authorities. Similarly, Mike Lewinski paid US$4,000 to settle a lawsuit against him for copyright violation. Mike expressed shock and couldn’t believe that this was happening to him. “I just wanted to save some money and I always thought the threat was just a scare tactic.” “You know, everyone does it,” added Mike.

The RIAA (Recording Industry Association of America), the organization that files lawsuits against illegal downloaders, states that suing students was by no means their first choice. Unfortunately, without the threat of consequences, students are just not changing their behavior. Education alone is not enough to stop the extraordinary growth of the illegal downloading practice.

They are against copyright protection over Internet music.

They think that illegal downloading behavior needs tough measures to correct.

閱讀測驗.title: 陶笛的歷史與文化（The History and Culture of the Ocarina）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The ocarina, a flute-like musical instrument, has been around since the Stone Age. Ocarinas have been found in Africa, Asia, Europe, and South America. Most of those found were made from clay while some were made of bone, wood, and other materials. Because they produce sounds similar to bird calls, ocarinas have been credited with magical powers.

One variation of the ocarina in Chinese culture is the xun, which has a history of more than 7,000 years. It is made of earthenware clay and often comes in the shape of an egg. At various times in Chinese music history, the instrument has played an important role in the imperial orchestra for religious worship and palace entertainment.

Ocarinas were also found to serve various purposes in other cultures. For example, the Mayans of South America, like the Chinese, also used ocarinas for special ceremonies. From there European travelers brought this South American “whistle” back, and it was later modified to play the Western scale. In the 1800s, Italy saw the greatest development of the ocarina, where musicians formed groups to play ocarinas of various sizes. During World War II the ocarina was introduced to the United States and playing it became a pastime for soldiers.

In the 20th century, the ocarina was popular among the general public, and the application of ocarina music was extended to video games. In 1999, Nintendo released Zelda: the Ocarina of Time, the most popular video game of all time. The game features a character named Link who plays songs on an ocarina in order to go to different areas of the game.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
陶笛是一種類似長笛的樂器，從石器時代就已經存在。非洲、亞洲、歐洲和南美洲都發現過陶笛。發現的陶笛大多是用黏土做的，也有一些是用骨頭、木頭和其他材料做成。陶笛發出的聲音很像鳥叫，所以人們認為陶笛有神奇的魔力。

陶笛在中國文化裡的一種變化型是塤，有七千多年的歷史。塤是用陶土燒製而成，常常做成蛋的形狀。在中國音樂史上的不同時期，塤曾經在宮廷樂隊裡扮演重要的角色，用於宗教祭祀和宮廷娛樂。

在其他文化裡，陶笛也有各種用途。例如南美洲的馬雅人和中國人一樣，也在特殊的儀式上使用陶笛。後來歐洲的旅人把這種南美洲的「哨子」帶回歐洲，經過改良，陶笛就能吹奏西方音階。1800 年代，陶笛在義大利發展得最好，樂手組成樂團，吹奏各種尺寸的陶笛。第二次世界大戰期間，陶笛傳入美國，吹陶笛成為士兵的消遣。

二十世紀時，陶笛在一般大眾之間很受歡迎，陶笛音樂的應用也延伸到電玩遊戲。1999 年，任天堂推出《薩爾達傳說：時之笛》，這是有史以來最受歡迎的電玩遊戲。遊戲裡有一個叫做 Link 的角色，他用陶笛吹奏樂曲，好前往遊戲裡的不同區域。

items.stem: Which of the following titles best describes the passage?
items.explanation: 第 1 段說陶笛從石器時代就存在；第 2 段講中國的塤；第 3 段講陶笛從馬雅人傳到歐洲、在義大利發展、二戰時傳入美國；第 4 段講二十世紀陶笛音樂延伸到電玩。全文依時間講陶笛的歷史，所以是 (A)。(B) 製作陶笛的材料只在第 1 段帶到；(C) 亞洲和歐洲只是第 2、3 段的一部分，文章還談到南美洲和美國；(D) 任天堂的遊戲只在第 4 段舉例，陶笛也不是任天堂的產品；三個選項都過於狹隘。

閱讀測驗.title: 加拿大、法國與義大利的親子關係研究（Parent-Child Bonds in Canada, France, and Italy Study）
閱讀測驗.passage:
A recent study examined the emotional bond between parents and their children. The researchers surveyed 1,256 students in Canada, France, and Italy. Professor Michel Claes, the leader of the research team, explained why they selected the three countries: “We chose French-Canadians because they share the same language as the French, and originally came from France. They share certain values. Italy was included because it was considered to have similar, strong, important family values.”

The most important finding of the study was the difference between Canadians and the others. Canadian parents value independence and are more willing to enter discussions with their children when there are disagreements. They are more tolerant and exercise less control. In contrast, Italian parents are stricter and more demanding. French parents are somewhere in the middle. In other words, Canadian parents are more lenient with their children than parents in France and Italy. Professor Claes explained the finding in terms of differences in education. “North America has its own democratic and educational values, which promote individualization. Tolerance and comprehension are encouraged and we exclude systems of control. Italy, on the other hand, promotes the respect of authority, control, and the need for permission,” he said.

Children from all three countries described their mothers as warm and open. Italian and Canadian children had similar feelings about their fathers and reported high levels of emotional bonding. But French fathers were seen by their children as being more distant. It seemed that the relationships of French mothers with their children were becoming closer over time; but fathers maintained a certain distance and coldness.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
最近一項研究探討父母和子女之間的情感連結。研究人員調查了加拿大、法國和義大利的 1,256 名學生。研究團隊的負責人 Michel Claes 教授說明他們選擇這三個國家的原因：「我們選擇法裔加拿大人，因為他們和法國人說同一種語言，祖先也來自法國，兩者有某些共同的價值觀。納入義大利，則是因為大家認為義大利也有類似的、強烈而重要的家庭價值觀。」

這項研究最重要的發現，是加拿大人和其他兩國的差異。加拿大的父母重視獨立，和子女意見不合時，比較願意和子女討論。加拿大的父母比較寬容，管得比較少。相反地，義大利的父母比較嚴格，要求也比較多。法國的父母則介於兩者之間。換句話說，加拿大的父母對子女比法國和義大利的父母寬鬆。Claes 教授從教育的差異解釋這項發現：「北美洲有自己的民主價值觀和教育價值觀，鼓勵個人化。我們鼓勵寬容和理解，排除控制的體系。另一方面，義大利重視尊重權威、控制，以及凡事要先得到允許。」

三個國家的子女都形容自己的母親溫暖、開放。義大利和加拿大的子女對父親的感覺相似，都表示和父親的情感連結很深。但是在法國子女眼中，父親比較疏遠。看起來法國母親和子女的關係隨著時間越來越親近，父親卻一直保持某種距離，態度冷淡。

items.stem: According to the passage, why were Canada, France, and Italy chosen for the study?
options: Because the ancestors of many Canadians came from Europe.
Because the languages of the three countries have a common origin.
Because the three countries are believed to have similar family values.

items.explanation:
They share certain values.
Italy was included because it was considered to have similar, strong, important family values.
第 1 段 Claes 教授說，法裔加拿大人和法國人有某些共同的價值觀；納入義大利，是因為大家認為義大利也有類似的家庭價值觀（similar, strong, important family values），三國的共同點就是選項說的 similar family values。(A) 照抄 came from，原文說的是法裔加拿大人的祖先來自法國，這只是選加拿大和法國的一部分理由，也沒說到義大利；(B) 照抄 language，說同一種語言的只有法裔加拿大人和法國人，義大利不在內；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 educational，教育價值觀是教授用來解釋加拿大和義大利不同的地方，正好相反。

items.stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?

Canadian parents value independence and are more willing to enter discussions with their children when there are disagreements.
In contrast, Italian parents are stricter and more demanding.
French parents are somewhere in the middle.
第 2 段比較三國父母怎麼對待子女：加拿大的父母重視獨立、比較寬容，義大利的父母比較嚴格、要求比較多，法國介於兩者之間。這些都是父母管教子女的方式，所以是 (D) 教養方式。(C) 段末教授用教育價值觀解釋差異，那是在說明原因，不是這一段的重點；(A) 家庭結構、(B) 社會習俗，這一段都沒談。

items.stem: Which of the following does “we” in the second paragraph most likely refer to?

Tolerance and comprehension are encouraged and we exclude systems of control.
第 2 段 Claes 教授說北美洲的價值觀鼓勵個人化，接著說 we 鼓勵寬容和理解、排除控制的體系；這和同一段前面說的加拿大父母一致：重視獨立、比較寬容、管得比較少。所以 we 指的是 (A) 加拿大的父母。(B) 義大利的父母正好相反，教授接著說義大利重視權威和控制；(C) 和 (D) 是子女，排除控制、鼓勵寬容的是管教子女的父母。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about the parents in the study?
options: Italian fathers are the coldest of all.
Canadian parents are both warm and open.
