items.explanation:
the threads of the web have to withstand the impact forces from large and heavy prey as well as environmental forces from wind and rain for at least a day in most cases.
題目問的是網絲（silk threads），答案在第 1 段：網絲必須承受獵物撞擊和風雨的力量，大多數情況下（in most cases）至少要維持一天（for at least a day）。選項把 in most cases 換成 usually，把承受得住、維持一天換成 strong enough to last for a day，所以是 (B)。(A) 的 all 是陷阱：第 2 段說蜘蛛網用了兩種絲，只有捕獵螺旋那一種有彈性、塗了黏液，另一種比較硬，不是全部的絲都會黏、都能拉長；(D) 第 2 段的植物（vegetation）是固定絲繫住的地方，蜘蛛絲是天然的複合材料，原文沒有說是用稀有植物做的；(C) 原文沒有提到去除昆蟲身上的化學物質。

閱讀測驗.title: 博士學位的發展與過剩問題（The Development and Oversupply of PhD Degrees）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Doctor of Philosophy, usually abbreviated as PhD or Ph.D., is an advanced academic degree awarded by universities. The first Doctor of Philosophy degree was awarded in Paris in 1150, but the degree did not acquire its modern status until the early 19th century. The doctorate of philosophy as it exists today originated at Humboldt University. The German practice was later adopted by American and Canadian universities, eventually becoming common in large parts of the world in the 20th century.

For most of history, even a bachelor’s degree at a university was the privilege of a rich few, and many academic staff did not hold doctorates. But as higher education expanded after the Second World War, the number of PhDs increased accordingly. American universities geared up first: By 1970, America was graduating half of the world’s PhDs in science and technology. Since then, America’s annual output of PhDs has doubled, to 64,000. Other countries are catching up. PhD production has sped up most dramatically in Mexico, Portugal, Italy, and Slovakia. Even Japan, where the number of young people is shrinking, has churned out about 46% more PhDs.

Researchers now warn that the supply of PhDs has far outstripped demand. America produced more than 100,000 doctoral degrees between 2005 and 2009, while there were just 16,000 new professorships. In research, the story is similar. Even graduates who find work outside universities may not fare all that well. Statistics show that five years after receiving their degrees, more than 60% of PhDs in Slovakia and more than 45% in Belgium, the Czech Republic, Germany, and Spain are still on temporary contracts. About one-third of Austria’s PhD graduates take jobs unrelated to their degrees.

Today, top universities around the world are still picking bright students and grooming them as potential PhDs. After all, it isn’t in their interests to turn the smart students away: The more bright students stay at universities, the better it is for academics. But considering the oversupply of PhDs, some people have already begun to wonder whether doing a PhD is a good choice for an individual.

items.stem: In which country did the modern practice of granting doctoral degrees start?
Which of the following words is closest in meaning to “churned out” in the second paragraph?
Which of the following may be inferred from the third paragraph?
options: PhD graduates in Austria are not encouraged to work outside university.
Most German PhDs work at permanent jobs immediately after graduation.
It is much easier for American PhD holders to find a teaching position than a research job.
It is more difficult for PhDs to get a permanent job five years after graduation in Slovakia than in Spain.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward the increase of PhDs in recent years?

閱讀測驗.title: 蘇格蘭裙（The Kilt）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The kilt is a skirt traditionally worn by Scottish men. It is a tailored garment that is wrapped around the wearer’s body at the waist starting from one side, around the front and back and across the front again to the opposite side. The overlapping layers in front are called “aprons.” Usually, the kilt covers the body from the waist down to just above the knees. A properly made kilt should not be so loose that the wearer can easily twist the kilt around the body, nor should it be so tight that it causes bulging of the fabric where it is buckled. Underwear may be worn as one prefers.

One of the most distinctive features of the kilt is the pattern of squares, or sett, it exhibits. The association of particular patterns with individual families can be traced back hundreds of years. Then in the Victorian era (19th century), weaving companies began to systematically record and formalize the system of setts for commercial purposes. Today there are also setts for States and Provinces, schools and universities, and general patterns that anybody can wear.

The kilt can be worn with accessories. On the front apron, there is often a kilt pin, topped with a small decorative family symbol. A small knife can be worn with the kilt too. It typically comes in a very wide variety, from fairly plain to quite elaborate silver- and jewel-ornamented designs. The kilt can also be worn with a sporran, which is the Gaelic word for pouch or purse.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
蘇格蘭裙是蘇格蘭男性傳統上穿的裙子。蘇格蘭裙是一件剪裁合身的衣服，從身體一側開始圍在腰部，繞過前面和後面，再橫過前面一次，到另一側為止。前面交疊的那幾層叫做「aprons」（前片）。蘇格蘭裙通常從腰部蓋到膝蓋上方一點。做得好的蘇格蘭裙不能鬆到穿的人能輕易把裙子在身上轉來轉去，也不能緊到扣環的地方布料鼓起來。裡面要不要穿內褲，全看個人喜好。

蘇格蘭裙最明顯的特色之一，是裙子上的方格圖案，也就是 sett。特定的圖案代表特定的家族，這種關聯可以追溯到幾百年前。後來到了維多利亞時代（十九世紀），紡織公司為了商業目的，開始有系統地記錄這些方格圖案，並且建立一套制度。現在也有代表州和省、學校和大學的方格圖案，還有任何人都能穿的一般圖案。

蘇格蘭裙可以搭配配件。前片上常常別著一根裙針，針頭有一個裝飾用的小型家族標誌。穿蘇格蘭裙也可以配戴一把小刀，小刀的樣式非常多，從相當簡單的，到用銀和寶石裝飾得很精緻的都有。蘇格蘭裙也可以搭配 sporran，這是蓋爾語，意思是小袋子或錢包。

items.stem: What’s the proper way of wearing the kilt?
options: It should be worn with underwear underneath it.
It should loosely fit on the body to be turned around.
It should be long enough to cover the wearer’s knees.
It should be wrapped across the front of the body two times.
items.explanation:
It is a tailored garment that is wrapped around the wearer’s body at the waist starting from one side, around the front and back and across the front again to the opposite side.
第 1 段說蘇格蘭裙從身體一側開始圍在腰部，繞過前面和後面，再橫過前面一次（across the front again），前面一共橫過兩次，選項換成 wrapped across the front of the body two times。另外三個選項都照抄第 1 段：(A) 照抄 underwear，原文說內褲穿不穿依個人喜好，不是一定要穿；(B) 照抄 loose，原文說裙子不能鬆到能在身上轉動，正好相反；(C) 照抄 knees，原文說裙子蓋到膝蓋上方一點，沒有蓋住膝蓋。

items.stem: Which of the following is a correct description about setts?
options: They were once symbols for different Scottish families.
They were established by the government for business purposes.
They represented different States and Provinces in the 19th century.
They used to come in one general pattern for all individuals and institutions.
items.explanation:
The association of particular patterns with individual families can be traced back hundreds of years.
第 2 段說特定的方格圖案代表特定的家族（individual families），這種關聯可以追溯到幾百年前，選項換成 symbols for different Scottish families。這一段依時間講了三件事，三個錯誤選項都把時間或主角接錯：(B) 照抄 purposes，為了商業目的整理圖案的是十九世紀的紡織公司，不是政府；(C) 照抄 States and Provinces，代表州和省的圖案是現在（Today）才有的，不是十九世紀；(D) 照抄 general pattern，任何人都能穿的一般圖案也是現在才有，以前並不是只有一種圖案。

items.stem: Which of the following items is NOT typically worn with the kilt for decoration?
items.explanation:
On the front apron, there is often a kilt pin, topped with a small decorative family symbol.
from fairly plain to quite elaborate silver- and jewel-ornamented designs.
The kilt can also be worn with a sporran, which is the Gaelic word for pouch or purse.
第 3 段提到的配件，選項換了說法：kilt pin 是 (A) 裙針；sporran 是蓋爾語的錢包，也就是 (B) purse；小刀可以用銀裝飾，就是 (D) 銀製小刀。apron 是第 1 段說的裙子前面交疊的那幾層，本身就是裙子的一部分，不是另外配戴的飾品，文章也沒提到紅寶石，所以選 (C)。

items.stem: What is the purpose of this passage?
options: To persuade men to wear kilts.
To compare a skirt with a kilt.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說明蘇格蘭裙的穿法和長度，第 2 段說明裙子上的方格圖案，第 3 段說明可以搭配的配件。全文都在介紹這件蘇格蘭傳統服裝，所以是 (A)。(B) 方格圖案只在第 2 段介紹，而且文章是說明，不是替某種圖案打廣告，過於狹隘；(C) 文章沒有勸男性穿蘇格蘭裙，(D) 也沒有拿一般的裙子和蘇格蘭裙比較，兩個選項都偏離主題。

閱讀測驗.title: 爵士歌手 Wesla Whitfield 的故事（The Story of Wesla Whitfield）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Wesla Whitfield, a famous jazz singer, has a unique style and life story, so I decided to see one of her performances and interview her for my column.

I went to a nightclub in New York and watched the stage lights go up. After the band played an introduction, Wesla Whitfield wheeled herself onstage in a wheelchair. As she sang, Whitfield’s voice was so powerful and soulful that everyone in the room forgot the wheelchair was even there.

At 57, Whitfield is small and pretty, witty and humble, persistent and philosophical. Raised in California, Whitfield began performing in public at age 18, when she took a job as a singing waitress at a pizza parlor. After studying classical music in college, she moved to San Francisco and went on to sing with the San Francisco Opera Chorus.

Walking home from rehearsal at age 29, she was caught in the midst of a random shooting that left her paralyzed from the waist down. I asked how she dealt with the realization that she’d never walk again, and she confessed that initially she didn’t want to face it. After a year of depression she tried to kill herself. She was then admitted to a hospital for treatment, where she was able to recover.

Whitfield said she came to understand that the only thing she had lost in this misfortunate event was the ability to walk. She still possessed her most valuable asset—her mind. Pointing to her head, she said, “Everything important is in here. The only real disability in life is losing your mind.” When I asked if she was angry about what she had lost, she admitted to being frustrated occasionally, “especially when everybody’s dancing, because I love to dance. But when that happens I just remove myself so I can focus instead on what I can do.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
Wesla Whitfield 是知名的爵士歌手，她的風格和人生故事都很獨特，所以我決定去看她的一場演出，並且為我的專欄採訪她。

我到紐約的一家夜總會，看著舞台燈光亮起。樂團演奏完前奏後，Wesla Whitfield 坐著輪椅，自己把輪椅推上台。她一開口唱歌，歌聲渾厚、充滿感情，全場的人都忘了輪椅的存在。

57 歲的 Whitfield 個子嬌小、長得漂亮，風趣又謙虛，堅毅又豁達。她在加州長大，18 歲開始公開演出，那時她在一家披薩店找到一份工作，當會唱歌的服務生。大學念古典音樂之後，她搬到舊金山，後來加入舊金山歌劇院合唱團演唱。

29 歲那年，她排練完走路回家，遇上一場隨機槍擊，從此腰部以下癱瘓。我問她得知自己再也不能走路時是怎麼面對的，她坦承一開始不想面對。憂鬱了一年之後，她企圖自殺。後來她住進醫院接受治療，在那裡才恢復過來。

Whitfield 說，她後來明白，在這場不幸的事件裡，她失去的只有走路的能力。她最寶貴的資產，也就是她的心智，依然還在。她指著自己的頭說：「重要的東西都在這裡。人生唯一真正的殘缺，是失去心智。」我問她會不會為失去的東西感到憤怒，她承認偶爾會覺得挫折，「尤其是大家都在跳舞的時候，因為我很愛跳舞。不過遇到這種時候，我就離開現場，好把心思放在我能做的事情上。」

items.stem: In which of the following places has Wesla Whitfield worked?
items.explanation:
when she took a job as a singing waitress at a pizza parlor.
第 3 段說 Whitfield 18 歲時在一家披薩店（pizza parlor）找到工作，當會唱歌的服務生，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 college，大學是她念古典音樂的地方，不是工作的地方；(B) 照抄第 4 段的 hospital，她是住院接受治療的病人；(D) 為專欄採訪她的是作者，文章沒說她在新聞機構工作過。

items.stem: What does “when that happens” mean in the last paragraph?
options: When Wesla is losing her mind.
When Wesla is singing on the stage.
When Wesla is going out in her wheelchair.
When Wesla is watching other people dancing.
items.explanation:
she admitted to being frustrated occasionally, “especially when everybody’s dancing, because I love to dance.
第 5 段 Whitfield 說她偶爾會覺得挫折，尤其是大家都在跳舞（everybody’s dancing）的時候，因為她很愛跳舞；緊接著說 when that happens，她就離開現場。that 指的就是前一句大家都在跳舞、她只能看的情況，選項換成 watching other people dancing。(A) 照抄 losing，原文說失去心智是人生唯一真正的殘缺，是她的看法，不是她遇到的情況；(B) 在台上唱歌、(C) 坐輪椅出門，都和她感到挫折的那一刻接不上。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about Wesla Whitfield’s physical disability?
options: It was caused by a traffic accident.
It made her sad and depressed at first.
It seriously affected her singing career.
It happened when she was a college student.
items.explanation:
she confessed that initially she didn’t want to face it.
After a year of depression she tried to kill herself.
第 4 段說 Whitfield 癱瘓後一開始不想面對，接著憂鬱（depression）了一年，選項換成 made her sad and depressed at first。(D) 照抄第 3 段的 college，她是 29 歲排練完走路回家時遇上槍擊，那時已經大學畢業、在歌劇院合唱團唱歌；(A) 原文說是隨機槍擊，不是車禍；(C) 第 2 段說她在台上的歌聲讓全場的人忘了輪椅的存在，歌唱事業並沒有受到嚴重影響。

items.stem: What advice would Wesla most likely give other disabled people?
options: Ignore what you have lost and make the best use of what you have.
Be modest and hard-working to earn respect from other people.
Acquire a skill so that you can still be successful and famous.
Try to sing whenever you feel upset and depressed.
items.explanation:
Whitfield said she came to understand that the only thing she had lost in this misfortunate event was the ability to walk.
But when that happens I just remove myself so I can focus instead on what I can do.
第 5 段 Whitfield 說她失去的只有走路的能力，最寶貴的心智還在；看到大家跳舞覺得挫折時，她就離開現場，把心思放在自己能做的事情上。不去想失去的，把握還擁有的，所以她最可能給其他身障者的建議是 (A)。(B) 謙虛勤奮、贏得別人尊重，(C) 學一技之長才能成功出名，(D) 心情不好時就唱歌，都不是她在文章裡說的想法。

閱讀測驗.title: 餐叉的演進史（The Evolution of the Fork）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Forks trace their origins back to the ancient Greeks. Forks at that time were fairly large with two tines that aided in the carving of meat in the kitchen. The tines prevented meat from twisting or moving during carving and allowed food to slide off more easily than it would with a knife.

By the 7th century A.D., royal courts of the Middle East began to use forks at the table for dining. From the 10th through the 13th centuries, forks were fairly common among the wealthy in Byzantium. In the 11th century, a Byzantine wife brought forks to Italy; however, they were not widely adopted there until the 16th century. Then in 1533, forks were brought from Italy to France. The French were also slow to accept forks, for using them was thought to be awkward.

In 1608, forks were brought to England by Thomas Coryate, who saw them during his travels in Italy. The English first ridiculed forks as being unnecessary. “Why should a person need a fork when God had given him hands?” they asked. Slowly, however, forks came to be adopted by the wealthy as a symbol of their social status. They were prized possessions made of expensive materials intended to impress guests. By the mid 1600s, eating with forks was considered fashionable among the wealthy British.

Early table forks were modeled after kitchen forks, but small pieces of food often fell through the two tines or slipped off easily. In late 17th century France, larger forks with four curved tines were developed. The additional tines made diners less likely to drop food, and the curved tines served as a scoop so people did not have to constantly switch to a spoon while eating. By the early 19th century, four-tined forks had also been developed in Germany and England and slowly began to spread to America.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
叉子的起源可以追溯到古希臘人。當時的叉子相當大，有兩根叉齒，在廚房裡用來幫忙切肉。切肉時，叉齒能讓肉不會扭動或移動，食物從叉子上滑下來，也比從刀子上滑下來容易。

到了西元七世紀，中東的宮廷開始在餐桌上用叉子吃飯。十到十三世紀，叉子在拜占庭的富人之間相當普遍。十一世紀時，一位拜占庭籍的妻子把叉子帶到義大利；不過，直到十六世紀，義大利人才廣泛使用叉子。接著在 1533 年，叉子從義大利傳到法國。法國人也很慢才接受叉子，因為他們認為用叉子很彆扭。

1608 年，Thomas Coryate 把叉子帶到英國，他是在義大利旅行時看到叉子的。英國人起初嘲笑叉子是多餘的東西。他們問：「上帝都給了人一雙手，人為什麼還需要叉子？」不過，富人慢慢用起叉子，把叉子當作社會地位的象徵。這些叉子是珍貴的財產，用昂貴的材料做成，為的是讓客人留下深刻的印象。到了 1600 年代中期，用叉子吃飯在英國富人之間已經是一種時尚。

早期的餐叉是照著廚房用的叉子做的，但小塊食物常常從兩根叉齒之間掉下去，或是很容易滑落。十七世紀末，法國發展出比較大、有四根彎曲叉齒的叉子。多了叉齒，用餐的人比較不容易讓食物掉下來；彎曲的叉齒還可以當杓子用，吃東西時就不必一直換成湯匙。到了十九世紀初，德國和英國也發展出四齒叉，並且慢慢傳到美國。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history of using forks for dining.
The development of fork-related table manners.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說叉子源自古希臘，原本是廚房切肉的工具；第 2、3 段說叉子從中東、義大利、法國一路傳到英國，成為餐桌上的用具；第 4 段說餐叉的形狀怎麼改良。全文依時間講人們用叉子吃飯的歷史，所以是 (C)。(A) 叉子的設計只在第 4 段談到，過於狹隘；(B) 用叉子幫忙烹調只出現在第 1 段，文章接下來講的是叉子在餐桌上怎麼傳開，(D) 用叉子的餐桌禮儀文章沒有談，兩個選項都偏離主題。

items.stem: By which route did the use of forks spread?
options: Middle East → Greece → England → Italy → France
Greece → Middle East → Italy → France → England
Greece → Middle East → France → Italy → Germany
Middle East → France → England → Italy → Germany
items.explanation:
Forks trace their origins back to the ancient Greeks.
By the 7th century A.D., royal courts of the Middle East began to use forks at the table for dining.
In the 11th century, a Byzantine wife brought forks to Italy;
Then in 1533, forks were brought from Italy to France.
In 1608, forks were brought to England by Thomas Coryate, who saw them during his travels in Italy.
照文章的時間標記排：古希臘（第 1 段）→ 西元七世紀中東（第 2 段）→ 十一世紀傳到義大利 → 1533 年從義大利傳到法國 → 1608 年傳到英國（第 3 段），所以是 (B)。(A) 和 (D) 的起點不是古希臘；(C) 把義大利和法國的順序顛倒了，而且德國是在十九世紀發展出四齒叉，講的是叉子的改良，不是用叉子的習慣傳到哪裡。

items.stem: How did forks become popular in England?
options: Wealthy British were impressed by the design of forks.
Wealthy British thought it awkward to use their hands to eat.
Wealthy British gave special forks to the nobles as luxurious gifts.
Wealthy British considered dining with forks a sign of social status.
items.explanation:
Slowly, however, forks came to be adopted by the wealthy as a symbol of their social status.
第 3 段說英國富人慢慢用起叉子，把叉子當作社會地位的象徵（a symbol of their social status），選項把 symbol 換成 sign。(A) 照抄 impress，原文說昂貴的叉子是用來讓客人留下深刻印象，不是富人自己對叉子的設計印象深刻，方向弄反了；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 awkward，覺得用叉子很彆扭的是法國人，不是英國人覺得用手吃飯彆扭；(C) 把叉子當禮物送給貴族，文章沒提。

items.stem: Why were forks made into a curved shape?
options: They could be used to scoop food as well.
They looked more fashionable in this way.
They were designed in this way for export to the US.
They ensured the meat would not twist while being cut.

the curved tines served as a scoop so people did not have to constantly switch to a spoon while eating.
第 4 段說彎曲的叉齒可以當杓子用（served as a scoop），吃東西時不必一直換湯匙，選項換成 scoop food as well。(B) 照抄第 3 段的 fashionable，時尚說的是英國富人用叉子吃飯這件事，和叉齒的形狀無關；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 twist，讓肉不會扭動是古希臘兩齒廚房叉的用途；(C) 原文說四齒叉後來慢慢傳到美國，不是為了外銷美國才做成彎的。

閱讀測驗.title: 如何拍攝動物（How to Photograph Animals）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Animals are a favorite subject of many photographers. Cats, dogs, and other pets top the list, followed by zoo animals. However, because it’s hard to get them to sit still and “perform on command,” some professional photographers refuse to photograph pets.

One way to get an appealing portrait of a cat or dog is to hold a biscuit or treat above the camera. The animal’s longing look toward the food will be captured by the camera, but the treat won’t appear in the picture because it’s out of the camera’s range. When you show the picture to your friends afterwards, they’ll be impressed by your pet’s loving expression.

If you are using fast film, you can take some good, quick shots of a pet by simply snapping a picture right after calling its name. You’ll get a different expression from your pet using this technique. Depending on your pet’s mood, the picture will capture an interested, curious expression or possibly a look of annoyance, especially if you’ve awakened it from a nap.

Taking pictures of zoo animals requires a little more patience. After all, you can’t wake up a lion! You may have to wait for a while until the animal does something interesting or moves into a position for you to get a good shot. When photographing zoo animals, don’t get too close to the cages, and never tap on the glass or throw things between the bars of a cage. Concentrate on shooting some good pictures, and always respect the animals you are photographing.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
動物是許多攝影師最喜歡拍的題材。貓、狗和其他寵物排第一，其次是動物園的動物。不過，因為很難讓動物乖乖坐好、「聽命令表演」，有些專業攝影師拒絕替寵物拍照。

要替貓或狗拍出討人喜愛的照片，有一個方法是把餅乾或零食舉在相機上方。相機會拍下寵物望著食物的渴望眼神，但零食不會出現在照片裡，因為零食在相機的拍攝範圍之外。事後你把照片拿給朋友看，朋友會對你家寵物充滿愛意的表情印象深刻。

如果你用的是高感光度底片，只要叫寵物的名字，然後馬上按下快門，就能迅速拍出幾張好照片。用這個技巧可以拍到寵物不同的表情。依寵物當時的心情而定，照片可能拍到感興趣、好奇的表情，也可能是一臉不耐煩，尤其是你把寵物從午睡中吵醒的時候。

拍動物園的動物需要多一點耐心。畢竟，你總不能把獅子叫醒吧！你可能得等一陣子，等動物做出有趣的動作，或是移動到好拍的位置。拍動物園的動物時，不要太靠近籠子，也絕對不要敲玻璃，或把東西丟進籠子的欄杆之間。專心拍出好照片，而且永遠要尊重你拍攝的動物。

One way to get an appealing portrait of a cat or dog is to hold a biscuit or treat above the camera.
The animal’s longing look toward the food will be captured by the camera,

閱讀測驗.title: 幽默的兩面性及其類型（The Dual Nature and Types of Humor）
閱讀測驗.passage:
A sense of humor is something highly valued. A person who has a great sense of humor is often considered to be happy and socially confident. However, humor is a double-edged sword. It can forge better relationships and help you cope with life, but sometimes it can also damage self-esteem and antagonize others.

People who use bonding humor tell jokes and generally lighten the mood. They’re perceived as being good at reducing the tension in uncomfortable situations. They often make fun of their common experiences, and sometimes they may even laugh off their own misfortunes. The basic message they deliver is: We’re all alike, we find the same things funny, and we’re all in this together.

Put-down humor, on the other hand, is an aggressive type of humor used to criticize and manipulate others through teasing. When it’s aimed against politicians, as it often is, it’s hilarious and mostly harmless. But in the real world, it may have a harmful impact. An example of such humor is telling friends an embarrassing story about another friend. When challenged about their teasing, the put-down jokers might claim that they are “just kidding,” thus allowing themselves to avoid responsibility. This type of humor, though considered by some people to be socially acceptable, may hurt the feelings of the one being teased and thus take a toll on personal relationships.

Finally, in hate-me humor, the joker is the target of the joke for the amusement of others. This type of humor was used by comedians John Belushi and Chris Farley—both of whom suffered for their success in show business. A small dose of such humor is charming, but routinely offering oneself up to be humiliated erodes one’s self-respect, and fosters depression and anxiety.

So it seems that being funny isn’t necessarily an indicator of good social skills and well-being. In certain cases, it may actually have a negative impact on interpersonal relationships.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
幽默感是很受重視的特質。很有幽默感的人，常常給人快樂、在社交上有自信的印象。然而，幽默是一把兩面刃。它可以建立更好的關係，幫助你面對生活，但有時候也會傷害自尊，引起別人的反感。

使用連結式幽默的人，會講笑話，通常能讓氣氛輕鬆起來。大家覺得他們很會在尷尬的場合化解緊張。他們常常拿彼此共同的經驗開玩笑，有時候甚至會一笑置之，看淡自己的不幸。他們傳達的基本訊息是：我們都一樣，我們覺得好笑的事情都一樣，我們同在一條船上。

相反地，貶低式幽默是一種具有攻擊性的幽默，透過嘲弄來批評、操控別人。拿政治人物開玩笑的時候（這種情形很常見），這種幽默很爆笑，大多也無傷大雅。但在現實生活中，它可能造成傷害。這種幽默的一個例子，是對朋友講另一個朋友的糗事。有人質疑他們的嘲弄時，愛用貶低式幽默的人可能會說他們「只是開玩笑」，讓自己逃避責任。這種幽默雖然有些人認為在社交上可以接受，卻可能傷害遭到嘲弄的人的感情，因而損害人際關係。

最後是自貶式幽默，說笑話的人拿自己當笑柄，逗別人開心。喜劇演員 John Belushi 和 Chris Farley 都用過這種幽默，兩人都在演藝圈獲得成功，也都為成功付出了代價。偶爾用一點這種幽默很討喜，但經常拿自己出來讓人取笑，會侵蝕一個人的自尊，助長憂鬱和焦慮。

所以，看來會搞笑不一定代表社交能力好、過得好。在某些情況下，幽默實際上可能對人際關係有負面的影響。

items.stem: According to the passage, which group is among the common targets of put-down humor?
options: People who are friendly to others.
items.explanation:
When it’s aimed against politicians, as it often is, it’s hilarious and mostly harmless.
第 3 段說貶低式幽默拿政治人物（politicians）開玩笑的時候，as it often is 說明這種情形很常見，可見政治人物是常見的對象，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 comedians，喜劇演員用的是自貶式幽默，拿自己當笑柄；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 tell jokes，講笑話是使用連結式幽默的人做的事；(D) 原文沒有說貶低式幽默針對友善的人。

items.stem: How can people create a relaxing atmosphere through bonding humor?
options: By laughing at other people’s misfortunes.
By joking about experiences that they all have.
By revealing their own personal relationships.
By making fun of unique experiences of their friends.
items.explanation:
They often make fun of their common experiences
第 2 段說使用連結式幽默的人，常常拿彼此共同的經驗（common experiences）開玩笑，選項換成拿大家都有的經驗開玩笑，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 misfortunes，原文說的是一笑置之、看淡自己的不幸，不是笑別人的不幸；(D) 照抄 make fun of，開玩笑的對象是共同的經驗，不是朋友獨特的經驗，拿朋友的事開玩笑比較接近第 3 段的貶低式幽默；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 personal relationships，那是貶低式幽默會傷害的東西。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about John Belushi and Chris Farley?
options: They suffered from over-dosage of anxiety pills.
They often humiliated other people on the stage.
They were successful in their careers as comedians.
They managed to rebuild their self-respect from their shows.
items.explanation:
comedians John Belushi and Chris Farley
both of whom suffered for their success in show business.
第 4 段說喜劇演員（comedians）John Belushi 和 Chris Farley 兩人都為了在演藝圈的成功（success）付出代價。suffered for their success 的前提是他們成功了，所以是 (C)。這一段的三個錯誤選項都照抄同一段的字：(A) 照抄 anxiety，原文說經常自貶會助長焦慮，沒有提到服用藥物；(B) 照抄 humiliated，自貶式幽默是讓別人取笑自己，不是羞辱別人；(D) 照抄 self-respect，原文說自貶式幽默會侵蝕自尊，選項說反了。

items.stem: What is the message that the author is trying to convey?
options: Humor deserves to be studied carefully.
Humor has both its bright side and dark side.
Humor is a highly valued personality trait.
Humor can be learned in many different ways.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說幽默是一把兩面刃（a double-edged sword），可以建立關係，也可能傷人；第 2 段的連結式幽默是好的一面，第 3、4 段的貶低式和自貶式幽默是壞的一面；第 5 段總結說，幽默可能對人際關係有負面的影響。全文要說的是幽默有好的一面，也有壞的一面，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄第 1 段的 highly valued，幽默感很受重視只是開頭第一句，接著就用 However 轉折，過於狹隘；(A) 作者分析幽默的類型，但沒有主張要仔細研究幽默，偏離主題；(D) 文章沒有談怎麼學幽默，偏離主題。

閱讀測驗.title: Sunny Airlines 機師拒飛事件與飛安呼籲（Sunny Airlines Pilots’ Refusal to Fly and a Safety Appeal）
閱讀測驗.passage:
On June 23, 2010, a Sunny Airlines captain with 32 years of experience stopped his flight from departing. He was deeply concerned about a balky power component that might eliminate all electrical power on his trans-Pacific flight. Despite his valid concerns, Sunny Airlines’ management pressured him to fly the airplane, over the ocean, at night. When he refused to jeopardize the safety of his passengers, Sunny Airlines’ security escorted him out of the airport, and threatened to arrest his crew if they did not cooperate.

Besides that, five more Sunny Airlines pilots also refused to fly the aircraft, citing their own concerns about the safety of the plane. It turned out the pilots were right: the power component was faulty and the plane was removed from service and, finally, fixed. Eventually a third crew operated the flight, hours later. In this whole process, Sunny Airlines pressured their highly experienced pilots to ignore their safety concerns and fly passengers over the Pacific Ocean at night in a plane that needed maintenance. Fortunately for all of us, these pilots stood strong and would not be intimidated.

Don’t just take our word that this happened. Please research this yourself and learn the facts. Here’s a starting point: www.SunnyAirlinePilot.org. Once you review this shocking information, please keep in mind that while their use of Corporate Security to remove a pilot from the airport is a new procedure, the intimidation of flight crews is becoming commonplace at Sunny Airlines, with documented events occurring on a weekly basis.

The flying public deserves the highest levels of safety. No airlines should maximize their revenues by pushing their employees to move their airplanes regardless of the potential human cost. Sunny Airlines’ pilots are committed to resisting any practices that compromise your safety for economic gain. We’ve been trying to fix these problems behind the scenes for quite some time; now we need your help. Go to www.SunnyAirlinePilot.org to get more information and find out what you can do.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
2010 年 6 月 23 日，Sunny 航空一位有 32 年經驗的機長，讓他的班機停止起飛。他非常擔心一個時好時壞的電源組件，可能讓他這班跨太平洋的班機完全斷電。儘管他的擔憂有道理，Sunny 航空的管理階層仍然施壓，要他在晚上駕駛這架飛機飛越大海。他拒絕拿乘客的安全冒險，Sunny 航空的保全人員就把他帶離機場，還威脅他的機組員，如果不配合就要逮捕他們。

除此之外，還有五位 Sunny 航空的機師也拒絕駕駛這架飛機，理由同樣是擔心飛機的安全。結果證明機師們是對的：電源組件確實故障，飛機停止服勤，最後也修好了。幾個小時後，這班飛機終於由第三組機組員執飛。整個過程中，Sunny 航空一直施壓這些經驗豐富的機師，要他們不顧安全的疑慮，在晚上駕駛一架需要維修的飛機，載著乘客飛越太平洋。我們大家都很幸運，這些機師堅持立場，沒有屈服於恐嚇。

不要只聽我們說有這件事。請自己查一查，了解事實。這裡有一個起點：www.SunnyAirlinePilot.org。看了這些令人震驚的資料以後，請記得：動用公司保全把機師帶離機場，雖然是新的做法，但恐嚇機組員在 Sunny 航空卻越來越常見，每個星期都有這類事件的紀錄。

搭飛機的大眾應該享有最高程度的安全。任何航空公司都不應該為了把營收提高到最大，不顧可能付出的人命代價，逼員工讓飛機起飛。Sunny 航空的機師承諾抵制任何為了賺錢而犧牲你的安全的做法。我們私下努力解決這些問題已經有一段時間了，現在我們需要你的幫助。請上 www.SunnyAirlinePilot.org，取得更多資訊，看看你能做些什麼。

items.stem: According to the passage, what happened to the captain after he refused to fly the aircraft?
options: He was asked to find another pilot to replace his position.
He was forced to leave the airport by security staff of Sunny Airlines.
He was made to help the Airlines find out what was wrong with the plane.
He was fired for refusing to fly the plane and abandoning the passengers.
items.explanation:
Sunny Airlines’ security escorted him out of the airport
第 1 段說機長拒絕拿乘客的安全冒險，Sunny 航空的保全人員（security）就把他帶離機場（escorted him out of the airport），選項換成他遭到保全人員強迫離開機場，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 plane，原文說電源組件確實故障、飛機也修好了，沒有說公司要機長幫忙找出問題；(D) 原文沒有說公司開除了他；(A) 第 2 段說最後由第三組機組員執飛，沒有說要機長自己找人代替。

items.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To introduce Sunny Airlines’ pilot training programs.
To review plans for improving Sunny Airlines’ service.
To expose problems with Sunny Airlines’ security practices.
items.explanation: 第 1、2 段描述 Sunny 航空施壓機師、用保全把機長帶離機場；第 3 段說恐嚇機組員的事情每週都有，請讀者自己去查；第 4 段呼籲大眾支持機師，抵制犧牲安全的做法。全文是在揭露 Sunny 航空不顧安全的做法，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 maximize，原文說航空公司不應該為了提高營收不顧安全，作者反對這樣做，偏離主題；(B) 照抄 pilot，文章談的是機師受到施壓，沒有介紹訓練課程，偏離主題；(C) 文章是在揭露問題，不是檢討改善服務的計畫，偏離主題。

items.stem: What happened to the aircraft after the pilots refused to operate the flight?
options: It was found to be too old for any more flight service.
Its mechanical problem was detected and finally repaired.
It was removed from the airport for a week-long checkup.
Its power component problem remained and no crew would operate the flight.
items.explanation:
the power component was faulty and the plane was removed from service and, finally, fixed.
第 2 段說電源組件確實故障（faulty），飛機停止服勤，最後（finally）也修好了（fixed），選項換成機械問題找出來，最後修好了，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 removed，原文說 removed from service 是停止服勤，不是移出機場，一星期也是第 3 段 on a weekly basis 的字，那是恐嚇事件的頻率；(D) 照抄 power component，問題修好以後，第三組機組員就執飛了；(A) 原文沒有說飛機太老。

items.stem: By whom was the passage most likely written?
options: Members of Sunny Airlines pilot organization.
One of the passengers of the Sunny Airlines flight.
items.explanation:
Don’t just take our word that this happened.
Sunny Airlines’ pilots are committed to resisting any practices that compromise your safety for economic gain.
We’ve been trying to fix these problems behind the scenes for quite some time; now we need your help.
這一題答對率只有 51%，關鍵是找出文章裡的「我們」是誰。判斷步驟：[1] 第 3 段說不要只聽我們（our word）說，第 4 段說我們（We）私下努力解決這些問題已經有一段時間，現在需要你的幫助；[2] 第 4 段的前一句說 Sunny 航空的機師（Sunny Airlines’ pilots）承諾抵制犧牲安全的做法，「我們」就是這些機師；[3] 文章用「我們」發聲，又附上機師的網站，最可能是機師組織的成員寫的，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 security，保全是把機長帶離機場的一方，不會寫文章批評自己；(B) 人事經理代表公司管理階層，也是文章批評的對象；(D) 照抄 passengers，乘客不會說自己私下努力解決問題已經很久。

閱讀測驗.title: 憤怒鳥在各種媒體的流行（The Spread of Angry Birds across Media）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Angry Birds is a video game developed by Finnish computer game developer Rovio Mobile. Inspired primarily by a sketch of stylized wingless birds, the game was first released for Apple’s mobile operating system in December 2009. Since then, over 12 million copies of the game have been purchased from Apple’s App Store.

With its fast-growing popularity worldwide, the game and its characters—angry birds and their enemy pigs—have been referenced in television programs throughout the world. The Israeli comedy A Wonderful Country, one of the nation’s most popular TV programs, satirized recent failed Israeli-Palestinian peace attempts by featuring the Angry Birds in peace negotiations with the pigs. Clips of the segment went viral, getting viewers from all around the world. American television hosts Conan O’Brien, Jon Stewart, and Daniel Tosh have referenced the game in comedy sketches on their respective series, Conan, The Daily Show, and Tosh.0. Some of the game’s more notable fans include Prime Minister David Cameron of the United Kingdom, who plays the iPad version of the game, and author Salman Rushdie, who is believed to be “something of a master at Angry Birds.”

Angry Birds and its characters have also been featured in advertisements in different forms. In March 2011, the characters began appearing in a series of advertisements for Microsoft’s Bing search engine. In the same year, Nokia projected an advertisement in Austin, Texas that included the game’s characters on a downtown building for its new handset. Later, a T-Mobile advertisement filmed in Spain included a real-life mock-up of the game in a city plaza. Nokia also used the game in Malaysia to promote an attempt to set a world record for the largest number of people playing a single mobile game.

Angry Birds has even inspired works of philosophical analogy. A five-part essay entitled “Angry Birds Yoga—How to Eliminate the Green Pigs in Your Life” was written by Giridhari Dasar in Brazil, utilizing the characters and gameplay mechanics to interpret various concepts of yoga philosophy. The piece attracted much media attention for its unique method of philosophical presentation.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
《憤怒鳥》是芬蘭電腦遊戲開發商 Rovio Mobile 開發的電玩遊戲。這款遊戲主要的靈感，來自一張畫著造型簡化、沒有翅膀的鳥的草圖，2009 年 12 月首先在蘋果的行動作業系統上推出。從那時起，蘋果的 App Store 已經賣出超過 1,200 萬份。

隨著在全世界的人氣快速成長，這款遊戲和裡面的角色──憤怒鳥和牠們的敵人綠豬──在世界各地的電視節目中都有人引用。以色列喜劇《美好國度》（A Wonderful Country）是以色列最受歡迎的電視節目之一，節目讓憤怒鳥和豬進行和平談判，藉此諷刺最近以色列和巴勒斯坦和談失敗。這一段節目的片段在網路上瘋傳，吸引了全世界的觀眾。美國電視主持人 Conan O’Brien、Jon Stewart 和 Daniel Tosh，都在各自的節目《Conan》、《The Daily Show》和《Tosh.0》的喜劇短劇裡引用過這款遊戲。這款遊戲比較有名的玩家，包括英國首相 David Cameron，他玩的是 iPad 版；還有作家 Salman Rushdie，據說他「玩憤怒鳥可以說是個高手」。

憤怒鳥和裡面的角色，也以各種形式出現在廣告裡。2011 年 3 月，這些角色開始出現在微軟 Bing 搜尋引擎的一系列廣告中。同一年，Nokia 在德州奧斯汀市中心的一棟大樓上，投影了一則有遊戲角色的廣告，宣傳新手機。後來，T-Mobile 在西班牙拍的一則廣告，在一座城市廣場上用實物重現了這款遊戲。Nokia 也在馬來西亞用這款遊戲，宣傳一場挑戰世界紀錄的活動，挑戰同時玩同一款手機遊戲的最多人數。

憤怒鳥甚至啟發了用哲學來類比的作品。巴西的 Giridhari Dasar 寫了一篇分成五部分的文章，題目是〈憤怒鳥瑜伽：如何消滅你生命中的綠豬〉，用遊戲的角色和玩法，詮釋瑜伽哲學的各種概念。這篇文章用獨特的方式呈現哲學，吸引了很多媒體的注意。

items.stem: What is the purpose of the passage?
options: To explain how the video game Angry Birds was devised.
To investigate why Angry Birds has quickly become well-liked.
To introduce Angry Birds characters in TV programs and advertisements.
To report on the spread of Angry Birds in different media around the world.
items.explanation: 第 1 段介紹憤怒鳥這款遊戲；第 2 段說它出現在各國的電視節目裡；第 3 段說它出現在各種廣告裡；第 4 段說它甚至啟發了巴西的哲學文章。全文報導憤怒鳥怎麼擴散到世界各地的各種媒體，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 3 段的 advertisements，電視節目和廣告只是第 2、3 段，漏了第 4 段的哲學文章，過於狹隘；(A) 遊戲怎麼設計出來，只有第 1 段提到靈感來自一張草圖，過於狹隘；(B) 文章說的是憤怒鳥出現在哪些地方，沒有分析它為什麼受歡迎，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word “viral” in the second paragraph?
items.explanation:
Clips of the segment went viral, getting viewers from all around the world.
viral 原本是「病毒的」，go viral 指影片或訊息像病毒一樣在網路上快速散播、爆紅。後面接著說這段節目吸引了全世界的觀眾（getting viewers from all around the world），所以是 (D) 很受歡迎。(B) 諷刺的，是這段節目的內容，前一句說它諷刺以巴和談失敗，但 went viral 說的是節目傳開了；(A) 明顯的、(C) 刺激的，都和吸引全世界的觀眾接不上。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following people is good at playing Angry Birds?
items.explanation:
author Salman Rushdie, who is believed to be
第 2 段說作家 Salman Rushdie 據說玩憤怒鳥可以說是個高手（something of a master），所以是 (C)。(B) Conan O’Brien 和 (D) Daniel Tosh 是在節目的短劇裡引用這款遊戲，原文沒有說他們很會玩；(A) Giridhari Dasar 是用遊戲來詮釋瑜伽哲學的作者。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about the use of Angry Birds, according to the passage?
options: It has been cited by UK Prime Minister to illustrate political issues.
Its characters are used in advertisements mainly for Apple’s products.
Its real-life mock-up has appeared in an advertisement for mobile phones.
It has been developed into a film about the life of a Brazilian yoga master.
items.explanation:
Later, a T-Mobile advertisement filmed in Spain included a real-life mock-up of the game in a city plaza.
第 3 段說 T-Mobile 在西班牙拍的廣告，在城市廣場上用實物重現了這款遊戲（a real-life mock-up），T-Mobile 是行動電話的電信業者，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 Prime Minister，英國首相只是玩 iPad 版的玩家，原文沒有說他用憤怒鳥說明政治議題；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 Apple，遊戲最早在蘋果的系統上推出，第 3 段的廣告是替微軟、Nokia 和 T-Mobile 做的；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 yoga，巴西的作者寫的是用遊戲詮釋瑜伽哲學的文章，不是瑜伽大師的電影。

閱讀測驗.title: 爆破拆除建築物（Explosive Demolition of Buildings）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Demolition is the tearing-down of buildings and other structures. You can level a five-story building easily with excavators and wrecking balls, but when you need to bring down a 20-story skyscraper, explosive demolition is the preferred method for safely demolishing the huge structure.

In order to demolish a building safely, blasters must map out a careful plan ahead of time. The first step is to examine architectural blueprints of the building to determine how the building is put together. Next, the blaster crew tours the building, jotting down notes about the support structure on each floor. Once they have gathered all the data they need, the blasters devise a plan of attack. They decide what explosives to use, where to position them in the building, and how to time their explosions.

Generally speaking, blasters will explode the major support columns on the lower floors first and then on a few upper stories. In a 20-story building, the blasters might blow the columns on the first and second floor, as well as the 12th and 15th floors. In most cases, blowing the support structures on the lower floors is sufficient for collapsing the building, but loading explosives on upper floors helps break the building material into smaller pieces as it falls. This makes for easier cleanup following the blast. The main challenge in bringing a building down is controlling the direction in which it falls. To topple the building towards the north, the blasters set off explosives on the north side of the building first. By controlling the way it collapses, a blasting crew will be able to tumble the building over on one side, into a parking lot or other open area. This sort of blast is the easiest to execute, and it is generally the safest way to go.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
拆除是把建築物和其他結構拆掉。用挖土機和破壞球，可以輕鬆夷平一棟五層樓的建築；但要拆掉一棟 20 層樓的摩天大樓，安全拆除這種龐大建築的首選方法是爆破拆除。

為了安全地拆除一棟建築物，爆破人員必須事先擬定周詳的計畫。第一步是研究建築物的藍圖，了解建築物是怎麼構成的。接著，爆破小組會在建築物裡實地走一遍，記下每一層樓的支撐結構。收集到需要的所有資料以後，爆破人員就擬定作戰計畫。他們決定要用哪些炸藥、炸藥放在建築物的什麼位置，以及引爆的時間怎麼安排。

一般來說，爆破人員會先炸低樓層的主要支柱，再炸幾層高樓層。以一棟 20 層樓的建築為例，爆破人員可能會炸一樓和二樓的支柱，以及 12 樓和 15 樓的支柱。大多數情況下，炸掉低樓層的支撐結構就足以讓建築物倒塌，但在高樓層裝炸藥，有助於讓建材在倒下時碎成比較小的塊，爆破以後比較容易清理。拆除建築物最大的挑戰，是控制倒下的方向。要讓建築物往北倒，爆破人員就先引爆建築物北側的炸藥。爆破小組控制建築物倒塌的方式，就能讓建築物倒向一側，倒進停車場或其他空曠的地方。這種爆破最容易執行，通常也是最安全的做法。

items.stem: What do the blasters need to do in preparing for the demolition of a building, according to the passage?
options: Study the structure of the building.
Make a miniature of the building.
items.explanation:
The first step is to examine architectural blueprints of the building to determine how the building is put together.
第 2 段說第一步是研究建築物的藍圖，了解建築物是怎麼構成的（how the building is put together），接著實地記下每一層樓的支撐結構，選項換成研究建築物的結構，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 tours，原文說爆破小組自己在建築物裡實地走一遍，不是請導遊；(D) 照抄 architectural，原文說要研究建築藍圖（architectural blueprints），沒有說要找原來的建築師；(C) 原文沒有提到做建築物的模型。

items.stem: In most cases, where does the explosion start in the building during its destruction?
items.explanation:
blasters will explode the major support columns on the lower floors first
第 3 段說一般來說，爆破人員會先（first）炸低樓層（lower floors）的主要支柱，選項換成 lower levels，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 upper floors，高樓層是後來才炸的，作用是讓建材碎成小塊；(A) 最頂層、(D) 地下室，原文都沒有提到。

items.stem: According to the following diagram, which part of the target building should the demolition team explode first to safely bring it down?
items.explanation:
To topple the building towards the north, the blasters set off explosives on the north side of the building first.
into a parking lot or other open area.
這一題答對率只有 47%，要把原文的規則套到圖上。判斷步驟：[1] 第 3 段說要讓建築物往北倒，就先引爆北側的炸藥，也就是先炸哪一側，建築物就往哪一側倒；[2] 原文又說要讓建築物倒進停車場或其他空曠的地方（open area），最安全；[3] 看圖：目標建築的北邊是百貨公司，西邊是教堂，東邊是學校，只有南邊是清空區（Cleared Area）；[4] 要讓建築物往南倒進清空區，就先炸南側，所以是 (C)。(D) 北側是照抄原文舉的例子，往北倒會壓到百貨公司；(A) 往東倒會壓到學校；(B) 往西倒會壓到教堂。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to execute demolition at the right time.
How to collapse a building with explosives.
How to use explosives for different purposes.
How to destroy a building with minimum manpower.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說拆除高樓的首選是爆破拆除；第 2 段說爆破前要怎麼規劃；第 3 段說先炸哪幾層，以及怎麼控制倒下的方向。全文講的是怎麼用炸藥讓建築物倒塌，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 time，原文的 how to time their explosions 是安排引爆的時間，只是計畫的一部分，過於狹隘；(C) 照抄 explosives，炸藥的用途很多，全文只談拆除建築物，太過廣泛；(D) 文章沒有談到怎麼節省人力，偏離主題。

閱讀測驗.title: 瑞士刀的起源（The Origin of the Swiss Army Knife）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The Swiss army knife is a popular device that is recognized all over the world. In Switzerland, there is a saying that every good Swiss citizen has one in his or her pocket. But the knife had humble beginnings.

In the late nineteenth century, the Swiss army issued its soldiers a gun that required a special screwdriver to dismantle and clean it. At the same time, canned food was becoming common in the army. Swiss generals decided to issue each soldier a standard knife to serve both as a screwdriver and a can opener.

It was a lifesaver for Swiss knife makers, who were struggling to compete with cheaper German imports. In 1884, Carl Elsener, head of the Swiss knife manufacturer Victorinox, seized that opportunity with both hands, and designed a soldier’s knife that the army loved. It was a simple knife with one big blade, a can opener, and a screwdriver.

A few years after the soldier’s knife was issued, the “Schweizer Offizier Messer,” or Swiss Officer’s Knife, came on the market. Interestingly, the Officer’s Knife was never given to those serving in the army. The Swiss military purchasers considered the new model with a corkscrew for opening wine not “essential for survival,” so officers had to buy this new model by themselves. But its special multi-functional design later launched the knife as a global brand. After the Second World War, a great number of American soldiers were stationed in Europe. And as they could buy the Swiss army knife at shops on military bases, they bought huge quantities of them. However, it seems that “Schweizer Offizier Messer” was too difficult for them to say, so they just called it the Swiss army knife, and that is the name it is now known by all over the world.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
瑞士刀是全世界都認得的熱門工具。瑞士有一句話說，每個好公民口袋裡都有一把瑞士刀。不過這把刀的出身其實很平凡。

19 世紀末，瑞士陸軍發給士兵一種步槍，拆卸和清理都需要特殊的螺絲起子。同一時期，罐頭食品在軍中越來越普遍。瑞士的將領於是決定發給每個士兵一把制式刀具，既能當螺絲起子，也能開罐頭。

這對當時苦於和比較便宜的德國進口刀競爭的瑞士刀具業者來說，簡直是救命稻草。1884 年，瑞士刀具製造商 Victorinox 的負責人 Carl Elsener 緊緊抓住這個機會，設計出一款軍方很喜歡的士兵刀。這是一把簡單的刀，有一片大刀刃、一個開罐器和一支螺絲起子。

士兵刀發放幾年後，Schweizer Offizier Messer，也就是「瑞士軍官刀」上市了。有意思的是，軍方從來沒有發軍官刀給軍人。瑞士軍方的採購人員認為，這款多了一支開葡萄酒用的軟木塞開瓶器的新刀，並不是「生存必需品」，所以軍官得自己掏錢買。但後來正是這種特殊的多功能設計，讓這把刀成了全球品牌。第二次世界大戰後，大批美軍駐紮在歐洲，他們可以在軍事基地的商店買到這種刀，於是大量購買。不過 Schweizer Offizier Messer 對美軍來說似乎太難唸了，他們乾脆叫它 Swiss army knife，現在全世界都用這個名字稱呼它。

items.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To explain the origin of the Swiss army knife.
To introduce the functions of the Swiss army knife.
To emphasize the importance of the Swiss army knife.
To tell a story about the designer of the Swiss army knife.
items.explanation: 從軍方需要一把刀、Victorinox 設計士兵刀、軍官刀上市，到美軍取名 Swiss army knife，全文依時間講瑞士刀的由來。(B) 刀有哪些功能，是交代由來時順帶提到的細節，過於狹隘；(D) Elsener 只出現在第 3 段，不是整篇的主角，同樣過於狹隘；(C) 文章沒有強調瑞士刀有多重要，偏離主題。

items.stem: What does “It” in the third paragraph refer to?
options: The Swiss army needed a knife for every soldier.
Every good Swiss citizen had a knife in his pocket.
Swiss knives were competing with imported knives.
Canned food was becoming popular in the Swiss army.
items.explanation:
Swiss generals decided to issue each soldier a standard knife to serve both as a screwdriver and a can opener.
It was a lifesaver for Swiss knife makers, who were struggling to compete with cheaper German imports.
對瑞士刀具業者來說是救命稻草的，是前一段結尾的那件事：軍方決定發給每個士兵一把刀，等於送上一筆大訂單。(C) 照抄同一句後半的 imports，那是業者的困境，不是救命稻草；(D) 罐頭普及只是軍方需要刀的原因之一。

items.stem: Why didn’t the Swiss army purchase the Swiss Officer’s Knife?
options: The design of the knife was too simple.
The knife was sold out to American soldiers.
The army had no budget to make the purchase.
The new design was not considered necessary for officers to own.
items.explanation:
The Swiss military purchasers considered the new model with a corkscrew for opening wine not “essential for survival,” so officers had to buy this new model by themselves.
採購人員認為多了開瓶器的新款不是生存必需品，essential 在選項換成 necessary。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 simple，但那是士兵刀的設計；(B) 照抄 American soldiers，美軍大量購買是二次大戰後的事。

items.stem: Who gave the name “the Swiss army knife” to the knife discussed in the passage?
items.explanation:
After the Second World War, a great number of American soldiers were stationed in Europe.
However, it seems that “Schweizer Offizier Messer” was too difficult for them to say, so they just called it the Swiss army knife, and that is the name it is now known by all over the world.
they 指前面幾句的美軍：瑞士德語的名字太難唸，他們乾脆叫它 Swiss army knife。其他三個選項都是文章出現過的人，但和取名無關：Elsener 設計士兵刀，瑞士將領決定發刀，德國人是競爭對手。

閱讀測驗.title: 太空垃圾的問題（The Problem of Space Junk）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Space is where our future is—trips to the Moon, Mars and beyond. Most people would think that aside from comets and stars there is little else out there. But, since our space journey started we have left so much trash there that scientists are now concerned that if we don’t clean it up, we may all be in mortal danger.

The first piece of space junk was created in 1964, when the American satellite Vanguard I stopped operating and lost its connection with the ground center. However, since it kept orbiting around the Earth without any consequences, scientists became increasingly comfortable abandoning things that no longer served any useful purpose in space.

It is estimated that there are currently over 500,000 pieces of man-made trash orbiting the Earth at speeds of up to 17,500 miles per hour. The junk varies from tiny pieces of paint chipped off rockets to cameras, huge fuel tanks, and even odd items like the million-dollar tool kit that astronaut Heidemarie Stefanyshyn-Piper lost during a spacewalk.

The major problem with the space trash is that it may hit working satellites and damage traveling spacecraft. Moreover, pieces of junk may collide with each other and break into fragments which fall back to the Earth. To avoid this, scientists have devised several ways for clearing the sky. Ground stations have been built to monitor larger pieces of space trash to prevent them from crashing into working satellites or space shuttles. Future plans include a cooperative effort among many nations to stop littering in space and to clean up the trash already there.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
太空是人類未來的所在，我們要去月球、火星，還要去更遠的地方。大部分人會以為，除了彗星和星星，太空裡沒什麼別的東西。但是，自從人類開始探索太空，我們已經在那裡留下太多垃圾，多到科學家現在擔心，如果不清理乾淨，我們可能全都會有生命危險。

第一件太空垃圾出現在 1964 年：美國的先鋒一號衛星停止運作，和地面中心失去聯繫。不過，先鋒一號一直繞著地球運行，沒有造成任何後果，於是科學家越來越習慣把太空中不再有用的東西丟著不管。

據估計，目前有超過五十萬件人造垃圾以最高每小時 17,500 英里的速度繞著地球運行。這些垃圾大小不一，小到火箭上剝落的油漆碎片，大到相機、巨大的燃料箱，甚至還有奇特的東西，例如太空人 Heidemarie Stefanyshyn-Piper 太空漫步時弄丟的那個價值百萬美元的工具箱。

太空垃圾的主要問題是可能撞上運作中的衛星，損壞航行中的太空船。此外，垃圾之間可能互相碰撞，碎成碎片掉回地球。為了避免這種情形，科學家想出了幾種清理天空的方法。目前已經建立地面站，監測體積較大的太空垃圾，防止這些垃圾撞上運作中的衛星或太空梭。未來的計畫包括各國合作，停止在太空亂丟垃圾，並且清理已經在那裡的垃圾。

items.stem: What was the first piece of man-made space trash?
items.explanation:
The first piece of space junk was created in 1964, when the American satellite Vanguard I stopped operating and lost its connection with the ground center.
第 2 段說第一件太空垃圾出現在 1964 年，是停止運作（stopped operating）、和地面失去聯繫的美國衛星先鋒一號，選項換成 a broken satellite。另外三個選項都照抄第 3 段：相機、工具箱、燃料箱是目前繞著地球的各種垃圾，不是第一件。

items.stem: Why were scientists NOT concerned about space trash in the beginning?
options: It no longer served any useful purpose.
It was millions of miles away from the Earth.
It did not cause any problems.
It was regarded as similar to comets and stars.
items.explanation:
However, since it kept orbiting around the Earth without any consequences, scientists became increasingly comfortable abandoning things that no longer served any useful purpose in space.
第 2 段說先鋒一號一直繞著地球運行，沒有造成任何後果（without any consequences），科學家才越來越習慣把東西丟著不管，選項換成 did not cause any problems。(A) 照抄 no longer served any useful purpose，這是在說科學家丟掉的是什麼東西，不是他們不擔心的原因；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 comets and stars，那是一般人以為太空裡只有的東西，和科學家的想法無關；(B) 文章沒說垃圾離地球幾百萬英里。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about space junk?
options: It floats slowly around the Earth.
It may cause problems for space shuttles.
items.explanation:
The major problem with the space trash is that it may hit working satellites and damage traveling spacecraft.
to prevent them from crashing into working satellites or space shuttles.
第 4 段說太空垃圾的主要問題是可能撞上衛星、損壞航行中的太空船（damage traveling spacecraft），地面站監測垃圾也是為了防止垃圾撞上太空梭，選項換成 may cause problems for space shuttles。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 huge，原文說垃圾小到油漆碎片、大到燃料箱都有，不全是巨大的機器；(C) 照抄 around the Earth，垃圾確實繞著地球運行，但第 3 段說速度最高每小時 17,500 英里，不是慢慢飄；(B) 垃圾一直繞著地球轉，位置當然會改變。

items.stem: What has been done about the space trash problem?
options: Scientists have cleaned up most of the trash.
Large pieces of space trash are being closely watched.
Many nations have worked together to stop polluting space.
Ground stations are built to help store the trash properly in space.
items.explanation:
Ground stations have been built to monitor larger pieces of space trash
題幹問的是已經做了什麼（What has been done），第 4 段只有地面站監測體積較大的垃圾是已經做到的（have been built），選項把 monitor 換成 closely watched。(C) 照抄 nations、(A) 照抄 clean：各國合作停止亂丟垃圾、清理已經在太空的垃圾，原文說是未來的計畫（Future plans），還沒做到；(D) 照抄 Ground stations，地面站是用來監測垃圾，不是在太空裡存放垃圾。

閱讀測驗.title: 能量飲料與酒測（Energy Drinks and Breathalyzer Tests）
閱讀測驗.passage:
An alcohol breath test (ABT) is often used by the police to find out whether a person is drunk while driving. In the United States, the legal blood alcohol limit is 0.08% for people aged 21 years or older, while people under 21 are not allowed to drive a car with any level of alcohol in their body. A “positive” test result, a result over the legal limit, allows the police to arrest the driver. However, many people who tested positive on the test have claimed that they only drank a “non-alcoholic” energy drink. Can one of these energy drinks really cause someone to test positive on an ABT? Researchers in Missouri set up an experiment to find out.

First, the amount of alcohol in 27 different popular energy drinks was measured. All but one had an alcohol level greater than 0.005%. In nine of the 27 drinks, the alcohol level was at least 0.096%. The scientists then investigated the possibility that these small levels of alcohol could be detected by an ABT. They asked test subjects to drink a full can or bottle of an energy drink and then gave each subject an ABT one minute and 15 minutes after the drink was finished.

For 11 of the 27 energy drinks, the ABT did detect the presence of alcohol if the test was given within one minute after the drink was taken. However, alcohol could not be detected for any of the drinks if the test was given 15 minutes after the drink was consumed. This shows that when the test is taken plays a crucial role in the test result. The sooner the test is conducted after the consumption of these drinks, the more likely a positive alcohol reading will be obtained.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
警察常用酒精呼氣檢測（ABT）判斷一個人是不是酒後駕車。在美國，21 歲以上的人法定血液酒精濃度上限是 0.08%，未滿 21 歲的人只要體內有任何酒精，就不准開車。「陽性」的檢測結果，也就是超過法定上限，警察就可以逮捕駕駛人。然而，許多檢測呈陽性的人都聲稱自己只喝了「不含酒精」的能量飲料。喝這些能量飲料，真的會讓人酒測呈陽性嗎？密蘇里州的研究人員設計了一項實驗來找出答案。

首先，研究人員測量了 27 種熱門能量飲料的酒精含量。除了一種以外，其他飲料的酒精含量都超過 0.005%。27 種飲料中，有 9 種的酒精含量至少 0.096%。接著，科學家研究酒測能不能測出這麼少量的酒精。他們請受試者喝完一整罐或一整瓶能量飲料，然後在喝完後 1 分鐘和 15 分鐘各替每位受試者做一次酒精呼氣檢測。

在 27 種能量飲料中，如果在喝完 1 分鐘內檢測，有 11 種確實測得出酒精。然而，如果在喝完 15 分鐘後才檢測，不論哪一種飲料都測不出酒精。這表示什麼時候檢測，對檢測結果有關鍵的影響。喝完這些飲料之後越早檢測，酒測讀數就越可能呈陽性。

items.stem: For a person who just turned 20, what is the legal alcohol level allowed while driving in the US?
items.explanation:
while people under 21 are not allowed to drive a car with any level of alcohol in their body.
第 1 段說美國 21 歲以上的人法定上限是 0.08%，未滿 21 歲的人只要體內有任何酒精（any level of alcohol）就不准開車。剛滿 20 歲還未滿 21 歲，允許的酒精濃度就是零，所以是 (A)。(C) 0.08% 是 21 歲以上的標準；(B) 和 (D) 照抄第 2 段的數字，那是能量飲料的酒精含量，不是法定上限。

items.stem: What is the purpose of the Missouri experiment?
options: To introduce a new method of calculating blood alcohol levels.
To discover the relation between energy drinks and ABT test results.
To warn about the dangers of drinking energy drinks mixed with alcohol.
To challenge the current legal alcohol limit for drivers in the United States.
items.explanation:
Can one of these energy drinks really cause someone to test positive on an ABT? Researchers in Missouri set up an experiment to find out.
第 1 段最後問：喝能量飲料真的會讓人酒測呈陽性（test positive on an ABT）嗎？密蘇里州的研究人員設計實驗就是要找出答案，選項換成 discover the relation between energy drinks and ABT test results。(A) 照抄 blood alcohol，實驗沒有提出計算血液酒精濃度的新方法；(D) 照抄 legal，法定上限只是文章開頭的背景說明，實驗沒有挑戰這個標準；(C) 實驗測的是能量飲料本身含的酒精，不是摻了酒的能量飲料有什麼危險。

items.stem: What were the participants of the experiment asked to do after they finished their energy drink?
options: To line up in the laboratory.
To take an alcohol breath test.
To check their breath for freshness.
items.explanation:
They asked test subjects to drink a full can or bottle of an energy drink and then gave each subject an ABT one minute and 15 minutes after the drink was finished.
第 2 段說受試者喝完能量飲料後，研究人員在 1 分鐘和 15 分鐘後各替每個人做一次 ABT。第 1 段開頭已經交代 ABT 就是 alcohol breath test（酒精呼氣檢測），選項把縮寫寫成全名，所以是 (C)。(A) 排隊、(B) 回想飲料品牌文章都沒提；(D) 呼氣檢測測的是酒精，不是口氣清不清新。

items.stem: What is the most important factor that affects the ABT test result for energy drink consumers?
options: The age of the person who takes the test.
The place where the test is given.
The equipment that the test uses.
The time when the test is taken.
items.explanation:
This shows that when the test is taken plays a crucial role in the test result.
第 3 段說喝完 1 分鐘內檢測，有 11 種飲料測得出酒精，15 分鐘後檢測，全都測不出來；因此結論是什麼時候檢測（when the test is taken）對結果有關鍵的影響，選項換成 the time when the test is taken。(A) 年齡在第 1 段決定的是法定上限，和能量飲料的檢測結果無關；(B) 檢測地點和 (C) 檢測儀器，實驗都沒有比較。

閱讀測驗.title: 印度 Bindi 的文化意涵（The Cultural Meaning of the Bindi in India）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The majority of Indian women wear a red dot between their eyebrows. While it is generally taken as an indicator of their marital status, the practice is primarily related to the Hindu religion. The dot goes by different names in different Hindi dialects, and “bindi” is the one that is most commonly known. Traditionally, the dot carries no gender restriction: Men as well as women wear it. However, the tradition of men wearing it has faded in recent times, so nowadays we see a lot more women than men wearing one.

The position of the bindi is standard: center of the forehead, close to the eyebrows. It represents a third, or inner eye. Hindu tradition holds that all people have three eyes: The two outer ones are used for seeing the outside world, and the third one is there to focus inward toward God. As such, the dot signifies piety and serves as a constant reminder to keep God in the front of a believer’s thoughts.

Red is the traditional color of the dot. It is said that in ancient times a man would place a drop of blood between his wife’s eyes to seal their marriage. According to Hindu beliefs, the color red is believed to bring good fortune to the married couple. Today, people go with different colors depending upon their preferences. Women often wear dots that match the color of their clothes. Decorative or sticker bindis come in all sizes, colors and variations, and can be worn by young and old, married and unmarried people alike. Wearing a bindi has become more of a fashion statement than a religious custom.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
大部分印度女性都會在兩眉之間點一個紅點。一般人通常把紅點看作已婚的記號，不過這個習俗主要和印度教有關。這個紅點在不同的印地語方言裡有不同的名稱，最廣為人知的是「bindi」。傳統上，紅點沒有性別限制：男性和女性都會點。不過近來男性點紅點的傳統逐漸式微，所以現在我們看到點紅點的女性比男性多得多。

bindi 的位置有固定的標準：額頭正中央、靠近眉毛的地方。bindi 代表第三隻眼，也就是內在的眼睛。印度教的傳統認為，每個人都有三隻眼：外面的兩隻眼用來看外在的世界，第三隻眼則用來向內專注於神。因此，這個點象徵虔誠，時時提醒信徒要把神放在心中最重要的位置。

紅色是 bindi 的傳統顏色。相傳古時候男人會在妻子兩眼之間點一滴血，作為婚姻的印記。根據印度教的信仰，紅色會替夫妻帶來好運。現在大家會依照自己的喜好選擇不同的顏色。女性常常點和衣服同色的 bindi。裝飾用的 bindi 或貼紙式的 bindi 大小、顏色、樣式應有盡有，不論老少、已婚未婚都可以戴。戴 bindi 已經比較像是在展現時尚，而不是遵循宗教習俗。

items.stem: Why did people in India start wearing a red dot on their forehead?
items.explanation:
While it is generally taken as an indicator of their marital status, the practice is primarily related to the Hindu religion.
第 1 段說一般人常把紅點看作已婚的記號，但這個習俗主要和印度教有關（related to the Hindu religion）；第 2 段也說紅點象徵虔誠。選項換成 show their religious belief，所以是 (B)。(A) 社會階級、(C) 經濟狀況、(D) 家世背景，文章都沒提。

items.stem: What is the significance of the third eye in Hindu tradition?
options: To stay in harmony with nature.
To observe the outside world more clearly.
To see things with a subjective view.
items.explanation:
the third one is there to focus inward toward God.
As such, the dot signifies piety and serves as a constant reminder to keep God in the front of a believer’s thoughts.
第 2 段說第三隻眼用來向內專注於神，所以這個點象徵虔誠（piety），提醒信徒時時把神放在心上，選項換成 pay respect to God。(B) 照抄 outside world，看外在世界的是另外兩隻眼，第三隻眼是向內看的；(A) 和自然和諧相處、(D) 用主觀的角度看事情，文章都沒提。

items.stem: Why was red chosen as the original color of the bindi?
options: The red dot represented the blood of God.
Red stood for a wife’s love for her husband.
The word “bindi” means “red” in some Hindi dialects.
Red was supposed to bring blessings to a married couple.
items.explanation:
According to Hindu beliefs, the color red is believed to bring good fortune to the married couple.
第 3 段說根據印度教的信仰，紅色會替夫妻帶來好運（bring good fortune to the married couple），選項把 good fortune 換成 blessings。(A) 照抄 blood，相傳點在妻子兩眼之間的是丈夫的血，不是神的血；(B) 照抄 wife，點血是為了替婚姻留下印記，原文沒說紅色代表妻子對丈夫的愛；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 Hindi dialects，原文說的是紅點在不同方言裡有不同的名稱，沒說 bindi 的意思是紅色。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the practice of wearing a bindi today?
options: Bindis are worn anywhere on the face now.
Bindis are now used as a decorative item.
Most Indian women do not like to wear bindis anymore.
Wearing a bindi has become more popular among Indian men.
items.explanation:
Decorative or sticker bindis come in all sizes, colors and variations
Wearing a bindi has become more of a fashion statement than a religious custom.
第 3 段說現在有裝飾用（decorative）的 bindi，大小、顏色、樣式應有盡有，戴 bindi 已經比較像是在展現時尚，選項換成 used as a decorative item。(C) 照抄第 1 段的 Indian women，原文說大部分印度女性都會點紅點，正好相反；(A) 第 2 段說 bindi 的位置有固定的標準，就在額頭正中央；(D) 第 1 段說男性點紅點的傳統逐漸式微，不是越來越流行。

閱讀測驗.title: 音樂產業的群眾募資（Crowd-funding in the Music Industry）
閱讀測驗.passage:
All pop artists like to say that they owe their success to their fans. In the case of British band SVM, it’s indeed true. The band is currently recording songs because 358 fans contributed the £100,000 needed for the project. The arrangement came via MMC, an online record label that uses Web-based, social-network-style “crowd-funding” to finance its acts.

Here’s how it works: MMC posts demos and videos of 10 artists on its website, and users are invited to invest from £10 to £1,000 in the ones they most enjoy or think are most likely to become popular. Once an act reaches £100,000, the financing process is completed, and the money is used to pay for recording and possibly a concert tour. Profits from resulting music sales, concerts, and merchandise are split three ways: investors get to divide 40%; another 40% goes to MMC; the artist pockets 20%. The payoff for investors can be big. One fan in France who contributed £4,250 got his money back 22 times over.

Crowd-funding musical acts is not new. But MMC takes the concept to another level. First of all, investors can get cash rather than just goodies like free downloads or tickets. Also, MMC is a record label. It has the means to get its music distributed around the world and to market artists effectively. “Artists need professional support,” says the CEO of MMC’s international division.

While digital technology and the Net have created a do-it-yourself boom among musicians, success is still a long shot. Out of the 20,000 records released in the U.S. in 2009, only 14 DIY acts made it to the Top 200. Also, with less revenue from recorded music, music companies have become less likely to take risks, which has led to fewer artists receiving funding. The crowd-funding model, however, allows for more records to be made by spreading risk among hundreds of backers. And the social-network aspect of the site helps expand fan bases; that is, investors become a promotional army.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
流行歌手都喜歡說，他們的成功要歸功於歌迷。以英國樂團 SVM 來說，這句話一點也不假。這個樂團正在錄製歌曲，因為有 358 位歌迷出資，籌到了這項計畫需要的 10 萬英鎊。這項安排是透過 MMC 促成的。MMC 是一家線上唱片公司，用網路上類似社群網站的「群眾募資」方式，替旗下的藝人籌措資金。

運作方式是這樣的：MMC 在網站上放 10 組藝人的試聽帶和影片，邀請用戶投資 10 到 1,000 英鎊，投給他們最喜歡、或認為最可能走紅的藝人。一組藝人募到 10 萬英鎊，籌資程序就完成了，這筆錢會用來支付錄音的費用，也可能用來辦巡迴演唱會。之後音樂銷售、演唱會和周邊商品的收益，分成三份：投資人一起分 40%，另外 40% 歸 MMC，藝人拿 20%。投資人的回報可能很高。法國有一位歌迷投資了 4,250 英鎊，拿回了 22 倍的錢。

替音樂人群眾募資並不新鮮，但 MMC 把這個概念推到了另一個層次。第一，投資人可以拿到現金，不只是免費下載或門票這類贈品。第二，MMC 本身是一家唱片公司，有能力把音樂發行到全世界，也能有效地行銷藝人。MMC 國際部門的執行長說：「藝人需要專業的支援。」

雖然數位科技和網路讓音樂人掀起了一股自己動手做（DIY）的風潮，要成功仍然很難。2009 年美國發行的兩萬張唱片中，只有 14 組自己動手做的藝人擠進前 200 名。此外，唱片的收入減少，唱片公司變得比較不敢冒險，獲得資金的藝人也就變少了。然而，群眾募資的模式把風險分散給數百位出資者，讓更多唱片能夠製作出來。網站的社群特性也有助於擴大歌迷群，也就是說，投資人成了宣傳大軍。

items.stem: Which of the following titles best expresses the main idea of the passage?
items.explanation: 第 1 段用英國樂團 SVM 的例子，帶出 MMC 用群眾募資替藝人籌錢；第 2 段說明運作方式；第 3 段說 MMC 和一般群眾募資有什麼不同；第 4 段說唱片公司不敢冒險，群眾募資能分散風險，讓更多唱片製作出來。全文講的是音樂產業的群眾募資，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (B)，這個選項照抄第 4 段的 music companies：原文說募來的錢用來替旗下的藝人（its acts）錄音，籌錢的對象是藝人，不是唱片公司，第 4 段還說唱片公司變得不敢冒險，偏離主題。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 Web-based，網路是募資的管道，全文談的是籌錢，不是用網路製作音樂，偏離主題；(C) 投資人拿到高額回報，只是第 2 段的一個例子，過於狹隘。

items.stem: How much money does a band have to raise via MMC to have their music recorded?
items.explanation:
Once an act reaches £100,000, the financing process is completed, and the money is used to pay for recording
第 2 段說一組藝人募到 10 萬英鎊（£100,000），籌資程序就完成了，這筆錢用來支付錄音的費用，第 1 段 SVM 的例子也是 10 萬英鎊，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 £10、(B) 照抄 £1,000，10 到 1,000 英鎊是每位用戶可以投資的金額；(C) 照抄 £4,250，那是一位法國歌迷投資的金額。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about MMC?
options: It has helped many do-it-yourself musicians get to the Top 200.
There are works of fourteen artists posted at a time on its website.
It allows fans to provide financial support to the musicians they like.
The biggest share of its profits from a crowd-funding project goes to the musician.
items.explanation:
users are invited to invest from £10 to £1,000 in the ones they most enjoy
第 2 段說 MMC 邀請用戶投資（invest）他們最喜歡的藝人（the ones they most enjoy），選項換成 provide financial support to the musicians they like，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 Top 200，只有 14 組自己動手做的藝人擠進前 200 名，那是 2009 年美國的整體情況，原文沒有說和 MMC 有關；(B) MMC 網站上放的是 10 組藝人，14 是擠進前 200 名的組數；(D) 收益分配是投資人和 MMC 各 40%，藝人只拿 20%，藝人拿得最少。

items.stem: What does the author mean by success is still a long shot in the fourth paragraph?
options: Success is not easy to achieve.
Success often starts with one big shot.
Success should be every musician’s long-term goal.
items.explanation:
Out of the 20,000 records released in the U.S. in 2009, only 14 DIY acts made it to the Top 200.
a long shot 是「希望渺茫的事」。這一句用 While 對比：雖然數位科技讓音樂人掀起自己動手做的風潮，要成功仍然……；下一句接著說，2009 年美國發行的兩萬張唱片中，只有 14 組自己動手做的藝人擠進前 200 名。成功的比例這麼低，可見成功並不容易，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 shot、(D) 照抄 long，都是把片語拆開來照字面解釋；(A) 成功的效果持久，和下一句的數字接不上。

閱讀測驗.title: 真實世界的牽引光束（A Real-life Tractor Beam）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In science fiction TV programs such as Star Trek, tractor beams are used to tow spaceships and move objects. For years, scientists have labored to replicate this feat. In 2013, they succeeded. A team of British and Czech scientists, led by Dr. Tomas Cizmar, say they have created a real-life “tractor beam,” like the kind from Star Trek, which uses a beam of light to attract objects, at least at a microscopic level.

Light manipulation techniques have existed since the 1970s, but this is thought to be the first time a light beam has been used to draw objects towards a light source. Usually when microscopic objects are hit by a beam of light, they are forced along the direction of the beam. After many years’ research, Dr. Cizmar’s team discovered a technique that allows for the radiant force of light to be reversed and to use the negative force to draw out certain particles.

Dr. Cizmar says that even though it is a few years away from practical use, the technology has huge potential for medical research. In particular, the tractor beam is highly selective in the particles it can attract, so it can pick up particles that have specific properties, such as size or composition, in a mixture. “Eventually, this could be used to separate white blood cells, for example,” Dr. Cizmar told BBC News.

It has been a primary plot device in science fiction TV programs and movies to allow objects like spaceships to be trapped in a beam of light. But Dr. Cizmar said this particular technique would not eventually lead to that. A transfer of energy happens in the process. On a microscopic scale that is OK, but on a large scale it would cause huge problems. A large object could be destroyed by the heating, which results from the massive amount of energy necessary to pull it.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
在《星艦迷航記》這類科幻電視節目裡，牽引光束用來拖曳太空船、移動物體。多年來，科學家一直努力想做出同樣的事。2013 年，他們成功了。一支由 Tomas Cizmar 博士領導的英國和捷克科學家團隊說，他們做出了真實世界的「牽引光束」，就像《星艦迷航記》裡的那種，用一道光束吸引物體，至少在顯微的尺度上做得到。

操控光的技術從 1970 年代就有了，但一般認為，這是第一次用光束把物體拉向光源。通常微小的物體受到光束照射時，會順著光束的方向推開。經過多年的研究，Cizmar 博士的團隊找到一種技術，可以讓光的輻射力反轉，再用這股負向的力把某些粒子吸出來。

Cizmar 博士說，雖然這項技術離實際應用還有好幾年，在醫學研究上卻有很大的潛力。特別是牽引光束對能吸引的粒子挑選得非常精準，所以能從摻在一起的許多粒子中，挑出具有特定性質（例如大小或成分）的粒子。Cizmar 博士告訴 BBC 新聞：「舉例來說，將來這可以用來分離白血球。」

讓太空船這類物體困在一道光束裡，一直是科幻電視節目和電影主要的情節安排。但 Cizmar 博士說，這種技術最後不會發展到那一步。這個過程會發生能量的轉移。在顯微的尺度上，這沒有問題，但在大的尺度上，就會造成很大的問題。拉動一個大型物體需要大量的能量，這些能量會產生熱，物體可能因此毀壞。

items.stem: What is this passage mainly about?
options: The application of lighting technology in modern society.
The uses and limitations of a scientific invention by a research team.
The adoption of light manipulation techniques in medical treatment.
The influences and effects of scientific developments on science fiction.
items.explanation: 這一題答對率只有 37%，要把四段的重點連起來看。第 1 段說 Cizmar 博士的團隊做出了真實世界的牽引光束（一項發明）；第 2 段說明原理；第 3 段說這項技術在醫學研究上有很大的潛力（用途）；第 4 段用 But 轉折，說這項技術不能用來拉大型物體，因為會產生熱，把物體毀壞（限制）。全文講的是一個研究團隊的發明，有什麼用途和限制，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 light manipulation techniques，醫學只是第 3 段的用途，而且原文說離實際應用還有好幾年，還談不上用在治療上，過於狹隘；(A) 光的技術在現代社會的應用範圍很廣，全文只談一項發明，太過廣泛；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 science fiction，文章用科幻節目開頭，談的卻是科學研究，沒有談科學對科幻作品的影響，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about Dr. Cizmar’s tractor beam?
options: It moves big objects as the tractor beam did in Star Trek.
It is the first light beam device that pushes objects forward.
It relies on negative force to pull out specific kinds of particles.
It is currently being used for separating blood cells in medical research.
items.explanation:
use the negative force to draw out certain particles.
這一題答對率只有 48%，三個錯誤選項都照抄原文，卻把意思改了。第 2 段說 Cizmar 博士的團隊讓光的輻射力反轉，用這股負向的力（negative force）把某些粒子吸出來（draw out certain particles），選項換成 pull out specific kinds of particles，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 first，原文說這是第一次用光束把物體「拉向」光源，把物體往前推是一般的光束，選項說反了；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 Star Trek，這項技術只在顯微尺度上做得到，第 4 段說不能拉大型物體；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 blood cells，原文說將來（Eventually）可能用來分離白血球，離實際應用還有好幾年，現在還沒有使用。

items.stem: What does that in the last paragraph refer to?
options: Transferring a massive amount of energy.
Making science fiction programs and movies.
Burning a large object into ashes.
Capturing spaceships in a beam of light.
items.explanation:
to allow objects like spaceships to be trapped in a beam of light.
But Dr. Cizmar said this particular technique would not eventually lead to that.
前一句說，讓太空船這類物體困在一道光束裡（trapped in a beam of light），一直是科幻節目主要的情節；這一句用 But 轉折，說這種技術最後不會發展到 that。that 指的是前一句說的情節，也就是用光束困住太空船，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄後一句的 transfer，能量轉移是不能發展到那一步的原因；(C) 照抄 large object，大型物體受熱毀壞是用光束拉大型物體的後果；(B) 照抄 science fiction，科幻節目只是那個情節出現的地方。

items.stem: What is the tone of this passage?
items.explanation: 這一題答對率只有 54%。全文報導一項研究：第 1、2 段說明研究成果和原理，第 3 段說潛力，第 4 段說限制。作者既說優點也說缺點，好處和限制都引用 Cizmar 博士自己的話，沒有加入個人的好惡，所以是 (A) 客觀的。(C) 讚賞的、(D) 悲觀的，都只看到其中一面：第 3 段說潛力很大，第 4 段說不能拉大型物體，作者兩邊都寫到；(B) 作者沒有懷疑研究的真假。

閱讀測驗.title: 非洲學校走向數位化（Schools in Africa Going Digital）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Grace Wambui, a 14-year-old pupil in Nairobi, had never touched a tablet computer. But it took her only about one minute to work out how to use one when such devices arrived at Amaf School in Kawangware, a slum in the Kenyan capital. Teaching used to be conducted with a blackboard and a handful of tattered textbooks. Now children in groups of five take turns to swipe the touch screen of the devices, which are loaded with a multimedia version of Kenya’s syllabus.

The tablets at Amaf School are part of a pilot project run by eLimu, a technology start-up. If it and other firms are right, tablets and other digital devices may soon be the rule in African schools. Many are betting on a boom in digital education in Kenya and elsewhere. Some executives even expect it to take off like M-Pesa, Kenya’s hugely successful mobile-money service.

Such growth in digital education would be timely. The flood of new pupils has overwhelmed state schools, which were already understaffed, underfunded and poorly managed. The prospect of Africa’s 300 million pupils learning digitally has caught the attention of global technology giants. Amazon has seen sales of its Kindle e-readers in Africa increase tenfold in the past year. Intel has been helping African governments buy entry-level computers. In Nigeria, Intel brought together a publisher and a telecom carrier to provide exam-preparation tools over mobile phones, a service that has become hugely popular.

A bigger question is whether digital tools actually improve education. Early results are encouraging. In Ghana, reading skills improved measurably among 350 children that had been given Kindle e-readers. In Ethiopia, in the absence of teachers, children figured out how to use tablets and learned the English ABCs. At Amaf School, average marks in science went from 58 to 73 in a single term.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
Grace Wambui 是奈洛比一名 14 歲的學生，從來沒有摸過平板電腦。但是平板電腦送到肯亞首都貧民區 Kawangware 的 Amaf 學校時，她只花了一分鐘左右，就學會怎麼使用。以前上課只有一塊黑板和幾本破舊的課本。現在孩子們五個人一組，輪流滑動平板的觸控螢幕，平板裡裝的是多媒體版本的肯亞課程。

Amaf 學校的平板電腦，是科技新創公司 eLimu 主持的試辦計畫的一部分。如果 eLimu 和其他公司的看法沒錯，平板和其他數位裝置可能很快就會在非洲的學校普及。許多人都看好肯亞和其他地方的數位教育會蓬勃發展。有些主管甚至預期，數位教育會像肯亞非常成功的行動支付服務 M-Pesa 一樣，一飛沖天。

數位教育這樣的成長，可以說來得正是時候。大量湧入的新學生，讓公立學校應付不來，這些學校原本就人手不足、經費不足，管理也不好。非洲三億名學生都用數位方式學習的前景，吸引了全球科技大廠的注意。Amazon 的 Kindle 電子書閱讀器，在非洲的銷量過去一年增加了十倍。Intel 一直在協助非洲各國政府購買入門級的電腦。在奈及利亞，Intel 找來一家出版社和一家電信業者合作，用手機提供準備考試的工具，這項服務變得非常受歡迎。

更重要的問題是，數位工具是不是真的能改善教育。初步的結果令人振奮。在迦納，350 名拿到 Kindle 電子書閱讀器的孩子，閱讀能力有了明顯的進步。在衣索比亞，沒有老師的情況下，孩子們自己摸索出怎麼使用平板，學會了英文字母。在 Amaf 學校，科學的平均分數在一個學期內從 58 分提高到 73 分。

items.stem: Which of the following is the best title for this passage?
options: Schools in Africa Are Going Digital
Tablet Computers Are in Great Demand in Kenya
items.explanation: 第 1 段用 Grace 的例子，說平板電腦送進了肯亞的學校；第 2 段說數位裝置可能很快在非洲學校普及；第 3 段說非洲的學生太多、學校應付不來，科技大廠紛紛投入；第 4 段說初步結果令人振奮。全文講的是非洲的學校走向數位化，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 Kenya，全文也談到奈及利亞、迦納和衣索比亞，只講肯亞的平板，過於狹隘；(B) 公立學校的問題只是第 3 段說數位教育來得正是時候的原因，過於狹隘；(A) 暢銷商品，文章沒有在談，偏離主題。

items.stem: What is the author trying to convey in citing Grace Wambui’s case?
options: Grace is a genius in computer skills.
The tablet computer is very user-friendly.
The delivery system in Kenya is very poor.
Tablet computers are common in Kawangware.
items.explanation:
But it took her only about one minute to work out how to use one
這一題答對率只有 49%，問的是作者舉 Grace 這個例子的用意。判斷步驟：[1] 第 1 段說 Grace 從來沒有摸過平板電腦；[2] 接著用 But 轉折，說她只花一分鐘左右就學會怎麼使用；[3] 一個從沒用過的孩子一分鐘就會用，表示平板很容易上手，所以是 (B)。(A) 作者沒有說 Grace 有特別的天分，例子的重點在平板好用；(D) 照抄 Kawangware，Grace 從沒摸過平板，可見平板在這個貧民區並不普遍；(C) 原文沒有談到肯亞的運送系統。

items.stem: According to the passage, what is eLimu?
items.explanation:
a pilot project run by eLimu, a technology start-up.
If it and other firms are right
這一題答對率只有 27%，是這一批最難的題目之一，關鍵是看懂逗點後面的同位語。判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段說平板是 eLimu 主持（run by eLimu）的試辦計畫的一部分；[2] eLimu 後面緊接著逗點和 a technology start-up，這是同位語，說明 eLimu 是什麼，start-up 是新創公司；[3] 下一句 If it and other firms are right 又把 eLimu 和其他公司（other firms）並列。所以 eLimu 是一家公司，答案是 (A)。最多人選錯的是 (D)，這個選項照抄 project：試辦計畫是 eLimu 主持的，計畫和主持計畫的公司是兩回事。(B) 電腦程式、(C) 電子書，是平板裡裝的東西，不是 eLimu。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about education in Africa?
options: The number of students keeps dropping in recent years.
There are more than enough teachers for traditional classroom teaching.
Students have received Kindle e-readers donated by Amazon to improve reading.
Early results from use of digital tools in teaching are quite positive in some countries.
items.explanation:
Early results are encouraging.
第 4 段說數位工具能不能改善教育，初步的結果（Early results）令人振奮（encouraging），接著舉迦納、衣索比亞和 Amaf 學校的例子，選項換成 quite positive in some countries，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 Kindle e-readers，原文說迦納的孩子拿到 Kindle，沒有說是 Amazon 捐的，第 3 段說的是 Kindle 在非洲的銷量增加；(B) 照抄 teachers，第 4 段說衣索比亞的孩子在沒有老師的情況下自己學，第 3 段也說公立學校人手不足，選項說反了；(A) 第 3 段說大量的新學生湧入，學生人數是在增加。

閱讀測驗.title: 斯巴達松超級馬拉松的魅力（The Allure of the Spartathlon Ultra-Marathon）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In the Spartathlon, one of the world’s toughest ultra-marathons, runners run 245 km, about six marathons, within 36 hours. The runners start in Athens, and run all the way to historical Sparta.

The Spartathlon’s heritage goes back to 490 B.C., when Pheidippides, an Athenian, made the journey to Sparta to ask the Spartans for help in fighting the invading Persians. It is recorded that he reached Sparta on the day after he left Athens. In 1982, this story sparked the interest of a British air-force officer and long-distance runner called John Foden, who wondered if it really was possible to run from Athens to Sparta and arrive the next day. With four other officers, Foden decided to see for himself; after a 36-hour slog they arrived in Sparti, as the town is now called. That achievement inspired the organization of the first Spartathlon a year later.

The Spartathlon’s attraction has two sources. The first is the difficulty of finishing it. The Spartathlon is not the most difficult race, but it combines lots of different tests. There is the heat of the Greek day, and then the plunge in temperatures when darkness falls. There are climbs: the route includes a series of ascents, among them a 1,200-meter mountain pass in the dead of night. Above all, there is the relentless pressure of the clock. The second reason is that the idea of retracing Pheidippides’s footsteps still grips many participants. It feels like racing in history, passing through places where history began.

As finishers receive a laurel wreath and water from schoolgirls, many are overjoyed with emotion. However, the euphoria is fleeting. Within a few minutes, their joints and muscles start to seize up: after the race, Sparti resembles the set of a zombie film as participants lumber slowly around on legs that will not bend. But the itch to do it all over again soon appears.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
斯巴達松是世界上最艱難的超級馬拉松之一，跑者要在 36 小時內跑完 245 公里，大約是六場馬拉松的距離。跑者從雅典出發，一路跑到歷史悠久的斯巴達。

斯巴達松的由來，可以追溯到西元前 490 年。當時雅典人 Pheidippides 一路跑到斯巴達，請斯巴達人幫忙抵抗入侵的波斯人。根據記載，他離開雅典的隔天就抵達了斯巴達。1982 年，這個故事引起了英國空軍軍官、長跑選手 John Foden 的興趣，他想知道從雅典跑到斯巴達，隔天就抵達，是不是真的做得到。Foden 和另外四名軍官決定親自試試看；經過 36 小時的艱苦跋涉，他們抵達了 Sparti，也就是斯巴達現在的名稱。這次的成就，促成了一年後第一屆斯巴達松的舉辦。

斯巴達松的吸引力有兩個來源。第一個是難以跑完。斯巴達松不是最難的比賽，卻結合了許多不同的考驗。有希臘白天的酷熱，入夜以後又有驟降的氣溫。有爬坡：路線有一連串的上坡，其中包括在深夜翻越一個 1,200 公尺高的山口。最重要的是，時間的壓力一刻也不放鬆。第二個原因是，重走 Pheidippides 足跡的想法，仍然深深吸引著許多參賽者。那種感覺就像在歷史中賽跑，經過歷史開始的地方。

完賽的跑者從女學生手中接過桂冠和水，許多人激動得欣喜若狂。不過，這種興奮很快就消失了。幾分鐘之內，他們的關節和肌肉就開始僵硬：賽後的 Sparti 看起來就像殭屍電影的片場，參賽者拖著彎不了的雙腿，步履蹣跚地慢慢走來走去。但想要再跑一次的念頭，很快又冒了出來。

items.stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?
options: The story of Pheidippides in ancient Athens.
items.explanation:
The Spartathlon’s heritage goes back to 490 B.C.
That achievement inspired the organization of the first Spartathlon a year later.
第 2 段第一句說斯巴達松的由來可以追溯到（heritage goes back to）西元前 490 年，接著說 Pheidippides 跑到斯巴達的故事，以及 1982 年 Foden 實際跑了一次，最後一句說這次成就促成了第一屆斯巴達松。整段講的是斯巴達松的由來，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 John Foden，這一段只說了他的身分，重點是他跑了一次，促成了比賽；(D) 照抄 Pheidippides，古代的故事只是由來的開頭，過於狹隘；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 route，路線上的爬坡是第 3 段的內容。

items.stem: Why do ultra-runners choose the Spartathlon?
options: It is the most classical ultra-marathon in the world.
Runners feel like racing through history.
Their personal problems will be solved in the race.
They have to finish all the tests in one day.
items.explanation:
The second reason is that the idea of retracing Pheidippides’s footsteps still grips many participants.
It feels like racing in history, passing through places where history began.
第 3 段說斯巴達松的吸引力有兩個來源，第二個是重走 Pheidippides 足跡的想法深深吸引參賽者，感覺就像在歷史中賽跑（racing in history），所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 tests，原文說斯巴達松結合了許多不同的考驗，跑者有 36 小時，不是一天之內要完成所有考驗；(A) 第 3 段說斯巴達松不是最難的比賽，原文也沒有說它是最經典的超級馬拉松；(C) 原文沒有提到個人問題。

items.stem: What does the euphoria is fleeting in the last paragraph mean?
options: The feeling of triumph will last forever.
The race is incomprehensibly difficult to finish.
The fatigue after the race is overwhelming.
The excitement of finishing the race is soon gone.
items.explanation:
However, the euphoria is fleeting.
Within a few minutes, their joints and muscles start to seize up
這一題答對率只有 37%，euphoria 和 fleeting 兩個字都不常見，要從前後句推。判斷步驟：[1] 前一句說完賽的跑者欣喜若狂（overjoyed），However 轉折以後說 the euphoria，euphoria 指的就是這種狂喜；[2] 下一句說幾分鐘之內（Within a few minutes），關節和肌肉就開始僵硬，狂喜維持不了多久；[3] 所以 fleeting 是「短暫的」，答案是 (D) 完賽的興奮很快就消失了。(A) 和 fleeting 的意思相反；(C) 疲勞是下一句的內容，不是 euphoria 的意思；(B) 比賽難跑完是第 3 段的內容。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about the Spartathlon?
options: The Spartathlon was first organized in 1983.
The event of the Spartathlon was made into a movie.
After completing the race, many decide not to try it again.
The runners have to endure high temperature day and night.
items.explanation:
In 1982, this story sparked the interest
That achievement inspired the organization of the first Spartathlon a year later.
這一題答對率只有 50%，要自己算年份。第 2 段說 1982 年 Foden 和另外四名軍官跑了一次，這次的成就促成一年後（a year later）第一屆斯巴達松的舉辦，1982 年的一年後是 1983 年，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 again，第 4 段最後說想再跑一次的念頭很快又冒出來，選項說反了；(D) 第 3 段說白天酷熱，入夜以後氣溫驟降，不是日夜都高溫；(B) 第 4 段說賽後的 Sparti 看起來像殭屍電影的片場，這是比喻，比賽並沒有拍成電影。

閱讀測驗.title: 小說家童妮·摩里森（Novelist Toni Morrison）
閱讀測驗.passage:
American writer Toni Morrison was born in 1931 in Ohio. She was raised in an African American family filled with songs and stories of Southern myths, which later shaped her prose. Her happy family life led to her excellent performance in school, despite the atmosphere of racial discrimination in the society.

After graduating from college, Morrison started to work as a teacher and got married in 1958. Several years later, her marriage began to fail. For a temporary escape, she joined a small writers’ group, in which each member was required to bring a story or poem for discussion. She wrote a story based on the life of a girl she knew in childhood who had prayed to God for blue eyes. The story was well received by the group, but then she put it away, thinking she was done with it.

In 1964, Morrison got divorced and devoted herself to writing. One day, she dusted off the story she had written for the writers’ group and decided to make it into a novel. She drew on her memories from childhood and expanded upon them using her imagination so that the characters developed a life of their own. The Bluest Eye was eventually published in 1970. From 1970 to 1992, Morrison published five more novels.

In her novels, Morrison brings in different elements of the African American past, their struggles, problems and cultural memory. In Song of Solomon, for example, Morrison tells the story of an African American man and his search for identity in his culture. The novels and other works won her several prizes. In 1993, Morrison received the Nobel Prize in Literature. She is the eighth woman and the first African American woman to win the honor.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
美國作家童妮·摩里森（Toni Morrison）1931 年生於俄亥俄州。她在一個非裔美國人家庭長大，家裡充滿了美國南方神話的歌謠和故事，這些歌謠和故事後來形塑了她的文字風格。雖然當時社會上瀰漫著種族歧視的氣氛，幸福的家庭生活仍讓她在學校表現優異。

大學畢業後，摩里森開始教書，1958 年結婚。幾年後，她的婚姻開始出問題。為了暫時逃離，她加入一個小型的寫作社團，每位社員都要帶一篇故事或一首詩來討論。她以童年認識的一個女孩為藍本寫了一篇故事，那個女孩曾經向上帝祈求擁有一雙藍眼睛。這篇故事在社團裡大受好評，但她之後就把故事收了起來，以為這篇故事已經寫完了。

1964 年，摩里森離婚，從此專心寫作。有一天，她把當年替寫作社團寫的那篇故事翻出來，決定擴寫成小說。她取材自童年的記憶，再用想像力加以擴充，讓書中的角色有了自己的生命。《最藍的眼睛》終於在 1970 年出版。從 1970 年到 1992 年，摩里森又出版了五本小說。

摩里森在小說裡融入非裔美國人過去的種種：他們的奮鬥、遭遇的問題和文化記憶。例如在《所羅門之歌》裡，摩里森講述一個非裔美國男子在自己的文化中尋找自我認同的故事。她的小說和其他作品替她贏得好幾個獎項。1993 年，摩里森獲得諾貝爾文學獎，是第八位得到這項榮譽的女性，也是第一位獲獎的非裔美國女性。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The life of black people in the U.S.
The life of an African American writer.
The history of African American culture.
The history of the Nobel Prize in Literature.
items.explanation: 第 1 段寫摩里森的出生和成長，第 2 段寫她教書、結婚、加入寫作社團，第 3 段寫她離婚後專心寫作、出版小說，第 4 段寫她作品的主題和得獎。全文依時間寫一位非裔美國作家的一生，所以是 (B)。(A) 把話題拉大到美國所有黑人的生活，太過廣泛；(C) 非裔美國人的過去是她小說的題材，文章沒有交代非裔美國文化的歷史，偏離主題；(D) 第 4 段只說她得到諾貝爾文學獎，文章沒有談這個獎的歷史，也偏離主題。

items.stem: Why did Morrison join the writers’ group?
options: She wanted to publish The Bluest Eye.
She wanted to fight racial discrimination.
She wanted to be a professional writer.
She wanted to get away from her unhappy marriage.
items.explanation:
Several years later, her marriage began to fail.
For a temporary escape, she joined a small writers’ group
