第 2 段說摩里森的婚姻開始出問題（her marriage began to fail），為了暫時逃離（escape），她加入寫作社團，選項換成 get away from her unhappy marriage。(A) 照抄書名 The Bluest Eye，她在社團寫的只是一篇故事，而且寫完就收起來，離婚後才擴寫成小說；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 racial discrimination，種族歧視是她成長時的社會氣氛，和加入社團無關；(C) 原文說她以為那篇故事寫完就結束了，看不出她當時想當職業作家。

items.stem: According to the passage, what is one of the themes in Morrison’s works?
options: A search for African American values.
Divorced black women in American society.
Songs and stories of African Americans in Ohio.
History of African Americans from the 1970s through the 1990s.
items.explanation:
In her novels, Morrison brings in different elements of the African American past, their struggles, problems and cultural memory.
In Song of Solomon, for example, Morrison tells the story of an African American man and his search for identity in his culture.
第 4 段說摩里森在小說裡融入非裔美國人的過去和文化記憶，並以《所羅門之歌》為例：一個非裔美國男子在自己的文化中尋找自我認同（search for identity in his culture）。在自己的文化裡找認同，就是在找非裔美國人的價值，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 1970，1970 到 1992 年是她陸續出版小說的期間，不是作品描寫的年代；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 songs and stories，那是她家裡的南方神話歌謠和故事，影響的是她的文字風格；(B) 照抄 divorced，離婚是她自己的經歷，文章沒說作品寫離婚的黑人女性。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about Toni Morrison?
options: She has been writing a lot since her adolescent years.
She suffered from severe racial discrimination in her family.
What she wrote in her novels are true stories of African Americans.
No African American woman ever received a Nobel Prize in Literature before her.
items.explanation:
She is the eighth woman and the first African American woman to win the honor.
第 4 段說摩里森是第一位得到諾貝爾文學獎的非裔美國女性（the first African American woman），選項換個方向說：在她之前沒有一位非裔美國女性得過這個獎。(B) 照抄 racial discrimination，第 1 段說社會上有種族歧視，她的家庭生活卻很幸福，不是在家裡受到歧視；(A) 第 2 段說她婚姻出問題後加入寫作社團，才寫了第一篇故事，不是從青少年時期就大量寫作；(C) 第 3 段說她取材自童年記憶，再用想像力擴充，不全是真實故事。

閱讀測驗.title: 伊曼紐三兄弟的成功之道（The Success of the Emanuel Brothers）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Below is an excerpt from an interview with Zeke Emanuel, a health-policy expert, on his famous brothers.

Interviewer: You’re the older brother of Rahm, the mayor of Chicago, and Ari, an extremely successful talent agent. And you’re a bioethicist and one of the architects of Obamacare. Isn’t writing a book about how great your family is a bit odd?

Zeke: I don’t write a book about how great my family is. There are lots of idiocies and foolishness—a lot to make fun of in the book. I wrote Brothers Emanuel because I had begun jotting stories for my kids. And then we began getting a lot of questions: What did Mom put in the cereal? Three successful brothers, all different areas.

I: To what do you attribute the Emanuel brothers’ success?

Z: I would put success in quotes. We strive. First, I think we got this striving from our mother to make the world a better place. A second important thing is you never rest on the last victory. There’s always more to do. And maybe the third important thing is my father’s admonition that offense is the best defense. We don’t give up.

I: Do you still not have a TV?

Z: I don’t own a TV. I don’t own a car. I don’t Facebook. I don’t tweet.

I: But you have four cell phones.

Z: I’m down to two, thankfully.

I: Your brothers are a national source of fascination. Where do you think they’ll be in five years?

Z: Ari will be a superagent running the same company. Rahm would still be mayor of Chicago. I will probably continue to be my academic self. The one thing I can guarantee is none of us will have taken a cruise, none of us will be sitting on a beach with a pina colada.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
以下節錄自一篇訪談，受訪者是衛生政策專家 Zeke Emanuel，談的是他那兩個有名的弟弟。

訪問者：你的弟弟 Rahm 是芝加哥市長，另一個弟弟 Ari 是非常成功的演藝經紀人，你是他們的哥哥。你本身是生命倫理學家，也是歐巴馬健保的設計者之一。寫一本書講自己的家人有多了不起，不覺得有點奇怪嗎？

Zeke：我寫的不是一本講我家人有多了不起的書。書裡有很多蠢事和傻事，有很多可以拿來取笑的地方。我寫《Brothers Emanuel》，是因為我原本開始替孩子們隨手記下一些故事。後來就有很多人來問我們：媽媽到底在麥片裡放了什麼？三兄弟都很成功，而且在不同的領域。

訪：你認為 Emanuel 兄弟成功的原因是什麼？

Z：「成功」這兩個字我會加上引號。我們是在努力。第一，我想我們這股努力的勁是從母親那裡來的，她希望讓世界變得更好。第二個重點是，永遠不要因為上一次的勝利就停下來，要做的事永遠還有。第三個重點，或許是父親的告誡：攻擊是最好的防禦。我們不放棄。

訪：你現在還是沒有電視嗎？

Z：我沒有電視，沒有車，不用臉書，也不發推特。

訪：但是你有四支手機。

Z：還好，我已經減到兩支了。

訪：全國都對你的兩個弟弟很感興趣。你認為五年後他們會在哪裡？

Z：Ari 會是一個超級經紀人，經營同一家公司。Rahm 應該還是芝加哥市長。我大概還是會繼續當學者。我唯一能保證的是，我們三個沒有人會去搭郵輪，也沒有人會坐在海灘上喝鳳梨可樂達。

items.stem: What does Zeke Emanuel have in mind when saying “What did Mom put in the cereal?”
options: The secret to bringing up successful kids.
The recipe for a breakfast food.
items.explanation:
And then we began getting a lot of questions: What did Mom put in the cereal? Three successful brothers, all different areas.
第 3 段說書出版後很多人來問：媽媽到底在麥片裡放了什麼？後面緊接著說三兄弟都很成功，而且在不同的領域。大家問的不是麥片，而是媽媽做了什麼，才養出三個成功的兒子，所以是 (A) 教出成功孩子的祕訣。(B) 只看字面，把 cereal 當成真的早餐；(D) 照抄 questions，這些問題是別人來問 Zeke 的，Zeke 的孩子是他寫故事的對象；(C) 三兄弟各在不同領域是問題的背景，大家想知道的是成功的原因。

items.stem: What does Zeke Emanuel think of the modern conveniences mentioned in the interview?
options: One can live without many of them.
items.explanation:
I don’t own a TV. I don’t own a car. I don’t Facebook. I don’t tweet.
I’m down to two, thankfully.
第 7 段 Zeke 說自己沒有電視、沒有車、不用臉書、不發推特；第 9 段說手機從四支減到兩支，還說了 thankfully（還好）。他少了這些東西照樣過日子，甚至樂於減少，所以是 (C) 很多東西沒有也能過活。(A) 遲做總比不做好、(B) 熟能生巧這兩句諺語和他的生活方式接不上；(D) 他不用這些東西，看不出他認為這些是偉大的發明。

items.stem: According to Zeke Emanuel, which of the following is a reason for the brothers’ success?
options: They defend themselves by attacking others.
They learn a lot from great people’s quotes.
They are committed to glorifying their parents.
They keep moving forward even after a big success.
items.explanation:
A second important thing is you never rest on the last victory.
There’s always more to do.
第 5 段說第二個重點是永遠不因上一次的勝利停下來（never rest on the last victory），要做的事永遠還有，選項換成 keep moving forward even after a big success。(B) 照抄 quotes，put success in quotes 是把「成功」加上引號，表示他不敢自稱成功，不是向名人的名言學習；(A) 父親說的攻擊是最好的防禦，意思是主動出擊、不放棄，Zeke 接著就說「我們不放棄」，不是靠攻擊別人保護自己；(C) 母親給他們的是讓世界更好的期許，文章沒說三兄弟要替父母增光。

items.stem: Which of the following best summarizes Zeke Emanuel’s response to the last question?
options: The brothers look forward to a family trip on a cruise.
Nothing much will change in the near future for them.
Higher positions and more power will be their goals.
None of the brothers will go to the beach.
items.explanation:
Ari will be a superagent running the same company.
Rahm would still be mayor of Chicago.
I will probably continue to be my academic self.
訪問者最後問五年後兄弟三人會在哪裡，Zeke 回答：Ari 還是經營同一家公司，Rahm 應該還是芝加哥市長，自己大概還是當學者。三個人都繼續做現在的事，所以是 (B) 近期不會有什麼改變。(A) 照抄 cruise，原文說的正好相反，三兄弟沒有人會去搭郵輪；(D) 照抄 beach，沒有人會坐在海灘上喝調酒，是用來說明他們不會停下來享樂，只是回答裡的一個細節，不能代表整段的意思；(C) Zeke 沒說三兄弟要追求更高的職位和權力。

閱讀測驗.title: 大規模線上開放課程（MOOCs）
閱讀測驗.passage:
MOOC, a massive open online course, aims at providing large-scale interactive participation and open access via the web. In addition to traditional course materials such as videos, readings, and problem sets, MOOCs provide interactive user forums that help build a community for the students, professors, and teaching assistants.

MOOCs first made waves in the fall of 2011, when Professor Sebastian Thrun from Stanford University opened his graduate-level artificial intelligence course up to any student anywhere, and 160,000 students in more than 190 countries signed up. This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways. Since the courses can be taken by hundreds of thousands of students at the same time, the number of universities might decrease dramatically. Professor Thrun has even envisioned a future in which there will only need to be 10 universities in the world. Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free. This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.

There is a lot of excitement and fear surrounding MOOCs. While some say free online courses are a great way to increase the enrollment of minority students, others have said they will leave many students behind. Some critics have said that MOOCs promote an unrealistic one-size-fits-all model of higher education and that there is no replacement for true dialogues between professors and their students. After all, a brain is not a computer. We are not blank hard drives waiting to be filled with data. People learn from people they love and remember the things that arouse emotion. Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
MOOC 是大規模線上開放課程，目標是透過網路提供大規模的互動參與和開放的學習管道。除了影片、閱讀材料和習題這些傳統的課程教材，MOOC 還提供互動式的使用者論壇，幫助學生、教授和助教建立一個社群。

MOOC 最早在 2011 年秋天引起轟動：史丹佛大學的 Sebastian Thrun 教授把他研究所程度的人工智慧課程開放給世界各地的任何學生，結果有 190 多個國家、16 萬名學生報名。這種新型態的線上課程在許多方面撼動了高等教育界。由於一門課可以同時讓數十萬名學生修讀，大學的數量可能會大幅減少。Thrun 教授甚至設想，未來全世界只需要 10 所大學。MOOC 有許多是由知名大學的教授授課，而它最引人注目的地方或許是免費。這對手頭很緊的學生來說當然是好消息。

MOOC 帶來許多期待，也引起許多擔憂。有些人說，免費的線上課程是增加少數族群學生入學人數的好方法；也有人說，這種課程會讓許多學生跟不上。有些批評者認為，MOOC 推行的是一種不切實際、一體適用的高等教育模式，而教授和學生之間真正的對話是無可取代的。畢竟，人腦不是電腦，我們不是等著裝滿資料的空白硬碟。人會向自己喜愛的人學習，也會記住引起情緒的事物。有些批評者擔心，線上學生會錯過大學的社交生活。

items.stem: What does the word “cash-strapped” in the second paragraph mean?
items.explanation:
Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free.
This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.
第 2 段說 MOOC 最引人注目的地方或許是免費，接著說這對 cash-strapped 學生當然是好消息。課程免費，最高興的會是缺錢的學生，所以 cash-strapped 是手頭很緊、缺錢，最接近 (B) Being short of money。(A) 賺很多錢，和「免費課程是好消息」接不上；(C) 用錢謹慎、(D) 花錢很少，說的是花錢的習慣，不是手頭缺錢。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the features of MOOCs?
options: It is free to take the courses.
Many courses are offered by famous universities.
Many students can take the course at the same time.
items.explanation:
Since the courses can be taken by hundreds of thousands of students at the same time,
many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities
is that they’re free.
文章提到的三個特色在選項都換了說法：第 2 段說 MOOC 最引人注目的是免費（they’re free），是 (A)；許多課程由知名大學的教授授課（professors at prestigious universities），是 (B)；一門課可以同時讓數十萬名學生修讀，是 (D)。人工智慧只是 Thrun 教授開的那一門課，文章沒說大部分的課程都在講人工智慧，所以選 (C)。

items.stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?
items.explanation:
This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways.
第 2 段先說 MOOC 在 2011 年引起轟動，接著用 This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways 點出重點：這種課程在許多方面撼動高等教育界。後面說的大學數量可能大減、全世界只需要 10 所大學、免費對手頭很緊的學生是好消息，都是它帶來的影響，所以是 (A)。(C) 課程規模和 (D) 費用都只是這一段用來說明影響的細節；(B) 目標是第 1 段的內容。

items.stem: Which of the following is a problem of MOOCs mentioned in the passage?
options: The disappearance of traditional course materials.
The limited number of courses offered around the world.
The overreliance on professors from prestigious universities.
The lack of social interaction among students and professors.
items.explanation:
there is no replacement for true dialogues between professors and their students
Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.
第 3 段批評者說教授和學生之間真正的對話無可取代，也擔心線上學生會錯過大學的社交生活（social aspects of college），選項換成 lack of social interaction among students and professors。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 traditional course materials，原文說 MOOC 除了傳統教材之外還有論壇，教材並沒有消失；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 prestigious universities，知名大學的教授授課是 MOOC 的特色，不是問題；(B) 文章沒說課程數量有限，第 2 段說可能減少的是大學的數量。

閱讀測驗.title: 自動駕駛汽車的未來（The Future of Driverless Cars）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Today the car seems to make periodic leaps in progress. A variety of driver assistance technologies are appearing on new cars. A developing technology called Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication, or V2V, is being tested by automotive manufacturers as a way to help reduce the number of accidents. V2V works by using wireless signals to send information back and forth between cars about their location, speed and direction, so that they keep safe distances from each other. Another new technology being tested is Vehicle-to-Infrastructure communication, or V2I. V2I would allow vehicles to communicate with road signs or traffic signals and provide information to the vehicle about safety issues. V2I could also request traffic information from a traffic management system and access the best possible routes. Both V2V and V2I have the potential to reduce around 80 percent of vehicle crashes on the road.

More and more new cars can reverse-park, read traffic signs, maintain a safe distance in steady traffic and brake automatically to avoid crashes. Moreover, a number of firms are creating cars that drive themselves to a chosen destination without a human at the controls. It is predicted that driverless cars will be ready for sale within five years. If and when cars go completely driverless, the benefits will be enormous. Google, which already uses prototypes of such cars to ferry its staff along Californian freeways, once put a blind man in a prototype and filmed him being driven off to buy takeaway hamburgers. If this works, huge numbers of elderly and disabled people can regain their personal mobility. The young will not have to pay crippling motor insurance, because their reckless hands and feet will no longer touch the wheel or the accelerator. People who commute by car will gain hours each day to work, rest, or read a newspaper.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
現今汽車似乎每隔一段時間就有大躍進。各式各樣的駕駛輔助技術紛紛出現在新車上。一項發展中的技術叫做車對車通訊（Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication，簡稱 V2V），汽車製造商正在測試這項技術，希望藉此減少事故的數量。V2V 的運作方式是用無線訊號在車輛之間互相傳送位置、速度和方向等資訊，讓車輛彼此保持安全距離。另一項正在測試的新技術是車對基礎設施通訊（Vehicle-to-Infrastructure communication，簡稱 V2I）。V2I 能讓車輛和道路標誌或交通號誌溝通，並且提供車輛安全相關的資訊。V2I 也可以向交通管理系統要求路況資訊，找出最佳路線。V2V 和 V2I 都有潛力減少道路上大約 80% 的車禍。

越來越多新車能自動倒車入庫、辨識交通標誌、在車流穩定時保持安全車距，還能自動煞車避免撞車。此外，好幾家公司正在研發不需要人操控、自己開到指定目的地的汽車。據預測，無人駕駛汽車五年內就能上市。如果汽車真有完全無人駕駛的一天，好處會非常大。Google 已經用這種車的原型車在加州的高速公路上接送員工，還曾讓一位盲人坐進原型車，拍下他坐車去買外帶漢堡的過程。如果這行得通，大批年長者和身心障礙者就能重新自由行動。年輕人不必再付高得嚇人的汽車保險費，因為他們莽撞的手腳再也不會碰到方向盤和油門。開車通勤的人每天會多出好幾個小時，可以工作、休息或看報紙。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about V2V?
options: V2V communication has been very well developed.
Through V2V, drivers can chat with each other on the road.
V2V is designed to decrease crashes by keeping safe distances.
Through V2V, a car can warn cyclists nearby of its approach.
items.explanation:
is being tested by automotive manufacturers as a way to help reduce the number of accidents.
so that they keep safe distances from each other.
第 1 段說 V2V 的目的是減少事故的數量（reduce the number of accidents），做法是讓車輛之間互傳資訊、保持安全距離（keep safe distances），選項換成 decrease crashes by keeping safe distances。(A) 原文說 V2V 是發展中的技術（a developing technology），還在測試，不是已經發展得很成熟；(B) V2V 傳送的是位置、速度和方向，不是讓駕駛彼此聊天；(D) 原文講的是車和車之間，沒有提到騎單車的人。

items.stem: What does “infrastructure” in Vehicle-to-Infrastructure refer to?
options: The basic structure of roads and bridges.
Knowledge and regulations about safe driving.
The traffic department of the government.
items.explanation:
V2I would allow vehicles to communicate with road signs or traffic signals and provide information to the vehicle about safety issues.
V2I could also request traffic information from a traffic management system and access the best possible routes.
第 1 段說 V2I 讓車輛和道路標誌、交通號誌（road signs or traffic signals）溝通，也能向交通管理系統（traffic management system）要路況資訊。和車輛溝通的這兩類東西，選項概括成 traffic facilities and information systems，所以是 (A)。(B) 道路和橋梁的基本結構是 infrastructure 的一般意思，但這篇裡和車輛溝通的是號誌和系統，不是道路本身；(C) 安全駕駛的知識和法規、(D) 政府的交通部門，文章都沒提。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a potential benefit of driverless cars?
options: The elderly will become more mobile.
“Drivers” can sleep in cars all the way to work.
People can race cars to their heart’s content.
A blind man can get into a car and travel safely.
items.explanation:
once put a blind man in a prototype and filmed him being driven off to buy takeaway hamburgers.
If this works, huge numbers of elderly and disabled people can regain their personal mobility.
People who commute by car will gain hours each day to work, rest, or read a newspaper.
有提到的三個好處都在第 2 段，選項換了說法：elderly people can regain their personal mobility 是 (A)；讓盲人坐原型車去買漢堡是 (D)；通勤的人每天多出時間休息（rest）是 (B) 在車上一路睡到公司。文章沒說無人車能讓人盡情飆車，原文反而說年輕人莽撞的手腳再也不會碰到方向盤和油門，所以選 (C)。

items.stem: What can be inferred from the passage?
options: Cars will refuse to start if the driver is drunk.
The future may be a vehicle-accident-free era.
Everyone, including children, can afford a car.
The production of driverless cars is still far away.
items.explanation:
Both V2V and V2I have the potential to reduce around 80 percent of vehicle crashes on the road.
brake automatically to avoid crashes
第 1 段說 V2V 和 V2I 有潛力減少大約 80% 的車禍，第 2 段說新車已經能自動煞車避免撞車，再加上不需要人操控的無人車。這些技術一起發展下去，可以推論未來可能是沒有車禍的時代，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 driverless cars，原文說無人車預計五年內上市，不是還很遙遠；(A) 文章沒有談酒駕；(C) 原文說的是年輕人不必付高額保險費，沒說包括兒童在內每個人都買得起車。

閱讀測驗.title: 布魯克林大橋的興建（The Building of the Brooklyn Bridge）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Opened in 1883, the Brooklyn Bridge was the first long-span suspension bridge to carry motor traffic, and it quickly became the model for the great suspension bridges of the following century. Spanning New York’s East River, it provided the first traffic artery between Manhattan Island and Brooklyn. Before that, the only transportation was by ferries, which were slow and could be dangerous in winter.

The construction of a bridge over the East River had been discussed since the early 19th century, but the outbreak of the Civil War in 1861 deflected all consideration of the project. When the war ended in 1865, the bridge became an important issue once more. In 1867, the New York State legislature passed an act incorporating the New York Bridge Company for the purpose of constructing and maintaining a bridge between Manhattan Island and Brooklyn.

John Augustus Roebling was chosen to design the bridge. Born in Germany in 1806, he held radical views as a student and was listed by the German police as a dangerous liberal. He emigrated to America in 1830 to escape political discrimination.

Roebling proposed a bridge with a span of 1,500 feet (465 m), with two masonry towers in the East River serving as the main piers. The bridge that was actually built is longer—1,597 feet (486 m), the longest suspension bridge at that time.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
布魯克林大橋在 1883 年啟用，是第一座通行汽車的長跨距吊橋，很快就成了下一個世紀各大吊橋的典範。這座橋橫跨紐約的東河，提供了曼哈頓島和布魯克林之間的第一條交通幹道。在那之前，唯一的交通方式是搭渡輪，渡輪速度慢，冬天還可能有危險。

從 19 世紀初，就有人討論要在東河上建一座橋，但是 1861 年南北戰爭爆發，大家就不再考慮這項計畫。1865 年戰爭結束，建橋再度成為重要的議題。1867 年，紐約州議會通過一項法案，成立紐約橋梁公司，目的是在曼哈頓島和布魯克林之間建造並維護一座橋。

大橋的設計者，選定了 John Augustus Roebling。他 1806 年在德國出生，學生時代思想激進，德國警方把他列為危險的自由派分子。1830 年，他為了逃避政治歧視，移民到美國。

Roebling 提議的橋，跨距是 1,500 英尺（465 公尺），以東河中的兩座石造塔作為主要的橋墩。實際建成的橋更長，有 1,597 英尺（486 公尺），是當時最長的吊橋。

items.stem: What was the purpose of building the Brooklyn Bridge?
options: To set up a model for bridge construction.
To build a suspension bridge for the Civil War.
To provide faster and safer transportation than boats.
items.explanation:
Before that, the only transportation was by ferries, which were slow and could be dangerous in winter.
第 1 段說大橋提供了曼哈頓島和布魯克林之間的第一條交通幹道，在那之前只能搭渡輪（ferries），渡輪速度慢（slow），冬天還可能有危險（dangerous）。建橋是為了提供比船更快、更安全的交通，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 model，大橋成為後來吊橋的典範，是建好以後的結果，不是建橋的目的；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 Civil War，南北戰爭反而讓建橋計畫停了下來；(A) 原文說這是第一條交通幹道，之前沒有橋，談不上取代舊橋。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “deflected” in the second paragraph?
items.explanation:
but the outbreak of the Civil War in 1861 deflected all consideration of the project.
When the war ended in 1865, the bridge became an important issue once more.
deflect 原來的意思是「使轉向」，例如球打到東西以後彈開、改變方向。這一句用 but 轉折：19 世紀初就有人討論建橋，但南北戰爭爆發，deflected 了所有對這項計畫的考慮；下一句又說戰爭結束以後，建橋再度（once more）成為重要議題。可見戰爭期間大家的注意力轉到別處，計畫停了下來，所以是 (A) 擋下來了。(C) 投入、(D) 指出，都和下一句的 once more 接不上；(B) 察覺，和 consideration 放在一起意思說不通。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about the Brooklyn Bridge?
options: It is shorter than originally planned.
It was first proposed after the Civil War.
It was built by the New York Bridge Company.
items.explanation:
In 1867, the New York State legislature passed an act incorporating the New York Bridge Company for the purpose of constructing and maintaining a bridge
第 2 段說 1867 年紐約州議會通過法案，成立紐約橋梁公司（the New York Bridge Company），目的是建造（constructing）並維護這座橋，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 1865，那是南北戰爭結束的年份，大橋 1883 年才啟用；(C) 照抄 Civil War，19 世紀初就有人討論建橋，比南北戰爭早；(B) 第 4 段說實際建成的橋比原來提議的 1,500 英尺更長，選項說反了。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following correctly describes John Augustus Roebling?
options: He participated in the Civil War and was seriously wounded.
He was chosen to design the bridge because of his radical views.
He was the first person to propose the construction of the bridge.
He moved to America because he was discriminated against in his home country.
items.explanation:
He emigrated to America in 1830 to escape political discrimination.
第 3 段說 Roebling 1830 年移民到美國（emigrated to America），為的是逃避政治歧視（political discrimination），選項換成他因為在祖國受到歧視而搬到美國，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 radical views，激進的思想是他學生時代在德國的事，原文沒有說他因此獲選設計大橋；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 Civil War，原文沒有說他參加南北戰爭；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 proposed，他提議的是橋的設計，19 世紀初就有人討論建橋了。

閱讀測驗.title: 社會連結對健康的影響（The Power of Social Connection on Health）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The Japanese have long puzzled public health researchers because they are such an apparent paradox: They have the world’s lowest rates of heart disease and the largest number of people that live to or beyond 100 years despite the fact that most Japanese men smoke—and smoking counts as one of the strongest risk factors for heart disease. So what’s protecting Japanese men?

Two professors at the University of California at Berkeley hoped to find out the answer. They investigated a pool of 12,000 Japanese men equally divided into three groups: One group had lived in Japan for all their lives, and the other two groups had emigrated to Hawaii or Northern California. It was found that the rate of heart disease among Japanese men increased five times in California and about half of that for those in Hawaii.

The differences could not be explained by any of the usual risk factors for heart disease, such as smoking, high blood pressure, or cholesterol counts. The change in diet, from sushi to hamburgers and fries, was also not related to the rise in heart disease. However, the kind of society they had created for themselves in their new home country was. The most traditional group of Japanese Americans, who maintained tight-knit and mutually supportive social groups, had a heart-attack rate as low as their fellow Japanese back home. But those who had adopted the more isolated Western lifestyle increased their heart-attack incidence by three to five times.

The study shows that the need to bond with a social group is so fundamental to humans that it remains the key determinant of whether we stay healthy or get ill, even whether we live or die. We need to feel part of something bigger to thrive. We need to belong, not online, but in the real world of hugs, handshakes, and pats on the back.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
日本人長久以來一直讓公共衛生研究人員感到困惑，因為他們明顯是一個矛盾的現象：雖然大多數日本男性抽菸，而抽菸是心臟病最主要的危險因子之一，日本人卻是全世界心臟病發生率最低、活到 100 歲以上的人數最多的國家。那麼，是什麼在保護日本男性呢？

加州大學柏克萊分校的兩位教授希望找出答案。他們調查了 12,000 名日本男性，平均分成三組：一組一輩子都住在日本，另外兩組移民到夏威夷或北加州。研究發現，移民到加州的日本男性，心臟病發生率增加為五倍；移民到夏威夷的，增加的倍數大約是加州的一半。

這些差異，無法用抽菸、高血壓或膽固醇指數這些常見的心臟病危險因子來解釋。從壽司改吃漢堡和薯條的飲食變化，也和心臟病增加無關。然而，他們在新的國家為自己建立的社會型態，卻和心臟病增加有關。最傳統的那一群日裔美國人，維持著緊密、互相扶持的社會團體，心臟病發作的比率和日本本地的同胞一樣低。但是，採用西方比較孤立的生活方式的人，心臟病發作的比率增加了三到五倍。

這項研究顯示，和社會團體建立連結，是人類非常基本的需求，基本到仍然是決定我們健康或生病、甚至存活或死亡的關鍵。我們需要覺得自己屬於某個更大的群體，才能過得好。我們需要歸屬感，不是在網路上，而是在真實的世界裡，在擁抱、握手和拍拍肩膀之中。

items.stem: What is the best title of this passage?
options: The Sense of Belonging vs. Isolation
items.explanation: 這一題答對率只有 52%，判斷的方法是先找出全文的結論在哪一段。第 1 段提出問題：日本男性大多抽菸，心臟病發生率卻最低，是什麼在保護他們？第 2、3 段說明研究結果：抽菸、飲食都無法解釋差異，有關的是社會型態；第 4 段說出結論：和社會團體建立連結，是決定健康的關鍵。全文講的是社會連結的力量，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 heart disease，心臟病只是研究用來衡量健康的指標，文章並沒有介紹心臟病的各種原因，太過廣泛；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 Japanese Americans，日裔美國人之間的差異只是研究的發現，過於狹隘；(D) 用 vs. 把歸屬感和孤立當成兩方來比較，卻沒有說到兩者對健康的影響，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following is a finding of the two American professors’ study?
options: Many Japanese men that lived up to 100 years were smokers.
Those who often ate hamburgers and fries were more likely to fall sick.
Japanese immigrants to America usually formed a tight-knit community.
Westernized social life was related to the heart-attack rate of Japanese Americans.
items.explanation:
However, the kind of society they had created for themselves in their new home country was.
But those who had adopted the more isolated Western lifestyle increased their heart-attack incidence by three to five times.
這一題答對率只有 54%，三個錯誤選項都照抄原文，但說的不是兩位教授的研究發現。第 3 段說，和心臟病增加有關的，是他們在新國家建立的社會型態；採用西方比較孤立的生活方式（Western lifestyle）的人，心臟病發作的比率增加三到五倍，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 100 years，日本人長壽、大多數男性抽菸是研究之前就知道的現象，原文也沒有說活到 100 歲的人大多抽菸；(B) 照抄 hamburgers and fries，第 3 段說飲食變化和心臟病增加無關；(C) 照抄 tight-knit，只有最傳統的那一群維持緊密的社群，原文沒有說日本移民通常都這樣。

items.stem: Which of the following is an example of “something bigger” in the last paragraph?
items.explanation:
We need to feel part of something bigger to thrive.
We need to belong, not online, but in the real world of hugs, handshakes, and pats on the back.
這一題答對率只有 45%，something bigger 不能照字面當成「體積更大的東西」。判斷步驟：[1] 這一段開頭說人需要和社會團體（a social group）建立連結；[2] something bigger 是比自己這個人更大的「群體」，就是前面說的社會團體；[3] 下一句又說這種歸屬感要在真實世界的擁抱、握手、拍肩裡，家人正是這樣的群體，所以是 (A)。(B) 體育場、(C) 宇宙，都是照字面把 bigger 解釋成體積大；(D) 照抄 world，原文說的是 real world，並且特別說歸屬感不是在網路上（not online），數位世界剛好相反。

items.stem: What is the ratio of heart disease between Japanese living in Japan and Japanese Americans in Hawaii?
items.explanation:
It was found that the rate of heart disease among Japanese men increased five times in California and about half of that for those in Hawaii.
這一題答對率只有 54%，要自己算。步驟：[1] 以住在日本的那一組為 1；[2] 第 2 段說移民到加州的心臟病發生率增加為五倍（five times），也就是 5；[3] 移民到夏威夷的，大約是加州的一半（about half of that），5 的一半是 2.5；[4] 日本和夏威夷的比例是 1 比 2.5，所以是 (A)。(B) 1 比 5 是日本和加州的比例；(C) 3 到 5 出自第 3 段的 three to five times，那是採用西方生活方式的人心臟病發作增加的倍數，不是夏威夷那一組。

閱讀測驗.title: 比特幣簡介與使用須知（Bitcoin: An Introduction and Cautions）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Bitcoin is an experimental, decentralized digital currency that enables instant payments to anyone, anywhere in the world. Bitcoin uses peer-to-peer technology to operate with no central authority; that is, managing transactions and issuing money are carried out collectively through the network.

Any transaction issued with Bitcoin cannot be reversed; it can only be refunded by the person receiving the funds. That means you should do business with people and organizations you know and trust, or who have an established reputation. Bitcoin can detect typos and usually won’t let you send money to an invalid address by mistake.

All Bitcoin transactions are stored publicly and permanently on the network, which means anyone can see the balance and transactions of any Bitcoin address. However, the identity of the user behind an address remains unknown until information is revealed during a purchase or in other circumstances.

The price of a bitcoin can unpredictably increase or decrease over a short period of time due to its young economy, novel nature, and sometimes illiquid markets. Consequently, keeping your savings with Bitcoin is not recommended at this point. Bitcoin should be seen like a high risk asset, and you should never store money that you cannot afford to lose with Bitcoin. If you receive payments with Bitcoin, many service providers can convert them to your local currency.

Bitcoin is an experimental new currency that is in active development. Although it becomes less experimental as usage grows, you should keep in mind that Bitcoin is a new invention that is exploring ideas that have never been attempted before. As such, its future cannot be predicted by anyone.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
比特幣是一種實驗性、去中心化的數位貨幣，能即時付款給世界上任何地方的任何人。比特幣用點對點的技術運作，沒有中央機構；也就是說，管理交易和發行貨幣，都由整個網路共同完成。

任何用比特幣進行的交易，都無法撤銷，只能由收款的人退款。這表示你應該和你認識、信任，或是已經建立良好信譽的人和機構往來。比特幣能偵測打錯的字，通常不會讓你不小心把錢轉到無效的地址。

所有的比特幣交易，都公開而且永久存放在網路上，這表示任何人都看得到任何一個比特幣地址的餘額和交易紀錄。不過，在購物或其他情況下揭露資訊以前，地址背後的使用者是誰，仍然沒有人知道。

由於比特幣的經濟還很年輕、性質很新，市場有時又缺乏流動性，比特幣的價格可能在短時間內無法預料地上漲或下跌。因此，目前不建議用比特幣存放儲蓄。應該把比特幣看作高風險的資產，輸不起的錢，絕對不要用比特幣存放。如果你收到比特幣付款，許多服務業者可以替你換成本國的貨幣。

比特幣是一種仍在積極發展的實驗性新貨幣。雖然使用的人越多，它的實驗性就越低，你還是要記得，比特幣是一項新的發明，正在探索前所未有的概念。正因為如此，沒有人能預測它的未來。

items.stem: What is the purpose of this article?
options: To prove the value of a young economy.
To explore ways to do online transactions.
To explain how to build up a business network.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說明比特幣是什麼、怎麼運作；第 2、3 段說交易無法撤銷、交易紀錄公開；第 4 段提醒價格不穩定，不要拿來存錢；第 5 段說比特幣還在發展，未來無法預測。全文在介紹比特幣這種新貨幣，以及使用時要注意的事，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 young economy，經濟還很年輕是價格不穩定的原因，文章是在提醒風險，不是證明它的價值，偏離主題；(C) 網路交易的方式很多，文章只談比特幣，太過廣泛；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 network，原文的網路指的是比特幣的運作系統，文章沒有談怎麼建立商業人脈，偏離主題。

items.stem: Why is the value of Bitcoin not stable?
options: Because it is not a valid investment.
Because its circulation is limited to the youth.
items.explanation:
due to its young economy, novel nature, and sometimes illiquid markets.
Bitcoin is an experimental new currency that is in active development.
第 4 段說比特幣的價格可能短時間內漲跌，原因是它的經濟還很年輕、性質很新；第 5 段說比特幣是仍在積極發展（in active development）的實驗性貨幣。還在發展中，所以價值不穩定，答案是 (C)。(D) 的 youth 和第 4 段的 young 看起來相關，但 young economy 是說比特幣的經濟剛起步，不是說只有年輕人在用；(A) 原文沒有說比特幣違法；(B) 原文說比特幣是高風險的資產，沒有說它不是有效的投資。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about Bitcoin?
options: Bitcoin addresses are known only to their owners.
Once a transaction is made, the Bitcoin cannot be refunded.
Bitcoin user’s identity is always open to the general public.
When a payment is received, the Bitcoin can be turned into local currency.
items.explanation:
If you receive payments with Bitcoin, many service providers can convert them to your local currency.
第 4 段最後一句說，收到比特幣付款，許多服務業者可以替你換成（convert）本國的貨幣（local currency），所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 address，原文說任何人都看得到任何比特幣地址的餘額和交易；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 refunded，交易無法撤銷，但收款人可以退款；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 identity，使用者的身分在揭露資訊以前沒有人知道，選項說反了。

items.stem: What advice would the author give to those who are interested in keeping money in Bitcoin?
options: Make hay while the sun shines.
items.explanation:
keeping your savings with Bitcoin is not recommended at this point.
you should never store money that you cannot afford to lose with Bitcoin.
第 4 段說目前不建議用比特幣存放儲蓄，輸不起的錢絕對不要放進去；第 5 段又說比特幣的未來沒有人能預測。作者是要想用比特幣存錢的人先想清楚風險，Look before you leap 是「三思而後行」，所以是 (B)。(A) Better late than never 是「晚做總比不做好」，(C) Make hay while the sun shines 是「打鐵趁熱」，(D) No pain, no gain 是「不勞則無獲」，這三句都是鼓勵人趕快去做，和作者提醒風險的意思相反。

閱讀測驗.title: 以基因改造蚊子對抗瘧疾（Genetically Modified Mosquitoes against Malaria）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Scientists are trying to genetically modify the world in which we live. They are even trying to wipe out diseases via genetic modification. For example, researchers have tried to engineer mosquitoes to kill malaria parasites. The malaria parasite is carried by the female Anopheles mosquito. When transmitted to a human, the parasite travels first to the liver and then on to the bloodstream, where it reproduces and destroys red blood cells. An estimated 250 million people suffer from malaria each year, and about one million die—many of them children. There are currently no effective or approved malaria vaccines.

To “kill” malaria, scientists are genetically modifying a bacterium in mosquitoes so that it releases toxic compounds. These compounds are not harmful to humans or the mosquito itself, but they do kill off the malaria parasite, making the mosquito incapable of infecting humans with malaria.

Despite this achievement, scientists are faced with the challenge of giving the modified mosquitoes a competitive advantage so that they can eventually replace the wild population. Complete blockage of the malaria parasite is very important. If some of the parasites slip through the mechanism, then the next generation will likely become resistant to it. And if that happens, the scientists are back where they started.

Another challenge for scientists is to gain public approval for this genetic modification regarding mosquitoes and malaria control. Environmental activists have raised concerns about the release of genetically engineered organisms without any clear knowledge of their long-term effect on ecosystems and human health. There is still a long way to go before genetic modification techniques are put to use in disease control.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
科學家正嘗試用基因改造來改變我們生活的世界，甚至想透過基因改造消滅疾病。例如，研究人員曾嘗試改造蚊子，讓蚊子殺死瘧疾寄生蟲。瘧疾寄生蟲由雌性瘧蚊攜帶。寄生蟲傳到人身上以後，先到肝臟，再進入血液，在血液裡繁殖，破壞紅血球。每年估計有 2.5 億人感染瘧疾，大約一百萬人死亡，其中有很多是兒童。目前還沒有有效、或經過核准的瘧疾疫苗。

為了「殺死」瘧疾，科學家正在改造蚊子體內的一種細菌，讓這種細菌釋放有毒的化合物。這些化合物對人和蚊子本身都無害，卻能殺死瘧疾寄生蟲，讓蚊子無法把瘧疾傳給人。

儘管有這項成果，科學家還要面對一個挑戰：讓改造過的蚊子具有競爭優勢，最後能取代野生的蚊子。完全阻斷瘧疾寄生蟲非常重要。要是有一些寄生蟲從這個機制中漏網，下一代很可能就會產生抗性。一旦發生這種情況，科學家就得從頭來過。

科學家的另一個挑戰，是讓大眾認同這項針對蚊子和瘧疾防治的基因改造。環保人士提出疑慮，擔心在還不清楚基因改造生物對生態系和人體健康有什麼長期影響的情況下，就把它們野放出去。基因改造技術要用在疾病防治上，還有很長的路要走。

items.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: Researchers have found an effective way to halt the spread of insect-borne diseases around the world.
Many people are worried about the effects of genetically modified organisms on the environment.
It takes time to gain public support for the application of genetic modification to disease control.
Genetic engineering looks promising in reducing malaria, though there may be unknown consequences.
items.explanation: 先看全文怎麼安排：第 1 段說瘧疾每年造成大約一百萬人死亡，還沒有有效的疫苗；第 2 段說科學家改造蚊子體內的細菌，讓蚊子無法傳播瘧疾；第 3、4 段說還有兩個挑戰，包括基因改造生物的長期影響還不清楚。主旨要同時說出這個方法有希望，也還有隱憂，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (A)，這個選項照抄第 1 段的 effective：原文只談瘧疾，不是全世界所有由蚊蟲傳播的疾病，而且第 3、4 段說還有很多挑戰，說已經找到有效的方法，說得太絕對，太過廣泛。(B) 照抄 environment、(C) 照抄 public，環保人士的疑慮和爭取大眾認同，都只是第 4 段的內容，過於狹隘。

items.stem: Which of the following best shows the organization of this passage?
items.explanation: 第 1 段說瘧疾每年造成大約一百萬人死亡，又沒有有效的疫苗，這是問題（Problem）；第 2 段說科學家改造蚊子體內的細菌，殺死瘧疾寄生蟲，這是解決方法（Solution）；第 3 段用 Despite this achievement 帶出第一個挑戰，第 4 段用 Another challenge 帶出第二個挑戰，這是可能遇到的困難（Potential difficulties）。所以是 (B)。(A) 全文沒有比較和對照；(C) 原文沒有正反兩方的辯論，第 4 段環保人士的疑慮是挑戰之一；(D) 第 1 段不是在下定義，最後也沒有暫時的結論。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about malaria parasites?
options: They are resistant to genetic modification and vaccines.
They reproduce in the human liver and grow stronger there.
They can be found in only one gender of a class of mosquitoes.
They are transmitted to around one million children each year.
items.explanation:
The malaria parasite is carried by the female Anopheles mosquito.
第 1 段說瘧疾寄生蟲由雌性（female）瘧蚊（Anopheles mosquito）攜帶。female 是一種性別（one gender），Anopheles 是蚊子裡的一類（a class of mosquitoes），所以只有一種性別的某一類蚊子身上有瘧疾寄生蟲，是 (C)。(B) 照抄 liver，寄生蟲先到肝臟，接著進入血液，在血液裡繁殖；(D) 照抄 one million，每年大約一百萬人死於瘧疾，其中很多是兒童，不是每年傳給一百萬名兒童；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 resistant，原文說下一代寄生蟲可能會對改造的機制產生抗性，這是還沒發生的情況，沒有疫苗也不表示寄生蟲對疫苗有抗性。

items.stem: What does “that” in the third paragraph refer to?
options: Some malaria parasites escaping from the ecosystems.
Malaria parasites becoming immune to the engineered bacterium.
Modified mosquitoes becoming more competitive than the wild ones.
Transmission of malaria being blocked from mosquitoes to humans.
items.explanation:
If some of the parasites slip through the mechanism, then the next generation will likely become resistant to it.
that 指前一句說的情況：要是有寄生蟲從這個機制漏網，下一代寄生蟲很可能對它產生抗性（become resistant to it）。句中的 it 指 the mechanism，也就是第 2 段說的方法，改造蚊子體內的細菌來殺死寄生蟲。選項把 resistant 換成 immune，把這個機制換成 the engineered bacterium，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 competitive，讓改造蚊子更有競爭力是科學家要達成的目標，如果做到了，不會「從頭來過」；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 ecosystems，生態系是環保人士擔心的事情，而且原文說的是寄生蟲從機制中漏網，不是從生態系逃走；(D) 阻斷瘧疾從蚊子傳給人，是第 2 段的成果，也不會讓科學家從頭來過。

閱讀測驗.title: 泰武國小古謠傳唱隊（Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In 2009, the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers were invited to perform in Belgium, France, Germany, and Luxemburg. In 2011, they were voted as one of the world’s top five performance groups by audiences of Japan Broadcasting Corporation’s Amazing Voice program.

Recalling the group’s first tour in Europe, Camake Valaule, a physical education teacher and the founder of the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers, admitted that he felt very nervous. He was worried that the audience would fall asleep since most of the 75-minute performance was a cappella, that is, singing without instrumental sound. Surprisingly, the audience listened with full focus and high spirits. Camake said, “They told me afterward that through our performance, they had a vision of our country, our village, without having to visit it. This experience greatly boosted our confidence.”

According to Camake Valaule, singing traditional ballads has helped students and their parents to re-understand their culture. “It used to be that the only ones who could sing these songs were tribal elders aged between 50 and 60. Now with the children performing the pieces, parents are beginning to ask, ‘Why do we not know how to sing these ballads?’ Many times nowadays, it is the children who teach the songs to their parents, putting back the pieces of a blurred memory.”

Winning international fame, however, was neither the original intention nor the main reason why Camake founded the group in 2006. The most important thing was to make children understand why they sing these songs and to preserve and pass on their culture. Referring to the relocation of Taiwu Elementary School and Taiwu Village following Typhoon Morakot in August 2009, Camake said, “We could not take the forest or our houses in the mountains with us; but we were able to bring our culture along. As long as the children are willing to sing, I will always be there for them, singing with them and leading them to experience the meaning of the ballads.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
2009 年，泰武國小古謠傳唱隊受邀到比利時、法國、德國和盧森堡演出。2011 年，傳唱隊獲日本放送協會（NHK）《Amazing Voice》節目的觀眾票選為全球五大表演團體之一。

體育老師 Camake Valaule 是泰武國小古謠傳唱隊的創辦人，回想起傳唱隊第一次到歐洲巡迴演出，他坦承當時非常緊張。75 分鐘的演出大部分是 a cappella，也就是沒有樂器伴奏的清唱，所以他擔心觀眾會睡著。出乎意料的是，觀眾聽得全神貫注、興致高昂。Camake 說：「他們事後告訴我，透過我們的演出，他們不必親自造訪，就看見了我們的國家、我們的村子。這次經驗讓我們的信心大增。」

Camake Valaule 說，唱傳統古謠讓學生和家長重新認識自己的文化。「以前會唱這些歌的，只有五、六十歲的部落長老。現在孩子們唱這些歌，家長開始問：『為什麼我們不會唱這些古謠？』如今常常是孩子教父母唱，把模糊的記憶一片一片拼回來。」

不過，Camake 在 2006 年成立傳唱隊，原本的用意並不是贏得國際名聲，這也不是主要的理由。最重要的是讓孩子明白自己為什麼唱這些歌，並且保存、傳承自己的文化。談到 2009 年 8 月莫拉克颱風過後泰武國小和泰武村遷校遷村，Camake 說：「我們帶不走山上的森林和房子，但是我們可以把文化帶著走。只要孩子們願意唱，我就會一直陪著他們，和他們一起唱，帶他們體會古謠的意義。」

items.stem: Which of the following is true about Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers?
options: The group was first established in 2009.
The group was founded by a PE teacher.
The singers usually sing popular folk songs.
The singers learn to sing from their parents.
items.explanation:
Camake Valaule, a physical education teacher and the founder of the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers,
第 2 段介紹 Camake Valaule 是體育老師（physical education teacher），也是傳唱隊的創辦人（founder），選項換成 founded by a PE teacher。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 2009，那一年傳唱隊到歐洲演出，第 4 段說傳唱隊在 2006 年成立；(D) 照抄 parents，第 3 段說的正好相反，常常是孩子教父母唱；(C) 傳唱隊唱的是傳統古謠（traditional ballads），不是流行歌曲。

items.stem: On his first trip to Europe, why did Camake think the audience might fall asleep?
options: The average age of the audience was between fifty and sixty.
Most of the performance was not accompanied by any instrument.
Nobody could understand the language and the meaning of the songs.
The audience could not visualize the theme sung by the school children.
items.explanation:
He was worried that the audience would fall asleep since most of the 75-minute performance was a cappella, that is, singing without instrumental sound.
第 2 段說 Camake 擔心觀眾睡著，因為 75 分鐘的演出大部分是 a cappella，原文緊接著用 that is 解釋：沒有樂器伴奏的清唱（without instrumental sound），選項換成 not accompanied by any instrument。(A) 五、六十歲是第 3 段說的部落長老的年紀，不是觀眾的平均年齡；(C) 文章沒說觀眾聽不懂歌詞；(D) 第 2 段說觀眾事後表示，透過演出就看見了傳唱隊的國家和村子，和選項說的正好相反。

items.stem: What does “the pieces of a blurred memory” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?
options: The children’s ignorance of their own culture.
The fading memories about old tribal people.
The broken pieces of knowledge taught at school.
The parents’ vague understanding of their own tradition.
items.explanation:
Now with the children performing the pieces, parents are beginning to ask, ‘Why do we not know how to sing these ballads?’
Many times nowadays, it is the children who teach the songs to their parents, putting back the pieces of a blurred memory.
第 3 段說以前只有部落長老會唱古謠，現在家長聽到孩子唱，才問自己為什麼不會唱；接著說孩子教父母唱，把模糊的記憶（a blurred memory）拼回來。記憶模糊的是家長，模糊的是他們對自己文化的認識，選項把 blurred 換成 vague，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 children，把不懂文化的人從家長換成孩子，方向錯了，孩子反而是教唱的人；(B) 照抄 tribal，部落長老是記得這些歌的人，記憶模糊的不是他們；(C) 照抄 pieces，原文的 pieces 指的是一片一片拼回來的記憶，文章沒有談學校教的知識。

items.stem: What did Camake realize after the incident of Typhoon Morakot?
options: The significance of the relocation of Taiwu Elementary School.
The need to respect nature to avoid being destroyed by it.
The importance of passing on the traditional culture.
The consequence of building houses in the forest.
items.explanation:
The most important thing was to make children understand why they sing these songs and to preserve and pass on their culture.
We could not take the forest or our houses in the mountains with us; but we were able to bring our culture along.
第 4 段說成立傳唱隊最重要的是保存、傳承文化（pass on their culture）；談到莫拉克颱風後遷校遷村，Camake 說森林和房子帶不走，文化卻帶得走，所以是 (C) 傳承傳統文化的重要。(A) 照抄 relocation，遷校遷村是颱風帶來的結果，他體會到的是文化帶得走；(D) 照抄 forest，帶不走森林是在對比文化帶得走，文章沒有談在森林裡蓋房子的後果；(B) 尊重自然以免遭到破壞，文章沒提。

閱讀測驗.title: 過度醫療的問題（The Problem of Overtreatment）
閱讀測驗.passage:
When it comes to medical care, many patients and doctors believe “more is better.” But what they do not realize is that overtreatment—too many scans, too many blood tests, too many procedures—may pose harm. Sometimes a test leads you down a path to more and more testing, some of which may be invasive, or to treatment for things that should be left alone.

Terrence Power, for example, complained that after his wife learned she had Wegener’s disease, an uncommon disorder of the immune system, they found it difficult to refuse testing recommended by her physician. The doctor insisted on office visits every three weeks, even when she was feeling well. He frequently ordered blood tests and X-rays, and repeatedly referred her to specialists for even minor complaints. Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered, and she was hospitalized as a precaution when she developed a cold. She had as many as 25 doctor visits during one six-month period. The couple was spending about $30,000 a year for her care.

After several years of physical suffering and near financial ruin from the medical costs, the couple began questioning the treatment after consulting with other patients in online support groups. “It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said. “You think she’s getting the best care in the world, but after a while you start to wonder: What is the objective?” Mr. Power then spoke with his own primary care doctor, who advised him to find a new specialist to oversee Mrs. Power’s care. Under the new doctor’s care, the regular testing stopped and Mrs. Power’s condition stabilized. Now she sees the doctor only four or five times a year.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
談到醫療照護，許多病人和醫生都相信「越多越好」。但是他們沒有意識到，過度醫療，也就是太多掃描、太多抽血檢驗、太多醫療程序，可能會造成傷害。有時候一項檢查會帶著你走上越來越多檢查的路，其中有些可能是侵入性的；有時候則會去治療一些原本應該放著不管的問題。

以 Terrence Power 為例，他抱怨妻子得知自己罹患韋格納肉芽腫（一種罕見的免疫系統疾病）之後，兩人發現很難拒絕醫師建議的檢查。醫生堅持她每三週回診一次，即使她覺得身體很好也一樣。醫生經常要她抽血、照 X 光，連小毛病也一再轉診給專科醫師。就算檢查結果正常，醫生還是安排更多檢查；她感冒時，醫生也為了預防萬一讓她住院。在某個半年期間，她看診多達 25 次。這對夫妻每年要花大約三萬美元在她的醫療上。

經過好幾年身體上的折磨，醫療費用也幾乎讓他們破產，這對夫妻在網路病友互助團體裡和其他病人交流之後，開始質疑這些治療。Power 先生說：「醫生什麼時候做得太過頭了，真的很難判斷。你以為她得到的是世界上最好的照顧，但過了一陣子你會開始懷疑：這樣做的目的到底是什麼？」Power 先生後來和自己的家庭醫師談過，醫師建議他另外找一位專科醫師負責 Power 太太的治療。在新醫師的照護下，例行檢查停了，Power 太太的病情也穩定下來。現在她一年只看醫生四、五次。

items.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: Treatments do not always cause harmful side effects.
Patients tend to believe more testing is better treatment.
Too much medical care may not be beneficial to patients.
Doctors generally recommend office visits that are necessary.
items.explanation: 第 1 段開門見山：很多人相信醫療越多越好，但過度醫療可能造成傷害；第 2、3 段用 Power 太太的例子說明，太多檢查讓她身心受苦、幾乎破產，停掉例行檢查後病情反而穩定。全文要說的是太多醫療對病人未必有益，所以是 (C)。(B) 病人相信檢查越多越好，只是第 1 段第一句的說法，過於狹隘；(A) 說治療不一定有副作用、(D) 說醫生通常只建議必要的回診，都和文章的立場相反，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following was a problem for Mrs. Power during her medical treatment?
options: She had to be hospitalized for three weeks whenever she had a cold.
She didn’t have any insurance, so she went broke because of her illness.
When test results showed she was fine, her doctor still ordered more tests.
Her doctor asked her to consult other specialists due to her constant complaints.
items.explanation:
Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered,
第 2 段說就算檢查結果正常（tests came back negative），醫生還是安排更多檢查，選項換成 test results showed she was fine 和 still ordered more tests。(A) 照抄 three weeks，原文說每三週回診一次，感冒住院是為了預防萬一，沒說住院三週；(D) 照抄 specialists，原文說連小毛病（minor complaints）也轉診，不是因為她一直抱怨；(B) 原文說醫療費用讓這對夫妻幾乎破產，沒提到有沒有保險。

items.stem: Who does “they” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?
items.explanation:
“It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said.
they 出現在 Power 先生說的話裡：很難判斷 they 什麼時候越過了界線（crossed the line）。第 2 段一路寫的是醫生堅持回診、一再安排檢查和轉診，做得太多、越過界線的是醫生，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄前一句的 other patients，(D) 照抄 online support groups，這對夫妻是和其他病友交流之後才開始質疑，病友和互助團體不是安排檢查的人；(C) Power 夫婦是承受過度醫療的一方。

items.stem: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward medical tests?
options: More tests than necessary are too much.
Medical tests are essential for disease prevention.
Many tests are needed for confirmation of diagnosis.
Doctors’ interpretations of test results are seldom wrong.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說過度醫療（太多掃描、太多抽血、太多醫療程序）可能造成傷害，一項檢查常會引出更多檢查；Power 太太的例子也說明檢查做得太多反而傷身又傷財，停掉例行檢查後病情穩定。作者認為超過需要的檢查就是太多了，所以是 (A)。(B)、(C) 強調檢查必要，和作者的立場相反；(D) 文章沒有談醫生判讀檢查結果準不準。

閱讀測驗.title: 攝影家布列松（Photographer Henri Cartier-Bresson）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Henri Cartier-Bresson (1908–2004) is one of the most original and influential figures in the history of photography. His humane, spontaneous photographs helped establish photojournalism as an art form.

Cartier-Bresson’s family was wealthy—his father made a fortune as a textile manufacturer—but Cartier-Bresson later joked that due to his parents’ frugal ways, it often seemed as though his family was poor.

Educated in Paris, Cartier-Bresson developed an early love for literature and the arts. As a teenager, Cartier-Bresson rebelled against his parents’ formal ways of education. In his early adulthood, he even drifted toward communism. But it was art that remained at the center of his life.

Cartier-Bresson traveled to Africa in 1931 to hunt antelope and boar. And Africa fueled another interest in him: photography. He then wandered around the world with his camera, using a handheld camera to catch images from fleeting moments of everyday life.

Not long after World War II, Cartier-Bresson traveled east, spending considerable time in India, where he met and photographed Gandhi shortly before his assassination in 1948. Cartier-Bresson’s subsequent work to document Gandhi’s death and its immediate impact on the country became one of Life Magazine’s most prized photo essays.

Cartier-Bresson’s approach to photography remained much the same throughout his life. He made clear his dislike of images that had been improved by artificial light, darkroom effects, and even cropping. The naturalist in Cartier-Bresson believed that all editing should be done when the photo is taken. In 1952, his first book, The Decisive Moment, a rich collection of his work spanning two decades, was published. “There is nothing in this world that does not have a decisive moment,” he said.

In 1968, he began to turn away from photography and returned to his passion for drawing and painting.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
布列松（Henri Cartier-Bresson，1908–2004）是攝影史上最有原創性、最具影響力的人物之一。他的照片充滿人情味、自然不做作，讓新聞攝影確立為一種藝術形式。

布列松家境富裕，父親經營紡織業發了大財；不過布列松後來開玩笑說，因為父母很節儉，家裡常常看起來好像很窮。

布列松在巴黎受教育，很早就熱愛文學和藝術。青少年時期，他反抗父母那套拘謹的教育方式。成年初期，他甚至一度傾向共產主義。不過，藝術始終是他生活的重心。

1931 年，布列松到非洲獵捕羚羊和野豬。非洲也引發了他另一個興趣：攝影。之後他帶著相機周遊世界，用手持相機捕捉日常生活中稍縱即逝的瞬間。

第二次世界大戰結束後不久，布列松往東方旅行，在印度待了相當長的時間。他在印度見到甘地，並替甘地拍照，不久之後甘地就在 1948 年遇刺身亡。布列松後來記錄甘地之死，以及甘地之死對印度立即造成的衝擊，這組作品成為《生活》雜誌最珍貴的攝影專題之一。

布列松一生拍照的方式幾乎沒有改變。他明白表示，不喜歡用人工光源、暗房效果，甚至裁切修飾過的照片。布列松是個自然主義者，認為所有的編修都應該在拍攝的當下完成。1952 年，他出版第一本書《決定性的瞬間》，收錄了他二十年來的作品。他說：「這世界上沒有一件事沒有決定性的瞬間。」

1968 年，布列松開始逐漸遠離攝影，回到他熱愛的素描和繪畫。

items.stem: Which of the following best describes Cartier-Bresson’s family background?
options: His family was rich but was very economical.
His father went to Paris to open a textile factory.
His wealthy family went bankrupt and became poor.
His parents were very liberal in their ways of education.
items.explanation:
Cartier-Bresson’s family was wealthy—his father made a fortune as a textile manufacturer—but Cartier-Bresson later joked that due to his parents’ frugal ways, it often seemed as though his family was poor.
第 2 段說布列松家境富裕（wealthy），但父母很節儉（frugal），選項換成 rich 和 economical。(B) 照抄 textile，原文只說父親經營紡織業發了財，去巴黎的是在巴黎受教育的布列松，不是父親去巴黎開工廠；(C) 照抄 poor，原文說的是父母節儉，家裡「看起來好像」很窮，不是真的破產；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 education，第 3 段說他反抗父母拘謹的教育方式，和選項說的開明正好相反。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about Cartier-Bresson’s career in photography?
options: He devoted himself to photography all his life.
He developed a passion for photography when he traveled to Africa.
He quit photography right after the publication of The Decisive Moment.
During World War II, he documented the everyday life of the Indian people.
items.explanation:
Cartier-Bresson traveled to Africa in 1931 to hunt antelope and boar.
And Africa fueled another interest in him: photography.
第 4 段說布列松 1931 年到非洲打獵，非洲引發了他另一個興趣：攝影（fueled another interest in him），選項換成 developed a passion for photography。(C) 照抄書名 The Decisive Moment，這本書 1952 年出版，他到 1968 年才開始遠離攝影，不是一出書就放棄；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 everyday life，捕捉日常生活是他周遊世界時的作品，他去印度是在二戰結束後，拍的是甘地；(A) 第 7 段說他晚年轉向素描和繪畫，並沒有一輩子都投入攝影。

items.stem: What significance did Cartier-Bresson have to Gandhi of India?
options: He was the first photographer to take Gandhi’s photo.
He used photos to document the effect of Gandhi’s death on India.
His photos told the world who was guilty of assassinating Gandhi.
items.explanation:
Cartier-Bresson’s subsequent work to document Gandhi’s death and its immediate impact on the country became one of Life Magazine’s most prized photo essays.
第 5 段說布列松記錄了甘地之死，以及甘地之死對這個國家立即造成的衝擊（impact on the country），選項把 impact 換成 effect，把 the country 換成 India。(A) 照抄 assassination in 1948，原文說他在甘地遇刺前不久替甘地拍照，沒說他親眼目睹甘地遇刺；(B) 文章沒說他是第一個替甘地拍照的人；(D) 文章沒有談兇手是誰。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about Cartier-Bresson’s approach to photography?
options: He never waited for a decisive moment to shoot photos.
He preferred to edit his images carefully in his darkroom.
Most of his photos described things that happen every day.
He experimented with different ways and settled on being a naturalist.
items.explanation:
using a handheld camera to catch images from fleeting moments of everyday life.
第 4 段說布列松用手持相機捕捉日常生活（everyday life）中稍縱即逝的瞬間，選項換成 things that happen every day。另外三個選項都照抄第 6 段：(B) 照抄 darkroom，原文說他不喜歡用暗房效果修飾過的照片，正好相反；(D) 照抄 naturalist，原文說他一生拍照的方式幾乎沒變，不是試過各種方法才決定當自然主義者；(A) 照抄 decisive moment，他說世上每件事都有決定性的瞬間，選項卻說他從不等待決定性的瞬間，和他的主張相反。

閱讀測驗.title: 「久坐病」的危害（The Dangers of "Sitting Disease"）
閱讀測驗.passage:
You’ve most likely heard the news by now: A car-commuting, desk-bound, TV-watching lifestyle can be harmful to our health. All the time that we spend rooted in the chair is linked to increased risks of so many deadly diseases that experts have named this modern-day health epidemic the “sitting disease.”

Sitting for too long slows down the body’s metabolism and the way enzymes break down our fat reserves, raising both blood sugar levels and blood pressure. Small amounts of regular activity, even just standing and moving around, throughout the day is enough to bring the increased levels back down. And those small amounts of activity add up—30 minutes of light activity in two or three-minute bursts can be just as effective as a half-hour block of exercise. But without that activity, blood sugar levels and blood pressure keep creeping up, steadily damaging the inside of the arteries and increasing the risk of diabetes, heart disease, stroke, and other serious diseases. In essence, fundamental changes in biology occur if you sit for too long.

But wait, you’re a runner. You needn’t worry about the harm of a sedentary lifestyle because you exercise regularly, right? Well, not so fast. Recent studies show that people spend an average of 64 hours a week sitting, whether or not they exercise 150 minutes a week as recommended by World Health Organization (WHO). Regular exercisers, furthermore, are found to be about 30 percent less active on days when they exercise. Overall, most people simply aren’t exercising or moving around enough to counteract all the harm that can result from sitting nine hours or more a day.

Scared straight out of your chair? Good. The remedy is as simple as standing up and taking activity breaks.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
你現在大概已經聽說了：開車通勤、整天坐辦公桌、看電視的生活方式可能有害健康。我們坐在椅子上不動的時間，和許多致命疾病的風險升高都有關，專家甚至把這種現代的健康流行病稱為「久坐病」。

坐太久會讓身體的新陳代謝變慢，酵素分解體內脂肪的速度也變慢，使血糖和血壓都升高。一整天裡只要有少量、規律的活動，即使只是站起來走動一下，就足以讓升高的數值降回來。而且這些少量的活動會累積起來：每次活動兩三分鐘，加起來 30 分鐘的輕度活動，效果可能和一次做完半小時的運動一樣好。但是如果沒有這些活動，血糖和血壓就會持續慢慢上升，不斷損害動脈內壁，增加糖尿病、心臟病、中風和其他重大疾病的風險。基本上，坐太久的話，身體在生理上就會產生根本的變化。

不過等等，你有在跑步。你有規律運動，所以不必擔心久坐不動的生活方式帶來的傷害，對吧？嗯，先別急著下結論。最近的研究顯示，不論有沒有照世界衛生組織（WHO）的建議每週運動 150 分鐘，人們平均每週都要坐 64 個小時。此外，研究還發現，規律運動的人在有運動的那幾天，活動量反而少了大約 30%。整體來說，大多數人的運動量或活動量根本不夠，抵銷不了每天坐九小時以上可能造成的種種傷害。

嚇得從椅子上跳起來了嗎？很好。解決方法很簡單，就是站起來，找時間休息、活動一下。

items.stem: What is the purpose of this passage?
options: To point out the challenges of the modern lifestyle.
To discuss how a modern epidemic may spread quickly.
To explore the effects of regular exercise to our body.
To explain the threat to our health from long hours of sitting.
items.explanation: 第 1 段點出久坐和許多致命疾病有關，專家稱為久坐病；第 2 段說明坐太久身體會產生哪些變化；第 3 段說就算有規律運動，也抵銷不了久坐的傷害；第 4 段給出解決方法。全文都在說久坐對健康的威脅，所以是 (D)。(A) 把話題拉大到現代生活的各種挑戰，太過廣泛；(C) 規律運動只在第 3 段談到，而且那一段要說的是運動抵銷不了久坐的傷害，過於狹隘；(B) 第 1 段用 epidemic 形容久坐病很普遍，文章沒有談流行病怎麼擴散，偏離主題。

items.stem: What does the word “sedentary” in the third paragraph most likely mean?
items.explanation:
All the time that we spend rooted in the chair is linked to increased risks of so many deadly diseases
You needn’t worry about the harm of a sedentary lifestyle because you exercise regularly, right?
第 3 段問：你有規律運動，所以不必擔心 sedentary 的生活方式帶來的傷害，對吧？前文一路講的都是坐在椅子上不動（rooted in the chair），規律運動是拿來對比的，可見 sedentary 是久坐不動、缺少活動的，最接近 (C) Inactive。(A) 和 (D) 照抄第 1 段的 modern-day 和 epidemic，那是在形容久坐病是現代的流行病；(B) 有風險是久坐的後果，不是 sedentary 這個字的意思。

items.stem: What is the best way to bring down high blood sugar level and blood pressure?
options: Exercising for 150 minutes or more every week.
Getting rid of the habit of car commuting and TV watching.
Interrupting sitting time with light activity as often as possible.
Standing or moving around for at least two or three minutes every day.
items.explanation:
Small amounts of regular activity, even just standing and moving around, throughout the day is enough to bring the increased levels back down.
30 minutes of light activity in two or three-minute bursts can be just as effective as a half-hour block of exercise.
第 2 段說一整天裡（throughout the day）只要有少量、規律的活動，即使只是站起來走動，就能讓升高的血糖和血壓降回來；每次兩三分鐘、累積 30 分鐘的輕度活動，效果和一次運動半小時一樣。重點是不斷打斷坐著的時間，選項換成 interrupting sitting time as often as possible。(D) 照抄 two or three，原文說的是每次兩三分鐘、一天累積到 30 分鐘，不是每天只要兩三分鐘；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 150 minutes，第 3 段說的正好是每週運動 150 分鐘的人照樣每週坐 64 小時；(B) 改掉開車通勤和看電視的習慣，文章沒有這樣建議。

items.stem: Which of the following may be inferred about those who do serious exercise?
options: They often live longer than those who don’t exercise.
They tend to stand or move around less on days they work out.
They generally spend less time sitting than those who are inactive.
They usually do not meet the standard of exercise recommended by WHO.
items.explanation:
Regular exercisers, furthermore, are found to be about 30 percent less active on days when they exercise.
第 3 段說規律運動的人在有運動的那幾天，活動量反而少了大約 30%（less active on days when they exercise），選項換成 stand or move around less on days they work out。(D) 照抄 recommended by，原文說不論有沒有達到世界衛生組織建議的運動量，人們每週都坐 64 小時，沒說認真運動的人通常達不到標準；(C) 原文說的正好相反，有沒有運動，坐的時間都差不多；(A) 壽命長短文章沒提。

閱讀測驗.title: 法貝熱彩蛋的歷史與象徵意義（History and Symbolic Meaning of Fabergé Eggs）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Fabergé eggs are jeweled eggs that were made by the famous Russian jeweler, the House of Fabergé, from 1885 to 1917. The eggs were made of valuable metals or stones coated with beautiful colors and decorated with precious jewels.

The first Fabergé egg was crafted for Tsar Alexander III, who gave his wife, the Empress Maria Fedorovna, an Easter egg to celebrate their 20th wedding anniversary. He placed an order with a young jeweler, Peter Carl Fabergé, whose beautiful creations had caught Maria’s eye earlier. On Easter morning of 1885, what appeared to be a simple enameled egg was delivered to the palace. But to the delight of the Empress, the egg opened to a golden yolk; within the yolk was a golden hen; and concealed within the hen was a diamond miniature of the royal crown and a tiny ruby egg. Unfortunately, the last two surprises are now lost to history.

Empress Maria was so delighted by this gift that Alexander appointed Fabergé a “goldsmith by special appointment to the Imperial Crown.” The Tsar also asked Fabergé to make an Easter egg every year. The requirements were straightforward: Each egg must be unique, and each must contain a pleasant surprise. With excellent craftsmanship and an inventive spirit, Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge. The House of Fabergé made approximately 50 Imperial Easter Eggs for Tsar Alexander III and his son Nicholas II until 1917, when the Russian revolution broke out.

Today, the term “Fabergé eggs” has become a synonym of luxury and the eggs are regarded as masterpieces of the jeweler’s art. More significantly, perhaps, they serve as reminders of the last Russian imperial family.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
法貝熱彩蛋是俄國著名的珠寶商法貝熱公司（the House of Fabergé）在 1885 年到 1917 年間製作的珠寶蛋。這些彩蛋用貴重的金屬或寶石做成，塗上美麗的色彩，再鑲上珍貴的珠寶。

第一顆法貝熱彩蛋，是替沙皇亞歷山大三世製作的。沙皇為了慶祝結婚 20 週年，要送妻子瑪麗亞皇后一顆復活節彩蛋。他向年輕的珠寶師 Peter Carl Fabergé 訂製，這位珠寶師美麗的作品，先前就吸引了瑪麗亞的目光。1885 年復活節早上，一顆看起來像是普通琺瑯蛋的彩蛋送進了宮。不過，讓皇后驚喜的是，蛋打開來，裡面是一顆金蛋黃；蛋黃裡有一隻金母雞；母雞裡還藏著一頂鑽石做的小皇冠和一顆小小的紅寶石蛋。可惜的是，最後這兩樣驚喜如今已經失傳。

瑪麗亞皇后非常喜歡這份禮物，亞歷山大於是任命法貝熱為「皇室特約金匠」。沙皇也要法貝熱每年做一顆復活節彩蛋。要求很簡單：每一顆彩蛋都必須獨一無二，每一顆都要藏著令人驚喜的東西。憑著精湛的工藝和創新的精神，Peter Fabergé 和他的繼承人一次又一次達成了這項挑戰。法貝熱公司替沙皇亞歷山大三世和他的兒子尼古拉二世，做了大約 50 顆皇室復活節彩蛋，一直到 1917 年俄國革命爆發為止。

如今，「法貝熱彩蛋」已經成為奢華的代名詞，這些彩蛋公認是珠寶藝術的傑作。或許更重要的是，這些彩蛋讓人想起俄國最後的皇室。

items.stem: Why did Tsar Alexander III choose Peter Fabergé to make the first Easter egg?
options: Peter Fabergé was the goldsmith for the royal family.
Empress Maria was impressed by Peter Fabergé’s work.
Tsar Alexander III received an order from Empress Maria.
Peter Fabergé owned the most famous Russian jewelry house.
items.explanation:
whose beautiful creations had caught Maria
第 2 段說沙皇向年輕的珠寶師 Peter Carl Fabergé 訂製，因為他美麗的作品（beautiful creations）先前就吸引了（had caught）瑪麗亞的目光，選項換成 Empress Maria was impressed by Peter Fabergé’s work，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 goldsmith，法貝熱是在第一顆彩蛋讓皇后滿意以後，才獲得皇室特約金匠的頭銜；(C) 照抄 order，下訂單的是沙皇，選項說沙皇接到皇后的訂單，說反了；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 famous Russian，法貝熱公司是後來才成為著名的珠寶商，沙皇訂製時，第 2 段說他還是年輕的珠寶師。

items.stem: What went missing from the first Fabergé egg?
options: A golden hen and a ruby egg.
A golden hen and a golden yolk.
A ruby egg and a diamond crown.
A golden yolk and a diamond crown.
items.explanation:
concealed within the hen was a diamond miniature of the royal crown and a tiny ruby egg.
Unfortunately, the last two surprises are now lost to history.
第 2 段依序說蛋打開來是金蛋黃，蛋黃裡有金母雞，母雞裡藏著鑽石小皇冠（a diamond miniature of the royal crown）和紅寶石小蛋（a tiny ruby egg），接著說最後兩樣驚喜（the last two surprises）已經失傳。最後兩樣就是鑽石皇冠和紅寶石蛋，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 golden hen、(B) 和 (D) 照抄 golden yolk，金母雞和金蛋黃是前面兩樣，沒有失傳。

items.stem: What does it mean by “Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge” in the third paragraph?
options: They repeated their designs over and over.
They fulfilled the Tsar’s requirements each time.
They challenged the Tsar’s expectations every year.
They were faced with unexpected difficulties time and again.
items.explanation:
The requirements were straightforward: Each egg must be unique, and each must contain a pleasant surprise.
Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge.
這裡的 meet 不是「遇到」，而是「達成、符合」，meet the challenge 是成功應付挑戰。the challenge 指的是前一句沙皇的要求（The requirements）：每一顆彩蛋都必須獨一無二，而且要藏著驚喜；repeatedly 是每年一次又一次。合起來就是法貝熱和繼承人每一次都做到了沙皇的要求，所以是 (B)。(D) 把 meet 當成「遇到」，又把 challenge 當成困難，照字面解釋；(C) 照抄 challenge，挑戰是沙皇給法貝熱的，選項說法貝熱挑戰沙皇，主客顛倒；(A) 照抄 repeated，原文要求每顆彩蛋都獨一無二，不可能重複同樣的設計。

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the Fabergé eggs is true, according to the passage?
options: They were all genuine creations of the jeweler, Peter Fabergé.
They were created to represent Russian emperors and their dynasty.
They were made for annual Easter parties in the Russian imperial court.
They were connected to the last two Russian emperors and their families.
items.explanation:
for Tsar Alexander III and his son Nicholas II until 1917, when the Russian revolution broke out.
they serve as reminders of the last Russian imperial family.
這一題要把兩段合起來看。第 3 段說法貝熱公司替沙皇亞歷山大三世和他的兒子尼古拉二世做彩蛋，一直到 1917 年俄國革命爆發為止；第 4 段說這些彩蛋讓人想起俄國最後的皇室。革命以後俄國就沒有沙皇了，所以這兩位是俄國最後兩位皇帝，彩蛋又是送給皇后等家人的禮物，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 Peter Fabergé，第 3 段說彩蛋是他和他的繼承人（his successors）做的，不全是他本人的作品；(C) 照抄 Easter，彩蛋是復活節送給皇后的禮物，原文沒有說是為宮廷的復活節派對做的；(B) 讓人想起俄國最後的皇室，是彩蛋今天的意義，彩蛋當初是沙皇送皇后的禮物，不是為了代表皇帝和王朝而做。

閱讀測驗.title: 六標準差管理（Six Sigma Management）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Six Sigma is a highly disciplined process that helps companies focus on developing and delivering near-perfect products and services. The word “sigma” is a statistical term that measures how far a given process falls short of perfection. The central idea behind Six Sigma is that if a company can measure how many “defects” they have in a commercial production process, they can systematically figure out how to eliminate the problems and get as close to “zero defects” as possible.

Training and teamwork are essential elements of the Six Sigma methodology. In other words, companies need to have their team leaders and team members trained to implement the Six Sigma processes. They must learn to use the measurement and improvement tools. They also need to learn communication skills necessary for them to involve customers and suppliers and to serve their needs.

Six Sigma was developed in 1986 by Motorola, an American telecommunications company. Engineers in Motorola used it as an informal name for a plan to reduce faults in production processes. A few years later, Motorola extended the name “Six Sigma” to mean a general performance improvement method, beyond purely “defect reduction” in the production process. In 1995, Jack Welch, CEO of General Electrics (GE), decided to implement Six Sigma in GE; and by 1998 GE claimed that Six Sigma had generated over three-quarters of a billion dollars of cost savings.

By 2000, Six Sigma was effectively established as an industry in its own right, involving the training, consultancy and implementation of Six Sigma methodology in all sorts of organizations around the world. Organizations as diverse as local governments, prisons, hospitals, the armed forces, banks, and multi-national corporations have been adopting Six Sigma for quality and process improvement.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
六標準差（Six Sigma）是一套非常嚴謹的流程，幫助公司專心開發並提供近乎完美的產品和服務。sigma 這個字是統計名詞，衡量一個流程離完美還差多遠。六標準差背後的核心概念是：如果公司能算出商業生產流程中有多少「瑕疵」，就能有系統地想出消除問題的方法，盡可能接近「零瑕疵」。

訓練和團隊合作，是六標準差方法不可或缺的要素。也就是說，公司要讓組長和組員接受訓練，才能執行六標準差的流程。他們必須學會使用測量和改善的工具，也要學會必要的溝通技巧，讓顧客和供應商參與，並且滿足他們的需求。

六標準差是美國電信公司摩托羅拉在 1986 年發展出來的。摩托羅拉的工程師用這個名稱，非正式地稱呼一項減少生產流程錯誤的計畫。幾年後，摩托羅拉把「六標準差」這個名稱的意思擴大，指一般的績效改善方法，不再只是生產流程中的「減少瑕疵」。1995 年，奇異公司（GE）的執行長傑克·威爾許決定在奇異公司實施六標準差；到了 1998 年，奇異公司宣稱六標準差已經替公司省下超過七億五千萬美元的成本。

到了 2000 年，六標準差已經實實在在地自成一個產業，在世界各地各種組織裡提供六標準差方法的訓練、諮詢和實施。地方政府、監獄、醫院、軍隊、銀行和跨國企業，這麼多不同的組織，都採用六標準差來提升品質、改善流程。

items.stem: According to the passage, what is “Six Sigma”?
options: A digital device to speed up production processes.
A near-perfect process in business communication.
A statistical term that measures a company’s budgets and profits.
A quality measure that detects problems to improve products and services.
items.explanation:
helps companies focus on developing and delivering near-perfect products and services.
they can systematically figure out how to eliminate the problems
第 1 段說六標準差幫助公司提供近乎完美的產品和服務（products and services），做法是算出生產流程有多少瑕疵，再有系統地找出消除問題（eliminate the problems）的方法，選項換成找出問題、改善產品和服務的品質管理方法，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 statistical term，原文說 sigma 這個字是統計名詞，衡量的是流程離完美多遠，不是預算和利潤；(B) 照抄 near-perfect，近乎完美的是產品和服務，不是商業溝通；(A) 六標準差是一套流程，不是數位裝置。

items.stem: For Six Sigma to be applied successfully, which of the following are the most crucial factors?
items.explanation:
Training and teamwork are essential elements of the Six Sigma methodology.
第 2 段第一句說訓練（Training）和團隊合作（teamwork）是六標準差不可或缺的要素（essential elements），題目的 most crucial factors 就是這一句，所以是 (C)。這一段後面幾句是在說明要訓練什麼：(A) 照抄 customers and suppliers，滿足顧客和供應商的需求，是溝通技巧要達成的事；(B) 照抄 tools，原文說的是測量和改善的工具，沒有提到行銷；(D) 照抄 leader，原文說要訓練組長（team leaders），沒有說領導能力是關鍵，也沒有提到預算。

items.stem: How are the author’s ideas developed in the last two paragraphs?
items.explanation:
Six Sigma was developed in 1986 by Motorola
A few years later
In 1995, Jack Welch
By 2000, Six Sigma was effectively established as an industry in its own right
這一題答對率只有 52%，判斷方法是找出兩段裡的時間詞。第 3 段依序是 1986 年（摩托羅拉發展出六標準差）、A few years later（擴大成一般的績效改善方法）、1995 年（奇異公司導入）、1998 年（省下成本）；第 4 段接著是 By 2000（自成一個產業）。兩段照時間先後說明六標準差的發展，所以是 (C)。(A) 下定義是第 1 段的寫法，第 1 段說明六標準差是什麼；(B) 兩段沒有拿六標準差和別的方法比較；(D) 空間順序是依位置描寫，例如描寫一個地方，這兩段沒有這樣寫。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true regarding Six Sigma?
options: It helped Motorola and General Motors to promote sales.
It requires multi-national efforts to generate satisfactory results.
It has gained popularity mostly among large telecommunications companies.
It has become a business model which provides services to organizations worldwide.
items.explanation:
involving the training, consultancy and implementation of Six Sigma methodology in all sorts of organizations around the world.
第 4 段說到了 2000 年，六標準差已經自成一個產業，在世界各地（around the world）各種組織裡提供訓練、諮詢（consultancy）和實施，選項換成成為一種商業模式，替全世界的組織提供服務，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 Motorola，第 3 段的另一家公司是奇異公司（General Electrics），不是通用汽車（General Motors），而且原文說的是省下成本，不是促進銷售；(B) 照抄 multi-national，跨國企業只是採用六標準差的組織之一；(C) 照抄 telecommunications，電信公司只是發展出六標準差的摩托羅拉，第 4 段說採用的組織從政府、監獄到銀行都有。

閱讀測驗.title: 瓶鼻海豚用哨聲互叫名字（Bottlenose Dolphins Calling Each Other by Name）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Imagine two bottlenose dolphins swimming in the Gulf of Mexico. You hear a series of clicks, whistles, and whines coming from each, much like a conversation. We can’t be sure what they are discussing, but scientists do believe dolphins call each other by “name.”

A recent study suggests the marine mammals not only produce their own unique “signature whistles,” but they also recognize and mimic whistles of other dolphins they are close to and want to see again. It seems that dolphins can call those they know by mimicking their distinct whistles. “They’re abstract names,” said Randall Wells, one of the authors of the study.

To conduct the study, the researchers listened to recordings of about 250 wild bottlenose dolphins made around Florida’s Sarasota Bay from 1984 to 2009, and four captive dolphins at a nearby aquarium. Some wild dolphins were briefly captured and held in separate nets by the research team, allowing them to hear but not see each other. Researchers found that dolphins familiar with each other would mimic the whistle of another in that group when they were separated. Most of this took place among mothers and calves, or among males who were close associates, suggesting it was affiliative and not aggressive—somewhat like calling out the name of a missing child or friend. Whistle copying of this sort was not found in dolphins that happened to cross paths in the wild.

This use of vocal copying is similar to its use in human language, where the maintenance of social bonds appears to be more important than the immediate defense of resources. This helps differentiate dolphins’ vocal learning from that of birds, which tend to address one another in a more “aggressive context.”

If confirmed, this would be a level of communication rarely found in nature. If dolphins can identify themselves and address friends with just a few squeaks, it’s easy to imagine what else they’re saying. However, as the authors of the study point out, all we can do right now is still imagine.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
想像兩隻瓶鼻海豚在墨西哥灣游泳。你聽到牠們各自發出一連串喀噠聲、哨聲和嗚咽聲，很像在對話。我們不能確定牠們在討論什麼，但科學家確實相信海豚會叫彼此的「名字」。

最近的一項研究指出，這種海洋哺乳動物不但會發出自己獨特的「專屬哨聲」，也會認出並模仿親近、想再見面的其他海豚的哨聲。看來海豚可以模仿認識的海豚特有的哨聲，來呼喚對方。這項研究的作者之一 Randall Wells 說：「這些是抽象的名字。」

為了進行這項研究，研究人員聽了大約 250 隻野生瓶鼻海豚的錄音，這些錄音是 1984 年到 2009 年在佛羅里達州的薩拉索塔灣（Sarasota Bay）一帶錄下的；他們也聽了附近一座水族館裡 4 隻人工飼養的海豚的錄音。研究團隊把一些野生海豚暫時捉起來，分別放在不同的網子裡，讓牠們聽得到、卻看不到彼此。研究人員發現，彼此熟識的海豚分開的時候，會模仿同一群裡另一隻海豚的哨聲。這種情形大多發生在母海豚和小海豚之間，或是關係密切的雄海豚之間，可見這是表示親近，而不是表示攻擊，有點像大聲呼喚走失的孩子或朋友的名字。野外偶然相遇的海豚之間，沒有發現這種模仿哨聲的情形。

這種模仿聲音的用法，和人類語言中的用法相似：在人類語言中，維繫社會關係似乎比立即保衛資源更重要。這一點也有助於區分海豚和鳥類學習聲音的方式。鳥類比較會在「具有攻擊性的情境」下呼叫彼此。

如果得到證實，這將是自然界很少見的溝通層次。如果海豚只用幾聲尖叫，就能表明自己的身分、呼叫朋友，不難想像牠們還說了些什麼。不過，就像這項研究的作者指出的，目前我們能做的，仍然只是想像。

items.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Bottlenose dolphins show strong ties to their family members.
Bottlenose dolphins recognize their friends’ voices in the wild.
Bottlenose dolphins produce whistles that distinguish themselves.
Bottlenose dolphins demonstrate a unique type of animal communication.
items.explanation: 這一題答對率只有 44%，三個錯誤選項都只講到全文的一部分。第 1 段說科學家相信海豚會叫彼此的名字；第 2、3 段說明海豚會模仿親近同伴的哨聲來呼喚對方；第 4 段說這種用法和人類語言相似，和鳥類不同；第 5 段說這是自然界少見的溝通層次（a level of communication rarely found in nature）。全文講的是海豚獨特的溝通方式，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 whistles，海豚發出自己的專屬哨聲只是一半，重點是模仿別的海豚的哨聲來呼叫對方，過於狹隘；(A) 母海豚和小海豚只是第 3 段說的情形之一，過於狹隘；(B) 第 3 段的研究是把海豚分開放在網子裡，而且說野外偶然相遇的海豚不會這樣做，選項只講認出朋友的聲音，過於狹隘。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about Wells’s research team?
options: Their data were collected over two decades.
They recorded the calls of dolphins and birds.
Their major research base was in Mexico.
They trained 250 wild dolphins for observation.
items.explanation:
made around Florida’s Sarasota Bay from 1984 to 2009
第 3 段說錄音是 1984 年到 2009 年（from 1984 to 2009）錄下的，前後 25 年，超過二十年，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 birds，鳥類只是拿來和海豚比較，研究團隊錄的是海豚的聲音；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 Mexico，墨西哥灣只是開頭請讀者想像的場景，研究地點在佛羅里達州的薩拉索塔灣；(D) 照抄 250 wild，研究人員是聽 250 隻野生海豚的錄音，沒有訓練牠們。

items.stem: What does “this” in the third paragraph refer to?
items.explanation:
dolphins familiar with each other would mimic the whistle of another in that group when they were separated.
Most of this took place among mothers and calves
Most of this 的前一句說，熟識的海豚分開時，會模仿另一隻海豚的哨聲（mimic the whistle）。大多發生在母海豚和小海豚之間的，就是這種模仿哨聲的行為，這一段最後一句也用 Whistle copying of this sort 再說一次，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 recordings，錄音是研究人員做的事；(B) 照抄 research，研究也是研究人員做的事，不會發生在海豚母子之間；(C) 原文沒有談到學習行為。

items.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: Birds may use their calls to claim territory.
Male dolphins whistle when fighting for mates.
Dolphins make harsh squeaks when hunting for food.
Both dolphins and birds tend to mimic their enemies’ whistles.
items.explanation:
the maintenance of social bonds appears to be more important than the immediate defense of resources.
which tend to address one another in a more
這一題答對率只有 41%，要把第 4 段的兩句連起來推。判斷步驟：[1] 第 4 段說海豚和人類一樣，用模仿聲音來維繫社會關係，這比立即保衛資源（defense of resources）重要；[2] 接著說鳥類和海豚不同，比較會在具有攻擊性的情境下呼叫彼此；[3] 和「維繫關係」相反的就是「保衛資源」，鳥類的叫聲比較可能用來保衛資源，地盤就是一種資源，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 3 段的 males，原文說關係密切的雄海豚之間會模仿哨聲，是表示親近，不是爭奪配偶；(C) 照抄第 5 段的 squeaks，那是用來表明身分、呼叫朋友的聲音，原文沒有提到獵食；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 mimic，海豚模仿的是親近、想再見面的同伴，不是敵人。

閱讀測驗.title: 土耳其哥樂美國家公園：自然與人文（Goreme National Park: Where Nature Meets Man）
閱讀測驗.passage:
With soaring rock formations, uniquely-rippled landscapes, and mysterious underground cities, the Goreme National Park is an incredible tourist attraction in central Turkey.

Thousands of years ago a group of ancient volcanoes spewed out layer upon layer of thick ash and lava which formed the Cappadocia region, where the Goreme National Park is now located. Over the centuries the wind and rain worked their magic on this land, carving out spectacular gorges and leaving behind the dramatic towering formations of rock pillars that reach heights of 40 meters. These amazing structures are usually called “fairy chimneys.” They come in an extraordinary range of shapes and sizes, but most are tall and resemble king trumpet mushrooms with a cap on top. The top stone is the hardest part of each formation and protects the softer rock underneath from erosion. Eventually, however, these caps fall off, whereupon the wind and rain start to cut away the cone until it, too, collapses. The unique landforms of the Goreme valley have created its lunar-like landscape, also known as a moonscape.

But the Goreme National Park has always been much more than its dramatic scenery. Humans, too, have left their unique mark on the region. The Byzantine Christians inhabited the area in the fourth century. They carved thousands of cave churches, chapels, and monasteries out of rock. Many of these churches were decorated with beautiful wall paintings whose colors still retain all their original freshness. The Byzantine Christians even carved out entire underground villages in an effort to hide from the Romans and later, the Muslims. To this day, many of these villages are still inhabited and many of the rock-cut storerooms are still stuffed with grapes, lemons, potatoes and flat bread waiting for the winter.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
哥樂美國家公園有高聳的岩石、獨特的波紋地形和神祕的地下城市，是土耳其中部很吸引人的觀光景點。

數千年前，一群古老的火山噴出一層又一層厚厚的火山灰和熔岩，形成了卡帕多奇亞地區，也就是哥樂美國家公園現在的所在地。幾百年來，風和雨在這片土地上施展魔法，切出壯觀的峽谷，留下高達 40 公尺、高聳壯觀的岩柱。這些令人驚奇的地形，一般叫做「仙女煙囪」。仙女煙囪的形狀和大小非常多樣，但大多數又高又直，頂端有一頂帽子，很像杏鮑菇。頂端的石頭是每根岩柱最硬的部分，保護下方比較軟的岩石不受侵蝕。不過，這些帽子最後還是會掉下來，接著風雨就開始削蝕下方的錐體，直到錐體也倒塌為止。哥樂美谷地獨特的地形，造就了像月球表面一樣的景觀，也就是所謂的月面景觀。

但是，哥樂美國家公園一直以來都不只有壯觀的風景。人類也在這個地區留下了獨特的印記。四世紀時，拜占庭的基督徒住在這一帶。他們在岩石上鑿出數千座洞穴教堂、禮拜堂和修道院。許多教堂裝飾著美麗的壁畫，壁畫的顏色到現在還和原來一樣鮮豔。拜占庭的基督徒甚至鑿出整座地下村莊，為的是躲避羅馬人，以及後來的穆斯林。直到今天，許多村莊仍然有人居住，許多岩石鑿成的儲藏室裡仍然堆滿了葡萄、檸檬、馬鈴薯和扁麵包，等著過冬。

items.stem: How is the landscape of the Goreme National Park formed?
options: It is the effect of erosions of volcanic rocks by wind and water.
It is the outcome of cumulative ash and lava from volcanoes.
It is the creation of some mysterious forces from the moon.
It is the result of rock cutting by the Byzantine Christians.
items.explanation:
Over the centuries the wind and rain worked their magic on this land, carving out spectacular gorges
the wind and rain start to cut away the cone until it, too, collapses.
這一題答對率只有 46%，要分清楚「土地怎麼來的」和「地形怎麼刻出來的」。判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段說火山噴出的火山灰和熔岩形成了卡帕多奇亞地區，這是岩石的來源；[2] 接著說風和雨（the wind and rain）在這片土地上切出峽谷，留下岩柱，後來又繼續削蝕錐體；[3] 題目問的是地形（landscape）怎麼形成的，刻出地形的是風雨對火山岩的侵蝕，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 ash and lava，火山灰和熔岩只是材料，還要經過風雨侵蝕才變成今天的地形；(C) 照抄 moonscape 的 moon，月面景觀是形容景觀像月球表面，不是月球的力量造成的；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 Byzantine Christians，基督徒鑿的是教堂和村莊，不是整片地形。

items.stem: Which of the following descriptions of the “fairy chimneys” is true?
options: They are almost identical in size and shape.
They have mushrooms growing on the top.
They are formed by rocks of different hardness.
They have strong bottoms to support their 40-meter height.
items.explanation:
The top stone is the hardest part of each formation and protects the softer rock underneath from erosion.
這一題答對率只有 49%。第 2 段說頂端的石頭最硬（the hardest），保護下方比較軟（softer）的岩石，可見仙女煙囪是由軟硬不同的岩石構成的，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 shape，原文說仙女煙囪的形狀和大小非常多樣，不是幾乎一樣；(B) 照抄 mushrooms，原文說仙女煙囪的外形像杏鮑菇，不是上面長了香菇；(D) 照抄 40，原文說下方的岩石比較軟，風雨會把錐體削蝕到倒塌，底部並不堅固。

items.stem: Which of the following has NOT been a function served by the carved rocks in the Goreme National Park?
items.explanation:
They carved thousands of cave churches, chapels, and monasteries out of rock.
in an effort to hide from the Romans
many of these villages are still inhabited
這一題答對率只有 42%，要逐一核對鑿出來的岩石有過哪些用途。第 3 段說拜占庭的基督徒在岩石上鑿出教堂、禮拜堂和修道院，是 (D) 做禮拜的地方；鑿出地下村莊來躲避羅馬人和穆斯林，是 (A) 避難所；這些村莊到今天還有人居住，是 (C) 住所。最容易選錯的是 (B)：原文雖然說教堂裡有美麗的壁畫，但壁畫是教堂的裝飾，鑿出來的岩石並沒有當作展示畫作的藝廊，所以選 (B)。

items.stem: Which of the following sentences best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Goreme is a wonder where nature meets man.
Goreme is a representation of ancient Turkish life.
Goreme is a living example of the power of nature.
Goreme is an attraction that mixes the new and the old.
items.explanation: 這一題答對率只有 28%，是這一批最低的，判斷的方法是找出段落之間的轉折。判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段講自然：火山和風雨造出峽谷和仙女煙囪；[2] 第 3 段第一句用 But 轉折，說這座公園不只有壯觀的風景，人類（Humans, too）也在這裡留下印記，接著講拜占庭基督徒鑿的教堂和地下村莊；[3] 第 1 段的三樣東西也是自然和人文都有：高聳的岩石、波紋地形是自然，地下城市是人文。全文是自然加上人文，所以是 (A)。(C) 只講第 2 段的自然力量，過於狹隘；(B) 只講第 3 段的人文，過於狹隘，而且在這裡生活的是拜占庭的基督徒，原文沒有說是古代土耳其人，ancient 是第 2 段形容火山的字；(D) 原文沒有拿新的和舊的東西做對比，偏離主題。

閱讀測驗.title: 日本的血型性格論（Blood Type Personality Theory in Japan）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In Japan, a person’s blood type is popularly believed to decide his/her temperament and personality. Type-A people are generally considered sensitive perfectionists and good team players, but over-anxious. Type Os are curious and generous but stubborn. Type ABs are artistic but mysterious and unpredictable, and type Bs are cheerful but eccentric, individualistic, and selfish. Though lacking scientific evidence, this belief is widely seen in books, magazines, and television shows.

The blood-type belief has been used in unusual ways. The women’s softball team that won gold for Japan at the Beijing Olympics is reported to have used blood-type theories to customize training for each player. Some kindergartens have adopted teaching methods along blood group lines, and even major companies reportedly make decisions about assignments based on an employee’s blood type. In 1990, Mitsubishi Electronics was reported to have announced the formation of a team composed entirely of AB workers, thanks to “their ability to make plans.”

The belief even affects politics. One former prime minister considered it important enough to reveal in his official profile that he was a type A, while his opposition rival was type B. In 2011, a minister, Ryu Matsumoto, was forced to resign after only a week in office, when a bad-tempered encounter with local officials was televised. In his resignation speech, he blamed his failings on the fact that he was blood type B.

The blood-type craze, considered simply harmless fun by some Japanese, may manifest itself as prejudice and discrimination. In fact, this seems so common that the Japanese now have a term for it: bura-hara, meaning blood-type harassment. There are reports of discrimination leading to children being bullied, ending of happy relationships, and loss of job opportunities due to blood type.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
在日本，一般人普遍相信血型決定一個人的脾氣和性格。A 型的人通常給人敏感、追求完美、善於團隊合作的印象，但過度焦慮；O 型的人好奇又大方，但固執；AB 型的人有藝術氣息，但神祕又難以捉摸；B 型的人開朗，但古怪、個人主義又自私。這種說法雖然缺乏科學根據，卻常常出現在書籍、雜誌和電視節目裡。

血型說還有一些不尋常的用法。據報導，在北京奧運替日本拿下金牌的女子壘球隊，就用血型理論替每位球員量身打造訓練。有些幼稚園依照血型採用不同的教學方法，據說連大公司也會根據員工的血型決定職務分派。1990 年，據報導三菱電機宣布成立一支全由 AB 型員工組成的團隊，理由是他們「有規劃的能力」。

血型說甚至影響政治。一位前首相認為血型重要到要在官方簡介裡公開，說自己是 A 型，而他的反對黨對手是 B 型。2011 年，一位部長松本龍和地方官員見面時脾氣暴躁，畫面在電視上播出，他上任才一週就不得不辭職。他在辭職演說中，把自己的過失歸咎於自己是 B 型。

有些日本人認為血型熱只是無傷大雅的娛樂，但它可能演變成偏見和歧視。事實上，這種情形似乎普遍到日本人已經為它造了一個詞：bura-hara，意思是「血型騷擾」。有報導指出，血型歧視造成兒童遭到霸凌、美好的感情破裂，以及失去工作機會。

items.stem: What is the speaker’s attitude toward the blood-type belief in Japan?
items.explanation: 作者介紹日本人對血型的看法時，用的是 popularly believed、is reported、reportedly 這類轉述的說法；第 1 段點出這種說法缺乏科學根據，第 4 段說有些人當作無傷大雅的娛樂，但可能演變成歧視，兩面都交代，沒有加上自己的褒貶，所以是 (C) 客觀。(A) 負面容易誤選：第 4 段提到血型騷擾和歧視，但作者是引述報導呈現這些現象，不是自己表態批評；(B) 辯護和 (D) 鼓勵都找不到依據。

items.stem: According to the examples mentioned in the passage, which blood type can we infer is the LEAST favored in Japan?
items.explanation:
type Bs are cheerful but eccentric, individualistic, and selfish.
One former prime minister considered it important enough to reveal in his official profile that he was a type A, while his opposition rival was type B.
In his resignation speech, he blamed his failings on the fact that he was blood type B.
文章舉的例子裡，B 型都是負面的：第 1 段說 B 型的人古怪、自私；第 3 段的前首相特地公開自己是 A 型、對手是 B 型；松本龍辭職時把過失歸咎於自己是 B 型。可以推論 B 型最不受歡迎。(D) AB 型在第 2 段是三菱電機組成全 AB 型團隊的正面例子；(A) A 型是前首相願意公開的血型；(C) O 型的例子文章沒有舉。
