items.stem: Why did Prime Minister Ryu Matsumoto resign from office?
options: He revealed his rival’s blood type.
He was seen behaving rudely on TV.
He blamed his failings on local officials.
He was discriminated against because of blood type.
items.explanation:
In 2011, a minister, Ryu Matsumoto, was forced to resign after only a week in office, when a bad-tempered encounter with local officials was televised.
第 3 段說松本龍和地方官員見面時脾氣暴躁（bad-tempered），畫面在電視上播出（was televised），上任一週就辭職，選項換成 behaving rudely on TV。這一段前後講了兩個人：(A) 照抄 rival，公開自己和對手血型的是前一句那位前首相；松本龍在原文是部長（a minister），題幹稱他 Prime Minister，別因此把兩人當成同一個人。(C) 照抄 blamed his failings on，他把過失歸咎於自己的血型，不是地方官員；(D) 原文是他自己拿血型當理由，不是因為血型受到歧視。

items.stem: Which field is NOT mentioned in the passage as being affected by blood-type beliefs?
items.explanation:
The women’s softball team that won gold for Japan at the Beijing Olympics is reported to have used blood-type theories to customize training for each player.
Some kindergartens have adopted teaching methods along blood group lines,
even major companies reportedly make decisions about assignments based on an employee’s blood type.
有提到的三個領域在選項都換了說法：第 2 段壘球隊依血型安排訓練是 (B) Sports，幼稚園依血型採用教學方法是 (A) Education，大公司依血型分派職務是 (C) Business；第 3 段另外還提到政治。文章沒有說血型說影響醫療，所以選 (D)。血型本身是醫學名詞，但這一題問的是哪個領域受到血型說的影響。

閱讀測驗.title: 小發明家的故事（The Story of a Young Inventor）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Like many other five-year-olds, Jeanie Low of Houston, Texas, would use a stool to help her reach the bathroom sink. However, the plastic step-stool she had at home was unstable and cluttered up the small bathroom shared by her whole family. After learning of an invention contest held by her school that year, Jeanie resolved to enter the contest by creating a stool that would be a permanent fixture in the bathroom, and yet could be kept out of the way when not in use.

Jeanie decided to make a stool attached to the bathroom cabinet door under the sink. She cut a plank of wood into two pieces, each about two feet wide and one foot long. Using metal hinges, Jeanie attached one piece of the wood to the front of the cabinet door, and the second piece to the first. The first piece was set just high enough so that when it swung out horizontally from the cabinet door, the second piece would swing down from the first, just touching the ground, and so serving as a support for the first piece of the wood. This created a convenient, sturdy platform for any person too short to reach the sink. When not in use, the hinges allowed the two pieces of wood to fold back up tightly against the cabinet, where they were held in place by magnets. Jeanie called her invention the “Kiddie Stool.”

Jeanie’s Kiddie Stool won first place in her school’s contest. Two years later, it was awarded first prize again at Houston’s first annual Invention Fair. As a result, Jeanie was invited to make a number of public appearances with her Kiddie Stool, and was featured on local TV as well as in newspapers. Many people found the story of the Kiddie Stool inspiring because it showed that with imagination, anyone can be an inventor.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
德州休士頓的 Jeanie Low 和許多五歲小孩一樣，要踩凳子才搆得到浴室的洗手台。不過，她家裡那張塑膠踏凳不穩，又讓全家人共用的小浴室顯得很擠。得知學校那一年要舉辦發明比賽之後，Jeanie 決定參加，做一張固定在浴室裡、不用時又能收起來不擋路的凳子。

Jeanie 決定做一張裝在洗手台下方櫃門上的凳子。她把一塊木板鋸成兩片，每片大約兩英尺寬、一英尺長。她用金屬鉸鏈把第一片木板裝在櫃門正面，再把第二片裝在第一片上。第一片的位置裝得剛好夠高，從櫃門往外水平展開時，第二片會從第一片往下擺，剛好碰到地面，成為第一片木板的支撐。這樣就成了一個方便又穩固的平台，任何個子太矮、搆不到洗手台的人都能用。不用的時候，鉸鏈讓兩片木板能緊緊摺回櫃門上，再用磁鐵固定。Jeanie 把她的發明取名為「Kiddie Stool」（兒童凳）。

Jeanie 的兒童凳在學校的比賽中得到第一名。兩年後，兒童凳在休士頓第一屆年度發明展又得到首獎。因此，Jeanie 受邀帶著兒童凳多次公開亮相，也登上地方電視和報紙。許多人覺得兒童凳的故事很激勵人心，因為它說明了只要有想像力，人人都可以當發明家。

items.stem: Why did Jeanie Low invent the Kiddie Stool, according to the passage?
options: Many other five-year-olds had problems reaching the bathroom sink.
She did not think that plastic stools were tall enough for her.
The stool in her bathroom was not firm and often got in the way.
She was invited to enter an invention contest held by her school.
items.explanation:
However, the plastic step-stool she had at home was unstable and cluttered up the small bathroom shared by her whole family.
第 1 段說 Jeanie 家裡的塑膠踏凳不穩（unstable），又讓小浴室很擠（cluttered up），選項換成 not firm 和 often got in the way。(D) 照抄 invention contest held by her school，學校的發明比賽是她動手做的契機，她要解決的是凳子不穩又占空間的問題，而且原文說她決定參加，不是受邀參加；(A) 照抄 five-year-olds，原文只說她和許多五歲小孩一樣要踩凳子，沒說其他小孩有困難；(B) 照抄 plastic，原文沒說塑膠凳不夠高。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about how the Kiddie Stool works?
options: The Kiddie Stool will swing out only when the cabinet door opens.
It uses hinges and magnets to keep the wooden pieces in place.
It swings from left to right to be attached to the cabinet door.
The platform is supported by two pieces of metal.
items.explanation:
Using metal hinges, Jeanie attached one piece of the wood to the front of the cabinet door, and the second piece to the first.
When not in use, the hinges allowed the two pieces of wood to fold back up tightly against the cabinet, where they were held in place by magnets.
第 2 段說 Jeanie 用金屬鉸鏈把兩片木板接起來，不用時鉸鏈讓木板摺回櫃門上，再用磁鐵固定（held in place by magnets），選項換成 uses hinges and magnets to keep the wooden pieces in place。(A) 照抄 cabinet door，凳子是從櫃門上往外展開，原文沒說要先打開櫃門；(C) 照抄 swing，原文說第一片木板水平展開、第二片往下擺，不是左右擺動；(D) 照抄 metal，金屬做的是鉸鏈，支撐平台的是兩片木板。

items.stem: What are the characteristics of Jeanie’s Kiddie Stool?
items.explanation:
Jeanie resolved to enter the contest by creating a stool that would be a permanent fixture in the bathroom, and yet could be kept out of the way when not in use.
When not in use, the hinges allowed the two pieces of wood to fold back up tightly against the cabinet, where they were held in place by magnets.
第 1 段說 Jeanie 要做一張固定在浴室裡（permanent fixture）、不用時又能收起來的凳子；第 2 段說不用時兩片木板能摺回櫃門上（fold back），選項換成 Permanent and foldable。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 convenient，方便說對了一半，但 recyclable 可回收文章沒提；(B) fragile 脆弱，和原文說的 sturdy 穩固正好相反；(C) touching 感人說的是第 3 段大家對這個故事的感受，conventional 傳統的也和新發明接不上。

items.stem: Which of the following sayings best captures the spirit of Jeanie Low’s story?
options: Failure is the mother of success.
There’s nothing new under the sun.
Necessity is the mother of invention.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說 Jeanie 因為家裡的凳子不穩又占空間，才想做一張更好的凳子；第 2 段說她怎麼做出兒童凳；第 3 段說兒童凳得獎、激勵許多人。整個故事是生活上有需要，才催生了發明，最貼切的是 (C) 需要為發明之母。(A) 失敗為成功之母，Jeanie 的發明一路得獎，文章沒有寫到失敗；(B) 太陽底下沒有新鮮事，和她做出新發明的故事不合；(D) 天才是 1% 的靈感加 99% 的汗水，強調的是苦幹，文章結尾強調的卻是想像力；三個選項都偏離主題。

閱讀測驗.title: 中東地區的失學兒童（Children Out of School in the Middle East）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Ongoing conflicts across the Middle East have prevented more than 13 million children from attending school, according to a report published by UNICEF, the United Nations Children’s Fund.

The report states that 40% of all children across the region are currently not receiving an education, which is a result of two consequences of violence: structural damage to schools and the displacement of populations, also called “forced migration.” Both issues result from the tide of violence that has crossed the region in recent years. The report examines nine countries where a state of war has become the norm. Across these countries, violence has made 8,500 schools unusable. In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.

The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011. With the crisis now in its fifth year, basic public services, including education, inside Syria have been stretched to breaking point. Within the country, the quality and availability of education depends on whether a particular region is suffering violence.

The report concludes with an earnest request to international policymakers to distribute financial and other resources to ease the regional crisis. With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance. The forces that are crushing individual lives and futures are also destroying the prospects for an entire region.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
根據聯合國兒童基金會發表的一份報告，中東各地持續不斷的衝突，使超過 1,300 萬名兒童無法上學。

報告指出，這個地區所有的兒童中，目前有 40% 沒有接受教育，原因是暴力帶來的兩個後果：學校建築遭到破壞，以及人口流離失所，也就是所謂的「強迫遷徙」。這兩個問題都來自近年席捲這個地區的暴力浪潮。報告調查了九個長期處於戰爭狀態的國家，在這些國家裡，暴力已經使 8,500 所學校無法使用。在某些情況下，社區把學校建築當作流離失所者的收容所，在伊拉克各地原本的學校裡，一間教室最多住了九戶人家。

報告特別關注敘利亞。敘利亞自 2011 年爆發血腥內戰以來，至少已有 900 萬人流離失所。危機如今已進入第五年，敘利亞境內包括教育在內的基本公共服務，都已經不堪負荷、瀕臨崩潰。在敘利亞國內，教育的品質和普及程度，要看某個地區是否正遭受暴力。

報告最後懇切呼籲國際決策者，提供資金和其他資源來緩解這個地區的危機。已經有超過 1,300 萬名兒童因為衝突離開教室，說一整個世代兒童的教育前景岌岌可危，一點也不誇張。摧毀個人生命和未來的這股力量，也正在摧毀整個地區的前景。

items.stem: What is this article mainly about?
options: Why people are moving away from their own countries.
Why there are civil wars and violence in the Middle East.
Why many schools have become shelters for displaced families.
Why many children in the Middle East are not attending school.
items.explanation: 第 1 段開頭就說中東的衝突使超過 1,300 萬名兒童無法上學；第 2 段說明兩個原因：學校遭到破壞、人口流離失所；第 3 段以敘利亞為例；第 4 段呼籲國際提供資源。全文要回答的是為什麼許多中東兒童沒有上學，所以是 (D)。(A) 人口遷離家園和 (C) 學校變成收容所，都只是第 2 段說明的原因，過於狹隘；(B) 文章沒有分析內戰和暴力為什麼發生，偏離主題。

items.stem: Why is “Iraq” mentioned in the second paragraph?
options: To convince people that temporary housing can be easily found.
To prove that classrooms there are big enough to host many families.
To give an example of why schools are not usable for children’s learning.
To show how structural damages of school can affect the quality of education.
items.explanation:
Across these countries, violence has made 8,500 schools unusable.
In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.
第 2 段先說暴力使 8,500 所學校無法使用（unusable），接著用 In certain cases 帶出伊拉克的例子：學校成了收容所，一間教室住到九戶人家。提到伊拉克，是為了舉例說明學校為什麼不能用來上課，選項把 unusable 換成 not usable。(D) 照抄 structural damage，但伊拉克的例子說的是學校拿來安置流離失所的人，不是建築毀損，教育品質是第 3 段講敘利亞時才提到；(B) 照抄 families，一間教室住九戶人家是說擁擠，不是說教室夠大；(A) 文章沒說臨時住處很容易找到。

items.stem: What does the phrase “in the balance” in the last paragraph most likely mean?
items.explanation:
With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance.
第 4 段說已經有超過 1,300 萬名兒童因為衝突離開教室，說一整個世代兒童的教育前景 in the balance 一點也不誇張。這麼多孩子失學，他們的教育前景會怎麼樣還說不定，in the balance 就是懸而未決、岌岌可危，最接近 (B) 處於不確定的狀況。(A) 受到妥善照顧、(C) 由當局控制，都和失學的處境不合；(D) 往錯誤的方向走，是把前景當成已經確定變壞，原文說的是結果還未定。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
options: The war in Syria has been going on since 2011.
More than nine thousand schools have been destroyed by wars.
Thirteen million people have been forced to leave their homes in the Middle East.
Forty percent of all children in the world are not attending schools due to ongoing conflict.
items.explanation:
The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011.
第 3 段說敘利亞的血腥內戰從 2011 年開始，選項把 since the war began in 2011 換成 has been going on since 2011。(B) 照抄 nine，原文的 nine 是九百萬人流離失所和九個國家，無法使用的學校是 8,500 所，不到九千所；(C) 照抄第 2 段 forced migration 的 forced，1,300 萬是無法上學的兒童人數，不是離開家園的人數；(D) 40% 指的是中東地區的兒童，不是全世界的兒童。

閱讀測驗.title: 海蛇的飲水策略（How Sea Snakes Drink）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Many marine animals, including penguins and marine iguanas, have evolved ways to get rid of excess salt by using special salt-expelling glands around their tongue. However, the sea snake’s salt glands cannot handle the massive amounts of salt that would enter their bodies if they actually drank seawater. This poses a serious problem when it comes to getting enough water to drink. If seawater is not an option, how does this animal survive in the ocean?

An international team of researchers focused on a population of yellow-bellied sea snakes living near Costa Rica, where rain often does not fall for up to seven months out of the year. Because yellow-bellied sea snakes usually spend all of their time far from land, rain is the animals’ only source of fresh water. When it rains, a thin layer of fresh water forms on top of the ocean, providing the snakes with a fleeting opportunity to lap up that precious resource. But during the dry season when there is no rain, snakes presumably have nothing to drink. Thus, the team became interested in testing whether sea snakes became dehydrated at sea.

The researchers collected more than 500 yellow-bellied sea snakes and weighed them. They found that during the dry season about half of the snakes accepted fresh water offered to them, while nearly none did during the wet season. A snake’s likelihood to drink also correlated with its body condition, with more withered snakes being more likely to drink, and to drink more. Finally, as predicted, snakes captured during the dry season contained significantly less body water than those scooped up in the rainy season. Thus, it seems the snake is able to endure certain degrees of dehydration in between rains. Scientists believe that dehydration at sea may explain the declining populations of sea snakes in some parts of the world.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
許多海洋動物，包括企鵝和海鬣蜥，都演化出排除多餘鹽分的方法，靠的是舌頭周圍專門排鹽的腺體。不過，海蛇如果真的喝下海水，大量的鹽分會進入體內，牠們的鹽腺應付不了。要喝到足夠的水，這就成了一個嚴重的問題。既然不能喝海水，這種動物要怎麼在海洋裡生存呢？

一個國際研究團隊鎖定一群住在哥斯大黎加附近的黃腹海蛇，當地一年中可能長達七個月不下雨。黃腹海蛇通常一直待在遠離陸地的海上，所以雨水是牠們唯一的淡水來源。下雨時，海面上會形成一層薄薄的淡水，海蛇才有短暫的機會舔飲這珍貴的資源。但是在不下雨的乾季，海蛇大概就沒有水可以喝了。因此，研究團隊想知道海蛇在海上是否會脫水。

研究人員捕捉了 500 多條黃腹海蛇，並替牠們秤重。他們發現，乾季時大約一半的海蛇會喝研究人員提供的淡水，雨季時則幾乎沒有一條海蛇會喝。海蛇喝不喝水，也和牠的身體狀況有關：越乾瘦的海蛇越可能喝水，也喝得越多。最後，一如預期，乾季捕獲的海蛇體內水分明顯比雨季捕獲的少。由此看來，海蛇似乎能在兩場雨之間忍受某種程度的脫水。科學家認為，海上脫水可能可以解釋某些地區海蛇數量為什麼減少。

items.stem: What is the purpose of the study described in this passage?
options: To test if sea snakes lose body water at sea.
To see whether sea snakes drink water offered to them.
To find out if sea snakes are greatly reduced in population.
To prove that sea snakes drink only water coming from rivers.
items.explanation:
Thus, the team became interested in testing whether sea snakes became dehydrated at sea.
第 2 段最後說研究團隊想知道海蛇在海上是否會脫水（became dehydrated），這就是研究目的，選項把 became dehydrated 換成 lose body water。(B) 照抄第 3 段的 offered to them，請海蛇喝淡水是研究的做法，不是目的；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 population，海蛇數量減少是研究結束後科學家提出的推測；(D) 原文說雨水是海蛇唯一的淡水來源，文章沒有提到河水。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about sea snakes?
options: Their salt glands can remove the salt in the seawater.
They can drink seawater when it mixes with rainwater.
The ocean is like a desert to them since they don’t drink seawater.
They usually live near the coastal area where there is more fresh water.
items.explanation:
However, the sea snake’s salt glands cannot handle the massive amounts of salt that would enter their bodies if they actually drank seawater.
But during the dry season when there is no rain, snakes presumably have nothing to drink.
第 1 段說海蛇的鹽腺應付不了海水的鹽分，不能喝海水；第 2 段說乾季不下雨時，海蛇大概沒有水可以喝。身在一大片海水中卻沒水可喝，就像在沙漠裡一樣，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 salt glands，原文說的正好相反，海蛇的鹽腺排不掉喝海水帶進來的鹽；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 fresh water，原文說黃腹海蛇通常待在遠離陸地的海上；(B) 原文說下雨時海面會形成一層淡水，海蛇喝的是這層淡水，不是摻了雨水的海水。

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the findings of the study?
options: If a sea snake was dried and weak, it drank more fresh water.
If captured in the wet season, sea snakes drank a lot of fresh water.
Most of the sea snakes had lost a lot of body water when captured.
Dehydration is not a problem among sea snakes since they live at sea.
items.explanation:
A snake’s likelihood to drink also correlated with its body condition, with more withered snakes being more likely to drink, and to drink more.
第 3 段說越乾瘦的海蛇（more withered）越可能喝水，也喝得越多，選項換成 dried and weak 和 drank more。(B) 照抄 wet season，原文說雨季時幾乎沒有海蛇喝水；(C) 照抄 body water，原文說的是乾季捕獲的海蛇體內水分比雨季少，不是大多數海蛇都失去很多水分；(D) 照抄 dehydration，研究發現海蛇會在海上脫水，脫水還可能造成某些地區海蛇減少，不是沒有問題。

items.stem: What can be inferred from the study?
options: Sea snakes can easily survive long years of drought.
Evolution will very likely enable sea snakes to drink seawater.
Sea snakes will be the last creature affected by global warming.
The sea snakes’ population distribution is closely related to rainfall.
items.explanation:
Because yellow-bellied sea snakes usually spend all of their time far from land, rain is the animals’ only source of fresh water.
Scientists believe that dehydration at sea may explain the declining populations of sea snakes in some parts of the world.
第 2 段說雨水是黃腹海蛇唯一的淡水來源，第 3 段說科學家認為海上脫水可能是某些地區海蛇減少的原因。雨少的地方海蛇容易脫水、數量減少，可以推論海蛇分布在哪裡和雨量有密切關係，所以是 (D)。(A) 原文說海蛇只能在兩場雨之間忍受某種程度的脫水，不是能熬過多年乾旱；(B) 文章沒說海蛇會演化出喝海水的能力；(C) 文章沒有談全球暖化。

閱讀測驗.title: 妮娜號複製船上的動手學習（Hands-on Learning aboard the Nina Replica Ship）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Some people call it a traveling museum. Others refer to it as a living or open-air museum. Built in Brazil to celebrate the quincentennial of Columbus’ first voyage to the New World, the Nina, a Columbus-era replica ship, provides visitors with an accurate visual of the size and sailing implements of Columbus’ favorite ship from over 500 years ago.

I joined the crew of the Nina in Gulf Shores, Alabama, in February 2013. As part of a research project sponsored by my university, my goal was to document my days aboard the ship in a blog. I quickly realized that I gained the most valuable insights when I observed or gave tours to school-age children. The field-trip tour of the Nina is hands-on learning at its best. In this setting, students could touch the line, pass around a ballast stone, and move the extremely large tiller that steered the ships in Columbus’ day. They soon came to understand the labor involved in sailing the ship back in his time. I was pleased to see the students become active participants in their learning process.

The Nina is not the only traveling museum that provides such field trips. A visit to Jamestown Settlement, for example, allows visitors to board three re-creations of the ships that brought the first settlers from England to Virginia in the early 1600s. Historical interpreters, dressed in period garb, give tours to the Susan Constant, Godspeed, and Discovery. These interpreters often portray a character that would have lived and worked during that time period. Students touring these ships are encouraged to interact with the interpreters in order to better understand the daily life in the past.

My experience on the Nina helps substantiate my long-held belief that students stay interested, ask better questions, and engage in higher-order thinking tasks when they are actively engaged in the learning process. The students who boarded the Nina came as passive learners. They left as bold explorers.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
有人說它是一座巡迴博物館，也有人說它是一座活的或露天的博物館。妮娜號是一艘哥倫布時代的複製船，在巴西建造，用來慶祝哥倫布第一次航行到新世界 500 週年。這艘船讓參觀的人親眼看到，500 多年前哥倫布最喜愛的那艘船有多大、用的是哪些航海器具，而且和原船一模一樣。

2013 年 2 月，我在阿拉巴馬州的海灣海岸（Gulf Shores）加入妮娜號的船員行列。這是我任職的大學贊助的研究計畫的一部分，我的目標是用網誌記錄我在船上的日子。我很快就發現，我觀察學齡孩子參觀、或是自己帶孩子參觀的時候，得到的心得最寶貴。妮娜號的校外教學導覽，是動手學習的最佳示範。在這裡，學生可以摸摸纜繩，傳遞壓艙石，還可以推動那根非常大的舵柄，哥倫布那個時代的船就是靠舵柄掌舵。學生很快就了解，在他那個時代駕船航行需要多少勞力。看到學生在學習過程中成為主動的參與者，我很高興。

提供這種校外教學的巡迴博物館，不只有妮娜號。舉例來說，參觀詹姆斯鎮殖民地（Jamestown Settlement），可以登上三艘重建的船。1600 年代初期，就是這三艘船把第一批移民從英國載到維吉尼亞。穿著那個時代服裝的歷史解說員，帶大家參觀 Susan Constant、Godspeed 和 Discovery 這三艘船。這些解說員常常扮演那個時代可能在那裡生活、工作的人物。參觀這些船的學生，都會受到鼓勵和解說員互動，好更了解過去的日常生活。

我長久以來相信，學生主動投入學習過程的時候，會保持興趣、問出更好的問題，也會投入高層次思考的任務。我在妮娜號上的經驗，有助於證實這個看法。登上妮娜號的學生，來的時候只會等著別人教，離開的時候已經成了勇敢的探險家。

items.stem: What line of business is the author engaged in?
items.explanation:
As part of a research project sponsored by my university
my long-held belief that students stay interested, ask better questions, and engage in higher-order thinking tasks
作者在第 2 段說，上船是任職大學（my university）贊助的研究計畫的一部分，最有收穫的是觀察學童參觀、帶學生導覽；第 4 段又說他長久以來相信，學生主動投入學習，會保持興趣、問出更好的問題。研究學生怎麼學習的大學教師，從事的是教育工作，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 ship，作者只是暫時加入船員，目的是寫網誌記錄；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 museum，妮娜號是一座巡迴博物館，作者不是博物館的管理人員；(C) 的 tourism 和第 2 段的 tours 看起來很像，但作者帶的是學生的校外教學，原文也沒有提到生態。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about the Nina introduced in the passage?
options: She is a replica of a ship that Columbus built in Brazil.
She is always crowded with foreign tourists during holidays.
She is the boat Columbus sailed in his voyage to the New World.
She displays a replica of the navigational equipment used in Columbus’ time.
items.explanation:
the Nina, a Columbus-era replica ship, provides visitors with an accurate visual of the size and sailing implements of Columbus’ favorite ship
這一題答對率只有 38%，關鍵是分清楚原船和複製船。判斷步驟：[1] 第 1 段說妮娜號是哥倫布時代的複製船（replica ship），是為了紀念 500 週年才在巴西造的；[2] 這艘船讓人看到哥倫布那艘船的大小和航海器具（sailing implements），器具也是照原樣複製的；[3] 選項把 sailing implements 換成 navigational equipment，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 Brazil，在巴西造的是複製船，原船不是哥倫布在巴西造的；(C) 照抄 New World，搭到新世界的是原船，現在這艘是複製的；(B) 原文沒有提到假日擠滿外國觀光客。

items.stem: What is the third paragraph mainly about?
options: Guidelines for visitors on the ships.
Life of the first settlers in Jamestown Settlement.
Duties of the interpreters in the British museums.
Introduction to some open-air museums similar to the Nina.
items.explanation:
The Nina is not the only traveling museum that provides such field trips.
A visit to Jamestown Settlement, for example
這一題答對率只有 41%，判斷的方法是看這一段的第一句。第 3 段第一句說，提供這種校外教學的巡迴博物館不只有妮娜號（not the only traveling museum），接著用 for example 舉詹姆斯鎮殖民地的三艘船為例。這一段講的是和妮娜號類似的博物館，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 Jamestown Settlement，這一段只說船載著第一批移民到維吉尼亞，沒有描述移民的生活；(C) 照抄 interpreters，解說員是這個例子裡的一部分，而且船在美國維吉尼亞，不是英國的博物館；(A) 照抄 visitors，原文沒有列出參觀須知。

items.stem: What does the author mean by the last two sentences of the passage?
options: The students are interested in becoming tour guides.
The experience has changed the students’ learning attitude.
The students become brave and are ready to sail the seas on their own.
The museums are successful in teaching the students survival skills at sea.
items.explanation:
The students who boarded the Nina came as passive learners.
They left as bold explorers.
最後兩句說，學生來的時候是 passive learners，只會等著別人教，離開的時候成了勇敢的探險家（bold explorers）。探險家是比喻，指學生變得主動去探索、去發問，呼應前一句作者說學生主動投入時會保持興趣、問出更好的問題，所以是 (B) 學習態度改變了。(C) 把 explorers 照字面解釋成真的要出海航行；(A) 和 (D) 原文都沒有提到。

閱讀測驗.title: 大型貓科動物起源的新發現（A New Finding on the Origin of Big Cats）
閱讀測驗.passage:
An ancient skull unearthed recently indicates that big cats originated in central Asia—not Africa as widely thought, paleontologists reported on Wednesday.

Dated at between 4.1 and 5.95 million years old, the fossil is the oldest remains ever found of a pantherine felid, as big cats are called. The previous felid record holder—tooth fragments found in Tanzania—is estimated to be around 3.8 million years old.

The evolution of big cats has been hotly discussed, and the issue is complicated by a lack of fossil evidence to settle the debate.

“This find suggests that big cats have a deeper evolutionary origin than previously suspected,” said Jack Tseng, a paleontologist of the University of Southern California who led the probe.

Tseng and his team made the find in 2010 in a remote border region in Tibet. The fossil was found stuck among more than 100 bones that were probably deposited by a river that exited a cliff. After three years of careful comparisons with other fossils, using DNA data to build a family tree, the team is convinced the creature was a pantherine felid.

The weight of evidence suggests that central or northern Asia is where big cats originated some 16 million years ago. They may have lived in a vast mountain refuge, formed by the uplifting Himalayas, feeding on equally remarkable species such as the Tibetan blue sheep. They then dispersed into Southeast Asia, evolving into the clouded leopard, tiger and snow leopard lineages, and later movements across continents saw them evolve into jaguars and lions.

The newly discovered felid has been called Panthera Blytheae, after Blythe Haaga, daughter of a couple who support a museum in Los Angeles, the university said in a news release.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
古生物學家星期三發表報告說，最近出土的一個古老頭骨顯示，大型貓科動物起源於中亞，而不是一般認為的非洲。

這個化石的年代在 410 萬到 595 萬年前之間，是目前發現最古老的豹亞科貓科動物遺骸，大型貓科動物就屬於豹亞科。之前的紀錄保持者，是在坦尚尼亞發現的牙齒碎片，估計大約有 380 萬年。

大型貓科動物的演化一直是熱烈討論的議題，由於缺乏化石證據來解決爭論，問題也就更加複雜。

領導這項研究的南加州大學古生物學家 Jack Tseng 說：「這項發現顯示，大型貓科動物演化的起源比之前推測的更早。」

Tseng 和他的團隊在 2010 年，在西藏一個偏遠的邊境地區發現了這個化石。化石卡在一百多根骨頭之間，這些骨頭可能是一條從懸崖流出的河流沖積下來的。團隊花了三年仔細和其他化石比對，又用 DNA 資料建立家族譜系，確信這種動物是豹亞科貓科動物。

證據大多顯示，大型貓科動物大約在 1,600 萬年前起源於中亞或北亞。牠們可能住在喜馬拉雅山隆起形成的廣大山區避難所，以同樣特別的物種為食，例如西藏岩羊。後來牠們散布到東南亞，演化出雲豹、老虎和雪豹這幾個分支；之後又跨越各大洲遷徙，演化成美洲豹和獅子。

大學在新聞稿中說，這種新發現的貓科動物命名為布氏豹（Panthera blytheae），名稱來自 Blythe Haaga。她的父母是洛杉磯一座博物館的贊助人。

items.stem: According to the passage, why is the origin of big cats a hot issue?
options: Because not many fossils have been found.
Because no equipment was available for accurate analysis.
Because they have evolved into many different species of felid.
items.explanation:
the issue is complicated by a lack of fossil evidence to settle the debate.
這一題答對率只有 45%，答案在一段只有一句話的第 3 段，很容易略過。第 3 段說大型貓科動物的演化一直是熱烈討論的議題，因為缺乏化石證據（a lack of fossil evidence）來解決爭論，選項換成沒有發現多少化石，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 6 段的 across continents，跨越各大洲遷徙是研究的結論，不是爭論的原因；(D) 照抄第 6 段的 evolve，演化出不同的物種也是結論的一部分；(C) 原文沒有提到缺乏儀器，第 5 段反而說團隊用 DNA 資料建立了家族譜系。

items.stem: Where was the new felid fossil found?
items.explanation:
Tseng and his team made the find in 2010 in a remote border region in Tibet.
第 5 段說 Tseng 的團隊在西藏（Tibet）偏遠的邊境地區發現了這個化石，所以是 (B)。(A) 坦尚尼亞是之前那塊最古老牙齒碎片的發現地點；(C) California 出自第 4 段的南加州大學，是 Tseng 任職的學校；(D) 東南亞是大型貓科動物後來散布的地方。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true regarding big cats?
options: Some big cats evolved into jaguars 16 million years ago.
The oldest fossil of big cats ever discovered is 3.8 million years old.
Big cats are descendants of snow leopards living in high mountains.
Tibetan blue sheep was a main food source for big cats in the Himalayas.
items.explanation:
feeding on equally remarkable species such as the Tibetan blue sheep.
這一題答對率只有 49%，三個錯誤選項都把原文的數字或順序弄錯了。第 6 段說大型貓科動物住在喜馬拉雅山的山區，以（feeding on）西藏岩羊這類物種為食，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 jaguars，1,600 萬年前是大型貓科動物起源的時間，演化成美洲豹是更後來（later）的事；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 3.8 million，380 萬年是之前的紀錄，這次發現的化石有 410 萬到 595 萬年，更古老；(C) 照抄 snow leopard，雪豹是大型貓科動物演化出來的分支，選項把祖先和後代說反了。

items.stem: What is the purpose of this passage?
options: To report on a new finding in paleontology.
To introduce a new animal species.
To compare the family trees of pantherine felids.
items.explanation: 第 1 段開頭就說古生物學家發表報告，新出土的頭骨顯示大型貓科動物起源於中亞；接下來各段說明化石的年代、發現的地點和研究方法，最後說明研究的結論。這是一篇報導古生物學新發現的新聞，所以是 (B)。(C) 第 7 段才說這種動物的命名，過於狹隘；(D) 照抄第 5 段的 family tree，建立家族譜系只是研究方法，文章沒有比較不同的譜系，過於狹隘；(A) 全文沒有談到保育，偏離主題。

閱讀測驗.title: 美國烹飪節目的演變（The Evolution of American Cooking Shows）
閱讀測驗.passage:
American cooking programs have taught audiences, changed audiences, and changed with audiences from generation to generation. In October 1926, the U.S. Department of Agriculture created this genre’s first official representative, a fictional radio host named Aunt Sammy. Over the airwaves, she educated homemakers on home economics and doled out advice on all kinds of matters, but it was mostly the cooking recipes that got listeners’ attention. The show provided a channel for transmitting culinary advice and brought about a national exchange of recipes.

Cooking shows transitioned to television in the 1940s, and in the 1950s were often presented by a cook systematically explaining instructions on how to prepare dishes from start to finish. These programs were broadcast during the day and aimed at middle-class women whose mindset leaned toward convenient foods for busy families. Poppy Cannon, for example, was a popular writer of The Can-Opener Cookbook. She appeared on various television shows, using canned foods to demonstrate how to cook quickly and easily.

Throughout the sixties and seventies, a few chef-oriented shows redefined the genre as an exhibition of haute European cuisine by celebrity gourmet experts. This elite cultural aura then gave way to various cooking styles from around the world. An example of such change can be seen in Martin Yan’s 1982 “Yan Can Cook” series, which demonstrated Chinese cuisine cooking with the catchphrase, “If Yan can cook, you can too!” By the 1990s, these cooking shows ranged from high-culture to health-conscious cuisine, with chefs’ personalities and entertainment value being two keys to successful productions.

At the beginning of the 21st century, new cooking shows emerged to satisfy celeb-hungry, reality-crazed audiences. In this new millennium of out-of-studio shows and chef competition reality shows, chefs have become celebrities whose fame rivals that of rock stars. Audiences of these shows tend to be people who are interested in food and enjoy watching people cook rather than those who want to do the cooking themselves, leaving the age-old emphasis on following recipes outmoded.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
美國的烹飪節目，一代又一代地教導觀眾、改變觀眾，也隨著觀眾而改變。1926 年 10 月，美國農業部創造了這類節目第一位官方的代表人物：一位虛構的廣播主持人，名叫 Aunt Sammy（山姆阿姨）。她透過電波教導家庭主婦家政知識，也對各種事情提供建議，但最吸引聽眾注意的，主要是烹飪的食譜。這個節目提供了傳遞烹飪建議的管道，也促成了全國性的食譜交流。

烹飪節目在 1940 年代轉到電視上。1950 年代的節目，通常由一位廚師有系統地說明一道菜從頭到尾怎麼做。這些節目在白天播出，對象是中產階級的婦女，她們心裡想的，是替忙碌的家庭準備方便的食物。例如 Poppy Cannon 是《開罐器食譜》（The Can-Opener Cookbook）的作者，很受歡迎。她上過許多電視節目，用罐頭食品示範怎麼快速、輕鬆地做菜。

整個 1960 和 1970 年代，少數以名廚為主的節目，把這類節目重新定位為由知名美食專家展示歐洲高級料理的舞台。後來這種菁英文化的氣息，讓位給世界各地各式各樣的烹飪風格。這種改變的一個例子，是甄文達（Martin Yan）1982 年的系列節目《甄能煮》（Yan Can Cook）。節目示範中國菜的做法，有一句經典台詞：「If Yan can cook, you can too!」（甄能煮，你也能煮！）到了 1990 年代，這些烹飪節目從高雅文化的料理到注重健康的料理都有，廚師的個人特色和娛樂性，成為節目成功的兩大關鍵。

21 世紀初，出現了新的烹飪節目，迎合渴望看到名人、熱愛實境秀的觀眾。在這個新的千禧年，有攝影棚外拍攝的節目，也有廚師比賽的實境秀，廚師成了名人，名氣和搖滾巨星不相上下。這些節目的觀眾，多半是對食物有興趣、喜歡看別人做菜的人，而不是想自己下廚的人，向來重視照著食譜做菜的傳統，也就過時了。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “haute” in the third paragraph?
items.explanation:
redefined the genre as an exhibition of haute European cuisine by celebrity gourmet experts.
This elite cultural aura then gave way to various cooking styles from around the world.
這一題答對率只有 40%，haute 是法文字，學生多半沒有見過，要靠上下文推。判斷步驟：[1] 這個字修飾 European cuisine，展示的人是知名的美食專家（celebrity gourmet experts）；[2] 下一句用 This elite cultural aura 回頭指這種節目，elite（菁英的）就是在說前一句的料理；[3] 所以 haute 是「高級的」，答案是 (D)。字典也把 haute cuisine 解釋為高水準的料理，通常指法國菜。(C) 照抄下一句的 various，各式各樣的烹飪風格是後來取代高級料理的東西，意思剛好相反；(A) 粗糙的、(B) 平民的，都和菁英的氣息相反。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about audiences of American cooking shows?
options: Those in the ’30s preferred advice on home economics to cooking instructions.
Those in the ’40s and ’50s were interested in food preparation for busy families.
Those in the ’60s and ’70s were eager to exchange recipes with each other.
Those in the ’80s enjoyed genuine American-style gourmet cooking.
items.explanation:
aimed at middle-class women whose mindset leaned toward convenient foods for busy families.
第 2 段說烹飪節目在 1940 年代轉到電視，1950 年代的節目對象是中產階級婦女，她們想的是替忙碌的家庭（busy families）準備方便的食物，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 home economics，那是 1926 年的廣播節目，而且最吸引聽眾的是食譜，不是家政建議；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 exchange，全國性的食譜交流也是 1926 年廣播節目的影響；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 gourmet，美食專家展示的是歐洲料理，1982 年的例子是中國菜，不是美式料理。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about the most recent cooking programs?
options: They are often hosted by rock stars.
They are often not filmed in the studios.
They invite hungry audience members to be judges.
items.explanation:
In this new millennium of out-of-studio shows and chef competition reality shows
這一題答對率只有 37%，三個錯誤選項都是把第 4 段的字拆開來，重新組合成錯的意思。第 4 段說新的千禧年有攝影棚外拍攝的節目（out-of-studio shows），選項換成常常不在攝影棚拍攝，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 rock stars，原文說廚師的名氣和搖滾巨星不相上下，不是搖滾巨星來主持；(C) 照抄 celeb，celeb-hungry 是觀眾渴望看到名人，不是觀眾本身是名人；(D) 照抄 hungry，hungry 在 celeb-hungry 裡是「渴望」，不是肚子餓，原文也沒有提到觀眾當評審。

items.stem: Which of the following would most likely be a hit cooking show in the ’90s?
options: A show dedicated to European cuisine and gourmet food.
A show sponsored by food companies advertising new products.
A show hosted by a humorous chef presenting low-calorie dishes.
A show with a professional cook demonstrating systematic ways of cooking.
items.explanation:
By the 1990s, these cooking shows ranged from high-culture to health-conscious cuisine, with chefs’ personalities and entertainment value being two keys to successful productions.
第 3 段說到了 1990 年代，節目有注重健康（health-conscious）的料理，廚師的個人特色和娛樂性是節目成功的兩大關鍵。幽默的廚師有個人特色、有娛樂性，低卡路里的菜注重健康，兩個條件都符合，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 European cuisine，那是 1960、1970 年代的節目，後來已經讓位給世界各地的料理；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 systematic，有系統地示範做菜是 1950 年代的節目；(B) 原文沒有提到食品公司贊助。

閱讀測驗.title: 尖叫的特性與應用（What Makes Screams Unique and How to Use It）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Screaming is one of the primal responses humans share with other animals. Conventional thinking suggests that what sets a scream apart from other sounds is its loudness or high pitch. However, many sounds that are loud and high-pitched do not raise goose bumps like screams can. To find out what makes human screams unique, neuroscientist Luc Arnal and his team examined a bank of sounds containing sentences spoken or screamed by 19 adults. The result shows screams and screamed sentences had a quality called “roughness,” which refers to how fast a sound changes in loudness. While normal speech sounds only have slight differences in loudness—between 4 and 5 Hz, screams can switch very fast, varying between 30 and 150 Hz, thus perceived as being rough and unpleasant.

Arnal’s team asked 20 subjects to judge screams as neutral or fearful, and found that the scariest almost always corresponded with roughness. The team then studied how the human brain responds to roughness using fMRI brain scanners. As expected, after hearing a scream, activity increased in the brain’s auditory centers where sound coming into the ears is processed. But the scans also lit up in the amygdala, the brain’s fear center.

The amygdala is the area that regulates our emotional and physiological response to danger. When a threat is detected, our adrenaline rises, and our body prepares to react to danger. The study discovered that screams have a similar influence on our body. It also found that roughness isn’t heard when we speak naturally, regardless of the language we use, but it is prevalent in artificial sounds. The most aggravating alarm clocks, car horns, and fire alarms possess high degrees of roughness.

One potential application for this research might be to add roughness to alarm sounds to make them more effective, the same way a bad smell is added to natural gas to make it easily detectable. Warning sounds could also be added to electric cars, which are particularly silent, so they can be efficiently detected by pedestrians.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
尖叫是人類和其他動物共有的原始反應之一。一般的想法認為，尖叫和其他聲音不同的地方，在於音量大或音調高。然而，許多又大聲、音調又高的聲音，並不像尖叫那樣讓人起雞皮疙瘩。為了找出人類的尖叫特別在哪裡，神經科學家 Luc Arnal 和他的團隊研究了一個聲音資料庫，裡面是 19 位成人說出或尖叫出來的句子。結果顯示，尖叫和尖叫出來的句子，都有一種叫做「粗糙度」（roughness）的特性，指的是聲音的音量變化得多快。一般說話的聲音，音量只有些微的差異，在 4 到 5 赫茲之間；尖叫的音量卻可以變化得非常快，在 30 到 150 赫茲之間，所以聽起來粗糙、刺耳。

Arnal 的團隊請 20 位受試者判斷尖叫聲是平常的還是恐懼的，發現最可怕的尖叫，幾乎都是最粗糙的。團隊接著用功能性磁振造影（fMRI）掃描儀，研究人腦對粗糙度有什麼反應。和預期的一樣，聽到尖叫以後，大腦處理耳朵接收到的聲音的聽覺中樞，活動增加了。不過，掃描影像上，大腦的恐懼中心杏仁核也亮了起來。

杏仁核是調節我們對危險的情緒和生理反應的區域。察覺到威脅的時候，我們的腎上腺素上升，身體準備對危險做出反應。研究發現，尖叫對身體也有類似的影響。研究也發現，不管我們說的是哪一種語言，自然說話的時候都聽不到粗糙度，但人工的聲音卻常常有粗糙度。最讓人煩躁的鬧鐘、汽車喇叭和火災警報器，粗糙度都很高。

這項研究可能的一個應用，是在警報聲裡加入粗糙度，讓警報更有效，就像在天然氣裡加入難聞的氣味，讓人容易察覺一樣。也可以替特別安靜的電動車加上警示音，讓行人能有效地察覺。

items.stem: What is the first paragraph mainly about?
items.explanation:
To find out what makes human screams unique
which refers to how fast a sound changes in loudness.
第 1 段先說一般認為尖叫的特別之處是大聲或高音，但許多大聲的高音並不讓人起雞皮疙瘩；接著說 Arnal 的團隊研究人類的尖叫特別在哪裡（what makes human screams unique），發現尖叫有「粗糙度」，也就是音量變化很快。這一段講的是尖叫有哪些特點，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 animal，人類和動物共有尖叫的反應只是第一句的開場；(D) 照抄 goose bumps，雞皮疙瘩是用來說明大聲的高音不等於尖叫；(A) 這一段沒有把尖叫分成不同種類。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT a finding by Arnal’s team?
options: Changes in volume make screams different from other sounds.
Only humans can produce sounds with great loudness variation.
Normal human speech sounds vary between 4 to 5 Hz in loudness.
Drastic volume variation in speech can effectively activate the amygdala.
items.explanation:
screams can switch very fast, varying between 30 and 150 Hz
but it is prevalent in artificial sounds.
題目問哪一個不是 Arnal 團隊的發現。(A) 第 1 段說尖叫的音量變化很快，這就是尖叫和其他聲音不同的地方，是發現；(C) 第 1 段說一般說話的音量變化在 4 到 5 赫茲之間，是發現；(D) 第 2 段說聽到尖叫以後，杏仁核亮了起來，是發現。(B) 和原文矛盾：第 3 段說人工的聲音也常常有粗糙度，鬧鐘、汽車喇叭和火災警報器的粗糙度都很高，可見不是只有人類發得出音量變化大的聲音，所以選 (B)。

items.stem: What does “it” in the third paragraph refer to?
items.explanation:
roughness isn’t heard when we speak naturally, regardless of the language we use, but it is prevalent in artificial sounds.
這一句用 but 連接兩個對比的部分：粗糙度（roughness）在自然說話時聽不到，但 it 在人工的聲音裡很普遍。前後兩部分講的是同一件事，聽得到或聽不到的是粗糙度，所以 it 指的是 roughness，答案是 (C)。(B) language 是離 it 最近的名詞，但「語言在人工的聲音裡很普遍」說不通；(A) the study 出現在前一句，研究不會在聲音裡。

items.stem: Which of the following devices may be improved with the researchers’ findings?
items.explanation:
One potential application for this research might be to add roughness to alarm sounds to make them more effective
The most aggravating alarm clocks, car horns, and fire alarms possess high degrees of roughness.
這一題答對率只有 40%。判斷步驟：[1] 第 4 段說這項研究可以用在警報聲（alarm sounds）上，加入粗糙度讓警報更有效；[2] 所以要找的是會發出警報聲的裝置；[3] 煙霧偵測器偵測到煙會發出警報，所以是 (A)。最多人選錯的是 (D)，這個選項照抄第 3 段的 fire，火災警報器會發出聲音，滅火器卻是用來滅火，不會發出警報；(B) 監視器錄的是影像；(C) 電蚊燈用來殺蟲，都不靠警報聲。

閱讀測驗.title: 狗狗認知測驗 Dognition（Dognition: Testing Dogs' Cognitive Traits）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Is your dog an Einstein or a Charmer? For US $60, a recently-founded company called Dognition will help you learn more about your dog’s cognitive traits. It offers an online test telling you about the brain behind the bark.

Dognition’s test measures a dog’s intellect in several aspects—from empathy to memory to reasoning skills. But don’t expect it to measure your pet’s IQ. Dr. Hare, one of the venture’s co-founders, says a dog’s intelligence can’t be described with a single number. Just as humans have a wide range of intelligences, so do dogs. The question is what type your dog relies on more.

After you plunk your money down, Dognition’s website will take you through a questionnaire about your dog: For example, how excited does your dog get around other dogs, or children? Do fireworks scare your pup? Then, Dognition guides you through tests that are as fun as playing fetch or hide-and-seek. At the end, you get a report of your dog’s cognitive profile.

Your dog could fall into one of nine categories: Ace, Stargazer, Maverick, Charmer, Socialite, Protodog, Einstein, Expert, or Renaissance Dog. That can give you something to brag about on Dognition’s Facebook page. It also can shed new light on why dogs do the things they do. For example, a Charmer is a dog that trusts you so much that it would prefer to solve problems using information you give it rather than information it can get with its own eyes.

Dognition helps people understand their dogs in ways that they have never been able to do. This new understanding can enrich the relationship between dogs and their owners.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
你的狗是 Einstein 型，還是 Charmer 型？只要 60 美元，一家新成立的公司 Dognition 就能幫你進一步了解狗狗的認知特質。這家公司提供線上測驗，告訴你狗狗吠叫的背後，那顆腦袋是怎麼運作的。

Dognition 的測驗從同理心、記憶力到推理能力，從好幾個面向衡量狗的智能。不過，別期待它會測出你寵物的智商。這家新創公司的共同創辦人之一 Hare 博士說，狗的智能沒辦法用單一數字描述。就像人類有各式各樣的智能，狗也一樣。問題在於你的狗比較依賴哪一種。

付錢之後，Dognition 的網站會帶你填一份關於狗狗的問卷，例如：狗狗在其他狗或小孩身邊會有多興奮？煙火會不會嚇到你的狗？接著，Dognition 會引導你帶狗做一些測驗，就像玩丟接球或捉迷藏一樣好玩。最後，你會拿到一份狗狗的認知特質報告。

你的狗會歸入九種類型之一：Ace、Stargazer、Maverick、Charmer、Socialite、Protodog、Einstein、Expert 或 Renaissance Dog。這可以讓你在 Dognition 的臉書粉絲專頁上炫耀一番，也能讓人從新的角度了解狗為什麼會做出那些行為。例如，Charmer 型的狗非常信任主人，解決問題時寧可依靠主人給的資訊，也不用自己親眼看到的資訊。

Dognition 幫助人們用前所未有的方式了解自己的狗。這種新的了解，能讓狗和主人之間的關係更加豐富。

items.stem: What is the third paragraph mainly about?
options: The theory behind the questionnaire used in the Dognition test.
The procedure for evaluating a dog’s intellect on Dognition.
The products one can get by paying a fee to Dognition.
The characteristics of the activities Dognition offers.
items.explanation:
After you plunk your money down, Dognition’s website will take you through a questionnaire about your dog:
Then, Dognition guides you through tests that are as fun as playing fetch or hide-and-seek.
At the end, you get a report of your dog’s cognitive profile.
第 3 段用 After、Then、At the end 標出先後：付錢之後先填問卷，接著帶狗做像遊戲一樣的測驗，最後拿到認知特質報告，講的是在 Dognition 評估狗狗智能的步驟，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 questionnaire，但這一段只舉了問卷問些什麼，沒有談問卷背後的理論；(C) 付費後拿到的報告只是最後一步；(D) 測驗像遊戲一樣好玩，只是對其中一個步驟的描述。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
options: Different dogs display strengths in different intelligences.
A dog’s cognitive profile is composed of nine cognitive skills.
The purpose of Dognition’s testing is to control a dog’s behavior.
A dog’s intelligence can be ranked based on the score of a Dognition’s test.
items.explanation:
Just as humans have a wide range of intelligences, so do dogs.
The question is what type your dog relies on more.
第 2 段說就像人類有各式各樣的智能，狗也一樣，問題在於你的狗比較依賴哪一種；不同的狗擅長的智能不同，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 nine，九種指的是狗的類型，不是認知特質由九種技能組成；(D) 原文說狗的智能沒辦法用單一數字描述，不能依分數排名；(C) 測驗的目的是了解狗，第 5 段說能讓狗和主人的關係更豐富，不是控制狗的行為。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word “venture” in the second paragraph?
items.explanation:
For US $60, a recently-founded company called Dognition will help you learn more about your dog’s cognitive traits.
Dr. Hare, one of the venture’s co-founders, says a dog’s intelligence can’t be described with a single number.
第 1 段說 Dognition 是一家新成立的公司（a recently-founded company），第 2 段說 Hare 博士是這個 venture 的共同創辦人（co-founders）。共同創辦的就是第 1 段那家新公司，venture 是換個字再說一次，所以是 (D) New business。(B) 冒險的嘗試是 venture 另一個常見的意思，但這裡和 co-founders 連用，指的是新創事業；(C) Dognition 收費 60 美元，不是非營利組織；(A) 創新的評量在文章找不到依據。

items.stem: According to the passage, what would a Charmer most likely do?
options: Stay away from people whenever possible.
Imitate how other dogs solve problems.
Rely on its owner to point out where a treat is.
Follow its own senses to get what it wants.
items.explanation:
For example, a Charmer is a dog that trusts you so much that it would prefer to solve problems using information you give it rather than information it can get with its own eyes.
第 4 段說 Charmer 型的狗非常信任主人，解決問題時寧可依靠主人給的資訊，也不用自己親眼看到的資訊；主人指出點心在哪裡，就是主人給的資訊，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 its own，原文說這種狗不用自己親眼看到的資訊，選項說牠依靠自己的感官，正好相反；(B) 照抄 solve problems，但牠依靠的是主人，不是模仿其他狗；(A) 原文說牠非常信任主人，不會遠離人。

閱讀測驗.title: 巴西戰舞卡波耶拉（Capoeira）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Capoeira is a martial art that combines elements of fight, acrobatics, drumming, singing, dance, and rituals. It involves a variety of techniques that make use of the hands, feet, legs, arms, and head. Although Capoeira appears dancelike, many of its basic techniques are similar to those in other martial arts.

Capoeira was created nearly 500 years ago in Brazil by African slaves. It is believed that the martial art was connected with tribal fighting in Africa, in which people fought body to body, without weapons, in order to acquire a bride or desired woman. In the sixteenth century, when the Africans were taken from their homes to Brazil against their will and kept in slavery, Capoeira began to take form among the community of slaves for self-defense. But it soon became a strong weapon in the life-or-death struggle against their oppressors. When the slave owners realized the power of Capoeira, they began to punish those who practiced it. Capoeiristas learned to camouflage the forbidden fights with singing, clapping, and dancing as though it were simply entertainment.

At first, Capoeira was considered illegal in Brazil. However, a man known as Mestre Bimba devoted a great deal of time and effort to convincing the Brazilian authorities that Capoeira has great cultural value and should become an official fighting style. He succeeded in his endeavor and transformed the martial art into Brazil’s national sport. He and Mestre Pastinha were the first to open schools, and the Capoeira tree grew, spreading its branches across the world. Nowadays, it is performed in movies and music clips. Capoeira is also believed to have influenced several dancing styles like breaking and hip-hop.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
卡波耶拉是一種武術，結合了格鬥、雜技、擊鼓、歌唱、舞蹈和儀式等元素，用到的技巧五花八門，會運用手、腳、腿、手臂和頭部。卡波耶拉雖然看起來像舞蹈，許多基本技巧卻和其他武術相似。

卡波耶拉是將近五百年前，巴西的非洲奴隸創造出來的。一般認為這種武術和非洲的部落格鬥有關，人們赤手空拳、徒手搏鬥，為的是娶到新娘或心儀的女子。十六世紀，非洲人遭到強行帶離家鄉，送到巴西當奴隸，卡波耶拉就在奴隸群體中開始成形，用來自衛。但是它很快就成了奴隸對抗壓迫者、攸關生死的強大武器。奴隸主發現卡波耶拉的威力後，開始懲罰練習的人。練卡波耶拉的人於是學會用歌唱、拍手和舞蹈掩飾這些禁止的打鬥，讓它看起來只是娛樂。

一開始，卡波耶拉在巴西是違法的。不過，一位叫 Mestre Bimba 的人花了大量時間和心力，說服巴西政府卡波耶拉有很高的文化價值，應該成為正式的格鬥技。他成功了，把這門武術變成巴西的國技。他和 Mestre Pastinha 最早開設學校，卡波耶拉這棵樹從此開枝散葉，傳遍全世界。現在，電影和音樂影片裡都看得到卡波耶拉。一般也認為卡波耶拉影響了霹靂舞、嘻哈舞等好幾種舞蹈風格。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
items.explanation: 第 1 段介紹卡波耶拉是什麼；第 2 段講它將近五百年前由巴西的非洲奴隸創造，從自衛變成反抗的武器；第 3 段講它從違法到成為巴西國技，再傳遍世界。全文依時間講卡波耶拉的發展，所以是 (A)。(D) 技巧只在第 1 段介紹，(B) 文化價值和 (C) 對舞蹈風格的影響只在第 3 段提到，都過於狹隘。

items.stem: Which of the following will probably NOT be found in the performance of Capoeira?
items.explanation:
Capoeira is a martial art that combines elements of fight, acrobatics, drumming, singing, dance, and rituals.
It involves a variety of techniques that make use of the hands, feet, legs, arms, and head.
in which people fought body to body, without weapons, in order to acquire a bride or desired woman.
第 1 段說卡波耶拉結合擊鼓和歌唱（drumming, singing），是 (A)；技巧會用到手、腳、腿（hands, feet, legs），是 (B) 用腿掃和 (D) 用手打。文章沒有提到刀劍，第 2 段反而說它源自赤手空拳、不用武器的部落格鬥，所以 (C) 用劍刺最不可能出現。

items.stem: What is the author’s attitude toward Capoeira as a sport?
items.explanation: 全文介紹卡波耶拉的起源、演變和現況，只陳述事實，沒有表達作者自己的好惡；說到起源和影響，還用 It is believed、is also believed to 這類保留的說法。作者的態度是客觀的，所以是 (B)。(A) 欣賞容易誤選：第 3 段說卡波耶拉有很高的文化價值，但那是 Mestre Bimba 說服政府的理由，不是作者的評價；(C) 懷疑和 (D) 嚴厲，文章都找不到依據。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about Capoeira?
options: It was greatly influenced by modern dancing styles.
It was initially created as a type of dance and ritual.
It was mainly performed to protect a bride or desired woman.
It was officially recognized in Brazil through the effort of Mestre Bimba.
items.explanation:
However, a man known as Mestre Bimba devoted a great deal of time and effort to convincing the Brazilian authorities that Capoeira has great cultural value and should become an official fighting style.
He succeeded in his endeavor and transformed the martial art into Brazil’s national sport.
第 3 段說 Mestre Bimba 花了大量時間和心力說服巴西政府，最後成功讓卡波耶拉成為巴西國技，選項把 convincing the Brazilian authorities 換成 officially recognized in Brazil。(A) 照抄 dancing styles，原文說的是卡波耶拉影響了霹靂舞、嘻哈舞，選項把影響的方向說反了；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 bride or desired woman，那是非洲部落格鬥的目的，而且是為了娶到新娘，不是保護新娘；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 ritual，但第 2 段說卡波耶拉一開始是奴隸用來自衛的武術，歌舞是後來用來掩飾的。

閱讀測驗.title: 畫家溫斯洛·霍默（Winslow Homer）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Winslow Homer (1836-1910) is regarded by many as the greatest American painter of the nineteenth century. Born and raised in Boston, he began his career at age eighteen in his hometown, working as an apprentice at a printing company. Skilled at drawing, he soon made a name for himself making illustrations for novels, sheet music, magazines, and children’s books.

He then moved to New York City, where he worked as a freelance illustrator with Harper’s Weekly, a popular magazine of the time, and began painting. Homer was assigned to cover the inauguration of President Lincoln and, later, the Civil War. His pictures of the Union troops won international recognition. Homer moved to England and, after a two-year stay, returned to America. He settled permanently in Maine in 1883.

From the late 1850s until his death in 1910, Winslow Homer produced a body of work distinguished by its thoughtful expression and its independence from artistic conventions. A man of multiple talents, Homer excelled equally in the arts of illustration, oil painting, and watercolor. Many of his works—depictions of children at play and in school, farm girls attending to their work, hunters and their prey—have become classic images of nineteenth-century American life. Others speak to more universal themes such as the primal relationship of humans to nature.

This two-week exhibition highlights a wide and representative range of Homer’s art. It shows his extraordinary career from the battlefields, farmland, and coastal villages of America, to the North Sea fishing village of Cullercoats, the rocky coast of Maine, the Adirondacks, and the Caribbean. The exhibition offers viewers an opportunity to experience and appreciate the breadth of his remarkable artistic achievement.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
許多人認為溫斯洛·霍默（1836–1910）是 19 世紀最偉大的美國畫家。他在波士頓出生長大，十八歲在家鄉展開職業生涯，在一家印刷公司當學徒。他擅長繪畫，很快就以替小說、樂譜、雜誌和兒童書繪製插畫而出名。

後來他搬到紐約市，替當時很受歡迎的雜誌 Harper’s Weekly 擔任自由插畫家，也開始作畫。霍默受派報導林肯總統的就職典禮，後來又報導南北戰爭。他描繪北軍的畫作贏得國際肯定。霍默後來搬到英國，住了兩年後回到美國，1883 年在緬因州定居。

從 1850 年代後期到 1910 年去世，霍默創作了大量作品，特色是表達深刻，而且不受藝術傳統束縛。霍默多才多藝，插畫、油畫和水彩都同樣出色。他的許多作品，像是描繪孩子遊戲和上學、農家女孩忙著做事、獵人和獵物的畫，都已經成為 19 世紀美國生活的經典畫面。其他作品則觸及更普遍的主題，例如人和大自然之間最原始的關係。

這次為期兩週的展覽，展出霍默藝術作品中範圍廣泛又具代表性的一批。展覽呈現他非凡的創作生涯，從美國的戰場、農田和海邊村落，到北海的漁村卡勒科茨、緬因州的岩岸、阿第倫達克山脈和加勒比海。觀眾可以藉這次展覽，體會並欣賞他卓越藝術成就的廣度。

items.stem: Where does this passage most likely appear?
options: On an ad featuring contemporary arts.
On a website of an art gallery.
In a booklet on American-born British artists.
In an encyclopedia on the art of printing.
items.explanation: 第 4 段說「這次為期兩週的展覽」呈現霍默的創作生涯，讓觀眾有機會欣賞他的作品；前三段介紹畫家的生平和作品特色，正是美術館網站介紹展覽的寫法，所以是 (B)。(D) 印刷只在第 1 段提到霍默當過印刷公司的學徒，過於狹隘；(A) 霍默是 19 世紀的畫家，不是當代藝術，(C) 霍默是美國畫家，只在英國住過兩年，都偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about Homer’s career?
options: He achieved international fame with his vivid paintings of England.
He is considered the greatest illustrator in the history of American art.
He is better known for his watercolors than his illustrations and oil paintings.
He first established his reputation as an illustrator in his hometown of Boston.
items.explanation:
Born and raised in Boston, he began his career at age eighteen in his hometown, working as an apprentice at a printing company.
Skilled at drawing, he soon made a name for himself making illustrations for novels, sheet music, magazines, and children’s books.
第 1 段說霍默在家鄉波士頓的印刷公司當學徒，很快就以繪製插畫出名（made a name for himself），選項換成 established his reputation as an illustrator。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 England，但讓他贏得國際肯定的是描繪北軍的畫作，不是描繪英國的畫；(B) 照抄 greatest，原文說他是最偉大的畫家（painter），不是最偉大的插畫家；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 watercolor，原文說他的插畫、油畫和水彩都同樣出色（excelled equally），沒說水彩比較有名。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following best characterizes Homer’s art?
options: His pictures vividly portrayed the life of nineteenth-century Americans.
His art thoughtfully expressed the voices of people suffering from war.
His style faithfully conformed to the artistic traditions of his time.
His paintings constantly reflected his desire to escape from society.
items.explanation:
Many of his works—depictions of children at play and in school, farm girls attending to their work, hunters and their prey—have become classic images of nineteenth-century American life.
第 3 段說霍默的許多作品，像是孩子遊戲和上學、農家女孩工作、獵人和獵物，都成了 19 世紀美國生活的經典畫面，選項把 classic images of nineteenth-century American life 換成 vividly portrayed the life of nineteenth-century Americans。(B) 照抄 thoughtful，原文說他的作品表達深刻，沒說是替受戰爭之苦的人發聲；(C) 照抄 artistic，原文說他不受藝術傳統束縛（independence from artistic conventions），選項說他遵循傳統，方向正好相反；(D) 文章沒說他想逃離社會。

items.stem: What does “Others” in the third paragraph refer to?
items.explanation:
Many of his works
Others speak to more universal themes such as the primal relationship of humans to nature.
第 3 段先說他的許多作品（Many of his works）成了美國生活的經典畫面，下一句接著說 Others 觸及更普遍的主題。Many of his works…Others… 前後對照，Others 是他的其他作品，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 themes，主題是這些作品觸及的內容，不是 Others 本身；(D) 照抄 images，經典畫面是前一句對那批作品的評價；(A) 這一段沒有提到其他藝術家。

閱讀測驗.title: 茶在英國的流行（How Tea Became Popular in Britain）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Tea, the most typical English drink, became established in Britain because of the influence of a foreign princess, Catherine of Braganza, the queen of Charles II. A lover of tea since her childhood in Portugal, she brought tea-drinking to the English royal court and set a trend for the beverage in the seventeenth century. The fashion soon spread beyond the circle of the nobility to the middle classes, and tea became a popular drink at the London coffee houses where people met to do business and discuss events of the day. Many employers served a cup of tea to their workers in the middle of the morning, thus inventing a lasting British institution, the “tea break.” However, drinking tea in social settings outside the workplace was beyond the means of the majority of British people. It came with a high price tag and tea was taxed as well.

Around 1800, the seventh Duchess of Bedford, Anne Maria, began the popular practice of “afternoon tea,” a ceremony taking place at about four o’clock. Until then, people did not usually eat or drink anything between lunch and dinner. At approximately the same time, the Earl of Sandwich popularized a new way of eating bread—in thin slices, with something (e.g., jam or cucumbers) between them. Before long, a small meal at the end of the afternoon, involving tea and sandwiches, had become part of the British way of life.

As tea became much cheaper during the nineteenth century, its popularity spread right through all corners of the British society. Thus, tea became Britain’s favorite drink. In working-class households, it was served with the main meal of the day, eaten when workers returned home after a day’s labor. This meal has become known as “high tea.”

Today, tea can be drunk at any time of the day, and accounts for over two-fifths of all beverages consumed in Britain—with the exception of water.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
茶是最典型的英國飲料，而茶能在英國流行起來，要歸功於一位外國公主，也就是查理二世的王后，布拉干薩的凱薩琳。凱薩琳在葡萄牙度過童年時就愛喝茶，她把飲茶的習慣帶進英國宮廷，在十七世紀帶動了喝茶的風氣。這股風氣很快就從貴族圈擴散到中產階級，茶也成了倫敦咖啡館裡受歡迎的飲料，人們在那裡碰面談生意、討論時事。許多雇主在上午工作到一半時，會請員工喝一杯茶，因而開創了一項延續至今的英國傳統：「喝茶休息時間」（tea break）。不過，大部分英國人負擔不起在工作場所以外的社交場合喝茶。茶的價格很高，還要課稅。

1800 年左右，第七代貝德福公爵夫人 Anne Maria 開始了大受歡迎的「下午茶」習慣，這是一種大約在下午四點舉行的儀式。在那之前，人們在午餐和晚餐之間通常不吃也不喝任何東西。差不多在同一個時候，三明治伯爵推廣了一種吃麵包的新方式：把麵包切成薄片，中間夾東西（例如果醬或小黃瓜）。不久之後，在下午快結束時吃一頓有茶有三明治的小餐點，就成了英國人生活的一部分。

十九世紀茶變得便宜許多，喝茶的風氣也傳遍英國社會的每個角落。因此，茶成了英國人最喜愛的飲料。在勞工家庭裡，茶搭配的是一天中最主要的那一餐，也就是工人做完一天的工作、回家後吃的那一餐。這一餐後來就叫做「high tea」。

現在，任何時間都可以喝茶；除了水以外，茶占英國人所喝飲料的五分之二以上。

items.stem: How is this passage organized?
items.explanation: 全文依時間先後排列：第 1 段是十七世紀凱薩琳王后帶動喝茶的風氣，第 2 段是 1800 年左右出現下午茶，第 3 段是十九世紀茶價下降、普及各階層，第 4 段是現在。seventeenth century、Around 1800、nineteenth century、Today 這些時間標記串起整篇，所以是 (C)。(A) 因果、(B) 重要性、(D) 比較對照都不是全文的組織方式。

items.stem: What does the phrase “a lasting British institution” in the first paragraph mean?
options: A long-standing tradition in the UK.
The last tea company in London.
items.explanation:
Many employers served a cup of tea to their workers in the middle of the morning, thus inventing a lasting British institution, the “tea break.”
第 1 段說許多雇主在上午工作到一半時請員工喝茶，因而開創了 a lasting British institution，也就是 tea break。上午喝茶休息是一種沿用下來的習慣做法：lasting 是持久的，institution 在這裡指制度、慣例，合起來就是 (B) 英國由來已久的傳統。(A) 組織和 (D) 企業，用的是 institution 另一個常見的意思「機構」；(C) 把 lasting 看成 last（最後的），文章也沒有談茶葉公司。

items.stem: According to the passage, why was tea NOT a common drink of everyday life in the seventeenth century?
options: It was only served at coffee houses in London.
It was taxed as an alcoholic drink.
It was forbidden outside of the business setting.
It was too expensive for most people.
items.explanation:
However, drinking tea in social settings outside the workplace was beyond the means of the majority of British people.
It came with a high price tag and tea was taxed as well.
第 1 段說在工作場所以外的社交場合喝茶，大部分英國人負擔不起（beyond the means of the majority），因為茶的價格很高，還要課稅，選項換成 too expensive for most people。(A) 照抄 coffee houses，咖啡館是茶受歡迎的地方之一，原文沒說只在那裡供應；(B) 照抄 taxed，原文只說茶要課稅，沒說是當作酒類課稅；(C) 照抄 business，原文說人們在咖啡館談生意，沒說商業場合以外禁止喝茶。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true?
options: High tea was served later in the day than afternoon tea in the nineteenth century.
British people had tea breaks twice a day in the eighteenth century.
Princess Catherine brought tea to England after visiting Portugal.
The Earl of Sandwich started the afternoon tea ceremony.
items.explanation:
Around 1800, the seventh Duchess of Bedford, Anne Maria, began the popular practice of “afternoon tea,” a ceremony taking place at about four o’clock.
In working-class households, it was served with the main meal of the day, eaten when workers returned home after a day’s labor.
第 2 段說下午茶大約在下午四點；第 3 段說勞工家庭的 high tea 搭配一天中最主要的那一餐，是工人做完一天的工作、回家後才吃的，可以推知 high tea 比下午茶晚，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 1 段的 tea break，原文說雇主在上午工作到一半時請員工喝茶，沒說一天兩次；(C) 照抄 Portugal，凱薩琳是在葡萄牙度過童年，不是去葡萄牙訪問之後才把茶帶到英國；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 Earl of Sandwich，三明治伯爵推廣的是三明治，開始下午茶習慣的是貝德福公爵夫人。

閱讀測驗.title: 札哈·哈蒂的藝術生涯與建築理念（Zaha Hadid's Artistic Career and Architectural Philosophy）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Often named as the most prominent contemporary female architect, Zaha Hadid, an Iraqi-born British woman, is significant for her intellectual toughness and her refusal to compromise on her artistic ideas. For many years, her designs filled the pages of architecture journals but were dismissed as impractical or too radical. Also, being female in a male-dominated field didn’t help her succeed.

Despite these setbacks, her star began to rise when her design for Cincinnati’s new Center for Contemporary Art was selected and built, earning her worldwide acclaim. The New York Times described the building as “the most important new building in America since the Cold War.” Once her talent was recognized, commissions started coming in to design a variety of projects, including public transportation, libraries, and opera houses. In 2004, Hadid became the first woman to win the prestigious Pritzker Prize. She also won the Stirling Prize in 2010 and 2011.

Hadid’s interest in architecture had roots in a trip her family took to the ancient Sumer region in southern Iraq, the site of one of the world’s oldest civilizations, when she was a teenager. She recalled: “The beauty of the landscape—where sand, water, reeds, birds, buildings, and people all somehow flowed together—has never left me. I’m trying to discover—invent, I suppose—an architecture, and forms of urban planning, that do something of the same thing in a contemporary way.”

Nature’s forms appear as a recurrent source of inspiration for Hadid’s architecture. Her designs are daring and visionary experiments with space and with the relationships of buildings to their urban surroundings. She consistently pushes the boundaries of architecture and urban design in the pursuit of a visionary aesthetic that expresses her ideals.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
札哈·哈蒂是在伊拉克出生的英國女性，常有人稱她是當代最傑出的女性建築師。她之所以重要，是因為她思想強韌，又絕不在藝術理念上妥協。多年來，她的設計常常登上建築期刊，卻也常常讓人覺得不切實際、太過激進而不予理會。此外，在男性主導的領域裡身為女性，對她的成功也沒有幫助。

儘管遇到這些挫折，她設計的辛辛那提新當代藝術中心獲選並且落成，讓她贏得全世界的讚譽，她從此開始走紅。《紐約時報》說這棟建築是「冷戰以來美國最重要的新建築」。她的才華一旦獲得肯定，各式各樣的設計委託就接踵而來，包括大眾運輸、圖書館和歌劇院。2004 年，哈蒂成為第一位獲得聲望崇高的普立茲克獎的女性。她也在 2010 年和 2011 年獲得斯特林獎。

哈蒂對建築的興趣，源自她青少年時期全家到伊拉克南部古蘇美地區的一趟旅行，那裡是世界上最古老的文明之一的所在地。她回憶說：「那裡的風景很美，沙、水、蘆葉、鳥、建築和人，都以某種方式融為一體，這片風景一直留在我心裡。我想找出──或者說創造出──一種建築和都市規劃的形式，用當代的方式做到同樣的事。」

大自然的形態一再成為哈蒂建築的靈感來源。她的設計是大膽而有遠見的實驗，探索空間，也探索建築和周圍城市環境的關係。她不斷突破建築和都市設計的界限，追求一種有遠見、能表達她理想的美學。

items.stem: According to the passage, what is a major factor in Hadid’s success?
items.explanation:
Once her talent was recognized, commissions started coming in
in the pursuit of a visionary aesthetic that expresses her ideals.
第 2 段說她的才華（talent）一旦獲得肯定，各類設計委託就接踵而來；第 4 段說她不斷突破建築的界限，追求有遠見（visionary）的美學。才華和遠見是她成功的主要原因，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 family，那一段說的是全家旅行讓她對建築產生興趣，原文沒有說家人支持她；(B) 第 1 段只說她在伊拉克出生，沒有說出身幫助她成功；(C) 第 1 段反而說身為女性對她的成功沒有幫助，教育背景原文也沒有提到。

items.stem: What does the author mean by “…her star began to rise…” in the second paragraph?
options: She started to make a fortune.
Her ideas started to take shape.
items.explanation:
earning her worldwide acclaim.
Once her talent was recognized
rising star 是人氣或地位快速上升的人，her star began to rise 就是她開始走紅、越來越有名。後面接著說她的設計獲選落成，贏得全世界的讚譽（worldwide acclaim），下一句又說她的才華獲得肯定（was recognized），所以是 (B)。(A) 原文沒有談到她賺了多少錢；(C) 照抄 design，原文說設計獲選並落成，沒有說成為經典；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 ideas，她的理念早就很明確，問題是一直沒有人接受。

items.stem: What is the third paragraph mainly about?
options: The cultural background of Hadid’s family.
The beautiful landscape of Hadid’s hometown.
A vivid recollection of Hadid’s life as a teenager.
A fundamental source of Hadid’s architectural philosophy.
items.explanation:
Hadid’s interest in architecture had roots in a trip her family took to the ancient Sumer region in southern Iraq
an architecture, and forms of urban planning, that do something of the same thing in a contemporary way.
第 3 段第一句說哈蒂對建築的興趣源自（had roots in）一趟古蘇美地區的旅行，接著引她自己的話：那裡的人和自然融為一體，她想用當代的方式，創造出有同樣效果的建築和都市規劃。這一段講的是她建築理念的根本來源，所以是 (D)。這一段的三個錯誤選項都照抄段落裡的字：(A) 照抄 family，旅行是全家一起去的，但這一段沒有談家族的文化背景；(B) 照抄 landscape，風景是在古蘇美地區，不是她的家鄉；(C) 照抄 teenager，旅行發生在她青少年時期，但這一段沒有描述她青少年時期的生活，重點是那趟旅行對她建築理念的影響。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about Hadid’s career in architecture?
options: She built the first Center for Contemporary Art in New York.
Her architecture projects mainly involve museums in urban areas.
Her works can be characterized as boldly contemporary and innovative.
Her early designs were often rejected because of her political background.
items.explanation:
Her designs are daring and visionary experiments
She consistently pushes the boundaries of architecture and urban design
第 4 段說她的設計大膽（daring）而有遠見，她不斷突破建築和都市設計的界限，選項換成 boldly contemporary and innovative，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 Center for Contemporary Art，這座當代藝術中心在辛辛那提，New York 只出現在《紐約時報》的報名；(B) 照抄第 4 段的 urban，第 2 段說她設計大眾運輸、圖書館、歌劇院等各類建築，不只是博物館；(D) 第 1 段說她早期的設計不受重視，原因是太激進，加上身為女性，原文沒有提到政治背景。

閱讀測驗.title: 迷你免費圖書館的創立與影響（The Founding and Impact of Little Free Library）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Todd Bol, a retired businessman, could never have expected that a wooden container he built on his deck one day in 2009 would have the global impact it does today.

Bol built a dollhouse-size structure that looked like a schoolhouse on a post, and he put it on his lawn as a free community library to commemorate his mother, who was a book lover and school teacher. Bol’s prototype gave birth to Little Free Library (LFL), a nonprofit organization that seeks to place small, accessible book exchange boxes in neighborhoods around the world. The concept is simple: Neighbors are invited to share a book, leave a book, or both. Today, there are over 50,000 of these libraries registered in 70 countries.

Almost everyone can register with LFL and start a library as long as the person keeps it in good shape and makes sure that book materials are appropriate for his/her neighborhood. Library owners can create their own library boxes; therefore, the libraries are usually unique in appearance, and there seems to be no limit to the possibilities. One library in California was built out of a used wine crate; another in Texas had tiny stairs and bright colored walls. Once registered, libraries are assigned a number at LFL’s website. The LFL Index lists the locations of all libraries with GPS coordinates and other information. Owners receive a sign that reads “Little Free Library.”

People say they have been more inclined to pick up a book when walking by a Little Free Library, out of curiosity and because it’s convenient. Some sidewalk librarians say they have met more neighbors since having a little library in their front yard. Bol is also most proud of the way Little Free Library is bringing communities together. “It’s started a neighborhood exchange. It gets people talking and more comfortable with their neighbors,” he says. “This leads to them helping each other.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
Todd Bol 是一位退休的商人。2009 年的某一天，他在自家露台上做了一個木箱，他絕對想不到，這個木箱今天會有全球性的影響。

Bol 做了一個玩具屋大小、立在柱子上、看起來像一間校舍的小箱子，放在草坪上當作免費的社區圖書館，用來紀念他的母親。他的母親很愛書，也是一位學校老師。Bol 做的這個原型，催生了「小小免費圖書館」（Little Free Library，LFL）。這是一個非營利組織，目標是在世界各地的社區設置容易取用的小型換書箱。概念很簡單：歡迎鄰居拿一本書、放一本書，或是兩樣都做。如今，70 個國家登記的這種圖書館已經超過五萬座。

幾乎每個人都可以向 LFL 登記，開設一座圖書館，只要這個人把圖書館維護好，並且確保書籍內容適合他的社區。圖書館的主人可以自己做書箱，所以每座圖書館的外觀通常都不一樣，似乎有無限的可能。加州有一座圖書館是用舊酒箱做的，德州有一座有小小的樓梯和色彩鮮豔的牆面。登記以後，每座圖書館會在 LFL 的網站上分到一個編號。LFL 的索引列出所有圖書館的位置，附上 GPS 座標和其他資料。主人會收到一塊寫著「Little Free Library」的牌子。

人們說，經過小小免費圖書館的時候，因為好奇，也因為方便，他們比較會拿起一本書來看。有些在人行道旁設圖書館的主人說，自從前院有了一座小圖書館，他們認識了更多鄰居。Bol 最自豪的，也是小小免費圖書館把社區的人凝聚在一起。他說：「這開啟了鄰里之間的交流，讓大家開始交談，和鄰居相處得更自在。」他又說：「這會讓他們互相幫忙。」

items.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT mentioned about Todd Bol?
options: His mother used to be a school teacher.
He was engaged in trade and commerce.
He provided a great service to his neighborhood.
He built a schoolhouse to pay tribute to his mother.
items.explanation:
Bol built a dollhouse-size structure that looked like a schoolhouse on a post
Todd Bol, a retired businessman
這一題答對率只有 53%，要逐一核對每個選項。(A) 第 2 段說他的母親是學校老師，有提到；(B) 第 1 段說他是退休的商人（a retired businessman），從商就是 engaged in trade and commerce，有提到；(C) 他在草坪上設免費的社區圖書館，第 4 段又說這讓鄰居互相熟悉、互相幫忙，有提到。(D) 是陷阱：第 2 段說他做的是一個看起來像（looked like）校舍的小箱子，大小和玩具屋差不多，並不是真的蓋了一間校舍，所以選 (D)。

items.stem: What does “prototype” refer to in the second paragraph?
items.explanation:
Bol’s prototype gave birth to Little Free Library (LFL)
seeks to place small, accessible book exchange boxes in neighborhoods around the world.
這一題答對率只有 42%。prototype 是「原型」，也就是第一個做出來、後來照著做的樣本。判斷步驟：[1] Bol’s prototype 指的是前一句 Bol 做的那個小箱子；[2] 這個原型催生了 LFL，LFL 做的事是在世界各地設置小型換書箱（book exchange boxes）；[3] 所以原型就是第一個換書箱，答案是 (B)。最多人選錯的是 (C)：原文說的是玩具屋大小（dollhouse-size）、看起來像校舍的小箱子，dollhouse 只是在形容大小，那個箱子不是玩具屋。(D) 照抄 nonprofit organization，非營利組織是原型催生出來的，不是原型本身；(A) 照抄 community，原文說的是免費的社區圖書館，不是社區中心。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about the operation of a Little Free Library?
options: The library can come in any shape and color.
There is no limit to the selection of its materials.
The owner must first be assigned a number from the LFL website.
The librarian is in charge of checking the books in and out of the library.
items.explanation:
the libraries are usually unique in appearance, and there seems to be no limit to the possibilities.
這一題答對率只有 52%，三個錯誤選項都把第 3 段的字搬到不對的地方。第 3 段說主人可以自己做書箱，所以每座圖書館外觀都不一樣，似乎有無限的可能（no limit to the possibilities），後面還舉了舊酒箱、小樓梯和鮮豔牆面的例子，選項換成可以是任何形狀和顏色，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 no limit，原文說的是外觀沒有限制；書籍內容反而有限制，主人要確保內容適合社區。(C) 照抄 assigned a number，原文說登記以後（Once registered）才會分到編號，選項說主人要先拿到編號，順序弄反了。(D) 照抄第 4 段的 librarian，換書箱是讓鄰居自己拿書、放書，原文沒有說主人要負責借還書。

items.stem: What is a contribution of Little Free Library?
options: The LFL Index can improve GPS functions.
It promotes reading and literacy in a simple way.
It helps to strengthen library associations around the world.
Its location satisfies people’s curiosity about their neighbors.
items.explanation:
The concept is simple
People say they have been more inclined to pick up a book when walking by a Little Free Library, out of curiosity and because it’s convenient.
這一題答對率只有 50%，要把兩段合起來推。第 2 段說 LFL 的概念很簡單（The concept is simple）：鄰居拿一本書、放一本書就好；第 4 段說人們經過時，因為好奇又方便，比較會拿起書來看。方法簡單，又讓更多人拿起書來讀，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄第 4 段的 curiosity，好奇的對象是書箱裡的書，不是鄰居的事；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 GPS，GPS 座標是用來標出圖書館的位置，不是改善 GPS 功能；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 around the world，LFL 在世界各地設置換書箱，原文沒有提到圖書館協會。

閱讀測驗.title: 鑑識語言學的應用與案例（The Application and Cases of Forensic Linguistics）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The term “forensic linguistics,” in its broadest sense, covers all areas of study where language and law intersect. A famous example of its application is the case of Chris Coleman, who was suspected of killing his family in 2009. Robert Leonard, the head of the forensic linguistics program at Hofstra University, presented some important linguistic evidence in the trial against Coleman. Relying heavily on word choice and spelling, Leonard suggested that the same person had written the threatening e-mails and sprayed the graffiti, and that those samples bore similarities to Coleman’s writing style. Coleman was later found guilty of the murder.

Robert Leonard was not the first one who resorted to linguistic evidence in criminal investigation. The field of forensic linguistics was brought to prominence by his colleague James Fitzgerald in 1996 with his work in the case of the Unabomber, who had sent a series of letter bombs to college professors over several years, causing serious casualties. Working for the FBI, Fitzgerald urged the publication of the Unabomber’s letter—a lengthy declaration of the criminal’s philosophy.

After the letter was published, many people called the FBI to say they recognized the writing style. By analyzing sentence structure, word choice, and other linguistic patterns, Fitzgerald narrowed down the range of possible authors and finally linked the letter to the writings of Ted Kaczynski, a solitary former mathematician. For instance, Kaczynski tended to use extensive parallel phrases, which were frequently found in the bomber’s letter. Both Kaczynski and the bomber also showed a preference for dozens of unusual words, such as “chimerical” and “anomic.” The bomber’s use of the terms “broad” for women and “negro” for African Americans also enabled Fitzgerald to roughly calculate the suspect’s age. The linguistic evidence was strong enough for the judge to search Kaczynski’s isolated cabin in Montana; what was found there put him in prison for life.

On some level, finding hidden meanings from linguistic evidence is what we all do intuitively in our daily language interaction. This is exactly the same work forensic professionals do. As one forensic-linguistics firm, Testipro, puts it in its online promotional ad, the field can be regarded as “the basis of the entire legal system.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
「鑑識語言學」這個名詞，最廣義的說法，涵蓋所有語言和法律交會的研究領域。它應用的一個著名例子，是 Chris Coleman 的案子。Coleman 在 2009 年涉嫌殺害家人。霍夫斯特拉大學鑑識語言學課程的主任 Robert Leonard，在審判 Coleman 的時候提出了一些重要的語言證據。Leonard 主要根據用字和拼字，指出寫恐嚇電子郵件和噴塗鴉的是同一個人，而且這些樣本和 Coleman 的寫作風格有相似之處。法院後來判 Coleman 謀殺罪成立。

Robert Leonard 並不是第一個在刑事調查中借助語言證據的人。讓鑑識語言學這個領域受到重視的，是他的同事 James Fitzgerald。1996 年，Fitzgerald 參與偵辦大學炸彈客的案子。大學炸彈客好幾年間陸續寄出郵包炸彈給大學教授，造成嚴重的死傷。Fitzgerald 當時替聯邦調查局（FBI）工作，他力主公開大學炸彈客的一封信，那是一篇很長的文章，宣揚這名罪犯的理念。

信公開以後，許多人打電話給 FBI，說他們認得這種寫作風格。Fitzgerald 分析句子結構、用字和其他語言模式，縮小了可能作者的範圍，最後把這封信和 Ted Kaczynski 的文章連結起來。Kaczynski 是一位獨來獨往的前數學家。舉例來說，Kaczynski 習慣大量使用平行的片語，炸彈客的信裡也常常出現這種片語。Kaczynski 和炸彈客也都偏好幾十個不常見的字，例如 chimerical（空想的）和 anomic（失序的）。炸彈客用 broad 稱呼女性、用 negro 稱呼非裔美國人，這也讓 Fitzgerald 能大致推算出嫌犯的年齡。語言證據強到讓法官同意搜索 Kaczynski 在蒙大拿州偏僻的小屋；在那裡找到的東西，讓他終身監禁。

從某個層面來說，從語言證據裡找出隱藏的意思，是我們每個人在日常的語言互動中憑直覺都在做的事。這正是鑑識專業人員所做的工作。就像一家鑑識語言學公司 Testipro 在網路宣傳廣告上說的，這個領域可以說是「整個法律體系的基礎」。

items.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Robert Leonard has provided linguistic evidence in court cases.
The FBI relies mainly on language experts to solve its crime cases.
Studying texts can provide critical evidence in criminal investigations.
Finding hidden meanings in language use is important for daily interactions.
items.explanation: 這一題答對率只有 44%，判斷的方法是看每個選項涵蓋幾段。第 1 段用 Coleman 的案子說明鑑識語言學的應用；第 2、3 段用大學炸彈客的案子，說明分析句子結構、用字等語言模式，怎麼幫忙找出嫌犯；第 4 段說找出語言裡隱藏的意思，是鑑識專業人員的工作。全文講的是分析文字能在刑事調查中提供關鍵證據，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 Robert Leonard，只講第 1 段的案子，過於狹隘；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 hidden meanings，日常互動只是第 4 段拿來比較的說法，過於狹隘；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 FBI，原文只說 Fitzgerald 替 FBI 工作，沒有說 FBI 辦案主要靠語言專家，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about the Unabomber?
options: He didn’t like to be called negro.
He was good at analyzing the use of language.
He declared his philosophy in a written statement.
He was a professor of mathematics living on Hofstra campus.
items.explanation:
a lengthy declaration of the criminal’s philosophy.
第 2 段說大學炸彈客的信是一篇很長的文章，宣揚（declaration）這名罪犯的理念（philosophy），選項換成他用一份書面聲明宣揚自己的理念，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 negro，是炸彈客自己用這個字稱呼非裔美國人，原文沒有說他不喜歡別人這樣叫他；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 analyzing，分析語言的是 Fitzgerald，不是炸彈客；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 Hofstra，霍夫斯特拉大學是 Leonard 任教的地方，Kaczynski 是前數學家，住在蒙大拿州偏僻的小屋。

items.stem: What type of language feature is NOT mentioned in the passage?
items.explanation:
Relying heavily on word choice and spelling
By analyzing sentence structure, word choice, and other linguistic patterns
第 1 段說 Leonard 根據用字（word choice）和拼字（spelling），是 (C) 和 (B)；第 3 段說 Fitzgerald 分析句子結構（sentence structure）和用字，句子結構屬於 (D) 文法的模式，平行的片語也是。全文分析的都是寫成文字的電子郵件、塗鴉和信，沒有提到聲音的模式，所以選 (A)。

items.stem: What can be inferred from the passage?
options: Meaning can be distorted in the process of writing.
Some features in language use are shared by everyone.
Crimes are usually committed by people who are highly educated.
People tend to stick to certain habitual patterns in their use of language.
items.explanation:
Kaczynski tended to use extensive parallel phrases, which were frequently found in the bomber’s letter.
Both Kaczynski and the bomber also showed a preference for dozens of unusual words
第 3 段說 Kaczynski 習慣（tended to）大量使用平行的片語，也偏好幾十個不常見的字，這些特徵在炸彈客的信裡都找得到；第 1 段也說，恐嚇郵件、塗鴉和 Coleman 的寫作風格相似。同一個人在不同文字裡會露出同樣的習慣，鑑識語言學才能靠這些習慣找出作者，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 writing，原文沒有談到寫作時意思會扭曲；(B) 剛好相反，鑑識語言學靠的是每個人不同的用語特徵；(C) 原文只說 Kaczynski 是前數學家，不能推論犯罪的人通常教育程度高。

閱讀測驗.title: 國歌的歷史演變與文化影響（The Historical Evolution and Cultural Impact of National Anthems）
閱讀測驗.passage:
During the past three hundred years, when a country gains its freedom or independence, one of the first things established is a national anthem. National anthems are generally played and sung at formal state occasions and other events which celebrate or support the country’s national identity.

Holland’s 16th-century hymn “Het Wilhelmus” is widely considered the world’s oldest national anthem, followed by the U.K.’s “God Save the King/Queen”—also a hymn, popularized in the 1740s. As nationalism spread throughout Europe in the 18th and 19th centuries, so did anthems. Many countries, such as the independent states that are today part of Germany, took “God Save the King/Queen” as a model and adopted hymns (songs of prayer typically addressed to a deity or VIP). Others, notably Spain and France, chose marches (songs with a strong, regular rhythm often performed by military bands)—which expressed a martial rather than monarchic spirit. With imperialism, Europeans spread their musical taste. Even when former colonies gained independence, they often imitated the traditions of their former rulers. The result is that most anthems are either hymns or marches, played on European instruments.

Japan’s anthem makes for a good case study of European influence. In the 1860s a British bandmaster living in Japan, John William Fenton, noted that the country did not have a national anthem. A local military officer, Ōyama Iwao, selected the lyrics from a Heian era poem and Fenton wrote the melody. About a decade later, a Japanese committee chose a replacement melody by a court musician—one that had been composed for traditional Japanese instruments, but in a mixed style influenced by Fenton’s arrangement. The version in use today was also altered by German Franz Eckert to fit a Western scale.

In addition to hymns and marches, British composer Michael Bristow identifies a couple of more minor categories. National anthems in South and Central America are often operatic, with long, elaborate orchestral introductions. These were influenced by 19th-century Italian opera. Burma and Sri Lanka are both in a folk group, as they rely more on indigenous instruments.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
過去三百年間，一個國家獲得自由或獨立的時候，最先確立的事情之一，就是國歌。國歌通常在國家正式的場合，以及其他慶祝或支持國家認同的活動上演奏和演唱。

荷蘭 16 世紀的聖歌〈威廉頌〉（Het Wilhelmus）普遍公認是世界上最古老的國歌，其次是英國的〈天佑吾王／女王〉（God Save the King/Queen），這首也是聖歌，在 1740 年代開始流行。18、19 世紀，民族主義在歐洲各地擴散，國歌也跟著擴散。許多國家，例如今天屬於德國的那些獨立邦國，以〈天佑吾王／女王〉為範本，採用聖歌（向神明或重要人物祈禱的歌）。其他國家，特別是西班牙和法國，選擇了進行曲（節奏強而規律的歌，通常由軍樂隊演奏），表達的是軍人的精神，而不是君主的精神。隨著帝國主義擴張，歐洲人也把他們的音樂品味傳播出去。前殖民地即使獨立了，也常常模仿以前統治者的傳統。結果是大多數國歌不是聖歌就是進行曲，而且用歐洲的樂器演奏。

日本的國歌，是研究歐洲影響的好例子。1860 年代，一位住在日本的英國軍樂隊隊長 John William Fenton 注意到，這個國家沒有國歌。當地的軍官大山巖從平安時代的一首詩選出歌詞，Fenton 譜了曲。大約十年後，日本的一個委員會選了宮廷樂師寫的曲子來取代原曲。這首曲子是為日本傳統樂器寫的，風格卻融合了 Fenton 編曲的影響。現在使用的版本，又經過德國人 Franz Eckert 修改，以配合西方的音階。

除了聖歌和進行曲，英國作曲家 Michael Bristow 還歸納出兩種比較少見的類別。中南美洲的國歌常常帶有歌劇風格，前面有很長、很繁複的管弦樂前奏，這是受到 19 世紀義大利歌劇的影響。緬甸和斯里蘭卡都屬於民謠類，因為這兩國比較依賴本土的樂器。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a basis to compose national anthems?
items.explanation:
adopted hymns (songs of prayer
chose marches
These were influenced by 19th-century Italian opera.
第 2 段說許多國家採用聖歌，括號解釋聖歌是祈禱的歌（songs of prayer），是 (A)；西班牙和法國選擇進行曲（marches），是 (B)；第 4 段說中南美洲的國歌受到 19 世紀義大利歌劇的影響，是 (C)。全文沒有提到電影配樂，所以選 (D)。

items.stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?
options: The origin and spread of national anthems.
Reasons why many countries have national anthems.
items.explanation:
is widely considered the world’s oldest national anthem
As nationalism spread throughout Europe in the 18th and 19th centuries, so did anthems.
With imperialism, Europeans spread their musical taste.
第 2 段先說最古老的國歌是荷蘭的〈威廉頌〉，接著是英國的國歌，這是國歌的起源（origin）；然後說民族主義在歐洲擴散，國歌也跟著擴散（spread），帝國主義又把歐洲的音樂品味帶到殖民地。這一段講的是國歌的起源和傳播，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 oldest national anthem，最古老的國歌只是這一段開頭的一句，過於狹隘；(A) 國歌在什麼場合演奏，是第 1 段的內容；(D) 國家獨立時要有國歌，也是第 1 段的內容。

items.stem: Which of the following is true regarding Japan’s national anthem?
options: It was not written until the 20th century.
The lyrics was written by a Japanese officer.
The melody was first composed by a British musician.
The current version is barely influenced by western music.
items.explanation:
a British bandmaster living in Japan, John William Fenton
Fenton wrote the melody
這一題答對率只有 51%，要把歌詞和曲子分開看。第 3 段說英國軍樂隊隊長（a British bandmaster）Fenton 注意到日本沒有國歌，軍官大山巖選了歌詞，Fenton 譜了曲（wrote the melody）；大約十年後，曲子才換成宮廷樂師的作品。最早的曲子是英國音樂家寫的，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 officer，軍官是從平安時代的詩裡選出歌詞，不是自己寫的；(D) 照抄 Western，現在的版本經過 Eckert 修改，配合西方的音階，曲子又融合了 Fenton 編曲的影響，受西方音樂的影響很深；(A) 1860 年代就有了國歌，十年後又換了曲子，都在 19 世紀。

items.stem: What can be inferred about the influence of European imperialism on national anthems?
options: Human rights are a common theme in national anthems.
National anthems of some countries share similar musical features.
Many national anthems were chosen by ruling European countries.
Local traditions were excluded in the composition of national anthems.
items.explanation:
With imperialism, Europeans spread their musical taste.
The result is that most anthems are either hymns or marches, played on European instruments.
第 2 段說隨著帝國主義擴張，歐洲人把音樂品味傳播出去，前殖民地也常常模仿以前統治者的傳統，結果大多數國歌不是聖歌就是進行曲（either hymns or marches），而且用歐洲的樂器演奏。許多國家的國歌類型和樂器都差不多，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 chose，原文說的是前殖民地模仿統治者的傳統，國歌還是各國自己選的；(D) 照抄 traditions，第 3 段說日本後來換的曲子是為日本傳統樂器寫的，本地的傳統並沒有完全排除；(A) 原文沒有談到國歌的主題是人權。

閱讀測驗.title: 過度醫療的問題（The Problem of Overtreatment）
閱讀測驗.passage:
When it comes to medical care, many patients and doctors believe “more is better.” But what they do not realize is that overtreatment—too many scans, too many blood tests, too many procedures—may pose harm. Sometimes a test leads you down a path to more and more testing, some of which may be invasive, or to treatment for things that should be left alone.

Terrence Power, for example, complained that after his wife learned she had Wegener’s disease, an uncommon disorder of the immune system, they found it difficult to refuse testing recommended by her physician. The doctor insisted on office visits every three weeks, even when she was feeling well. He frequently ordered blood tests and X-rays, and repeatedly referred her to specialists for even minor complaints. Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered, and she was hospitalized as a precaution when she developed a cold. She had as many as 25 doctor visits during one six-month period. The couple was spending about $30,000 a year for her care.

After several years of physical suffering and near financial ruin from the medical costs, the couple began questioning the treatment after consulting with other patients in online support groups. “It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said. “You think she’s getting the best care in the world, but after a while you start to wonder: What is the objective?” Mr. Power then spoke with his own primary care doctor, who advised him to find a new specialist to oversee Mrs. Power’s care. Under the new doctor’s care, the regular testing stopped and Mrs. Power’s condition stabilized. Now she sees the doctor only four or five times a year.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
談到醫療照護，許多病人和醫生都相信「越多越好」。但是他們沒有意識到，過度醫療，也就是太多掃描、太多抽血檢驗、太多醫療程序，可能會造成傷害。有時候一項檢查會帶著你走上越來越多檢查的路，其中有些可能是侵入性的；有時候則會去治療一些原本應該放著不管的問題。
