以 Terrence Power 為例，他抱怨妻子得知自己罹患韋格納肉芽腫（一種罕見的免疫系統疾病）之後，兩人發現很難拒絕醫師建議的檢查。醫生堅持她每三週回診一次，即使她覺得身體很好也一樣。醫生經常要她抽血、照 X 光，連小毛病也一再轉診給專科醫師。就算檢查結果正常，醫生還是安排更多檢查；她感冒時，醫生也為了預防萬一讓她住院。在某個半年期間，她看診多達 25 次。這對夫妻每年要花大約三萬美元在她的醫療上。

經過好幾年身體上的折磨，醫療費用也幾乎讓他們破產，這對夫妻在網路病友互助團體裡和其他病人交流之後，開始質疑這些治療。Power 先生說：「醫生什麼時候做得太過頭了，真的很難判斷。你以為她得到的是世界上最好的照顧，但過了一陣子你會開始懷疑：這樣做的目的到底是什麼？」Power 先生後來和自己的家庭醫師談過，醫師建議他另外找一位專科醫師負責 Power 太太的治療。在新醫師的照護下，例行檢查停了，Power 太太的病情也穩定下來。現在她一年只看醫生四、五次。

items.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: Treatments do not always cause harmful side effects.
Patients tend to believe more testing is better treatment.
Too much medical care may not be beneficial to patients.
Doctors generally recommend office visits that are necessary.
items.explanation: 第 1 段開門見山：很多人相信醫療越多越好，但過度醫療可能造成傷害；第 2、3 段用 Power 太太的例子說明，太多檢查讓她身心受苦、幾乎破產，停掉例行檢查後病情反而穩定。全文要說的是太多醫療對病人未必有益，所以是 (C)。(B) 病人相信檢查越多越好，只是第 1 段第一句的說法，過於狹隘；(A) 說治療不一定有副作用、(D) 說醫生通常只建議必要的回診，都和文章的立場相反，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following was a problem for Mrs. Power during her medical treatment?
options: She had to be hospitalized for three weeks whenever she had a cold.
She didn’t have any insurance, so she went broke because of her illness.
When test results showed she was fine, her doctor still ordered more tests.
Her doctor asked her to consult other specialists due to her constant complaints.
items.explanation:
Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered,
第 2 段說就算檢查結果正常（tests came back negative），醫生還是安排更多檢查，選項換成 test results showed she was fine 和 still ordered more tests。(A) 照抄 three weeks，原文說每三週回診一次，感冒住院是為了預防萬一，沒說住院三週；(D) 照抄 specialists，原文說連小毛病（minor complaints）也轉診，不是因為她一直抱怨；(B) 原文說醫療費用讓這對夫妻幾乎破產，沒提到有沒有保險。

items.stem: Who does “they” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?
items.explanation:
“It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said.
they 出現在 Power 先生說的話裡：很難判斷 they 什麼時候越過了界線（crossed the line）。第 2 段一路寫的是醫生堅持回診、一再安排檢查和轉診，做得太多、越過界線的是醫生，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄前一句的 other patients，(D) 照抄 online support groups，這對夫妻是和其他病友交流之後才開始質疑，病友和互助團體不是安排檢查的人；(C) Power 夫婦是承受過度醫療的一方。

items.stem: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward medical tests?
options: More tests than necessary are too much.
Medical tests are essential for disease prevention.
Many tests are needed for confirmation of diagnosis.
Doctors’ interpretations of test results are seldom wrong.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說過度醫療（太多掃描、太多抽血、太多醫療程序）可能造成傷害，一項檢查常會引出更多檢查；Power 太太的例子也說明檢查做得太多反而傷身又傷財，停掉例行檢查後病情穩定。作者認為超過需要的檢查就是太多了，所以是 (A)。(B)、(C) 強調檢查必要，和作者的立場相反；(D) 文章沒有談醫生判讀檢查結果準不準。

閱讀測驗.title: 大規模線上開放課程（MOOCs）
閱讀測驗.passage:
MOOC, a massive open online course, aims at providing large-scale interactive participation and open access via the web. In addition to traditional course materials such as videos, readings, and problem sets, MOOCs provide interactive user forums that help build a community for the students, professors, and teaching assistants.

MOOCs first made waves in the fall of 2011, when Professor Sebastian Thrun from Stanford University opened his graduate-level artificial intelligence course up to any student anywhere, and 160,000 students in more than 190 countries signed up. This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways. Since the courses can be taken by hundreds of thousands of students at the same time, the number of universities might decrease dramatically. Professor Thrun has even envisioned a future in which there will only need to be 10 universities in the world. Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free. This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.

There is a lot of excitement and fear surrounding MOOCs. While some say free online courses are a great way to increase the enrollment of minority students, others have said they will leave many students behind. Some critics have said that MOOCs promote an unrealistic one-size-fits-all model of higher education and that there is no replacement for true dialogues between professors and their students. After all, a brain is not a computer. We are not blank hard drives waiting to be filled with data. People learn from people they love and remember the things that arouse emotion. Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
MOOC 是大規模線上開放課程，目標是透過網路提供大規模的互動參與和開放的學習管道。除了影片、閱讀材料和習題這些傳統的課程教材，MOOC 還提供互動式的使用者論壇，幫助學生、教授和助教建立一個社群。

MOOC 最早在 2011 年秋天引起轟動：史丹佛大學的 Sebastian Thrun 教授把他研究所程度的人工智慧課程開放給世界各地的任何學生，結果有 190 多個國家、16 萬名學生報名。這種新型態的線上課程在許多方面撼動了高等教育界。由於一門課可以同時讓數十萬名學生修讀，大學的數量可能會大幅減少。Thrun 教授甚至設想，未來全世界只需要 10 所大學。MOOC 有許多是由知名大學的教授授課，而它最引人注目的地方或許是免費。這對手頭很緊的學生來說當然是好消息。

MOOC 帶來許多期待，也引起許多擔憂。有些人說，免費的線上課程是增加少數族群學生入學人數的好方法；也有人說，這種課程會讓許多學生跟不上。有些批評者認為，MOOC 推行的是一種不切實際、一體適用的高等教育模式，而教授和學生之間真正的對話是無可取代的。畢竟，人腦不是電腦，我們不是等著裝滿資料的空白硬碟。人會向自己喜愛的人學習，也會記住引起情緒的事物。有些批評者擔心，線上學生會錯過大學的社交生活。

items.stem: What does the word “cash-strapped” in the second paragraph mean?
items.explanation:
Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free.
This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.
第 2 段說 MOOC 最引人注目的地方或許是免費，接著說這對 cash-strapped 學生當然是好消息。課程免費，最高興的會是缺錢的學生，所以 cash-strapped 是手頭很緊、缺錢，最接近 (B) Being short of money。(A) 賺很多錢，和「免費課程是好消息」接不上；(C) 用錢謹慎、(D) 花錢很少，說的是花錢的習慣，不是手頭缺錢。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the features of MOOCs?
options: It is free to take the courses.
Many courses are offered by famous universities.
Many students can take the course at the same time.
items.explanation:
Since the courses can be taken by hundreds of thousands of students at the same time,
many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities
is that they’re free.
文章提到的三個特色在選項都換了說法：第 2 段說 MOOC 最引人注目的是免費（they’re free），是 (A)；許多課程由知名大學的教授授課（professors at prestigious universities），是 (B)；一門課可以同時讓數十萬名學生修讀，是 (D)。人工智慧只是 Thrun 教授開的那一門課，文章沒說大部分的課程都在講人工智慧，所以選 (C)。

items.stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?
items.explanation:
This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways.
第 2 段先說 MOOC 在 2011 年引起轟動，接著用 This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways 點出重點：這種課程在許多方面撼動高等教育界。後面說的大學數量可能大減、全世界只需要 10 所大學、免費對手頭很緊的學生是好消息，都是它帶來的影響，所以是 (A)。(C) 課程規模和 (D) 費用都只是這一段用來說明影響的細節；(B) 目標是第 1 段的內容。

items.stem: Which of the following is mentioned in the passage as a problem of MOOCs?
options: The disappearance of traditional course materials.
The limited number of courses offered around the world.
The overreliance on professors from prestigious universities.
The lack of social interaction among students and professors.
items.explanation:
there is no replacement for true dialogues between professors and their students
Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.
第 3 段批評者說教授和學生之間真正的對話無可取代，也擔心線上學生會錯過大學的社交生活（social aspects of college），選項換成 lack of social interaction among students and professors。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 traditional course materials，原文說 MOOC 除了傳統教材之外還有論壇，教材並沒有消失；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 prestigious universities，知名大學的教授授課是 MOOC 的特色，不是問題；(B) 文章沒說課程數量有限，第 2 段說可能減少的是大學的數量。

閱讀測驗.title: 中東地區的失學兒童（Children Out of School in the Middle East）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Ongoing conflicts across the Middle East have prevented more than 13 million children from attending school, according to a report published by UNICEF, the United Nations Children’s Fund.

The report states that 40% of all children across the region are currently not receiving an education, which is a result of two consequences of violence: structural damage to schools and the displacement of populations, also called “forced migration.” Both issues result from the tide of violence that has crossed the region in recent years. The report examines nine countries where a state of war has become the norm. Across these countries, violence has made 8,500 schools unusable. In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.

The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011. With the crisis now in its fifth year, basic public services, including education, inside Syria have been stretched to breaking point. Within the country, the quality and availability of education depends on whether a particular region is suffering violence.

The report concludes with an earnest request to international policymakers to distribute financial and other resources to ease the regional crisis. With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance. The forces that are crushing individual lives and futures are also destroying the prospects for an entire region.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
根據聯合國兒童基金會發表的一份報告，中東各地持續不斷的衝突，使超過 1,300 萬名兒童無法上學。

報告指出，這個地區所有的兒童中，目前有 40% 沒有接受教育，原因是暴力帶來的兩個後果：學校建築遭到破壞，以及人口流離失所，也就是所謂的「強迫遷徙」。這兩個問題都來自近年席捲這個地區的暴力浪潮。報告調查了九個長期處於戰爭狀態的國家，在這些國家裡，暴力已經使 8,500 所學校無法使用。在某些情況下，社區把學校建築當作流離失所者的收容所，在伊拉克各地原本的學校裡，一間教室最多住了九戶人家。

報告特別關注敘利亞。敘利亞自 2011 年爆發血腥內戰以來，至少已有 900 萬人流離失所。危機如今已進入第五年，敘利亞境內包括教育在內的基本公共服務，都已經不堪負荷、瀕臨崩潰。在敘利亞國內，教育的品質和普及程度，要看某個地區是否正遭受暴力。

報告最後懇切呼籲國際決策者，提供資金和其他資源來緩解這個地區的危機。已經有超過 1,300 萬名兒童因為衝突離開教室，說一整個世代兒童的教育前景岌岌可危，一點也不誇張。摧毀個人生命和未來的這股力量，也正在摧毀整個地區的前景。

items.stem: What is this article mainly about?
options: Why people are moving away from their own countries.
Why there are civil wars and violence in the Middle East.
Why many schools have become shelters for displaced families.
Why many children in the Middle East are not attending school.
items.explanation: 第 1 段開頭就說中東的衝突使超過 1,300 萬名兒童無法上學；第 2 段說明兩個原因：學校遭到破壞、人口流離失所；第 3 段以敘利亞為例；第 4 段呼籲國際提供資源。全文要回答的是為什麼許多中東兒童沒有上學，所以是 (D)。(A) 人口遷離家園和 (C) 學校變成收容所，都只是第 2 段說明的原因，過於狹隘；(B) 文章沒有分析內戰和暴力為什麼發生，偏離主題。

items.stem: Why is “Iraq” mentioned in the second paragraph?
options: To convince people that temporary housing can be easily found.
To prove that classrooms there are big enough to host many families.
To give an example of why schools are not usable for children’s learning.
To show how structural damages of school can affect the quality of education.
items.explanation:
Across these countries, violence has made 8,500 schools unusable.
In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.
第 2 段先說暴力使 8,500 所學校無法使用（unusable），接著用 In certain cases 帶出伊拉克的例子：學校成了收容所，一間教室住到九戶人家。提到伊拉克，是為了舉例說明學校為什麼不能用來上課，選項把 unusable 換成 not usable。(D) 照抄 structural damage，但伊拉克的例子說的是學校拿來安置流離失所的人，不是建築毀損，教育品質是第 3 段講敘利亞時才提到；(B) 照抄 families，一間教室住九戶人家是說擁擠，不是說教室夠大；(A) 文章沒說臨時住處很容易找到。

items.stem: What does the phrase “in the balance” in the last paragraph most likely mean?
items.explanation:
With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance.
第 4 段說已經有超過 1,300 萬名兒童因為衝突離開教室，說一整個世代兒童的教育前景 in the balance 一點也不誇張。這麼多孩子失學，他們的教育前景會怎麼樣還說不定，in the balance 就是懸而未決、岌岌可危，最接近 (B) 處於不確定的狀況。(A) 受到妥善照顧、(C) 由當局控制，都和失學的處境不合；(D) 往錯誤的方向走，是把前景當成已經確定變壞，原文說的是結果還未定。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
options: The war in Syria has been going on since 2011.
More than nine thousand schools have been destroyed by wars.
Thirteen million people have been forced to leave their homes in the Middle East.
Forty percent of all children in the world are not attending schools due to ongoing conflict.
items.explanation:
The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011.
第 3 段說敘利亞的血腥內戰從 2011 年開始，選項把 since the war began in 2011 換成 has been going on since 2011。(B) 照抄 nine，原文的 nine 是九百萬人流離失所和九個國家，無法使用的學校是 8,500 所，不到九千所；(C) 照抄第 2 段 forced migration 的 forced，1,300 萬是無法上學的兒童人數，不是離開家園的人數；(D) 40% 指的是中東地區的兒童，不是全世界的兒童。

閱讀測驗.title: 畫家溫斯洛·霍默（Winslow Homer）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Winslow Homer (1836-1910) is regarded by many as the greatest American painter of the nineteenth century. Born and raised in Boston, he began his career at age eighteen in his hometown, working as an apprentice at a printing company. Skilled at drawing, he soon made a name for himself making illustrations for novels, sheet music, magazines, and children’s books.

He then moved to New York City, where he worked as a freelance illustrator with Harper’s Weekly, a popular magazine of the time, and began painting. Homer was assigned to cover the inauguration of President Lincoln and, later, the Civil War. His pictures of the Union troops won international recognition. Homer moved to England and, after a two-year stay, returned to America. He settled permanently in Maine in 1883.

From the late 1850s until his death in 1910, Winslow Homer produced a body of work distinguished by its thoughtful expression and its independence from artistic conventions. A man of multiple talents, Homer excelled equally in the arts of illustration, oil painting, and watercolor. Many of his works—depictions of children at play and in school, farm girls attending to their work, hunters and their prey—have become classic images of nineteenth-century American life. Others speak to more universal themes such as the primal relationship of humans to nature.

This two-week exhibition highlights a wide and representative range of Homer’s art. It shows his extraordinary career from the battlefields, farmland, and coastal villages of America, to the North Sea fishing village of Cullercoats, the rocky coast of Maine, the Adirondacks, and the Caribbean. The exhibition offers viewers an opportunity to experience and appreciate the breadth of his remarkable artistic achievement.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
許多人認為溫斯洛·霍默（1836–1910）是 19 世紀最偉大的美國畫家。他在波士頓出生長大，十八歲在家鄉展開職業生涯，在一家印刷公司當學徒。他擅長繪畫，很快就以替小說、樂譜、雜誌和兒童書繪製插畫而出名。

後來他搬到紐約市，替當時很受歡迎的雜誌 Harper’s Weekly 擔任自由插畫家，也開始作畫。霍默受派報導林肯總統的就職典禮，後來又報導南北戰爭。他描繪北軍的畫作贏得國際肯定。霍默後來搬到英國，住了兩年後回到美國，1883 年在緬因州定居。

從 1850 年代後期到 1910 年去世，霍默創作了大量作品，特色是表達深刻，而且不受藝術傳統束縛。霍默多才多藝，插畫、油畫和水彩都同樣出色。他的許多作品，像是描繪孩子遊戲和上學、農家女孩忙著做事、獵人和獵物的畫，都已經成為 19 世紀美國生活的經典畫面。其他作品則觸及更普遍的主題，例如人和大自然之間最原始的關係。

這次為期兩週的展覽，展出霍默藝術作品中範圍廣泛又具代表性的一批。展覽呈現他非凡的創作生涯，從美國的戰場、農田和海邊村落，到北海的漁村卡勒科茨、緬因州的岩岸、阿第倫達克山脈和加勒比海。觀眾可以藉這次展覽，體會並欣賞他卓越藝術成就的廣度。

閱讀測驗.title: 白宮的歷史（The History of the White House）
閱讀測驗.passage:
For more than two hundred years, the White House has stood as a symbol of the United States Presidency, the U.S. government, and the American people. In 1790, President George Washington declared that the federal government would reside in a district “not exceeding ten miles square … on the river Potomac.” As preparations began, a competition was held to find a builder of the “President’s House.” Nine proposals were submitted, and the Irish-born architect James Hoban won the gold medal for his practical and handsome design. Construction began when the first cornerstone was laid in October of 1792. Although President Washington oversaw the construction of the house, he never lived in it. It was not until 1800, when the White House was nearly completed, that its first residents, President John Adams and his wife Abigail, moved in.

American presidents can express their individual style in how they decorate the house and in how they receive the public. Thomas Jefferson held the first inaugural open house in 1805; many of those who attended the swearing-in ceremony at the U.S. Capitol simply followed him home. President Jefferson also opened the house for public tours, and it has remained open, except during wartime, ever since. In addition, Jefferson welcomed visitors to annual receptions on New Year’s Day and on the Fourth of July. Abraham Lincoln did the same, but then the inaugural crowds became far too large for the White House to accommodate comfortably, and this also created a security issue. It was not until Grover Cleveland’s first presidency that some effective crowd control measures were implemented to address the problem caused by this practice.

At various times in history, the White House has been known as the “President’s Palace,” the “President’s House,” and the “Executive Mansion.” President Theodore Roosevelt officially gave the White House its current name in 1901.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
兩百多年來，白宮一直是美國總統職位、美國政府和美國人民的象徵。1790 年，華盛頓總統宣布聯邦政府將設在波多馬克河畔一個「不超過十英里見方」的特區。籌備工作展開後，政府舉辦了一場比賽，徵求「總統府」的建造者。比賽共收到九件設計提案，出生於愛爾蘭的建築師霍本以實用又美觀的設計贏得金牌。1792 年 10 月，第一塊基石奠下，工程正式開始。華盛頓總統雖然監督了白宮的興建，卻從來沒有住過。一直到 1800 年白宮快要完工時，第一批住戶亞當斯總統和夫人 Abigail 才搬進去。

美國總統可以從白宮的布置和接待民眾的方式，展現個人的風格。傑佛遜在 1805 年舉辦了第一次就職開放日；許多在美國國會大廈參加宣誓典禮的民眾，乾脆跟著他一路回到白宮。傑佛遜總統也開放白宮讓民眾參觀，從此以後，除了戰爭期間，白宮一直對外開放。此外，傑佛遜每年元旦和七月四日國慶日也開放白宮，歡迎訪客。林肯也照著這麼做，但是後來就職的人潮多到白宮無法舒適地容納，也造成了安全問題。一直到克里夫蘭第一次擔任總統時，才實施了一些有效的人潮管制措施，解決這個做法帶來的問題。

白宮在歷史上不同時期，曾經叫做「總統宮」、「總統府」和「行政官邸」。1901 年，老羅斯福總統正式把它定名為現在的名稱。

items.explanation:

閱讀測驗.title: 西尼羅病毒（West Nile Virus）
閱讀測驗.passage:
West Nile is a tropical disease that begins in birds, which pass it on to mosquitoes that then go on to infect human beings with a bite. Most people who contract West Nile do not experience any symptoms at all, but, if they do, symptoms typically develop between 3 to 14 days after a mosquito bite. About 1 in 5 persons suffers fever, headaches, and body aches, usually lasting a week or so. A far less lucky 1 in 150 experiences high fever, tremors, paralysis, and coma. Some—especially the elderly and those with weak immune systems—die.

That is what made the major outbreaks of West Nile in the U.S. in the summer of 2012 so scary. The situation was particularly bad in Dallas, Texas, where the West Nile virus killed 10 people and sickened more than 200. The city declared a state of emergency and began aerial spraying of a pesticide to kill the mosquitoes, even though residents argued that the pesticide could be more dangerous than the disease.

Why was the summer of 2012 so hospitable to the West Nile virus and the mosquitoes that carry it? Blame the weather. An extremely mild winter allowed more mosquitoes than usual to survive, while the unusually high temperatures in that scorching summer further increased their number by speeding up their life cycle. The economic crisis may have also played a role: Homeowners who were not able to pay their bank loans were forced to abandon their properties, sometimes leaving behind swimming pools that made excellent mosquito breeding grounds.

The severity of tropical diseases is also a matter of whether governments are capable—and willing—to defend their populations against infections. Dallas County was not doing some of the key things to slow the spread of West Nile, such as testing dead birds and setting mosquito traps to test for the presence of the disease. Tropical infections are thus as much related to government inaction as they are to climate.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
西尼羅病毒會引起一種熱帶疾病。病毒最先出現在鳥類身上，鳥再把病毒傳給蚊子，蚊子接著叮人，把病毒傳染給人類。大部分感染西尼羅病毒的人完全沒有症狀；如果出現症狀，通常是在蚊子叮咬後 3 到 14 天之間。大約五分之一的人會發燒、頭痛、全身痠痛，通常持續一個星期左右。比較不幸的，大約每 150 人有 1 人會高燒、顫抖、癱瘓甚至昏迷。有些人會因此死亡，特別是年長者和免疫系統較弱的人。

正因為這樣，2012 年夏天西尼羅病毒在美國大爆發，才會那麼令人害怕。德州達拉斯的情況特別嚴重，病毒在當地造成 10 人死亡、200 多人染病。達拉斯市宣布進入緊急狀態，開始從空中噴灑農藥撲殺蚊子，儘管居民認為農藥可能比疾病本身還危險。

為什麼 2012 年夏天特別適合西尼羅病毒和傳播病毒的蚊子？要怪天氣。極為溫和的冬天讓比平常更多的蚊子活了下來，那年夏天又異常炎熱，高溫加快了蚊子的生命週期，數量因此更多。經濟危機可能也有影響：付不出銀行貸款的屋主不得不棄屋離開，有時留下的游泳池正好成了蚊子絕佳的繁殖場所。

熱帶疾病嚴不嚴重，也要看政府有沒有能力、有沒有意願保護人民不受感染。達拉斯郡沒有做到一些減緩西尼羅病毒擴散的關鍵措施，例如檢驗死鳥、設置捕蚊器來檢測病毒是否存在。因此，熱帶傳染病和政府不作為的關係，跟它和氣候的關係一樣密切。

items.stem: What is this passage mainly about?
options: West Nile and methods to fight it.

items.explanation: 第 1 段說明西尼羅病毒怎麼傳染、有哪些症狀；第 2 段說 2012 年達拉斯疫情嚴重；第 3 段說天氣和經濟危機讓蚊子大量繁殖；第 4 段說政府不作為也讓疾病擴散。第 3、4 段講的都是病毒在什麼條件下容易蔓延，所以是 (C)。(A) 對抗疾病的方法只在第 2、4 段帶到（空中噴藥、檢驗死鳥），(B) 政府效率只在第 4 段談到，都過於狹隘；(D) 把話題拉大到熱帶疾病整體，太過廣泛。這一題考後有人主張 (B) 也對，大考中心邀集專家討論後維持 (C)，說明試題文章是從原始報導大幅刪節改寫而成，作答要以考卷上這篇文章的脈絡為準。

items.explanation:
An extremely mild winter allowed more mosquitoes than usual to survive,
第 3 段說極為溫和的冬天讓比平常更多的蚊子活了下來，an extremely mild winter 在選項換成 not as cold as usual。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 residents，居民擔心的是噴藥的危險，這是政府處理疫情時的爭議，不是疫情嚴重的原因；(A) 照抄 Texas，文章沒說德州人口增加；(B) 第 4 段批評的是郡政府沒有檢驗死鳥、設置捕蚊器，不是沒有及時發布警告。

閱讀測驗.title: 海水淡化（Desalination）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Most parts of Taiwan have access to sufficient supplies of fresh water for drinking. But fresh water can be in short supply in many arid regions of the world such as Saudi Arabia, where there are limited water resources. As the world population continues to grow, shortages of fresh water will occur more often and the need for additional water supplies will become critical. Some may ask, “Since the ocean covers more than 70 percent of the Earth, why not just get drinking water from the ocean?”

To turn seawater into fresh water, we need to remove the salt in seawater, that is, to desalinate seawater. The problem is that the desalination of water requires a lot of energy. Salt dissolves very easily in water, forming strong chemical bonds, and those bonds are difficult to break. The energy and technology to desalinate water are both expensive, and this means that desalinating water can be costly.

There are environmental costs of desalination as well. Sea life can get sucked into desalination plants, killing small ocean creatures like baby fish and plankton, upsetting the food chain. Also, there is the problem of what to do with the separated salt, which is left over as a very concentrated brine. Pumping this super-salty water back into the ocean can harm local aquatic life. Reducing these impacts is possible, but it adds to the costs.

Despite the economic and environmental hurdles, desalination is becoming increasingly attractive as human beings are using up fresh water from other sources. At present, desalinating seawater is the only viable way to provide water to growing populations in rural areas of the Middle East and North Africa. Therefore, the race is on to find a cheaper, cleaner, and more energy-efficient way of desalinating seawater, and promising new findings are being reported.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
台灣大部分地方都有充足的淡水可以飲用。不過，世界上許多乾旱地區的淡水可能供應不足，例如水資源有限的沙烏地阿拉伯。隨著世界人口持續成長，淡水短缺會越來越常發生，增加供水也會變得非常迫切。有些人可能會問：「既然海洋覆蓋了地球百分之七十以上的面積，為什麼不乾脆從海洋取得飲用水呢？」

要把海水變成淡水，就得去除海水中的鹽分，也就是把海水淡化。問題是，海水淡化需要大量能源。鹽很容易溶解在水中，形成很強的化學鍵，而這些化學鍵很難打斷。淡化海水所需的能源和技術都很昂貴，這表示淡化海水的成本可能很高。

海水淡化也有環境上的代價。海洋生物可能隨著海水吸進淡化廠，小魚、浮游生物這類小型海洋生物因此死亡，擾亂了食物鏈。另外，分離出來的鹽要怎麼處理也是個問題，這些鹽會以極濃的鹽水留下來。把這種超鹹的水抽回海中，可能會傷害當地的水中生物。要降低這些影響是做得到的，但是會增加成本。

儘管有經濟和環境上的障礙，隨著人類漸漸用盡其他來源的淡水，海水淡化越來越受到重視。目前在中東和北非的鄉村地區，淡化海水是供水給日漸增加的人口唯一可行的辦法。因此，各方競相尋找更便宜、更乾淨、更節能的海水淡化方式，也陸續有令人振奮的新發現。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “arid” in the first paragraph?

第 1 段說世界上許多 arid 地區的淡水可能供應不足，並以水資源有限的沙烏地阿拉伯為例。淡水不足、水資源有限，可見 arid 是乾旱的意思，最接近 (C) Dry。(A) 有人居住的、(B) 孤立的、(D) 偏遠的都和缺水無關。

items.stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?

The major chemical characteristics of seawater.
The urgent need to turn seawater into fresh water.
The amount of energy produced in the desalination of seawater.
items.explanation:
The problem is that the desalination of water requires a lot of energy.
The energy and technology to desalinate water are both expensive, and this means that desalinating water can be costly.
第 2 段第一句先說淡化海水要去除鹽分，接著用 The problem is that 帶出這一段的重點：淡化需要大量能源，能源和技術都很昂貴，所以成本很高（costly），選項換成 high cost。(C) 照抄這一段第一句的 turn seawater into fresh water，但那句只是引出話題，迫切需要淡水是第 1 段的內容；(B) 照抄 chemical，化學鍵是用來解釋淡化為什麼耗費能源；(D) 照抄 energy，原文說的是淡化要消耗能源，不是產生能源，方向正好相反。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

Covering 70% of the Earth, the ocean has always satisfied human needs for water.

第 3 段說海洋生物可能隨著海水吸進淡化廠，小魚和浮游生物因此死亡，擾亂食物鏈；upsetting the food chain 在選項換成 disturb the food chain。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 salt，原文說鹽很容易溶解在水中，難的是把鹽去除，選項把難易說反了；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 of the Earth，海洋覆蓋地球七成以上只是那個問句的前提，文章接著說淡水會短缺，不是海洋一直滿足人類用水；(D) 照抄 Saudi Arabia，原文說的是沙烏地阿拉伯水資源有限，人口成長說的是全世界。

items.stem: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward the future of desalination?
items.explanation: 作者在第 2、3 段先說海水淡化成本高、對環境有害，第 4 段用 Despite 轉回來：淡化越來越受重視，各方競相研發更便宜、更乾淨、更節能的方法，也有令人振奮的新發現（promising new findings）。作者對淡化的未來抱著希望，所以是 (D)。(B) 懷疑和 (C) 保守只看到第 2、3 段的障礙，忽略了 Despite 之後的結論；(A) 驚訝，文章沒有表現出這種情緒。

閱讀測驗.title: 搖籃曲的功能（The Functions of Lullabies）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Four millennia ago, an ancient Babylonian wrote down what is possibly the first lullaby. It is a rather threatening lullaby, in which the baby is scolded for disturbing the house god with its crying and warned of terrifying consequences. It may have got the baby to sleep, but its message is far from comforting: If he/she does not stop crying, the demon will eat him/her. This lullaby may sound more scary than sleep-inducing, yet it is true that many lullabies—including those sung today—have dark undertones.

Research has shown that lullabies, when used correctly, can soothe and possibly even help to heal an infant; but it is the caretaker’s voice and the rhythm and melody of the music that babies respond to, not the content of the song. Then, what is the function of the content? According to studies, some lullabies provide advice, like the Babylonian lullaby, and quite a few others offer the space to sing the unsung, say the unsayable. Lyrics to those lullabies can indeed be interpreted as a reflection of the caregiver’s emotions.

Researchers believe that a large part of the function of lullabies is to help a mother vocalize her worries and concerns. The mother’s fear of loss especially makes sense since the infant/toddler years of life are fragile ones. Since there is a special physical bond between mother and child during this period, mothers feel they can sing to their child about their own fears and anxieties. Lullabies, therefore, serve as therapy for the mother. In addition, the songs are seemingly trying to work some magic—as if, by singing, the mother is saying, “Sadness has already touched this house; no need to come by again.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
四千年前，一位古巴比倫人寫下了可能是史上第一首的搖籃曲。這首搖籃曲帶著相當濃的威脅意味，歌詞責罵寶寶哭聲吵到了家神，還警告寶寶會有可怕的後果。這首歌也許真的哄得寶寶睡著，但傳達的訊息一點也不令人安心：寶寶如果不停止哭鬧，惡魔就會把他吃掉。這首搖籃曲聽起來與其說催人入眠，不如說嚇人；不過，許多搖籃曲，包括現在還在唱的，確實都帶著陰暗的弦外之音。

研究顯示，搖籃曲用得正確，可以安撫嬰兒，甚至可能有助於嬰兒康復；但嬰兒回應的是照顧者的聲音，以及音樂的節奏和旋律，不是歌曲的內容。那麼，歌詞有什麼作用呢？研究指出，有些搖籃曲像那首巴比倫搖籃曲一樣提供建議，還有不少搖籃曲提供一個空間，讓人唱出沒唱出口的心聲、說出說不出口的話。這些搖籃曲的歌詞，確實可以解讀成照顧者情緒的反映。

研究人員認為，搖籃曲很大一部分的作用，是幫助母親把擔憂和掛念說出來。嬰幼兒時期很脆弱，母親害怕失去孩子的心情特別可以理解。這段時期母子之間有一種特殊的身體連結，母親覺得可以對孩子唱出自己的恐懼和焦慮。因此，搖籃曲成了母親的心理治療。此外，這些歌似乎也想施一點法術，彷彿母親藉著歌唱在說：「悲傷已經來過這個家了，不必再來了。」

items.stem: Which of the following titles best describes the main idea of this passage?
items.explanation: 第 1 段以最早的巴比倫搖籃曲帶出搖籃曲常有陰暗的弦外之音；第 2 段說搖籃曲能安撫嬰兒，歌詞則能提供建議、反映照顧者的情緒；第 3 段說搖籃曲幫母親說出擔憂，是母親的心理治療。全文一路在談搖籃曲有什麼作用，所以是 (B)。(A) 起源和 (C) 帶有威脅的搖籃曲只是第 1 段的例子，(D) 催人入眠只對應第 2 段開頭安撫嬰兒的部分，都過於狹隘。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word “undertones” in the first paragraph?
items.explanation:
It may have got the baby to sleep, but its message is far from comforting: If he/she does not stop crying, the demon will eat him/her.
This lullaby may sound more scary than sleep-inducing, yet it is true that many lullabies—including those sung today—have dark undertones.
第 1 段說這首搖籃曲傳達的訊息（message）一點也不令人安心，接著說許多搖籃曲都帶著陰暗的 undertones；第 2 段也說歌詞可以解讀成照顧者情緒的反映。undertone 是話裡隱含的意思、弦外之音，最接近 (D) Messages。(A) 照抄同一段的 consequences，那是歌詞警告寶寶的可怕後果，不是弦外之音；(B) 歌聲和 (C) 耳語是從 tone 聯想到聲音，但這裡講的是歌詞的意思。

items.stem: What does the author use to support the idea that lullabies can have a soothing effect?
items.explanation:
Research has shown that lullabies, when used correctly, can soothe and possibly even help to heal an infant;
第 2 段一開頭就說研究顯示（Research has shown），搖籃曲用得正確可以安撫嬰兒，作者用的是研究報告，選項照用原字 Research。(C) 照抄 caretaker，原文說嬰兒回應的是照顧者的聲音，不是照顧者的故事；(B) 第 1 段的巴比倫搖籃曲是歷史上的例子，但用來說明搖籃曲帶有威脅意味，不是證明搖籃曲能安撫嬰兒；(D) 文章沒有寫到作者的親身經驗。

items.stem: According to this passage, which of the following statements is true?
options: Scary lullabies better help babies fall asleep.
Mothers prefer to sing lullabies with a joyful melody.

閱讀測驗.title: 音樂產業的群眾募資（Crowd-funding in the Music Industry）
閱讀測驗.passage:
All pop artists like to say that they owe their success to their fans. In the case of British band SVM, it’s indeed true. The band is currently recording songs because 358 fans contributed the £100,000 needed for the project. The arrangement came via MMC, an online record label that uses Web-based, social-network-style “crowd-funding” to finance its acts.

Here’s how it works: MMC posts demos and videos of 10 artists on its website, and users are invited to invest from £10 to £1,000 in the ones they most enjoy or think are most likely to become popular. Once an act reaches £100,000, the financing process is completed, and the money is used to pay for recording and possibly a concert tour. Profits from resulting music sales, concerts, and merchandise are split three ways: investors get to divide 40%; another 40% goes to MMC; the artist pockets 20%. The payoff for investors can be big. One fan in France who contributed £4,250 got his money back 22 times over.

Crowd-funding musical acts is not new. But MMC takes the concept to another level. First of all, investors can get cash rather than just goodies like free downloads or tickets. Also, MMC is a record label. It has the means to get its music distributed around the world and to market artists effectively. “Artists need professional support,” says the CEO of MMC’s international division.

While digital technology and the Net have created a do-it-yourself boom among musicians, success is still a long shot. Out of the 20,000 records released in the U.S. in 2009, only 14 DIY acts made it to the Top 200. Also, with less revenue from recorded music, music companies have become less likely to take risks, which has led to fewer artists receiving funding. The crowd-funding model, however, allows for more records to be made by spreading risk among hundreds of backers. And the social-network aspect of the site helps expand fan bases; that is, investors become a promotional army.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
流行歌手都喜歡說，他們的成功要歸功於歌迷。以英國樂團 SVM 來說，這句話一點也不假。這個樂團正在錄製歌曲，因為有 358 位歌迷出資，籌到了這項計畫需要的 10 萬英鎊。這項安排是透過 MMC 促成的。MMC 是一家線上唱片公司，用網路上類似社群網站的「群眾募資」方式，替旗下的藝人籌措資金。

運作方式是這樣的：MMC 在網站上放 10 組藝人的試聽帶和影片，邀請用戶投資 10 到 1,000 英鎊，投給他們最喜歡、或認為最可能走紅的藝人。一組藝人募到 10 萬英鎊，籌資程序就完成了，這筆錢會用來支付錄音的費用，也可能用來辦巡迴演唱會。之後音樂銷售、演唱會和周邊商品的收益，分成三份：投資人一起分 40%，另外 40% 歸 MMC，藝人拿 20%。投資人的回報可能很高。法國有一位歌迷投資了 4,250 英鎊，拿回了 22 倍的錢。

替音樂人群眾募資並不新鮮，但 MMC 把這個概念推到了另一個層次。第一，投資人可以拿到現金，不只是免費下載或門票這類贈品。第二，MMC 本身是一家唱片公司，有能力把音樂發行到全世界，也能有效地行銷藝人。MMC 國際部門的執行長說：「藝人需要專業的支援。」

雖然數位科技和網路讓音樂人掀起了一股自己動手做（DIY）的風潮，要成功仍然很難。2009 年美國發行的兩萬張唱片中，只有 14 組自己動手做的藝人擠進前 200 名。此外，唱片的收入減少，唱片公司變得比較不敢冒險，獲得資金的藝人也就變少了。然而，群眾募資的模式把風險分散給數百位出資者，讓更多唱片能夠製作出來。網站的社群特性也有助於擴大歌迷群，也就是說，投資人成了宣傳大軍。

items.stem: Which of the following titles best expresses the main idea of the passage?
items.explanation: 第 1 段用英國樂團 SVM 的例子，帶出 MMC 用群眾募資替藝人籌錢；第 2 段說明運作方式；第 3 段說 MMC 和一般群眾募資有什麼不同；第 4 段說唱片公司不敢冒險，群眾募資能分散風險，讓更多唱片製作出來。全文講的是音樂產業的群眾募資，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (B)，這個選項照抄第 4 段的 music companies：原文說募來的錢用來替旗下的藝人（its acts）錄音，籌錢的對象是藝人，不是唱片公司，第 4 段還說唱片公司變得不敢冒險，偏離主題。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 Web-based，網路是募資的管道，全文談的是籌錢，不是用網路製作音樂，偏離主題；(C) 投資人拿到高額回報，只是第 2 段的一個例子，過於狹隘。

items.stem: How much money does a band have to raise via MMC to have their music recorded?
items.explanation:
Once an act reaches £100,000, the financing process is completed, and the money is used to pay for recording
第 2 段說一組藝人募到 10 萬英鎊（£100,000），籌資程序就完成了，這筆錢用來支付錄音的費用，第 1 段 SVM 的例子也是 10 萬英鎊，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 £10、(B) 照抄 £1,000，10 到 1,000 英鎊是每位用戶可以投資的金額；(C) 照抄 £4,250，那是一位法國歌迷投資的金額。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about MMC?
options: It has helped many do-it-yourself musicians get to the Top 200.
There are works of fourteen artists posted at a time on its website.
It allows fans to provide financial support to the musicians they like.
The biggest share of its profits from a crowd-funding project goes to the musician.
items.explanation:
users are invited to invest from £10 to £1,000 in the ones they most enjoy
第 2 段說 MMC 邀請用戶投資（invest）他們最喜歡的藝人（the ones they most enjoy），選項換成 provide financial support to the musicians they like，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 Top 200，只有 14 組自己動手做的藝人擠進前 200 名，那是 2009 年美國的整體情況，原文沒有說和 MMC 有關；(B) MMC 網站上放的是 10 組藝人，14 是擠進前 200 名的組數；(D) 收益分配是投資人和 MMC 各 40%，藝人只拿 20%，藝人拿得最少。

items.stem: What does the author mean by “success is still a long shot” in the fourth paragraph?
options: Success is not easy to achieve.
Success often starts with one big shot.
Success should be every musician’s long-term goal.
items.explanation:
Out of the 20,000 records released in the U.S. in 2009, only 14 DIY acts made it to the Top 200.
a long shot 是「希望渺茫的事」。這一句用 While 對比：雖然數位科技讓音樂人掀起自己動手做的風潮，要成功仍然……；下一句接著說，2009 年美國發行的兩萬張唱片中，只有 14 組自己動手做的藝人擠進前 200 名。成功的比例這麼低，可見成功並不容易，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 shot、(D) 照抄 long，都是把片語拆開來照字面解釋；(A) 成功的效果持久，和下一句的數字接不上。

閱讀測驗.title: 法貝熱彩蛋的歷史與象徵意義（History and Symbolic Meaning of Fabergé Eggs）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Fabergé eggs are jeweled eggs that were made by the famous Russian jeweler, the House of Fabergé, from 1885 to 1917. The eggs were made of valuable metals or stones coated with beautiful colors and decorated with precious jewels.

The first Fabergé egg was crafted for Tsar Alexander III, who gave his wife, the Empress Maria Fedorovna, an Easter egg to celebrate their 20th wedding anniversary. He placed an order with a young jeweler, Peter Carl Fabergé, whose beautiful creations had caught Maria’s eye earlier. On Easter morning of 1885, what appeared to be a simple enameled egg was delivered to the palace. But to the delight of the Empress, the egg opened to a golden yolk; within the yolk was a golden hen; and concealed within the hen was a diamond miniature of the royal crown and a tiny ruby egg. Unfortunately, the last two surprises are now lost to history.

Empress Maria was so delighted by this gift that Alexander appointed Fabergé a “goldsmith by special appointment to the Imperial Crown.” The Tsar also asked Fabergé to make an Easter egg every year. The requirements were straightforward: Each egg must be unique, and each must contain a pleasant surprise. With excellent craftsmanship and an inventive spirit, Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge. The House of Fabergé made approximately 50 Imperial Easter Eggs for Tsar Alexander III and his son Nicholas II until 1917, when the Russian revolution broke out.

Today, the term “Fabergé eggs” has become a synonym of luxury and the eggs are regarded as masterpieces of the jeweler’s art. More significantly, perhaps, they serve as reminders of the last Russian imperial family.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
法貝熱彩蛋是俄國著名的珠寶商法貝熱公司（the House of Fabergé）在 1885 年到 1917 年間製作的珠寶蛋。這些彩蛋用貴重的金屬或寶石做成，塗上美麗的色彩，再鑲上珍貴的珠寶。

第一顆法貝熱彩蛋，是替沙皇亞歷山大三世製作的。沙皇為了慶祝結婚 20 週年，要送妻子瑪麗亞皇后一顆復活節彩蛋。他向年輕的珠寶師 Peter Carl Fabergé 訂製，這位珠寶師美麗的作品，先前就吸引了瑪麗亞的目光。1885 年復活節早上，一顆看起來像是普通琺瑯蛋的彩蛋送進了宮。不過，讓皇后驚喜的是，蛋打開來，裡面是一顆金蛋黃；蛋黃裡有一隻金母雞；母雞裡還藏著一頂鑽石做的小皇冠和一顆小小的紅寶石蛋。可惜的是，最後這兩樣驚喜如今已經失傳。

瑪麗亞皇后非常喜歡這份禮物，亞歷山大於是任命法貝熱為「皇室特約金匠」。沙皇也要法貝熱每年做一顆復活節彩蛋。要求很簡單：每一顆彩蛋都必須獨一無二，每一顆都要藏著令人驚喜的東西。憑著精湛的工藝和創新的精神，Peter Fabergé 和他的繼承人一次又一次達成了這項挑戰。法貝熱公司替沙皇亞歷山大三世和他的兒子尼古拉二世，做了大約 50 顆皇室復活節彩蛋，一直到 1917 年俄國革命爆發為止。

如今，「法貝熱彩蛋」已經成為奢華的代名詞，這些彩蛋公認是珠寶藝術的傑作。或許更重要的是，這些彩蛋讓人想起俄國最後的皇室。

items.stem: Why did Tsar Alexander III choose Peter Fabergé to make the first Easter egg?
options: Peter Fabergé was the goldsmith for the royal family.
Empress Maria was impressed by Peter Fabergé’s work.
Tsar Alexander III received an order from Empress Maria.
Peter Fabergé owned the most famous Russian jewelry house.
items.explanation:
whose beautiful creations had caught Maria
第 2 段說沙皇向年輕的珠寶師 Peter Carl Fabergé 訂製，因為他美麗的作品（beautiful creations）先前就吸引了（had caught）瑪麗亞的目光，選項換成 Empress Maria was impressed by Peter Fabergé’s work，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 goldsmith，法貝熱是在第一顆彩蛋讓皇后滿意以後，才獲得皇室特約金匠的頭銜；(C) 照抄 order，下訂單的是沙皇，選項說沙皇接到皇后的訂單，說反了；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 famous Russian，法貝熱公司是後來才成為著名的珠寶商，沙皇訂製時，第 2 段說他還是年輕的珠寶師。

items.stem: What went missing from the first Fabergé egg?
options: A golden hen and a ruby egg.
A golden hen and a golden yolk.
A ruby egg and a diamond crown.
A golden yolk and a diamond crown.
items.explanation:
concealed within the hen was a diamond miniature of the royal crown and a tiny ruby egg.
Unfortunately, the last two surprises are now lost to history.
第 2 段依序說蛋打開來是金蛋黃，蛋黃裡有金母雞，母雞裡藏著鑽石小皇冠（a diamond miniature of the royal crown）和紅寶石小蛋（a tiny ruby egg），接著說最後兩樣驚喜（the last two surprises）已經失傳。最後兩樣就是鑽石皇冠和紅寶石蛋，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 golden hen、(B) 和 (D) 照抄 golden yolk，金母雞和金蛋黃是前面兩樣，沒有失傳。

items.stem: What does it mean by “Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge” in the third paragraph?
options: They repeated their designs over and over.
They fulfilled the Tsar’s requirements each time.
They challenged the Tsar’s expectations every year.
They were faced with unexpected difficulties time and again.
items.explanation:
The requirements were straightforward: Each egg must be unique, and each must contain a pleasant surprise.
Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge.
這裡的 meet 不是「遇到」，而是「達成、符合」，meet the challenge 是成功應付挑戰。the challenge 指的是前一句沙皇的要求（The requirements）：每一顆彩蛋都必須獨一無二，而且要藏著驚喜；repeatedly 是每年一次又一次。合起來就是法貝熱和繼承人每一次都做到了沙皇的要求，所以是 (B)。(D) 把 meet 當成「遇到」，又把 challenge 當成困難，照字面解釋；(C) 照抄 challenge，挑戰是沙皇給法貝熱的，選項說法貝熱挑戰沙皇，主客顛倒；(A) 照抄 repeated，原文要求每顆彩蛋都獨一無二，不可能重複同樣的設計。

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the Fabergé eggs is true, according to the passage?
options: They were all genuine creations of the jeweler, Peter Fabergé.
They were created to represent Russian emperors and their dynasty.
They were made for annual Easter parties in the Russian imperial court.
They were connected to the last two Russian emperors and their families.
items.explanation:
for Tsar Alexander III and his son Nicholas II until 1917, when the Russian revolution broke out.
they serve as reminders of the last Russian imperial family.
這一題要把兩段合起來看。第 3 段說法貝熱公司替沙皇亞歷山大三世和他的兒子尼古拉二世做彩蛋，一直到 1917 年俄國革命爆發為止；第 4 段說這些彩蛋讓人想起俄國最後的皇室。革命以後俄國就沒有沙皇了，所以這兩位是俄國最後兩位皇帝，彩蛋又是送給皇后等家人的禮物，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 Peter Fabergé，第 3 段說彩蛋是他和他的繼承人（his successors）做的，不全是他本人的作品；(C) 照抄 Easter，彩蛋是復活節送給皇后的禮物，原文沒有說是為宮廷的復活節派對做的；(B) 讓人想起俄國最後的皇室，是彩蛋今天的意義，彩蛋當初是沙皇送皇后的禮物，不是為了代表皇帝和王朝而做。

閱讀測驗.title: 蜘蛛網的構造與絲線特性（Structure and Silk Thread Characteristics of Spider Webs）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Spider webs are one of the most fascinating examples of animal architecture. The most beautiful and structurally ordered are the orb webs. The main function of the web is to intercept and hold flying prey, such as flies, bees and other insects, long enough for the spider to catch them. In order to do so, the threads of the web have to withstand the impact forces from large and heavy prey as well as environmental forces from wind and rain for at least a day in most cases.

The orb web is found to have two main characteristics. The first is its geometry, which consists of an outer frame and a central part from which threads radiate outward. Enclosed in the frame are capture spirals winding round and round from the web center out to the frame. The whole web is in tension and held in place by anchor threads, which connect the frame to the surrounding vegetation or objects. The second and perhaps most important characteristic is the material with which it is built. Spider silk is a kind of natural composite that gives this lightweight fiber a tensile strength comparable to that of steel, while at the same time making it very elastic. Two types of silk threads are used in the web. One is highly elastic and can stretch to almost twice its original length before breaking and, for most types of spiders, is covered in glue. This type is used in the capture spiral for catching and holding prey. The other is stiffer and stronger, and is used for the radius, frames and anchor threads, which allows the web to withstand prey impact and to keep its structural strength through a wide range of environmental conditions.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
蜘蛛網是動物建築中最迷人的例子之一，其中最美麗、結構最有秩序的，是圓網。蜘蛛網的主要功能，是攔住並困住蒼蠅、蜜蜂和其他昆蟲等飛行的獵物，讓蜘蛛有足夠的時間把獵物抓住。為了做到這一點，蜘蛛網的絲必須承受又大又重的獵物撞上來的衝擊力，也要承受風雨等環境的力量，大多數情況下，至少要維持一天。

研究發現，圓網有兩大特點。第一是它的幾何結構，由一個外框和一個中心組成，絲從中心向外放射。外框裡圍著捕獵螺旋，從網的中心一圈又一圈繞到外框。整張網處在繃緊的狀態，靠固定絲（anchor threads）固定在原位，固定絲把外框繫在周圍的植物或物體上。第二個特點，也可能是最重要的特點，是建造蜘蛛網的材料。蜘蛛絲是一種天然的複合材料，這種輕盈的纖維，抗拉強度和鋼差不多，同時又非常有彈性。蜘蛛網用了兩種絲。一種彈性很高，可以拉長到將近原來的兩倍才斷，大多數種類的蜘蛛，還會在這種絲上塗上黏液。這種絲用在捕獵螺旋上，用來捕捉並困住獵物。另一種絲比較硬、比較強韌，用在輻射絲、外框和固定絲上，讓蜘蛛網承受得住獵物的撞擊，在各種環境條件下都能保持結構的強度。

items.stem: What is this passage mainly about?
options: The environmental challenges for spider webs.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說圓網是最美、結構最有秩序的蜘蛛網，並說明網的功能；第 2 段介紹圓網的兩大特點：幾何結構和建造的材料。全文講的是圓網怎麼構成，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 environmental，網要承受風雨，只是第 1 段說明網絲需要多強韌，過於狹隘；(A) 蜘蛛網的功能是捕捉獵物，但全文沒有談自然界的食物網，偏離主題；(C) 第 2 段的幾何結構是在描述網的形狀，不是談幾何學的研究，偏離主題。

items.stem: What does the word “so” in the first paragraph refer to?
options: To catch and keep small creatures.
To find a good material for the web.
To observe the behavior patterns of spiders.
To present a fantastic architecture by animals.
items.explanation:
The main function of the web is to intercept and hold flying prey
In order to do so 的 do so 指的是前一句說的事：蜘蛛網的主要功能是攔住並困住（intercept and hold）蒼蠅、蜜蜂等飛行的獵物，讓蜘蛛有時間抓住。選項把飛行的獵物換成 small creatures，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 architecture，動物建築是第 1 段第一句的開場；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 material，網的材料是後面才談的特點；(C) 原文沒有提到觀察蜘蛛的行為。

items.stem: Which part of the web is used for supporting the web itself?
items.explanation:
The whole web is in tension and held in place by anchor threads, which connect the frame to the surrounding vegetation or objects.
第 2 段說整張網靠固定絲（anchor threads）固定在原位，固定絲把外框繫在周圍的植物或物體上；後面也說比較強韌的那種絲用在固定絲上。讓整張網維持在原位的是固定絲，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 capture spiral，捕獵螺旋是用來捕捉並困住獵物的；(B) 照抄 glue，黏液塗在捕獵螺旋的絲上，作用也是黏住獵物；(A) 照抄 center，網的中心是放射絲的起點，原文沒有說網靠中心固定。

items.stem: According to the passage, which statement is true about the silk threads?
options: They are all sticky and extendable.
They are usually strong enough to last for a day.
They remove harmful chemicals from insects.
They are made of rare plants in the environment.
items.explanation:
the threads of the web have to withstand the impact forces from large and heavy prey as well as environmental forces from wind and rain for at least a day in most cases.
題目問的是網絲（silk threads），答案在第 1 段：網絲必須承受獵物撞擊和風雨的力量，大多數情況下（in most cases）至少要維持一天（for at least a day）。選項把 in most cases 換成 usually，把承受得住、維持一天換成 strong enough to last for a day，所以是 (B)。(A) 的 all 是陷阱：第 2 段說蜘蛛網用了兩種絲，只有捕獵螺旋那一種有彈性、塗了黏液，另一種比較硬，不是全部的絲都會黏、都能拉長；(D) 第 2 段的植物（vegetation）是固定絲繫住的地方，蜘蛛絲是天然的複合材料，原文沒有說是用稀有植物做的；(C) 原文沒有提到去除昆蟲身上的化學物質。

閱讀測驗.title: 以基因改造蚊子對抗瘧疾（Genetically Modified Mosquitoes against Malaria）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Scientists are trying to genetically modify the world in which we live. They are even trying to wipe out diseases via genetic modification. For example, researchers have tried to engineer mosquitoes to kill malaria parasites. The malaria parasite is carried by the female Anopheles mosquito. When transmitted to a human, the parasite travels first to the liver and then on to the bloodstream, where it reproduces and destroys red blood cells. An estimated 250 million people suffer from malaria each year, and about one million die—many of them children. There are currently no effective or approved malaria vaccines.

To “kill” malaria, scientists are genetically modifying a bacterium in mosquitoes so that it releases toxic compounds. These compounds are not harmful to humans or the mosquito itself, but they do kill off the malaria parasite, making the mosquito incapable of infecting humans with malaria.

Despite this achievement, scientists are faced with the challenge of giving the modified mosquitoes a competitive advantage so that they can eventually replace the wild population. Complete blockage of the malaria parasite is very important. If some of the parasites slip through the mechanism, then the next generation will likely become resistant to it. And if that happens, the scientists are back where they started.

Another challenge for scientists is to gain public approval for this genetic modification regarding mosquitoes and malaria control. Environmental activists have raised concerns about the release of genetically engineered organisms without any clear knowledge of their long-term effect on ecosystems and human health. There is still a long way to go before genetic modification techniques are put to use in disease control.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
科學家正嘗試用基因改造來改變我們生活的世界，甚至想透過基因改造消滅疾病。例如，研究人員曾嘗試改造蚊子，讓蚊子殺死瘧疾寄生蟲。瘧疾寄生蟲由雌性瘧蚊攜帶。寄生蟲傳到人身上以後，先到肝臟，再進入血液，在血液裡繁殖，破壞紅血球。每年估計有 2.5 億人感染瘧疾，大約一百萬人死亡，其中有很多是兒童。目前還沒有有效、或經過核准的瘧疾疫苗。

為了「殺死」瘧疾，科學家正在改造蚊子體內的一種細菌，讓這種細菌釋放有毒的化合物。這些化合物對人和蚊子本身都無害，卻能殺死瘧疾寄生蟲，讓蚊子無法把瘧疾傳給人。

儘管有這項成果，科學家還要面對一個挑戰：讓改造過的蚊子具有競爭優勢，最後能取代野生的蚊子。完全阻斷瘧疾寄生蟲非常重要。要是有一些寄生蟲從這個機制中漏網，下一代很可能就會產生抗性。一旦發生這種情況，科學家就得從頭來過。

科學家的另一個挑戰，是讓大眾認同這項針對蚊子和瘧疾防治的基因改造。環保人士提出疑慮，擔心在還不清楚基因改造生物對生態系和人體健康有什麼長期影響的情況下，就把它們野放出去。基因改造技術要用在疾病防治上，還有很長的路要走。

items.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: Researchers have found an effective way to halt the spread of insect-borne diseases around the world.
Many people are worried about the effects of genetically modified organisms on the environment.
It takes time to gain public support for the application of genetic modification to disease control.
Genetic engineering looks promising in reducing malaria, though there may be unknown consequences.
items.explanation: 先看全文怎麼安排：第 1 段說瘧疾每年造成大約一百萬人死亡，還沒有有效的疫苗；第 2 段說科學家改造蚊子體內的細菌，讓蚊子無法傳播瘧疾；第 3、4 段說還有兩個挑戰，包括基因改造生物的長期影響還不清楚。主旨要同時說出這個方法有希望，也還有隱憂，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (A)，這個選項照抄第 1 段的 effective：原文只談瘧疾，不是全世界所有由蚊蟲傳播的疾病，而且第 3、4 段說還有很多挑戰，說已經找到有效的方法，說得太絕對，太過廣泛。(B) 照抄 environment、(C) 照抄 public，環保人士的疑慮和爭取大眾認同，都只是第 4 段的內容，過於狹隘。

items.stem: Which of the following best shows the organization of this passage?
items.explanation: 第 1 段說瘧疾每年造成大約一百萬人死亡，又沒有有效的疫苗，這是問題（Problem）；第 2 段說科學家改造蚊子體內的細菌，殺死瘧疾寄生蟲，這是解決方法（Solution）；第 3 段用 Despite this achievement 帶出第一個挑戰，第 4 段用 Another challenge 帶出第二個挑戰，這是可能遇到的困難（Potential difficulties）。所以是 (B)。(A) 全文沒有比較和對照；(C) 原文沒有正反兩方的辯論，第 4 段環保人士的疑慮是挑戰之一；(D) 第 1 段不是在下定義，最後也沒有暫時的結論。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about malaria parasites?
options: They are resistant to genetic modification and vaccines.
They reproduce in the human liver and grow stronger there.
They can be found in only one gender of a class of mosquitoes.
They are transmitted to around one million children each year.
items.explanation:
The malaria parasite is carried by the female Anopheles mosquito.
第 1 段說瘧疾寄生蟲由雌性（female）瘧蚊（Anopheles mosquito）攜帶。female 是一種性別（one gender），Anopheles 是蚊子裡的一類（a class of mosquitoes），所以只有一種性別的某一類蚊子身上有瘧疾寄生蟲，是 (C)。(B) 照抄 liver，寄生蟲先到肝臟，接著進入血液，在血液裡繁殖；(D) 照抄 one million，每年大約一百萬人死於瘧疾，其中很多是兒童，不是每年傳給一百萬名兒童；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 resistant，原文說下一代寄生蟲可能會對改造的機制產生抗性，這是還沒發生的情況，沒有疫苗也不表示寄生蟲對疫苗有抗性。

items.stem: What does “that” in the third paragraph refer to?
options: Some malaria parasites escaping from the ecosystems.
Malaria parasites becoming immune to the engineered bacterium.
Modified mosquitoes becoming more competitive than the wild ones.
Transmission of malaria being blocked from mosquitoes to humans.
items.explanation:
If some of the parasites slip through the mechanism, then the next generation will likely become resistant to it.
that 指前一句說的情況：要是有寄生蟲從這個機制漏網，下一代寄生蟲很可能對它產生抗性（become resistant to it）。句中的 it 指 the mechanism，也就是第 2 段說的方法，改造蚊子體內的細菌來殺死寄生蟲。選項把 resistant 換成 immune，把這個機制換成 the engineered bacterium，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 competitive，讓改造蚊子更有競爭力是科學家要達成的目標，如果做到了，不會「從頭來過」；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 ecosystems，生態系是環保人士擔心的事情，而且原文說的是寄生蟲從機制中漏網，不是從生態系逃走；(D) 阻斷瘧疾從蚊子傳給人，是第 2 段的成果，也不會讓科學家從頭來過。

閱讀測驗.title: 德萊斯的滑行車與自行車的起源（Karl Drais’s Running Machine and the Origin of the Bicycle）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Born in 1785 in southwestern Germany, Baron Karl Drais was one of the most creative German inventors of the 19th century. The baron’s numerous inventions include, among others, the earliest typewriter, the meat grinder, a device to record piano music on paper, and two four-wheeled human-powered vehicles. But it was the running machine, the modern ancestor of the bicycle, that made him famous.

The running machine, also called Draisine or hobby horse, was in effect a very primitive bicycle: it had no chains and was propelled by riders pushing off the ground with their feet. Though not a bike in the modern sense of the word, Drais’ invention marked the big bang for the bicycle’s development. It was the first vehicle with two wheels placed in line. The frame and wheels were made of wood; the steering already resembled a modern handlebar. Drais’ big democratic idea behind his invention was to find a muscle-powered replacement for the horses, which were expensive and consumed lots of food even when not in use. The machine, he believed, would allow large numbers of people faster movement than walking or riding in a coach.

Drais undertook his first documented ride on June 12, 1817, covering a distance of 13 kilometers in one hour. A few months later, Drais created a huge sensation when he rode 60 kilometers in four hours. These were later followed by a marketing trip to Paris, where the hobby horse quickly caught on. The fad also quickly spread to Britain.

The success of the hobby horse was short-lived, though. They were heavy and difficult to ride. Safety was an issue, too: They lacked a brake, as well as cranks and pedals. There were frequent collisions with unsuspecting pedestrians, and after a few years Drais’ invention was banned in many European and American cities. Drais’ ideas, however, did not disappear entirely. Decades later, the machine was equipped by Frenchmen Pierre Lallement and Pierre Michaux with pedals to become the modern bicycle.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
德萊斯男爵（Baron Karl Drais）1785 年生於德國西南部，是 19 世紀德國最有創意的發明家之一。他的發明很多，包括最早的打字機、絞肉機、一種把鋼琴音樂記錄在紙上的裝置，還有兩種用人力推動的四輪車。不過，讓他成名的，是現代自行車的始祖：滑行車（running machine）。

滑行車又叫 Draisine 或 hobby horse，其實就是一種非常原始的自行車：沒有鏈條，靠騎的人用腳蹬地前進。雖然不是現代意義上的自行車，德萊斯的發明卻是自行車發展的重大起點。滑行車是第一輛兩個輪子前後排成一直線的車。車架和輪子都是木頭做的，轉向裝置已經很像現代的把手。德萊斯發明滑行車，背後有一個讓一般大眾都能受益的遠大構想：找一種靠人力的交通工具來取代馬，因為馬很貴，不用的時候也要吃很多飼料。他認為，這種車能讓許多人移動得比走路或坐馬車更快。

1817 年 6 月 12 日，德萊斯第一次有紀錄的試騎，一個小時騎了 13 公里。幾個月後，他四個小時騎了 60 公里，轟動一時。之後他到巴黎推銷，滑行車很快就在巴黎流行起來，這股熱潮也很快傳到英國。

不過，滑行車的成功很短暫。這種車很重，也很難騎。安全也是問題：沒有煞車，也沒有曲柄和踏板。滑行車常常撞上沒有防備的行人，幾年以後，歐洲和美國的許多城市都禁止使用德萊斯的發明。然而，德萊斯的構想並沒有完全消失。數十年後，法國人 Pierre Lallement 和 Pierre Michaux 替滑行車裝上踏板，成了現代的自行車。

items.stem: Why did Drais invent the running machine?
options: To prove his creativity as an inventor.
To protect the horses from being abused.
To provide a new gadget for the royal class.
To give the general public a better means of transportation.
items.explanation:
to find a muscle-powered replacement for the horses
The machine, he believed, would allow large numbers of people faster movement than walking or riding in a coach.
第 2 段說德萊斯的構想是讓一般大眾受益（big democratic idea）：找一種靠人力的交通工具取代昂貴的馬，讓許多人（large numbers of people）移動得比走路或坐馬車更快。選項換成 give the general public a better means of transportation，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 horses，原文說要取代馬，是因為馬很貴、很會吃，不是為了保護馬不受虐待；(A) 第 1 段說他是很有創意的發明家，但那是作者的介紹，不是他發明滑行車的理由；(C) 原文說的是讓大眾受益，不是替貴族做新玩意兒。

items.stem: What does “marked the big bang” mean in the second paragraph?
items.explanation:
Though not a bike in the modern sense of the word
It was the first vehicle with two wheels placed in line.
big bang 原本指宇宙的大霹靂，也就是宇宙的起點；mark 是「標誌著」。這一句用 Though 讓步：雖然滑行車不是現代意義上的自行車，卻標誌著自行車發展的 big bang。下一句接著說，滑行車是第一輛兩個輪子前後排成一直線的車。這是開創性的成就，所以是 (D)。(A) 把 bang 照字面當成巨響；(B) 第 4 段滑行車常撞上行人，那是後來的事，不是這一句的意思；(C) 滑行車在巴黎流行是第 3 段的事，big bang 說的是開創，不是受歡迎。

items.stem: Which of the following descriptions is true about the running machine?
options: It was equipped with cranks and pedals.
Its wheels and frame were made of iron.
It had a brake to control the speed of its movement.
Its steering was similar to the handlebar of a modern bike.
items.explanation:
the steering already resembled a modern handlebar.
第 2 段說滑行車的轉向裝置已經很像（resembled）現代的把手，選項換成 was similar to the handlebar of a modern bike，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 cranks and pedals、(C) 照抄 brake，第 4 段說滑行車沒有煞車，也沒有曲柄和踏板（lacked），選項說反了；(B) 照抄 frame，第 2 段說車架和輪子都是木頭做的，不是鐵。

items.stem: Why did the hobby horse fail to become a common vehicle in the 19th century?
options: It was expensive and not durable enough.
It did not go as fast as people had expected.
It was hard to control and dangerous to ride on the road.
It did not receive enough public attention in European cities.
items.explanation:
They were heavy and difficult to ride.
There were frequent collisions with unsuspecting pedestrians
第 4 段說滑行車很重，也很難騎（difficult to ride），而且沒有煞車，常常撞上行人，安全是問題，所以許多城市禁止使用。選項換成 hard to control and dangerous to ride on the road，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 expensive，昂貴的是馬，滑行車是要取代馬的交通工具；(D) 照抄 European，歐洲城市禁止使用，是因為太危險，不是沒人注意，第 3 段還說滑行車在巴黎很快流行起來；(B) 第 3 段說德萊斯四個小時騎了 60 公里，轟動一時，原文沒有說速度不如預期。

閱讀測驗.title: Li-Fi技術的優勢與應用（Advantages and Applications of Li-Fi Technology）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Flickering lamps can induce headaches. But if the flickering happens millions of times a second—far faster than the eye can see or the brain process—then it might be harnessed to do something useful, like transmitting data. This is the idea behind Li-Fi, or Light Fidelity. The term Li-Fi was coined by University of Edinburgh Professor Harald Haas in a 2011 TED Talk, where he introduced the idea of “wireless data from every light.” Today, Li-Fi has developed into a wireless technology that allows data to be sent at high speeds, working with light-emitting diodes (LEDs), an increasingly popular way to illuminate public areas and homes.

Using LED lights as networking devices for data transmission, Li-Fi has several advantages over Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity). First, Li-Fi allows for greater security on local networks, as light cannot penetrate walls or doors, unlike radio waves used in Wi-Fi. As long as transparent materials like glass windows are covered, access to a Li-Fi channel is limited to devices inside the room, ensuring that signals cannot be hacked from remote locations. Also, Li-Fi can operate in electromagnetic sensitive areas such as aircraft cabins, hospitals, and nuclear power plants, for light does not interfere with radio signals. The most significant advantage of Li-Fi is speed. Researchers have achieved speeds of 224 gigabits per second in lab conditions, much faster than Wi-Fi broadband.

How could Li-Fi enrich daily life? Anywhere there is LED lighting, there is an opportunity for Li-Fi enabled applications. Li-Fi-enabled street lights could provide internet access to mobile phones, making walking at night safer. The LED bulbs in traffic lights could provide drivers with weather conditions and traffic updates. Li-Fi could help with tourism by providing an easier access to local information. At home, smart light could also provide parents with solutions to their children’s Internet addiction: Just turn off the lights and you’ve turned off their access.

When 14 billion light bulbs mean 14 billion potential transmitters of wireless data, a cleaner, a greener, and even a brighter future is on the way.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
閃爍的燈會讓人頭痛。不過，如果燈一秒鐘閃爍幾百萬次，遠遠快過眼睛看得到、大腦處理得了的速度，也許就能用來做有用的事，例如傳輸資料。這就是 Li-Fi（Light Fidelity，光照上網）背後的構想。Li-Fi 這個名詞，是愛丁堡大學的 Harald Haas 教授在 2011 年的一場 TED 演講中創造的，他在演講中提出「每一盞燈都能傳送無線資料」的構想。今天，Li-Fi 已經發展成一種能高速傳送資料的無線技術，搭配的是發光二極體（LED），LED 也越來越常用來照明公共場所和住家。

Li-Fi 用 LED 燈當作傳輸資料的網路裝置，比起 Wi-Fi（Wireless Fidelity，無線上網）有幾項優勢。第一，Li-Fi 讓區域網路更安全，因為光線穿不透牆壁或門，不像 Wi-Fi 用的無線電波。只要把玻璃窗等透明的材料遮住，能連上 Li-Fi 頻道的，就只有房間裡的裝置，可以確保訊號不會從遠端遭到駭客入侵。第二，Li-Fi 可以在對電磁敏感的地方運作，例如機艙、醫院和核電廠，因為光線不會干擾無線電訊號。Li-Fi 最大的優勢是速度。研究人員在實驗室的條件下，已經達到每秒 224 gigabits 的速度，比 Wi-Fi 寬頻快得多。

Li-Fi 能怎樣豐富日常生活呢？只要有 LED 照明的地方，就有機會應用 Li-Fi。能使用 Li-Fi 的路燈，可以讓手機上網，夜間走路也就更安全。紅綠燈裡的 LED 燈泡，可以提供駕駛天氣狀況和最新路況。Li-Fi 能讓人更容易取得當地的資訊，對觀光也有幫助。在家裡，智慧燈光還能幫家長解決孩子網路成癮的問題：只要把燈關掉，孩子就上不了網。

當 140 億顆燈泡代表 140 億個可能的無線資料發射器，一個更乾淨、更環保，甚至更光明的未來，就快到來了。

items.stem: What is this passage mainly about?
options: Potential applications of Li-Fi for military use.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說燈光每秒閃爍幾百萬次，就能用來傳輸資料，這就是 Li-Fi；第 2 段說 Li-Fi 比 Wi-Fi 安全、快速；第 3 段說 Li-Fi 在日常生活中的應用；第 4 段展望未來。Li-Fi 就是用照明的燈光（illumination）來無線傳輸資料，所以是 (B)。最容易選錯的是 (A)，這個選項照抄第 3 段的 lighting：原文用的是已經越來越普遍的 LED 燈，重點是用燈光傳資料，不是新的照明設計，偏離主題。(C) 照抄第 1 段的 public areas，不干擾無線電訊號只是第 2 段說的優勢之一，過於狹隘；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 applications，原文舉的應用是路燈、紅綠燈、觀光和家庭，沒有提到軍事用途，偏離主題。

items.stem: What does “This” in the first paragraph refer to?
options: The brain can be affected by lighting.
Human eyes can perceive changes in light.
items.explanation:
then it might be harnessed to do something useful, like transmitting data.
This is the idea behind Li-Fi 的 This，指的是前一句說的構想：如果燈一秒鐘閃爍幾百萬次，就能用來做有用的事，例如傳輸資料（transmitting data）。選項換成 Light flashes can deliver messages，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 Flickering，閃爍的燈讓人頭痛是第一句，接著用 But 轉到 Li-Fi 的構想；(C) 照抄 brain、(D) 照抄 eye，原文說閃爍的速度快過眼睛看得到、大腦處理得了的範圍，正好是說眼睛和大腦察覺不到。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is NOT true about Li-Fi?
options: It transmits data at high speed.
items.explanation:
light cannot penetrate walls or doors
第 2 段說光線穿不透牆壁或門（light cannot penetrate walls or doors），Li-Fi 才比較安全，所以說 Li-Fi 能穿過水泥牆，和原文不符，選 (A)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：第 1 段說 Li-Fi 這個名詞是 2011 年在 TED 演講中提出的，是 (B)；第 2 段說 Li-Fi 最大的優勢是速度，是 (C)；第 3 段說家長只要關燈，孩子就上不了網，是 (D)。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is an advantage of Li-Fi over Wi-Fi?
options: Li-Fi can be powered by radio and save more energy.
Li-Fi guides pedestrians in areas where vehicles cannot travel.
Li-Fi provides safer transmission of data during a power failure.
Li-Fi can be used in areas where Wi-Fi may interfere with radar signals.
items.explanation:
Li-Fi can operate in electromagnetic sensitive areas such as aircraft cabins, hospitals, and nuclear power plants, for light does not interfere with radio signals.
第 2 段說 Li-Fi 可以在機艙、醫院、核電廠等對電磁敏感的地方運作，因為光線不會干擾無線電訊號（does not interfere with radio signals）；Wi-Fi 用的是無線電波，就可能造成干擾。選項說 Li-Fi 可以用在 Wi-Fi 可能干擾雷達訊號的地方，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 radio，原文說 Li-Fi 用的是 LED 燈的光，無線電波是 Wi-Fi 用的；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 safer，那是說路燈讓人夜間走路更安全，而且 Li-Fi 要靠燈光，停電時燈不亮，就無法傳輸；(B) 第 3 段說路燈讓手機上網、夜間走路更安全，沒有說 Li-Fi 能替行人引路。

閱讀測驗.title: 氣候變暖讓大型甲蟲變小（Large Beetles Shrinking with Climate Warming）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Some of the world’s largest beetles are getting smaller because their habitats are warming up, according to new research from the University of British Columbia, Canada. The study, published in the Journal of Animal Ecology in January 2018, shows that climate change is having an impact on these “teeny tiny” organisms.

The study began with a deep dive into the scientific literature. Evolutionary ecologist Michelle Tseng and her students combed through all the articles they could find, looking for laboratory studies of temperature effects on insects. They found 19 that indicated at least 22 beetle species shrank when raised in warmer than normal temperatures.

To see whether this pattern held true in the wild, the team made use of the university’s 600,000-specimen insect collection, which included thousands of bugs collected locally since the late 1800s. The researchers took photographs of more than 6,500 beetles from the eight species with the most extensive records. They also looked at climate records to determine trends in rainfall and other factors besides temperature. Sorting the beetles into size categories, they found that five of the eight species have shrunk over the past century. The four largest species of beetles, including the snail-killer ground beetles, shrank 20% in the past 45 years. In contrast, smaller beetles were unaffected or even slightly increased in size.

Some ecologists are cautious about Tseng’s findings, saying that it hasn’t yet been proved whether the warming temperatures are the actual cause for the beetle shrinkage. UK biologist Alan Ronan Baudron, however, is convinced. Baudron’s studies have documented shrinkage of certain fish species due to climate warming. His account is that warmer temperatures lower the concentration of oxygen in the water, causing fish to burn energy faster and mature at a smaller size. But neither he nor Tseng is convinced that decreased oxygen can explain the shrinkage in the beetles.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
根據加拿大英屬哥倫比亞大學的新研究，世界上一些最大型的甲蟲正在變小，因為牠們的棲地正在變暖。這項研究 2018 年 1 月發表在《動物生態學期刊》（Journal of Animal Ecology），顯示氣候變遷正在影響這些「小不點」生物。

這項研究從深入查閱科學文獻開始。演化生態學家 Michelle Tseng 和她的學生，把找得到的論文全部仔細看過一遍，尋找探討溫度對昆蟲影響的實驗室研究。他們找到 19 篇，顯示至少有 22 種甲蟲在比正常溫暖的環境中飼養時，體型會縮小。

為了確認野外是不是也有這種現象，研究團隊利用學校收藏的 60 萬件昆蟲標本，其中包括 1800 年代末以來在當地採集的數千隻蟲子。研究人員從紀錄最完整的 8 個物種中，拍攝了超過 6,500 隻甲蟲的照片。他們也查看氣候紀錄，找出降雨量等溫度以外其他因素的變化趨勢。研究人員把甲蟲依體型分類，發現 8 種甲蟲中有 5 種在過去一百年縮小了。最大的 4 種甲蟲，包括捕食蝸牛的步行蟲，在過去 45 年縮小了 20%。相反地，比較小的甲蟲沒有受到影響，體型甚至還稍微變大。

有些生態學家對 Tseng 的發現持保留態度，他們說，還沒有證明暖化就是甲蟲縮小的真正原因。不過，英國生物學家 Alan Ronan Baudron 對此深信不疑。Baudron 的研究記錄過某些魚類因為氣候暖化而縮小。他的解釋是，溫度升高讓水中的氧氣濃度降低，魚燃燒能量的速度變快，體型還比較小就成熟了。不過，他和 Tseng 都不認為氧氣減少能解釋甲蟲縮小的現象。

items.stem: What is the best title for the passage?
options: Large Beetles Are Shrinking, Thanks to Climate Change
Beetles vs. Fish: Are They Becoming Smaller?
What We Know About Evolutionary Ecology
items.explanation: 第 1 段第一句就點出主旨：世界上一些最大型的甲蟲正在變小，因為棲地變暖；第 2 段從實驗室研究的文獻、第 3 段從野外採集的標本找證據；第 4 段介紹其他學者的看法。標題要說出大型甲蟲因為氣候變遷而縮小，所以是 (A)，標題的 Thanks to 是「由於」。要注意的是「大型」：第 3 段說比較小的甲蟲沒有受到影響。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 Animal Ecology，那是刊登研究的期刊名稱，動物生態學的過去和現在，範圍太大，太過廣泛；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 Evolutionary，演化生態學是 Tseng 的專業領域，談這門學問也太過廣泛；(B) 照抄第 4 段的 fish，魚類縮小只是 Baudron 的研究，第 4 段拿來對照，過於狹隘。

items.stem: What does “a deep dive” most likely mean in the second paragraph?
items.explanation:
The study began with a deep dive into the scientific literature.
combed through all the articles they could find
dive 是潛水，deep dive 是潛到深處，比喻深入研究。從下一句也推得出來：Tseng 和學生把找得到的論文全部（all the articles they could find）仔細看過一遍，comb through 原本是用梳子梳過，比喻仔細翻查。全部論文都仔細翻查，就是徹底的檢視，所以是 (C)。(B) 重要的發現是查閱之後才找到的 19 篇研究，a deep dive 說的是查閱的過程；(A) 明確的跡象、(D) 有見地的評論，都和下一句的仔細翻查接不上。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about the research method of Tseng’s team?
options: They conducted both laboratory and field studies.
They took pictures of 600,000 specimens of insects.
They divided the beetles into different size groups for examination.
They recorded the degrees of oxygen concentration since the late 1800s.
items.explanation:
Sorting the beetles into size categories
第 3 段說研究人員把甲蟲依體型分類（Sorting the beetles into size categories），選項換成 divided the beetles into different size groups，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 laboratory，團隊是查閱別人做的實驗室研究，自己沒有做實驗；(B) 照抄 600,000，60 萬件是學校收藏的昆蟲標本總數，研究人員拍了照片的是 6,500 多隻甲蟲；(D) 照抄 since the late 1800s，1800 年代末以來採集的是昆蟲標本，記錄水中氧氣濃度的是第 4 段 Baudron 對魚類的研究。

items.stem: Which of the following is a finding of Tseng’s team?
options: Eight species of beetles have shrunk over the past century.
Some beetles were not affected by temperature change.
Most beetles tend to live longer with climate warming.
Beetles and fish may shrink down to the same size.
items.explanation:
In contrast, smaller beetles were unaffected or even slightly increased in size.
第 3 段說相反地，比較小的甲蟲沒有受到影響（unaffected），甚至體型還稍微變大，選項換成 Some beetles were not affected by temperature change，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 eight species，原文說 8 種中有 5 種縮小，不是 8 種都縮小；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 fish，魚類縮小是 Baudron 的研究，原文沒有說甲蟲和魚會縮到一樣大；(C) 原文談的是體型，沒有提到壽命。

閱讀測驗.title: 斯瓦巴全球種子庫的爭議（The Debate over the Svalbard Global Seed Vault）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In order to protect the diversity of crops from catastrophe, the Svalbard Global Seed Vault, a seed bank, was built beneath a mountain on an Arctic island halfway between Norway and the North Pole. The Vault is meant to help farmers and scientists find the genes they need to improve today’s crops. It also aims to breed varieties that might better respond to emerging challenges, such as climate change and population growth. Currently, the Vault holds more than 860,000 samples, originating from almost every country in the world.

There is now, however, a growing body of opinion that the world’s faith in Svalbard is misplaced. Those who have worked with farmers in the field say that diversity cannot be boxed up and saved in a single container—no matter how secure it may be. Crops are always changing, pests and diseases are always adapting, and global warming will bring additional challenges that remain unforeseen. In a perfect world, the solution would be as diverse and dynamic as plant life itself.

The dispute about how best to save crop diversity centers on whether we should work with communities in the fields or with institutions, since it will be extremely difficult to find enough funding to do both. Now the isolated Svalbard seed vault is sucking up available funding. Yet, the highly centralized approach may not be able to help farmers cope with climate change, fifty or a hundred years from now. According to new research findings, as much as 75 percent of global crop diversity exists outside the big institutional seed banks. Such diversity is held instead by some of the world’s most marginal farmers. Moreover, it is argued with increasing force that seed banks can neither make up for the practical knowledge of farmers on the ground, nor compete with their ingenuity.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
為了保護作物的多樣性，不受浩劫毀滅，斯瓦巴全球種子庫這座種子銀行，建在北極一座島嶼的山底下，這座島嶼位在挪威和北極點的中間。種子庫的用意，是幫助農民和科學家找到改良現有作物所需要的基因。種子庫也希望培育出更能因應新挑戰的品種，例如氣候變遷和人口成長。目前，種子庫保存了超過 86 萬份樣本，來自世界上幾乎每一個國家。

然而，現在有越來越多人認為，世界對斯瓦巴種子庫的信心放錯了地方。曾經在田間和農民一起工作的人說，多樣性沒辦法裝箱，存放在單一的容器裡，不管這個容器有多安全都一樣。作物不斷在改變，病蟲害不斷在適應，全球暖化還會帶來更多目前無法預見的挑戰。在理想的世界裡，解決的方法應該像植物本身一樣多樣、一樣不斷變化。

怎麼保存作物多樣性最好，爭議的焦點在於：我們應該和田間的社群合作，還是和機構合作，因為經費非常難找，很難兩邊都做。現在，偏遠的斯瓦巴種子庫正吸走可用的經費。然而，這種高度集中的做法，五十年或一百年後，可能沒辦法幫助農民因應氣候變遷。根據新的研究結果，全球多達 75% 的作物多樣性，存在於大型機構的種子庫之外，掌握在世界上一些最邊緣的農民手中。此外，越來越多人強力主張，種子庫既無法取代第一線農民的實務知識，也比不上他們的巧思。

items.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: Seed banks can help farmers improve their crops.
The practice of seed banks requires global cooperation.
The idea of saving crop diversity in seed banks is debatable.
Seed banks are able to deal with challenges of climate change.
items.explanation: 第 1 段介紹斯瓦巴全球種子庫和它的目的；第 2 段用 however 一轉，說越來越多人認為世界對種子庫的信心放錯了地方；第 3 段說明爭議的焦點，以及種子庫做不到的事。全文談的是用種子庫保存作物多樣性這個做法有爭議，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 improve，幫助改良作物只是第 1 段說的設立目的，後面兩段正是在質疑這一點，過於狹隘；(D) 照抄 climate change，第 3 段反而說這種做法可能沒辦法幫助農民因應氣候變遷，偏離主題；(B) 照抄 global，Global 是種子庫名稱的一部分，原文沒有談全球合作，偏離主題。

items.stem: According to this passage, which of the following statements is true about the Svalbard Global Seed Vault?
options: It is using up a lot of the funding.
It is located in the center of Norway.
It aims to fight against gene modified crops.
It holds 75 percent of global crop diversity.
items.explanation:
Now the isolated Svalbard seed vault is sucking up available funding.
第 3 段先說經費非常難找，很難兩邊都做，接著說斯瓦巴種子庫正吸走（sucking up）可用的經費。suck up 是「吸光、吸走」，經費本來就少，種子庫又把錢都吸走，選項換成 is using up a lot of the funding，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 75 percent，75% 的作物多樣性是在大型機構的種子庫之外，掌握在農民手中，選項說反了；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 Norway，種子庫在挪威和北極點之間的島上，不在挪威中部；(C) 照抄 gene，種子庫是要幫人找到改良作物的基因，原文沒有提到對抗基因改造作物。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about the role of farmers in preserving crop variety?
items.explanation:
seed banks can neither make up for the practical knowledge of farmers on the ground, nor compete with their ingenuity.
最後一句用 neither…nor 句型，主詞是種子庫（seed banks）：種子庫既無法取代（make up for）第一線農民的實務知識（practical knowledge），也比不上（compete with）農民的巧思。可見在保存作物多樣性這件事上，農民提供的是種子庫取代不了的實務知識，所以是 (B)。(A) 原文的 compete with 是說種子庫比不上農民，主詞是種子庫，選項把主詞換成農民，說成農民和種子庫競爭；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 population growth，因應人口成長是種子庫希望培育新品種的目的之一；(C) 第 2 段說多樣性沒辦法裝箱保存，原文沒有說農民替研究包裝種子。

items.stem: What does “the highly centralized approach” in the third paragraph refer to?
items.explanation:
centers on whether we should work with communities in the fields or with institutions
Now the isolated Svalbard seed vault is sucking up available funding.
第 3 段第一句先說爭議在兩種做法之間：和田間的社群合作，或和機構合作（with institutions）。接著說斯瓦巴種子庫正吸走經費，種子庫就是第 2 段說的，把全世界的種子集中存放在單一容器裡的機構。下一句說 the highly centralized approach（高度集中的做法）可能幫不了農民，指的就是這種把種子集中在機構保存的做法，也就是和機構合作，所以是 (A)。再下一句說 75% 的作物多樣性在大型機構的種子庫之外，對照的也是機構。(B) 和田間的農民合作，種子分散在各地，正好是不集中的做法；(C) 照抄 crop diversity，保存作物多樣性是兩種做法共同的目標，不是其中一種做法；(D) 照抄 funding 的 fund，經費難找是爭議的原因，不是做法。

閱讀測驗.title: 神仙魚的變性能力（The Gender-Changing Angelfish）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Angelfish, often found in the warm seas and coral reefs, are among the most brightly colored fish of the ocean. Brilliant colors and stripes form amazing patterns on their body. These patterns actually help the fish to hide from danger among roots and plants. At night, when these fish become inactive, their colors may become pale. Often, the young ones are differently colored than the adults. Some scientists believe that the color difference between the young and the old indicates their different social positions.

Another interesting fact about angelfish is that they have an occupation in the fish world. Most of them act as cleaners for other fish and pick dead tissue from their bodies. This is not their food, though. Their diet consists mainly of sponge and algae.

One particular kind of angelfish, the blackspot angelfish, has a special capability that allows it to change gender from female to male. However, the change is not made at random; it happens for a specific reason. Angelfish live in groups, and each group has one male fish, which is blue in color, and four female fish, which are yellow. The male angelfish is the strongest and largest member of the group. He is the one who protects and looks after the females. When the male dies, the group needs a new “security guard.” This is when the largest female in the group begins to change in appearance. She begins to grow larger in size, and after a week, she starts changing color, from yellow to blue. Slowly, her behavior toward the other fish also changes. She begins behaving like a male. Two weeks later, black stripes appear on her body, indicating the gender change is complete. She is now completely male!
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
神仙魚常見於溫暖的海域和珊瑚礁，是海洋中色彩最鮮豔的魚類之一。亮麗的色彩和條紋在牠們身上形成令人驚嘆的花紋，這些花紋其實能幫助牠們躲在樹根和植物之間，避開危險。到了晚上，神仙魚不太活動，顏色可能會變淡。幼魚的顏色也常常和成魚不同，有些科學家認為，這種顏色上的差異代表牠們在群體中的地位不同。

神仙魚另一個有趣的地方，是牠們在魚類世界裡有一份「職業」。大部分的神仙魚替其他魚當清潔工，啄掉牠們身上的死皮。不過，這些死皮並不是牠們的食物，牠們主要吃的是海綿和藻類。

有一種神仙魚叫黑斑神仙魚，具有一種特殊的能力，可以從雌性變成雄性。不過，這種轉變不是隨機發生的，而是有特定的原因。神仙魚成群生活，每一群有一條藍色的雄魚和四條黃色的雌魚。雄魚是群體裡最強壯、體型最大的成員，負責保護和照顧雌魚。雄魚死掉之後，群體需要一位新的「守衛」，這時群體裡最大的雌魚就開始改變外觀。牠先是體型開始變大，一週之後，顏色從黃色變成藍色。接著，牠對其他魚的行為也慢慢改變，開始表現得像雄魚。兩週之後，牠身上出現黑色條紋，表示變性已經完成。牠現在完全是一條雄魚了！

items.stem: What is the job of an angelfish in the sea?
options: Being a cleaner for other fish.
Being a bodyguard for other fish.
Being a gardener for roots and plants.
Being a caretaker for sponge and algae.
items.explanation:
Most of them act as cleaners for other fish and pick dead tissue from their bodies.
第 2 段說大部分的神仙魚替其他魚當清潔工，啄掉牠們身上的死皮，選項幾乎照用原字。(C) 照抄第 1 段的 roots and plants，原文說神仙魚躲在樹根和植物之間避開危險，不是照顧植物；(D) 照抄 sponge and algae，那是神仙魚的食物，不是牠們照顧的對象；(B) 保護群體的「守衛」是第 3 段的雄魚，不是神仙魚替其他魚做的工作。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the color of angelfish?
options: Female angelfish are blue in color.
The colors of the fish become less bright at night.
Male angelfish do not have black stripes on them.
The adult fish and the young ones have the same colors.
items.explanation:
At night, when these fish become inactive, their colors may become pale.
第 1 段說神仙魚晚上不活動時，顏色可能會變淡；選項把 become pale 換成 become less bright。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 blue in color，但藍色的是雄魚，雌魚是黃色；(C) 照抄 black stripes，原文說黑色條紋出現就表示已經變成雄魚，正好相反；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 young ones，原文說幼魚和成魚的顏色常常不同。

items.stem: According to the passage, what triggers the gender change in the blackspot angelfish?
options: The death of the male fish in a group.
items.explanation:
When the male dies, the group needs a new “security guard.”
This is when the largest female in the group begins to change in appearance.
第 3 段說雄魚死掉之後，群體需要新的守衛，這時最大的雌魚就開始改變；the male dies 在選項換成 the death of the male fish。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 danger，原文說的是花紋幫助神仙魚躲避危險，和變性無關；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 diet，(C) 照抄第 1 段的 young，文章都沒有說這兩件事會引發變性。

items.stem: Which of the following describes the order of changes in the features of a blackspot angelfish during gender change?
items.explanation:
She begins to grow larger in size, and after a week, she starts changing color, from yellow to blue.
Slowly, her behavior toward the other fish also changes.
Two weeks later, black stripes appear on her body, indicating the gender change is complete.
第 3 段依序寫出四個變化：先是體型變大（size），一週後變色（color），接著對其他魚的行為慢慢改變（behavior），兩週後出現黑色條紋（stripes）。after a week、Slowly、Two weeks later 這幾個表示先後的字詞標出了順序，所以是 (C)。

閱讀測驗.title: 北美原住民的圖騰柱（Totem Poles in North America）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Totem poles in North America are poles or posts carved with symbols or figures by Aboriginal peoples of the Northwest Coast. Carved from large, straight trees and painted vibrant colors, the totem poles are not just unique works of art. The coastal peoples have long passed on knowledge from generation to generation through oral traditions, and totem poles were the traditional way of telling the story of an individual family or clan.

The totem pole can be grouped into specific categories, depending on its location and the occasion for which it was carved. Welcome poles were traditionally placed on village beachfronts to greet visitors arriving by canoe. Inside the homes of high-ranking chiefs is where house poles were found. The family’s history was carefully carved into each pole. Placed along the rear or front walls of a house, house poles also helped to support the main beam of the roof.

Memorial poles stood in front of a house. They were erected in memory of a deceased chief or a high-ranking clan member. The poles depicted the person’s accomplishments or family history. Mortuary poles were also raised to honor the dead, but they differed from memorial poles, having a burial box placed at the top of the pole. Inside the burial box were the remains of the deceased.

While many of these poles can still be found in various locations on the west coast of North America, there is one pole that can now only be found in a museum—the shame pole. Traditionally, shame poles were carved for a chief to embarrass and ridicule another who had done something wrong. Once the wrong was made right, the pole was taken down.

Totem poles are important expressions of specific Aboriginal cultures. Despite the threats posed by cultural and political encroachment of colonial forces, the art of totem pole carving has survived. Aboriginal carvers continue to carve totems as symbols of their cultural pride and clan kinship.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
北美的圖騰柱，是西北海岸的原住民刻上符號或人物圖案的柱子。圖騰柱取材自高大筆直的樹木，雕刻之後漆上鮮豔的色彩，不只是獨特的藝術品。沿海的原住民長久以來靠口述傳統，把知識一代一代傳下去，圖騰柱就是他們講述某個家族或氏族故事的傳統方式。

圖騰柱可以依照設立的位置和雕刻的場合，分成幾個類別。迎賓柱傳統上立在村落的海灘邊，迎接划獨木舟來訪的客人。屋柱則設在地位崇高的酋長家中，每一根都仔細刻上家族的歷史。屋柱立在房屋的後牆或前牆邊，也幫忙支撐屋頂的大梁。

紀念柱立在房屋前面，用來紀念過世的酋長或地位崇高的氏族成員，柱上刻畫這個人的功績或家族歷史。墓葬柱同樣是為了紀念死者而立，但和紀念柱不同的是，墓葬柱的頂端放了一個葬箱，裡面安放著死者的遺骸。

這些圖騰柱有許多到現在仍然可以在北美西岸各地看到，但有一種柱子現在只能在博物館裡看到，那就是羞辱柱。傳統上，酋長會刻羞辱柱，讓另一位做錯事的酋長難堪、受人嘲笑；等對方把錯誤彌補好，柱子就會拆下來。

圖騰柱是特定原住民文化的重要表現。儘管殖民勢力在文化和政治上的侵逼帶來威脅，圖騰柱的雕刻藝術仍然流傳了下來。原住民雕刻師至今仍持續雕刻圖騰柱，作為他們文化自豪與氏族情誼的象徵。

items.stem: Which of the following is the best title for this passage?
options: Totem Poles, the Legends of Aboriginal Peoples
Totem Poles, Symbols of Historical Resistance
items.explanation: 第 1 段說圖騰柱不只是藝術品，也是講述家族故事的方式；第 2–4 段依位置和用途，介紹迎賓柱、屋柱、紀念柱、墓葬柱和羞辱柱各有什麼作用，所以最好的標題是圖騰柱的功能。(D) 柱子的雕刻和色彩只在第 1 段帶到，(C) 抵抗殖民勢力只在第 5 段提到，都過於狹隘；(A) 圖騰柱記錄的是家族和氏族的歷史，文章沒有談原住民的傳說，偏離主題。

items.stem: How is the information about totem poles organized in Paragraphs 2 to 4?
items.explanation: 第 2 段一開頭就說圖騰柱可以依位置和場合分成幾類（can be grouped into specific categories），接著第 2 到 4 段逐一介紹迎賓柱、屋柱、紀念柱、墓葬柱和羞辱柱，所以是分類。交卷後「這一篇的文章結構」也把這篇歸為分類。

items.stem: Which of the following is located at the edge of a body of water?
items.explanation:
Welcome poles were traditionally placed on village beachfronts to greet visitors arriving by canoe.
題幹的 at the edge of a body of water（水邊），是第 2 段 beachfronts（海灘邊）的換句話說；立在海灘邊、迎接划獨木舟來訪客人的是迎賓柱。(A) 屋柱在酋長家中，(C) 紀念柱立在房屋前面，(B) 羞辱柱現在只在博物館裡，都不在水邊。

items.stem: Which is closest in meaning to the word “encroachment” in the last paragraph?
items.explanation:
Despite the threats posed by cultural and political encroachment of colonial forces, the art of totem pole carving has survived.
Despite 表示讓步：儘管殖民勢力帶來威脅，雕刻藝術仍然流傳下來。會對原住民文化構成威脅的，是殖民勢力在文化和政治上的侵逼，所以 encroachment 最接近 invasion（侵略、侵入）。(D) enrichment 是使豐富，方向正好相反；(B) 任命、(C) 反對都談不上威脅。

閱讀測驗.title: 「腦中神曲」現象（Earworms）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Music has a tendency to get stuck in our heads. Sometimes a tune intrudes on our thoughts and then plays, and replays, in a never-ending loop. This interesting phenomenon becomes a subject explored by many scientists. They use a range of terms to describe it—stuck-song syndrome, sticky music, cognitive itch, or most commonly “earworm.” Earworms can run around our heads for several minutes to numerous hours. As the melody repeats, it becomes embedded into our mind. Even though our ears do not hear the tune, our brain continues to play it.

Earworms often take the form of song fragments rather than entire songs, and the song is usually a familiar one. Researchers are not sure why some songs are more likely to get stuck in our heads than others, but everyone has their own tunes. Often those songs have a simple, upbeat melody and catchy, repetitive lyrics, such as popular commercial jingles and slightly annoying radio hits. Recent or repeated exposure to a song or even a small part of a song can also trigger earworms, as can word associations, such as a phrase similar to the lyrics of a song.

While earworms might be annoying, most people who experience them nevertheless report that they are pleasant or at least neutral. Only a third of people are disturbed by the song in their heads. How people cope with their earworms seems to depend on how they feel about them. Those who have positive feelings about their stuck songs prefer to just “let them be,” while those with negative feelings turn to more behavioral responses, which include coping strategies such as singing, talking, or even praying.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
音樂很容易卡在腦子裡。有時候一段旋律闖進我們的思緒，接著不停播放、重播，沒完沒了。這個有趣的現象成了許多科學家研究的主題，他們用各種名稱來描述它：卡歌症候群、黏人音樂、認知搔癢，最常用的是「耳蟲」。耳蟲可以在腦中盤旋幾分鐘到好幾個小時。旋律一再重複，就深深嵌進我們的腦海；即使耳朵沒有聽到這段旋律，大腦還是繼續播放。

耳蟲常常是歌曲的片段，而不是整首歌，而且通常是熟悉的歌。研究人員不確定為什麼有些歌比其他歌更容易卡在腦中，不過每個人都有自己的耳蟲歌。這些歌常常旋律簡單輕快，歌詞朗朗上口、一再重複，像是流行的廣告歌曲，以及有點煩人的電台熱門歌曲。最近聽過或反覆聽到一首歌，甚至只是歌曲的一小段，都可能引發耳蟲；字詞的聯想也會，例如聽到和某首歌歌詞相似的句子。

耳蟲雖然可能惱人，大部分有過這種經驗的人卻表示，感覺是愉快的，至少無所謂，只有三分之一的人會因為腦中的歌感到困擾。人們怎麼應付耳蟲，似乎取決於他們對耳蟲的感受。對卡在腦中的歌有正面感受的人，寧願「隨它去」；有負面感受的人則會採取比較多的行動，像是唱歌、說話，甚至祈禱，來應付耳蟲。
