閱讀測驗.title: 除蟲炸彈的無效性（The Ineffectiveness of Bug Bombs）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Got a bug bite problem? Many people who are troubled by skin rashes caused by bug bites use “foggers,” or “bug bombs,” to get rid of the annoying crawlers in their homes. Many people think these bug killers or pesticides will penetrate every place where the insects hide. Actually, quite the opposite is true. Once the pests detect the chemical fog in the room, they’ll hide themselves in walls or other hideaways, where you’ll never be able to treat them effectively.

Ohio State University researchers tested three commercially sold foggers in a study on the effect of foggers on bedbugs. After testing these brands on five different groups of live bedbugs for two hours, the scientists saw that the foggers had little—if any—effect on the insects. The researchers said bedbugs hide in cracks and crevices such as under sheets and mattresses, or deep in carpets where foggers won’t reach. Moreover, bugs that do come in contact with the mist may be resistant to the pesticide.

Foggers, or bug bombs, should really be a measure of last resort. First of all, the gases used in bug bombs are highly flammable and thus pose a serious risk of fire or explosion if the product is not used properly. Second, once a bug bomb is used, every surface in your home will be covered with the toxic pesticide. When you use a bug bomb, a chemical mixture rains down on your counters, furniture, floors, and walls, leaving behind oily and toxic substances. Your health might thus be endangered. Therefore, it is suggested that people leave the problem to the professionals.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
有蟲咬的困擾嗎？許多人因為蟲咬引起皮膚起疹子，就用「噴霧器」，也就是「除蟲彈」，來消滅家裡惱人的小蟲。很多人以為這些殺蟲劑能滲透到蟲子藏身的每個地方，事實上正好相反。害蟲一察覺室內的化學藥霧，就會躲進牆壁或其他藏身處，在那裡你永遠沒辦法有效地處理牠們。

俄亥俄州立大學的研究人員研究除蟲彈對床蝨的效果，測試了三種市售的除蟲彈。他們用這幾個品牌對五組活的床蝨測試兩個小時後，發現除蟲彈對這些蟲子幾乎沒有效果，甚至毫無效果。研究人員說，床蝨會躲在縫隙裡，像是床單和床墊底下，或是地毯深處，這些地方除蟲彈都噴不到。此外，真的接觸到藥霧的蟲子，也可能對殺蟲劑有抗藥性。

除蟲彈其實應該是最後的手段。首先，除蟲彈用的氣體非常易燃，使用不當就有起火或爆炸的嚴重危險。其次，一旦用了除蟲彈，家裡每一個表面都會蓋上一層有毒的殺蟲劑。使用除蟲彈時，化學藥劑會像雨一樣落在流理台、家具、地板和牆壁上，留下油膩、有毒的物質，你的健康可能因此受到危害。所以，建議大家把這個問題交給專業人員處理。

閱讀測驗.title: 印尼天貝：從傳統食物到世界之寶（Indonesian Tempeh: From Traditional Food to World Treasure）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Tempeh (or tempe), a traditional soy product from Indonesia, is hailed as the country’s “gift to the world,” like kimchi from Korea or miso from Japan.

A stable, cheap source of protein in Indonesia for centuries, tempeh is a fermented food originating from the island of Java. It was discovered during tofu production when discarded soybean residue caught microbial spores from the air and grew certain whitish fungi around it. When this fermented residue was found to be edible and tasty, people began producing it at home for daily consumption across the country. This has given rise to many variations in its flavor and texture throughout different Indonesian regions.

Tempeh is high in protein and low in fat, and contains a host of vitamins. In fact, it is the only reported plant-based source of vitamin B12. Apart from being able to help reduce cholesterol, increase bone density, and promote muscle recovery, tempeh has a lot of polyphenols that protect skin cells and slow down the aging process. Best of all, with the same protein quality as meat and the ability to take on many flavors and textures, tempeh is a great meat substitute—something the vegetarian and vegan communities have been quick in adopting.

In addition to its highly nutritional makeup, tempeh has diverse preparation possibilities. It can be served as a main course (usually in curries) or a side dish to be eaten with rice, as a deep-fried snack, or even blended into smoothies and healthy juices. Though not yet a popular food among international diners, you may find tempeh-substituted BLTs (bacon, lettuce, tomato sandwiches) in San Francisco as easily as you can find vegetarian burgers with tempeh patties in Bali.

For the people of Indonesia, tempeh is not just food but also has cultural value. With the Indonesian traditional fabric batik being recognized by UNESCO as “Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity,” tempeh has great potential for this honor as well.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
天貝（tempeh，也拼作 tempe）是印尼傳統的大豆製品，就像韓國的泡菜、日本的味噌一樣，素有印尼「送給世界的禮物」之稱。

幾百年來，天貝一直是印尼穩定又便宜的蛋白質來源，這種發酵食品源自爪哇島。天貝是在製作豆腐時發現的：丟棄的豆渣沾上空氣中的微生物孢子，周圍長出一層白色的真菌。後來人們發現這種發酵過的豆渣可以吃，而且很美味，全國各地就開始在家自己做，天天吃。印尼各地因此發展出許多風味和口感不同的天貝。

天貝蛋白質高、脂肪低，還含有多種維生素；事實上，天貝是目前唯一已知含維生素 B12 的植物性食物。天貝除了有助於降低膽固醇、增加骨質密度、促進肌肉恢復，還含有大量的多酚，可以保護皮膚細胞、延緩老化。最棒的是，天貝的蛋白質品質和肉一樣好，又能做出各種風味和口感，是很好的肉類替代品，素食者和純素食者很快就接受了。

天貝不但營養豐富，料理方式也很多元。可以當主菜（通常做成咖哩）或配飯的小菜，可以炸成點心，甚至可以打進果昔和健康果汁裡。雖然天貝在國際上還不算熱門的食物，但你在舊金山可以輕易找到用天貝取代培根的 BLT（培根、生菜、番茄三明治），就像在峇里島可以輕易找到天貝肉排做的素食漢堡一樣。

對印尼人來說，天貝不只是食物，也有文化價值。印尼的傳統布料蠟染已經列入聯合國教科文組織的「人類非物質文化遺產」，天貝也很有希望獲得這項殊榮。

閱讀測驗.title: 催眠的科學與應用（The Science and Application of Hypnosis）
閱讀測驗.passage:
When Dr. David Spiegel emerged from a three-hour shoulder surgery in 1972, he didn’t use any pain medication to recover. Instead, he hypnotized himself. It worked—to the surprise of everyone but Spiegel himself, who has studied hypnosis for 45 years.

Hypnosis is often misunderstood as a sleep-like state in which a person is put to sleep and does whatever he is asked to do. But according to Dr. Spiegel, it is a state of highly focused attention and intense concentration. Being hypnotized, you tune out most of the stimuli around you. You focus intently on the subject at hand, to the near exclusion of any other thought. This trance-like state can be an effective tool to control pain, ease anxiety, and deal with stress.

Not all people, however, are equally hypnotizable. In a recent study, Dr. Spiegel and his colleagues found that people who are easily hypnotized tend to be more trusting of others, more intuitive, and more likely to get caught up in a good movie. The research team compared people who were highly hypnotizable with those low in hypnotizability. Both groups were given fMRI scans during several different conditions: at rest, while recalling a memory, and during two sessions of hypnotism. The researchers saw some interesting changes in the brain during hypnosis—but only in the highly hypnotizable group. Specifically, there was a drop in activity in the part of the brain which usually fires up when there is something to worry about.

This helps explain how hypnosis can have powerful effects, including reducing stress, anxiety, pain, and self-consciousness. Spiegel hopes that the practice can be used to replace painkillers. His own previous research has shown that when people in pain were taught self-hypnosis, they needed half the pain medication and suffered half the pain of those who were only given access to painkillers. However, more needs to be learned about hypnosis in order to harness its potential effects.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
1972 年，David Spiegel 醫師動完三個小時的肩部手術，復原期間沒有用任何止痛藥，而是替自己催眠。結果真的有效。除了研究催眠已經 45 年的 Spiegel 本人，大家都很驚訝。

很多人誤以為催眠是一種像睡覺一樣的狀態，人在這種狀態下睡著了，別人叫他做什麼，他就做什麼。不過，根據 Spiegel 醫師的說法，催眠是一種高度專注、注意力非常集中的狀態。處在催眠狀態時，你會把周遭大部分的刺激都屏除在外，全神貫注在眼前的事情上，幾乎不去想任何別的事情。這種恍惚般的狀態，可以是控制疼痛、緩解焦慮、應付壓力的有效工具。

不過，並不是每個人都一樣容易催眠。Spiegel 醫師和同事在最近一項研究中發現，容易催眠的人往往比較信任別人，比較依賴直覺，看到一部好電影，也比較容易沉浸其中。研究團隊把很容易催眠的人和不容易催眠的人做比較，兩組人都在幾種不同的情況下接受功能性磁振造影（fMRI）掃描：休息時、回想一段記憶時，以及兩次催眠過程中。研究人員看到大腦在催眠時出現一些有趣的變化，但只出現在容易催眠的那一組。具體來說，大腦中通常在有事情要擔心時就會活躍起來的區域，活動下降了。

這有助於解釋催眠為什麼能有強大的效果，包括減輕壓力、焦慮、疼痛和自我意識。Spiegel 希望催眠可以用來取代止痛藥。他自己先前的研究顯示，身體疼痛的人學了自我催眠以後，和只用止痛藥的人相比，需要的止痛藥只有一半，感受到的疼痛也只有一半。不過，要善用催眠的潛在效果，對催眠還需要更多的了解。

This trance-like state can be an effective tool to control pain, ease anxiety, and deal with stress.
Spiegel hopes that the practice can be used to replace painkillers.
第 2 段說催眠是控制疼痛、緩解焦慮、應付壓力的有效工具；第 4 段說 Spiegel 希望催眠可以用來取代止痛藥（replace painkillers），還研究了自我催眠能讓病人少用一半的止痛藥。他研究的是催眠怎麼當作醫療方法，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 pain，他研究的是用催眠減輕疼痛，不是找出疼痛的原因；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 brain，研究人員只是觀察到催眠時大腦的變化，沒有說要強化大腦的功能；(B) 第 2 段的專注是說明催眠時的狀態，不是要幫人專心工作。

items.stem: According to Dr. Spiegel, which of the following is true when people are hypnotized?
options: Their mind is fixed only on what they are doing.
They do whatever they are told to do.
They have greater awareness of things around them.
items.explanation:
You focus intently on the subject at hand, to the near exclusion of any other thought.
第 2 段先說一般人的誤解（is often misunderstood as），再用 But according to Dr. Spiegel 帶出他的看法。題目問的是 According to Dr. Spiegel，答案要在 But 後面找：催眠時你會全神貫注在眼前的事情上（focus intently on the subject at hand），幾乎不去想別的事，選項換成 Their mind is fixed only on what they are doing，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 whatever，別人叫你做什麼就做什麼，是 But 前面一般人的誤解；(D) 照抄 around，原文說催眠時會把周遭（around you）大部分的刺激屏除在外，選項說更能察覺周遭的事物，意思正好相反；(A) 第 3 段的回想記憶，是研究中掃描大腦的其中一種情況，不是催眠時的狀態，原文也沒有提到快樂的記憶。

items.stem: What can be inferred about highly hypnotizable people?
options: They tend to be isolated from the society.
They are more likely to fall asleep during the day.
They may easily identify themselves with characters in fictions.
They are more trustworthy than people who are less hypnotizable.
items.explanation:
more likely to get caught up in a good movie.
第 3 段說容易催眠的人，看到一部好電影，比較容易沉浸其中（get caught up in a good movie）。看電影容易入戲，就是容易把自己投入片中角色的處境，電影也是虛構的故事，選項換成 identify themselves with characters in fictions，所以是 (C)。最容易選錯的是 (D)，這個選項照抄 trust：原文說的是容易催眠的人比較信任別人（more trusting of others），trusting 是「信任別人」，選項的 trustworthy 是「值得別人信任」，兩個字意思不同。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 sleep，把催眠當成睡著，正是 Spiegel 說的誤解；(A) 容易催眠的人比較信任別人，看不出他們和社會隔絕。

閱讀測驗.title: 語言與嗅覺描述的文化差異（Cultural Differences in Language and Smell Description）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In many languages, such as English, there is no straightforward way to talk about smell. For want of dedicated odor terminology, English speakers are often forced to use odor-sources such as “flowery” and “vanilla” and metaphors like “sweet” and “oriental” in their descriptions of smell.

But the difficulty with talking about smell is not universal. The Maniq, a group of hunter-gatherers in southern Thailand, can describe smells using at least fifteen different terms, which express only smells and are not applicable across other sensory domains. In addition to Maniq, researchers found that there are also a dozen words for various smells in Jahai, a language spoken by a neighboring hunter-gatherer population.

Interestingly, the difficulty for English speakers to translate smell directly into words seems to have very little to do with the nose’s actual capabilities. According to findings of a recent study, English speakers are capable of discriminating more than a trillion different odors. Then, why is there a gap between their ability to discriminate scent and their vocabulary? The researchers suggest that surroundings may play a significant role.

Maniq and Jahai speakers live in tropical rainforest regions with a hunting-gathering lifestyle, and these two ethnic groups evaluate their surroundings through their noses to survive in nature. In an environment that is still largely untouched by humans, they are surrounded by smells at all times. They need to use their sense of smell to identify animals that they can hunt, and to recognize objects or events, such as spoiled food, that can pose a danger. Unlike the Maniq and the Jahai, many English speakers inhabit the post-industrial west and do not rely on smells to survive in their environment. This difference may explain the interesting linguistic phenomenon discussed above.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
在英語等許多語言裡，沒有直截了當談論氣味的方法。因為缺少專門的氣味詞彙，說英語的人描述氣味時，常常只好借用氣味的來源，例如「flowery」（花香的）和「vanilla」（香草的），或是用「sweet」（甜的）、「oriental」（東方的）這類比喻。

不過，談論氣味的困難並不是每種語言都有。Maniq 人是泰國南部以狩獵採集維生的一個族群，他們至少能用十五個不同的詞描述氣味，這些詞只用來表達氣味，不能用在其他的感官上。除了 Maniq 語，研究人員還發現，鄰近另一個狩獵採集族群說的 Jahai 語，也有十幾個描述各種氣味的詞。

有趣的是，說英語的人很難把氣味直接化為文字，這似乎和鼻子實際的能力沒什麼關係。根據最近一項研究的結果，說英語的人能分辨超過一兆種不同的氣味。那麼，為什麼他們分辨氣味的能力和詞彙之間，會有這樣的落差呢？研究人員認為，周遭的環境可能扮演了重要的角色。

說 Maniq 語和 Jahai 語的人住在熱帶雨林地區，過著狩獵採集的生活，這兩個族群要靠鼻子評估周遭的環境，才能在大自然中生存。在一個大部分仍未經人類開發的環境裡，他們隨時都處在各種氣味之中。他們需要用嗅覺辨認可以獵捕的動物，也要辨認會帶來危險的東西或情況，例如腐壞的食物。和 Maniq 人、Jahai 人不同，很多說英語的人住在後工業化的西方，不必靠氣味在環境中生存。這個差異或許可以解釋上面談到的有趣語言現象。

items.stem: What is the purpose of this passage?
options: To evaluate the languages used by different ethnic groups.
To prove how civilization slows down language development.
To describe how terms of smell are found in different languages.
To point out the link between language use and the environment.
items.explanation: 第 1、2 段比較英語和 Maniq 語、Jahai 語描述氣味的詞彙；第 3 段說英語的困難和鼻子的能力無關，研究人員認為是環境的關係；第 4 段說明兩種生活環境的差異，最後說這個差異或許能解釋這個語言現象。全文要指出的是語言使用和環境之間的關係，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 terms，介紹各種語言有多少氣味詞彙，只是第 2 段的內容，全文還要解釋原因，過於狹隘；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 ethnic groups，原文沒有評價哪一種語言比較好，偏離主題；(B) 原文說英語使用者不必靠氣味生存，沒有說文明讓語言發展變慢，偏離主題。

items.stem: What does the word “want” in the first paragraph most likely mean?
items.explanation:
For want of dedicated odor terminology, English speakers are often forced to use odor-sources
for want of 是固定片語，意思是「因為缺少」，want 在這裡當名詞用。從上下文也推得出來：第 1 段第一句說英語沒有直截了當談論氣味的方法，後面說英語使用者只好（are forced to）借用氣味的來源和比喻。只好借用別的說法，是因為缺少專門的氣味詞彙，所以 want 最接近 (A) Lack。(C) Loss 是「失去」，表示原本有、後來沒了，原文沒有說英語曾經有這些詞彙；(B) 成長、(D) 尋找，都接不上後面的「只好借用」。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about the Maniq?
options: They live in a different climate zone from the Jahai.
Their ability to smell is stronger than that of the Jahai.
They use smell terms to describe how food looks and tastes.
Their living environment is similar to that in earlier human history.
items.explanation:
Maniq and Jahai speakers live in tropical rainforest regions with a hunting-gathering lifestyle
In an environment that is still largely untouched by humans
第 4 段說 Maniq 人住在熱帶雨林，過著狩獵採集的生活，而且環境大部分仍未經人類開發（still largely untouched by humans）。以打獵、採集維生，住在沒有開發的大自然裡，和人類早期的生活環境相似，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 smell，原文說兩個族群都靠嗅覺生存，沒有比較誰的嗅覺比較好；(C) 照抄 food，腐壞的食物是他們要用嗅覺察覺的危險，第 2 段也說這些氣味詞只用來表達氣味，不能用在其他感官上，不會拿來描述食物的外觀和味道；(A) 兩個族群是鄰居，第 4 段說兩者都住在熱帶雨林，氣候帶相同。

items.stem: Why is it difficult for English speakers to describe smells directly?
options: They cannot distinguish the smells around them.
The sense of smell is not critical for their survival.
They consider it uncivilized to talk about smells directly.
There are not many sources of odor in their surroundings.
items.explanation:
do not rely on smells to survive in their environment.
第 4 段說很多說英語的人住在後工業化的西方，不必靠氣味（do not rely on smells）就能在環境中生存，這個差異或許能解釋英語缺少氣味詞彙的現象。選項換成 The sense of smell is not critical for their survival，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄第 3 段的 surroundings，研究人員說的是環境扮演重要的角色，原因在於要不要靠氣味生存，不是環境裡的氣味來源少；(A) 第 3 段說說英語的人能分辨超過一兆種氣味，所以不是分辨不出來；(C) 原文沒有說談論氣味不文明。

閱讀測驗.title: 霍加狓的發現、特徵與保育困境（Okapi: Discovery, Characteristics, and Conservation Challenges）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The okapi is a mammal living above the equator in one of the most biodiverse areas in central Africa. The animal was unknown to the western world until the beginning of the 20th century, and is often described as half-zebra, half-giraffe, as if it were a mixed-breed creature from a Greek legend. Yet its image is prevalent in the Democratic Republic of Congo—the only country in the world where it is found living in the wild. The okapi is to Congo what the giant panda is to China or the kangaroo to Australia.

Although the okapi has striped markings resembling those of zebras’, it is most closely related to the giraffe. It has a long neck, and large, flexible ears. The face and throat are greyish white. The coat is a chocolate to reddish brown, much in contrast with the white horizontal stripes and rings on the legs and white ankles. Overall, the okapi can be easily distinguished from its nearest relative. It is much smaller (about the size of a horse), and shares more external similarities with the deer than with the giraffe. While both sexes possess horns in the giraffe, only males bear horns in the okapi.

The West got its first whiff of the okapi in 1890 when Welsh journalist Henry Morton Stanley had puzzled over a strange “African donkey” in his book. Other Europeans in Africa had also heard of an animal that they came to call the “African unicorn.” Explorers may have seen the fleeting view of the striped backside as the animal fled through the bushes, leading to speculation that the okapi was some sort of rainforest zebra. Some even believed that the okapi was a new species of zebra. It was only later, when okapi skeleton was analyzed, that naturalists realized they had a giraffe on their hands.

In 1987, the Okapi Wildlife Reserve was established in eastern Congo to protect this rare mammal. But decades of political turbulence has seen much of the Congo’s natural resources spin out of the government’s control, and okapi numbers have fallen by 50 percent since 1995. Today, only 10,000 remain.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
霍加狓是一種哺乳動物，生活在赤道以北、中非生物多樣性最豐富的地區之一。一直到 20 世紀初，西方世界才知道有這種動物。人們常形容牠半斑馬、半長頸鹿，好像牠是希臘神話裡由兩種動物合成的生物。然而，在剛果民主共和國，霍加狓的形象隨處可見，剛果也是世界上唯一有野生霍加狓的國家。霍加狓對剛果的意義，就像大貓熊之於中國，袋鼠之於澳洲。

雖然霍加狓身上的條紋和斑馬很像，牠的親緣關係卻和長頸鹿最近。霍加狓的脖子很長，耳朵又大又靈活，臉和喉嚨是灰白色。身上的毛是巧克力色到紅棕色，和腿上白色的橫紋、環紋，以及白色的腳踝，形成強烈的對比。整體來說，霍加狓很容易和牠最近的親戚長頸鹿區分。霍加狓的體型小得多（大約和馬一樣大），外觀和鹿相似的地方，比和長頸鹿還多。長頸鹿公母都有角，霍加狓卻只有公的有角。

西方第一次聽到霍加狓的一點風聲，是在 1890 年。威爾斯記者 Henry Morton Stanley 在他的書裡，提到一種讓他百思不解的奇怪「非洲驢」。其他在非洲的歐洲人也聽說過一種動物，後來他們把牠稱為「非洲獨角獸」。探險家看到的，可能只是這種動物逃進樹叢時，一閃而過的條紋臀部，於是有人猜測霍加狓是某種雨林斑馬，有些人甚至相信霍加狓是一種新的斑馬。一直到後來分析了霍加狓的骨骸，博物學家才發現，他們遇到的其實是長頸鹿家族的動物。

1987 年，剛果東部設立了霍加狓野生動物保護區，保護這種稀有的哺乳動物。但是，數十年的政治動盪，讓剛果大部分的天然資源脫離了政府的掌控，霍加狓的數量從 1995 年以來減少了一半，如今只剩下一萬隻。

items.stem: Which of the following is a picture of an okapi?
items.explanation:
The coat is a chocolate to reddish brown, much in contrast with the white horizontal stripes and rings on the legs and white ankles.
the fleeting view of the striped backside
第 2 段說霍加狓身上的毛是巧克力色到紅棕色，白色的橫紋和環紋長在腿上，腳踝是白色的；第 3 段也說探險家瞥見的是牠帶條紋的臀部。條紋在腿和臀部、身體是深色的毛、腳踝是白色，四張圖裡只有 (B) 符合。(A)、(C) 的條紋畫在身體前半部的軀幹上，不在腿上；(D) 雖然後腿有條紋，身體中段卻是淺色，不是巧克力色到紅棕色，頭上還長著像鹿一樣分岔的大角，原文說霍加狓只是外觀像鹿，沒有說牠有這種角，(A) 也一樣。

items.stem: Which of the following descriptions is true about the okapi?
options: It is an important symbol of Congo.
It is a mystical creature from a Greek legend.
It has been well protected since 1987.
It is more closely related to the zebra than the giraffe.
items.explanation:
Yet its image is prevalent in the Democratic Republic of Congo
The okapi is to Congo what the giant panda is to China or the kangaroo to Australia.
第 1 段說在剛果，霍加狓的形象隨處可見（its image is prevalent），又說霍加狓之於剛果，就像大貓熊之於中國、袋鼠之於澳洲。大貓熊、袋鼠都是代表一個國家的動物，所以霍加狓是剛果重要的象徵，是 (A)。(B) 照抄 Greek legend，原文用 as if 說「好像」希臘神話裡的生物，是比喻，霍加狓是真實存在的動物；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 1987，那一年設立了保護區，但後來政治動盪，霍加狓的數量減少了一半，不能說一直受到很好的保護；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 zebra，原文說霍加狓的條紋像斑馬，親緣關係卻和長頸鹿最近，選項說反了。

items.stem: What does the word “whiff” most likely mean in the third paragraph?
items.explanation:
The West got its first whiff of the okapi in 1890 when Welsh journalist Henry Morton Stanley had puzzled over a strange
Explorers may have seen the fleeting view of the striped backside
whiff 原本是「一陣氣味」，引申為一點點跡象或風聲。從上下文也推得出來：第 3 段說 1890 年 Stanley 只是在書裡提到一種讓他百思不解的「非洲驢」，連那是什麼動物都不知道；探險家可能也只瞥見一閃而過的條紋臀部。西方第一次得到的，只是一點點線索，所以 whiff 最接近 (C) Slight trace。(A) 堅定的信念，和 Stanley 的百思不解正好相反；(B) 善意、(D) 強烈的厭惡，都和認識霍加狓這件事接不上。

items.stem: Which of the following can be inferred about Henry Morton Stanley?
options: He was the first European to analyze okapi skeleton.
He had found many new species of animals in Africa.
He did not know the “African donkey” in his book was the okapi.
He had seen the backside of an okapi dashing through the bushes.
items.explanation:
Henry Morton Stanley had puzzled over a strange
第 3 段說 Stanley 在書裡提到一種讓他百思不解（had puzzled over）的奇怪「非洲驢」。他對這種動物感到困惑，可見他並不知道那就是霍加狓，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 skeleton，分析骨骸的是後來的博物學家；(D) 照抄 backside，瞥見條紋臀部的是探險家，而且原文用 may have seen，只是推測；(B) 照抄 new species，有人以為霍加狓是新的斑馬，原文沒有說 Stanley 在非洲發現了很多新物種。

閱讀測驗.title: 人字拖的歷史與影響（The History and Impact of Flip-flops）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The flip-flop is the simplest shoe on the planet. It consists of a piece of rubber, plastic, leather, or woven material in the outline of a foot, with a strap holding the sandal to a wearer’s toes. The name comes from the sound the sandals make when they slap the walking feet.

The earliest record of people wearing the flip-flop comes from Egypt, but many ancient cultures had their own variants of the footwear. In the Greek version, the toe strap ran between the first and second toes, while Roman sandals had the strap between the second and third toes. The Mesopotamians wore the strap between the third and fourth toes. In India, “toe knob” sandals had a knob between the first and second toes.

Modern flip-flops derive from Japanese zōris, which were often worn with socks dividing the big toe from the rest, and were typically made of rice straw. During World War II, Japan seized much of Southeast Asia’s rubber. In 1945, devastated from the war, the country set about establishing a cheap industry that could rebuild its economy. The Japanese used their rubber reserves from the war to mass-produce the simplest Japanese footwear. Rubber thus replaced rice straw as the major material for the flip-flop.

In the 1950s, flip-flops became popular in the United States as soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home. The sandals have subsequently undergone redesign, often appearing in bright colors in line with Californian beach culture. They have remained popular due to their convenience, and are often worn with bathing suits or summer clothing. Some people also wear dressy versions for more formal occasions.

Despite their popularity, flip-flops provoke some questions. Their simple design is responsible for many foot injuries. Another issue is the suitability of exposing feet on the street and places other than the beach. But even more serious is their environmental impact: Millions of plastic discards end up in landfills or the ocean, releasing chemicals and at the same time taking centuries to decompose.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
人字拖是世界上最簡單的鞋子，用一片橡膠、塑膠、皮革或編織材料做成腳的形狀，再用一條帶子把鞋固定在腳趾上。英文名稱 flip-flop 來自走路時鞋子拍打腳底的聲音。

最早有人穿人字拖的紀錄來自埃及，不過許多古文明都有自己的版本。希臘式的腳趾帶穿過大拇趾和第二趾之間，羅馬涼鞋的帶子則在第二趾和第三趾之間，美索不達米亞人的帶子在第三趾和第四趾之間。印度則有一種「趾鈕」涼鞋，大拇趾和第二趾之間有一個圓鈕。

現代的人字拖源自日本的草履。草履通常用稻草編成，常搭配把大拇趾和其他腳趾分開的襪子來穿。二次世界大戰期間，日本奪取了東南亞大部分的橡膠。1945 年，飽受戰爭摧殘的日本著手建立低成本的產業來重建經濟，用戰時囤積的橡膠大量生產這種最簡單的日本鞋子。於是橡膠取代稻草，成為人字拖的主要材料。

1950 年代，從美軍占領下的日本返國的士兵把草履帶回家，人字拖便在美國流行起來。此後這種涼鞋經過重新設計，常以鮮豔的顏色出現，和加州的海灘文化相互呼應。人字拖穿脫方便，所以一直很受歡迎，常搭配泳裝或夏季服裝；也有人在比較正式的場合穿講究一點的款式。

人字拖雖然受歡迎，也引發一些問題。人字拖的設計太簡單，許多腳傷都是這樣造成的。另一個問題是，在街上和海灘以外的地方露出雙腳是否合宜。不過更嚴重的是人字拖對環境的衝擊：數以百萬計的廢棄塑膠拖鞋最後進了垃圾掩埋場或海洋，不但釋放化學物質，還要好幾百年才能分解。

items.stem: Which culture most likely created the sandals shown in the picture?
items.explanation:
In the Greek version, the toe strap ran between the first and second toes, while Roman sandals had the strap between the second and third toes.
圖裡的帶子夾在第二趾和第三趾之間，對照第 2 段，是羅馬式的涼鞋。這一題要把文字描述轉成圖像，三個錯誤選項都是同一段列出的其他文化。

items.stem: Why is the footwear discussed in the passage called “flip-flop”?
options: Because of the noise it makes.
Because of the comfort of wearing it.
items.explanation:
The name comes from the sound the sandals make when they slap the walking feet.
名稱來自走路時發出的聲音，sound 在選項換成 noise。(C) 的 simple 取自第 1 段開頭 the simplest shoe，但那一句講的是鞋子的樣子，不是名稱的由來。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about the modern development of the flip-flop?
options: Modern flip-flops originated from Indian toe knob sandals.
Americans loved the Japanese flip-flop because of its bright colors.
Rubber became the major material of the flip-flop before World War II.
The sandals American soldiers brought home from Japan later became modern flip-flops.
items.explanation:
Modern flip-flops derive from Japanese zōris
In the 1950s, flip-flops became popular in the United States as soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home.
第 3 段說現代人字拖源自日本草履，第 4 段說美國士兵把草履從日本帶回家，兩段合起來就是 (D)。(A) 的 toe knob 在第 2 段，和現代人字拖無關；(B) 鮮豔的顏色是後來重新設計才有的，不是美國人喜歡的原因；(C) 橡膠是戰後才取代稻草。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a concern of wearing the flip-flop?
items.explanation:
Their simple design is responsible for many foot injuries.
Another issue is the suitability of exposing feet on the street and places other than the beach.
Millions of plastic discards end up in landfills or the ocean, releasing chemicals and at the same time taking centuries to decompose.
第 5 段提到三個問題，在選項裡都換了說法：foot injuries 是 Personal health，suitability 是 Social appropriateness，plastic discards end up in the ocean 是 Marine pollution。只有 (B) 品質不好文章沒提。

閱讀測驗.title: 領港員的專業（The Profession of Marine Pilot）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Ships are the lifeline of trade among countries. Almost everything, from food to machinery, comes by way of the sea in huge ships piloted by captains. But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor. The task of bringing the ship into the harbor and anchoring it is taken up by a different captain. This captain is called a marine pilot.

A marine pilot is a boat pilot with specialized knowledge of a particular port or harbor. The pilot is needed to direct large ships into a port, where there are often deep water channels surrounded by shallower seabeds. Without the services of a marine pilot, docking ships would be hazardous. There would be a real chance of running aground and damaging the ship and the cargo, some of which might be dangerous if released into a water-based ecosystem.

In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port. During different tides, currents may change from one direction to the other. The same strategy for docking a vessel during an incoming tide may not work during an outgoing tide. Also, the wind can significantly alter the direction of the ship and how it reacts, adding to the difficulty of anchoring the ship.

Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking. Above all, it is about risk management. A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time and controls the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand. The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
船舶是國際貿易的命脈。從糧食到機械，幾乎所有東西都由船長駕駛的巨型船隻經海路運來。不過船長只負責把船開到港口、等候進港為止；把船帶進港內並下錨停泊的工作，則交給另一位船長，這位船長就叫做領港員。

領港員是對某個港口有專門知識的船隻駕駛。港口常有深水航道，四周卻是比較淺的海床，所以需要領港員引導大型船隻進港。少了領港員，船隻靠岸會很危險，很可能擱淺，損壞船身和貨物；有些貨物一旦流進水域的生態系，還可能造成危害。

除了海床較淺，潮汐和風也讓船隻進港更加困難。漲潮和退潮時，海流的方向可能完全相反，漲潮時讓船靠岸的方法，退潮時不一定行得通。此外，風也會大幅改變船的方向和反應，讓停泊更加困難。

領港這份工作需要高度的專業，也需要能迅速、獨立地思考。最重要的是，這份工作講究的是風險管理。領港員在關鍵時刻登船，根據自己對港口和當下狀況的了解來操控船隻。領港員不但要負責船的安全，也要保護港口和海洋環境。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
items.explanation: 第 1 段引出領港員這個職業，第 2–3 段說這份工作為什麼需要、難在哪裡，第 4 段總結這份工作的要求和責任，所以全文介紹的是一種特殊的職業。(B) 航運與貿易是第 1 段開頭的引子，範圍比領港員大得多，太過廣泛；(C) 船隻靠港的難處只在第 2、3 段，文章也沒有列出什麼準則，(D) 海洋環境的保護只在第 2 段和第 4 段末尾帶到，兩個都過於狹隘。

items.stem: Which of the following is part of the knowledge that a marine pilot must have?
items.explanation:
In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port.
controls the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand
第 3 段說潮汐和風會改變船的方向，第 4 段說領港員要依當下的狀況操控船隻，所以天氣狀況是必備的知識，原文的 wind 在選項換成概括的 weather conditions。(B) 的 cargo 取自第 2 段，那裡講的是擱淺時貨物會受損，不是領港員要懂貨物內容。

items.stem: What does “a crucial time” in the last paragraph refer to?
options: When the vessel hits a flat.
When the channel is not deep enough.
When there is a collision of two ships.
When a ship is waiting to enter the port.
items.explanation:
But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor.
A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time
第 1 段說船長把船開到港口、等候進港時，就換領港員接手，這正是領港員登船的關鍵時刻；harbor 在選項換成 port。(B) 的 channel 取自第 2 段，講的是港口的地形，不是登船的時間點。

items.stem: How does the author conclude the passage in the last paragraph?
options: By giving advice to the general public.
items.explanation:
Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking.
The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.
末段把前面講過的內容再收一次：專業知識對應第 2 段，迅速獨立的判斷對應第 3 段的潮汐和風，船和海洋環境的安全對應第 2 段的擱淺與貨物外洩，所以是總結重點，沒有新的細節，也沒有預測或給一般大眾的建議。

閱讀測驗.title: 橄欖油的等級與保存（The Grades and Storage of Olive Oil）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Probably the most widely used oil in cooking, olive oil is made by crushing olives with stone or steel blades to release the oil. Extra virgin oil, the finest grade, is made from the first pressing of the olives and has a very low acidity rate (under 1%). To be qualified as “extra virgin,” the oil must also pass both an official test in a laboratory and a sensory evaluation by a trained tasting panel. It must be free from impurity, while exhibiting some fruitiness and creating a pleasant bitter flavor along with a peppery sensation in the mouth. Second on the ranking is virgin olive oil. It is also a first pressing, but has a slightly higher acidity level (under 2%). Lastly, pure olive oil is the cheapest olive oil. It is refined to remove its impurities and blended to improve flavor, and is recommended for all-purpose cooking.

Packaging and storage also have an impact on the quality of olive oil. Olive oil spoils quickly when exposed to direct sunlight, so it should be stored in the dark at 16-18°C. Moisture and oxygen promote oxidation and therefore limit its shelf life. Plastic containers usually do not provide adequate protection from light, heat, or moisture; additionally, small particles in plastics can leak into the oil, which further reduces its quality.

Olive oil tasters have long adopted descriptive terms such as “pure” and “light” to evaluate the quality of olive oil. Recently, however, the International Olive Council (IOC) is seeking input on test methods to improve the transparency of the testing process and boost the accuracy of the results. A redefinition of the term “olive oil” is also proposed to make a clear distinction between virgin olive oil and pure olive oil. Industry members of the IOC hope to promote the trade of olive oil by initiating these changes.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
橄欖油大概是烹飪時用得最廣的油，製作方式是用石頭或鋼製的刀片壓碎橄欖，讓油流出來。特級初榨橄欖油是最高等級，取自橄欖的第一道壓榨，酸度非常低（低於 1%）。要稱得上「特級初榨」，這種油還必須通過實驗室的官方檢驗，以及受過訓練的品油小組的感官評鑑。它不能有任何雜質，同時要帶點果香，入口有討喜的苦味和胡椒般的辛辣感。排名第二的是初榨橄欖油，同樣是第一道壓榨，但酸度略高（低於 2%）。最後是精製橄欖油，也就是最便宜的橄欖油；它經過精煉去除雜質，再調和改善風味，建議用在一般的烹調。

包裝和保存方式也會影響橄欖油的品質。橄欖油直接照到陽光很快就會變質，所以應該存放在 16 至 18°C 的陰暗處。濕氣和氧氣會促進氧化，因此縮短保存期限。塑膠容器通常無法充分阻隔光線、熱和濕氣；此外，塑膠裡的微粒可能滲入油中，讓品質進一步下降。

長久以來，品油師一直用「純」「淡」這類描述性的字眼來評定橄欖油的品質。不過，國際橄欖油理事會（IOC）最近正在徵詢對檢驗方法的意見，希望提高檢驗過程的透明度，並提升結果的準確性。理事會也提議重新定義「橄欖油」這個名稱，清楚區分初榨橄欖油和精製橄欖油。IOC 的業界成員希望藉由這些改變，促進橄欖油的貿易。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
items.explanation: 第 1 段講橄欖油的等級，第 2 段講包裝和保存對品質的影響，第 3 段講國際橄欖油理事會想改進檢驗方法，三段都繞著橄欖油的品質，所以答案是 (D)。(A) 風味只在第 1 段談特級初榨的條件時提到，(B) 貿易、(C) 推廣都只出現在第 3 段最後一句，三個錯誤選項都過於狹隘。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about extra virgin olive oil?
options: It is free from any bitter flavor.
It is refined to remove its impurities.
It requires mixing of more than one kind of oil.
It has a lower acidity rate than virgin olive oil.
items.explanation:
Extra virgin oil, the finest grade, is made from the first pressing of the olives and has a very low acidity rate (under 1%).
It is also a first pressing, but has a slightly higher acidity level (under 2%).
第 1 段說特級初榨的酸度低於 1%，初榨橄欖油的酸度略高、低於 2%，反過來說，就是特級初榨的酸度比初榨低。(A) 照抄 bitter flavor，原文說特級初榨要有討喜的苦味，不是沒有苦味；(B) 照抄 remove its impurities，那是精製橄欖油的做法；(C) 把幾種油調和在一起，說的也是精製橄欖油（blended），不是特級初榨。

items.stem: According to the passage, what is the best way to store olive oil?
options: In a plastic container in a damp cellar.
In a clear glass bottle near the kitchen stove.
In an airtight glass bottle in a kitchen cupboard.
In an airproof bottle next to a well-lighted window.
items.explanation:
Olive oil spoils quickly when exposed to direct sunlight, so it should be stored in the dark at 16-18°C.
Moisture and oxygen promote oxidation and therefore limit its shelf life.
第 2 段說橄欖油要避光、存放在 16 至 18°C，濕氣和氧氣會加速氧化，塑膠容器也不適合。放在廚房櫥櫃裡的密封玻璃瓶，可以避光、隔絕空氣，溫度也不會太高，所以選 (C)。(A) 照抄 plastic container，原文正好說塑膠容器擋不住光、熱和濕氣，潮濕的地窖也不行；(B) 透明玻璃瓶擋不住光，放在爐子旁邊又太熱；(D) 窗邊光線充足，油很快就會變質。

items.stem: What is the IOC trying to do?
options: Train more qualified olive oil tasters.
Improve the ways of grading olive oil.
Look for new techniques to boost production.
Build better connections among industry members.
items.explanation:
Recently, however, the International Olive Council (IOC) is seeking input on test methods to improve the transparency of the testing process and boost the accuracy of the results.
第 3 段說 IOC 正在徵詢對檢驗方法的意見，要讓檢驗更透明、結果更準確，也就是改進評定橄欖油等級的方式；test methods 在選項換成 ways of grading。(C) 照抄 boost，原文提升的是檢驗結果的準確性，不是產量；(D) 照抄 industry members，原文說業界成員希望藉此促進貿易，沒有說要加強彼此的聯繫；(A) 照抄 tasters，原文只說品油師一向用描述性的字眼評定品質，沒有說要訓練更多品油師。

閱讀測驗.title: 用聲音驅趕鹿隻（Using Sound to Deter Deer）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Researchers in Japan have installed on a train a speaker that barks like a dog and snorts like a deer in order to prevent collisions with animals on the tracks.

The country has been troubled by a problem with trains colliding with deer on its railways. According to Japan’s transport ministry, there were 613 cases of train services suspended or delayed for at least 30 minutes resulting from collisions with deer and other wild animals in 2016-17.

Deer are attracted to railway lines because of a need for iron in their diets. They lick the rails to pick up iron filings caused by the action of wheels against tracks. This dietary need has led to a constant battle to keep the deer separate from the unforgiving nature of tons of onrushing rolling stock. In the past, flashing red lights and even lion faces have been unsuccessfully trialed in an attempt to keep deer off the tracks.

This new device has been invented by a team at the country’s Railway Technical Research Institute (RTRI). RTRI officials explain that deer have a habit of repeatedly snorting short, shrill sounds to alert other deer when they perceive danger. The barking of the hound, which drives deer to panic, strengthens the effect of the warning noise, according to the RTRI. When the deer hear a combination of a 3-second-long recording of a deer’s snort and 20 seconds of a barking dog, they panic and flee rapidly.

RTRI researchers say late-night tests, at times when deer are most frequently seen by railway tracks, have resulted in a 45 percent reduction of deer sighting. Future plans include static barking sites where deer are commonly seen, but “the noises will not be blared in areas where people live beside the tracks.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
日本的研究人員在火車上裝了一個喇叭，可以發出狗吠聲和鹿鳴聲，用來防止火車撞上軌道上的動物。

火車在鐵路上撞到鹿，一直是日本頭痛的問題。根據日本國土交通省的資料，2016 至 2017 年間，因為撞上鹿和其他野生動物，火車停駛或延誤 30 分鐘以上的情形共有 613 起。

鹿之所以靠近鐵路，是因為飲食中需要鐵質。車輪和鐵軌摩擦會產生鐵屑，鹿就舔鐵軌來攝取這些鐵屑。這種飲食上的需求，讓人們不斷設法讓鹿遠離重達數噸、疾駛而來、毫不留情的列車。過去也曾經試過閃爍的紅燈，甚至獅子的臉，想讓鹿遠離鐵軌，但都沒有成功。

這個新裝置是日本鐵道綜合技術研究所（RTRI）的團隊發明的。RTRI 的人員說明，鹿察覺危險時，習慣重複發出短促尖銳的鳴聲，警告其他的鹿。RTRI 表示，狗吠聲會讓鹿陷入恐慌，可以加強警告聲的效果。鹿聽到 3 秒的鹿鳴錄音加上 20 秒的狗吠聲，就會驚慌失措，迅速逃開。

RTRI 的研究人員說，他們在鹿最常出現在鐵軌旁的深夜時段進行測試，結果看到鹿的次數減少了 45%。未來計畫在鹿經常出現的地點設置固定的狗吠裝置，不過「鐵軌旁有住家的地區不會播放這些聲音」。

items.stem: Why are deer attracted to train tracks?
options: They mate at night near railways.
They need nutrition from train tracks.
They like to snort at the passing train.
They sharpen their horns rubbing against the rails.
items.explanation:
Deer are attracted to railway lines because of a need for iron in their diets.
They lick the rails to pick up iron filings caused by the action of wheels against tracks.
第 3 段第一句說鹿的飲食需要鐵質，下一句說牠們舔鐵軌上的鐵屑；選項把 a need for iron 換成 need nutrition。(D) 照抄 rails，原文是舔鐵軌，不是在鐵軌上磨角；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 snort，那是鹿察覺危險時警告同伴的叫聲，和鹿靠近鐵軌的原因無關；(A) 夜間交配，文章沒有提。

items.stem: What device has NOT been used to solve the railway problem in Japan?
items.explanation:
Researchers in Japan have installed on a train a speaker that barks like a dog and snorts like a deer in order to prevent collisions with animals on the tracks.
In the past, flashing red lights and even lion faces have been unsuccessfully trialed in an attempt to keep deer off the tracks.
三個有提到的裝置都換了說法：第 3 段的 flashing red lights 是 (A) Flashing lights，lion faces 是 (D) Lion face paintings；第 1 段裝在火車上、會學狗叫的 speaker 是 (B) Barking speakers。文章沒有提到會發出噪音的鐵軌，所以選 (C)。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about the deer issue discussed in the passage?
options: RTRI’s new invention prompts deer to run away.
People living near the tracks complain about deer snorts.
45 percent of train delays in Japan was caused by deer collision.
A combination of sound and visual devices attracts more deer to the tracks.
items.explanation:
When the deer hear a combination of a 3-second-long recording of a deer’s snort and 20 seconds of a barking dog, they panic and flee rapidly.
第 4 段說鹿聽到 3 秒的鹿鳴錄音加上 20 秒的狗吠，就會驚慌逃走；flee rapidly 在選項換成 run away。(C) 照抄第 5 段的 45 percent，原文說的是測試後看到鹿的次數減少 45%，不是火車延誤有 45% 是撞鹿造成的；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 combination，原文組合的是兩種聲音，而且是要把鹿趕走，不是吸引鹿；(B) 照抄 snort，第 5 段只說有住家的地區不會播放這些聲音，沒有說居民抱怨。

items.stem: What does the author mean by “the unforgiving nature of tons of onrushing rolling stock” in the third paragraph?
options: The heavy weight of iron materials.
The cruelty of a barking hound.
The battle between deer and other animals.
The danger of a fast-moving train.
items.explanation:
This dietary need has led to a constant battle to keep the deer separate from the unforgiving nature of tons of onrushing rolling stock.
rolling stock 指鐵路上的車輛，tons of onrushing 是重達數噸、迎面疾駛而來，unforgiving 是毫不留情，整個詞組說的就是高速行駛的火車有多危險。(C) 照抄同一句的 battle，原文是人想讓鹿遠離火車的長期抗戰，不是鹿和其他動物之間的戰鬥；(A) 照抄 iron，鐵質是鹿想吃的東西，不是這個詞組的意思；(B) 狗吠是第 4 段的新裝置，和這裡無關。

閱讀測驗.title: 羅傑·伊伯特影展歡迎詞（Welcome to Roger Ebert’s Film Festival）
閱讀測驗.passage:
I am thrilled to welcome you to the 20th annual Roger Ebert’s Film Festival, a special event in partnership with the University of Illinois College of Media, the greater Champaign-Urbana community, and movie lovers everywhere. Little did we think, back in 1999, that our experiment in reinventing the film festival—to make a festival that celebrated overlooked films, formats and genres, and the women and men who made those films—would become a landmark annual event in the life of our community and contribute to the renovation of the remarkable Virginia Theater, our home from the very beginning.

In selecting the films for this year, Chaz Ebert and I looked to women filmmakers for our inspiration. Fully half of our films are either directed or co-directed by women, and several others have women in powerful producing roles. Films directed or co-directed by women include “13th,” directed by Ava DuVernay, “Belle,” directed by Amma Asante, and “American Splendor,” directed by Shari Springer Berman and Robert Pulcini. And women producers include Lynda Obst and Emma Thomas (“Interstellar”) and Ruth Ann Harnisch and Danielle Renfrew Behrens (“Columbus”).

Our opening night film is “The Fugitive,” directed by University of Illinois alumnus Andrew Davis. Our Saturday night film is the classic “The Big Lebowski.” Our guest will be the Hollywood legend Jeff Dowd. And of course The Alloy Orchestra will be back, this year with “A Page of Madness,” the classic Japanese silent film.

We would like to thank our sponsors, volunteers, festival pass holders, and individual ticket holders for their welcome participation in this endeavor. We look forward to your unwavering support as our festival continues to blossom each spring in central Illinois. We especially want to thank the University of Illinois for their loyal support year after year.

This festival is Roger Ebert’s gift to his hometown, and for that we thank him and his wife Chaz. They continue to be a remarkable team, and it is an honor to work with them.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
我非常興奮，歡迎各位來參加第 20 屆羅傑·伊伯特影展。這個特別的活動，由伊利諾大學媒體學院、香檳–厄巴納（Champaign-Urbana）一帶的社區，以及各地的影迷共同參與。回到 1999 年，我們嘗試重新打造影展，想辦一個表揚受到忽略的電影、形式和類型，也表揚拍出這些電影的男男女女的影展。我們當時萬萬沒想到，這個實驗會成為社區生活裡具有指標意義的年度盛事，還幫忙修復了了不起的 Virginia 戲院，這座戲院從一開始就是影展的根據地。

今年選片的時候，Chaz Ebert 和我以女性電影人作為靈感來源。整整一半的影片由女性執導或共同執導，另外還有好幾部片子由女性擔任重要的製片。由女性執導或共同執導的影片，包括 Ava DuVernay 執導的《13th》、Amma Asante 執導的《Belle》，以及 Shari Springer Berman 和 Robert Pulcini 共同執導的《American Splendor》。女性製片則有《Interstellar》的 Lynda Obst 和 Emma Thomas，以及《Columbus》的 Ruth Ann Harnisch 和 Danielle Renfrew Behrens。

開幕片是伊利諾大學校友 Andrew Davis 執導的《The Fugitive》。星期六晚上放映的是經典電影《The Big Lebowski》。我們的嘉賓是好萊塢傳奇人物 Jeff Dowd。當然，Alloy 管弦樂團今年也會回來，帶來的是日本經典默片《A Page of Madness》。

我們要感謝贊助者、志工、影展通行證持有人和單場購票的觀眾，謝謝各位熱情參與。影展每年春天在伊利諾州中部持續茁壯，期待各位繼續堅定支持。我們特別要感謝伊利諾大學年年忠實的支持。

這個影展是羅傑·伊伯特送給家鄉的禮物，為此我們感謝他和他的妻子 Chaz。他們兩位一直是了不起的搭檔，能和他們一起工作，是我們的榮幸。

閱讀測驗.title: 風暴追逐的興起與安全問題（The Rise and Safety Issues of Storm Chasing）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Storm chasing is broadly defined as the pursuit of any severe weather condition, for reasons ranging from curiosity, adventure, and scientific exploration to media coverage.

Chasing often involves driving thousands of miles in order to witness a relatively short window of time of severe weather. It is not uncommon for a storm chaser to end up empty-handed on any particular day. Most storm chasers are not professional meteorologists, and many chasers devote significant time and effort to learning meteorology, the study of the atmosphere, and the weather forming process. The amount of equipment used for storm chasing also varies. Some prefer a minimalist approach where only basic photographic equipment is taken on a chase, while others use everything from satellite-based tracking systems and live data feeds to vehicle-mounted weather stations and hail guards.

There are inherent dangers involved in pursuing hazardous weather. These range from lightning and tornadoes to unsafe road conditions and reduced visibility from heavy rain. In some situations, a severe downburst airstream can happen unexpectedly and push automobiles around. Tornadoes affect a relatively small area and are predictable enough to be avoided if a safe distance is maintained. Lightning, however, is an unavoidable hazard. “Core punching,” which is storm chasers’ slang for driving through the part of a thunderstorm that has the heaviest rain to collect critical information, is recognized as extremely hazardous.

Today, interest in storm chasing has surged. Amateurs and YouTube fame seekers with video cameras now race with professionals to see who can get the closest and most dramatic images of churning storms, and this is causing a growing safety threat. A group of storm-chase veterans has advocated the adoption of a code of ethics emphasizing safety, courtesy, and objectivity. However, many chasers oppose self-policing, as is often the case with people involved in other dangerous leisure activities.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
追風暴（storm chasing）廣義來說，是指追逐任何惡劣的天氣，原因從好奇、冒險、科學探索到媒體報導都有。

追風暴常常要開好幾千英里的車，只為了親眼看到時間相對短暫的惡劣天氣。追風暴的人在某一天空手而回，並不少見。大部分追風暴的人都不是專業的氣象學家，很多人花了大量的時間和心力，學習氣象學，也就是研究大氣和天氣形成過程的學問。追風暴用的裝備多寡也各不相同。有些人喜歡極簡，追風暴時只帶基本的攝影器材；也有人從衛星追蹤系統、即時資料傳輸，到車上的氣象站和防冰雹罩，什麼都用上。

追逐危險的天氣，本身就有危險。這些危險從閃電、龍捲風，到不安全的路況、大雨造成的能見度降低都有。有時候，強烈的下爆氣流會突然出現，把汽車推來推去。龍捲風影響的範圍相對小，也相當可以預測，只要保持安全距離，就能避開。不過，閃電是避不開的危險。「core punching」是追風暴者的行話，指開車穿過雷雨中雨勢最大的區域，蒐集關鍵資料，大家公認這種做法極度危險。

如今，追風暴的熱潮急速升溫。帶著攝影機的業餘玩家和想在 YouTube 成名的人，現在和專業人士競爭，看誰能拍到最近、最震撼的翻騰風暴畫面，這帶來越來越大的安全威脅。一群資深的追風暴者提倡採用一套倫理守則，強調安全、禮貌和客觀。然而，許多追風暴者反對自我約束的規範，參與其他危險休閒活動的人，往往也是這樣。

items.explanation:
and this is causing a growing safety threat.
第 4 段說如今追風暴越來越熱門，業餘玩家和想在 YouTube 成名的人搶拍風暴畫面，帶來越來越大的安全威脅（safety threat），所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 media coverage，媒體報導是追風暴的原因之一；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 weather condition，惡劣天氣是追逐的對象，不是熱潮帶來的新問題；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 Equipment，原文只說裝備多寡不同，沒有談到費用。

items.explanation:

第 4 段說一群資深的追風暴者提倡採用倫理守則（a code of ethics），而且這套守則強調安全。他們提倡守則，又特別強調安全，可見他們認為守則能降低追風暴的危險，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 ethics，原文最後一句說參與其他危險休閒活動的人，往往也反對自我約束，意思正好相反；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 meteorologists，原文說大部分追風暴的人不是氣象學家，沒有說大部分氣象學家追過龍捲風；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 media，媒體報導本來就是追風暴的原因之一，第 4 段又說有人想在 YouTube 成名，不能推論追風暴還沒有引起媒體注意。

閱讀測驗.title: 育空路標森林的起源與特色（Origin and Characteristics of Yukon's Signpost Forest）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Deep within the Yukon, one of the most densely wooded areas of Canada, sits a patch of land that is unlike any other forest on the planet. Instead of a canopy of treetops spreading across the horizon, tens of thousands of signposts perch haphazardly one on top of the other. They are all part of the Signpost Forest, the largest collection of signs from places around the world. At last count, the Signpost Forest in Watson Lake, located about 10 miles north of the U.S.-Canadian border, contains 91,000 signs from spots near and far, including Berlin, Moscow, Dublin, and Hawaii.

The tradition began during the Alaska Highway Project in 1942, when U.S. soldier Carl K. Lindley spent time in Watson Lake recovering from an injury. A commanding officer asked him to repair and erect the directional signposts, and while completing the job, the homesick soldier added a sign that indicated the direction and mileage to his hometown: “Danville, Illinois, 2,835 miles.” Others followed suit, and the trend caught on. Each year, an average of 1,000 new signs are being added to the collection. Lindley’s original sign has since been lost to time. Fifty years later, in 1992, Lindley and his wife Elinor made the pilgrimage back to Watson Lake to place a replica, which is still there.

The Signpost Forest takes up a couple of acres, with huge panels snaking through the trees. There are street signs, welcome signs, signatures on dinner plates, and license plates from around the world. There are also a lot of familial signs; for example, a grandfather will put up a sign and then years later family will come back and try to find it. A lot of these are personal signs to literally say that they are here. Though the visitor center has wood and paints on hand to help create a sign, many people opt to bring their own signs, though illegally, by snatching a metal sign from their hometown and nailing it to one of the wood posts. The forest has grown so vast that the visitor center no longer tries to keep a detailed list of the signs.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
育空地區是加拿大林木最茂密的地區之一，在育空深處，有一片和地球上其他森林都不一樣的土地。放眼望去，看到的不是一片延伸到地平線的樹冠，而是好幾萬個雜亂地一個疊著一個的路標。這些路標都屬於「路標森林」，這裡是全世界蒐集各地路標最多的地方。根據最近一次的統計，位在美加邊界以北約 10 英里處、Watson Lake 的路標森林，共有 91,000 塊來自遠近各地的牌子，包括柏林、莫斯科、都柏林和夏威夷。

這個傳統始於 1942 年的阿拉斯加公路工程。當時，美國士兵 Carl K. Lindley 在 Watson Lake 養傷，一位指揮官要他修理、豎立指示方向的路標。想家的 Lindley 在完成工作的時候，加上了一塊牌子，標出家鄉的方向和里程：「伊利諾州丹維爾，2,835 英里」。其他人也跟著這樣做，這股風氣就流行起來。每年平均有 1,000 塊新的牌子加進來。Lindley 原來的那塊牌子，隨著時間過去，已經遺失了。五十年後的 1992 年，Lindley 和妻子 Elinor 專程回到 Watson Lake，放上一塊複製品，這塊複製品到現在還在那裡。

路標森林占地好幾英畝，一片片巨大的板子在樹林間蜿蜒。這裡有路牌、歡迎牌、簽了名的餐盤，還有來自世界各地的車牌。也有很多家族的牌子，例如祖父立了一塊牌子，多年以後，家人回來想找到它。這些牌子很多是私人的，就是要告訴大家「我們來過這裡」。雖然遊客中心備有木板和顏料，可以幫忙做牌子，很多人還是選擇自己帶牌子來，有些人甚至違法從家鄉拔下金屬路牌，釘在其中一根木柱上。這片森林已經大到遊客中心不再試著詳細記錄每一塊牌子。

items.stem: What does “The tradition” in the second paragraph refer to?
options: Counting the number of signs in the Signpost Forest.
Replacing the natural forest with signs of different kinds.
Putting directional signposts on the highways of the Yukon.
Bringing signs to the Signpost Forest from around the world.
items.explanation:
the largest collection of signs from places around the world
Others followed suit, and the trend caught on.
第 1 段介紹路標森林，說這裡是全世界蒐集各地路標最多的地方（the largest collection of signs from places around the world）。第 2 段一開頭說 The tradition began…，接著講 Lindley 加上指向家鄉的牌子，其他人跟著做，這股風氣就流行起來。所以 The tradition 指的是從世界各地帶牌子來路標森林的做法，是 (D)。(C) 照抄 directional signposts，修理、豎立指示方向的路標是指揮官交給 Lindley 的工作，不是後來大家跟著做的傳統；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 count，統計路標數量只是用來說明森林的規模；(B) 原文說這片土地看不到樹冠，但沒有說有人砍掉森林、換成牌子。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about the first sign in the Signpost Forest?
options: It remained in the Forest until 1992.
It was erected by an American soldier.
It was first put on the Alaska Highway.
It was brought from Lindley’s hometown.
items.explanation:
U.S. soldier Carl K. Lindley spent time in Watson Lake recovering from an injury.
the homesick soldier added a sign that indicated the direction and mileage to his hometown
第 2 段說路標森林的第一塊牌子，是美國士兵（U.S. soldier）Carl K. Lindley 在 Watson Lake 養傷、修理路標的時候加上的，選項換成 American soldier，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 1992，原來的牌子早就遺失了，1992 年放的是 Lindley 回去補上的複製品；(D) 照抄 hometown，那塊牌子標的是往他家鄉的方向和里程，不是從家鄉帶來的，從家鄉拔路牌來的是第 3 段說的其他人；(C) 照抄 Alaska Highway，阿拉斯加公路工程是當時進行中的工程，原文說牌子是在 Watson Lake 加上的，沒有說先放在公路上。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word “replica” in the second paragraph?
items.explanation:

items.stem: What is the last paragraph mainly about?

The quantity and variety of the signs in the Signpost Forest.

閱讀測驗.title: 匯率的歷史演變與體系（The Historical Evolution and Systems of Exchange Rates）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In finance, an exchange rate is the rate at which one country’s currency is exchanged for the currency of another. The rate is set according to the respective values of the currencies to be exchanged. Before World War I, most currencies were evaluated by the Gold Standard. That is, paper currency issued by a government represented a real amount of gold held by that government. For example, in the 1930s, the British government owned about 8 times as much gold as the U.S. government. Therefore, 1 ounce of gold was worth 4.24 GBP (United Kingdom pound sterling) or 35 USD (U.S. dollars). The difference in the price of gold became the exchange rate for the two currencies: 1GBP was worth 8.25 USD.

The Gold Standard started to break down during the Second World War, when European powers printed more money than they had in gold reserves in order to fund military projects. After World War II, the Bretton Woods System was established. The U.S. dollar was chosen as the international reserve currency for trading. Every country knew how much gold a USD was worth, and thus they based the value of their currencies on the USD. All countries were expected to maintain a fixed exchange rate, but were permitted to change it in extraordinary times, such as a recession or inflation.

Unfortunately, this system could not keep pace with the fast-changing global economy. As the U.S. increased its military spending, foreign aid, and international investment in the 1960s, it no longer held gold reserves necessary to cover the volume of USD circulation around the world. Other major currencies thus became more valuable and stable compared to the USD, and the Bretton Woods System was finally abolished in 1971.

In 1976, the Jamaica Agreement formalized the floating exchange rate system that continues to this day. The value of a country’s currency may vary according to the supply and demand of the foreign exchange market. Countries around the world can also allow their central banks to determine their own exchange rate.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
在金融上，匯率是一國貨幣兌換另一國貨幣的比率。匯率依照要兌換的兩種貨幣各自的價值來決定。第一次世界大戰以前，大多數貨幣的價值都以金本位評定。也就是說，政府發行的紙幣，代表政府實際持有的一定數量的黃金。例如在 1930 年代，英國政府擁有的黃金大約是美國政府的 8 倍。因此，1 盎司黃金值 4.24 英鎊（GBP），或 35 美元（USD）。黃金價格的差異，就成了這兩種貨幣的匯率：1 英鎊值 8.25 美元。

第二次世界大戰期間，歐洲列強為了支應軍事計畫，印出超過黃金儲備的鈔票，金本位開始瓦解。二戰以後，布列敦森林體系建立。美元獲選為國際貿易的儲備貨幣。每個國家都知道一美元值多少黃金，因此各國都以美元作為訂定本國貨幣價值的基準。所有國家原則上都要維持固定匯率，但遇到經濟衰退或通貨膨脹等特殊時期，可以調整匯率。

可惜的是，這個體系跟不上快速變化的全球經濟。1960 年代，美國增加軍事支出、對外援助和國際投資，持有的黃金儲備已經不足以支應全世界流通的美元數量。因此，其他主要貨幣和美元相比，變得更有價值、也更穩定，布列敦森林體系終於在 1971 年廢除。

1976 年，牙買加協定正式確立了沿用至今的浮動匯率制度。一國貨幣的價值，可能隨外匯市場的供需而變動。世界各國也可以讓中央銀行決定自己的匯率。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about the Gold Standard?
options: It showed the importance of gold for currency exchange.
It reflected the dominance of the U.S. economy in the world.
It demonstrated how rich countries manipulated exchange rates.
It decided that the GBP was worth less than the USD in the 1930s.
items.explanation:
paper currency issued by a government represented a real amount of gold held by that government.
The difference in the price of gold became the exchange rate for the two currencies
第 1 段說在金本位之下，政府發行的紙幣代表政府實際持有的黃金，兩國黃金價格的差異，就成了兩種貨幣的匯率。匯率是由黃金決定的，可見黃金對貨幣兌換非常重要，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 1930s，原文算出 1 英鎊值 8.25 美元，英鎊比美元值錢，不是比較不值錢；(B) 照抄 U.S.，原文說英國政府擁有的黃金大約是美國的 8 倍，看不出美國經濟獨霸世界；(C) 原文說匯率依黃金決定，沒有提到富國操縱匯率。

items.stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?
options: Changes in currency rates and European powers.
World War II and the drop in gold prices.
The rise of a new currency exchange system.
items.explanation:
After World War II, the Bretton Woods System was established.
they based the value of their currencies on the USD.
第 2 段第一句說金本位在二戰期間開始瓦解，接著說二戰以後建立了布列敦森林體系（the Bretton Woods System was established），各國以美元訂定本國貨幣的價值，維持固定匯率。這一段的重點是新的貨幣兌換體系出現，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 European powers，歐洲列強印鈔票只是金本位瓦解的原因；(A) 照抄 recession，經濟衰退只是可以調整匯率的特殊時期的例子；(C) 照抄 World War II，原文沒有提到金價下跌。

items.stem: What caused the Bretton Woods System to fail?
options: Major world powers fell into economic depression.
The U.S. did not have enough gold to cover the amount of U.S. dollars.
The system was too complicated for the practice of currency exchange.
European countries printed more paper money than they had in gold reserves.
items.explanation:
it no longer held gold reserves necessary to cover the volume of USD circulation around the world.
第 3 段說 1960 年代美國持有的黃金儲備，已經不足以支應（no longer held gold reserves necessary to cover）全世界流通的美元，其他貨幣因此比美元更穩定，布列敦森林體系終於廢除。選項換成 did not have enough gold to cover，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 than they had in gold reserves，歐洲列強印出超過黃金儲備的鈔票，是二戰期間金本位瓦解的原因，不是布列敦森林體系失敗的原因；(A) 原文沒有說世界強權陷入經濟蕭條；(C) 原文說的是這個體系跟不上快速變化的全球經濟，不是體系太複雜。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about the Jamaica Agreement?
options: Individual countries may not decide their own exchange rate.
In a recession, all countries need to follow a fixed exchange rate.
Gold is again used as the standard of the currency exchange rate.
Supply and demand in the currency market determines the exchange rate.
items.explanation:
may vary according to the supply and demand of the foreign exchange market.
第 4 段說牙買加協定確立了浮動匯率制度，一國貨幣的價值隨外匯市場的供需（supply and demand of the foreign exchange market）變動，選項換成 Supply and demand in the currency market，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 their own exchange rate，原文說各國可以讓中央銀行決定自己的匯率，選項加上 not，意思相反；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 fixed exchange rate，固定匯率是布列敦森林體系的做法；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 Gold，金本位在二戰期間就開始瓦解，牙買加協定沒有恢復金本位。

閱讀測驗.title: 現代廢水處理流程（Modern Wastewater Treatment Process）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Early civilizations often built drainage systems in urban areas to handle rainwater that ran down the street during a storm. The Romans constructed elaborate systems that also drained wastewater from the public baths. However, as the population of the cities grew, the old drainage systems became overloaded. During the Industrial Revolution, manufacturing waste was added to sewage, which increased the need for more efficient sewage treatment. In the mid-19th century, the first steps were taken to treat wastewater.

Sewage or wastewater treatment in modern times is the process of removing harmful physical, chemical, and biological elements from wastewater and house sewage. The whole process starts with screening out large objects such as paper and wood, and removing heavy materials like dirt. The screened wastewater is then ready to go through a series of concrete tanks for further treatment. In the second step, the sewage passes into the primary tanks. Here, human waste, called sludge, settles to the bottom while oils and grease float to the top, where they are collected. At the same time, organic matter like eggshells or coffee grounds in the sewage is broken down into smaller substances. The remaining sewage then enters the secondary tanks for the third stage of treatment. The solids that were not treated in the primary tanks are removed here through decomposition, which digests the material. Then, the liquid sewage is filtered through sand. This filtering process gets rid of almost all bacteria, as well as other solid particles that remain in the water. Finally, the wastewater flows into the last tanks, where the chemical chlorine is added to kill the remaining bacteria. After the bacteria are destroyed, the chlorine is eliminated from the water, and the treated clean water is discharged into a river or the ocean.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
早期的文明常在都市地區興建排水系統，處理暴風雨時順著街道流下的雨水。羅馬人建造了精密的排水系統，也排放公共浴場的廢水。然而，隨著城市人口增加，舊的排水系統變得不堪負荷。工業革命時期，製造業的廢棄物加進了汙水，處理汙水更需要有效率的方法。到了 19 世紀中期，人類開始踏出處理廢水的第一步。

現代的汙水（廢水）處理，是把廢水和家庭汙水中有害的物理、化學和生物成分去除的過程。整個過程從篩除紙張、木頭等大型物品開始，同時去除泥土等重物。篩過的廢水接著要流經一連串的混凝土池，做進一步的處理。第二步，汙水流進初級池。在這裡，人類的排泄物，也就是所謂的汙泥，沉到池底，油和油脂則浮到上面，收集起來。同時，汙水裡蛋殼、咖啡渣等有機物，會分解成比較小的物質。剩下的汙水接著進入二級池，做第三階段的處理。初級池沒有處理到的固體，在這裡經過分解，消化掉。然後，液態汙水用沙過濾。這道過濾程序可以去除幾乎所有的細菌，以及水中殘留的其他固體微粒。最後，廢水流進最後的池子，加入氯這種化學物質，殺死剩下的細菌。細菌消滅以後，再把水中的氯除去，處理乾淨的水就排進河川或海洋。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The ways to control manufacturing waste.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說明為什麼需要更有效率的汙水處理，第 2 段從篩除大型物品、初級池、二級池、沙過濾一直講到加氯消毒，一步一步介紹現代的廢水處理，所以是 (B)。(C) 排水系統的歷史只在第 1 段，是全文的引子，過於狹隘；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 elements，汙水裡的有害成分只是第 2 段第一句下定義時提到的，過於狹隘；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 manufacturing waste，製造業的廢棄物只是需要處理汙水的原因之一，全文沒有談怎麼控制這些廢棄物，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a reason for developing more effective systems to deal with wastewater?
options: Heavy rainfall due to climate change.
items.explanation:
as the population of the cities grew, the old drainage systems became overloaded.
manufacturing waste was added to sewage, which increased the need for more efficient sewage treatment.
第 1 段說城市人口增加（the population of the cities grew），是 (A)；舊的排水系統不堪負荷（became overloaded），是 (C)；工業革命時期製造業的廢棄物加進汙水，更需要有效率的處理方法，是 (B)。第 1 段雖然提到早期排水系統是用來處理暴風雨時的雨水，但全文沒有提到氣候變遷帶來大雨，所以選 (D)。

items.stem: Which of the following can be removed in the primary tanks?
items.explanation:
oils and grease float to the top, where they are collected.
這一題要照處理的步驟一步一步對。第 1 步，汙水還沒進池子以前，先篩掉紙張、木頭（wood）等大型物品，去除泥土等重物（heavy materials）；第 2 步才進初級池（primary tanks），這時汙泥沉到池底，油和油脂（grease）浮到上面，收集起來（collected），也就是在初級池去除了，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 wood、(B) 照抄 heavy material，都是在第 1 步、進初級池以前就去除了；(D) 照抄 organic matter，有機物在初級池只是分解成比較小的物質，還留在汙水裡，跟著進入二級池。

items.stem: What is the main reason that liquid sewage needs to go through sand?
items.explanation:
This filtering process gets rid of almost all bacteria
第 2 段說液態汙水用沙過濾，這道程序可以去除（gets rid of）幾乎所有的細菌，選項換成 eliminate，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 solid particles，沙過濾也去除殘留的固體微粒，但是去除，不是溶解；(D) 照抄 oil，油和油脂是在初級池浮上來收集的；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 drain，排水系統是早期處理雨水的方法，和沙過濾無關。

閱讀測驗.title: 馬里亞納海溝的深海污染（Deep-Sea Pollution in Mariana Trench）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The planet’s deepest point is in the Pacific Ocean’s Mariana Trench, which lies miles below the sea surface. According to a new study published in Nature Ecology & Evolution, even in this remote locale, creatures cannot escape pollution.

A team of researchers recently sent a remotely operated vehicle into the depths of the Mariana Trench. They found that extraordinarily high levels of forbidden industrial chemicals are contaminating marine life more than 7 miles deep in the trench. The small hard-shelled marine life that the robotic submarine brought to the surface was polluted with toxic chemicals, with toxin levels 50 times greater than those of the most heavily polluted rivers in the world.

These pollution levels were not the only alarming aspect of the discovery. The types of compounds found were all considered “persistent organic pollutants” (POPs), meaning they stick around in the environment for a very long time. Two of the most prevalent types are PCBs and PBDEs. PCBs were once used in many industrial applications, but were outlawed in the United States in the 1970s after being linked to cancer. Similarly, PBDEs were used in a wide range of products—from electronics to couch cushions. Neither chemical breaks down in the environment.

These compounds stick to the surface of materials like plastic. Many creatures mistakenly eat this colorful but toxic material, causing the POPs to build up in their bodies, lurking in their fat tissues. When these sea creatures die, their POP-riddled bodies sink to the ocean floor, where deep-sea marine life eat their remains. POPs are therefore transferred to other creatures along the food chain.

The Mariana Trench is many miles away from any industrial source. This suggests that these pollutants travel over long distances despite having been prohibited worldwide decades ago.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
地球最深的地方，在太平洋的馬里亞納海溝，位於海面下好幾英里。根據《Nature Ecology & Evolution》期刊最新發表的一項研究，即使在這麼偏遠的地方，生物也逃不過汙染。

一個研究團隊最近派了一具遙控載具潛入馬里亞納海溝深處。他們發現，在海溝 7 英里以下的深處，濃度極高的禁用工業化學物質正在汙染海洋生物。這艘機器潛水艇帶回海面的小型甲殼類海洋生物，體內有有毒的化學物質，毒素濃度是全世界汙染最嚴重的河川的 50 倍。

令人憂心的，不只是這些汙染程度。研究找到的化合物，全都屬於「持久性有機汙染物」（POPs），意思是這些物質會在環境中留存很長的時間。最常見的兩種是 PCBs 和 PBDEs。PCBs 過去用在許多工業用途上，但在 1970 年代發現和癌症有關以後，美國就禁用了。同樣地，PBDEs 也曾用在各式各樣的產品上，從電子產品到沙發坐墊都有。這兩種化學物質都不會在環境中分解。

這些化合物會附著在塑膠等材料的表面。很多生物誤吃了這些色彩鮮豔卻有毒的東西，POPs 就在牠們體內累積，潛藏在脂肪組織裡。這些海洋生物死後，充滿 POPs 的屍體沉到海底，深海的海洋生物再吃下這些遺骸。POPs 就這樣沿著食物鏈，傳到其他生物身上。

馬里亞納海溝離任何工業汙染源都有好幾英里遠。這表示，雖然這些汙染物幾十年前就已經在全球禁用，仍然能夠遠距離移動。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The decrease of polluted creatures in the food chain.
Using remote control in research on marine pollution.
Pollution of the deep sea by persistent toxic chemicals.
Types of chemical pollution caused by industrial applications.
items.explanation: 第 1 段說即使在地球最深的馬里亞納海溝，生物也逃不過汙染；第 2 段說海溝深處的生物體內有濃度極高的有毒化學物質；第 3 段說這些都是會在環境中留存很久的持久性有機汙染物；第 4、5 段說明這些汙染物怎麼沿著食物鏈、長距離傳到深海。全文講的是持久性有毒化學物質汙染深海，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 remote，遙控載具只是研究用的工具，過於狹隘；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 industrial applications，化學物質的種類和用途只是第 3 段的內容，過於狹隘；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 food chain，原文說汙染物沿著食物鏈傳下去，沒有說受汙染的生物變少，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “POP-riddled” in paragraph 4?
items.explanation:
causing the POPs to build up in their bodies, lurking in their fat tissues.
第 4 段先說生物誤吃了沾著 POPs 的塑膠，POPs 就在牠們體內累積（build up in their bodies），潛藏在脂肪組織裡；接著說這些生物死後，POP-riddled 的屍體沉到海底。體內累積了大量 POPs 的屍體，就是充滿 POPs 的屍體，所以是 (B)。be riddled with 是「充滿（不好的東西）」。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 operated，遙控操作的是研究用的載具；(C) 完成、(D) 丟棄，都接不上前一句說的累積。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
options: PCBs are often used in making electronic products.
Chemicals washed down to the ocean stay on the surface.
The deepest point of the Mariana Trench is free from pollution.
A robotic vehicle was used to help study pollution in the Mariana Trench.
items.explanation:
A team of researchers recently sent a remotely operated vehicle into the depths of the Mariana Trench.
第 2 段說研究團隊派了一具遙控載具（remotely operated vehicle）潛入馬里亞納海溝，後面也稱它為 robotic submarine，選項換成 A robotic vehicle was used，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 electronic，用在電子產品上的是 PBDEs，不是 PCBs；(B) 照抄第 4 段的 surface，化合物附著在塑膠的表面，生物死後還會沉到海底，不是一直留在海面；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 deepest point，原文說即使在最深的地方，生物也逃不過汙染。

items.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: Marine pollution poses a threat to human health.
Strict regulations are being developed to stop ocean pollution.
PCBs and PBDEs become less harmful over long periods of time.
Chemical pollution is more serious in rivers than in industrial areas.
items.explanation:
were outlawed in the United States in the 1970s after being linked to cancer.
POPs are therefore transferred to other creatures along the food chain.
這一題要把兩段合起來推論。第 3 段說 PCBs 發現和癌症有關（linked to cancer）以後，美國就禁用了；第 4 段說 POPs 會沿著食物鏈傳到其他生物身上。人吃海裡的魚貝，也在這條食物鏈上，海洋裡的這些汙染物就可能進到人體，所以可以推論海洋汙染威脅人類健康，是 (A)。(C) 照抄 PCBs and PBDEs，原文說這兩種化學物質都不會在環境中分解，時間久了也不會變得比較無害；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 rivers，原文是拿汙染最嚴重的河川來比較海溝生物體內的毒素濃度，沒有比較河川和工業區；(B) 第 5 段說這些汙染物幾十年前就已經禁用，沒有提到正在制定新的法規。

閱讀測驗.title: 紐西蘭全黑隊與毛利哈卡舞（New Zealand’s All Blacks and the Māori Haka）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The All Blacks, New Zealand’s national rugby team, is widely credited for bringing the “haka” to the world stage. Immediately before kick-off, the whole team will issue a warlike chant, stamping their feet, slapping their thighs, rolling their eyes, flicking their tongues, and making aggressive gestures in unison. This performance before each match, which is intended to heighten their morale and intimidate opponents, is a sight to behold. No other international sporting team possesses a pre-match ritual as powerful as the famed All Blacks haka.

What does “haka” mean? Haka is often thought of as a broad term for Māori war dances traditionally used to intimidate the enemy and prepare the warriors for battle. Most people believe it was performed either on the battlefield prior to engaging the enemy, or as the warriors were leaving their own village en route to a battle. But in the language of Māori, the word haka simply means a dance. The dance is accompanied by a chant that expresses emotions or tells ancient stories. While many haka should be performed by males, there are some haka that can be performed by anyone, male or female. There are even some women-only haka.

Thanks to the All Blacks, two of the haka have become widely renowned: Ka Mate and Kapa o Pango. The former was composed by a Māori chief in the early 1800s about how he outsmarted his enemies. It was first performed by the All Blacks in 1906. The latter was written specifically for the team in 2005. They are now performed interchangeably by the All Blacks.

Today, different varieties of haka are performed on various ceremonial occasions—from receiving distinguished guests to birthdays, weddings, or the funerals of chiefs and people of high status. Though the practice had traditionally been limited to Māori communities, it has now spread far beyond that. Māori and New Zealanders of European heritage alike view doing the haka with a sense of pride, both on the rugby field and outside it. The haka has become the most recognizable symbol of New Zealanders as a people.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
全黑隊（All Blacks）是紐西蘭國家橄欖球隊，一般公認，是他們把「哈卡」（haka）帶上了世界舞台。比賽一開球之前，全隊會齊聲喊出好戰的吟唱，一面跺腳、拍打大腿、轉動眼珠、吐舌頭，一面做出各種威嚇的動作，動作整齊劃一。這是全黑隊每場比賽前的表演，目的是提振自己的士氣、震懾對手，場面十分壯觀。沒有其他國際運動隊伍的賽前儀式，像著名的全黑隊哈卡舞這麼有氣勢。

「哈卡」是什麼意思？一般人常把哈卡當作毛利戰舞的統稱，傳統上用來威嚇敵人，讓戰士做好作戰的準備。大多數人認為，哈卡是在戰場上和敵人交戰之前，或是戰士離開自己的村落、前往戰場的途中表演的。不過，在毛利語中，haka 這個字只是「舞蹈」的意思。跳舞的時候會搭配吟唱，用來表達情感或講述古老的故事。雖然很多哈卡應該由男性表演，也有一些哈卡不分男女，誰都可以跳，甚至還有一些只限女性的哈卡。

因為全黑隊的關係，有兩支哈卡變得廣為人知：Ka Mate 和 Kapa o Pango。前者是一位毛利酋長在 1800 年代初創作的，內容是他怎麼智取敵人，全黑隊在 1906 年第一次表演這支哈卡。後者是 2005 年專門替全黑隊寫的。現在全黑隊兩支都會表演，交替使用。

現在，各種不同的哈卡在許多典禮場合表演，從迎接貴賓到生日、婚禮，或是酋長和地位崇高的人的葬禮都有。表演哈卡傳統上只限於毛利社群，現在卻已經普及到毛利社群以外。不論是毛利人，還是歐洲裔的紐西蘭人，都以跳哈卡為榮，在橄欖球場上是這樣，在球場外也是。哈卡已經成為紐西蘭人最具代表性的象徵。

items.stem: Which of the following best describes the tone of this article?
items.explanation: 作者介紹哈卡的意義、來源和現在的用途，用的都是正面的說法：第 1 段說全黑隊賽前的哈卡場面壯觀（a sight to behold），沒有其他隊伍的賽前儀式這麼有氣勢；第 4 段說毛利人和歐洲裔的紐西蘭人都以跳哈卡為榮，哈卡已經成為紐西蘭人最具代表性的象徵。作者對這項傳統抱著尊重的態度，所以是 (D)。全文沒有嘲諷，(A) 憤世嫉俗不對；也沒有開玩笑，(B) 幽默不對；更沒有擔心哈卡會消失，(C) 悲觀不對。

which is intended to heighten their morale and intimidate opponents

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word “practice” in the last paragraph?

Though the practice had traditionally been limited to
最後一段第一句說各種哈卡在許多典禮場合表演（are performed），下一句的 the practice 接著談同一件事：表演哈卡傳統上只限於毛利社群，現在已經普及。the practice 指的就是表演哈卡這個做法，最接近 (B) Performance。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 sporting，運動是全黑隊從事的項目，但哈卡在婚禮、葬禮上也跳，不是運動；(C) 比賽、(D) 職業，都接不上前一句說的表演。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

different varieties of haka are performed on various ceremonial occasions

最後一段說現在哈卡在迎接貴賓、婚禮、葬禮等典禮場合（ceremonial occasions）表演，而且毛利人和歐洲裔的紐西蘭人（New Zealanders of European heritage）都以跳哈卡為榮。選項把典禮場合換成 important events，把歐洲裔的紐西蘭人換成 non-Māori New Zealanders，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄最後一段的 limited to，傳統上只限於毛利社群，不是只限男性戰士，第 2 段還說有些哈卡男女都能跳，甚至有只限女性的；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 war dance，那是一般人的看法，接著 But 一轉，說在毛利語中 haka 只是「舞蹈」的意思；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 1906，1906 年全黑隊第一次表演的是 Ka Mate，Kapa o Pango 是 2005 年才寫的，不可能從 1906 年起就輪流表演。

閱讀測驗.title: 美國聯邦教育法案ESSA與評估改革（US Federal Education Act ESSA and Assessment Reform）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In 2015, President Obama of the USA signed the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA), replacing the Bush-era No Child Left Behind (NCLB) that had been in effect since 2001. This new Act provides states with more decision-making power regarding curriculum, instruction, and assessment. Below are some big-picture ideas influencing many states as they approach the assessment task.

One important idea is flexibility. For years, states have used standardized K-12 assessments, similar to the SAT and ACT for college application, to measure student achievement. They are easy to use, but they fail to give a complete picture of how a student is progressing. Thus, states are rethinking one-size-fits-all standardized assessments and are instead considering personalized, student-centered assessments in schools. Obviously, the task is difficult and time-consuming. Fortunately, modern technology can help solve this dilemma. For instance, computer adaptive assessments can automatically adjust questions based on a student’s performances on the previous questions. This mechanism prevents the computer from giving questions that are obviously too easy or too difficult for the student. It thus allows teachers to quickly assess a student’s level of understanding and provide instant feedback to help in the learning process.

Another idea is multi-subject testing. Several states have started to incorporate subjects beyond the traditional math and reading items in their K-12 assessments. All 50 states include tests on science at least twice prior to senior high school, and some are now starting to include social studies, government, or economics. Some states are also moving toward assessing multiple subjects on one test, for example, reading and social studies.

A third idea is the emphasis on students’ learning process. In pursuit of a student-centered approach, many states are putting more emphasis on assessments throughout the learning process rather than on traditional end-of-year summative tests. Teachers are encouraged to accumulate data at different points in their students’ learning process. These data together present a more complete picture of a student’s learning.

The last idea regards the purpose of assessment. Assessment should be used to inform both teachers’ instruction and students’ learning. Teachers can modify their teaching based on students’ performance on tests; students can identify their own problems and make plans for improvement.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
2015 年，美國總統歐巴馬簽署了《每個學生都成功法》（ESSA），取代小布希時代從 2001 年起實施的《有教無類法》（NCLB）。這項新法讓各州在課程、教學和評量上，有更多的決定權。以下是影響許多州規劃評量工作的幾個大方向。

一個重要的方向是彈性。多年來，各州都用從幼稚園到 12 年級（K-12）的標準化評量來測量學生的學習成就，就像申請大學用的 SAT 和 ACT 一樣。這些評量容易使用，卻無法完整呈現學生的學習進展。因此，各州正在重新思考這種一體適用的標準化評量，改為考慮在學校採用個人化、以學生為中心的評量。顯然，這項工作既困難又費時。幸好，現代科技可以幫忙解決這個難題。例如，電腦適性測驗可以依照學生前面幾題的表現，自動調整題目。這套機制能避免電腦出明顯太簡單或太難的題目給學生，讓老師很快就能評估學生理解的程度，立即給予回饋，幫助學生學習。

另一個方向是多科目測驗。有幾個州已經開始在 K-12 評量中，加入傳統的數學和閱讀以外的科目。全部 50 個州在高中以前，都至少考兩次自然科學，有些州現在也開始加考社會、公民或經濟。有些州還朝著在一份測驗裡同時評量多個科目發展，例如閱讀加上社會。

第三個方向是重視學生的學習過程。為了以學生為中心，許多州更重視學習過程中的評量，而不是傳統的學年末總結性測驗。老師也受到鼓勵，在學生學習過程的不同時間點累積資料。這些資料合在一起，可以更完整地呈現學生的學習情形。

最後一個方向和評量的目的有關。評量應該同時用來引導老師的教學和學生的學習。老師可以依照學生在測驗中的表現調整教學；學生可以找出自己的問題，擬定改進的計畫。

items.stem: Which of the following is the best title for this passage?
options: From NCLB to ESSA, with a Focus on Assessment
items.explanation: 第 1 段先說 ESSA 取代了 NCLB，讓各州在課程、教學、評量上有更多決定權，最後一句說 Below are some big-picture ideas influencing many states as they approach the assessment task，點出後面要談的是各州規劃評量（assessment）的方向；第 2 到 5 段依序談彈性、多科目測驗、重視學習過程、評量的目的，四段都在講評量。標題要同時涵蓋從 NCLB 換成 ESSA，以及談的重點是評量，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (B)：後面四段是影響各州的四個大方向（ideas influencing many states），不是 ESSA 這個法案的四個組成部分，偏離主題。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 student-centered，全文談的是評量，不是課程和教學，偏離主題；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 computer，電腦適性測驗只是第 2 段舉的例子，過於狹隘。

items.stem: What does the word “dilemma” in paragraph 2 refer to?
options: The choice between SAT and ACT.
The choice between NCLB and ESSA.
Whether or not to use student-centered assessment.
Whether or not to replace computer-based assessment.
items.explanation:
Thus, states are rethinking one-size-fits-all standardized assessments and are instead considering personalized, student-centered assessments in schools.
Obviously, the task is difficult and time-consuming.
第 2 段先說標準化評量容易使用，卻無法完整呈現學生的進展，所以各州考慮改用以學生為中心的評量（student-centered assessments）；接著說這項工作既困難又費時。一邊是比較完整的評量，一邊是做起來很難，要不要採用以學生為中心的評量，就是這裡的 dilemma（難題），所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 SAT and ACT，那是拿來比喻標準化評量的例子，不是要在兩者之間做選擇；(D) 照抄 computer，電腦適性測驗是解決難題的方法，不是難題本身；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 NCLB，2015 年 ESSA 就已經取代了 NCLB，這是已經決定的事。

items.stem: Which of the following is an emerging new subject in the ESSA assessment?
items.explanation:
some are now starting to include social studies, government, or economics.
題目問的是新興（emerging）的科目，要把第 3 段提到的科目分成舊的和新的。第 3 段說數學和閱讀是傳統（traditional）科目，(A)、(B) 都不是新的；自然科學是全部 50 個州都已經至少考兩次的科目，(C) 也不是新的；接著說有些州現在才開始（now starting to）加考社會、公民或經濟，所以新興的科目是 (D) Economics。(A) 照抄 math、(B) 照抄 reading、(C) 照抄 science，三個字都在第 3 段，但都是已經在考的科目。
