Teachers are encouraged to accumulate data at different points in their students
These data together present a more complete picture of a student
要插入的兩句說，現在很多老師要學生建立學習歷程檔案，蒐集學期中不同時間點（at different points of time）的作品，呈現學生的努力、進步和成就。第 4 段說各州重視學習過程，老師在學生學習過程的不同時間點（at different points）累積資料，這些資料合起來，能更完整地呈現學生的學習。學習歷程檔案正是第 4 段這個做法的例子，所以插入句開頭說 One good example，放在第 4 段，是 (C)。(A) 第 2 段講的是彈性和電腦適性測驗；(B) 第 3 段講的是多科目測驗；(D) 第 5 段講的是評量的目的，都和不同時間點蒐集作品接不上。

閱讀測驗.title: 福斯特法則：島嶼效應（Foster's Rule: The Island Effect）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Islands are different from a continent or mainland. The size and isolation of islands have a profound effect on island ecosystems and their inhabitants.

Scientists who specialize in species evolution have found that, among mammal species that settle on islands, big species tend to shrink while small ones are apt to enlarge. This phenomenon, discovered by J. Bristol Foster in 1964, has been called Foster’s rule, or the island effect. For instance, rodents (such as rats and squirrels) living on islands tend toward gigantism, while big mammals (like deer and elephants) are more likely to become dwarfed. Although there are a number of exceptions to this pattern, the trend generally holds true for both fossil species and living island mammals.

Foster’s rule shows that body size regulates everything. In a mainland environment, being large is often a safer and adaptive form of avoiding predators. On an island, with few natural predators and less competition, being really big is no longer an advantage; in fact, it can be a hindrance since a huge animal will need a lot more food in order to survive and reproduce.

A new fossil study of island-dwelling proboscideans (i.e. prehistoric hairy elephants) further shows that the physical attributes and ecological structure of an island may affect the degree of shrinking in big mammals. On relatively balanced and species-rich islands, competition with other species often result in a relatively less dwarfed body size. In contrast, on smaller islands where food sources are limited and competitors lacking, members of this group become smaller surprisingly quickly. On one of the Channel Islands 15 miles off the coast of France, the red deer dwarfed to one-sixth the size of deer on continental Europe in a mere 6,000 years after the island became isolated.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
島嶼和大陸不一樣。島嶼的面積和與世隔絕的環境，對島上的生態系和生物有深遠的影響。

專門研究物種演化的科學家發現，遷居到島上的哺乳類當中，大型物種往往會變小，小型物種則容易變大。這個現象是 J. Bristol Foster 在 1964 年發現的，稱為福斯特法則，也叫島嶼效應。例如住在島上的囓齒類（像是老鼠和松鼠）有變大的傾向，大型哺乳類（像是鹿和大象）則比較可能變小。這個模式雖然有不少例外，但無論是化石物種還是現存的島嶼哺乳類，大致上都符合這個趨勢。

福斯特法則顯示，體型決定一切。在大陸上，體型大往往比較安全，也是一種適應環境、躲避掠食者的方式。到了島上，天敵少、競爭也少，體型很大不再是優勢；事實上，體型大反而可能成為負擔，因為大型動物需要多得多的食物才能生存和繁衍。

一項針對島上長鼻目動物（也就是史前多毛的象）的化石新研究進一步顯示，島嶼的自然條件和生態結構，可能影響大型哺乳類縮小的程度。在生態相對平衡、物種豐富的島上，和其他物種競爭的結果，往往讓體型縮小得比較少。相反地，在食物來源有限、又缺乏競爭者的小島上，這一類動物縮小的速度快得驚人。在距離法國海岸 15 英里的英法海峽群島中的一座島上，島嶼和大陸隔絕之後短短 6,000 年，紅鹿就縮小到歐洲大陸鹿的六分之一。

items.stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?
options: The reasons why mammals change and evolve through time.
A comparison of gigantism and dwarfism on different islands.
The different patterns of evolution for big and small island mammals.
The similarity between the evolution of fossil species and that of living species.
items.explanation:
Scientists who specialize in species evolution have found that, among mammal species that settle on islands, big species tend to shrink while small ones are apt to enlarge.
第 2 段第一句就是這一段的主題句：島上的大型哺乳類會變小、小型的會變大，後面再舉囓齒類和鹿、象為例，所以這一段講的是大小兩種哺乳類在島上不同的演化方向。(D) 照抄段末的 fossil species，但原文只是補充說化石物種和現存物種都符合這個趨勢，不是這一段的重點；(A) 動物為什麼會變，是第 3 段才講的原因；(B) 拿不同的島來比較是第 4 段的內容，第 2 段沒有。

items.stem: According to the passage, what is a problem big mammals might face on an island?
options: There may not be enough food.
It is harder to find shelter on small islands.
It may be difficult to move around on small islands.
They become less competitive due to lack of natural enemies.
items.explanation:
On an island, with few natural predators and less competition, being really big is no longer an advantage; in fact, it can be a hindrance since a huge animal will need a lot more food in order to survive and reproduce.
第 3 段最後說，大型動物需要多得多的食物才能生存繁衍，所以體型大在島上反而是負擔；選項把「需要更多食物」換成「食物可能不夠」。(D) 看起來很像原文，但原文說的是島上天敵少、競爭少，所以體型大不再是優勢，並沒有說大型動物因此變得比較沒有競爭力；(B) 找不到棲身之處、(C) 行動不便，文章都沒有提。

items.stem: What does “this group” in the fourth paragraph refer to?
items.explanation:
A new fossil study of island-dwelling proboscideans (i.e. prehistoric hairy elephants) further shows that the physical attributes and ecological structure of an island may affect the degree of shrinking in big mammals.
In contrast, on smaller islands where food sources are limited and competitors lacking, members of this group become smaller surprisingly quickly.
第 4 段第一句是主題句，點出整段講的是大型哺乳類縮小的程度；後面說物種多的島上縮小得比較少，小島上 this group 縮小得很快，會縮小的正是大型哺乳類。this group 和主題句的 big mammals 中間隔了一句，要回到段首才找得到。(D) 照抄同一句的 competitors，原文說小島上缺乏競爭者，競爭者不是縮小的對象；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 fossil species，(B) 照抄第 3 段的 natural predators，都是別段的字詞。

items.stem: How does the author conclude the last paragraph?
items.explanation:
On one of the Channel Islands 15 miles off the coast of France, the red deer dwarfed to one-sixth the size of deer on continental Europe in a mere 6,000 years after the island became isolated.
拿末段的最後一句和前面比對：第 4 段前面幾句說化石研究發現，小島上的大型哺乳類縮小得特別快，最後一句接著舉英法海峽群島的紅鹿為例，六千年內縮小到歐陸的六分之一，正好印證第 2 段的福斯特法則和第 4 段的研究結果，所以是用實例收尾。這一句沒有預測未來，沒有把前面的重點再說一次，也沒有提出建議。

閱讀測驗.title: 大富翁遊戲的真實起源（The True Origin of Monopoly）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Monopoly is a very popular board game around the world today, but little is known about its American inventor, Elizabeth Magie, and the philosophy behind her invention.

Born in 1866, Magie was a rebel against the norms and politics of her times. Inspired by Henry George who believed that all men should have an equal right to use the land as they have to breathe air, she challenged the capitalist system of property ownership—in the form of a board game. In 1904, she patented her Landlord’s Game, which consisted of a circuit of streets and landmarks for sale.

Magie’s game contained two sets of rules: The Prosperity rules and the Monopolist rules. The Prosperity rules stated that every player should gain each time someone acquired a new property. The game was won (by all!) when the player starting with the least money doubled his or her fortune. Under Monopolist rules, on the other hand, each player advanced by acquiring properties and collecting rent from all who landed there later. Whoever managed to bankrupt the other players won the game. The purpose of the dual sets of rules, said Magie, was for players to understand how these different approaches to property can lead to different social outcomes: “all win” or “win all.”

The game soon became a hit on college campuses and among Quaker communities, and some people modified the game board. An unemployed player named Charles Darrow sold this modified version to the manufacturer Parker Brothers as his own. However, when the game’s true origin came to light, Parker Brothers bought the patent from Magie for only $500. They then re-launched the game as Monopoly, including only the rules leading to the triumph of one over all. Darrow was publicized as the inventor who had become a millionaire from selling the game. Thus a rags-to-riches myth was created, ironically exemplifying Monopoly’s implicit values: Chase wealth and crush your opponents if you want to come out on top.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
大富翁是今天風行全世界的桌遊，但很少人知道它的美國發明人 Elizabeth Magie，以及她發明這款遊戲背後的理念。

Magie 生於 1866 年，是個反抗當時社會規範和政治的人。Henry George 認為，人人都應該有平等使用土地的權利，就像人人都有呼吸空氣的權利一樣；Magie 受到他的啟發，用桌遊的形式挑戰資本主義的土地財產所有制。1904 年，她為自己的「地主遊戲」申請專利，遊戲由一圈可以買賣的街道和地標組成。

Magie 的遊戲有兩套規則：繁榮規則和壟斷規則。繁榮規則規定，每當有人取得新的地產，每一位玩家都能獲益；等到起始資金最少的玩家把財富翻倍，遊戲就算贏了，而且是所有人一起贏！壟斷規則則不同，每位玩家靠取得地產、向之後停在那裡的人收租來前進，能讓其他玩家全部破產的人就是贏家。Magie 說，設計兩套規則的用意，是讓玩家了解對待財產的不同方式，會帶來不同的社會結果：「大家都贏」或「贏家通吃」。

這款遊戲很快在大學校園和貴格會社群中流行起來，有些人還修改了遊戲版面。一個名叫 Charles Darrow 的失業玩家，把這個修改版當成自己的作品，賣給遊戲廠商 Parker Brothers。不過，遊戲的真正起源曝光之後，Parker Brothers 只花 500 美元就向 Magie 買下專利，接著把遊戲改名為大富翁重新推出，只保留讓一個人打敗所有人的規則。Darrow 則在宣傳中成了靠賣遊戲成為百萬富翁的發明人。一段白手起家的神話就這樣誕生，諷刺的是，它正好體現了大富翁隱含的價值觀：想要出人頭地，就要追求財富、擊垮對手。

items.stem: What is this passage mainly about?
options: The creation and modification of a board game.
A fight between patent owners of a popular game.
A socio-economic victory behind a landlord game.
The person who became a millionaire from a fun game.
items.explanation: 第 1 段點出大富翁背後的發明人和理念，第 2、3 段講 Magie 發明地主遊戲和兩套規則，第 4 段講遊戲怎麼經人修改、改名推出，所以全文講一款桌遊的誕生和演變。(D) 靠賣遊戲成為百萬富翁的 Darrow 只出現在第 4 段，過於狹隘；(B) 文章沒有寫專利持有人之間起了爭執，(C) 文章也沒有說 Magie 的理念在社會經濟上獲勝，結果正好相反，這兩個選項都偏離主題。

items.stem: What was the main purpose of Magie’s Prosperity rules?
options: To emphasize the value of the capitalist system.
To introduce different approaches to obtaining new land.
To advocate that all should be rewarded when one acquires wealth.
To challenge George’s idea that men should have an equal right to the land.
items.explanation:
The Prosperity rules stated that every player should gain each time someone acquired a new property.
第 3 段說繁榮規則規定，每次有人取得新地產，每一位玩家都能獲益；選項把 every player should gain 換成 all should be rewarded。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 capitalist system，但 Magie 是要挑戰資本主義，不是強調它的價值；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 different approaches，原文說的是對待財產的不同方式會帶來不同的社會結果，不是取得土地的方法；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 equal right，Magie 是受到 George 這個想法的啟發，不是要挑戰它。

items.stem: What does “a rags-to-riches myth” refer to in the last paragraph?
options: Darrow’s success after selling the game.
Parker Brothers’ purchase of Magie’s patent.
The popularity of the game on college campuses.
items.explanation:
An unemployed player named Charles Darrow sold this modified version to the manufacturer Parker Brothers as his own.
Darrow was publicized as the inventor who had become a millionaire from selling the game.
rags-to-riches 指從一無所有到大富大貴。同一段先交代 Darrow 原本是失業的玩家，倒數第二句又說宣傳中把他說成靠賣遊戲成為百萬富翁的發明人，這段從窮到富的故事就是 a rags-to-riches myth；myth 則點出這個故事並不真實。選項把 become a millionaire 換成 success。(A) 照抄 modified version，(C) 照抄 Parker Brothers，(D) 照抄 college campuses，都是同一段的字詞，卻不是這個詞組指的事。

items.stem: Which of the following would best describe Magie’s feelings toward today’s version of her game?
items.explanation: 第 2 段說 Magie 受到 Henry George 的啟發，用桌遊挑戰資本主義的土地所有制；第 4 段卻說大富翁只保留贏家通吃的規則，諷刺地體現「追求財富、擊垮對手」的價值觀。今天的版本和她的理念正好相反，所以她最可能感到不滿。(A) 興奮、(B) 鬆一口氣都說不通；(C) 尷尬要是她自己做錯了事才合理，遊戲走樣並不是她造成的。

閱讀測驗.title: 印度單一時區的爭議（Controversy of India's Single Time Zone）
閱讀測驗.passage:
For decades, India’s time zone has been a hotly debated issue. Back in 1884 when time zones were officially established, two time zones were used—Bombay Time and Calcutta Time. Indian Standard Time (IST) was introduced in 1906, but Calcutta Time and Bombay Time continued to be maintained after India’s independence in 1947, until 1948 and 1955 respectively. The current single time zone, though a legacy of British rule, is often viewed as a symbol of unity. Yet, not everyone thinks it is a good idea.

India stretches 3,000 km from east to west, spanning roughly 30 degrees longitude. This corresponds to a two-hour difference in mean solar time, based on the position of the sun in the sky. Thus, the sun rises nearly two hours earlier in the east than in India’s far west. In Northeastern states, sunrise can be as early as 4 a.m. in summer and sunset by 4 p.m. in winter, much earlier than the official working hours. This results in great loss of daylight hours and more consumption of electricity, and often reduced productivity.

Meanwhile, recent studies point out that the current system leads to a serious problem in education for some students. Nationwide, the school day starts at roughly the same time; thus, children go to bed later and have reduced sleep in west India, where the sun sets later. Such sunset-induced sleep deprivation is more pronounced among the poor, mostly due to their noisy environment and lack of sleep-inducing facilities like window shades or indoor beds. On average, an hour’s delay in sunset time reduces children’s sleep by 30 minutes, and an hour’s delay in annual average sunset time reduces education by about 0.8 years. As a result, children living in locations with later sunsets are less likely to complete primary and middle school education.

Despite various requests and proposals for multiple time zones, the government is keen to retain the current system. Reasons provided include prevention of confusion and safety issues regarding railway and flight operations.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
數十年來，印度的時區一直是爭論激烈的議題。早在 1884 年正式劃定時區的時候，印度使用兩個時區：孟買時間和加爾各答時間。1906 年開始實施印度標準時間（IST），不過 1947 年印度獨立之後，加爾各答時間和孟買時間仍然繼續使用，分別到 1948 年和 1955 年才停用。目前的單一時區雖然是英國統治留下來的制度，卻常常有人把它看成國家團結的象徵。然而，並不是每個人都認為這是好主意。

印度東西綿延 3,000 公里，橫跨大約 30 度經度，換算成依太陽在天空中的位置計算的平均太陽時，相差兩個小時。因此，東部的日出比最西部早將近兩個小時。在東北各邦，夏天的日出可能早在清晨 4 點，冬天的日落則在下午 4 點，都比官方的上班時間早得多。結果造成大量日照時間浪費、用電量增加，生產力也常常因此降低。

同時，最近的研究指出，現行制度讓部分學生的教育出現嚴重的問題。全國各地學校的上課時間大致相同，因此在日落比較晚的印度西部，孩子上床的時間比較晚，睡眠也比較少。這種日落造成的睡眠不足，在窮人家庭更加明顯，主要是因為他們的環境吵雜，又缺少窗簾或室內床鋪這類幫助入睡的設施。平均來說，日落時間晚一小時，孩子的睡眠就減少 30 分鐘；每年平均日落時間晚一小時，受教育的年數就減少大約 0.8 年。結果，住在日落較晚地區的孩子，比較不容易完成小學和國中教育。

儘管有各種要求和提議改用多個時區，政府仍然堅持維持現行制度，提出的理由包括避免混亂，以及鐵路和航班營運的安全問題。

items.stem: Which of the following illustrates the Indian time zone system since 1955?
items.explanation:
Indian Standard Time (IST) was introduced in 1906, but Calcutta Time and Bombay Time continued to be maintained after India’s independence in 1947, until 1948 and 1955 respectively.
The current single time zone, though a legacy of British rule, is often viewed as a symbol of unity.
第 1 段說加爾各答時間和孟買時間分別在 1948 年和 1955 年停用，又說目前是單一時區，所以 1955 年以後全國只用一個時區，四張圖裡只有 (A) 整個印度同一個時間。(B) 分成兩個時區，是單一時區全面實施以前的情形；(C)、(D) 分成三個時區，文章都沒有提。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word “pronounced” in the third paragraph?
items.explanation:
Meanwhile, recent studies point out that the current system leads to a serious problem in education for some students.
Such sunset-induced sleep deprivation is more pronounced among the poor, mostly due to their noisy environment and lack of sleep-inducing facilities like window shades or indoor beds.
pronounced 在這裡不是「發音」的意思，而是「明顯、嚴重」。同一段第一句已經說現行制度造成嚴重的教育問題，這一句又說睡眠不足在窮人家庭 more pronounced，原因是環境吵雜、缺少幫助入睡的設施，可見窮人家庭的情況更嚴重。(D) 照抄同一句的 noisy，但吵雜是造成問題的原因，不是 pronounced 的意思；(B) 有彈性、(C) 遙遠都接不上。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is a supporting argument for multiple time zones?
options: The number of traffic accidents can be reduced.
Children may have better-quality sleep and education.
India may have more energy resources to generate electricity.
The country may rid itself of the impact of British colonization.
items.explanation:
On average, an hour’s delay in sunset time reduces children’s sleep by 30 minutes, and an hour’s delay in annual average sunset time reduces education by about 0.8 years.
As a result, children living in locations with later sunsets are less likely to complete primary and middle school education.
第 3 段說單一時區讓西部日落晚，孩子睡得少，受教育的年數也跟著減少；反過來說，改成多個時區，孩子就可能睡得比較好、受更完整的教育，所以這是支持多時區的論點。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 electricity，原文說的是現制讓用電量增加，不是多時區能帶來更多發電的能源；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 British，原文只說單一時區是英國統治留下來的，沒有人拿擺脫殖民影響當作改制的理由；(A) 交通安全是第 4 段政府維持現制的理由，方向正好相反。

items.stem: According to the passage, when is most likely the sunset hour in December in the city of Varanasi shown on the map?
items.explanation:
Thus, the sun rises nearly two hours earlier in the east than in India’s far west.
In Northeastern states, sunrise can be as early as 4 a.m. in summer and sunset by 4 p.m. in winter, much earlier than the official working hours.
第 2 段說印度東西兩端相差將近兩個小時，東北各邦冬天下午 4 點就日落。地圖上的 Varanasi 在東經 83 度，大約在 68 度和 97 度的中間，和最東邊差一個小時左右，所以 12 月的日落時間大約是下午 5 點。(D) 4 點是東北部的日落時間，(B) 6 點大約是最西部的日落時間，(A) 7 點比最西部還晚，都不對。

閱讀測驗.title: 仙人掌的再生能源應用（Prickly Pear Cactus as Renewable Energy）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The prickly pear cactus is such a powerful symbol in Mexico that it occupies a prime spot on Mexico’s national flag. The plant was considered sacred by the ancient Aztecs, and modern-day Mexicans eat it, drink it, and even use it in medicines and shampoos. Now scientists have come up with a new use for the bright green plant: producing renewable energy.

Known locally as nopal, the prickly pear is farmed on a massive scale in Mexico. Over the years, only the edible soft inner flesh has been used. The cactus’s thick outer layer (i.e., husk), with all those spines, had always been viewed as a waste product until researchers developed a biogas generator to turn the husks into electricity.

The pilot project dedicated to developing the cactus biogas generator began in the south of Mexico City. The area produces 200,000 tons a year of prickly pear cactus—up to 10 tons of which ends up as waste on the floor of the cactus market each day. Then, a local green energy startup company got the idea to turn that waste into energy. The generator is now in place at the cactus market, where the vendors are enthusiastic about this new way to utilize the tons of cactus husks that once went directly into the trash.

The prickly pear has a number of advantages over other biofuel crops, such as wheat, sugarcane, and soybeans. For one thing, only the husk of the cactus is used for generating biofuel, while its inner flesh is still preserved for food. Therefore, using the plant as a fuel source will not put pressure on food prices. Moreover, the cactus requires minimum water, and thus is not grown on traditional agricultural pasture. This means that no increased competition arises for the water or land presently used for food production.

The project in Mexico City has brought new hope to reducing the use of fossil fuels. If it can be expanded, the prickly pear could be the key to Mexico’s energy future.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
仙人掌在墨西哥是極具分量的象徵，甚至占據墨西哥國旗上的顯要位置。古代阿茲特克人把仙人掌視為神聖的植物，現代的墨西哥人會吃仙人掌、喝仙人掌汁，甚至用在藥品和洗髮精裡。如今科學家為這種鮮綠色的植物找到了新用途：生產再生能源。

這種仙人掌在當地叫做 nopal，墨西哥大規模種植。多年來，人們只用仙人掌裡面可以吃的柔軟嫩肉，布滿尖刺的厚外皮一直視為廢棄物，直到研究人員開發出一種沼氣發電機，把外皮變成電力。

開發仙人掌沼氣發電機的試驗計畫，從墨西哥城南部開始。這個地區每年生產 20 萬噸仙人掌，其中每天多達 10 噸成了丟在仙人掌市場地上的廢棄物。後來，當地一家綠能新創公司想到把這些廢棄物變成能源。現在發電機已經在仙人掌市場運轉，以前直接丟進垃圾桶的大量仙人掌外皮，現在可以拿來利用，攤販對這個新方法都很熱衷。

和小麥、甘蔗、大豆等其他生質燃料作物相比，仙人掌有幾項優勢。首先，生產生質燃料只用仙人掌的外皮，裡面的嫩肉仍然留下來當食物，所以拿仙人掌當燃料來源，不會對糧食價格造成壓力。此外，仙人掌需要的水極少，不會種在傳統的農地和牧場上，也就是說，目前用來生產糧食的水和土地，不會因此多了競爭。

墨西哥城的這項計畫，為減少使用化石燃料帶來了新希望。如果能夠擴大推行，仙人掌可能就是墨西哥能源未來的關鍵。

items.stem: What is the purpose of this passage?
options: To argue for the benefits of nopales.
To introduce a new source of energy.
To predict the future agriculture policy of Mexico.
To change people’s ideas about energy consumption.
items.explanation: 第 1 段最後一句點出仙人掌的新用途：生產再生能源，後面幾段接著講沼氣發電機、試驗計畫、比其他作物好的地方和未來的展望，所以全文在介紹一種新的能源來源。(A) 第 4 段確實列出仙人掌比其他生質作物好的地方，但那只是其中一段，過於狹隘；(C) 墨西哥未來的農業政策、(D) 改變大家對能源消耗的看法，文章都沒有談，偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a function of the prickly pear?
items.explanation:
and modern-day Mexicans eat it, drink it, and even use it in medicines and shampoos
有提到的用途在選項都換了說法：eat it, drink it 是 food and beverage，medicines 是 treating illnesses，shampoos 是 personal hygiene。用來園藝造景，文章沒提。

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the prickly pear cactus is true?
options: Its soft inner part is often discarded.
It was not discovered until the modern era.
It turns into 200,000 tons of waste in Mexico each year.
It appears in a prominent place on Mexico’s national flag.
items.explanation:
The prickly pear cactus is such a powerful symbol in Mexico that it occupies a prime spot on Mexico’s national flag.
prime spot 在選項換成 prominent place。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 soft inner，但丟掉的是外皮，嫩肉一直都在吃；(C) 照抄 200,000 tons，那是每年的產量，每天的廢棄物是 10 噸；(B) 照抄 modern，原文說古代阿茲特克人就把仙人掌視為神聖。

items.stem: What advantage does the prickly pear cactus have over other biofuel crops?
options: It will not influence food prices.

閱讀測驗.title: 護照的歷史（The History of Passports）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The concept of a travel document, which shows a person is under a ruler’s protection while in a foreign land, has probably existed since rulers and states were first invented. But the earliest mention of an object which we might recognize as a passport appeared in about 450 B.C. The Hebrew Bible states that Nehemiah, an official serving King Artaxerxes of ancient Persia, asked permission to travel to Judah. The King agreed and gave Nehemiah a letter “to the governors of the province beyond the river,” requesting safe passage for him as he travelled through their lands.

Later, in the medieval Islamic Caliphate, a form of passport was the bara’a, a receipt for taxes paid. Only people who paid their taxes were permitted to travel to different regions of the Caliphate. In medieval Europe, on the other hand, travel documents were issued by local authorities, and generally contained a list of towns and cities which the document holder was permitted to enter or pass through. On the whole, documents were not required for travel to seaports, which were considered open trading points, but documents were required to travel inland from seaports.

King Henry V of England is credited with having invented the first true passport, as a way of helping his subjects prove who they were in foreign lands. The earliest reference to these documents is found in a 15th-century Act of Parliament, while the term “passport” came into use about a century later. Nevertheless, passports were not generally required for international travel until the First World War. It was at this time that passports as we would recognize them today began to be used.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
旅行文件用來證明一個人身在異地時仍受統治者保護，這個概念大概從有統治者和國家以來就存在了。不過，最早提到一樣我們會認為是護照的東西，大約在西元前 450 年。希伯來聖經記載，古波斯國王亞達薛西的官員尼希米，請求准許他前往猶大。國王答應了，給了尼希米一封信，寫給「河那邊的各省省長」，請他們讓尼希米安全通過他們的領土。

後來，在中世紀的伊斯蘭哈里發國，有一種護照叫做 bara’a，是一張繳稅的收據，只有繳了稅的人才能到哈里發國的其他地區旅行。另一方面，在中世紀的歐洲，旅行文件由地方當局核發，上面通常列出持有人可以進入或通過的城鎮。大致來說，前往海港不需要文件，因為海港視為開放的貿易據點，但從海港往內陸走就需要文件了。

一般認為英王亨利五世發明了第一本真正的護照，用來幫助他的子民在國外證明自己的身分。最早提到這種文件的，是 15 世紀的一項國會法案，而 passport（護照）這個詞大約一百年後才開始使用。不過，一直到第一次世界大戰，國際旅行才普遍需要護照。我們今天所熟悉的護照，也是從那時候開始使用的。

閱讀測驗.title: 玻璃琴的興衰（The Rise and Fall of the Glass Armonica）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Benjamin Franklin, one of the Founding Fathers of the United States, was not only a great politician but also a highly accomplished scientist and inventor. Of his many achievements, probably the least well-known are his accomplishments in music. He invented an instrument for which both Mozart and Beethoven composed music—the glass armonica.

In 1761, while living in England, Franklin heard a performer playing musical glasses. Franklin was charmed by the music, but felt that there was a better way to create the same sound. He had a glassmaker create thirty-seven hemispheres made of glass, with each being a different size and thickness to produce different pitches. The glass hemispheres were color coded with paint to identify the notes. Franklin ran an iron rod through a hole in the top of each hemisphere so that they could nest together from largest to smallest. He linked all of this to a device shaped like a spinning wheel, with a foot control that turned the rod, making the glass hemispheres rotate. Franklin moistened his fingers and held them against the rims of the glass hemispheres as they turned, producing a unique sound. He mastered the instrument and took it to parties and gatherings to play for his friends and acquaintances. The instrument became so popular that thousands were built and sold.

But musical fashions changed. Music was moving out of the relatively small halls of Mozart’s day into the large concert halls of the 19th century, and without amplification, the glass armonica simply couldn’t be heard. Concert reviews from the period mourned the fact that the armonica sounded wonderful—only when it could be heard. So, alas, Franklin’s marvelous invention was ultimately abandoned. The popularity of the instrument faded early in the 19th century, but it is still played occasionally today.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
美國開國元勳之一的富蘭克林，不只是偉大的政治家，也是成就非凡的科學家和發明家。在他眾多的成就裡，最少人知道的大概是他在音樂方面的貢獻。他發明了一種樂器，莫札特和貝多芬都曾為這種樂器作曲，那就是玻璃琴。

1761 年，富蘭克林住在英國時，聽到有人演奏玻璃杯樂器。富蘭克林很喜歡這種音樂，但覺得應該有更好的方法發出同樣的聲音。他請玻璃工匠做了 37 個玻璃半球，每一個的大小和厚度都不同，可以發出不同的音高。玻璃半球用油漆標上顏色，方便辨認音符。富蘭克林用一根鐵棒穿過每個半球頂端的孔，讓這些半球由大到小一個套一個排在一起。他把整組裝置接到一個像紡車的機構上，用腳踏板轉動鐵棒，讓玻璃半球旋轉。富蘭克林把手指沾濕，在半球轉動時按住半球的邊緣，就發出一種獨特的聲音。他把這種樂器練得十分純熟，帶到派對和聚會上演奏給朋友和熟人聽。這種樂器大受歡迎，製造、賣出了好幾千台。

但是音樂的潮流改變了。音樂從莫札特時代比較小的廳堂，移到 19 世紀的大型音樂廳，少了擴音設備，玻璃琴的聲音根本聽不見。當時的音樂會評論惋惜地說，玻璃琴的聲音很美，可惜只有在聽得到的時候才是如此。所以，富蘭克林這項了不起的發明，最後還是遭到淘汰。玻璃琴在 19 世紀初就不再流行，不過今天偶爾還有人演奏。

閱讀測驗.title: 摩根奇幻樂園（Morgan's Wonderland）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Morgan’s Wonderland, located in San Antonio, Texas, is a theme park geared mainly toward mentally or physically disabled children. The park was built by Gordon Hartman, a former real estate developer. The creation of the park was inspired by his daughter, Morgan, who suffers from severe cognitive delay and physical challenges.

The world’s first ultra-accessible family fun park, Morgan’s Wonderland opened in the spring of 2010. Admission for guests with special needs is free, and fees for the general public are set at a much discounted price so that people of all ages and abilities can come together and play in a fun and safe environment.

Completely wheelchair-accessible, the park features 25 acres of attractions including rides, playgrounds, a catch-and-release fishing lake, and picnic areas throughout the park. The rides are custom-designed to accommodate wheelchair riders so that every family member can enjoy the fun. The adapted rides include the Off-Road Adventure, where guests can test their driving skills in sporty vehicles. Moreover, each visitor is offered the option to wear a GPS Adventure Band, which allows them to keep track of each other while in the park. The band also enables them to take part in electronic activities. For example, when the riders scan the band at the Off-Road Adventure, a photo will be taken and sent to their email.

In June 2017, Morgan’s Wonderland celebrated the opening of Morgan’s Inspiration Island. The new expansion is composed of five themed splash pads and a River Boat Adventure Ride. The wheelchair guests can transfer out of their chairs into unique, waterproof chairs and enjoy the splash park without risking damage to their personal wheelchairs.

“Morgan taught me that there’s more to life in many ways than what I saw before,” said Hartman. “The blessing that Morgan has brought is beyond anything that I ever could have imagined and could explain.”
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
摩根奇幻樂園位在德州聖安東尼奧，是一座主要為身心障礙兒童設計的主題樂園。樂園由前房地產開發商 Gordon Hartman 興建，建園的靈感來自他的女兒 Morgan，Morgan 有嚴重的認知發展遲緩和肢體障礙。

摩根奇幻樂園是全世界第一座「超無障礙」的家庭遊樂園，2010 年春天開幕。有特殊需求的遊客免費入園，一般民眾的門票也大幅打折，讓各種年齡、各種能力的人都能聚在一起，在有趣又安全的環境裡玩樂。

樂園全區都能讓輪椅通行，25 英畝的園區裡有遊樂設施、遊戲場、釣了再放生的釣魚湖，四處還有野餐區。遊樂設施都經過特別設計，坐輪椅也能搭乘，讓每一位家人都能同樂。這些經過改造的設施包括「越野冒險」，遊客可以開著跑車造型的車子測試駕駛技術。此外，每位遊客都可以選擇戴上 GPS 冒險手環，在園區裡隨時掌握彼此的位置。手環也能讓遊客參加電子互動活動，例如在越野冒險掃描手環，就會拍下照片，寄到遊客的電子信箱。

2017 年 6 月，摩根奇幻樂園慶祝「摩根靈感島」開幕。這個新擴建的園區有五座主題戲水區和一項河船冒險設施。坐輪椅的遊客可以換坐特製的防水椅，盡情享受戲水樂園，不必擔心弄壞自己的輪椅。

Hartman 說：「Morgan 讓我明白，人生在許多方面，比我以前所看到的還要豐富。」「Morgan 帶給我的福氣，遠遠超過我所能想像，也超過我能解釋的。」

閱讀測驗.title: 胡佛水壩的建設與意義（Construction and Significance of Hoover Dam）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Located in Black Canyon straddling the border between Nevada and Arizona in the southwestern region of the United States, Hoover Dam is named one of the Top 10 Construction Achievements of the 20th century. The dam, constructed between 1931 and 1936, was the largest of its kind at the time. Its construction was the result of a massive effort involving thousands of workers and cost over one hundred lives.

Since about 1900, the Black Canyon and nearby Boulder Canyon had been investigated for their potential to support a dam that would control floods, provide irrigation water, and produce hydroelectric power. In 1928, the US Congress authorized the project. The winning bid to build the dam was submitted by Six Companies, Inc. However, such a large concrete structure had never been built before, and some of the techniques were unproven. The extreme summer heat and lack of facilities near the site also presented tremendous difficulties. Nevertheless, Six Companies turned over the finished dam to the federal government on March 1, 1936, more than two years ahead of schedule.

The initial design of the dam, which was more concerned with the dam’s functionality than its exterior, was criticized by many as being too plain and unremarkable for a project of such immense scale. So Gordon B. Kaufmann, the architect who was brought in to redesign the exterior, greatly streamlined the design and applied an elegant Art Deco style to the entire project. Allen Tupper True, an American illustrator, was also hired to handle the design and decoration of the walls and floors of the new dam. He integrated into his design the images and colors based on Native American visions of rain, lightning, clouds, and animals, thereby creating symbolic patterns which appear both ancient and modern.

Today, Hoover Dam has become a national historic landmark. Standing at more than 725 feet above the Colorado River, the highest concrete dam in the Western Hemisphere continues to draw crowds 85 years after its creation, attracting more than a million visitors a year.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
胡佛水壩位於美國西南部，坐落在內華達州和亞利桑那州交界的黑峽谷，名列 20 世紀十大營建成就之一。這座水壩在 1931 年到 1936 年間興建，在當時是同類建築中最大的。興建工程動員了數千名工人，也有超過一百人在工程中喪命。

大約從 1900 年起，就有人在評估黑峽谷和附近的博爾德峽谷適不適合興建水壩，用來防洪、提供灌溉用水和水力發電。1928 年，美國國會核准了這項工程，由 Six Companies 公司得標興建。不過，這麼大的混凝土結構以前從來沒有人蓋過，有些施工技術也還沒有經過驗證。再加上夏天酷熱，工地附近又缺乏設施，困難重重。儘管如此，Six Companies 還是在 1936 年 3 月 1 日把完工的水壩交給聯邦政府，比預定時間早了兩年多。

水壩最初的設計重視功能，不太講究外觀，很多人批評，以這麼大規模的工程來說，這個設計太平淡、太普通了。於是，建築師 Gordon B. Kaufmann 受邀重新設計外觀，他把造型大幅簡化成流線型，整個工程都採用優雅的裝飾藝術（Art Deco）風格。美國插畫家 Allen Tupper True 也受聘負責新水壩牆面和地板的設計與裝飾。他把美洲原住民對雨、閃電、雲和動物的想像，連同相關的圖像和色彩，融入自己的設計，創造出既古老又現代的象徵圖案。

如今，胡佛水壩已經成為國家歷史地標。這座西半球最高的混凝土水壩，高出科羅拉多河 725 英尺以上，完工 85 年後仍然吸引大批人潮，每年有超過一百萬名遊客造訪。

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a reason for building the dam in the beginning?
items.explanation:
a dam that would control floods, provide irrigation water, and produce hydroelectric power
題目問當初興建水壩的理由，哪一個沒有提到。第 2 段說當初評估興建水壩，是為了防洪（control floods），是 (D) 防止天然災害；提供灌溉用水（provide irrigation water），是 (B) 支援農業；水力發電（produce hydroelectric power），是 (C) 發電。第 4 段雖然說胡佛水壩每年吸引一百多萬名遊客，但那是今天的情況，不是當初興建的理由，所以選 (A)。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about Hoover Dam?
options: Its construction lasted for more than a decade.
It is strong in functionality, but plain in design.
Its site stretches over two states in the United States.
It became famous because it led to the discovery of Black Canyon.
items.explanation:
Located in Black Canyon straddling the border between Nevada and Arizona
第 1 段說胡佛水壩所在的黑峽谷橫跨內華達州和亞利桑那州的州界（straddling the border between Nevada and Arizona），選項換成 stretches over two states，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 Black Canyon，原文沒有說水壩讓人發現了黑峽谷，第 2 段說早在 1900 年左右就有人在評估黑峽谷；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 plain，太平淡的是最初的設計，後來已經請建築師重新設計；(A) 水壩在 1931 年到 1936 年興建，只花了五年左右，不到十年。

items.stem: According to the passage, what did Six Companies, Inc. experience in the process of building the dam?
options: It was defeated by the harsh working conditions.
It lost some workers in the construction of the dam.
It benefited from prior experience of building dams of similar scale.
It gave up the project authorized by the government before the deadline.
items.explanation:
cost over one hundred lives
The winning bid to build the dam was submitted by Six Companies, Inc.
這一題要把兩段合起來看。第 1 段說興建工程有超過一百人喪命（cost over one hundred lives），第 2 段說得標興建水壩的就是 Six Companies，所以 Six Companies 在興建過程中失去了一些工人，是 (B)。(A) 第 2 段雖然說夏天酷熱、工地缺乏設施，但接著用 Nevertheless 轉折，說 Six Companies 還是完工了，可見並沒有因為困難而放棄；(C) 原文說這麼大的混凝土結構以前沒有人蓋過，所以不可能有類似規模的經驗；(D) 照抄 authorized，國會核准的工程 Six Companies 並沒有放棄，反而提早兩年多完工。

items.stem: What contribution did Gordon B. Kaufmann make to Hoover Dam?
options: He improved the outer appearance of the dam.
He enhanced the practical functions of the dam.
He added aboriginal flavor to the design of the floor.
He decorated the walls of the dam with images from nature.
items.explanation:
the architect who was brought in to redesign the exterior
第 3 段說最初的設計太平淡，所以請建築師 Kaufmann 重新設計外觀（redesign the exterior），選項換成 improved the outer appearance，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 walls、(C) 照抄 floor，負責牆面和地板裝飾、融入美洲原住民圖像的是插畫家 Allen Tupper True，不是 Kaufmann；(B) 原文說最初的設計太重視功能，Kaufmann 改的是外觀，不是實用功能。

閱讀測驗.title: 餐廳的起源與發展（The Origin and Development of Restaurants）
閱讀測驗.passage:
France gave birth to restaurants, but it was no civilized affair. In fact, today’s restaurant business is a byproduct of the class warfare that arose during the French Revolution.

Back in the Middle Ages, fine dining was a privilege enjoyed exclusively by noble families who had their own grand kitchens and personal chefs. The only commercial diners for the masses were dusty, shabby roadside inns, where strangers crowded around mediocre buffets of lukewarm roasts and over-sauced beans. But sometime in the 1760s, the merchant class of Paris developed a taste for healthy clear broths which were considered restorative; hence the term “restaurant.” By the 1780s, this new Parisian “healthy food” craze led to a handful of reputable dining halls, where customers could sit at individual tables and choose from a wide range of dishes.

Ironically, the popularity of these restaurants grew at a time when the majority of the French population could not afford bread. Decades of harsh winters and oppressive taxation had taken their toll on kitchen tables. By 1789, the starving French masses could no longer be controlled. Looting and riots erupted throughout Paris, ushering in the French Revolution. Rich nobles fled to the countryside, leaving behind their highly skilled chefs and the fine wines from their cellars. Suddenly, unemployed cooks found their way to the city’s eateries, and within a year, nearly 50 elegant restaurants had popped up in Paris.

The restaurant business truly came into its own during the early 1800s, after General Napoleon seized control of the country. He granted “freedom of pleasure” to all citizens, as he reasoned that people who were focused on champagne and fine food probably would not conspire against him. The number of restaurants rose quickly. By 1814, about three thousand restaurants were listed in a popular travel guide. Paris became the center of the new restaurant scene, which, to some degree, it remains today.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
餐廳誕生在法國，過程卻一點也不文明。事實上，今天的餐飲業，是法國大革命期間階級鬥爭的副產品。

早在中世紀，精緻餐飲是貴族家庭獨享的特權，他們有自己的大廚房，也有私人廚師。一般大眾唯一能去的營業用餐處所，是路邊塵土滿布、破舊簡陋的旅店，陌生人擠在一起，吃的是不冷不熱的烤肉和醬汁太多的豆子，這些自助式的菜色都很普通。不過，大約在 1760 年代，巴黎的商人階級愛上了健康的清湯，大家認為這種湯能恢復元氣（restorative），「restaurant」（餐廳）這個字就是這樣來的。到了 1780 年代，這股巴黎的「健康飲食」熱潮，帶動了幾家有名的餐廳，客人可以坐在各自的桌子用餐，從許多菜色中挑選。

諷刺的是，這些餐廳越來越受歡迎的時候，大多數法國人卻連麵包都買不起。數十年的嚴冬和沉重的苛稅，讓一般人家的餐桌越來越空。到了 1789 年，政府再也控制不了飢餓的法國群眾。巴黎各地發生搶劫和暴動，揭開了法國大革命的序幕。有錢的貴族逃到鄉下，留下了技術高超的廚師和酒窖裡的好酒。失業的廚師一下子紛紛進了城裡的餐館，不到一年，巴黎就冒出了將近 50 家高級餐廳。

19 世紀初，拿破崙將軍掌控法國以後，餐飲業才真正蓬勃發展。他給所有公民「享樂的自由」，因為他認為，一心想著香檳和美食的人，大概不會密謀推翻他。餐廳的數量迅速增加。到了 1814 年，一本受歡迎的旅遊指南就列了大約三千家餐廳。巴黎成了這股新興餐廳風潮的中心，在某種程度上，到今天仍然是。

items.stem: According to the passage, where does the word “restaurant” originate from?
items.explanation:
the merchant class of Paris developed a taste for healthy clear broths which were considered restorative; hence the term
第 2 段說 1760 年代巴黎的商人愛上了健康的清湯（clear broths），大家認為這種湯能恢復元氣（restorative），hence（因此）restaurant 這個字就是這樣來的。hence 表示這個字是從前面那句來的，前面那句講的是大家都愛喝的清湯，broth 就是湯，選項換成 popular soups，所以是 (B)。restorative 和 restaurant 拼法相近，也看得出兩個字的關係。(C) 照抄 dining halls，1780 年代出現的有名餐廳，是清湯熱潮帶來的結果，不是這個字的來源；(A) 照抄 chefs，中世紀有私人廚師的是貴族，和這個字的來源無關；(D) 原文沒有提到菜單。

items.stem: What does “taken their toll on kitchen tables” mean in the third paragraph?
options: Deprived people of adequate food for living.
Controlled the nutrients in people’s diet.
Charged people for using kitchen tables.
Paid tribute to chefs working in kitchens.
items.explanation:
the majority of the French population could not afford bread
By 1789, the starving French masses could no longer be controlled.
take a toll on 是「對……造成嚴重的不良影響」，kitchen tables 指每戶人家的餐桌，也就是一般人家吃的東西。前一句說大多數法國人連麵包都買不起（could not afford bread），後面又說飢餓的群眾（the starving French masses）失控，可見嚴冬和苛稅讓人民沒有足夠的食物，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 kitchen tables，toll 雖然也有「通行費」的意思，但這裡不是說使用餐桌要收費；(D) 照抄 chefs，第 3 段的廚師是貴族留下來的，和這句話無關；(B) 原文沒有提到營養。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about commercial diners before the French Revolution?
options: Many fine restaurants were owned by highly skilled chefs.
Reputable dining halls were popular in Paris during the 1760s.
Public dining halls in the Middle Ages were run-down and dirty.
A limited variety of food was served in Parisian restaurants in the 1780s.
items.explanation:
The only commercial diners for the masses were dusty, shabby roadside inns
第 2 段說中世紀時，一般大眾唯一能去的營業用餐處所，是塵土滿布（dusty）、破舊簡陋（shabby）的路邊旅店，選項換成 run-down and dirty，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 Reputable dining halls，有名的餐廳是 1780 年代才出現的，1760 年代巴黎商人才剛愛上清湯；(D) 照抄 1780s，原文說那時候的餐廳可以從許多菜色中挑選，菜色不是有限；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 highly skilled chefs，技術高超的廚師原本替貴族工作，大革命以後才流向城裡的餐館，原文也沒有說餐廳是廚師開的。

items.stem: What was the main reason for Napoleon to promote the development of restaurants?
options: He hoped to improve the life of his citizens.
He wanted to help unemployed chefs find new jobs.
He feared that reductions in restaurants might hurt the travel business.
He believed that the development of restaurants would bring political stability.
items.explanation:
as he reasoned that people who were focused on champagne and fine food probably would not conspire against him
第 4 段說拿破崙給公民「享樂的自由」，因為他認為一心想著香檳和美食的人，大概不會密謀推翻他（would not conspire against him）。沒有人密謀推翻他，政權就穩定，所以是 (D)。(A) 讓公民享樂看起來像是為人民著想，但原文用 as 點出真正的理由是保住自己的政權；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 unemployed，失業的廚師進城開店是大革命時期的事，在拿破崙掌權以前；(C) 照抄 travel，旅遊指南只是用來說明餐廳的數量增加，原文沒有提到餐廳減少會影響旅遊業。

閱讀測驗.title: 獵鷹術的歷史、訓練與文化意涵（History, Training, and Cultural Significance of Falconry）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Falcons are powerful birds that may be trained to hunt in cooperation with humans. The art of training falcons as “hunting dogs of the skies” is called falconry. It was developed in the ancient Arabian Desert around 4000 B.C. In the past, falconry mainly involved hunting with falcons to supplement one’s diet. But now, it has become the favorite sport and pastime in the Arabian Peninsula.

Falconry includes three major processes: acquiring the falcons, training them, and hunting with them. Every year, falconers begin capturing wild falcons in June and July, the migration season. The best birds to catch are the ones with naturally nurtured hunting skills, aged one or two years. Once the falcons are captured, their heads are immediately covered with a leather hood. This is essential because they imprint as their master whomever they see first after the hood is removed. Right after a bird is caught, the training process starts. It begins by depriving the bird of food to make it easier to tame. The birds are taught to know their own name and respond to their master when called. Arab falconers live with their birds day and night in order to build a strong relationship with them.

By the end of October or mid-November, the trained falcons are ready to hunt in the desert. They have excellent vision, 2.6 times greater than that of a human. They are also the fastest divers on the planet. One hunting technique that sets them apart from other animals is that they can be trained to deliver their prey, without killing it first. This is vital in Islamic culture because animals used for food must still be alive to ensure that the meat is halal, that is, properly prepared according to Islamic law.

Falcons have played such a crucial role in traditional Islamic cultures that a number of countries in the Middle East have made them their national bird. Falconry has grown so popular that specialist hospitals have been established to take care of these magnificent birds. Falcons are even issued their own passports. They are the only animals in the United Arab Emirates that are legally allowed to travel inside planes, enjoying a level of luxury that some humans can only dream of.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
獵鷹是強壯有力的鳥，可以訓練來和人類合作打獵。把獵鷹訓練成「天空獵犬」的技藝，稱為鷹獵。鷹獵大約在西元前 4000 年發源於古代的阿拉伯沙漠。過去，鷹獵主要是帶著獵鷹打獵，用獵物補充食物；不過現在，鷹獵已經成為阿拉伯半島最受歡迎的運動和休閒活動。

鷹獵包括三個主要過程：取得獵鷹、訓練獵鷹，以及帶著獵鷹打獵。每年六月和七月是獵鷹遷徙的季節，鷹獵者在這時開始捕捉野生獵鷹。最適合捕捉的是一、兩歲，天生就有狩獵本領的獵鷹。獵鷹一捉到，就要立刻用皮製頭罩蓋住牠的頭。這一步非常重要，因為拿掉頭罩以後，獵鷹第一眼看到誰，就會把誰認作主人。獵鷹捉到以後，訓練馬上開始。第一步是先不給牠食物，讓牠比較容易馴服。接著教牠認得自己的名字，聽到主人呼喚就回應。阿拉伯的鷹獵者日夜和他們的獵鷹住在一起，和牠們建立緊密的關係。

到了十月底或十一月中，訓練好的獵鷹就可以到沙漠打獵了。獵鷹的視力極佳，是人類的 2.6 倍；牠們也是地球上俯衝速度最快的動物。獵鷹有一項狩獵本領和其他動物不同：經過訓練，牠們可以把獵物帶回來，不先殺死。這在伊斯蘭文化中非常重要，因為當作食物的動物必須還活著，才能確保肉是清真（halal）的，也就是依照伊斯蘭律法妥善處理。

獵鷹在傳統伊斯蘭文化中非常重要，好幾個中東國家都把獵鷹定為國鳥。鷹獵越來越受歡迎，甚至有專門照顧這些雄偉鳥類的醫院。獵鷹還能領到自己的護照。在阿拉伯聯合大公國，獵鷹是唯一可以合法搭飛機、待在機艙裡的動物，享受的奢華待遇，有些人只能夢想。

items.stem: What makes falcons a unique animal for hunting in Islamic culture?
options: Falcons are relatively easy to train for hunting.
Falcons can form a strong bond with their owners quickly.
Falcons’ vision is particularly suitable for hunting in deserts.
Falcons keep their prey alive before delivering it to falconers.
items.explanation:
they can be trained to deliver their prey, without killing it first.
animals used for food must still be alive
第 3 段說獵鷹經過訓練，可以把獵物帶回來，不先殺死（without killing it first），這在伊斯蘭文化很重要，因為當作食物的動物必須還活著，肉才是清真的。選項換成 keep their prey alive，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 vision，獵鷹的視力是人類的 2.6 倍，但這和伊斯蘭文化的規定無關；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 strong，緊密的關係是鷹獵者日夜和獵鷹住在一起建立的，原文沒有說很快就能建立；(A) 第 2 段說先不給食物，是讓獵鷹比較容易馴服，原文沒有說獵鷹本來就比較好訓練，也和伊斯蘭文化無關。

items.stem: What is the main reason for Arabic people to hunt with falcons today?
options: To serve as entertainment and exercise.
To replace the practice of hunting with dogs.
items.explanation:
But now, it has become the favorite sport and pastime in the Arabian Peninsula.
第 1 段說鷹獵過去是為了補充食物，But now（不過現在）已經成為阿拉伯半島最受歡迎的運動（sport）和休閒活動（pastime），選項換成 entertainment and exercise，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 supplement，補充食物是過去的目的，題目問的是今天（today）；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 national bird，有些國家把獵鷹定為國鳥，原文沒有說打獵是為了崇拜國鳥；(D) 照抄 dogs，「天空獵犬」（hunting dogs of the skies）是比喻獵鷹的說法，原文沒有說用獵鷹取代獵犬。

items.stem: According to the article, what privilege do falcons enjoy in the Arab world?
items.explanation:
specialist hospitals have been established to take care of these magnificent birds
第 4 段說鷹獵越來越受歡迎，甚至有專門照顧獵鷹的醫院（specialist hospitals），選項換成 specialized medical care，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (B)，這個選項照抄 Passports，但原文只說獵鷹還能領到自己的護照（are even issued their own passports），沒有說護照是誰發的，選項加上的 by the King，原文沒有這個資訊。(C) 照抄第 3 段的 halal，清真講的是獵鷹抓回來、要給人吃的獵物，不是獵鷹自己吃的餐點；(A) 原文說獵鷹可以合法搭飛機、待在機艙裡，沒有說機票免費。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true?
options: Falconers deprive the falcons of food in order to capture them.
Falcons are not allowed to see their masters during the training process.
The trainers’ names are imprinted on the hoods covering the birds’ heads.
Wild falcons with natural hunting skills are most ideal for falconers to catch.
items.explanation:
The best birds to catch are the ones with naturally nurtured hunting skills, aged one or two years.
第 2 段說最適合捕捉的（The best birds to catch）是一、兩歲、天生就有狩獵本領（naturally nurtured hunting skills）的獵鷹，選項換成 most ideal for falconers to catch，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 of food，不給食物是捉到以後的訓練步驟，目的是讓獵鷹容易馴服，不是為了捕捉；(C) 照抄 imprint，原文的 imprint 是獵鷹把第一眼看到的人認作主人，不是把名字印在頭罩上；(B) 照抄 master，原文說鷹獵者日夜和獵鷹住在一起，訓練時並沒有不讓獵鷹看到主人。

閱讀測驗.title: 高爾夫球的演進與凹洞的空氣動力學原理（Evolution of Golf Balls and Dimple Aerodynamics）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Since golf started in the 15th century, many advances have occurred in the game, including significant changes to the golf ball. Early golf was played with a rounded wooden ball before the Featherie, a leather sack stuffed with goose or chicken feathers, became the norm. Then, in 1848, the Gutta Percha ball was introduced, which was made from the juice of the leaves of the gutta tree (a tropical tree native to Malaysia) and was considerably more durable and affordable than its predecessor. The next advancement occurred in the early 1900s with the development of the Haskell. It was the first ball featuring a center rubber core and an outer cover. The Haskell traveled up to 20 yards farther than the Gutta Percha ball and was more durable. In 1905, William Taylor introduced the first dimpled ball, a ball covered with tiny holes on the surface. By the 1930s, golf balls with rows of dimples were accepted as the standard design. Most golf balls today consist of rubber thread wound around a rubber core and coated with dimpled enamel.

Dimples play an important role in a golf ball’s performance because these markings and patterns enhance the ball’s aerodynamics. When a ball is hit and moves through the air, it experiences two major aerodynamic forces: lift and drag. Drag slows the forward motion, and lift acts in a direction vertical to it. With dimples added to the ball, the force that pulls back on the ball is minimized, allowing it to travel faster and longer. Dimples also help to force the airflow downward, which pushes the ball upward. These are the same principles of aerodynamics that airplanes use to fly. In general, golf balls with small, shallow dimples tend to have a longer, lower flight path, whereas those with deeper dimples have a higher flight path. Golfers can choose their balls based on what they need for a particular shot or for particular weather.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
自從高爾夫球在 15 世紀出現以來，這項運動有了許多進步，其中包括高爾夫球本身的重大改變。早期的高爾夫球用的是圓形木球，後來羽毛球（Featherie）成了主流，這種球是在皮囊裡塞滿鵝毛或雞毛。接著在 1848 年，古塔膠球（Gutta Percha）問世，原料是古塔樹（一種原產於馬來西亞的熱帶樹木）葉子的汁液，比之前的羽毛球耐用得多，也便宜得多。下一個進展出現在 1900 年代初，也就是 Haskell 球的發明。這是第一顆有橡膠核心、外面再包一層外殼的球。Haskell 球最多可以比古塔膠球多飛 20 碼，也更耐用。1905 年，William Taylor 推出第一顆有凹洞的球，也就是表面布滿小凹洞的球。到了 1930 年代，表面有成排凹洞的高爾夫球，已經是公認的標準設計。現在的高爾夫球大多是用橡膠線纏繞橡膠核心，外面再包一層有凹洞的琺瑯。

凹洞對高爾夫球的表現非常重要，因為這些凹痕和紋路能改善球的空氣動力。球擊出以後在空中前進時，會受到兩種主要的空氣動力：升力和阻力。阻力讓球往前的速度變慢，升力的方向則和阻力垂直。球加上凹洞以後，往後拉的力量就減到最小，讓球飛得更快、更遠。凹洞也有助於把氣流往下推，讓球往上升。飛機能飛，靠的也是同樣的空氣動力原理。一般來說，凹洞小而淺的高爾夫球，飛行路徑比較遠、比較低；凹洞比較深的球，飛行路徑則比較高。球員可以依照某一桿的擊球需要或當天的天氣選球。

items.stem: Which of the following best states the main idea of the first paragraph?
options: Science and technology have influenced the game of golf.
Price, durability, and function determine the quality of golf balls.
Accumulated efforts have resulted in changes in how golf balls are made.
Golfers who have a sound knowledge of aerodynamics play the game well.
items.explanation:
many advances have occurred in the game, including significant changes to the golf ball.
第 1 段第一句說高爾夫球這項運動有了許多進步，其中包括球本身的重大改變（significant changes to the golf ball），接著依時間順序介紹木球、羽毛球、古塔膠球、Haskell 球、有凹洞的球，一直到現在的球。一代一代累積的改良，改變了球的製作方式，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 aerodynamics，空氣動力是第 2 段的內容，第 1 段沒有談；(A) 科學和科技影響高爾夫球運動，說得太籠統，第 1 段只談球的演進；(B) 價格、耐用度只是用來比較各代的球，第 1 段沒有說這些條件決定球的品質。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about golf balls?
options: William Taylor added a rubber center to golf balls.
The Gutta Percha ball was stuffed with bird feathers.
The Featherie was the first golf ball ever used in the game.
The Haskell lasted longer and traveled farther than its predecessor.
items.explanation:
The Haskell traveled up to 20 yards farther than the Gutta Percha ball and was more durable.
第 1 段說 Haskell 球比之前的古塔膠球多飛 20 碼（traveled up to 20 yards farther），也更耐用（more durable），選項換成 lasted longer and traveled farther than its predecessor，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 rubber，第一顆有橡膠核心的是 Haskell 球，William Taylor 推出的是第一顆有凹洞的球；(B) 照抄 feathers，塞羽毛的是羽毛球，古塔膠球的原料是古塔樹葉子的汁液；(C) 照抄 Featherie，羽毛球之前已經有圓形木球，羽毛球不是最早的高爾夫球。

items.stem: How do dimples on a golf ball affect its performance?
options: They keep it in a better shape.
They allow it to endure stronger impact.
items.explanation:
With dimples added to the ball, the force that pulls back on the ball is minimized, allowing it to travel faster and longer.
第 2 段說球加上凹洞以後，往後拉的力量減到最小，讓球飛得更快、更遠（travel faster and longer），選項換成 travel farther，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 drag，往後拉的力量就是阻力（drag），凹洞把阻力減到最小，選項說增加阻力，剛好相反；(B) 保持形狀、(D) 承受更強的撞擊，原文都沒有提到。

items.stem: Which ball will give golfers a better shot to get a ball out of a deep sand trap?
options: A ball made from Gutta trees.
A ball with a leather sack.
A ball with a smooth outer cover.
items.explanation:
whereas those with deeper dimples have a higher flight path.
球掉進很深的沙坑，要讓球飛得高，才打得出來。第 2 段說凹洞比較深的球（deeper dimples），飛行路徑比較高，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 1 段的 Gutta、(C) 照抄 leather sack，古塔膠球和塞羽毛的皮囊球都是舊式的球，原文沒有說它們適合打沙坑；(D) 照抄 outer cover，Haskell 球有外殼，但原文說凹洞才影響飛行高度，表面光滑的球沒有凹洞的好處。

閱讀測驗.title: 瑞士刀的起源（The Origin of the Swiss Army Knife）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The Swiss army knife is a popular device that is recognized all over the world. In Switzerland, there is a saying that every good Swiss citizen has one in his or her pocket. But the knife had humble beginnings.

In the late nineteenth century, the Swiss army issued its soldiers a gun that required a special screwdriver to dismantle and clean it. At the same time, canned food was becoming common in the army. Swiss generals decided to issue each soldier a standard knife to serve both as a screwdriver and a can opener.

It was a lifesaver for Swiss knife makers, who were struggling to compete with cheaper German imports. In 1884, Carl Elsener, head of the Swiss knife manufacturer Victorinox, seized that opportunity with both hands, and designed a soldier’s knife that the army loved. It was a simple knife with one big blade, a can opener, and a screwdriver.

A few years after the soldier’s knife was issued, the “Schweizer Offizier Messer,” or Swiss Officer’s Knife, came on the market. Interestingly, the Officer’s Knife was never given to those serving in the army. The Swiss military purchasers considered the new model with a corkscrew for opening wine not “essential for survival,” so officers had to buy this new model by themselves. But its special multi-functional design later launched the knife as a global brand. After the Second World War, a great number of American soldiers were stationed in Europe. And as they could buy the Swiss army knife at shops on military bases, they bought huge quantities of them. However, it seems that “Schweizer Offizier Messer” was too difficult for them to say, so they just called it the Swiss army knife, and that is the name it is now known by all over the world.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
瑞士刀是全世界都認得的熱門工具。瑞士有一句話說，每個好公民口袋裡都有一把瑞士刀。不過這把刀的出身其實很平凡。

19 世紀末，瑞士陸軍發給士兵一種步槍，拆卸和清理都需要特殊的螺絲起子。同一時期，罐頭食品在軍中越來越普遍。瑞士的將領於是決定發給每個士兵一把制式刀具，既能當螺絲起子，也能開罐頭。

這對當時苦於和比較便宜的德國進口刀競爭的瑞士刀具業者來說，簡直是救命稻草。1884 年，瑞士刀具製造商 Victorinox 的負責人 Carl Elsener 緊緊抓住這個機會，設計出一款軍方很喜歡的士兵刀。這是一把簡單的刀，有一片大刀刃、一個開罐器和一支螺絲起子。

士兵刀發放幾年後，Schweizer Offizier Messer，也就是「瑞士軍官刀」上市了。有意思的是，軍方從來沒有發軍官刀給軍人。瑞士軍方的採購人員認為，這款多了一支開葡萄酒用的軟木塞開瓶器的新刀，並不是「生存必需品」，所以軍官得自己掏錢買。但後來正是這種特殊的多功能設計，讓這把刀成了全球品牌。第二次世界大戰後，大批美軍駐紮在歐洲，他們可以在軍事基地的商店買到這種刀，於是大量購買。不過 Schweizer Offizier Messer 對美軍來說似乎太難唸了，他們乾脆叫它 Swiss army knife，現在全世界都用這個名字稱呼它。

items.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To explain the origin of the Swiss army knife.
To introduce the functions of the Swiss army knife.
To emphasize the importance of the Swiss army knife.
To tell a story about the designer of the Swiss army knife.
items.explanation: 從軍方需要一把刀、Victorinox 設計士兵刀、軍官刀上市，到美軍取名 Swiss army knife，全文依時間講瑞士刀的由來。(B) 刀有哪些功能，是交代由來時順帶提到的細節，過於狹隘；(D) Elsener 只出現在第 3 段，不是整篇的主角，同樣過於狹隘；(C) 文章沒有強調瑞士刀有多重要，偏離主題。

items.stem: What does “It” in the third paragraph refer to?
options: The Swiss army needed a knife for every soldier.
Every good Swiss citizen had a knife in his pocket.
Swiss knives were competing with imported knives.
Canned food was becoming popular in the Swiss army.
items.explanation:
Swiss generals decided to issue each soldier a standard knife to serve both as a screwdriver and a can opener.
It was a lifesaver for Swiss knife makers, who were struggling to compete with cheaper German imports.
對瑞士刀具業者來說是救命稻草的，是前一段結尾的那件事：軍方決定發給每個士兵一把刀，等於送上一筆大訂單。(C) 照抄同一句後半的 imports，那是業者的困境，不是救命稻草；(D) 罐頭普及只是軍方需要刀的原因之一。

items.stem: Why did the Swiss army NOT purchase the Swiss Officer’s Knife?
options: The design of the knife was too simple.
The knife was sold out to American soldiers.
The army had no budget to make the purchase.
The new design was not considered necessary for officers to own.
items.explanation:
The Swiss military purchasers considered the new model with a corkscrew for opening wine not “essential for survival,” so officers had to buy this new model by themselves.
採購人員認為多了開瓶器的新款不是生存必需品，essential 在選項換成 necessary。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 simple，但那是士兵刀的設計；(B) 照抄 American soldiers，美軍大量購買是二次大戰後的事。

items.stem: Who gave the name “the Swiss army knife” to the knife discussed in the passage?
items.explanation:
After the Second World War, a great number of American soldiers were stationed in Europe.
However, it seems that “Schweizer Offizier Messer” was too difficult for them to say, so they just called it the Swiss army knife, and that is the name it is now known by all over the world.
they 指前面幾句的美軍：瑞士德語的名字太難唸，他們乾脆叫它 Swiss army knife。其他三個選項都是文章出現過的人，但和取名無關：Elsener 設計士兵刀，瑞士將領決定發刀，德國人是競爭對手。

閱讀測驗.title: 印尼天貝：從傳統食物到世界之寶（Indonesian Tempeh: From Traditional Food to World Treasure）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Tempeh (or tempe), a traditional soy product from Indonesia, is hailed as the country’s “gift to the world,” like kimchi from Korea or miso from Japan.

A stable, cheap source of protein in Indonesia for centuries, tempeh is a fermented food originating from the island of Java. It was discovered during tofu production when discarded soybean residue caught microbial spores from the air and grew certain whitish fungi around it. When this fermented residue was found to be edible and tasty, people began producing it at home for daily consumption across the country. This has given rise to many variations in its flavor and texture throughout different Indonesian regions.

Tempeh is high in protein and low in fat, and contains a host of vitamins. In fact, it is the only reported plant-based source of vitamin B12. Apart from being able to help reduce cholesterol, increase bone density, and promote muscle recovery, tempeh has a lot of polyphenols that protect skin cells and slow down the aging process. Best of all, with the same protein quality as meat and the ability to take on many flavors and textures, tempeh is a great meat substitute—something the vegetarian and vegan communities have been quick in adopting.

In addition to its highly nutritional makeup, tempeh has diverse preparation possibilities. It can be served as a main course (usually in curries) or a side dish to be eaten with rice, as a deep-fried snack, or even blended into smoothies and healthy juices. Though not yet a popular food among international diners, you may find tempeh-substituted BLTs (bacon, lettuce, tomato sandwiches) in San Francisco as easily as you can find vegetarian burgers with tempeh patties in Bali.

For the people of Indonesia, tempeh is not just food but also has cultural value. With the Indonesian traditional fabric batik being recognized by UNESCO as “Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity,” tempeh has great potential for this honor as well.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
天貝（tempeh，也拼作 tempe）是印尼傳統的大豆製品，就像韓國的泡菜、日本的味噌一樣，素有印尼「送給世界的禮物」之稱。

幾百年來，天貝一直是印尼穩定又便宜的蛋白質來源，這種發酵食品源自爪哇島。天貝是在製作豆腐時發現的：丟棄的豆渣沾上空氣中的微生物孢子，周圍長出一層白色的真菌。後來人們發現這種發酵過的豆渣可以吃，而且很美味，全國各地就開始在家自己做，天天吃。印尼各地因此發展出許多風味和口感不同的天貝。

天貝蛋白質高、脂肪低，還含有多種維生素；事實上，天貝是目前唯一已知含維生素 B12 的植物性食物。天貝除了有助於降低膽固醇、增加骨質密度、促進肌肉恢復，還含有大量的多酚，可以保護皮膚細胞、延緩老化。最棒的是，天貝的蛋白質品質和肉一樣好，又能做出各種風味和口感，是很好的肉類替代品，素食者和純素食者很快就接受了。

天貝不但營養豐富，料理方式也很多元。可以當主菜（通常做成咖哩）或配飯的小菜，可以炸成點心，甚至可以打進果昔和健康果汁裡。雖然天貝在國際上還不算熱門的食物，但你在舊金山可以輕易找到用天貝取代培根的 BLT（培根、生菜、番茄三明治），就像在峇里島可以輕易找到天貝肉排做的素食漢堡一樣。

對印尼人來說，天貝不只是食物，也有文化價值。印尼的傳統布料蠟染已經列入聯合國教科文組織的「人類非物質文化遺產」，天貝也很有希望獲得這項殊榮。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

items.explanation: 第 1 段介紹天貝是印尼的傳統食物，第 2–5 段依序講源自爪哇的起源、營養、料理方式和文化價值，所以全文介紹的是一種來自爪哇的傳統美食。(A) 料理方式只講第 4 段，(C) 素食者只在第 3 段提到，都過於狹隘；(D) 印尼的文化遺產範圍比天貝大得多，第 5 段只說天貝有機會列入，太過廣泛。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about tempeh?

items.explanation:

In addition to its highly nutritional makeup, tempeh has diverse preparation possibilities.
看每段的第一句就能抓出重點：第 2 段源自爪哇，第 3 段營養成分，第 4 段料理方式。第 4 段開頭 In addition to its highly nutritional makeup 先回顧上一段的營養，再轉到料理，正好把兩段接起來。文章沒有談行銷。

options: Senior citizens will eat tempeh as vitamin supplement.
Tempeh will soon be more popular than kimchi or miso.

items.explanation:

蠟染已經列入人類非物質文化遺產，天貝也很有希望得到這項殊榮，換個說法就是很可能成為國際認可的文化象徵。(B) 照抄 kimchi，文章沒有比較誰比較受歡迎，還說天貝在國際上不算熱門；(A) 照抄 vitamin，文章沒提年長者。

閱讀測驗.title: 車輛撞擊測試（Vehicle Crash Testing）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Crash testing for vehicles is very important in helping minimize deaths, injuries, and property damage from vehicle crashes. One unit of the U.S. government responsible for ensuring the correct undertaking of this task is the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS), a nonprofit, independent scientific body and educational organization. Another branch of government, the Highway Loss Data Institute, supports the mission of the IIHS. Auto insurers also support both organizations.

There are multiple kinds of crash tests for vehicle safety undertaken to provide the necessary information and guidance to vehicle owners. Some examples are frontal impact tests, offset tests, side impact tests, and rollover tests. The front-crash test accelerates a car straight into a solid concrete barrier. The scenario mimics what would happen if two cars crash head-on or a single vehicle crashes into a fixed object. An offset test requires only a portion of the front of the car to impact the barrier or a vehicle. It is important since impact forces in this kind of test remain the same as those with the frontal impact test, but only a small portion of the car absorbs all the force of the impact.

A side impact test simulates a car that is crossing an intersection being hit on the side by a car running a red light. The test is very important since side impact accidents in vehicles result in a high fatality rate. This happens because cars usually do not have a significant crumple zone on the side to cushion all the impact forces before the occupant is injured. A rollover test verifies the car’s ability to support itself, especially from the pillars supporting the roof, during a dynamic impact.

A lot of crash test programs are practiced around the world and provide necessary safety performance data based on real-world conditions.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
車輛撞擊測試對於減少車禍造成的死亡、傷害和財物損失非常重要。美國負責確保這項工作正確執行的單位之一，是公路安全保險協會（IIHS），這是一個非營利、獨立的科學與教育機構。另一個單位「公路損失數據協會」則支援 IIHS 的任務。汽車保險業者也支持這兩個組織。

為了提供車主必要的資訊和指引，車輛安全的撞擊測試有很多種，例如正面撞擊測試、偏置撞擊測試、側面撞擊測試和翻滾測試。正面撞擊測試是讓車子加速，直直撞上堅固的混凝土牆，模擬兩車迎面相撞，或單一車輛撞上固定物體的情況。偏置撞擊測試只讓車頭的一部分撞上障礙物或另一輛車。這項測試很重要，因為撞擊力道和正面撞擊測試相同，卻只由車子的一小部分承受全部的衝擊力。

側面撞擊測試模擬車子穿越路口時，遭闖紅燈的車子從側面撞上的情況。這項測試非常重要，因為側面撞擊事故的死亡率很高。原因是車子側面通常沒有足夠的潰縮區，無法在乘客受傷之前緩衝所有的撞擊力。翻滾測試則是檢驗車子在動態撞擊時支撐自身的能力，尤其是支撐車頂的車柱。

世界各地有許多撞擊測試計畫，根據真實世界的狀況，提供必要的安全性能數據。

items.stem: Which of the following is the mission of IIHS?
items.explanation:
Crash testing for vehicles is very important in helping minimize deaths, injuries, and property damage from vehicle crashes.
One unit of the U.S. government responsible for ensuring the correct undertaking of this task is the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS)
IIHS 負責的 this task，指前一句的車輛撞擊測試。(C) 照抄 property damage，那是撞擊測試想減少的損失，IIHS 不負責賠償；(D) 照抄 independent 和 Insurance，但 independent 形容的是這個機構，名稱裡的保險也不表示它研究保單。

items.stem: How does the frontal impact test differ from the offset test?
options: The vehicle travels at a higher speed in the frontal test.
The vehicle receives fewer impact forces in the offset test.
Only a small part of the vehicle takes the impact forces in the offset test.
The front of a vehicle crashes into another vehicle only in the frontal test.
items.explanation:

閱讀測驗.title: 馬賽人的文化與傳統（The Culture and Traditions of the Maasai People）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Standing proud in the savannah with their red blankets and painted shields, the Maasai people are one of the widely known symbols of East Africa. Their unique style, as remarked by Karen Blixen, author of Out of Africa, “has grown from the inside, and is an expression of the race and its history.”

The Maasai are a semi-nomadic group in Kenya and northern Tanzania, wandering in bands and living almost entirely on the meat, blood, and milk of their herds. Over the years, the fearless tribesmen have stood strong against slavery, and resisted the urging of the Kenyan and Tanzanian governments to adopt a more modern lifestyle. In fact, they are one of the few tribes that have retained most of their traditions. Up until recently, the only way for a Maasai boy to achieve warrior status was to single-handedly kill a lion with his spear.

Maasai clothing varies with age, gender, and place. The most recognizable piece of clothing is the shúkà, a sheet of fabric worn wrapped around the body. Red is a popular color, and women generally opt for checked, striped, or patterned pieces of cloth. Young men wear black for several months after their circumcision, a ritual signifying their coming of age. A Maasai warrior is rarely seen without his spear and shield. In Blixen’s words, “their weapons and finery are as much a part of their being as are a stag’s antlers” (a male deer’s horns).

Beadwork is an important part of Maasai culture. Beaded jewelry is made by women, and is famous for its complexity. Natural materials such as clay, shells, and ivory were used before trading with the Europeans in the 19th century. They were then replaced by colorful glass beads, allowing for more detailed beadwork and color patterns. Multicolored beadwork is popular among both men and women. Each color holds a special meaning: White stands for peace, green for land and production, while red—the most favored color among the Maasai—is the symbol of unity and bravery.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
披著紅色毯子、拿著彩繪盾牌，傲然佇立在大草原上的馬賽人，是東非廣為人知的象徵之一。《遠離非洲》的作者 Karen Blixen 曾說，馬賽人獨特的風格「是從內在長出來的，表現的是這個民族和他們的歷史」。

馬賽人是住在肯亞和坦尚尼亞北部的半游牧民族，成群結隊四處遷徙，幾乎完全靠牲畜的肉、血和奶維生。多年來，這群無所畏懼的族人頑強抵抗奴役，也不理會肯亞和坦尚尼亞政府要他們改採較現代生活方式的勸說。事實上，馬賽人是少數保留了大部分傳統的部落之一。直到不久以前，馬賽男孩要取得戰士的身分，唯一的方法就是獨自用長矛殺死一頭獅子。

馬賽人的服裝因年齡、性別和地區而不同。最具代表性的是 shúkà，一塊裹在身上的布。紅色很受歡迎，女性通常選擇格子、條紋或有圖案的布。年輕男子行割禮之後的幾個月穿黑色，割禮是象徵成年的儀式。馬賽戰士幾乎長矛和盾牌從不離身。用 Blixen 的話來說，「他們的武器和華麗的裝飾，就和雄鹿的角一樣，是他們身體的一部分」。

串珠工藝是馬賽文化重要的一部分。串珠飾品由女性製作，以繁複精細聞名。19 世紀和歐洲人通商以前，用的是黏土、貝殼、象牙這些天然材料，後來改用彩色的玻璃珠，可以做出更細緻的串珠和配色圖案。男女都喜歡多色的串珠飾品。每一種顏色都有特別的意義：白色代表和平，綠色代表土地和生產，而馬賽人最喜愛的紅色，象徵團結和勇敢。

閱讀測驗.title: 安全帽的演進史（The Evolution of the Hard Hat）
閱讀測驗.passage:
A hard hat is a helmet used mostly at worksites to protect the head from injuries due to falling objects. Since its introduction in the early 20th century, the headgear has saved countless lives and is considered the number one safety tool for construction workers.

The hard hat was invented in 1919 by Edward W. Bullard, who had just returned from World War I. Before the war, workers used to smear their hats with coal tar for protection of their head. Bullard, having witnessed the life-saving power of the metal helmet in the War, decided to produce a head protection device that was affordable for every worker and lightweight enough to be worn all day long. The Hard Boiled Hat was thus born, using steamed canvas and leather, covered with black paint, and featuring a suspension system to reduce impact. Soon, hard hats became widely used. The headgear was later made mandatory at construction sites in major construction projects, such as the Hoover Dam in 1931 and the Golden Gate Bridge in 1933.

Over the past century, hard hats have advanced considerably, evolving from canvas and leather to aluminum, fiberglass, and, eventually, to thermoplastic. Recently, new models have been introduced and accessories added to meet the needs of laborers working on various job sites. For instance, a ventilated hard hat was developed to keep wearers cooler, and see-through face shields were attached to better see the hazards lurking above. Today, attachments include radios, sensors, cameras, and a lot more. A common color code has also been developed for recognizing people and their roles on site. Yellow is used for general laborers and contractors, white (or sometimes black) for supervisors and managers, and green for inspectors and new workers.

New products continue to expand the market. Global sales of hard hats totaled USD 2.1 billion in 2016, and are expected to reach USD 3.19 billion in 2025.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
安全帽是主要用在工地的頭盔，保護頭部不受掉落物砸傷。安全帽在 20 世紀初問世以來，拯救了無數生命，公認是建築工人的頭號安全裝備。

安全帽是 Edward W. Bullard 在 1919 年發明的，他當時剛從第一次世界大戰返鄉。戰前，工人習慣在帽子上塗煤焦油來保護頭部。Bullard 在戰場上親眼看到金屬頭盔救人一命，決定做一種每個工人都買得起、又輕到可以戴一整天的頭部防護裝置。Hard Boiled Hat 就這樣誕生了：用蒸過的帆布和皮革製成，外面塗上黑漆，裡面有減輕撞擊的懸吊系統。不久，安全帽就普及開來。後來在大型工程裡，工地規定一定要戴安全帽，例如 1931 年的胡佛水壩和 1933 年的金門大橋。

過去一百年來，安全帽有了長足的進步，材質從帆布和皮革，演變為鋁、玻璃纖維，最後是熱塑性塑膠。近年來，業者推出了新款式，也加上各種配件，滿足在各種工作場所的勞工需求。例如，透氣的安全帽讓配戴的人比較涼爽；加裝透明面罩，則能更清楚看見頭頂上潛藏的危險。如今的配件還有無線電、感測器、攝影機等等。業界也發展出通用的顏色標示，用來辨識工地上的人和他們的職務：黃色代表一般工人和承包商，白色（有時是黑色）代表監工和經理，綠色代表檢查人員和新進工人。

新產品持續擴大市場。2016 年全球安全帽銷售額總計 21 億美元，預計 2025 年將達到 31.9 億美元。

閱讀測驗.title: 斑馬魚的再生能力（The Regenerative Ability of Zebrafish）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Zebrafish, named for their characteristic stripes, have been a popular test subject for researchers. Only a few centimeters in length, the fish breed easily in captivity, grow quickly, and their transparent body makes it easy to study their organs. Above all, they possess some amazing “self-healing” power. When part of their heart is removed, they can grow it back in a matter of weeks. When blinded, they can quickly regain the ability to see.

Recent studies show that humans and zebrafish have the same major organs and share 70 percent of the genes. Moreover, 84 percent of human genes associated with disease find a counterpart in zebrafish. Scientists thus hope that understanding the self-healing mystery of the fish may one day allow humans to regenerate such organs as eyes, hearts, and spines.

Researchers at Vanderbilt University are particularly interested in zebrafish retina regeneration. They have learned that damage of retina can cause blindness in zebrafish, yet it only takes about three to four weeks before vision is restored. The structure and cell types of zebrafish retinas are almost identical to those of humans. If the process can be replicated in humans, it may give rise to new treatments for blindness caused by retinal damage.

In order to know exactly how zebrafish retina is regenerated, the team looked at the neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a chemical messenger in the brain that reduces the activity of neurons. They found that lowering GABA levels in zebrafish can trigger retina regeneration, while a high level of GABA concentration will suppress the regeneration process. This suggested that GABA plays an important role in the fish’s ability to regain their sight.

The team is beginning to test the GABA theory on mice. If that works, human trials will be next on the agenda. If the research proves successful in humans, some of the nearly 40 million blind people worldwide may one day have a tiny, striped fish to thank.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
斑馬魚因身上特有的條紋而得名，一直是研究人員愛用的實驗對象。斑馬魚只有幾公分長，在人工飼養下容易繁殖、長得快，身體又是透明的，觀察器官十分方便。最重要的是，斑馬魚擁有驚人的「自我修復」能力：心臟切掉一部分，幾個星期就能長回來；眼睛看不見了，也能很快恢復視力。

近來的研究顯示，人類和斑馬魚有相同的主要器官，基因有 70% 相同。而且與疾病相關的人類基因，有 84% 在斑馬魚身上找得到對應的基因。因此科學家希望，弄懂斑馬魚自我修復的奧祕，或許有一天能讓人類的眼睛、心臟、脊椎這些器官再生。

范德堡大學的研究人員對斑馬魚視網膜的再生特別感興趣。他們發現，視網膜受損會讓斑馬魚失明，但只要大約三到四個星期，視力就能恢復。斑馬魚視網膜的結構和細胞種類幾乎和人類一模一樣，如果這個過程能在人類身上重現，或許能為視網膜受損造成的失明帶來新的療法。

為了弄清楚斑馬魚的視網膜究竟怎麼再生，研究團隊觀察了神經傳導物質 GABA（γ-胺基丁酸）。GABA 是腦中的化學信使，會降低神經元的活動。研究團隊發現，降低斑馬魚體內的 GABA 濃度可以啟動視網膜再生，GABA 濃度高則會抑制再生的過程。這表示 GABA 在斑馬魚恢復視力的能力中扮演重要的角色。

研究團隊開始在老鼠身上測試 GABA 的理論，如果成功，下一步就是人體試驗。要是研究在人體上也證實有效，全世界將近 4,000 萬名盲人當中，也許有些人有一天要感謝這種小小的條紋魚。

閱讀測驗.title: 呼拉圈的歷史（The History of the Hula Hoop）
閱讀測驗.passage:
When did people first experience the joy of the hula hoop? Although the term did not emerge until the 18th century, toy hoops twirled around the waist, limbs, or neck can be traced back to ancient times. As early as 1000 BC, Egyptian children played with hoop toys of dried grapevine. They threw, jumped, and slung them around their bodies as we do today. They also struck them with sticks to roll them down the road. Hoop rolling was also popular in ancient Greece. Their hoops, often made of metal, were not merely toys for Greek children but served as exercise devices as well.

In the 14th century, hoops were popular as a form of recreation in Great Britain. The craze for hoops even resulted in dislocated backs and heart attacks, according to medical records. The term “hula,” however, did not enter the English language until the 1700s, when British sailors first witnessed hula dancing in the Hawaiian Islands. Though no hoops were used, the movements of the ritual dances looked very similar to those in hooping. Thus “hula” and “hoop” came together, resulting in the term “hula hooping.”

Hoops spun their way through the cultures of pre-colonial America as well. Often considered as representing the circle of life, hoops featured prominently in the ritual dances of Native Americans. Dancers used small reed hoops as symbolic representations of animals such as eagles or snakes. With very rapid movements, they used the hoops to construct the symbolic forms around their bodies.

The hula hoop gained international popularity in the late 1950s, when a plastic version was successfully marketed by California’s Wham-O toy company. Twenty-five million plastic hoops were sold in less than four months. The hula hoop “fad” is still going strong today.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
人類最早是什麼時候開始享受呼拉圈的樂趣？雖然「呼拉圈」這個名稱到 18 世紀才出現，但套在腰部、手腳或脖子上轉動的玩具圈，可以追溯到古代。早在西元前 1000 年，埃及兒童就拿乾燥的葡萄藤做成的圈圈當玩具。他們會丟圈、跳圈，還會把圈圈套在身上甩動，就跟我們今天一樣；他們也會用棍子敲打圈圈，讓圈圈在路上滾動。滾圈在古希臘也很流行，希臘人的圈圈通常是金屬做的，對希臘兒童來說不只是玩具，也是運動器材。

14 世紀時，玩圈圈是英國很流行的消遣。根據醫療紀錄，這股熱潮甚至讓人背部脫臼、心臟病發作。不過 hula 這個字一直到 1700 年代才進入英文，當時英國水手在夏威夷群島第一次見到草裙舞（hula）。雖然跳舞時沒有用圈圈，但這種儀式舞蹈的動作看起來和轉圈圈非常相似，於是 hula 和 hoop 結合在一起，就有了 hula hooping 這個說法。

在殖民時期以前的美洲文化裡，也看得到圈圈的蹤影。北美原住民常把圈圈當作生命循環的象徵，在儀式舞蹈中占有重要的地位。舞者用小小的蘆葦圈象徵老鷹或蛇之類的動物，以非常快速的動作，在身體周圍用圈圈排出這些象徵的形狀。

1950 年代末期，加州的 Wham-O 玩具公司成功推出塑膠呼拉圈，呼拉圈從此風靡全球，不到四個月就賣出了 2,500 萬個。這股呼拉圈「熱潮」到今天依然不退。

閱讀測驗.title: 大象與茶園的衝突（Elephants and Tea Gardens）
閱讀測驗.passage:
When you enjoy your morning cup of tea, you are probably not aware that those tea leaves can mean injury, or even death, for Asian elephants roaming Indian tea gardens.

In the Indian state of Assam, growing numbers of tea farms are destroying the Asian elephant’s habitats and endangering their population. Much of the forest land where tea is grown in Assam is flat and thus farmers must dig drainage trenches to prevent water from accumulating and hurting the shrubs. The trenches, however, can be death traps for the elephants. Since the elephants need to use tea plantations as landmarks when navigating forests, they almost inevitably have to move through the farms. Moreover, because there are fewer humans around, pregnant females often use tea-growing areas as safe shelters to give birth. But baby elephants, not used to negotiating rough ground, may easily fall into the trenches and get hurt; and once injured, they might not be able to climb out. When mothers try to dig their babies out, both may be trapped and smothered by thick mud. Furthermore, elephants are known to resist leaving their sick or dying behind, and a herd may linger at a trench with a trapped baby for hours, reluctant to move on until all hope is lost.

Is it possible for elephants to coexist with the prosperous tea business? Elephant Friendly Tea is an organization that takes the initiative to make it possible. The organization encourages consumers to choose brands that take precautions to protect elephants and has set up a certification program to reward tea growers who are doing it right. Until now, only smaller tea brands have been certified, but awareness is growing. The organization believes that people may be motivated to buy elephant-friendly brands when they know more about the risk tea can pose to these endangered animals.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
當你享用早晨那杯茶時，大概不知道那些茶葉對漫步在印度茶園裡的亞洲象來說，可能意味著受傷，甚至死亡。

在印度的阿薩姆邦，茶園越來越多，正在破壞亞洲象的棲地，危及亞洲象的生存。阿薩姆種茶的林地大多平坦，農民必須挖排水溝，免得積水傷害茶樹。然而這些溝渠可能成為大象的死亡陷阱。大象在森林裡辨認方向時，需要拿茶園當地標，所以幾乎不可避免地要穿過茶園。此外，由於茶園附近人比較少，懷孕的母象常把種茶的地方當作安全的庇護所來生產。可是小象還不習慣走崎嶇不平的地面，很容易掉進溝裡受傷；一旦受傷，小象可能就爬不出來。母象想把小象挖出來時，母子可能都會陷在厚厚的泥巴裡窒息。再者，大象向來不肯丟下生病或垂死的同伴，整個象群可能守在困住小象的溝渠旁好幾個小時，直到完全絕望才肯離開。

大象有可能和興旺的茶葉產業共存嗎？「大象友善茶」這個組織主動出擊，想讓這件事成真。這個組織鼓勵消費者選擇有採取措施保護大象的品牌，還設立了認證制度，獎勵做法正確的茶農。到目前為止，取得認證的只有規模較小的茶葉品牌，但大家越來越關心這個問題。這個組織相信，人們更了解茶葉可能對這些瀕危動物造成的危險，就會更願意購買對大象友善的品牌。

items.stem: Why are baby elephants easily injured in the Assam tea gardens according to the passage?

閱讀測驗.title: 桑吉巴的貿易史（The Trading History of Zanzibar）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Situated off the coast of Tanzania and washed by the warm, clean waters of the Indian Ocean, Zanzibar is a tropical archipelago comprised of several scattered islands. This popular beach destination is now famous for its white sand beaches, slender palms, and turquoise seas. But few people know that in the past, control of Zanzibar meant access to unimaginable wealth.

From ancient times, Zanzibar has been a trading hotspot, thanks to its location on the trade route between Arabia and Africa. Traders from Asia had already visited the islands 900 years before the arrival of its first permanent settlers from the African mainland (around 1000 AD). In the 8th century, Persian merchants built settlements here, which grew over the next four centuries into their trading posts. Between the 12th and 15th centuries, trade increased between Arabia, Persia, and Zanzibar, bringing the archipelago both wealth and power.

During the Age of Exploration, commerce in Zanzibar quickly boomed, largely due to the rise of the spice trade. At the close of the 15th century, Europeans’ craze for spices gave rise to the Spice Route, a network of sea lanes joining Europe with the Far East, where most spices came from. In 1498, Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama made the first sea voyage to India, via the southernmost tip of Africa. In 1499, he arrived at Zanzibar, an archipelago sitting at the crossroads of the Spice Route. The islands soon attracted traders from different lands. Hundreds of ships sailing the Spice Route docked here, bringing spices and goods for transaction, and Zanzibar became one of the biggest trading centers in the world.

Since the 16th century, Zanzibar has come under the rule of the Portuguese, the Arabians, and then the British, each leaving a mark on the place. The paths of various religions also crossed here: Muslims have lived peacefully with Christians and Buddhists on the islands for centuries. The unique cultural intersections, scented with the aroma of cloves, vanilla, and cinnamon floating in the air, give these jewels on the Indian Ocean an amazing charm that goes far beyond tropical beach fun.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
桑吉巴位在坦尚尼亞外海，四周是印度洋溫暖清澈的海水，是由幾座分散的島嶼組成的熱帶群島。這個熱門的海灘勝地如今以白色沙灘、纖細的棕櫚樹和湛藍的海水聞名。但很少人知道，在過去，控制了桑吉巴，就等於能取得難以想像的財富。

由於位在阿拉伯和非洲之間的貿易路線上，桑吉巴自古就是貿易重鎮。第一批永久定居的居民約在西元 1000 年從非洲大陸來到這裡，而早在這之前 900 年，亞洲商人就已經到過這些島嶼。8 世紀時，波斯商人在這裡建立聚落，之後四百年間，這些聚落發展成他們的貿易據點。12 到 15 世紀之間，阿拉伯、波斯和桑吉巴之間的貿易日益頻繁，為這片群島帶來財富和勢力。

探險時代，主要由於香料貿易興起，桑吉巴的商業迅速繁榮。15 世紀末，歐洲人對香料的狂熱催生了「香料之路」，這是連接歐洲和遠東的海上航線網路，大部分的香料都產自遠東。1498 年，葡萄牙探險家達伽馬繞過非洲最南端，首度從海路航行到印度。1499 年，他抵達位在香料之路交會點的桑吉巴。這些島嶼很快就吸引了各地的商人，數以百計航行香料之路的船隻在這裡停靠，帶來香料和各種貨物進行交易，桑吉巴於是成為世界上最大的貿易中心之一。

從 16 世紀起，桑吉巴先後由葡萄牙人、阿拉伯人和英國人統治，每一個統治者都在這裡留下了印記。各種宗教也在這裡交會：幾百年來，穆斯林和基督徒、佛教徒在島上和平共處。獨特的文化交融，加上空氣中飄散的丁香、香草和肉桂香氣，讓這幾顆印度洋上的珠寶散發出迷人的魅力，遠遠不只是熱帶海灘的玩樂而已。

give these jewels on the Indian Ocean an amazing charm

閱讀測驗.title: 魔鬼氈的發明（The Invention of Velcro）
閱讀測驗.passage:
One fine morning in 1941, Swiss engineer George de Mestral went for a walk in the woods with his dog. Upon their return home, he found a lot of burrs (from plants) stuck to the dog’s fur and his pants. He immediately rushed to his microscope and examined the burrs attached on his pants—feeling a lightbulb moment coming on.

Upon closer examination, de Mestral observed that the burrs, which appeared straight to the naked eye, actually contained many small hooks that clung firmly to the loops in the fabric of his pants. He determined that if he could recreate the same thing, making hooks-and-loops that bind to each other firmly, he could produce a strong fastener with many uses.

De Mestral’s first challenge was finding a fabric for a strong bonding system. He first tried cotton, but it proved too soft and could not withstand repeated openings and closures. After years of research and testing, he learned that synthetics worked best and eventually settled on heat-treated nylon, a strong and durable substance. By 1955, he had completed an improved version of the product, with each square inch of material containing 300 hooks, which made it stay fastened and yet easy enough to pull apart when needed. Named “Velcro,” from the French words velours (velvet) and crochet (hook), the new product received a patent from the Swiss government in 1955. De Mestral thus began mass-producing Velcro, opening plants in Europe and eventually into Canada and the United States.

Initially Velcro did not fare well. As most fashion critics considered it ugly and cheap-looking, the use of Velcro was limited to athletic equipment. In the early 1960s, the product received a huge boost in popularity when NASA began using it in a lot of equipment that went into space along with astronauts. Today, de Mestral’s design is found almost everywhere: clothing and footwear, toys, airline seat cushions, blood pressure cuffs and surgeons’ gowns. Most impressively, the magical fastener was used in the first human artificial heart transplantation to hold together parts of the device.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
1941 年一個晴朗的早晨，瑞士工程師 George de Mestral 帶著狗到樹林裡散步。回家後，他發現狗毛和自己的褲子上黏了許多植物的刺果。他立刻衝到顯微鏡前，仔細觀察黏在褲子上的刺果，感覺好點子就要冒出來了。

進一步仔細觀察後，de Mestral 發現，肉眼看起來筆直的刺果，其實有許多小鉤子，牢牢勾住褲子布料上的線圈。他斷定，如果能重現同樣的構造，做出彼此緊緊扣住的鉤子和線圈，就能製造出牢固又用途廣泛的扣件。

de Mestral 的第一個難題，是找到一種能牢牢黏合的布料。他先試了棉布，可是棉布太軟，經不起反覆撕開、黏合。經過多年的研究和測試，他發現合成纖維效果最好，最後選定經過熱處理的尼龍，一種堅固耐用的材料。到了 1955 年，他完成了改良版的產品，每平方英寸的材料上有 300 個鉤子，可以黏得很牢，需要時又能輕鬆扯開。這項新產品取名為 Velcro，來自法文的 velours（天鵝絨）和 crochet（鉤子），1955 年取得瑞士政府核發的專利。de Mestral 於是開始量產魔鬼氈，在歐洲設廠，後來又擴展到加拿大和美國。

魔鬼氈一開始並不成功。大多數時尚評論家認為魔鬼氈很醜，看起來很廉價，所以只用在運動器材上。1960 年代初期，美國太空總署開始在許多隨太空人上太空的設備上使用魔鬼氈，魔鬼氈的人氣因此大增。如今 de Mestral 的設計幾乎隨處可見：衣服和鞋子、玩具、飛機座椅的坐墊、血壓計的壓脈帶和外科醫師的手術衣都有。最令人驚嘆的是，第一次人工心臟移植手術也用了這種神奇的扣件，把裝置的零件固定在一起。
