He determined that if he could recreate the same thing, making hooks-and-loops that bind to each other firmly, he could produce a strong fastener with many uses.
de Mestral 模仿的是刺果上的小鉤子勾住布料線圈，做成一面鉤子、一面線圈的布料扣件，就是 (B) 的魔鬼氈。(D) 雖然也有鉤和環，但那是縫在布上的金屬鉤扣，不是布料本身的鉤子和線圈。

items.stem: What does the author mean by “a lightbulb moment” in the first paragraph?
items.explanation:
He immediately rushed to his microscope and examined the burrs attached on his pants—feeling a lightbulb moment coming on.
像漫畫人物頭上突然亮起一顆燈泡，lightbulb moment 是突然想到好點子；第 2 段他果然想到可以做成扣件。

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Velcro is true?
options: It has been a market favorite since its first appearance.
Cotton was not durable enough to be used as its materials.
It was given a French name because it was first produced in France.
The design was intended to look as shiny and smooth as velvet.
items.explanation:
He first tried cotton, but it proved too soft and could not withstand repeated openings and closures.
經不起反覆撕開、黏合，就是不夠耐用。(C) 照抄 French，但原文說名稱取自法文字，產品是在瑞士取得專利；(D) 照抄 velvet，但那只是名稱的來源，不是要做得像天鵝絨；(A) 第 4 段一開頭就說魔鬼氈起初並不成功。

items.stem: Which of the following fields is NOT mentioned for Velcro uses in the passage?
items.explanation:
As most fashion critics considered it ugly and cheap-looking, the use of Velcro was limited to athletic equipment.
In the early 1960s, the product received a huge boost in popularity when NASA began using it in a lot of equipment that went into space along with astronauts.
Most impressively, the magical fastener was used in the first human artificial heart transplantation to hold together parts of the device.
有提到的三個領域在選項都換了說法：athletic equipment 是 Sports and recreation，NASA 的太空設備是 Aerospace industry，血壓計、手術衣和人工心臟是 Medical technology。(A) 的 engineering 只是呼應第 1 段 de Mestral 的職業 engineer，文章沒說魔鬼氈用在土木工程上。

閱讀測驗.title: 畫家 Thomas Moran 與黃石公園（Painter Thomas Moran and Yellowstone）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Thomas Moran, a famous painter in the 19th century, played an important role in the establishment of American national parks. His vivid paintings brought the splendor of the extraordinary landscapes before the eyes of American people, thus setting the stage for the regions to be widely recognized and officially established as national parks.

Moran came to the United States at age 7 with his family and settled in Philadelphia. They came from northwest England, the blackened heart of the Industrial Revolution: Its main street was “a dark, unattractive hole” and the river running through it was a string of dirty water. That was all the nature that Moran knew. Moran began painting by age 15, inspired by the landscape paintings of the British master J.M.W. Turner. There was plenty of landscape for him to paint in America, much different from his hometown. Showing great talent in painting, Moran was soon hired as an illustrator at Scribner’s Monthly, and later appointed chief illustrator by age 34. In 1871, he was appointed to illustrate The Wonders of Yellowstone, a story by Nathaniel P. Langford, who had participated in an expedition to Yellowstone. Captivated by the utterly fantastic sights Langford described, Moran became eager to see this odd territory for himself.

In 1871 Moran joined the first US government survey of the Yellowstone region with photographer William Henry Jackson. For two weeks he filled his sketchbook with the landscape’s most stunning sights. Moran’s watercolors—the first color renderings of the area—as well as Jackson’s photos and the survey results were presented to the Congress. His powerful images of Yellowstone fired the imagination of Congress members. In March 1872, lawmakers officially made Yellowstone a national park, the world’s first.

Before Moran arrived, Yellowstone in the popular imagination was a harsh, wild place with hot water and steam coming out of hellish holes in the ground. Since the painter’s work appeared, Yellowstone National Park has come to be known as a picturesque wonderland. By the time Moran died, he had painted a dozen other areas that would become national parks or monuments.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
Thomas Moran 是 19 世紀的知名畫家，在美國國家公園的設立上扮演了重要的角色。他生動的畫作讓美國人親眼看到那些非凡景觀的壯麗，為這些地區日後廣受肯定、正式成為國家公園鋪好了路。

Moran 7 歲時隨家人來到美國，在費城定居。他們來自英格蘭西北部，那裡是工業革命燻得烏黑的核心地帶：大街是「一個又暗又難看的洞」，流經當地的河是一條髒水。這就是 Moran 所認識的大自然。Moran 15 歲就開始作畫，靈感來自英國大師 J.M.W. Turner 的風景畫。美國有大量和他家鄉截然不同的風景，可以讓他盡情作畫。Moran 展現了繪畫天分，不久就受聘為《Scribner’s Monthly》的插畫家，34 歲時升任首席插畫家。1871 年，他受命為 Nathaniel P. Langford 的〈黃石奇景〉繪製插圖，Langford 曾參加過黃石的探險隊。Langford 描述的奇幻景象深深吸引了 Moran，讓他迫不及待想親眼看看這片奇特的土地。

1871 年，Moran 和攝影師 William Henry Jackson 一起參加美國政府第一次的黃石地區考察。兩個星期裡，他的素描本畫滿了當地最壯觀的景色。Moran 的水彩畫是這個地區最早的彩色圖像，連同 Jackson 的照片和考察結果一起呈交國會。他筆下震撼人心的黃石景象，激發了國會議員的想像。1872 年 3 月，國會正式把黃石設為國家公園，這是全世界第一座國家公園。

在 Moran 去之前，一般人想像中的黃石是個荒涼的蠻荒之地，地上有冒著熱水和蒸氣、像地獄一樣的洞。這位畫家的作品問世以後，黃石國家公園才開始以如畫般的仙境聞名。到 Moran 過世時，他還畫了另外十二處後來成為國家公園或國家保護區的地方。

items.stem: What can we learn from the passage?
options: How national parks around the world were established.
How Yellowstone’s natural features were formed.
Why Moran’s family moved to the United States.
items.explanation:
In 1871, he was appointed to illustrate The Wonders of Yellowstone, a story by Nathaniel P. Langford, who had participated in an expedition to Yellowstone.
Captivated by the utterly fantastic sights Langford described, Moran became eager to see this odd territory for himself.
他接下為 Langford 的黃石故事畫插圖的工作，又受到書裡描述的奇景吸引，才想親眼去看，這就是他開始畫黃石的原因。(A) 文章只講黃石一座公園的設立經過；(C) 只說他隨家人移民，沒說為什麼搬家；(B) 黃石的地貌怎麼形成，文章沒提。

items.stem: Why does the author use “the blackened heart” in paragraph 2 to describe Moran’s hometown?
options: The town was filled with darkened holes.
There were many evil-hearted industry owners.
The laborers mostly wore dark and dirty uniforms.
items.explanation:
They came from northwest England, the blackened heart of the Industrial Revolution: Its main street was “a dark, unattractive hole” and the river running through it was a string of dirty water.
冒號後面就是解釋：街道又暗又難看，河是一條髒水，工業革命把這裡燻黑了，所以 blackened 指的是汙染嚴重。(B) 照抄 hole，但「洞」是形容大街的比喻；(C) 照抄 heart，但這裡的 heart 是「核心地帶」，不是人心。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the Yellowstone National Park?
options: Its establishment was proposed by Langford.
Americans knew little about its beauty before the 1870s.
The government project was started due to its rich natural resources.
It was the only national park established because of Moran’s works.
items.explanation:
Before Moran arrived, Yellowstone in the popular imagination was a harsh, wild place with hot water and steam coming out of hellish holes in the ground.
Moran 1871 年去黃石之前，一般人以為那裡荒涼可怕，可見並不知道黃石的美。(A) 照抄 Langford，他只是寫了探險故事；(C) 照抄 government，原文說政府考察後設立公園，沒說是因為天然資源；(D) 照抄 national park，但第 4 段說 Moran 還畫了另外十二處後來成為國家公園或保護區的地方。

items.stem: What can be inferred from the passage?
options: Scribner’s Monthly was a magazine promoting national parks.
Moran had visited Yellowstone before he started painting its landscapes.
Color photos were not common when Moran started painting Yellowstone.
Watercolor was the most popular form of landscape painting in the 19th century.
items.explanation:
Moran’s watercolors—the first color renderings of the area—as well as Jackson’s photos and the survey results were presented to the Congress.
同行的 Jackson 拍了照片，最早的彩色圖像卻是 Moran 的水彩畫，可見當時的照片不是彩色的。(B) 方向相反：他在 1871 年親自去黃石之前，已經在為黃石的故事畫插圖；(D) 照抄 watercolors，但文章沒有比較哪一種風景畫最流行；(A) 文章沒說那份雜誌在推廣國家公園。

閱讀測驗.title: 「100% Fish」計畫（The "100% Fish" Project）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In 2020, Petur Oddsson, a power station worker in Iceland, was struck by a 60,000-volt current. The electrical shock burned almost half of his body and melted layers of his skin off. Such deep and extensive burns can be fatal. But Oddsson’s life was saved by a creative invention: transplanting codfish skins onto human bodies.

A triumph for medical technology, Oddsson’s fish skin transplantation was actually part of the astonishing achievement of “100% Fish,” an ambitious task in promoting environmental efficiency. The Icelandic project, from which this pioneering procedure emerged, strives for making a fundamental change in the marine industry. It aims to encourage full utilization of each fish caught, and to strengthen innovation in seafood products.

Reducing waste of fish catch has become a serious issue today, when many countries are faced with food crises. According to a 2003 study, about 60% of a codfish caught in Iceland was lost or wasted during the production process for human consumption. Under the guidance of 100% Fish, however, Icelanders are now using almost 95% of a cod. Cod skin, for example, is made into calcium supplement and energy drinks, and even as material for skin transplantation as in Oddsson’s case. Dried fish heads and spines are exported to West Africa, where they are used as the base of a protein-rich soup. Other groundbreaking products, including Omega-3 capsules, cold virus pretreatment sprays, and dog snacks are made from what was once cod catch detritus.

The Icelandic success is accomplished largely through cooperative efforts across various industries. 100% Fish takes the initiative to show seafood companies the importance of collaboration, and facilitate valuable connections between fishing companies and other participants of the project, including academia, start-ups, and research and development teams. By sharing knowledge and information, the different sectors are able to come up with improved processing and handling, through which creation of various innovative products was made possible. The project not only helps Icelanders to get 30% more value from each cod than most developed countries, but also provides an effective model to promote resource efficiency worldwide.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
2020 年，冰島電廠員工 Petur Oddsson 觸電，電流高達 6 萬伏特。這次電擊燒傷他將近一半的身體，好幾層皮膚都熔掉了。這麼深、面積又這麼大的燒傷可能致命，但一項創新的發明救了 Oddsson 一命：把鱈魚皮移植到人體上。

Oddsson 的魚皮移植是醫療科技的一大勝利，其實也是「100% Fish」計畫驚人成就的一部分；這是一項推動資源有效利用的遠大計畫，這種開創性的療法就是出自這項冰島的計畫。計畫的宗旨是從根本改變漁業，目標是鼓勵充分利用捕到的每一條魚，並加強海鮮產品的創新。

如今許多國家面臨糧食危機，減少漁獲的浪費成了一大課題。根據 2003 年的一項研究，冰島捕到的鱈魚在加工成食品的過程中，大約有 60% 流失或浪費掉了。不過在 100% Fish 的帶動下，冰島人現在幾乎能利用一條鱈魚的 95%。舉例來說，鱈魚皮可以做成鈣片和能量飲料，甚至像 Oddsson 的例子那樣，當作皮膚移植的材料。曬乾的魚頭和魚骨外銷到西非，在當地用來熬煮富含蛋白質的湯。其他突破性的產品，包括 Omega-3 膠囊、預防感冒病毒的噴劑和狗零食，原料都是過去當作廢棄物的鱈魚下腳料。

冰島的成功，主要靠的是跨產業的合作。100% Fish 主動向海鮮業者說明合作的重要，並促成漁業公司和計畫其他參與者建立寶貴的連結，包括學術界、新創公司和研發團隊。各領域分享知識和資訊，改良了加工和處理的方式，才開發出各種創新的產品。這項計畫不但讓冰島人從每一條鱈魚得到的價值比大多數已開發國家多出 30%，也為全世界推動資源有效利用提供了有效的模式。

items.stem: What is the primary goal of 100% Fish?
options: To make the most of marine resources.
items.explanation:
It aims to encourage full utilization of each fish caught, and to strengthen innovation in seafood products.
aims to 直接說出目標：充分利用捕到的每一條魚，在選項換成 make the most of marine resources。(C) 跨產業合作是第 4 段說的達成方法，不是目標；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 food crises，那是減少浪費之所以重要的背景。

items.stem: What does “this pioneering procedure” in the second paragraph refer to?
options: A fundamental change in seafood business.
A new approach to protect the environment.
items.explanation:
A triumph for medical technology, Oddsson’s fish skin transplantation was actually part of the astonishing achievement of “100% Fish,” an ambitious task in promoting environmental efficiency.
The Icelandic project, from which this pioneering procedure emerged
this pioneering procedure 是「從這個計畫裡產生的開創性療法」，指前一句講的 Oddsson 魚皮移植；procedure 在醫學上就是手術、療法。(C) 照抄同一句後半的 fundamental change，那是計畫要做的事，不是從計畫裡產生的療法。

items.stem: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Iceland has increased their fish catch by 30% in the last 20 years.
Petur Oddsson was an important member of the Icelandic project.
Cross-field collaboration has proved to be very fruitful for 100% Fish.
100% Fish is a big international enterprise marketing seafood products.
items.explanation:
The Icelandic success is accomplished largely through cooperative efforts across various industries.
冰島的成功主要靠跨產業合作，在選項換成 cross-field collaboration 很有成效。(A) 照抄 30%，但那是每條鱈魚多得到的價值，不是漁獲量增加；(B) Oddsson 是受惠的病人，不是計畫成員；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 seafood products，但 100% Fish 是一項計畫，不是賣海鮮的國際企業。

items.stem: Here is a sentence: “Almost nothing of a fish is left for the trash bin.” Which paragraph is most suitable to have it as the final sentence?
items.explanation:
Under the guidance of 100% Fish, however, Icelanders are now using almost 95% of a cod.
Other groundbreaking products, including Omega-3 capsules, cold virus pretreatment sprays, and dog snacks are made from what was once cod catch detritus.
第 3 段說冰島人幾乎用掉一條鱈魚的 95%，再列舉魚皮、魚頭、魚骨和下腳料都派上用場，最後接「一條魚幾乎沒有什麼留給垃圾桶」正好收尾；almost nothing … left 呼應 almost 95%。

閱讀測驗.title: 紅綠燈的發明史（The Invention History of Traffic Lights）
閱讀測驗.passage:
While waiting to cross the street at busy intersections, have you ever wondered who invented the traffic light? Most people credit the first traffic light to Nottingham engineer John Peake Knight. A railway manager, Knight specialized in designing the signaling system for Britain’s growing railway network in the 1860s. He saw no reason why this could not be adapted for use on the busy London intersections. Thus, he proposed a signaling system based on the railway movable-arm signal: Arms extending horizontally commanded drivers to stop, whereas arms lowered to a 45-degree angle told drivers to move on, resembling a traffic director’s gestures. Red and green gas lamps were added to the signal for use at night. A police officer was stationed by the side to operate the system.

Knight’s traffic signal was installed near London’s Westminster Bridge in December 1868, but the system was short-lived. A gas leak one month later caused an explosion in the lights, injuring the policeman operating it. Deemed a public hazard, the project was immediately dropped, and traffic lights were banned until their return in 1929 back to the British streets.

In the early 1900s, versions of the British traffic lights appeared in big cities in America, where traffic was on a sharp rise. Systems using movable arms were popular in Chicago, while those using the red and green lights were adopted in San Francisco. Patents with innovations on Knight’s ideas were filed nationwide. A major breakthrough was the yellow light invented by a Detroit police officer William Potts. Installed in Detroit in 1920, Potts’ three-color system allowed for the added signal “proceed with caution” to be displayed.

Now, with the emergence of self-driving cars, researchers have begun to suggest that traffic signals are no longer necessary. Intersections will operate in a way that cars automatically adjust their speed to cross through, while maintaining safe distances from other vehicles. In the near future, we may experience a brand new form of traffic management!
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
在繁忙的十字路口等著過馬路時，你有沒有想過紅綠燈是誰發明的？大多數人認為第一座紅綠燈出自諾丁漢的工程師 John Peake Knight。Knight 是一位鐵路經理，1860 年代英國的鐵路網不斷擴張，他專門設計鐵路的號誌系統。他認為這套系統一樣可以改用在倫敦繁忙的路口，於是以鐵路的可動臂號誌為基礎，提出一套號誌系統：號誌臂水平伸出，表示駕駛人要停下來；號誌臂下降到 45 度角，表示可以通行，就像指揮交通的人在打手勢。號誌上另外加裝紅、綠兩色的煤氣燈，供夜間使用，旁邊還派駐一名警察負責操作。

Knight 的交通號誌在 1868 年 12 月裝設在倫敦西敏橋附近，但這套系統沒用多久。一個月後，煤氣外洩引起燈具爆炸，操作號誌的警察因此受傷。當局認定這套號誌危害公共安全，計畫隨即喊停，紅綠燈也從此禁止使用，直到 1929 年才重回英國街頭。

1900 年代初期，美國大城市的交通量急遽增加，各地陸續出現仿照英國紅綠燈的號誌。芝加哥流行用可動臂的系統，舊金山則採用紅綠燈的系統。全美各地都有人以 Knight 的構想為基礎，申請改良的專利。其中一大突破是底特律警察 William Potts 發明的黃燈。Potts 的三色系統 1920 年裝設在底特律，多了一個「小心通行」的號誌。

如今隨著自駕車出現，研究人員開始提出交通號誌已經沒有必要的看法。未來的路口會這樣運作：車輛自動調整速度通過路口，同時和其他車輛保持安全距離。在不久的將來，我們或許就會體驗到全新的交通管理方式！

items.stem: What is this passage mainly about?
options: The evolution of traffic control systems.
The inventors of traffic lights in history.
The functions of different traffic signals.
items.explanation: 從 Knight 參考鐵路號誌的設計、美國的可動臂與三色燈，到自駕車時代可能不再需要號誌，全文依時間講交通號誌系統怎麼演變。(B) 發明者只寫到 Knight 和 Potts 兩位，(C) 各種號誌代表什麼意思只在第 1、3 段帶到，都過於狹隘；(D) 文章只講號誌，沒講整個現代交通運輸，太過廣泛。

items.stem: Which of the following pictures shows Knight’s proposed traffic signal?
items.explanation:
Thus, he proposed a signaling system based on the railway movable-arm signal: Arms extending horizontally commanded drivers to stop, whereas arms lowered to a 45-degree angle told drivers to move on, resembling a traffic director’s gestures.
Red and green gas lamps were added to the signal for use at night.
Knight 的號誌要同時有可以擺動的號誌臂和夜間用的燈，四張圖裡只有 (C) 兩者都有。(B) 只有臂、沒有燈，比較像他參考的鐵路號誌本身；(A) 只有燈；(D) 寫 STOP、GO 的牌子文章沒提。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true, according to the passage?
options: Knight was injured in the explosion of his traffic light.
Potts’ traffic light was the first one to appear in the USA.
The first traffic signal originated from the idea of a traffic director.
Future vehicles may not need traffic lights to cross an intersection.
items.explanation:
Now, with the emergence of self-driving cars, researchers have begun to suggest that traffic signals are no longer necessary.
Intersections will operate in a way that cars automatically adjust their speed to cross through, while maintaining safe distances from other vehicles.
自駕車在選項換成 Future vehicles，「號誌不再必要」換成「可能不需要紅綠燈」。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 explosion，但受傷的是操作號誌的警察，不是 Knight；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 traffic director，原文說的是號誌臂像交通指揮的手勢，構想其實來自鐵路號誌；(B) 黃燈是改良，不是美國第一座。

items.stem: Here is a sentence: “This design was adopted in later traffic light designs across the world.” Which paragraph is most suitable to have it as the final sentence?
items.explanation:
Installed in Detroit in 1920, Potts’ three-color system allowed for the added signal “proceed with caution” to be displayed.
This design 要接一個前面剛講完的設計，而且是之後世界各地都採用的；第 3 段最後一句的三色系統正好符合，今天的紅綠燈就是紅、黃、綠三色。第 2 段結尾是號誌遭到禁用，第 4 段講的是未來，都接不上 later designs。

閱讀測驗.title: 恐怖電影的利弊（The Pros and Cons of Horror Movies）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Typically featuring zombies and serial killers, horror movies are too frightening to be fun for some people. But many others enjoy a good fear spectacle, and line up to see the latest scary movie. Given the variations in preferences, new studies have started to untangle the benefits and risks of horror movies.

One benefit of horror movies revolves around the concept of so-called “safe fear.” When watching a frightening film, people are in the comfort of their own home or theater seats rather than under the threat of any real danger. In a controlled environment, these films may actually reduce the negative impact on viewers and help them become tougher. Secondly, as people are drawn into the story, they tend to take the perspective of the characters and rehearse the plot unconsciously. Researchers believe that viewers are learning vicariously this way, picking up tips on how to handle threats in the real world. In addition, studies show that the thrill and excitement linked with scary films can be therapeutic: It allows viewers to release bottled-up emotions and experience a sense of relief after the movie is over. This probably explains why during the COVID-19 pandemic, horror and pandemic thrillers were the most-watched movies on digital movie apps.

However, researchers also find that horror movies can have negative effects on some people. People who are more sensitive to anxiety can panic after viewing a thriller. For those with unpleasant experiences, trauma may be triggered by the themes and images in the movies, which could make their symptoms worse. Furthermore, watching horror movies can disturb sleep patterns, as the residual fear and anxiety they evoke may keep people awake all night, thus leading to fatigue and irritability the following day. Finally, specialists warn that frightening films can have a negative impact on children. Children under 14 who watch horror movies have a greater chance of developing anxiety later in adulthood. Worse yet, exposure to graphic violence and bloodshed can make them less sensitive to real-life violence and more accepting of aggression.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
恐怖電影常有殭屍和連續殺人犯，對某些人來說太嚇人，一點也不好玩。但也有很多人喜歡看一場精彩的驚悚好戲，會排隊去看最新的恐怖片。既然每個人的喜好差這麼多，新的研究開始釐清恐怖電影的好處和風險。

恐怖電影的一個好處，和所謂的「安全的恐懼」有關。看恐怖片時，觀眾舒舒服服地待在自己家裡或電影院的座位上，沒有面臨任何真正的危險。在這種可以掌控的環境裡，這類電影反而可能減少對觀眾的負面衝擊，讓他們變得更堅強。其次，觀眾融入劇情時，往往會站在角色的立場，不自覺地在腦中預演情節。研究人員認為，觀眾就是這樣透過別人的經歷來學習，學到在現實世界中應付威脅的方法。此外，研究顯示，恐怖片帶來的刺激和興奮有療癒的效果：可以讓觀眾宣洩壓抑已久的情緒，電影結束後感到一陣輕鬆。這大概可以解釋，為什麼在新冠肺炎疫情期間，恐怖片和疫情題材的驚悚片是線上影音平台上觀看次數最多的電影。

不過，研究人員也發現，恐怖電影對某些人會有負面影響。比較容易焦慮的人，看完驚悚片可能會驚慌失措。有過不愉快經歷的人，電影的主題和畫面可能勾起心理創傷，讓症狀更加惡化。再者，看恐怖片可能打亂睡眠，因為片子引發的恐懼和焦慮久久不散，可能讓人整夜睡不著，隔天就容易疲倦、煩躁。最後，專家警告，恐怖電影可能對兒童造成負面影響。14 歲以下看恐怖片的兒童，成年後比較容易出現焦慮的問題。更糟的是，接觸血腥暴力的畫面，可能讓兒童對現實生活中的暴力變得麻木，也更能接受攻擊行為。

閱讀測驗.title: 俄羅斯人的飲酒文化史（The History of Drinking Culture in Russia）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Russia is widely portrayed as the most alcohol-dependent country in the world. Critics of the country say that drinking is almost an inherent trait of the Russian people. However, there is more to the story.

The consumption of alcoholic beverages was unusual in ancient Russia. Before the adoption of Christianity in Russia (10th century), there were no vineyards and therefore no wine. People only drank beverages with low alcohol content. Vodka, Russia’s national drink, was not a Russian invention. The liquid was originally a grape alcohol introduced from France in the late 14th century. The first Russian-made vodka appeared in the 15th century, and the drink remained relatively low in alcohol content until the mid-18th century.

There is contradictory information about Russians’ inclination toward alcohol in the 15th and 16th centuries. Some documents noted that Russians “indulge in excessive drinking whenever the occasion arises,” while others claimed that Russians “rarely drink wine.” The heaviest drinkers in medieval Europe were actually Germans. There were many sayings about their desire for alcohol, such as “drunk as a German.”

The Russian state played a significant role in the spread of alcohol consumption in the country. In the 19th century, the emperors began to establish a state monopoly, largely due to the rise of illegal production of low-quality vodka. Thus, only the government was permitted to produce the alcohol. This soon filled the state treasury with huge revenues, but it also encouraged vodka consumption. The situation worsened when the industrial production of vodka began in the country, causing its prices to drop sharply and making it available to even low-income citizens.

Meanwhile, a powerful anti-alcohol movement started in the 19th century. Government policies were made and public organizations established to prevent the spread of alcoholism in the country. The movement continued over the years; however, the problem remains. Although Russia does not occupy first place when it comes to alcohol consumption per capita, it is still close to the top.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
一般人常把俄羅斯說成全世界最依賴酒精的國家，批評俄羅斯的人更說，愛喝酒幾乎是俄羅斯人與生俱來的特質。不過，事情沒有這麼簡單。

在古代俄羅斯，喝酒其實並不常見。俄羅斯在 10 世紀接受基督教之前，沒有葡萄園，所以也沒有葡萄酒，人們只喝酒精濃度低的飲料。俄羅斯的國酒伏特加並不是俄羅斯人發明的，原本是 14 世紀末從法國傳入的葡萄烈酒。第一批俄羅斯自製的伏特加在 15 世紀出現，一直到 18 世紀中葉，伏特加的酒精濃度都還相對偏低。

關於 15、16 世紀的俄羅斯人愛不愛喝酒，史料的說法互相矛盾。有的文獻記載俄羅斯人「一有機會就喝得過量」，有的卻說俄羅斯人「很少喝葡萄酒」。中世紀歐洲最會喝酒的其實是德國人，當時有許多俗語形容德國人嗜酒，例如「醉得像個德國人」。

俄羅斯在酒類消費的擴散上，國家扮演了重要的角色。19 世紀時，由於非法製造的劣質伏特加大增，沙皇開始建立國家專賣制度，從此只有政府可以生產酒。專賣制度很快為國庫帶來龐大的收入，卻也助長了伏特加的消費。後來俄羅斯開始以工業化方式生產伏特加，價格大幅下跌，連低收入的民眾都買得起，情況就更加惡化。

同一時期，19 世紀也興起一股強大的禁酒運動：政府制定政策，民間成立團體，要防止酗酒在國內蔓延。這股運動持續多年，問題卻依然存在。雖然以人均飲酒量來說，俄羅斯並不是第一名，但仍然名列前茅。

items.stem: What is the main purpose of the second paragraph in the passage?

第一批俄羅斯自製的伏特加出現，就是俄羅斯開始生產伏特加。(B) 照抄 France，但原文說從法國傳入的是葡萄烈酒，沒提小麥；(C) 照抄第 3 段的德國人和中世紀歐洲，但原文說德國人最會喝酒，不是最會生產伏特加；(D) 19 世紀其實只准政府生產。

items.explanation:
In the 19th century, the emperors began to establish a state monopoly, largely due to the rise of illegal production of low-quality vodka.
This soon filled the state treasury with huge revenues, but it also encouraged vodka consumption.
讓國庫進帳、又助長伏特加消費的，是只准政府生產酒的國家專賣制度。(C) illegal production 是建立專賣制度的原因，(B) government 是專賣制度裡的主角，都照抄同一段的字詞，卻不是 This 指的那件事。

閱讀測驗.title: 人字拖的歷史與影響（The History and Impact of Flip-flops）
閱讀測驗.passage:
The flip-flop is the simplest shoe on the planet. It consists of a piece of rubber, plastic, leather, or woven material in the outline of a foot, with a strap holding the sandal to a wearer’s toes. The name comes from the sound the sandals make when they slap the walking feet.

The earliest record of people wearing the flip-flop comes from Egypt, but many ancient cultures had their own variants of the footwear. In the Greek version, the toe strap ran between the first and second toes, while Roman sandals had the strap between the second and third toes. The Mesopotamians wore the strap between the third and fourth toes. In India, “toe knob” sandals had a knob between the first and second toes.

Modern flip-flops derive from Japanese zōris, which were often worn with socks dividing the big toe from the rest, and were typically made of rice straw. During World War II, Japan seized much of Southeast Asia’s rubber. In 1945, devastated from the war, the country set about establishing a cheap industry that could rebuild its economy. The Japanese used their rubber reserves from the war to mass-produce the simplest Japanese footwear. Rubber thus replaced rice straw as the major material for the flip-flop.

In the 1950s, flip-flops became popular in the United States as soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home. The sandals have subsequently undergone redesign, often appearing in bright colors in line with Californian beach culture. They have remained popular due to their convenience, and are often worn with bathing suits or summer clothing. Some people also wear dressy versions for more formal occasions.

Despite their popularity, flip-flops provoke some questions. Their simple design is responsible for many foot injuries. Another issue is the suitability of exposing feet on the street and places other than the beach. But even more serious is their environmental impact: Millions of plastic discards end up in landfills or the ocean, releasing chemicals and at the same time taking centuries to decompose.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
人字拖是世界上最簡單的鞋子，用一片橡膠、塑膠、皮革或編織材料做成腳的形狀，再用一條帶子把鞋固定在腳趾上。英文名稱 flip-flop 來自走路時鞋子拍打腳底的聲音。

最早有人穿人字拖的紀錄來自埃及，不過許多古文明都有自己的版本。希臘式的腳趾帶穿過大拇趾和第二趾之間，羅馬涼鞋的帶子則在第二趾和第三趾之間，美索不達米亞人的帶子在第三趾和第四趾之間。印度則有一種「趾鈕」涼鞋，大拇趾和第二趾之間有一個圓鈕。

現代的人字拖源自日本的草履。草履通常用稻草編成，常搭配把大拇趾和其他腳趾分開的襪子來穿。二次世界大戰期間，日本奪取了東南亞大部分的橡膠。1945 年，飽受戰爭摧殘的日本著手建立低成本的產業來重建經濟，用戰時囤積的橡膠大量生產這種最簡單的日本鞋子。於是橡膠取代稻草，成為人字拖的主要材料。

1950 年代，從美軍占領下的日本返國的士兵把草履帶回家，人字拖便在美國流行起來。此後這種涼鞋經過重新設計，常以鮮豔的顏色出現，和加州的海灘文化相互呼應。人字拖穿脫方便，所以一直很受歡迎，常搭配泳裝或夏季服裝；也有人在比較正式的場合穿講究一點的款式。

人字拖雖然受歡迎，也引發一些問題。人字拖的設計太簡單，許多腳傷都是這樣造成的。另一個問題是，在街上和海灘以外的地方露出雙腳是否合宜。不過更嚴重的是人字拖對環境的衝擊：數以百萬計的廢棄塑膠拖鞋最後進了垃圾掩埋場或海洋，不但釋放化學物質，還要好幾百年才能分解。

閱讀測驗.title: 領港員的專業（The Profession of Marine Pilot）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Ships are the lifeline of trade among countries. Almost everything, from food to machinery, comes by way of the sea in huge ships piloted by captains. But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor. The task of bringing the ship into the harbor and anchoring it is taken up by a different captain. This captain is called a marine pilot.

A marine pilot is a boat pilot with specialized knowledge of a particular port or harbor. The pilot is needed to direct large ships into a port, where there are often deep water channels surrounded by shallower seabeds. Without the services of a marine pilot, docking ships would be hazardous. There would be a real chance of running aground and damaging the ship and the cargo, some of which might be dangerous if released into a water-based ecosystem.

In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port. During different tides, currents may change from one direction to the other. The same strategy for docking a vessel during an incoming tide may not work during an outgoing tide. Also, the wind can significantly alter the direction of the ship and how it reacts, adding to the difficulty of anchoring the ship.

Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking. Above all, it is about risk management. A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time and controls the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand. The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
船舶是國際貿易的命脈。從糧食到機械，幾乎所有東西都由船長駕駛的巨型船隻經海路運來。不過船長只負責把船開到港口、等候進港為止；把船帶進港內並下錨停泊的工作，則交給另一位船長，這位船長就叫做領港員。

領港員是對某個港口有專門知識的船隻駕駛。港口常有深水航道，四周卻是比較淺的海床，所以需要領港員引導大型船隻進港。少了領港員，船隻靠岸會很危險，很可能擱淺，損壞船身和貨物；有些貨物一旦流進水域的生態系，還可能造成危害。

除了海床較淺，潮汐和風也讓船隻進港更加困難。漲潮和退潮時，海流的方向可能完全相反，漲潮時讓船靠岸的方法，退潮時不一定行得通。此外，風也會大幅改變船的方向和反應，讓停泊更加困難。

領港這份工作需要高度的專業，也需要能迅速、獨立地思考。最重要的是，這份工作講究的是風險管理。領港員在關鍵時刻登船，根據自己對港口和當下狀況的了解來操控船隻。領港員不但要負責船的安全，也要保護港口和海洋環境。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
items.explanation: 第 1 段引出領港員這個職業，第 2–3 段說這份工作為什麼需要、難在哪裡，第 4 段總結這份工作的要求和責任，所以全文介紹的是一種特殊的職業。(B) 航運與貿易是第 1 段開頭的引子，範圍比領港員大得多，太過廣泛；(C) 船隻靠港的難處只在第 2、3 段，文章也沒有列出什麼準則，(D) 海洋環境的保護只在第 2 段和第 4 段末尾帶到，兩個都過於狹隘。

items.stem: Which of the following is part of the knowledge that a marine pilot must have?
items.explanation:
In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port.
controls the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand
第 3 段說潮汐和風會改變船的方向，第 4 段說領港員要依當下的狀況操控船隻，所以天氣狀況是必備的知識，原文的 wind 在選項換成概括的 weather conditions。(B) 的 cargo 取自第 2 段，那裡講的是擱淺時貨物會受損，不是領港員要懂貨物內容。

items.stem: What does “a crucial time” in the last paragraph refer to?
options: When the vessel hits a flat.
When the channel is not deep enough.
When there is a collision of two ships.
When a ship is waiting to enter the port.
items.explanation:
But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor.
A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time
第 1 段說船長把船開到港口、等候進港時，就換領港員接手，這正是領港員登船的關鍵時刻；harbor 在選項換成 port。(B) 的 channel 取自第 2 段，講的是港口的地形，不是登船的時間點。

items.stem: How does the author conclude the passage in the last paragraph?
options: By giving advice to the general public.
items.explanation:
Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking.
The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.
末段把前面講過的內容再收一次：專業知識對應第 2 段，迅速獨立的判斷對應第 3 段的潮汐和風，船和海洋環境的安全對應第 2 段的擱淺與貨物外洩，所以是總結重點，沒有新的細節，也沒有預測或給一般大眾的建議。

閱讀測驗.title: 斑馬魚的再生能力（The Regenerative Ability of Zebrafish）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Zebrafish, named for their characteristic stripes, have been a popular test subject for researchers. Only a few centimeters in length, the fish breed easily in captivity, grow quickly, and their transparent body makes it easy to study their organs. Above all, they possess some amazing “self-healing” power. When part of their heart is removed, they can grow it back in a matter of weeks. When blinded, they can quickly regain the ability to see.

Recent studies show that humans and zebrafish have the same major organs and share 70 percent of the genes. Moreover, 84 percent of human genes associated with disease find a counterpart in zebrafish. Scientists thus hope that understanding the self-healing mystery of the fish may one day allow humans to regenerate such organs as eyes, hearts, and spines.

Researchers at Vanderbilt University are particularly interested in zebrafish retina regeneration. They have learned that damage of retina can cause blindness in zebrafish, yet it only takes about three to four weeks before vision is restored. The structure and cell types of zebrafish retinas are almost identical to those of humans. If the process can be replicated in humans, it may give rise to new treatments for blindness caused by retinal damage.

In order to know exactly how zebrafish retina is regenerated, the team looked at the neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a chemical messenger in the brain that reduces the activity of neurons. They found that lowering GABA levels in zebrafish can trigger retina regeneration, while a high level of GABA concentration will suppress the regeneration process. This suggested that GABA plays an important role in the fish’s ability to regain their sight.

The team is beginning to test the GABA theory on mice. If that works, human trials will be next on the agenda. If the research proves successful in humans, some of the nearly 40 million blind people worldwide may one day have a tiny, striped fish to thank.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
斑馬魚因身上特有的條紋而得名，一直是研究人員愛用的實驗對象。斑馬魚只有幾公分長，在人工飼養下容易繁殖、長得快，身體又是透明的，觀察器官十分方便。最重要的是，斑馬魚擁有驚人的「自我修復」能力：心臟切掉一部分，幾個星期就能長回來；眼睛看不見了，也能很快恢復視力。

近來的研究顯示，人類和斑馬魚有相同的主要器官，基因有 70% 相同。而且與疾病相關的人類基因，有 84% 在斑馬魚身上找得到對應的基因。因此科學家希望，弄懂斑馬魚自我修復的奧祕，或許有一天能讓人類的眼睛、心臟、脊椎這些器官再生。

范德堡大學的研究人員對斑馬魚視網膜的再生特別感興趣。他們發現，視網膜受損會讓斑馬魚失明，但只要大約三到四個星期，視力就能恢復。斑馬魚視網膜的結構和細胞種類幾乎和人類一模一樣，如果這個過程能在人類身上重現，或許能為視網膜受損造成的失明帶來新的療法。

為了弄清楚斑馬魚的視網膜究竟怎麼再生，研究團隊觀察了神經傳導物質 GABA（γ-胺基丁酸）。GABA 是腦中的化學信使，會降低神經元的活動。研究團隊發現，降低斑馬魚體內的 GABA 濃度可以啟動視網膜再生，GABA 濃度高則會抑制再生的過程。這表示 GABA 在斑馬魚恢復視力的能力中扮演重要的角色。

研究團隊開始在老鼠身上測試 GABA 的理論，如果成功，下一步就是人體試驗。要是研究在人體上也證實有效，全世界將近 4,000 萬名盲人當中，也許有些人有一天要感謝這種小小的條紋魚。

items.stem: What can we learn about zebrafish from the passage?
options: How they should be studied in labs.
Where they derive their regenerative ability.
Why they share humans’ genetic code.
What they may offer in medical advancements.
items.explanation:
Scientists thus hope that understanding the self-healing mystery of the fish may one day allow humans to regenerate such organs as eyes, hearts, and spines.
it may give rise to new treatments for blindness caused by retinal damage
第 2 段說斑馬魚或許能讓人類的器官再生，第 3 段說可能帶來治療失明的新療法，這些都是醫學上的進展。(B) 文章只說 GABA 在視網膜再生中扮演重要角色，沒說再生能力從哪裡來；(C) 只說基因有 70% 相同，沒說為什麼相同。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding GABA in zebrafish?
options: Increasing GABA level facilitates neuron activities.
There is a high level of GABA in the brain of zebrafish.
Lowering GABA levels in the brain can stimulate retina regrowth.
GABA contains chemical elements that trigger the growth of neurons.
items.explanation:
They found that lowering GABA levels in zebrafish can trigger retina regeneration
trigger 在選項換成 stimulate，regeneration 換成 regrowth。(A) 方向相反，原文說 GABA 降低神經元的活動；(D) 照抄同一段的 chemical 和 trigger，可是會啟動再生的是降低 GABA，不是 GABA 含有什麼成分；(B) 文章沒有比較斑馬魚腦中 GABA 的高低。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “replicated” in the third paragraph?
items.explanation:
If the process can be replicated in humans, it may give rise to new treatments for blindness caused by retinal damage.
把斑馬魚視網膜再生的過程在人類身上「再做一次」，replicate 和 reproduce 都是複製、重現。(D) Restored 照抄同一段 vision is restored，但恢復的是視力，不是把過程複製到人身上。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is an opinion, but NOT a fact?
options: Humans and zebrafish have 70 percent of genes in common.
Zebrafish can quickly recover vision after damage to the retina.
Scientists are testing if the GABA theory works on mice as it does on zebrafish.
Understanding regeneration in zebrafish may allow humans to regrow their organs.
items.explanation:
Scientists thus hope that understanding the self-healing mystery of the fish may one day allow humans to regenerate such organs as eyes, hearts, and spines.
hope 和 may 表示的是科學家的期望和推測，還沒有證實，屬於意見。(A)、(B)、(C) 文章都當作研究結果或正在進行的事來陳述，是事實。

閱讀測驗.title: 堅忍號的南極探險傳奇（The Legendary Antarctic Expedition of the Endurance）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In March 2022, the Endurance—the lost vessel of the famed polar explorer Ernest Shackleton—was found in Antarctica, 107 years after it sank. The news made headlines around the world, not only for the incredible achievement of the search team, but because the discovery marked the final chapter in a legendary story of extraordinary courage and perseverance.

On August 4, 1914, Sir Ernest Shackleton, along with a skilled crew of 27, set sail on the Endurance toward the South Pole, hoping to make the first land crossing over Antarctica. From Plymouth, UK, the team arrived in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and on November 5 reached South Georgia Island, the last settlement of civilization en route to Antarctica. There, the real challenge began. Two days after leaving South Georgia in December, the Endurance encountered floating ice, and was soon completely trapped in pack ice.

The worthy vessel held up for nine months, drifting down south slowly and then pushed northward by the ice. Gradually, the pressure from the ice buckled the planks. Freezing water rushed in and exacerbated the situation. On October 27, 1915, Shackleton ordered his crew to abandon the ship, pitching tents on the ice a mile and a half away. Weeks later, they watched the Endurance sink beneath the Weddell Sea.

The next five months, the crew camped out on the pack ice as it drifted north, surviving on penguins, seals, and seaweed. Finally, the ice broke up enough for them to escape in lifeboats. For seven days, they sailed more than a hundred miles to the uninhabited Elephant Island. But the crew couldn’t survive long there. So, Shackleton made a dangerous attempt to get help: With five crew members, he sailed 800 miles over 16 days across freezing, stormy seas to South Georgia Island. Then the group hiked for 36 hours across the island to reach a whaling station.

Help was almost at hand, but ice and bad weather hindered their return. On August 30, 1916, Shackleton finally got back to Elephant Island with a ship big enough to rescue the rest of his men. All the members of the expedition team survived, but the Endurance remained lost under the sea until its discovery in 2022.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
2022 年 3 月，著名極地探險家 Shackleton 失落的船「堅忍號」在南極尋獲，距離它沉沒已經過了 107 年。這則消息登上世界各地的頭條，不只是因為搜尋團隊的成就驚人，也因為這次發現為一段充滿非凡勇氣與毅力的傳奇故事，寫下了最後一章。

1914 年 8 月 4 日，Ernest Shackleton 爵士帶著 27 名經驗豐富的船員，搭乘堅忍號航向南極，希望成為第一支從陸路橫越南極大陸的隊伍。他們從英國普利茅斯出發，抵達阿根廷布宜諾斯艾利斯，11 月 5 日到達南喬治亞島，這是前往南極途中最後一個有人居住的地方。真正的考驗也從這裡開始。12 月離開南喬治亞島兩天後，堅忍號就碰上浮冰，不久便完全困在密集的浮冰群裡。

這艘船相當堅固，在冰裡過了九個月都沒有解體，先是緩緩往南漂，接著又讓浮冰推著往北走。冰的壓力漸漸把船板擠得變形，冰冷的海水灌進船艙，情況更加惡化。1915 年 10 月 27 日，Shackleton 下令船員棄船，在一英里半外的冰面上搭起帳篷。幾個星期後，他們眼看著堅忍號沉入威德爾海。

接下來五個月，船員在往北漂的浮冰上紮營，靠企鵝、海豹和海草維生。後來浮冰終於裂得夠開，他們才搭救生艇脫困，航行七天、一百多英里，到了無人居住的象島。可是船員沒辦法在島上久留，於是 Shackleton 冒險出海求救：他帶著五名船員，花了 16 天在冰冷又狂風暴雨的海上航行 800 英里，回到南喬治亞島，接著又在島上徒步 36 個小時，才抵達一座捕鯨站。

救援看似近在眼前，冰和惡劣的天氣卻讓他們一直回不去。1916 年 8 月 30 日，Shackleton 終於開著一艘大到足以載走其餘隊員的船回到象島。探險隊全員生還，堅忍號卻一直沉在海底，直到 2022 年才重見天日。

items.stem: What is this passage mainly about?
options: The amazing discovery of a sunken ship.
items.explanation: 第 1 段點出這是一段勇氣與毅力的傳奇，第 2–5 段依時間寫整趟航程從出發、受困、棄船到獲救，所以全文講的是一次艱難的南極航行。(D) 沉船的發現只講第 1 段，是用來引出故事的新聞，過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有介紹 Shackleton 這個人的生平，(B) 天候只是航程的背景，這兩個選項都偏離主題。

items.stem: Which of the following idioms is closest in meaning to “exacerbated the situation” in the third paragraph?
options: Cost an arm and a leg.
items.explanation:
Freezing water rushed in and exacerbated the situation.
船板已經擠壞，冰水又灌進來，情況雪上加霜；exacerbate 是讓壞事變得更糟，和 add fuel to the fire（火上加油）意思相同。

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about Shackleton and his Antarctic expedition?
options: His journey lasted more than two years.
He was the first man to cross over the Antarctic.
His team camped out on Elephant Island for five months.
He sent five crew members on a lifeboat to get help from a whaling station.
items.explanation:
On August 4, 1914, Sir Ernest Shackleton, along with a skilled crew of 27, set sail on the Endurance toward the South Pole, hoping to make the first land crossing over Antarctica.
On August 30, 1916, Shackleton finally got back to Elephant Island with a ship big enough to rescue the rest of his men.
原文沒有直接寫「兩年」，要把第 2 段出發的日期和第 5 段救回所有人的日期相減，1914 年 8 月到 1916 年 8 月底，超過兩年。(C) 和 (D) 都照抄第 4 段的字詞，卻把事情接錯：在浮冰上紮營五個月的是船員，不是在象島；五名船員是跟著 Shackleton 一起去求救，不是他派出去的。

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct route of the Endurance after leaving South Georgia?
items.explanation:
Two days after leaving South Georgia in December, the Endurance encountered floating ice, and was soon completely trapped in pack ice.
The worthy vessel held up for nine months, drifting down south slowly and then pushed northward by the ice.
Weeks later, they watched the Endurance sink beneath the Weddell Sea.
題目問的是堅忍號這艘船的路線，不是船員的路線：船離開南喬治亞島後困在浮冰裡，先往南漂、再往北推，最後沉在威德爾海，沒有到過象島，對應 (C)。(A) 畫到象島再回南喬治亞島，那是第 4 段船員搭救生艇和 Shackleton 求救的路線。

閱讀測驗.title: 螺旋梯的歷史與功能演變（The History and Functional Evolution of Spiral Staircases）
閱讀測驗.passage:
In many old castles in Europe, visitors often find a fantastic spiral staircase, which provides a captivating focal point as it winds up the building. This prominent structure actually has a long and rich heritage.

In the Old Testament, reference is made to spiral staircases in the Temple of Solomon, suggesting that they were already in use by around 1,000 BC. The oldest spiral staircase still standing today is at Trajan’s Column in Rome. The staircase was built in 113 AD, with a total of 185 steps carved in stone and marble. Around this time, spiral staircases began to find much wider use in Roman architecture and across Europe.

Throughout the Middle Ages, winding staircases became a well-established feature of European castles, mainly for their advantages in helping to defend against attackers. To begin with, these staircases were quite narrow, so attackers would have to ascend one at a time, making it impossible to launch a mass attack. Also, the stairs were designed to turn clockwise upwards. This means that ascenders would have their right hand tight against the narrowest part of the staircases, close to the central pole, and as a result were unable to use their sword effectively. The attackers’ challenge was further complicated by the uneven steps of the staircase, often strategically designed by the castle owners. The defenders, living in the castles, were familiar with the stair pattern and could retreat up them very swiftly; while the attackers were much more likely to stumble and fall, particularly in the dimly lit confines of the staircase.

Being associated with medieval castles and kings, spiral staircases gradually won popularity in European architecture, with new materials emerging to cope with customers’ needs. In Victorian times, cast iron spiral staircases were popular for public buildings and homes for the rich. In the latter half of the 20th century, steel frames became cost-effective, and thus affordable for a much wider staircase market. Then, steel spiral staircases as fire escape stairs appeared in many buildings. Today, spiral staircases come in a wide variety of materials: steel, wood, concrete, and recently even glass. The timeless appeal of their classical design makes spiral staircases a much-desired feature in luxury homes, offices, and public buildings nowadays.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
在歐洲許多古堡裡，遊客常會看到一座漂亮的螺旋梯沿著建築盤旋而上，成為吸引目光的焦點。這種顯眼的結構，其實有一段悠久而豐富的歷史。

舊約聖經提到所羅門聖殿裡有螺旋梯，可見大約西元前 1000 年就已經有人使用。現存最古老、至今仍然屹立的螺旋梯，在羅馬的圖拉真柱裡面。這座螺旋梯建於西元 113 年，共有 185 級，是用石頭和大理石鑿成的。大約從這個時候起，螺旋梯在羅馬建築乃至整個歐洲用得越來越廣。

整個中世紀，螺旋梯成了歐洲城堡常見的設計，主要是因為它有助於抵禦敵人。首先，這種樓梯相當狹窄，進攻的人只能一個接一個往上爬，沒辦法大舉進攻。其次，樓梯設計成順時針往上轉，也就是說，往上爬的人右手會緊貼著樓梯最窄、靠近中柱的那一側，因此沒辦法好好揮劍。城堡主人往往還刻意把階梯做得高低不一，讓進攻的一方更加吃力。住在城堡裡的守方熟悉階梯的樣子，可以很快退到樓上；進攻的人在昏暗狹小的樓梯間裡，就容易絆倒摔跤。

螺旋梯讓人聯想到中世紀的城堡和國王，在歐洲建築裡漸漸受到歡迎，也陸續出現新的材料來因應顧客的需求。維多利亞時期，鑄鐵螺旋梯常見於公共建築和富人的住宅。到了二十世紀下半葉，鋼骨架變得划算，更多人買得起，螺旋梯的市場也跟著擴大。後來，許多建築開始用鋼製螺旋梯當逃生梯。如今螺旋梯的材質五花八門，有鋼、木頭、混凝土，最近甚至還有玻璃。古典的設計歷久不衰，讓螺旋梯成為現今豪宅、辦公室和公共建築很受青睞的設計。

items.stem: Which question can the passage answer?
options: Where was the first spiral staircase constructed?
Who was the first designer of the spiral staircase?
What is the world’s most famous spiral staircase?
Why is the spiral staircase popular in modern times?
items.explanation:
The timeless appeal of their classical design makes spiral staircases a much-desired feature in luxury homes, offices, and public buildings nowadays.
最後一句說古典設計歷久不衰，所以螺旋梯現今很受青睞，回答了 (D) 的「為什麼」。(A) 文章只說最早的記載在舊約、現存最古老的在圖拉真柱，沒說第一座建在哪裡；(B)、(C) 文章都沒提。

items.stem: What does “them” in the third paragraph refer to?
items.explanation:
The defenders, living in the castles, were familiar with the stair pattern and could retreat up them very swiftly
retreat up 後面要接可以往上退的地方，就是同一句前面 the stair pattern 說的樓梯。(D) Defenders 是這一句的主詞，(C) Attackers 在後半句，兩者都是人，不能「退到人上面」。

items.stem: According to the passage, which is a correct time sequence of the materials used in making spiral staircases?
items.explanation:
The staircase was built in 113 AD, with a total of 185 steps carved in stone and marble.
In Victorian times, cast iron spiral staircases were popular for public buildings and homes for the rich.
In the latter half of the 20th century, steel frames became cost-effective, and thus affordable for a much wider staircase market.
Today, spiral staircases come in a wide variety of materials: steel, wood, concrete, and recently even glass.
依時間把材料排出來：西元 113 年的石頭、維多利亞時期的鑄鐵、二十世紀的鋼、最近的玻璃。選項照用原文的材料名稱，難處在把散在兩段的時間點串起來。

items.stem: Which of the following statements can be inferred about spiral staircases in the Medieval Ages?
options: The staircase was too narrow to allow any quick retreat.
The clockwise design favored right-handed castle defenders.
The uneven steps made it easier to ascend than descend the stairs.
The staircase was dark enough for defenders to hide from attackers.
items.explanation:
Also, the stairs were designed to turn clockwise upwards.
This means that ascenders would have their right hand tight against the narrowest part of the staircases, close to the central pole, and as a result were unable to use their sword effectively.
原文只說往上爬的攻方右手貼著中柱、揮不了劍；守方站在上面往下打，右手剛好在寬的那一側，所以推得出順時針的設計對慣用右手的守方有利。

閱讀測驗.title: 地圖方位的歷史演變（The Historical Evolution of Map Orientation）
閱讀測驗.passage:
Have you ever wondered why north comes at the top of a map? Well, north may seem a natural choice for the top spot today, but that wasn’t always the case.

Documents from ancient times indicate that many maps in early ages were pointing to the east, where the sun rose. In ancient India, for example, maps were most likely oriented to the east. Though there is no physical evidence to support this, the word dakshina “south” in Indian languages also means “right,” suggesting that ancient Indians were oriented toward the east, and therefore south was on their right-hand side. Ample evidences from the Old Testament also suggest that east was at the top of maps in pre-Biblical and Biblical eras, a reason why east is still referred to as the “Orient” today.

In the oldest surviving maps, south is at the top, and north points down. Early Egyptian maps showed south on top, most likely because the Nile, vital to Egyptian livelihood, originated in the south. As rivers were believed to flow downward, “up” was therefore south. Map makers in Arabia also drew maps with south on top since the earliest Muslims lived north of Mecca, and a south-oriented map would show the followers looking up toward their holy city.

The preference for north arose during the European age of exploration. At the time, sailors relied on the North Star to find their way across the Mediterranean and later the Atlantic. By the 16th century, when Europe’s search for trading routes was at its peak, maps became Eurocentric, with north on top. The expansion of European imperialism in the following centuries further established the “north up” practice as the standard.

Today, map orientation is taking on a new perspective. In perhaps our most common interaction with maps—the use of GPS systems on our phones and in our cars, directions have ceased to be as important. The layouts are dynamic, oriented toward our travel path.

So, perhaps the north-on-top practice is less a rule and more a blip. After centuries of technological advancements, it seems we’ve ended up right where we began in ancient times: with ourselves in the middle, and our destinations at the top.
閱讀測驗.passageZh:
你有沒有想過，為什麼地圖的上方是北方？如今北方朝上看起來理所當然，但其實並不是一向如此。

古代文獻顯示，早期許多地圖都朝向東方，也就是太陽升起的方向。以古印度為例，當時的地圖很可能以東方為上方。雖然沒有實物證據可以證明這一點，不過印度語言裡表示「南」的 dakshina 這個字也有「右」的意思，可見古印度人面向東方，南方因此在他們的右手邊。舊約聖經裡也有大量證據顯示，在聖經成書之前和聖經時代，地圖上方是東方，這也是東方至今仍叫做 Orient 的原因之一。

現存最古老的地圖是南方朝上、北方朝下。早期埃及地圖把南方畫在上面，很可能是因為對埃及人生計至關重要的尼羅河發源於南方；古人認為河水往下流，所以「上」就是南方。阿拉伯的製圖者也把南方畫在上面，因為最早的穆斯林住在麥加北邊，南方朝上的地圖可以讓信徒抬頭望向他們的聖城。

北方朝上的習慣，是在歐洲的探險時代形成的。當時水手靠北極星辨認方向，航行地中海，後來又橫渡大西洋。到了十六世紀，歐洲尋找貿易航線的熱潮達到高峰，地圖變成以歐洲為中心、北方朝上。之後幾個世紀歐洲帝國主義擴張，更讓「北方朝上」成為標準做法。

如今地圖的方位又有了新的樣貌。我們最常接觸地圖的方式，大概就是用手機和車上的 GPS 系統；在這種情況下，東南西北已經不再那麼重要，畫面會隨時變動，跟著我們的行進路線轉向。

所以，北方朝上這個慣例與其說是規則，不如說只是一時的現象。經過幾百年的科技進步，我們似乎又回到了古代的起點：自己在中間，目的地在上方。

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why east is referred to as the “Orient.”
How maps differ from GPS in function.
How map orientation evolved over time.
Why maps were important during the age of exploration.
items.explanation: 第 1 段提問地圖為什麼北方朝上，第 2–5 段依時間寫東方朝上、南方朝上、北方朝上到 GPS 隨路線轉向，所以全文講方位怎麼隨時代演變。(A) 只講第 2 段最後一句，(B) 只講第 5 段的 GPS，(D) 只講第 4 段的時代背景，三個錯誤選項都過於狹隘。

items.stem: What does “this” refer to in the second paragraph?
items.explanation:
In ancient India, for example, maps were most likely oriented to the east.
Though there is no physical evidence to support this
沒有實物證據可以支持的是前一句的整件事：古印度地圖很可能以東方為上方。(B) Physical evidence 是同一個子句裡的字，(A)、(C) 也都照抄這一段的字詞，但都不是要「證明」的那件事。

items.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “a blip” in the last paragraph?
items.explanation:
So, perhaps the north-on-top practice is less a rule and more a blip.
less A and more B 是「與其說是 A，不如說是 B」，blip 和 rule（長久的規則）相對；下一句又說我們回到了古代的起點，可見北方朝上只是一時的現象。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true?
options: Sailors took the North Star as their final destination.
The GPS system has a fixed direction for orientation.
South was placed at the top of maps in the pre-Biblical era.
Old Islamic maps put south at the top for religious purposes.
items.explanation:
Map makers in Arabia also drew maps with south on top since the earliest Muslims lived north of Mecca, and a south-oriented map would show the followers looking up toward their holy city.
讓信徒抬頭望向聖城麥加，就是出於宗教的理由。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 pre-Biblical，但那個時代是東方朝上；(A) 北極星是用來辨認方向，不是目的地；(B) 第 5 段說 GPS 畫面隨路線轉向，不是固定方向。

中翻英.zh: 他點頭表示贊同。
中翻英.en: He indicated approval with a nod.

中翻英.zh: 我深信寫日記的價值。
中翻英.en: I am convinced of the value of keeping a diary.

中翻英.zh: 就交通安全而言，台北大部分駕駛員應該再受教育。
中翻英.en: As far as traffic safety is concerned, most drivers in Taipei should be reeducated.

中翻英.zh: 假如當時受到鼓勵和幫助，他就不會失敗了。
中翻英.en: Given encouragement and help, he would not have failed.

中翻英.zh: 強大的國防是和平與自由最確切的保證。
中翻英.en: A strong national defense is the most certain guarantee of peace and freedom.

中翻英.zh: 運動對健康有益。
中翻英.en: Exercise is good for one's health.

中翻英.zh: 我的腳踏車，上禮拜被偷了。
中翻英.en: My bicycle was stolen last Sunday.

中翻英.zh: 大多數的學生，都不曉得如何使用圖書館。
中翻英.en: Most students do not know how to use a library.

中翻英.zh: 我在今天的報紙上，看到一則很有趣的新聞。
中翻英.en: I read an interesting piece of news in today's newspaper.

中翻英.zh: 要學好英文，必須下功夫。
中翻英.en: If you want to learn English well, you have to work hard.

中翻英.zh: 這一篇文章值得仔細閱讀。
中翻英.en: This article is worth reading carefully.

中翻英.zh: 中國字很難寫嗎？
中翻英.en: Is it very hard to write Chinese characters?

中翻英.zh: 那一位戴黃帽子的外國人是誰？
中翻英.en: Who is the foreigner that is wearing a yellow hat?

中翻英.zh: 天氣一天比一天熱起來了。
中翻英.en: It is getting hotter day by day.

中翻英.zh: 我不是告訴過你，我到車站的時候他們已經走了嗎？
中翻英.en: Haven't I told you that they had already gone when I got to the station?

中翻英.zh: 今天早晨有一位穿綠色制服的人，把信件送到我們的社區來。
中翻英.en: Every morning a man in a green uniform delivers mail to our community.

中翻英.zh: 無論是晴天或下雨，天天都可以看到他。
中翻英.en: Rain or shine, we can see him every day.

中翻英.zh: 如果有掛號信要送給我們，他就會在門口按一下鈴。
中翻英.en: Whenever he has registered letters for us, he will ring the doorbell.

中翻英.zh: 他認識我們附近的每一個人，而我們每一個人也都認識他。
中翻英.en: He knows everyone in our neighborhood, and everyone of us also knows him.

中翻英.zh: 有時候我在上學的途中遇到他，他就以微笑跟我打招呼。
中翻英.en: Sometimes I meet him on my way to school, and he greets me with a smile.

中翻英.zh: 很多學生都不太注意讀書的方法，以至於浪費許多寶貴的時間。
中翻英.en: Many students pay so little attention to reading skills that they waste a lot of precious time.

中翻英.zh: 他們讀英文讀了好幾年，還是看不懂相當容易的文章。
中翻英.en: They have studied English for many years, but they still cannot understand articles which are rather easy.

中翻英.zh: 其實，只要方法正確，英文的閱讀能力並不難培養。
中翻英.en: In fact, as long as the method is correct, English reading ability is not difficult to develop.

中翻英.zh: 在老師還沒有講解課文之前，一定要自己先讀兩三遍。
中翻英.en: Before your teacher explains the text to you, you must go over it two or three times.

中翻英.zh: 不要讀太難的文章，也不要遇到生字就立刻查字典。
中翻英.en: Don't read articles which are too difficult for you and don't look up a new word in a dictionary the moment you see it, either.

中翻英.zh: 英語是一種重要的語言，所以很多人都在學習。
中翻英.en: English is an important language, so many people are learning it.

中翻英.zh: 許多中國學生認為學習說英語很難。
中翻英.en: Many Chinese students think that it is very hard to learn to speak English.

中翻英.zh: 但是只要經常練習，任何困難都可以克服。
中翻英.en: But if you keep practicing speaking English, you can overcome any difficulty.

中翻英.zh: 會背課本上的對話，並不表示會說英語。
中翻英.en: Memorizing the dialogues in the text does not mean that you are able to speak English.

中翻英.zh: 最重要的是，要能用英語說自己想說的話。
中翻英.en: The most important thing is that you should be able to say whatever you want to say in English.

中翻英.zh: 讀小學的時候，我身體很虛弱，並且常感冒。
中翻英.en: When I was in elementary school, I was very weak and often caught colds.

中翻英.zh: 自從上了國中以後，我就儘量找機會運動。
中翻英.en: Ever since I entered junior high school, I have been trying hard to find opportunities for exercise.

中翻英.zh: 雖然功課一直很繁重，我還是每天慢跑半小時。
中翻英.en: Although my schoolwork has been heavy, I have managed to jog for half an hour every day.

中翻英.zh: 六年繼續不斷的鍛鍊使我不但更加強壯，而且也長得更高。
中翻英.en: Six years of constant training has made me not only stronger but also taller.

中翻英.zh: 現在大家都說他們無法相信我從前又矮又瘦。
中翻英.en: Now everyone says that they cannot believe that I was short and thin before.

中翻英.zh: 昨天早上我出門的時候，天氣相當暖和。
中翻英.en: It was quite warm when I left home yesterday morning.

中翻英.zh: 所以我沒有穿毛衣，只穿了一件襯衫。
中翻英.en: Therefore, I didn't wear a sweater but only a shirt.

中翻英.zh: 但是到了下午，溫度卻急速下降了。
中翻英.en: But the temperature dropped sharply in the afternoon.

中翻英.zh: 雖然晚上比往常早回家，我還是覺得有點不舒服。
中翻英.en: Though I got back home earlier than usual in the evening, I still felt slightly under the weather.

中翻英.zh: 今天我不但打噴嚏而且頭痛，我想我最好馬上去看醫生。
中翻英.en: Not only am I sneezing today, but I also have a headache. I think I had better see a doctor right away.

中翻英.zh: 我生長在鄉下的一個小村落。
中翻英.en: I grew up in a small village in the country.

中翻英.zh: 那時，我家附近有一條清澈的小溪。
中翻英.en: At that time, there was a clear brook near the house where I lived.

中翻英.zh: 我夏天常到那裡游泳、釣魚。
中翻英.en: I used to go swimming and fishing there in the summer.

中翻英.zh: 現在溪水髒得連魚都不能活。
中翻英.en: Now the water in the brook has become so filthy that fish cannot live in it.

中翻英.zh: 我不知道甚麼時候才能再見到童年的美景。
中翻英.en: I have no idea when I'll be able to see that beautiful view I remember from my childhood.

中翻英.zh: 老實說，一直到昨天我才知道他已經去美國了。
中翻英.en: To tell the truth, not until yesterday did I know he had gone to the United States.

中翻英.zh: 首先，我要說明清楚，我並不反對你的意見。
中翻英.en: To begin with, I want to make it clear that I don't disagree with your opinion.

中翻英.zh: 這個月，我的運氣真是好得我都不敢相信。
中翻英.en: This month I have been so lucky that I can hardly believe it. (My luck has been so good this month that I can hardly believe it.)

中翻英.zh: 月初，我的數學月考考了九十分。
中翻英.en: Early this month, I received a score of 90 on the monthly math exam. (Early this month, I scored 90 on the monthly math exam.)

中翻英.zh: 月中，父親送我一部電腦當生日禮物。
中翻英.en: In the middle of the month, Father gave me a computer as my birthday gift.

中翻英.zh: 前幾天，英語演講比賽我得了第二名。
中翻英.en: A few days ago, I was placed second in the English speech contest. (A few days ago, I won second place in the English speech contest.)

中翻英.zh: 這輩子，我的運氣從來沒有這麼好過。
中翻英.en: I have never been so lucky in my life.

中翻英.zh: 我弟弟過去經常整日虛混，一件有意義的事也不做。
中翻英.en: My brother used to fool around all day long, not doing anything meaningful.

中翻英.zh: 現在，他努力用功，並且對未來有明確的計劃。
中翻英.en: Now, he is studying very hard; besides, he has a clear plan for the future.

中翻英.zh: 是什麼使得他在行為和態度上有這樣明顯的改變呢？
中翻英.en: What changed him so obviously in his behavior and attitude?

中翻英.zh: 是他的高中老師發現了他的潛力，並且不斷地鼓勵他。
中翻英.en: It was his high school teacher that discovered his potential and kept encouraging him.

中翻英.zh: 弟弟說他會永遠記得並感謝這位老師。
中翻英.en: My younger brother says that he will forever remember and be grateful to his teacher.

中翻英.zh: 對於什麼是最佳的渡假方式，大家都有不同的看法。
中翻英.en: Everyone has different opinions about what the best way to spend a vacation is.

中翻英.zh: 有些人喜歡到寧靜的森林中去，在那兒他們可以暫時遠離人群。
中翻英.en: Some people like to go to peaceful forests, where they can get away from the crowds temporarily.

中翻英.zh: 有些人卻寧願到大都市去，因為他們可以參觀博物館或購物。
中翻英.en: Others, however, prefer to go to big cities because they can visit museums or go shopping.

中翻英.zh: 還有一些人喜歡到海邊去，讓海浪沖走他們的煩惱。
中翻英.en: Still others like to go to the beach to let the waves wash away their troubles.

中翻英.zh: 有少數人則決定留在家裡，做一些像打掃屋子之類的事。
中翻英.en: A few people, on the other hand, decide to stay at home and do things like cleaning the house.

中翻英.zh: 台灣的生活最近十年變了很多。
中翻英.en: Life in Taiwan has changed quite a lot over the past ten years.

中翻英.zh: 年輕的一代有許多新的生活方式。
中翻英.en: The younger generation has many new ways of living.

中翻英.zh: 和他們父母親那一輩相當不同。
中翻英.en: Young people are quite different from their parents.

中翻英.zh: 舉個例，很多年輕人喜歡吃美式速食，喝加糖飲料。
中翻英.en: For example, many young people like to eat American fast food and consume sweet drinks.

中翻英.zh: 而老一輩的大多寧可吃中國菜，喝中國茶。
中翻英.en: However, the older generation would rather eat Chinese food and drink tea.

中翻英.zh: 昨天在回家的路上，我看到一個小女孩在路邊哭泣。
中翻英.en: On my way home yesterday, I saw a little girl crying by the roadside.

中翻英.zh: 我趕緊跑過去，問她到底發生了什麼事。
中翻英.en: I hurried over to her and asked her what on earth had happened.

中翻英.zh: 小女孩說她按了好幾次門鈴，卻沒有人來開門。
中翻英.en: The little girl said that she had rung the doorbell several times, but nobody came to open the door.

中翻英.zh: 看到她哭得那麼傷心，我就陪她等媽媽回來。
中翻英.en: Seeing her crying so bitterly, I stayed with her and waited for her mother to come back.

中翻英.zh: 雖然晚了半個鐘頭才回到家，我覺得我做了一件有意義的事。
中翻英.en: Although I got home half an hour late, I felt that I had done something meaningful.

中翻英.zh: 每次放假，我都會到台灣某個地方去旅行。
中翻英.en: Whenever we have a vacation, I'll travel somewhere in Taiwan.

中翻英.zh: 今年春假，我和一些同學搭巴士到墾丁國家公園。
中翻英.en: This spring vacation, I went with some of my classmates by bus to Kenting National Park.

中翻英.zh: 我們在那兒待了三天，很欣賞那裡的山林和海岸。
中翻英.en: We stayed there for three days, appreciating the mountain forests and sea.

中翻英.zh: 這學期還沒結束，可是我們就在計畫夏天的旅行了。
中翻英.en: This semester is not over yet, but we are planning for our summer vacation travels.

中翻英.zh: 我們大概會到台灣東部去，因為那兒風景很美。
中翻英.en: We'll probably go to the east of Taiwan for the scenery there is very beautiful.

中翻英.zh: 有沒有想過未來的旅館會是什麼樣子?
中翻英.en: Have you ever wondered what the hotels of the future will look like?

中翻英.zh: 每個房間附有一部收音機，一台電視機和一個鬧鐘。
中翻英.en: Each room comes with a radio, a television, and an alarm clock.

中翻英.zh: 此外，所有房間都有空調。
中翻英.en: In addition, all the rooms are air-conditioned.

中翻英.zh: 廁所及洗衣設施位於旅館的共同區域。
中翻英.en: The restrooms and laundry facilities are located in the common areas of the hotel.

中翻英.zh: 信不信由你，這家旅館幾乎經常是客滿
中翻英.en: Believe it or not, this hotel is almost always fully booked,

中翻英.zh: 我們即將進入二十一世紀。
中翻英.en: We are going into the 21st century.

中翻英.zh: 那時，人們會活得更長久。
中翻英.en: Then, people will live longer.

中翻英.zh: 那的確是個好消息。
中翻英.en: That is nice indeed.

中翻英.zh: 但是會有一個問題：
中翻英.en: But there exists a problem:

中翻英.zh: 更多的老人必須由更少的年輕人奉養。
中翻英.en: There will be more senior citizens to be supported by fewer young people.

中翻英.zh: 以前，我常常到書店去，
中翻英.en: I used to go to the bookstore,

中翻英.zh: 主要是隨便看看一些書。
中翻英.en: mainly to read some books casually.

中翻英.zh: 有時會買一些小說來讀。
中翻英.en: Sometimes I would buy a few novels to read.

中翻英.zh: 現在因為忙著準備考試，
中翻英.en: Now as I am busy preparing for the examination,

中翻英.zh: 再也沒時間去找小說了。
中翻英.en: I can spare no more time to look for some books to read.

中翻英.zh: 年輕人和老年人的睡眠習慣很不相同。
中翻英.en: Young people's sleeping habit is very different from that of old people.

中翻英.zh: 許多年輕人往往很晚還不睡，第二天早上就不能早起。
中翻英.en: Many young people often stay up so late that they can't get up early the next morning.

中翻英.zh: 老年人通常晚上沒事做，所以很早上床。
中翻英.en: Old people usually have nothing to do, so they go to bed early.

中翻英.zh: 這兩種不同的睡眠習慣，哪一種比較有益健康呢？
中翻英.en: Of these two different habits, which is better for health?

中翻英.zh: 其實，只要睡飽，早睡晚睡都沒關係。
中翻英.en: In fact, as long as you get enough sleep, it doesn't matter whether you go to bed early or not.

中翻英.zh: 不關心注意是中止對話的最快速方法之一。
中翻英.en: Not paying attention is one of the fastest ways to stop a conversation.

中翻英.zh: 而是真的聽懂了。
中翻英.en: but you really understand.

中翻英.zh: 他如何在上學途中被狗咬了。
中翻英.en: how he was bitten by a dog on his way to school.

中翻英.zh: 因為他很餓，所以考試考得不好。
中翻英.en: He didn't do well in a test because he was hungry.

中翻英.zh: 聽起來你今天很倒楣。
中翻英.en: Sounds like you really had a bad day. (It sounds like today wasn't your day.) (You seem to have had a really bad day.)

中翻英.zh: 昨天晚上我感覺有點不舒服。
中翻英.en: I didn't feel quite well last night.

中翻英.zh: 我的媽媽要我去看中醫師。
中翻英.en: My mother wanted me to go to the Chinese herbalist.

中翻英.zh: 她說中葯比西葯自然。
中翻英.en: She said that Chinese medicine is more natural than Western medicine.

中翻英.zh: 我生病的時候通常都會去看西醫。
中翻英.en: When I am ill, I usually go to a Western medical doctor.

中翻英.zh: 但是現在我想我有另外的選擇了。
中翻英.en: But now I guess I have another choice.

中翻英.zh: 她通常在晚餐後吃藥。
中翻英.en: She usually takes medicine after dinner.

中翻英.exam: 英文寫作能力研究用試卷
中翻英.zh: 去年中秋節（Moon Festival）我們吃了不少月餅。
中翻英.en: Last year at the Moon Festival, we ate quite a few mooncakes.

中翻英.exam: 英文寫作能力研究用試卷
中翻英.zh: 請打開收音機，但音量不要開太大。
中翻英.en: Please turn on the radio, but don't turn it up too loud.

中翻英.exam: 英文寫作能力研究用試卷
中翻英.zh: 這本小說有很高的研究價值。
中翻英.en: This novel is of great research value.

中翻英.exam: 英文寫作能力研究用試卷
中翻英.zh: 沒人知道是誰先動手打人的。
中翻英.en: No one knows who threw the first punch.

中翻英.exam: 英文寫作能力研究用試卷
中翻英.zh: 昨晚祖母身體不舒服，所以早上6點我們就開車帶著祖母去看醫生。7點不到，我們就到台北了。但是因為一直找不到停車位，只好開著車子在醫院附近繞了又繞。到了8點，終於停好了車，可是那時祖母已經累壞了。
中翻英.en: Last night my grandmother wasn't feeling well, so at six in the morning we drove her to see a doctor. We got to Taipei before seven. But since we couldn't find a parking space, we had to drive around and around near the hospital. By eight we finally parked the car, but by then my grandmother was worn out.

中翻英.zh: 雖然 Lily 生來又瞎又聾，但她從來不氣餒。
中翻英.en: Although Lily was born both blind and deaf, she has never been discouraged.

中翻英.zh: 她的故事證明了，我們只要努力必能成功。
中翻英.en: Her story proves that we can succeed if we put in effort.

中翻英.zh: 科技讓我們的生活更舒適，然而它也被利用來犯罪。
中翻英.en: Although technology can make our lives more comfortable, it can also be used to commit crimes.

中翻英.zh: 根據最近的新聞報導，最常見的例子是網際網路詐財(Internet scams)。
中翻英.en: According to the latest news report(s), the most common example is Internet scams.

中翻英.zh: 你的性格決定你將會與誰相愛。
中翻英.en: Your personality determines who you will fall in love with.

中翻英.zh: 這個學校不但提供實用課程，也聘用好的老師。
中翻英.en: This school not only offers practical courses but also employs good teachers.

中翻英.zh: 關渡（Guandu）位於台灣的西北部，是觀賞鳥類最佳的地點之一。
中翻英.en: Located in Northwestern Taiwan, Guandu is one of the best places to observe birds.

中翻英.zh: 在這裡你會看到不同的鳥類，有些甚至是在台灣極為罕見的。
中翻英.en: You can see a variety of birds here; some of them are rarely seen in Taiwan.

中翻英.zh: 人類對外太空所知非常有限，但長久以來我們對它卻很感興趣。
中翻英.en: Humans know very little about outer space, but we have long been fascinated by it.

中翻英.zh: 太空科技的快速發展，使我們得以探索它的奧秘。
中翻英.en: The rapid development of space technology allows us to explore its mysteries.

中翻英.zh: 身為地球村的成員，我們不應把自己侷限在這個小島上。
中翻英.en: As members of the global village, we should not confine ourselves to this small island.

中翻英.zh: 我們不但應該參與國際性的活動，並且應該展現我們自己的文化特色。
中翻英.en: We should not only participate in international affairs but also exhibit our distinctive cultural characteristics.

中翻英.zh: 蚵仔煎（oyster omelets）是在每個夜市都找得到的本地食物。
中翻英.en: Oyster omelets are a local food found in every night market.

中翻英.zh: 其味道取決於蚵仔的品質：蚵仔越新鮮蚵仔煎越好吃。
中翻英.en: Their taste depends on the quality of the oysters: the fresher the oysters, the better the omelet.

中翻英.zh: 一般人都知道閱讀對孩子有益。
中翻英.en: Most people know that reading is beneficial for children.

中翻英.zh: 老師應該多鼓勵學生到圖書館借書。
中翻英.en: Teachers should encourage students to borrow books from the library more often.

中翻英.zh: 為提供一個無煙的用餐環境，許多餐廳不允許室內抽煙。
中翻英.en: In order to provide a dining environment free from cigarette smoke, many restaurants have banned smoking.

中翻英.zh: 雖然遭到許多癮君子的反對，這對不抽煙的人的確是一大福音。
中翻英.en: Although many regular smokers oppose the ban, it is good news for people who don't smoke.

中翻英.zh: 如果我們只為自己而活，就不會真正地感到快樂。
中翻英.en: If we live only for ourselves, we will not truly feel happy.

中翻英.zh: 當我們開始為他人著想，快樂之門自然會開啟。
中翻英.en: When we start to think of others, the door to happiness will naturally open.

中翻英.zh: 大眾運輸的快速發展已逐漸縮短了都市和鄉村的距離。
中翻英.en: The rapid development of mass transportation has gradually shortened the distance between the city and the countryside.

中翻英.zh: 有了高速鐵路，我們可以在半天內往返台灣南北兩地。
中翻英.en: With high-speed rail, we can travel from northern Taiwan to southern Taiwan and back within half a day.

中翻英.zh: 聽音樂是一個你可以終生享受的嗜好。
中翻英.en: Listening to music is a hobby you can enjoy for a lifetime.

中翻英.zh: 但能彈奏樂器可以為你帶來更多的喜悅。
中翻英.en: But being able to play an instrument can bring you even more joy.

中翻英.zh: 全球糧食危機已經在世界許多地區造成嚴重的社會問題。
中翻英.en: The global food crisis has already caused serious social problems in a lot of places around the world.

中翻英.zh: 專家警告我們不應該再將食物價格低廉視為理所當然。
中翻英.en: Experts warn that we should no longer take low food prices for granted.

中翻英.zh: 所以我爺爺就開始帶著一個裝滿空罐子和垃圾的大袋子。
中翻英.en: So my grandfather started to carry a large bag filled with empty cans and garbage

中翻英.zh: 當他正要告訴駕駛他不需要任何幫忙的時候，
中翻英.en: When he was about to tell the driver that he didn't need any assistance,

中翻英.zh: 由於英語已成世界語，英語能力對於求職很重要。
中翻英.en: As English has become a global language, English proficiency is important for job application.

中翻英.zh: 要學好英語，除了強烈的動機，還要有好的學習策略。
中翻英.en: To learn English successfully, in addition to strong motivation, good learning strategies are needed.

中翻英.zh: 大部分學生不習慣自己解決問題，他們總是期待老師提供標準答案。
中翻英.en: Most students are not used to solving problems on their own; they always expect teachers to provide standard answers.

中翻英.zh: 除了用功讀書獲取知識外，學生也應該培養獨立思考的能力。
中翻英.en: In addition to studying hard to acquire knowledge, students should also cultivate the ability to think independently.

中翻英.zh: 玉山是東亞第一高峰，以生態多樣聞名。
中翻英.en: Mt. Jade is the highest mountain in East Asia and is well known for its biological diversity.

中翻英.zh: 大家在網路上投票給它，要讓它成為世界七大奇觀之一。
中翻英.en: Many people voted online for it to be made one of the Seven Wonders of the World.

中翻英.zh: 在過去，腳踏車主要是作為一種交通工具。
中翻英.en: In the past, bicycles were mainly used as a means of transportation.

中翻英.zh: 然而，騎腳踏車現在已經成為一種熱門的休閒活動。
中翻英.en: However, cycling has now become a popular leisure activity.

中翻英.zh: 近二十年來我國的出生率快速下滑。
中翻英.en: The birth rate in our country has declined sharply in the last twenty years.

中翻英.zh: 這可能導致我們未來人力資源的嚴重不足。
中翻英.en: This may result in a serious shortage of human resources in the future.

中翻英.zh: 臺灣的夜市早已被認為足以代表我們的在地文化。
中翻英.en: Taiwan's night markets have long been considered representative of our local culture.

中翻英.zh: 每年它們都吸引了成千上萬來自不同國家的觀光客。
中翻英.en: Every year, they attract tens of thousands of tourists from different countries.

中翻英.zh: 日本的核電廠爆炸已經引起全球對核子能源安全的疑慮。
中翻英.en: The explosion at the nuclear power plant in Japan has aroused global concern about the safety of nuclear energy.

中翻英.zh: 科學家正尋求安全、乾淨又不昂貴的綠色能源，以滿足我們對電的需求。
中翻英.en: Scientists are seeking safe, clean, and inexpensive green energy to satisfy our need for electricity.

中翻英.zh: 我們必須體認到每個孩子生來就有不同的興趣與天賦。
中翻英.en: We must recognize that every child is born with different interests and talents.

中翻英.zh: 學校應該提供一個好的環境，來幫助學生發展個人特質。
中翻英.en: Schools should provide a good environment to help students develop their personal characteristics.

中翻英.zh: 近年來，許多臺灣製作的影片已經受到國際的重視。
中翻英.en: In recent years, many Taiwanese-made films have gained international attention.

中翻英.zh: 拍攝這些電影的地點也成為熱門的觀光景點。
中翻英.en: The locations where these movies were filmed have also become popular tourist attractions.

中翻英.zh: 有些我們認為安全的包裝食品可能含有對人體有害的成分。
中翻英.en: Some packaged foods that we consider safe may contain ingredients that are harmful to humans.

中翻英.zh: 為了我們自身的健康，在購買食物前我們應仔細閱讀包裝上的說明。
中翻英.en: For the sake of our health, we should read the nutritional information on food packages carefully.

中翻英.zh: 都會地區的高房價對社會產生了嚴重的影響。
中翻英.en: High housing prices in urban areas have had a serious impact on society.

中翻英.zh: 政府正推出新的政策，以滿足人們的住房需求。
中翻英.en: The government is introducing new policies to meet people's housing needs.

中翻英.zh: 對現今的許多學生而言，在課業與課外活動間取得平衡是一大挑戰。
中翻英.en: For many students today, striking a balance between schoolwork and extracurricular activities is a great challenge.

中翻英.zh: 有效的時間管理是每位有責任感的學生必須學習的首要課題。
中翻英.en: Effective time management is the primary concern for every responsible student.

中翻英.zh: 有些年輕人辭掉都市裡的高薪工作，返回家鄉種植有機蔬菜。
中翻英.en: Some young people quit high-paying jobs in the city to return to their hometowns and grow organic vegetables.

中翻英.zh: 藉由決心與努力，很多人成功了，不但獲利更多，還過著更健康的生活。
中翻英.en: Through determination and hard work, many have succeeded, not only earning more but also living healthier lives.

中翻英.zh: 食用過多油炸食物可能會導致學童體重過重，甚至更嚴重的健康問題。
中翻英.en: Consuming too much fried food can lead to overweight children and even more serious health problems.

中翻英.zh: 因此，家長與老師應該共同合作，找出處理這個棘手議題的有效措施。
中翻英.en: Therefore, parents and teachers should work together to find effective measures to address this thorny issue.

中翻英.zh: 一個成功的企業不應該把獲利當作最主要的目標。
中翻英.en: A successful business should not consider profit as its main goal.

中翻英.zh: 它應該負起社會責任，以增進大眾的福祉。
中翻英.en: It should take on social responsibility to improve public welfare.

中翻英.zh: 台灣便利商店的密集度是全世界最高的，平均每兩千人就有一家。
中翻英.en: Taiwan has the highest density of convenience stores in the world, with an average of one store for every 2,000 people.

中翻英.zh: 除了購買生活必需品，顧客也可以在這些商店繳費，甚至領取網路訂購之物品。
中翻英.en: Besides purchasing daily necessities, customers can also pay bills and even pick up items ordered online at these stores.

中翻英.zh: 相較於他們父母的世代，現今年輕人享受較多的自由和繁榮。
中翻英.en: Compared to their parents' generation, young people today enjoy more freedom and prosperity.

中翻英.zh: 但是在這個快速改變的世界中，他們必須學習如何有效地因應新的挑戰。
中翻英.en: However, in this rapidly changing world, they must learn how to effectively cope with new challenges.

中翻英.zh: 蚊子一旦叮咬過某些傳染病的患者，就可能將病毒傳給其他人。
中翻英.en: Once mosquitoes bite patients with certain infectious diseases, they can potentially transmit the virus to others.

中翻英.zh: 它們在人類中快速散播疾病，造成的死亡遠超乎我們所能想像。
中翻英.en: They spread diseases rapidly among humans, causing more deaths than we can imagine.

中翻英.zh: 玉山(Jade Mountain)在冬天常常覆蓋著厚厚的積雪，使整個山頂閃耀如玉。
中翻英.en: Jade Mountain is often covered with thick snow in winter, making the entire peak shine like jade.

中翻英.zh: 征服玉山一直是國內外登山者最困難的挑戰之一。
中翻英.en: Conquering Jade Mountain has been one of the most difficult challenges for mountain climbers at home and abroad.

中翻英.zh: 世界大學運動會（The Universiade）是一項國際體育與文化盛事，每兩年一次由不同城市舉辦。
中翻英.en: The Universiade is an international sporting and cultural event held by different cities every two years.

中翻英.zh: 在比賽中，來自全球大學的學生運動員建立友誼，並學習運動家精神的真諦。
中翻英.en: During the competition, student athletes from universities all over the world build friendship and learn the true meaning of sportsmanship.

中翻英.zh: 近年來，有越來越多超級颱風，通常造成嚴重災害。
中翻英.en: In recent years, there have been an increasing number of super typhoons, which usually cause severe damage.

中翻英.zh: 颱風來襲時，我們應準備足夠的食物，並待在室內，若有必要，應迅速移動至安全的地方。
中翻英.en: When a typhoon strikes, we should prepare enough food, stay indoors, and if necessary, quickly move to a safe place.

中翻英.zh: 快速時尚以速度與低價為特色，讓人們可以用負擔得起的價格買到流行的服飾。
中翻英.en: Fast fashion is characterized by speed and low prices, allowing people to buy trendy clothing at affordable prices.

中翻英.zh: 然而，它所鼓勵的「快速消費」卻製造了大量的廢棄物，造成巨大的污染問題。
中翻英.en: However, the "fast consumption" it encourages has produced huge amounts of waste, resulting in enormous pollution problems.

中翻英.zh: 自2007年營運以來，高鐵（the High Speed Rail）已成為臺灣最便利、最快速的交通工具之一。
中翻英.en: Since its operation in 2007, the High Speed Rail has become one of the most convenient and fastest means of transportation in Taiwan.

中翻英.zh: 對於強調職場效率的人而言，高鐵當然是商務旅行的首選。
中翻英.en: For those who emphasize workplace efficiency, the High Speed Rail is certainly the first choice for business travel.

中翻英.zh: 創意布條最近在夜市成了有效的廣告工具，也刺激了買氣的成長。
中翻英.en: Creative banners have recently become effective advertising tools in night markets and have stimulated the growth of sales.

中翻英.zh: 其中有些看似無意義，但卻相當引人注目，且常能帶給人們會心的一笑。
中翻英.en: Some of them seem meaningless, but they are quite eye-catching and often bring people a knowing smile.

中翻英.zh: 我們有時會違背自己的意願去做某些事情，就只為了要取悅朋友。
中翻英.en: We sometimes do things against our will just to please our friends.

中翻英.zh: 其實，在面對同儕壓力的時候，我們應該學習堅持自己的原則。
中翻英.en: In fact, when facing peer pressure, we should learn to stick to our principles.

中翻英.zh: 早期的博物館只開放給中上階層，而且參觀者必須事先申請進入許可。
中翻英.en: The early museums were only open to the upper-middle class, and visitors had to apply for admission in advance.

中翻英.zh: 現今多數人可以親自或透過線上導覽，享受探索文化珍寶的樂趣。
中翻英.en: Nowadays, most people can enjoy the fun of exploring cultural treasures in person or via online tour.

中翻英.zh: 學習不再侷限於學校內的正規教育，非正式學習已開始扮演重要的角色。
中翻英.en: Learning is no longer confined to formal education in schools; informal learning has begun to play an important role.

中翻英.zh: 例如，志工服務讓學生學到如何與不同背景及不同年齡層的人互動。
中翻英.en: For example, volunteer service allows students to learn how to interact with people from different backgrounds and age groups.

中翻英.zh: 根據新聞報導，每年全球有超過百萬人在道路事故中喪失性命。
中翻英.en: According to news reports, over a million people lose their lives in road accidents globally each year.

中翻英.zh: 因此，交通法規必須嚴格執行，以確保所有用路人的安全。
中翻英.en: Therefore, traffic regulations must be strictly enforced to ensure the safety of all road users.

中翻英.zh: 很多人好奇今年年初在美國破紀錄的低溫是否與全球暖化有關。
中翻英.en: Many people are curious about whether the record-breaking low temperatures at the beginning of this year in the US were related to global warming.

中翻英.zh: 不論答案為何，氣候專家預告這種不正常的天氣將會變成新的常態。
中翻英.en: No matter what the answer is, climate experts have predicted that this kind of abnormal weather will become the new normal.

中翻英.zh: 很多人害怕公開演講，常在上台之前發抖、覺得頭昏。
中翻英.en: Many people are afraid of public speaking, often trembling and feeling dizzy before going on stage.

中翻英.zh: 只要我們對自己有信心，並持續練習，就可以克服怯場的問題。
中翻英.en: As long as we have confidence in ourselves and keep practicing, we can overcome the problem of stage fright.

中翻英.zh: 飼養寵物並非一項短暫的人生體驗，而是一個對動物的終生承諾。
中翻英.en: Keeping a pet is not a short-term life experience, but a lifelong commitment to an animal.

中翻英.zh: 在享受寵物所帶來的歡樂時，我們不該忽略要善盡照顧他們的責任。
中翻英.en: When we enjoy the joy pets bring us, we should not ignore the responsibility of taking good care of them.

中翻英.zh: 歷史一再證明，戰爭會造成極為可怕的災難。
中翻英.en: History proves time and again that wars will cause extremely terrible disasters.

中翻英.zh: 避免衝突、確保世界和平應該是所有人類追求的目標。
中翻英.en: To avoid conflicts and ensure world peace should be the goal pursued by all human beings.

中翻英.zh: 每逢選舉季節，總會看到政治人物造訪各地著名廟宇。
中翻英.en: Every election season, politicians can be seen visiting famous temples in different places.

中翻英.zh: 除了祈求好的選舉結果，他們也希望展現對在地文化與習俗的尊重。
中翻英.en: Besides praying for good election results, they also hope to show respect to local culture and customs.

中翻英.zh: 人類的想像和創意是科技進步最大的驅動力。
中翻英.en: Human's imagination and creativity is the biggest driving force for technological advancement.

中翻英.zh: 過去在科幻電影中出現的神奇物件，現在正逐一成真。
中翻英.en: Amazing things that appeared in science-fiction movies in the past are now becoming reality one by one.

中翻英.zh: 現在越來越多高中英文老師已經增加在課堂上使用英文的百分比。
中翻英.en: Now, more and more senior high school English teachers have increased the percentage of English use in class.

中翻英.zh: 他們將學生依英語能力分成不同組別，進行多樣的聽、說活動。
中翻英.en: They divide students into different groups based on their English ability and conduct various listening and speaking activities.
